title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Aug 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from August 14, 2015 to August 14, 2015. Affected areas: Outagamie. Episode summary: Thunderstorms that developed ahead of an approaching surface boundary moved south across Wisconsin. Some of the storms produced heavy rainfall that caused minor urban flooding, damaging winds that downed trees and power lines, and hail up to golf ball size across eastern Wisconsin. As the storms moved across southern Lake Winnebago they produced gusts to around 40 mph that caused large waves to quickly develop, capsizing a boat with four people on board. Three of the boat's passengers reached shore while the fourth had to be rescued by the Winnebago County Sheriff's Department. Details: Heavy rainfall caused street flooding on Highway 47 in Black Creek. Water was about six inches deep.

title: Tornado: California, Aug 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Tornado, from August 06, 2015 to August 06, 2015. Affected areas: Riverside. Episode summary: Monsoon moisture and some instability from an easterly wave resulted in scattered thunderstorms over the mountains and lower deserts. Most notable of these was a severe thunderstorm that occurred near Mecca in the southern Coachella Valley during the evening. This storm produced a copious amount of lightning and very strong, damaging winds (over 100 power poles damaged or destroyed). While the precipitation did not hit many gages, the Kent Sea Farms gage, near Mecca, recorded 0.32 inches of rain with this storm. After storm damage surveys, it was concluded that the most likely cause of the damage was a brief, nearly-stationary, EF1 tornado. Details: The damage was west of Highway 111 between 64th and 66th Avenues, paralleling Highway 86 towards the mountains, or approximately 3 1/2 miles. An emergency manager for the Imperial irrigation water district (IID) reported a total of 140 poles damaged, 30 of which were steel. Reported property and crop damage: about $18,000,000.

title: Flood: Texas, Oct 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from October 22, 2015 to October 22, 2015. Affected areas: Lubbock. Episode summary: A slow-moving upper low in Arizona helped spread unseasonably rich moisture and strong upper diffluence over all of eastern New Mexico and West Texas from the 21st through the 22nd. Multiple rounds of scattered showers and storms spread north during the day on the 21st before strong lift arrived from New Mexico late in the evening in the form of a squall line. This large complex of storms crawled slowly east over the South Plains and Rolling Plains during the overnight hours accompanied by heavy rainfall rates at times; however, the majority of the heavy rain amounts of 1.5 to three inches and subsequent minor flooding were attributed more to the long duration of the precipitation event which limited the severity of flooding. Only one road closure due to flooding was logged by TXDOT. Isolated severe wind gusts accompanied the squall line over the South Plains, but one severe thunderstorm well ahead of this line of storms impacted far northeast Childress County where several power poles were felled. By far, the greatest impact of this event was dealt to regional cotton farmers who would suffer a moderate financial toll due to deteriorated cotton quality. This rainfall did alleviate short term drought conditions region wide, particularly in the Rolling Plains where D2 (severe) and D3 (extreme) drought levels were abated by two to four inches of rain. Details: A portion of Farm-to-Market Road 835 at Buffalo Springs Lake was closed for several hours due to high water.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 12, 2015

The Cox Ranch Fire, located 19 miles west southwest of Ozona, burned 433 acres.

title: Flash Flood: California, Oct 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from October 15, 2015 to October 16, 2015. Affected areas: Los Angeles, Santa Barbara. Episode summary: An unseasonable cutoff low brought a moist and unstable air mass across Southern California. Widespread thunderstorm activity was observed. Many of these storms were very strong, producing large hail, heavy rain, flash flooding as well as significant mud and debris flows. Details: Strong thunderstorms generated flash flooding and mud and debris flows near Lake Hughes and Elizabeth Lake. On Elizabeth Lake Road, a car was stuck in mud. Along Lake Hughes Road, four people were rescued by the Los Angeles county Swift Water Rescue Team. Strong thunderstorms generated flash flooding across the Antelope Valley. At the intersection of Highway 138 and 170th Street, a car was trapped in flood waters. Strong thunderstorms generated flash flooding across the mountains of Los Angeles county. Due to flash flooding as well as mud flows, both Elizabeth Lake Road and Bouquet Canyon Road were closed.

Neither, Fresno or Bakersfield received any precipitation during the month of August.||The U.S. Drought Monitor continued to report exceptional drought conditions across the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The general trend of below normal precipitation and above normal temperatures has continued this year. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. title: Drought: Texas, Sep 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from September 01, 2015 to September 30, 2015. Affected areas: Bastrop, Blanco, Burnet, Caldwell, Gillespie, Guadalupe, Kendall, Llano, Williamson, Wilson, Zavala. Episode summary: Most of South Central Texas had less than normal precipitation in September with many counties getting less than 25% of normal. The result of this dryness was Burnet, Gillespie, Kendall, Llano, Williamson, Wilson, and Zavala Counties went into severe drought category (Stage D2) and Guadalupe County went into extreme drought category (Stage D3). Bastrop, Blanco, and Caldwell Counties remained in Stage D2. Of the counties in Stage D2 or worse all had burn bans in effect at the end of the month except Zavala. The Texas Crop and Weather Report issued by Texas A&M indicated grasses were becoming dry and some ranchers were feeding hay due to poor grazing conditions. The seven day stream flow average at the end of the month was much below normal (less than 10 percent) in the Colorado and Lower Nueces River basins and below normal (10-24 percent) in the Lower Guadalupe basin. The Edwards Aquifer fell during the month and was at 645.2 feet. This was 14.6 feet higher than at the end of September 2014, but 18.1 feet below average. The Barton Springs Edwards Aquifer Conservation District was in Stage 1 (10 percent reduction) drought status. Area lakes and reservoirs continued below normal pool elevations. Lake Buchanan was 14.3 feet below normal and Lake Georgetown was 9.2 feet below normal. Fredericksburg remained in stage 3 water restrictions. Details: A four month old boy died after being left in a car during the early afternoon hours of September 8th. The temperature was around 90 degrees with heat index value around 100 degrees.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Sep 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from September 06, 2015 to September 08, 2015. Affected areas: Johnson, Mclennan. Episode summary: Dry vegetation resulting from summer drought across north and central Texas led to a few grass fires across the region. Details: A grass and brush fire burned approximately 150 acres about half a mile west of New Dallas Highway in Lacy Lakeview, TX. There were no injuries and no known structures were damaged, but 50 or so firefighters from at least 9 different fire departments were used to battle the fire and bring it under control. A fire in a travel trailer sparked a grass fire, which burned around 2 acres of grass, brush and trees around the 9700 block of CR 529A in Johnson County. The fire also burned a shed and a barn. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, Sep 08, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from September 08, 2015 to September 08, 2015. Affected areas: Brown, Outagamie. Episode summary: Heavy rain developed as low pressure moved across Wisconsin. The heaviest rain fell during the morning, with numerous locations in the Fox Valley receiving more than 2 inches of rain, much of which fell in just 2 to 3 hours. The highest rainfall totals were 3.50 inches in Allouez (Brown Co.) and 3.15 inches near Kaukauna (Outagamie Co.). Green Bay received 2.50 inches of rain, including 0.81 inch in just 15 minutes, more than doubling the previous record rainfall (1.21 inches in 2006) for September 8th. Details: Torrential rainfall on the west side of Green Bay flooded roads and caused manhole covers to pop off of their bases. Torrential rainfall in the Kaukauna area caused street flooding and popped manhole covers from their bases.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Sep 11, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from September 11, 2015 to September 11, 2015. Affected areas: Aransas, Kleberg, Nueces, San Patricio. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms formed over South Texas in advance of a slow moving frontal boundary and a weak upper level disturbance. Locally heavy rainfall over portions of the Coastal Bend produce flooding of roads during the afternoon. Details: Water covered the roadways in several locations in Rockport including West Market Street, Business 35, and Austin Street. Water covered the road in several locations in Flour Bluff along Waldron Road and in North Padre Island near the Padre Isles Country Club. Public reported flooding of roads in Riviera.

title: Tornado: Texas, Sep 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from September 26, 2015 to September 26, 2015. Affected areas: Jim Wells, Nueces. Episode summary: An upper level low combined with abundant moisture and a coastal trough to produce scattered thunderstorms over South Texas. Thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts near Portland. Two weak tornadoes near Alice and Petronila. Details: Public reported a weak tornado occurred near Farm to Market Road 665 at Petronila. Public shared a video on social media of a brief tornado east of Alice.

title: High Wind: California, Nov 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from November 14, 2015 to November 14, 2015. Affected areas: North Central & Southeast Siskiyou County. Episode summary: A strong front brought high winds to parts of northern California. Details: The TT109 RAWS unit reported a gust to 58 mph at 14/2220 PST and a gust to 62 mph at 14/2320 PST.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 05, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 05, 2015 to November 05, 2015. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: The passage of strong upper trough resulted in strong winds in the Guadalupe Mountains.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 11, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 11, 2015 to November 11, 2015. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: A strong upper trough moving from the Four Corners to the central U.S.Plains resulted in strong winds in the Guadalupe Mountains.

title: Tornado: Texas, Nov 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from November 17, 2015 to November 17, 2015. Affected areas: Grimes. Episode summary: A strong storm system moved eastward across the state and produced a round of showers and thunderstorms along and ahead of a cold front. Some of the thunderstorms produced wind damage and a tornado. Details: This EF-1 tornado produced a damage path that started three miles west of Carlos near Route 30 with damage to trees and structures along Ada Oaks Lane. The path continued to the north northeast crossing County Road 173 then ran more parallel to County Road 244, crossing County Road 244 twice along its over 9 mile path. Damage was intermittent with numerous large trees uprooted or with their trunks Reported property and crop damage: about $200,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 21, 2015 to October 22, 2015. Affected areas: Andrews, Ector, Gaines, Martin, Midland, Scurry, Upton. Episode summary: A strong upper level low pressure area over western Arizona moved slowly eastward. This feature increased upper level lift over West Texas and southeast New Mexico. This upper low was pulling moisture northward into the area from the Gulf of Mexico allowing for precipitable water values to rise to around one inch. Sufficient heating, instability, and high moisture content contributed to severe thunderstorms with large hail as well as flash flooding. Thunderstorms increased in coverage overnight as an upper level disturbance moved over the region. Details: The Gaines County Sheriffs Office reported 6-12 inches of water flowing over US Highway 180 on the east side of Seminole. At least 16 homes were flooded in Odessa around the 3600 block of Walnut Avenue and on Tom Green between 13th and 14th Street. The Central Fire Department reported 3.7 inches of rain in the prior 4 hours before 1:00 AM CST. The damage costs are a very rough estimate. Andrews County Sheriffs Office reported water flooding residents' yards and 1 to 2 feet of water covering some roadways. A vehicle was submerged under water and southbound lanes of N Main and NW Mustang Streets were being barricaded. Damage costs are a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $376,450.

title: Tornado: Texas, Oct 31, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from October 31, 2015 to October 31, 2015. Affected areas: Brazoria, Galveston, Harris. Episode summary: Tornadoes formed along a near coastal county warm frontal boundary that was downstream of a central Texas cold front. Details: The EF-2 tornado touched down just east of Clover Field Airport (Brazoria County) and continued on a narrow northeast track into Galveston County. This tornado expanded in size and weakened in intensity as it approached FM 518 over the last half of its track. There was extensive tree damage along the entire track. Homes sustained partial roof loss and tree damage consistent with an EF-1 rating fro A small EF-1 tornado moved from a wildlife management area one mile southwest south of Jones Creek where it uprooted several large trees. The tornado then crossed Highway 36 and severely damaged a mobile home just north of the roadway. The tornado caused minor damage for approximately a mile toward the northeast before reaching the Brazos River, or one mile northeast of Jones Creek. Estimated peak A brief EF-0 tornado caused damage to homes near the intersection of Clear Lake City Boulevard and El Dorado Boulevard. The estimated peak wind was 85 mph. Reported property and crop damage: about $17,895,000.

title: Cold/Wind Chill: California, Oct 03, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Cold/Wind Chill, from October 03, 2015 to October 03, 2015. Affected areas: Eastern Sierra Slopes Of Inyo County. Episode summary: Two hikers on the Mount Whitney Trail were treated for hypothermia. Details: Two hikers attempting a day hike on the Mount Whitney Trail were rescued and treated for hypothermia.

title: Flash Flood, Winter Weather: California, Oct 04, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Winter Weather, from October 04, 2015 to October 05, 2015. Affected areas: Eastern Sierra Slopes Of Inyo County, Inyo, San Bernardino. Episode summary: A strong upper level low fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Many storms produced flash flooding, and isolated severe weather also occurred. Details: Rocks and mud covered Highway 168 just east of Death Valley Road. Several rooms at the Furnace Creek Inn were flooded. Many roads were closed, including Daylight Pass Road, Badwater Road, Highway 190, and Scotty's Castle Road. Large boulders washed onto Whitney Portal Road. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,128,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Oct 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from October 15, 2015 to October 19, 2015. Affected areas: Inyo, San Bernardino. Episode summary: An upper level low pressure system brought a round of thunderstorms to the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Significant flash flooding occurred, along with isolated severe weather. Details: Numerous roads were closed in Death Valley National Park, and some were damaged. A vehicle was stuck in a flooded wash on Winter Road. The intersection of Sunfair Road and Aberdeen Drive was flooded. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,104,000.

title: Flood: California, Oct 19, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from October 19, 2015 to October 20, 2015. Affected areas: Inyo. Episode summary: A few thunderstorms lingered over the Mojave Desert as the low pressure system responsible for the previous three days' worth of flash flooding and severe weather slowly moved east. Isolated flash flooding occurred. Details: The Amargosa River flowed a few inches deep over Highway 178 near Shoshone in the morning. Later that night, the river crested at 14.5 feet at Tecopa, which was the fourth highest crest on record. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 22, 2015 to October 22, 2015. Affected areas: Oldham. Episode summary: A severe thunderstorm caused wind damage in the town of Dodson in Collingsworth County during the evening of the 21st. Earlier that afternoon, storms occurred further west in the southwest portion of the Texas Panhandle, but were non-severe. Hail, strong wind gusts, and heavy rain were all that was reported. As the night went on, heavy rain continued in some locations. This resulting in flooding in some areas. Flash flooding was reported in Vega where flood waters invaded 11 homes. Streets were impacted by flood waters, including Highway 385 through Vega. Minor flooding of streets throughout the city of Amarillo was reported. Rainfall amounts at many locations ranged from 2 to 3 inches. Details: Heavy rain from thunderstorms resulted in flooding in Vega during the late evening of the 21st through the early morning hours of the 22nd. Water invaded 11 homes in Vega and some streets were flooded, including Highway 385.

title: High Wind: Texas, Oct 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from October 27, 2015 to October 27, 2015. Affected areas: Hartley, Moore, Randall. Episode summary: A strong cold front moved south through the Texas Panhandle during the evening of the 28th. Immediately behind the cold front, strong winds occurred. High winds were measured at Dalhart, Dumas, Umbarger and Canyon. No damage was reported. Details: The Automated Surface Observing System located at the Dalhart airport measured a wind gust of 62 mph. This occurred shortly after a strong cold front moved through. The KVII Schoolnet located at Dumas High School measured a wind gust of 59 mph. This occurred behind a strong cold front that moved through. The West Texas Mesonet located 2 miles northeast of Umbarger recorded a wind gust of 62 mph. This occurred behind a strong cold front that passed through.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Nov 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from November 17, 2015 to November 17, 2015. Affected areas: Angelina, Nacogdoches, Shelby. Episode summary: A deep upper trough exited the Inter-Mountain West and moved into the Southern Plains on the 17th of November. Ahead of this trough, copious amounts of moisture streamed northward from the Eastern Pacific and Gulf of Mexico. A warm front also lifted northward form the Gulf Coast, through Northeast Texas, Northwest Louisiana and Southern Arkansas. The atmosphere became weakly unstable across the region after sunrise on the 17th but atmospheric wind shear was very strong, both in the lower levels and the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere. As a result, storms took on bowing line segments with a few discrete storms also present during the day. These storms produced widespread wind damage and some flash flooding from excessive heavy rainfall with thunderstorm training occurred. Details: High water rescues from flooded automobiles became necessary when excessive heavy rainfall resulted in a rapid rise of the Bonita Creek in Nacogdoches, Texas. There were no reports of injuries. Several roads in the Hudson and Pollock communities were washed out due to flash flooding. High water was reported on Hwy. 21 between Nacogdoches and San Augustine, Texas. Reported property and crop damage: about $200,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Sep 28, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from September 28, 2015 to September 30, 2015. Affected areas: Van Zandt. Episode summary: At the end of the month of September, most of north and central Texas were under dry conditions. Around the 28th and 29th, windy conditions helped spread grass fires across the area. Details: On September 28th, multiple departments were dispatched to a grass fire south of Wills Point, between FM47 and CR3918. The fire was reportedly triggered when workers in the area were clearing a portion of the land and brush got into old fencing or metal, creating sparks. This fire damaged or destroyed over 200 acres, and threatened homes, but no homes were damaged. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Nov 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from November 12, 2015 to November 12, 2015. Affected areas: Ozaukee. Episode summary: Strong low pressure tracked from northeast Wisconsin into Ontario Canada and generated strong gusty winds in the 40 mph range over southern Wisconsin. Some damage occurred in Ozaukee County. Details: A power pole was blown down in the village of Belgium. A 10 inch diameter tree was blown down and blocking a roadway near Saukville. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Winter Storm, Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Nov 20, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, Winter Weather, from November 20, 2015 to November 21, 2015. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Green, Iowa, Jefferson, Kenosha, Lafayette, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Racine, Rock and 4 more areas. Episode summary: A strengthening polar trough and front brought heavy snow to southern Wisconsin, mainly along and south of a line from Lone Rock to Milwaukee. Lake enhanced snow contributed to the overall snow totals over far southeast Wisconsin. Snow totals ranged from 5 to 18 inches with the heaviest totals in the counties bordering Illinois. Wet, heavy snow brought branches down onto electrical wires causing power outages mainly in the counties bordering Illinois where the heaviest snow fell. Vehicle slide-offs and accidents were prevalent. Details: Six to ten inches of snow. Six to thirteen inches of snow. Four to seven inches of snow.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Sep 02, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from September 02, 2015 to September 03, 2015. Affected areas: Shackelford. Episode summary: A very dry and hot summer with very little precipitation and abundant fuels from the spring continued to result in ideal conditions for wildfires across portions of West Central Texas. One large wildfire called the Chimney Creek 2 Wildfire scorched over 2000 acres of land in western Shackelford County. Details: The Chimney Creek 2 fire burned approximately 2200 acres near the intersection of U.S. Highway 180 and Private Road 2210 in western Shackelford County or 5 miles southeast of Lueders. Four homes were threatened. This fire was 100% contained on September 3rd.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Sep 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from September 26, 2015 to September 30, 2015. Affected areas: Coleman, Sutton. Episode summary: A very dry and hot summer with very little precipitation and abundant fuels from the spring continued to result in ideal conditions for wildfires across portions of West Central Texas. Two large wildfires developed in Sutton and Coleman Counties. Details: The Eiesenhower Wildfire burned approximately 336 acres near U.S. Highway 283 and County Road 152 or 3 miles west of Echo. The fire was 100% contained on September 30. The Bar None Fire burned approximately 480 acres just off of Private Road 3346 or 15 miles east southeast of Sonora. The fire was 100% contained on September 28.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jul 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from July 30, 2015 to July 30, 2015. Affected areas: Mason. Episode summary: Very dry conditions and hot temperatures for the last three weeks of July followed a very wet spring. The abundant fuels quickly dried and began to fuel wildfires. A wildfire burned about 550 acres near Mason. Details: The Eckert Road Fire burned 550 acres near the intersection of U.S. Highway 87 and Ranch Road 783 or about 7 miles northwest of Loyal Valley. The fire was 100% contained and one structure was lost in the fire.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: California, Sep 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, from September 07, 2015 to September 09, 2015. Affected areas: Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego. Episode summary: Subtropical moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Linda brought widespread showers to most of the area, deserts included. The first isolated thunderstorm developed on the 6th in San Diego County as a moisture surge in monsoon warm upper level flow arrived. Intense heavy rain from thunderstorms occurred on the 7th with flash flooding in several locations including Victorville and Forest Falls. A swift water rescue in Victorville was successful, but another incident in Forest Falls had one rescue but a drowning occurred when a 30-year-old couple crossed Mill Creek and were swept away. Most areas received between a few hundredths to one-third of an inch of rain, with a few upslope areas of the San Bernardino Mountains receiving up to around one inch. Additional thunderstorms developed on the 8th by noon over the mountains and quickly spread into the Inland Empire and Orange County, as well as near I-15 in San Diego County. Locally heavy rain and several trees and poles were downed in the Riverside area including a small dust storm. Several hail reports, mostly nickel-sized, but a few larger. Activity decreased on the 9th with only isolated thunderstorms formed. Details: CHP reported mud and rocks on Highway 78 near Yaqui Pass, closing Highway 78. CHP also reported flash flooding Highway S2 from mile marker 36 to mile marker 44, blocking the southbound lanes. CHP reported a rock/mudslide blocking the roadway at Highway S-22 near San Felipe Road. Multiple swift water rescues along Bear Valley Road. Water flowed fast down the road with some areas of water around 5 feet deep. A spotter reported water 4-6 deep at the intersection of Bear

title: Flash Flood, Flood: California, Sep 07, 2015
text: Highway S-22 near San Felipe Road. Multiple swift water rescues along Bear Valley Road. Water flowed fast down the road with some areas of water around 5 feet deep. A spotter reported water 4-6 deep at the intersection of Bear Valley Road and Apple Valley Road. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain: California, Sep 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, from September 15, 2015 to September 15, 2015. Affected areas: Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego. Episode summary: A broad upper level Pacific trough moved through the West Coast on September 14-15 and tapped into remnant tropical cyclone Linda moisture west of the California Bight. Widespread and locally heavy rainfall developed across the entire CWA with 1 to 2 inches of rainfall common. The heavy rain resulted in a major traffic impact during the morning commute in LA and Orange County, along with a debris flow in Silverado Canyon, and widespread urban flooding in San Diego, Orange, Riverside and San Bernardino Counties. Details: Several businesses in the Midway District were flooded...with water up to knee deep. Several vehicles were flooded in an underground parking garage in Ocean Beach, including a brand new Lamborghini luxury car flooded halfway deep. An Orange County Emergency Manager reported a debris flow 2 feet deep over Silverado Canyon Road at Maple Springs Truck Trail. Further downstream, there was another debris flow at Silverado Canyon Road and Oak Lane, but the road was still passable. A spotter reported the right lane of the Pacific Coast Highway flooded at the intersection with Main Street...road was nearly impassable. Reported property and crop damage: about $875,000.

title: High Wind: California, Nov 02, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from November 02, 2015 to November 02, 2015. Affected areas: Owens Valley, Western Mojave Desert. Episode summary: A strong trough of low pressure brought strong winds to southeast California and southern Nevada, along with snow in the higher elevations of the southern Great Basin. Details: This gust occurred 3 miles SE of Independence. This gust occurred at Bicycle Lake.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Nov 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from November 15, 2015 to November 16, 2015. Affected areas: Morongo Basin, Owens Valley, Western Mojave Desert. Episode summary: Another Pacific storm system brought strong winds to the Mojave Desert. Details: Strong winds blew over a big rig on Highway 395 11 miles S of Olancha. This gust occurred at Bicycle Lake. High winds 2 miles WSW of Landers blew over several storage sheds and damaged an air conditioning unit. A spotter estimated the winds to be 60-70 mph. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Oct 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from October 01, 2015 to October 27, 2015. Affected areas: Bastrop, Blanco, Burnet, Caldwell, Gillespie, Guadalupe, Kendall, Llano, Williamson, Wilson, Zavala. Episode summary: South Central Texas had several very heavy rain events and much of the region received five to 20 inches of rain during the month. This was two to four times normal rainfall in many places. The excessive rainfall was sufficient to move all of our counties out of Severe (Stage D2) drought category. Details: South Central Texas had several very heavy rain events and much of the region received five to 20 inches of rain during the month. This was two to four times normal rainfall in many places. The excessive rainfall was sufficient to move all of our counties out of Severe (Stage D2) drought category.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 08, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 08, 2015 to October 09, 2015. Affected areas: Dimmit, Kinney, Maverick, Uvalde, Zavala. Episode summary: An upper level low pressure center moved across northern Mexico and acted on a moist boundary layer to produce thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced heavy rain with Eagle Pass getting 10.00 inches and Uvalde 9.39 inches. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing FM481 with one foot of water over the road southwest of Uvalde. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing FM1021, Loop480, and Hwy277 near Seco Creek. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing FM1407 between Hwy83 and Hwy85. The junction of FM191 and Hwy277 was also closed due to flooding. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 15, 2015 to November 17, 2015. Affected areas: Davis / Apache Mountains Area, Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: A strong upper low will pass by just north of the region and result in high winds in the Guadalupe and Davis Mountains and portions of the Van Horn Highway 54 corridor. Details: A 72 mph gust was recorded at McDonald Observatory.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Nov 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from November 27, 2015 to November 28, 2015. Affected areas: Red River. Episode summary: A deep upper level trough became cut off from the westerlies across the Inter-Mountain West. This trough helped to bring up Gulf of Mexico moisture as well as Eastern Pacific moisture into the Southern Plains and Lower Mississippi Valley. The heavy rain threat was aided by moisture streaming northward from Hurricane Sandra which was just off the western Mexican coast at this time. Rainfall became quite heavy on the 27th and 28th of the month with two day rainfall totals in excess of 4 to 8 inches across portions of Northeast Texas. The result was widespread flooding across a few counties. Details: A truck was was stranded in high water on CR. 2149 near the Bagwell, Texas community. Intersection of FM 909 and FM1487 was closed south southwest of Clarksville, Texas. FM 1487 south of Clarksville, Texas was flooded and closed. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 21, 2015 to November 21, 2015. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: Intense northeast gap winds are expected through Guadalupe Pass behind a strong cold front.

title: Ice Storm: Texas, Nov 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, from November 26, 2015 to November 28, 2015. Affected areas: Andrews, Borden, Davis / Apache Mountains Area, Dawson, Gaines, Howard, Martin, Mitchell, Scurry. Episode summary: Abundant moisture ahead of an approaching upper level trough combined with cold air at the surface and resulted in icy conditions across the northern Permian Basin and western Low Rolling Plains. Details: At least 1/4 inch of ice accumulated on trees in Snyder and broke up to 5 inch diameter limbs. Heavy ice covering all exposed surfaces. Large tree limbs bowed to the ground under the weight of ice of 1/4-1/2 inch thick. Ice of 1/4 to 3/8 inch thick covered all exposed surfaces. Tree limbs bent to the ground, but roads were not icy.

title: Ice Storm: Texas, Nov 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, from November 26, 2015 to November 28, 2015. Affected areas: Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hall, King, Lubbock, Lynn and 3 more areas. Episode summary: Following a sharp cold front which ignited a few strong thunderstorms during the late afternoon hours on Thanksgiving Day, brisk northerly winds and freezing temperatures overspread the region and remained in place for nearly 48 hours. Atop this shallow layer of cold air, anomalously moist air from the Gulf of Mexico combined with a strong subtropical upper jet to produce periodic rounds of mostly freezing rain from Thanksgiving night through the morning hours on the 28th. A few periods of sleet and even very light snow accompanied this multi-day storm; however, all significant impacts were the direct result of icing from freezing rain. As the brunt of the freezing rain fell on the 27th, many dubbed this as the Black Friday ice storm. With the exception of the western South Plains and parts of the southern Rolling Plains, most locations received ice amounts of around 0.25. A pronounced swath of 0.50 to nearly 1 fell from just east of Crosbyton, northeast to Matador, Paducah, and Childress. The core of this heavy icing was the result of elevated thunderstorms during the evening on the 27th that trained across the northern Rolling Plains for nearly two hours. Thousands of people in Motley, Dickens, Cottle, and Childress Counties were without power for up to three days as power lines suffered extensive damage spanning long distances. Additionally, vehicle accidents peaked by Friday night as road temperatures finally cooled to the freezing point. In Lubbock, some overpasses were closed periodically through the night due to recurring accidents. From about 1920 CST until 2300 CST, Lubbock DPS was unable to

title: Ice Storm: Texas, Nov 26, 2015
text: accidents peaked by Friday night as road temperatures finally cooled to the freezing point. In Lubbock, some overpasses were closed periodically through the night due to recurring accidents. From about 1920 CST until 2300 CST, Lubbock DPS was unable to keep pace with the rate of vehicle accidents, some of which involved minor injuries. Fortunately, Lubbock International Airport reported very few delays and no cancellations that were directly attributable to the storm. This multi-day storm dealt a heavy economic blow to the city of Lubbock in the form of lost business revenue (estimated as high as $5M) as thousands of holiday shoppers wisely chose to stay home on Friday and Saturday instead of travel in such hazardous weather conditions. Dozens of weekend school athletic games and functions were either rescheduled or cancelled. Regional utility providers reported a combined loss of just over 90 utility poles with around 100 miles worth of damaged power lines - much of which occurred in Motley, Cottle, Childress, and Dickens Counties. Combined with property damage from fallen limbs and trees (many that still had leaves) and scores of vehicle accidents, total damages throughout the region could approach several million USD. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,387,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado: Texas, Nov 05, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado, from November 05, 2015 to November 06, 2015. Affected areas: Bell, Cooke, Grayson, Hunt, Navarro, Tarrant. Episode summary: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across north Texas on Thursday November 5 as a cold front moved southeast across the area. Severe storms produced wind and hail damage, as well as a couple of confirmed tornadoes, across the northern half of the region during the afternoon and evening hours. Details: Emergency management reported that Interstate 45 at mile marker 230 was under 1 foot of water. A water rescue was needed in this location. A public report was received around 615 PM indicating that low water crossings had become impassable and bar ditches had become full. Emergency management reported that 4 to 6 inches of water covered Highway 289 at FM 406. Reported property and crop damage: about $120,000.

title: Coastal Flood: Texas, Oct 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Coastal Flood, from October 21, 2015 to October 23, 2015. Affected areas: Aransas, Calhoun, Kleberg, Nueces, San Patricio. Episode summary: Persistent onshore flow over several days produced large swells with long periods which impacted the middle Texas coast. Tide levels ranged from 1.5 to 2 feet above the expected levels over the period from October 21st to the 23rd. This caused minor to almost moderate tidal overflow along the coast when tide levels approached 3 feet above mean sea level. Bay levels also increased to above 2 feet above mean sea level during this time. Water reached the dunes on Padre Island National Seashore where some erosion of the dunes occurred. Many roads were closed from Flour Bluff and North Beach to Rockport and Magnolia Beach. Details: Indian Point Pier and Park south of Portland was closed due to coastal flooding. Water was into the dunes during high tide and for much of the day. Some erosion of the dunes occurred at the Padre Island National Seashore. Tide levels reached a surge height of slightly above 2 feet. Laguna Shores Road was under water in numerous places. Businesses between Flour Bluff and Padre Island were forced to close due to roadways being flooded. Many roads were closed at North Beach including portions of Pearl Drive and Bridge Point Avenue. Several businesses and residential facilities experienced impacts from the coastal flooding. Water reached the dunes at Mustang Island and Padre Bal

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 24, 2015 to October 24, 2015. Affected areas: Duval, Nueces. Episode summary: Moisture depth reached record levels for this time of year as the remnants of Hurricane Patricia moving into the area combined with deep Gulf moisture already in place. Numerous showers and thunderstorms moved across the region on the 24th. Rainfall amounts of 4 to 6 inches occurred over portions of the coastal plains and the eastern Brush Country. This produced flash flooding around Corpus Christi and San Diego. Some thunderstorms produced minor wind damage in Freer and Orange Grove. Details: Nueces County Sheriffs Office reported flooding over portions of Staples Street in Corpus Christi. Several streets were flooded within the city of San Diego. Water was over the roadway on Interstate 37 at Callicoate Road. Streets were flooded in Calallen.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 09, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 09, 2015 to October 09, 2015. Affected areas: Webb. Episode summary: An upper level storm system over northern Mexico interacted with high moisture over South Texas to produce a large area of showers and thunderstorms over the Brush Country during the morning hours. The heavy rainfall produced flooding of roads across portions of Laredo. Details: Several roads were closed due to high water in Laredo. Jacaman Road was closed at the intersection with McPherson Road, Bartlett Avenue, and Polaris Drive. The intersections of San Dario Avenue at Mann Road and Loop 20 at Los Cabos Drive were closed also.

title: Ice Storm: Texas, Nov 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, from November 27, 2015 to November 29, 2015. Affected areas: Hardeman. Episode summary: An upper low moving in combined with abundant moisture from the gulf to produce a four day rain event from the 26th through the 29th. When strong front came down Thursday night (11/26), temperatures began to drop below freezing across northern, western, and central Oklahoma and parts of western north Texas. These areas experienced a shift from rain to freezing rain. Freezing rain continued into early Sunday morning as temperatures continued to hover in the 20s to lower 30s. Details: Observed 0.5 inches of ice accumulation.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Nov 20, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from November 20, 2015 to November 21, 2015. Affected areas: Crawford, Grant. Episode summary: An area of low pressure tracked across the Central Plains and spread a band of heavy snow into southwest Wisconsin during the afternoon of November 20th. The snow continued through much of the early morning hours of the 21st before tapering off during the late morning. The heaviest snow fell primarily south of U.S. Highway 18 with amounts of 6 to 10 inches common and there were some localized amounts in excess of a foot. The highest reported totals were across Grant County with 14 inches southeast of Platteville and 12 inches near Lancaster and in Platteville. Details: COOP and volunteer observers measured between 4 and 7 inches of snow across Crawford County. The highest reported total was 7.1 inches in Prairie du Chien. COOP and volunteer observers measured between 9 and 14 inches of snow across Grant County. The highest reported total was 14 inches southeast of Platteville.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Nov 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from November 24, 2015 to November 25, 2015. Affected areas: Modoc County, North Central & Southeast Siskiyou County, South Central Siskiyou County. Episode summary: The first big winter storm of the season brought heavy snow to some locations in northern California. Details: Mesonet Station Adin Mountain 8ENE Adin reported 15 inches of snow in 24 hours. Mesonet Station 3S McCloud reported 10 inches of snow in 24 hours. A weather spotter in Tennant reported 10 inches of snow in 12 hours.

title: Tornado: Texas, Nov 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from November 16, 2015 to November 16, 2015. Affected areas: Gaines. Episode summary: An upper low was over the Four Corners region with strong upper level jet winds over West Texas. Plentiful moisture was in place across the area to the east of a surface trough and dryline. A Pacific cold front moving in from the west collided with the dryline and increased lift. These conditions, along with good instability, allowed for a tornado and thunderstorms with large hail and strong winds to develop across the Permian Basin. Details: A thunderstorm moved across Gaines County and produced a tornado. The tornado began east southeast of Seminole at approximately 6:46 pm CST and moved northeast. It had caused power pole and irrigation equipment damage and was likely an EF-1 at 6:48 pm. At 6:50 pm, the tornado briefly reached EF-2 intensity as it caused damage to a well service rig. The last visible damage was to an area of tre

title: Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, High Wind: California, Dec 09, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, High Wind, from December 09, 2015 to December 11, 2015. Affected areas: Mt Shasta/Western Plumas County, Northern Sacramento Valley, Shasta, West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A cold storm from the Gulf of Alaska merged with subtropical moisture to bring heavy snow to the mountains and gusty winds. There were snowfall amounts of 1 to 2 feet above 6000 ft, with measurable snow down to as low as 3200 feet. This caused travel delays and accidents on mountain roads. Details: Heavy snow fell over the southern Cascades and into the mountains of western Plumas County, with over a foot of snow above 7000 feet. Snow caused travel difficulties on mountain roads. Lassen Volcanic National Park and Hwy 89 were closed on December 10th. There was 1.13 inches of rain over 24 hours, ending at 6 am. There was 2.24 inches of rain over 24 hours, ending at 7 am. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000.

title: Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow: California, Dec 03, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, from December 03, 2015 to December 04, 2015. Affected areas: Plumas, West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A winter storm brought snow to the mountains, and when combined with gusty winds brought poor visibility at times. There were snowfall amounts up to 15 inches above 7000 ft, causing travel delays on mountain roads. There was minor tree limb damage from winds and some locally heavy rain. Details: There were snowfall amounts of 12 to 15 inches above 6000 ft, with 6-12 inches above 5000 feet. Snow caused disruption to travel over trans-Sierra highways, including spin-outs, car accidents, jackknifed big rigs, and travel delays, reported by Caltrans. There were 1.5 inches of heavy rain in Quincy. Gusty winds damaged small limbs. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Dec 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from December 12, 2015 to December 12, 2015. Affected areas: Montgomery. Episode summary: Low-topped showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a strong storm system. Activity moved northward across the area, and multiple cells began to rotate. One of the storms produced an EF-2 tornado that damaged an area in Willis (Montgomery County). Details: This tornado touched down near Calvary Road around Robertson Park where tree trunks were snapped. Damage became more continuous just to the north near Pollard Road on the west side of Interstate 45 where large strands of pine trees were snapped. The tornado appeared to cross Interstate 45 near Exit 97 where it hit a large metal industrial building. Damage to this structure warranted the EF-2 ratin

title: Coastal Flood, Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 31, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Coastal Flood, Flash Flood, from October 31, 2015 to October 31, 2015. Affected areas: Fort Bend, Galveston, Harris, Liberty. Episode summary: A strong upper level storm system, combined with high moisture levels to produce a bands of excessive rainfall that caused flash flooding across Fort Bend, Harris and Liberty Counties. Thunderstorms rapidly developed shortly after midnight on the 31st over Matagorda and Fort Bend Counties and moved into Harris County around 1:00 a.m. The thunderstorms trained or moved over the same areas between 1:00 a.m. and 4:00 a.m. with significant rainfall occurring over the southwest and south-central portions of Harris County into the east-central part of the county. After a brief break between 5:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m. an additional round of thunderstorms slowly moved across Harris County from west to east producing additional heavy rainfall and worsening ongoing flooding conditions. Saturated grounds from previous heavy rainfall the week before coupled with intense short term rainfall rates resulted in widespread flooding. There was one confirmed flood related death and one possible flood related death. Details: High rainfall rates created flooding in both towns of Dayton and Liberty. The underpass at the intersection of US Highway 90 and FM 321, along with other streets in Dayton, were closed due to high water. The city of Liberty reported flood waters in six homes with numerous road closures due to high water. There was widespread flooding across the city of Houston and surrounding areas. The worst flooding occurred across eastern and southern Houston and towns north and east of the city. Numerous roadways were flooded including all main lanes of Highway 288 north of Brays Bayou. High rainfall rates caused Brays Bayou to go out of banks and inundate the Lawndale Wayside part of eastern Houston. Four

High rainfall rates caused Brays Bayou to go out of banks and inundate the Lawndale Wayside part of eastern Houston. Four to There were flood waters in homes in the Mayfair Park area with flooding occurring on Maywood Street and Arthington Avenue. The roadway was closed at Highway 99 and West Bellfort Street in Pecan Grove due to high water. The southbound lanes of the Fort Bend Parkway were closed due to high water east of Lake Olympia. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,715,000.

title: Coastal Flood, Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Oct 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Coastal Flood, Flash Flood, Tornado, from October 24, 2015 to October 25, 2015. Affected areas: Brazoria, Brazos, Burleson, Harris, Matagorda, Washington. Episode summary: The remnants of Hurricane Patricia merged with a developing frontal low to produce an intense surface low off the Texas Gulf Coast. As this low moved up the upper Texas coast it produced moderate to heavy rainfall that broad flooding to some areas, an isolated tornado and waterspout, and minor coastal flooding due to elevated stormtides. Details: There was widespread flooding around the city of Houston. There were numerous reports of flooded and impassable roadways with submerged vehicles. Vehicles were submerged near Fondren Road and the Highway 59 southwest freeway as well as in the Galleria area. The Katy exit ramp to the north freeway was closed due to high water. Interstate 45 at North Shepherd had two feet of water flowing across all Sections of the Blue Water Highway from San Luis Pass to Freeport were closed due to high gulf water inundation. The tornado damaged the metal roof of a large business south of Beltway 8 west of Cullen Blvd. The damage path extended north of Beltway 8 into the Brunswick Place subdivision. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, High Wind: California, Dec 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, High Wind, from December 12, 2015 to December 13, 2015. Affected areas: El Dorado, Mt Shasta/Western Plumas County, Northern Sacramento Valley, West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A cold storm from the Gulf of Alaska merged with subtropical moisture to bring gusty winds, local road flooding, and heavy snow to the mountains. There were snowfall amounts of 1 to 2 feet above 6000 ft, with measurable snow down to as low as 3400 feet. This caused significant travel delays and accidents on mountain roads. Winds knocked down trees and tree branches causing power outages in the Valley and foothills. Details: Heavy snow fell impacting Lassen Volcanic National Park and the surrounding area into western Plumas County. There were 14 inches of new snow at measured at Manzanita Lake over the weekend. Lighter amounts were measured further east, with 2 inches at Portola and 1 inch at Chester. Heavy snow fell impacting the northern Sierra, especially the I80 and Highway 50 corridors. Numerous accidents occurred, and 30 minute hold caused long backups over I80. There were 24 inches of new snow at ski resort peaks, 19 inches at Donner Summit, and 11 inches measured at Kingvale, 7 inches at Blue Canyon, 2.5 inches at Kyburz. Accumulating snow fell down to around 3400 feet, with 1 inch at P There was 1.17 inches of rain measured between 7 am and 4 pm.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Oct 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from October 22, 2015 to October 22, 2015. Affected areas: Fisher, Jones, Nolan, Sterling, Taylor. Episode summary: A slow moving cold front and a deep upper trough resulted in isolated severe thunderstorm reports. However, these systems interacted with plenty of moisture and resulted in very heavy rain and several reports of flash flooding across portions of West Central Texas. Very heavy rainfall in the Concho River watershed resulted in river flooding near Sterling City. Details: Two inches of heavy rain fell in 30 minutes across Sweetwater. This heavy rain resulted in street flooding with water over the curbs and traffic nearly at stand still. The intersection of Rebecca Lane and Catclaw Drive was flooded. There was one vehicle stalled at the intersection. Texas State Highway 163 just north of Sterling City was closed due to high water.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Oct 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from October 06, 2015 to October 07, 2015. Affected areas: Schleicher. Episode summary: The Mertz wildfire burned many acres in extreme Western Schleicher County. A long period of dry hot weather and abundant fuels created the ideal conditions for this wildfire. Details: The Mertz Wildfire burned an estimated 2250 acres about 13 miles east of Midway or in extreme western Schleicher County just north of U.S. Highway 190.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Oct 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from October 14, 2015 to October 19, 2015. Affected areas: Brown, Crockett, Menard. Episode summary: A long period of dry hot weather and abundant fuels created the conditions for three large wildfires. Details: The Preston Ranch Wildfire burned around 860 acres in far western Menard County near FM 1674 or about 4 miles south of Fort McKavett. The Whitley Wildfire burned an estimated 750 acres approximately 5 miles southwest of Brownwood. The fire began along County Road 201 and spread to FM 1176 and County Road 190. Twelve structures were threatened. The fire resulted in the closure of FM 1176 and the evacuations of several homes. The Rim Rock Ranch Wildfire burned approximately 350 acres on the Rim Rock Ranch in southern Crockett County 25 miles south-southwest of Ozona. The fire was located east of FM 2083 just off of Clegg Road.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Dec 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from December 13, 2015 to December 14, 2015. Affected areas: Morongo Basin, Western Mojave Desert. Episode summary: A series of fast-moving cold fronts brought intermittent strong winds to the Mojave Desert for several days. Minor damage occurred. Details: Strong winds blew down a ten-foot tree in Twentynine Palms. This gust occurred at Bicycle Lake on Fort Irwin. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Coastal Flood: California, Oct 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Coastal Flood, from October 27, 2015 to October 28, 2015. Affected areas: Orange County Coastal, San Diego County Coastal Areas. Episode summary: High astronomical tides near 7.2 feet on the 27th and 28th of October brought minor flooding to vulnerable areas along the immediate coast. Details: Minor street flooding was reported along Strand Way in Coronado. Several low lying roads in south Mission Beach were inundated by minor tidal overflow. Minor sandbagging was required to keep water out of some structures. Minor coastal flooding occurred at the end of Avenida de la Playa Street at the boat launch ramp in La Jolla Shores. Small waves were breaking against the windows of the Marine Room Restaurant.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 21, 2015 to October 21, 2015. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: Strong southerly flow developed ahead of an upper low moving through Southern Arizona. Plenty of moisture was brought into the region with sufficient wind shear and instability to combine with several upper level disturbances. Flash flooding and damaging hail were reported in and around El Paso. Details: Flooding reported along Resler between Loop 375 and Redd Road. Flooding around US 54 and Montana in Central El Paso. Flooding occurred near Hawkins and Viscount.

title: High Wind: California, Oct 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from October 30, 2015 to October 30, 2015. Affected areas: Santa Ana Mountains And Foothills. Episode summary: Surface high pressure over the great basin forced Santa Ana Winds, with the strongest winds occurring in the Santa Ana Mountains. Details: The Santiago Peak mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 71 mph between 530PST and 600PST with sustained winds near or above 50 mph between 400PST and 730PST.

title: Tornado: California, Oct 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Tornado, from October 17, 2015 to October 17, 2015. Affected areas: Riverside. Episode summary: From the 12th to the 20th of October, an upper low traversed the southwest in a large loop, passing over Southern California twice. This period saw scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms. The majority of activity stayed below severe limits, but a brief landspout was reported near Menifee on the 17th. Details: Numerous reports through the broadcast media and social media of a brief landspout near Menifee. The funnel was nearly stationary and occurred over open terrain, with no damage reported.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 24, 2015 to October 24, 2015. Affected areas: Bastrop, Bexar, Blanco, Burnet, De Witt, Edwards, Real, Travis, Williamson. Episode summary: An upper level trough combined with a cold front and deep moisture produced heavy rainfall across much of South Central Texas on October 24th and 25th. The heaviest rainfall amounts were generally along and east of the I-35 corridor, where 4 to 6 inch amounts were common. Some of the highest recorded totals were 14.45 near Fayetteville (Fayette county), 11.81 near Anderson Mill (Travis county) and 11.08 near La Grange (Fayette county). Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing Director Dr. at Creekview Dr. near Salado Creek in San Antonio. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing Toutant Beauregard Rd. in Leon Springs. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing Trainer Wuest Rd. at RR 1623, Crab Apple at RR 1888, and RR 165 at the bridge in Blanco all near the Blanco River.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Oct 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from October 30, 2015 to October 31, 2015. Affected areas: Bastrop, Bexar, Caldwell, Comal, Guadalupe, Hays, Lee, Medina, Travis, Wilson. Episode summary: A warm front combined with an upper level trough and deep moisture produced heavy rainfall and severe thunderstorms across much of South Central Texas on October 30th and 31st. Damage surveys confirmed four tornadoes. Along with the severe weather, excessive rainfall resulted in widespread flash flooding along the Interstate 35 corridor Friday morning. Rainfall rates on the order of 5-7 inches per hour fell from San Marcos up through South Austin. Historic rainfall totals fell at the Austin Airport where over 1 foot of rain fell within a few hours time. 12.49 inches of rain for Oct 30 was the most ever in one day for Austin. Other daily rainfall totals exceeded 15 inches. Record flooding occurred in southern Travis County and portions of Hays County. River and creek flooding was extensive across Hays, Travis, Bastrop, Caldwell, and Comal Counties. Many areas, especially in San Marcos, compared this flooding to the record flooding of Oct 1998. Estimates of 2000 homes were flooded in or near this I-35 corridor, many of them destroyed or sustained Major damage. Estimates of insured losses were not available as of this writing, but the counties experienced monetary losses in the tens of millions. Details: A tornado developed near Centerpoint Rd. and Old Zorn Rd. in Guadalupe County and continued to the north-northeast for approximately 2.25 miles into Hays County ending near Centerpoint Rd. and Viewpoint Rd. . The tornado caused minor roof damage to a few homes where it first developed. As it continued north-northeastward, the tornado struck a series of electrical transmission line towers, causing Additional rains in the predawn hours caused additional flooding across Caldwell County and surrounding counties. Many roads were flooded and impassable. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing at least 10 streets around San Antonio. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,850,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Oct 31, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from October 31, 2015 to October 31, 2015. Affected areas: Hardin, Jasper, Newton, Orange. Episode summary: Deep moisture moved into Southeast Texas from the gulf ahead of an approaching shortwave and cold front. Heavy rain fell across portions of the area that had just received several inches less than a week before. The radar estimated a storm total of 10 to 20 inches over the week with some locations receiving almost one foot from this event alone. Details: As rainwater drained toward Pine Island Bayou and Black Creek flooding continued in south portions of Hardin County for a few days. Around 15 homes flooded in Pinewood Estates while Pine Island Bayou crested. Heavy rain moved into Jasper County early in the morning of the 31st. Flooding was reported along County Road 784 near Buna by 7 AM. Numerous roads were reported flooded through the rest of the morning in different sections of the county with some being impassable especially at low water crossings. A COCORAHS report from near Kirbyville reported 7 inches of rain during the morning. Heavy rain moved into Hardin County early during the morning of the 31st. Flooding of roadways with water at least 2 feet deep was reported in Silsbee by 6:15 AM. By 10:51 AM the Department of Highways reported that most roads in the county had water covering them and water rescues were ongoing by 11 AM according to the county police department near Silsbee and Kountze. title: Wildfire: Texas, Oct 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from October 13, 2015 to October 24, 2015. Affected areas: Bastrop. Episode summary: The Hidden Pines wildfire started on October 13 near Buescher State Park north of Smithville. The fire eventually consumed 4,582 acres before being contained on October 24. One hundred forty-three (143) homes were threatened and 64 were destroyed, two were damaged, and 77 were saved. One hundred thirty-seven (137) vehicles were threatened with 69 destroyed and 68 saved. Twenty-one (21) recreational vehicles (RVs) were threatened and five were destroyed and 16 were saved. Four hundred (400) homes were evacuated during the course of the fire. Details: The Hidden Pines wildfire started on October 13 near Buescher State Park north of Smithville. The fire eventually consumed 4,582 acres before being contained on October 24. One hundred forty-three (143) homes were threatened and 64 were destroyed, two were damaged, and 77 were saved. title: Flash Flood: California, Oct 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from October 18, 2015 to October 18, 2015. Affected areas: Mono. Episode summary: Thunderstorms with heavy rain over the White Mountains caused flash flooding over highway 6 and in the town of Chalfant. Details: Heavy rain upstream in the White Mountains caused flash flooding, both on highway 6 with mud and debris over the road (causing a closure), and in the town of Chalfant with 20 homes damaged from flood waters. Four or 5 of those homes (on Sacramento St) suffered major damage per a Cal OES report. The timing of the flash flood is estimated from between the time highway 6 was reported to have debris o Reported property and crop damage: about $300,000.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Oct 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from October 22, 2015 to October 23, 2015. Affected areas: Willacy. Episode summary: A plume of tropical moisture through the mid levels of the atmosphere combined with a weak upper level disturbance created a slow���moving intense thunderstorm that eased into Willacy County. While over Willacy, mainly along and east of Farm���to���Market Road (FM) 1420 and west of the Laguna Madre, the cell dumped more than three hours of torrential rain in and near the communities of San Perlita, Willamar, and Santa Monica. As the rain totals increased, the water piled up; FM 1420 was inundated by several inches to more than a foot of water (some flowing), and nearby farms turned into one big lake. In Raymondville, heavy rains estimated at 2 to 4 inches fell, with urban flooding that would later reach into a few businesses in town due to additional drainage. title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Oct 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from October 24, 2015 to October 26, 2015. Affected areas: Hidalgo. Episode summary: Bands of thunderstorms pushed across Hidalgo County as pieces of upper level energy linked up with the remaining moisture of Hurricane Patricia. These bands began dropped rainfall at a one to two inch rate per hour for hours across southeastern Hidalgo County. Nuisance flooding soon became a flash flood, with numerous water rescues from flooded neighborhoods. An estimated and measured ten to twelve plus inches of rain fell in the Weslaco/Progresso area. Details: After hours of rainfall the nuisance flooding became a flash flood. Several inches to at least a foot of water rose into homes in the Las Brisas subdivision on the east side of town, with three to five feet of water on neighborhood streets. At least three feet of water submerged vehicles along the frontage roads between the Westgate and Airport Road exits during the peak of the flash flooding. Add The estimated and measured ten to twelve plus inches of rain that fell in the Weslaco and Progresso area was far too much for drainage systems to handle, and even well after the rainfall stopped, numerous neighborhoods remained flooded and roads remained closed through the 26th. Please see flash flood event for damage estimates. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 30, 2015 to October 30, 2015. Affected areas: Cameron. Episode summary: An upper level trough slid across the southwestern U.S. and northern Mexico inducing an intensifying surface and low level low pressure trough and increasing southerly flow bringing deep tropical moisture to the area. Thunderstorms developed over northern Mexico and turned into a mesoscale convective system over Brownsville. Citywide four to seven inches of rain fell within a two to three hour window causing flash flooding across Brownsville. Many roads were inundated with two to three feet of water and dozens of homes and businesses were flooded. The rainfall was accompanied by excessive, nearly continuous cloud to ground lightning. Details: Heavy and persistent rain fell across the City of Brownsville, mainly from downtown east towards the Port of Brownsville, and including all of the neighborhoods in Southmost, which took the brunt of the heavy rainfall. Four to seven inches of rain fell, with highest totals in the more densely populated sections of town where poor drainage is more of an issue as well. The heaviest rainfall, four to Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Oct 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from October 30, 2015 to October 30, 2015. Affected areas: Willacy. Episode summary: A wave of upper level energy, arriving well ahead of a vigorous trough of surface and high level low pressure, acted on a very unstable airmass that was also conducive to producing rotating thunderstorms during the pre���dawn hours of October 30th to produce a mini���supercell thunderstorm in northern Cameron County, which raced northward through Willacy and into Kenedy County. The lack of material in the metal container allowed winds to get underneath and lift; pressures on the minimally anchored columns caused the damage. Other damage included a portion of roof peeled back from a mobile Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: Strong Wind: California, Dec 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, from December 13, 2015 to December 13, 2015. Affected areas: Northern Monterey Bay, San Francisco Bay Shoreline. Episode summary: On Sunday, December 13, a cold front swept across the San Francisco Bay Area and Santa Cruz County. Strong winds were observed in the San Francisco Bay Area and Santa Cruz county as the cold front swept through during the late morning hours. Several large trees were blown down, some onto homes and automobiles. Details: A large eucalyptus tree was blown down in the city of San Pablo, damaging a home and a car. A tree was blown over onto three vehicles in front of the Woodland Park Apartments in East Palo Alto. A tree was blown over onto a van in Hayward, CA. Reported property and crop damage: about $18,000.

title: Heavy Rain: California, Oct 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, from October 17, 2015 to October 18, 2015. Affected areas: El Dorado, Tehama. Episode summary: Locally heavy rain from thunderstorms brought low debris and local mudslides to the Butte Fire burn area. Ponding of water on roadways and reduced visibility from heavy rain caused travel difficulties on mountain and foothill roads such as Highways 4, 88 and 50. Details: Rainfall measurement of 1.16 inches from 700 am PST until 4 pm. Locally heavy rain, with 2.85 inches measured for the 24 hour total. Locally heavy rain from a thunderstorm, with 1.25 inches measured in about 30 minutes.

title: High Wind: California, Oct 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from October 30, 2015 to October 30, 2015. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area. Episode summary: Strong north to south pressure gradients generate gusty northerly winds across the mountains of Los Angeles county. Sustained winds over 40 MPH and gusts over 60 MPH were reported. Details: The RAWS sensor at Malibu Hills reported sustained north winds of 43 MPH. The RAWS sensor at Camp Nine reported northerly wind gusts of 63 MPH.

title: High Wind: California, Nov 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from November 15, 2015 to November 15, 2015. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Clarita Valley, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: Strong north-south pressure gradients generated strong and gusty north winds across the mountains of Ventura and Los Angeles counties as well as the Santa Clarita Valley. Wind gusts between 61 and 71 MPH were reported. Details: The sensor at Rose Valley measured a northerly wind gust of 64 MPH. Strong northerly wind developed in the mountains of Los Angeles county. The RAWS sensor at Warm Springs reported a northerly wind gust of 73 MPH while gusts of 61 MPH were reported at Camp Nine and gusts of 66 MPH were reported at Oat Mountain. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from December 23, 2015 to December 23, 2015. Affected areas: Barron, Polk. Episode summary: A strong winter storm, but with mild temperatures, moved across the Upper Midwest during the day of Wednesday, December 23rd. Bands of mainly light snow developed early Wednesday morning, intensified during the afternoon, before tapering off Wednesday evening. Some light rain and drizzle also occurred as warmer air wrapped into this system during the day. This warmer air limited snowfall amounts in west central Wisconsin where most areas only received between 2 and 4 inches of snow. The heaviest snow fell in far northern Wisconsin where locally 6 to 10 inches fell. High water of 1 to 3 feet covered many streets and surrounded more than a dozen buildings, especially in the San Perlita area. title: Wildfire: Texas, Oct 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from October 14, 2015 to October 23, 2015. Affected areas: Anderson, Ellis, Stephens. Episode summary: Dry weather in the middle part of the month of October allowed for conditions to be ripe for wildfires to begin. Several fires occurred in the western half of north Texas. Details: The Fuller Fire burned an estimated 1,000 acres across Stephens County. The fire was concentrated along Stephens County roads 324 and 325. A few residences were evacuation for precautionary measures, but the fire did not threaten any homes. The fire was extinguished by rainfall during the afternoon of October 23rd. Ellis County emergency management reported a grass fire which burned over 300 acres near Union Hill Road and Farm to Market Road 660. The fire destroyed one barn and two small buildings. There were two fires in Anderson County on the afternoon and evening of October 15th. The local newspaper published a report of a fire near Neches, off of Anderson County road 338, and another fire near Montabla ,near Anderson County road 471. The Neches fire burned an estimated 125 acres, while the Montalba fire burned approximately 50 acres. No homes or structures were burned in either fire. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

The wildfire was contained around 1900CST or so and a total of nine fire departments or other agencies responded to the wildfire.

There were no homes or other structures reported to be threatened or damaged and there were no reports of injuries or fatalities. The wildfire was contained by 0330CST or so on November 21 and twelve fire departments, including the Texas Forest Service, along with other fire agencies, responded to the wildfire.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Dec 20, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from December 20, 2015 to December 21, 2015. Affected areas: Hutchinson. Episode summary: The Sunday Evening wildfire began around 1912CST about four miles southeast of Pringle Texas in the central Texas Panhandle or just east of County Road 12 and State Highway 207 and was moving in a northeasterly direction. The wildfire consumed two thousand one hundred and ninety-seven acres and was caused by downed power lines. One home was threatened but saved and there were no reports of homes or any other structures being damaged or lost. There were also no reports of damage to any farm fencing or livestock. There was one report of an injury, however there were no reports of fatalities. Although the wildfire was contained around 0730CST on Monday December 21, the wildfire rekindled again by 1500CST on Monday December 21. The wildfire was finally contained by 1840CST on Monday December 21. A portion of the wildfire was located in the Canadian River breaks making it extremely difficult for firefighters and fire trucks to gain access to the wildfire because of the rugged terrain. A total of eleven fire departments and other fire agencies, including the Texas Forest Service, the National Park Service at Lake Meredith, and multiple personnel from area ranches, responded to the wildfire. The Texas Forest Service provided dozers and other heavy equipment to assist with wildfire operations.

While instability was very weak, the strong shear made up for the development of strong to severe thunderstorms, some of which produced tornadoes across Northeast Texas. Training of storm echoes also occurred which resulted in widespread flash flooding across the region as well. Details: A NWS Storm Survey team concluded that the damage in Franklin County, Texas west of Purley community was consistent with that of tornado damage. The EF-2 tornado first touched down near County Road 3250 and traveled in a northerly direction, crossing County Road 2376 before lifting after crossing County Road 3055. NWS forecasters were keen to alert residents that a second and more potent round of snow was to arrive later in the day once the upper low lifted northeast across central Texas. Although this second round was initially complicated by sleet at times thanks to a redeveloping warm nose, by late afternoon on the 27th the warm nose disappeared for good as several bands of heavy snow enveloped the South Plains before shifting into the Rolling Plains and the southeast Texas Panhandle overnight and slowly dissipating. Until that point, areas off the Caprock contended with as much as three inches of sleet and up to 1/2 inch of freezing rain. Several snowbursts with rates measured as high as 2.7 inches at the NWS Lubbock office produced whiteout conditions and compounded already treacherous travel conditions. The snow and strong winds quickly tapered off in coverage and intensity from southwest-to-northeast late on the 27th through the pre-dawn hours of the 28th.||Unfortunately, there were two fatalities from this blizzard. A homeless man in Lubbock succumbed to hypothermia late in the night on the 27th. He was found wearing only a light jacket, jeans and a thin blanket. No information was known on the second fatality.||Despite full sun and high temperatures reaching the middle 30s on the 28th, thousands of South Plains residents found themselves marooned by tall snow drifts that blocked roads and driveways.
