title: Strong Wind, Tornado: Texas, Nov 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, Tornado, from November 17, 2015 to November 17, 2015. Affected areas: Denton, Leon, Navarro, Tarrant. Episode summary: A cold front and approaching upper level storm system combined to produce nighttime thunderstorms across much of north Texas, including the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex. Daylight revealed several swaths of wind damage, including two tornadoes. Details: A National Weather Service storm survey team found evidence of a narrow, yet long tornado in the Hickory Creek and Corinth areas of Denton County. As the tornado began near the Steeplechase North subdivision, several homes suffered minor roof damage as well as garage door damage. A car wash suffered heavy damage to the east side of the business along the path. As the tornado began to dissipate, a A trained spotter reported a tree on a house near the intersection of Enfield and Dobbins in Corsicana, TX. A trained spotter reported multiple trees down and power poles down approximately 4 miles north of Normangee, TX. Reported property and crop damage: about $717,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado: Texas, Dec 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado, from December 26, 2015 to December 28, 2015. Affected areas: Anderson, Collin, Cooke, Dallas, Delta, Denton, Ellis, Fannin, Freestone, Grayson, Henderson, Hill and 9 more areas. Episode summary: A potent storm system brought deadly tornadoes and severe weather to North Texas on the 26th followed by waves of heavy rainfall that resulted in significant flooding across parts of North and Central Texas. Twelve tornadoes were confirmed on the afternoon and evening of the 26th, killing 13 and injuring over 300. The strongest tornado was an EF-4 that struck the Garland and Rowlett areas of Dallas and Rockwall County and where most of the fatalities occurred. Then the waves of heavy rain persisted through the night of the 27th until the upper level low moved past the region. The heaviest rainfall and thus most significant flooding was along and east of Interstate 35 where an average of 3-6+ of rain fell. Details: The Hubbard Volunteer Fire Department observed a tornado just north of the city of Hubbard. Trained spotters observed and photographed a brief tornado over open land to the northeast of Eustace. The Midlothian / Ovilla / Glenn Heights tornado began near Midlothian, before ending on the city border of DeSoto and Glenn Heights. In Dallas County, the tornado damaged approximately 35 homes, along with an additional 10 mobile homes. The strongest portion of the tornado occurred near the Ellis / Dallas County line, with EF3 damage observed in both counties. Reported property and crop damage: about $40,521,000.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 31, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from December 31, 2015 to December 31, 2015. Affected areas: Lubbock. Episode summary: By late afternoon on New Year's Eve, freezing drizzle overspread much of the South Plains and continued into the early morning hours of January 1st. Although very light snow was reported in some areas at times, hours of steady freezing drizzle (particularly in Lubbock) glazed over many roads and overpasses with ice. The treacherous road conditions that ensued caused many holiday revelers to celebrate at home. This dealt one final blow to several downtown Lubbock restaurants and clubs that had already been closed for six consecutive days due to snow-clogged streets following the Christmas weekend blizzard. The ice was so bad along the West Loop 289 flyover in Lubbock that TX-DOT closed this stretch of highway at 10 PM following multiple vehicle spinouts. Lubbock Police Dispatch responded to around 220 vehicle accidents related to icy roads this night, two of which were rollovers with minor injuries. The freezing drizzle ended in many areas near or just after midnight, but icy roads remained through midday on New Year's Day until temperatures rose above freezing. Reported property and crop damage: about $200,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Dec 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from December 27, 2015 to December 28, 2015. Affected areas: Angelina, Bowie, Camp, Cass, Franklin, Gregg, Harrison, Panola, Red River, Rusk, San Augustine, Smith and 3 more areas. Episode summary: A strong negatively tilted upper level trough slowly moved into the Central and Southern Plains during the morning of December 27th. This trough of low pressure was accompanied by a strong subtropical jet stream which provided abundant lift necessary for the development of widespread showers and thunderstorms. The trough was able to draw up not only Gulf of Mexico moisture but also Eastern Pacific moisture and with a very slow movement to the activity once it developed, the end result was widespread flooding across a large portion of Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas and Northwest Louisiana. A very unstable airmass for late December was present across the region with a very strongly wind sheared environment. Discrete storms developed across the region ahead of an eventual line of strong to severe thunderstorms. Some of these discrete storms produced tornadoes across the region with several storms producing strong and damaging wind gusts as well. For the month of December, 2015, the city of Tyler, Texas recorded 9.77 inches of rain which was their 3rd wettest December on record. At the conclusion of December, the city of Tyler, Texas also recorded their all time wettest year on record with a total of 68.05 inches for the year. For the city of Longview, Texas ,the city recorded their 5th wettest year on record with a total of 68.02 inches. Details: County Roads 2217 and 2219 were flooded and closed. Several county roads were flooded and closed including 419, 420, 436, 434, 433, 168, 411, 494 and 492. Several vehicles were flooded out across these

title: Ice Storm: Texas, Dec 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, from December 27, 2015 to December 28, 2015. Affected areas: Hardeman. The 27th saw precipitation transition to sleet and freezing rain. Combined with high winds, this caused extensive damage to trees and power lines. By the 28th, all of the precipitation had turned to snow. Details: Media reported 0.25 inches of ice accumulation.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Nov 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from November 07, 2015 to November 07, 2015. Affected areas: Leon. Episode summary: A slow-moving front lingered just southeast of our County Warning Area, leading to the additional development of showers and thunderstorms over our southeastern counties as an upper level disturbance moved overhead. Training thunderstorms led to localized flash flooding across Leon County. Details: Leon County Sheriff's Department reported that FM 3 approximately half a mile north of Hilltop Lakes was impassable due to flood waters. Leon County Sheriff's Department reported that the service road along Interstate 45 just north of TX-OSR was impassable. Leon County Sheriff's Department reported water over FM 1119 approximately 3 miles south of Centerville, TX. One eastbound lane of Highway 7 just east of FM 1119 was closed due to high water.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Dec 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from December 26, 2015 to December 27, 2015. Affected areas: Hutchinson. Episode summary: The Christmas After wildfire began around 1430CST about three miles northeast of Stinnett, Texas in central Hutchinson county east of County Road 11 and north of Farm to Market Road 1526. The wildfire consumed an estimated three hundred acres and was caused by downed power lines. There were no reports of homes or any other structures being threatened and no homes or other structures were damaged or lost. There were also no reports of injuries or fatalities. The wildfire was contained around 0130CST to 0200CST on Sunday December 27. A total of nine fire departments and other fire agencies responded to the wildfire including the Texas Forest Service.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Nov 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from November 26, 2015 to November 30, 2015. Affected areas: Collin, Dallas, Denton, Ellis, Fannin, Grayson, Hopkins, Hunt, Johnson, Kaufman, Lamar, Parker and 1 more areas. Episode summary: An Arctic cold front pushed south through north Texas Thanksgiving night through the following morning. Showers and thunderstorms accompanied the front, then continued through the weekend as a strong overrunning pattern remained in place after the front moved through the area. Flash flooding not only created travel problems, but took the lives of 4 people that holiday weekend. Details: Emergency management reported flooding due to a levee breach along the Trinity River south of highway 34. Several high water crossings remained closed and barricaded per the Dallas Alert Gage Network after several inches of rain fell in the county. A social media report indicated that the intersections of Brand/Campbell roads and Pleasant Valley/Miles Roads were closed due to high water. Multiple news media sources reported that a 29 year old man drowned when his car was overcome by floodwaters after Multiple road closures were required in the county, mostly due to flooding along and near the Sulphur River. A few of those closings included FM 71 and FM 1571 at the Sulphur River. The sheriff's department reported additional high water problems on FM 900 between Saltillo and FM 69. Reported property and crop damage: about $305,000.

title: Winter Weather: California, Nov 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from November 01, 2015 to November 02, 2015. Affected areas: West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A cool early season storm brought wintry weather which impacted travel over Sierra mountain passes. This system also brought rain across the area at lower elevations, locally heavy with thunderstorms. Thunderstorms also caused local damage to power poles from a microburst in Butte County, as well as numerous reports of small hail. Details: There were 4 to 5 inches of snow measured at Donner Pass (Castle Peak area). This caused traffic slowdowns and chain restrictions at elevations above 6000 feet.

title: Heavy Rain: California, Nov 08, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, from November 08, 2015 to November 10, 2015. Affected areas: Butte, El Dorado. Episode summary: A cold storm from the Gulf of Alaska brought the first significant snow to the mountains and down into the upper foothills. There were snowfall amounts up to a foot above 6000 ft, with measurable snow down to as low as 2700 feet. This caused travel delays and accidents on mountain roads. Details: There was a 24 hour total of 1.30 inches of rain, snowfall 0.7 inches at Pacific House. There was a 24 hour total of 1.75 inches of rain. Observer location Oroville.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Dec 28, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from December 28, 2015 to December 29, 2015. Affected areas: Adams, Buffalo, Clark, Crawford, Grant, Jackson, Juneau, La Crosse, Monroe, Richland, Trempealeau, Vernon. Episode summary: A winter storm hit western Wisconsin on December 28th and 29th with heavy snow, sleet and strong winds. As the storm lifted north out of the Southern Plains states, snow moved into western Wisconsin during the late morning of the 28th. For parts of southwest Wisconsin, this snow was mixed with or completely changed over to sleet during the afternoon and early evening of the 28th. The heaviest snow fell during the late afternoon and early evening of the 28th with 1 to 2 inch per hour rates. This caused a rapid deterioration in road conditions causing travel conditions to quickly become dangerous. By the time the snow ended on the 29th, totals across western Wisconsin ranged from 5 to 11 inches. The highest reported total was 11.5 inches near Black River Falls (Jackson County) and Warrens (Monroe County). Blowing and drifting of the snow occurred as winds gusted into the 25 to 40 mph range. title: High Wind: California, Dec 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 21, 2015 to December 22, 2015. Affected areas: Owens Valley, Western Mojave Desert. Episode summary: A Pacific trough and associated strong jet stream brought high winds to the Owens Valley and western Mojave Desert. Details: The Bicycle Lake (KBYS) ASOS on Fort Irwin measured high winds for an hour, with the peak gust occurring at 1841 PST. The Barstow-Daggett (KDAG) ASOS measured high winds for 35 minutes, with the peak gust occurring at 0817 PST. The high winds were measured at a mesonet site 4 miles NW of Independence. Law enforcement reported that a tree was blown down onto telephone lines nearby. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Coastal Flood, Flood, Tornado: California, Jan 06, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Coastal Flood, Flood, Tornado, from January 06, 2016 to January 06, 2016. Affected areas: Alameda, Monterey, North Bay Interior Valleys, San Benito, San Francisco, Santa Cruz, Sonoma. Episode summary: A strong Pacific storm swept through the San Francisco Bay Area and Monterey Bay Area on Wednesday, January 6. This storm produced heavy rain, minor flooding, damaging winds, a funnel cloud, and one confirmed tornado. Details: Roadway flooded on Pleasant Hill Road at Mitchell Court. Roadway was completely flooded. CHP reported that I-80 East at El Portal Drive was flooded. The HOV lane was flooded and water was flowing across all lanes. Southbound 101 between SR 1 and Marin City closed due to coastal flooding. Reported property and crop damage: about $75,000.

title: Flood: California, Nov 03, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from November 03, 2015 to November 04, 2015. Affected areas: San Diego. Episode summary: A deep trough developed just off the West Coast on the 2nd and swung through California on the 3rd and 4th, bringing cold, unstable air to southern California with thunderstorms and record rainfall for San Diego. Lindbergh Field recorded a one-day total of 1.09 inches on the 3rd, setting a daily rainfall record. Elsewhere, amounts varied widely with coast and valley locations recording 2-day totals of one-tenth to almost an inch and a half (highest amounts in southern San Diego County). The heavy rain resulted in urban flooding in Spring Valley and Lemon Grove with water up to the doors of some vehicles and several roads closed. Orange County and the Inland Empire received around one-tenth of an inch to one-half of an inch of rain with no flooding. Thunderstorms resulted in several reports of hail one-quarter inch in diameter near Dana Point and in southern San Diego County, but no damage. Strong, gusty west winds also accompanied this event on the 2nd with several gusts in the mountains and desert slopes around 60-65 mph. No wind damage was reported. Details: News media reports flooding near Federal Blvd. and San Miguel Ave in Lemon Grove, with debris also covering the road. Two blocks were impassable with water up to the doors of vehicles on College Ave. off of State Route 94. Pacific Highway was closed from Juniper to Laurel Streets due to flooding. San Diego County officials reported that Quarry Dip Road was closed between Lakeview Road and State R

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Nov 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from November 16, 2015 to November 16, 2015. Affected areas: Orange County Coastal, San Diego County Coastal Areas. Episode summary: An upper-level trough developed along the West Coast, deepening into a strong low over southern California on the 16th, bringing scattered light rain/snow showers. A couple thunderstorms produced one-quarter inch sized hail near Lake Arrowhead (accumulated to around a half-inch depth) and Running Springs in the San Bernardino mountains. Rainfall totals were mostly one-third of an inch or less, with up to one-half of an inch in the mountains, again, highest amounts in San Diego County. The snow level was around 5500 to 6000 feet, with enough moisture to produce around 4 inches of snow in the Big Bear area, with a rain/melted snow total of 1.5 inches. No flooding reported. This system did produce strong and gusty westerly winds with several trees down in San Diego County and power poles down in Orange County, resulting in power outages for several thousand customers. The strong winds brought a large swell and high surf to the Orange and San Diego County coasts as well. The coastal waters experienced low-end gale force winds during this event, with the San Clemente Basin buoy reporting winds gusting from 35 to 41 kt between 1050 pm on the 15th through 950 am on the 16th, and wave heights peaking at 18 feet. title: Ice Storm: Texas, Nov 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, from November 26, 2015 to November 28, 2015. Affected areas: Armstrong, Carson, Collingsworth, Dallam, Deaf Smith, Donley, Gray, Hansford, Hartley, Hemphill, Hutchinson, Lipscomb and 8 more areas. Episode summary: A cold front moved through the Texas Panhandle on the night of the 25th resulting in a layer of shallow cold air across the area on the 26th. A strong storm system approached from the west bringing moisture and relatively warm air atop the cold shallow layer. This is an optimal setup for freezing rain and sleet. Amounts ranged from around a quarter of an inch of ice in the northwest Texas Panhandle to as much as an inch in the eastern Texas Panhandle. Roads became slick causing hazardous travel conditions. Some power outages occurred, especially in the southeastern portion s of the Panhandle where ice amounts were greatest. Details: One quarter to one half inch of ice accumulation from freezing rain occurred in Amarillo. Some sleet was also reported. One half inch of ice accumulation from freezing rain and an additional one quarter inch of sleet accumulation was reported at 2:14 AM on the 28th in Pampa. One half to three quarters of an inch of ice from predominately freezing rain accumulated was reported in Texline. Similar amounts occurred throughout the county. Some sleet also occurred. One quarter to one half of an inch of ice accumulated from predominately freezing rain and some sleet in Stratford. Minimal snow occurred.

The peak gust was 85 mph recorded at 13/0420 PST. The Bolam RAWS recorded gusts exceeding 63 mph continously from 13/0104 PST until 13/0503 PST. The peak gust was 69 mph at 13/0403 PST. The Indian Well RAWS recorded a gust to 58 mph at 13/0401 PST.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 18, 2015 to December 18, 2015. Affected areas: North Central & Southeast Siskiyou County. Episode summary: Another in a series of storms brought high winds to portions of northern California. Details: The KNF98 RAWS recorded several gusts exceeding 57 mph during this interval. The peak gust was 63 mph recorded at 18/0320 PST and 18/0420 PST. The Bolam RAWS recorded a gust to 58 mph at 18/0403 PST.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 20, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 20, 2015 to December 21, 2015. Affected areas: North Central & Southeast Siskiyou County. Episode summary: Another in a series of storms brought high winds to isolate portions of northern California. Details: The KNF98 RAWS recorded gusts exceeding 58 mph almost continuously during this interval. The peak gust was 74 mph recorded at 21/0920 PST.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Nov 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from November 24, 2015 to November 24, 2015. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Lassen/Eastern Plumas/Eastern Sierra. Episode summary: Low pressure just west of the mouth of the Columbia River on the morning of the 24th moved into eastern California and northwest Nevada early on the 25th. This pushed a sharp cold front into northeast California with heavy snow on the 24th. Details: Four to 6 inches of heavy, wet snow (6-7 to 1 snow to liquid ratio) fell on the 24th south and west of Susanville, including the Sierra Valley and near Bieber. Eleven inches was reported just southeast of Lake Davis at 6000 feet. Heavy snowfall of 8 to 15 inches fell from the Truckee airport to along and west of highway 89 on the 24th, with the highest amount in the Tahoe-Donner area. Lesser amounts of 5 to 7 inches fell for most other locations. Areas from Homewood to Glenshire reported 4 inches of snowfall between 1000PST and 1400PST.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 21, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from January 21, 2016 to January 21, 2016. Affected areas: Harrison. Episode summary: In wake of the strong to severe thunderstorms that developed during the early morning through the afternoon on January 21st, colder air began to spill south into portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northern Louisiana during the evening and overnight hours. As the air column began to cool near the upper level disturbance as it approached the region from the west, areas of light rain began to change over to snow across portions of extreme Eastern Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana. Some light snow accumulations occurred across portions of Harrison County, Texas, as well as portions of Southwest Arkansas and extreme Northern Louisiana generally north of the Interstate 20 corridor. Snowfall amounts of around one inch fell in the city of Marshall, Texas from a quick burst of moderate snow. This resulted in some light snow accumulations on the roads and grassy surfaces, with the snow quickly melting soon afterwards as temperatures were above freezing.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Dec 28, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from December 28, 2015 to December 29, 2015. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green, Green Lake, Iowa, Jefferson, Kenosha, Lafayette, Marquette, Milwaukee and 8 more areas. Episode summary: A winter storm affected Southern WI as strong low pressure tracked from the Lower Mississippi River Valley to Northeast IL and Lower MI. Most areas saw 5 to 10 inches of wet snow and sleet combined, with sleet accumulations up to two inches in some areas. East to northeast wind gusts of 30 to 45 mph occurred with visibility restrictions of 1/4 to 1/2 mile. There were more than 300 accidents on interstate and state highways mainly in the Milwaukee and Madison areas. Two men collapsed and died while shoveling the afternoon of Dec. 29th in Milwaukee County. A Golf Dome was damaged by the weight of the heavy snow in Milwaukee County. Details: Wet snow and sleet accumulation of 5 to 10 inches. East to northeast wind gusts up to 45 mph. Visibility reduced to 1/4 to 1/2 mile at times. Wet snow and sleet accumulation of 5 to 9 inches. East to northeast wind gusts up to 40 mph. Visibility reduced to 1/4 to 1/2 mile at times. Wet snow and sleet accumulation of 6 to 11 inches. East to northeast wind gusts up to 45 mph. Visibility reduced to 1/4 to 1/2 mile at times. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jan 29, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 29, 2016 to January 30, 2016. Affected areas: Dickens. Episode summary: Very windy, dry, and unseasonably warm conditions helped fuel the spread of a wildfire this afternoon about five miles north-northwest of Dickens (Dickens County). Volunteer fire crews from Dickens, McAdoo, and Spur helped combat the fire through the early overnight hours of the 30th and prevented it from jumping US Highway 70. This fire consumed around 150 acres of open ranch land including one power pole and a section of utility line. The subsequent power outage affected all residents of Spur, McAdoo, and Dickens for about two hours. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,500.

title: High Wind: Texas, Feb 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from February 01, 2016 to February 01, 2016. Affected areas: Garza. Episode summary: A powerful storm system moved out of the southern Rockies into the Plains during the evening of the first. Strong winds aloft spread over the region resulting in robust surface winds. One severe wind gust of 64 mph was recorded at 1716 CST at Lake Alan Henry (Garza County) by the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet.

title: Lake-Effect Snow: Wisconsin, Jan 27, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Lake-Effect Snow, from January 27, 2016 to January 28, 2016. Affected areas: Iron. Episode summary: Light snow across northwest Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening of January 27th transitioned to lake effect snow overnight into the morning of January 28th. A couple locations in northern Iron County reported more than 8 of snow within 24 hours, including 9.3 in Gile, WI and 10 in Hurley, WI. Ironwood, MI, which is just across the border from Iron County, reported about 11.5.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Feb 02, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from February 02, 2016 to February 03, 2016. Affected areas: Ashland, Bayfield, Burnett, Iron, Price, Sawyer, Washburn. Episode summary: An area of low pressure moved across Iowa and southern Wisconsin. After the low moved east of the area the snow transitioned to lake effect snow. ||There was a band of about 6 to 10 inches of the low-induced snow that fell from the Twin Cities to the Rice Lake, Hayward, and Hurley areas. Additional lake enhancement and post-storm lake effect snow showers resulted in total snowfall in excess of one foot across northern Iron County. Specific snowfall totals across northwest Wisconsin included 16.6 in Gile and 11.0 near Saxon (both in Iron County), 12.0 near Butternut and 8.7 in Ashland (both in Ashland County), 10.0 several miles south of Butternut and 8.0 in Park Falls (both in Price County), 9.0 near Sarona and 8.0 in Springbrook (both in Washburn County), 8.0 in Stone Lake (Sawyer County), and 7.0 in Siren (Burnett County).

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jan 19, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 19, 2016 to January 19, 2016. Affected areas: Randall. Episode summary: The Dowlen Road wildfire began around 1202CST around ten miles south southwest of Canyon Texas in Randall county just east of the intersection of Dowlen Road and Farm to Market Road 1705. The wildfire consumed approximately two hundred and forty acres and the cause of the wildfire was determined to be from the use of welding equipment. There were no reports of homes or other structures damaged or destroyed and there were no reports of injuries or fatalities. A total of four fire departments and other fire agencies, including the Texas A&M Forest Service and the Randall County Fire Department, responded to the wildfire. The wildfire was contained between 1600CST and 1630CST.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jan 20, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 20, 2016 to January 20, 2016. Affected areas: Randall. Episode summary: The Wayside Road wildfire began about eight miles west of Wayside Texas in Randall county around 1501CST just east of Parsley Road between Farm to Market Road 285 and County Road 418. The wildfire consumed approximately two hundred and ninety-six acres and the cause of the wildfire was determined to be from downed power lines. Although no homes were threatened, damaged or destroyed, three out buildings were reported lost. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities from the wildfire. The wildfire was contained between 1900CST and 1930CST and there were a total of five fire departments and other fire agencies that responded to the wildfire, including the Texas A&M Forest Service and the Randall County Fire Department. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jan 30, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 30, 2016 to January 31, 2016. Affected areas: Potter. Episode summary: The River Wildfire began about fourteen miles east of Valley de Oro around 1440CST near U.S. Highway 287 and the Canadian River and burned on both sides of the highway. The wildfire did shut down the highway north of Amarillo due to poor visibility in smoke. Although the wildfire threatened two homes, no homes or other structures were reported to be damaged or lost. There were also no reports of injuries or fatalities. The wildfire consumed an estimated one thousand seven hundred and fifty acres and was fully contained by 1958CST on Sunday January 31. Several fire departments and other fire agencies responded to the wildfire, including the Texas A&M Forest Service.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jan 30, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 30, 2016 to January 30, 2016. Affected areas: Carson. Episode summary: The Grass Fire 2016-5 wildfire began around 1615CST about four miles north northwest of Kingsmill in Carson county. There were no reports of homes or other structures damaged or destroyed and there were also no reports of injuries or fatalities. The wildfire consumed an estimated four hundred and thirty acres and was caused by downed power lines. The wildfire was contained around 2100CST and a total of five fire departments and other fire agencies responded to the wildfire.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jan 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from January 01, 2016 to January 01, 2016. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: High northeast gap winds occurred through Guadalupe Pass behind a strong cold front. Details: Several hours of sustained northeast winds of 40-47 mph occurred in Guadalupe Pass behind a strong cold front.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jan 06, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from January 06, 2016 to January 07, 2016. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: An upper trough translated eastward over the region and resulted in high winds in the Guadalupe Mountains. Details: Sustained west winds of 40 mph or greater occurred in Guadalupe Pass for three hours.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jan 15, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from January 15, 2016 to January 16, 2016. Affected areas: Davis / Apache Mountains Area, Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: The passage of an upper level trough resulted in high winds in the Guadalupe and Davis Mountains. Details: West winds of 60 mph occurred at the McDonald Observatory. Sustained west winds of 40-45 mph occurred through Guadalupe Pass.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jan 24, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from January 24, 2016 to January 25, 2016. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: Strong west to northwest winds occurred over the Guadalupe and Davis Mountains in the wake of an upper trough which moved over the region.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jan 30, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from January 30, 2016 to January 31, 2016. Affected areas: Davis / Apache Mountains Area, Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: The base of a strong upper trough translated eastward over the region, and resulted in strong surface winds affecting much of the area. Details: The RAWS site at Guadalupe Peak registered very strong west winds, the highest of which was 92 mph. A measured gust of 70 mph was recorded at McDonald Observatory.

title: Heavy Snow: Texas, Jan 26, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, from January 26, 2016 to January 26, 2016. Affected areas: Pecos. Episode summary: An upper level trough translated southeastward over west Texas and resulted in heavy snowfall over the Stockton Plateau. Details: Snowfall of 4-5 inches reported in Fort Stockton, but 6-8 inches of snowfall reported 2 miles south of Fort Stockton. Interstate 10 had only one lane open due to heavy snowfall and the power company in Fort Stockton reported up to 2,000 people were without power.

title: Extreme Cold/Wind Chill: California, Jan 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Extreme Cold/Wind Chill, from January 01, 2016 to January 01, 2016. Affected areas: Modoc County. Episode summary: Very cold temperatures combined with moderate winds to create very low wind chill temperatures over parts of northeast California. Details: The Juniper Creek RAWS recorded wind chill temperatures ranging from -16F to -24F during this interval.

title: Ice Storm: California, Jan 05, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Ice Storm, from January 05, 2016 to January 06, 2016. Affected areas: South Central Siskiyou County. Episode summary: Snow, ice, and freezing rain fell across northern California on these days. Details: A spotter in Mount Shasta City reported ice accumulations of 0.5 inches in freezing rain. He stated the the back roads and sidewalks in northern Mount Shasta City were an ice rink.

title: High Wind, Winter Storm, Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, Winter Storm, Winter Weather, from December 26, 2015 to December 28, 2015. Affected areas: Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mcculloch, Menard and 6 more areas. Episode summary: A powerful upper level storm system brought heavy snow and strong winds to portions of West Central Texas. The snow fell over a large part of the area. Snowfall amounts ranged from a tenth of an inch of snow to almost 5 inches in Abilene. The strong winds resulted in drifting of snow over a foot deep in places. Several folks commented, saying, it took nearly a week for all the snow to melt. Unofficially, there were higher snowfall amounts in the higher elevations. As a result of a tight pressure gradient, strong northeast winds of 40 to 50 mph with higher gusts to near 60 mph blew from the evening of the 26th to the early morning hours of the 27th, knocking down over 300 power poles and power lines across portions of the Big Country. Details: Kimble County Sheriff's Office measured 3.5 inches of snow 3 miles west of Junction. A trained spotter measured 3 inches of snow 7 miles west northwest of Junction. National Weather Service Cooperative Observers measured 3 inches of snow in Putnam and they measured 2 inches of snow 12 miles south of Baird. A trained spotter measured 3 inches of snow in Mertzon. A National Weather Service Cooperative Observer measured 2 inches of snow 12 miles north northwest of Mertzon.

title: Heavy Rain: California, Dec 20, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, from December 20, 2015 to December 22, 2015. Affected areas: El Dorado, Plumas, Shasta, Tuolumne. Episode summary: A wet storm brought heavy rain and heavy high mountain snow, along with strong winds. The heavy rain caused some debris and mud flows in recently burned areas. Details: There was 4.98 inches of rain measured over 24 hours at Pacific House. The 24 rain total was 1.80 inches, with observer located in Castella. There was 1.24 inches of rain reported over 5 hours in Camino.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Feb 08, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from February 08, 2016 to February 08, 2016. Affected areas: Lipscomb. Episode summary: The 3260 Wreck grass fire began around 1330CST around nine miles west southwest of Lipscomb Texas in Lipscomb county. The grass fire occurred less than a mile south of the intersection of Farm to Market Road 3260 and Farm to Market Road 1920 and was caused by sparks from a vehicle or vehicles, possibly due to a motor vehicle accident. The wildfire consumed an estimated one thousand acres and one home was reported to be threatened but was saved by fire fighters. There were no reports of any homes or other structures being damaged or lost and there were no reports of injuries or fatalities from the grass fire. A total of ten fire departments and other fire agencies responded to the wildfire which was contained between 1730CST and 1800CST.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow: California, Jan 05, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, from January 05, 2016 to January 06, 2016. Affected areas: Eastern Sierra Slopes Of Inyo County, San Bernardino. Episode summary: A series of three Pacific storms impacted the desert Southwest, bringing periods of heavy rain, heavy snow, and locally dense fog. Details: Eight inches of snow fell 1 mile W of Aspendell. Highway 95 was closed from I-40 to the NV state line due to flooding near mile marker 79. Rain caused power poles to catch fire in Yucca Valley and Joshua Tree, with 1200 customers losing power. Reported property and crop damage: about $23,000.

title: High Wind: California, Jan 15, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from January 15, 2016 to January 15, 2016. Affected areas: Eastern Sierra Slopes Of Inyo County, Morongo Basin, Western Mojave Desert. Episode summary: A passing shortwave trough brought a brief period of high winds to the Sierra and the western Mojave Desert. Details: The event time was estimated. This gust occurred at Bicycle Lake on Fort Irwin. This gust occurred at Twentynine Palms.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Jan 23, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from January 23, 2016 to January 23, 2016. Affected areas: Eastern Sierra Slopes Of Inyo County. Episode summary: A Pacific storm system brought heavy snow to the higher elevations of the Sierra. Details: Multiple spotters and sensors reported anywhere from eight to 15 inches of snow in and around Aspendell at elevations ranging from 8500 to 10200 feet.

title: Heavy Snow, High Wind: California, Jan 29, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, High Wind, from January 29, 2016 to January 31, 2016. Affected areas: Eastern Sierra Slopes Of Inyo County, Morongo Basin, Owens Valley, Western Mojave Desert. Episode summary: A strong Pacific storm system brought high winds to the Owens Valley and Mojave Desert, high winds and severe thunderstorms to the Mojave Desert, and heavy snow to the southern Great Basin. The episode continued into February. Details: The peak gust was measured 5 miles NW of Independence at 0342 PST. A big rig was blown over on Highway 395 8 miles SSE of Big Pine at 0154 PST, blocking both lanes of the highway. The high winds occurred at Bicycle Lake on Fort Irwin, and the peak gust was measured at 1355 PST. Twenty four inches of snow fell at Aspendell. Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

title: High Wind: California, Jan 12, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from January 12, 2016 to January 12, 2016. Affected areas: North Central & Southeast Siskiyou County. Episode summary: One in a series of fronts brought high winds to parts of northern California...mostly at higher elevations. Details: The KNF-98 RAWS recorded a gust to 62 mph at 12/1920 PST.

title: High Wind: California, Jan 19, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from January 19, 2016 to January 19, 2016. Affected areas: North Central & Southeast Siskiyou County. Episode summary: Another in a series of cold fronts brought high winds to portions of northern California...mostly over higher terrain. Details: The KNF-98 RAWS recorded gusts exceeding 62 mph continuously during this interval. The peak gust was 69 mph at 19/1120 PST.

title: High Wind: California, Jan 21, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from January 21, 2016 to January 22, 2016. Affected areas: North Central & Southeast Siskiyou County. Episode summary: Another in a series of cold fronts brought high winds to portions of northern California, mostly over higher terrain. Details: The KNF-98 RAWS recorded gusts exceeding 61 mph continuously from 21/2221 PST until 22/0120 PST. The peak gust was 71 mph recorded at 22/0120 PST. The Bolam RAWS recorded a gust to 59 mph at 22/0103 PST. The Van Bremmer RAWS recorded a gust to 60 mph at 22/0131 PST.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Dec 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from December 23, 2015 to December 23, 2015. Affected areas: Bayfield, Douglas, Washburn. Episode summary: The event began in the morning as sleet then switched to a heavy wet snow in northwestern Wisconsin. This created very dangerous conditions along U. S. Highway 2 in Bayfield County where 6 to 7 inches of snow fell in a few short hours. A band of 6 to 7 inches stretched from Shell Lake to Cornucopia. Four miles southeast of Cornucopia had 6.5 inches of snow by late afternoon while the Brule DNR ranger station had 7.0 inches.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Dec 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from December 26, 2015 to December 27, 2015. Affected areas: Ashland, Bayfield, Burnett, Douglas, Iron. Episode summary: Snowfall ranged from 6 to 8 inches from Burnett County to Ashland. The snow fell in a short time on a busy travel day. The heaviest snow fell from mid morning to mid afternoon. Snow continued into the night over the snowbelt of northern Wisconsin. Some specific snowfall amounts include 7 inches at Grantsburg, 6 inches in Superior and Washburn and 8.6 inches in Ashland.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from December 27, 2015 to December 28, 2015. Affected areas: Burnet, Kerr, Llano, Val Verde, Williamson. Episode summary: A deep upper level trough and strong cold front moved into a near record warm airmass over South Central Texas. Initially, this caused strong convection that produced near severe size hail. As cold air moved in behind the front, precipitation changed to snow over northern parts of the area. Details: A strong cold front brought snow to Val Verde county with 1.6 inches reported by a CoCoRAHS observer 30 miles northwest of Comstock. Light snow fell in Kerr County and although there was no accumulation reported, there were some icy spots on bridges along I-10 in northern parts of the county. Light snow fell in Llano, but there was no accumulation.

title: Heavy Snow: Texas, Dec 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, from December 26, 2015 to December 27, 2015. Affected areas: Eastern/Central El Paso County, Southern Hudspeth Highlands, Western El Paso County. Episode summary: A deep upper low dove south out of the Great Basin into Northern Mexico. A cold front pushed in from the northeast and a second one from the west which brought sub-freezing temperatures to the region. The storm ranked as the 8th snowiest 2-day snow in the history of El Paso with 6 to 10 inches common across the city. Details: A solid 6 to 10 inches were reported from all of the CoCoRaHS observers across Western El Paso County. Total snowfall accumulations over the zone ranged from 5 to 10 inches with the El Paso Airport officially reporting 8.1 inches. The 10 inches was reported on the southeast side of the Franklin Mountains. An observer in Sierra Blanca reported 9 inches of snow with up to 2 foot drifts.

title: Tornado: Texas, Feb 23, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from February 23, 2016 to February 23, 2016. Affected areas: Wharton. Episode summary: A late night through early morning storm system moved eastward out of south central Texas and across southeast Texas. The southern edge of the storms produced a weak a severe thunderstorm and a weak tornado. Details: This EF-0 tornado destroyed three sheds. Three residences also sustained structural damage. Irrigation equipment was damaged as the tornado crossed a grass field. Trees and power lines were downed, and parts of County Road 100 were blocked by debris.

title: Tornado: Texas, Dec 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from December 12, 2015 to December 12, 2015. Affected areas: Gray. Episode summary: Sufficient moisture for instability combined with wind shear to produce a favorable environment for severe thunderstorms across the southeast portion of the Texas Panhandle. Severe thunderstorms are quite rare for this geographical area during the month of December. Three hail events were documented along with one brief tornado. Details: A brief tornado touchdown was observed by a storm chaser. No damage was reported.

title: Blizzard: Texas, Dec 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Blizzard, from December 26, 2015 to December 28, 2015. Affected areas: Armstrong, Carson, Collingsworth, Dallam, Deaf Smith, Donley, Gray, Hartley, Hemphill, Hutchinson, Lipscomb, Moore and 5 more areas. Episode summary: A blizzard impacted much of the Texas Panhandle from late on the 26th through early on the 28th. Sustained winds over 35 mph were ongoing the evening of the 26th across much of the Texas Panhandle and these winds continued through the event. The 24 hour average wind speed at Amarillo was 35 mph on December 27th while peak wind gusts reached 64 mph. Some additional observation sites in the area indicated peak gusts reached 70 mph during the event. The strong winds caused significant drifting of snow, even in areas that received a relatively minor amount of accumulation. Visibility was significantly reduced due to the blowing snow, and for at least a short period fell to less than one quarter mile at many locations. Deaf Smith County was most significantly impacted in the area served by the National Weather Service in Amarillo, but adjacent counties to the south of Deaf Smith County received snowfall totals that rivaled all-time record levels. See the Storm Data entry by the National Weather Service in Lubbock for details on snowfall amounts and impacts in areas further south. Details: Wind gusts as high as 65 mph were recorded at the West Texas Mesonet site near Hereford just before 8:00 PM CST on the 26th. This preceded the snowfall which began a few hours later. The first report from Deaf Smith County was received at around 6:00 AM on the 27th of 3 inches of snow accumulation with 4 to 5 foot drifts. title: Extreme Cold/Wind Chill: Wisconsin, Jan 17, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Extreme Cold/Wind Chill, from January 17, 2016 to January 17, 2016. Affected areas: Adams, Clark, Jackson, Taylor. Episode summary: Arctic air spread into western and central Wisconsin on the morning of January 17th, producing wind chills of 35 to 40 below. Details: Wind chill values dropped into the -35 to -40 F range. Wind chills values hit -35 F in the Friendship area. Wind chill values dropped to -39 F at the Black River Falls Airport.

title: Coastal Flood: Texas, Dec 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Coastal Flood, from December 27, 2015 to December 27, 2015. Affected areas: Galveston. Details: Coastal flooding inundated portions of Highway 87 near the Highway 24 intersection on the eastern beaches of the Bolivar Peninsula.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Feb 02, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from February 02, 2016 to February 03, 2016. Episode summary: Western and central Wisconsin was covered by 5 to 11 inches of snow on February 2nd. This snow fell as a winter storm tracked from Kansas into lower Michigan. A band of heavy snow developed ahead of the storm, which moved into western Wisconsin during the morning of the 2nd and produced snowfall rates up to two inches an hour. This caused roads to quickly become snow covered. The highest reported snowfall amount was 11.2 inches near Cashton (Monroe County). Blowing and drifting snow became an issue as the storm moved past with wind gusts of 25 to 35 mph. Most schools closed February 2nd in advance of the storm and many of these remained closed on the 3rd as well. In addition to the school closings, the shopping mall and colleges in the city of La Crosse (La Crosse County) also closed. Details: COOP and volunteer snow observers reported 7 to 9 inches of snow across Adams County. The highest reported total was 9.5 inches in Friendship. Considerable blowing and drifting snow occurred with wind gusts of 25 to 35 mph. COOP and volunteer snow observers reported 5 to 6 inches of snow across Buffalo County. Considerable blowing and drifting snow occurred with wind gusts of 25 to 35 mph. COOP and volunteer snow observers reported 5 to 10 inches of snow across Crawford County. The highest reported total was 10.8 inches near De Soto. Considerable blowing and drifting snow occur with wind gusts of 25 to 35 mph. The highest reported wind gust was 29 mph by a mesonet reporting station near Mt. Sterling.

Episode summary: The California drought continues in full force during the month of December, 2015. Fresno received 2.97 inch of rainfall while Bakersfield only received 0.58 of precipitation during the month of December. Even with these rainfall amount there has been little response in water storage across Central California. ||The U.S. Drought Monitor continued to report exceptional drought conditions across the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The general trend of below normal precipitation and above normal temperatures has continued this year. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, loss or reduction of ground water, wells drying up in several communities leaving them with no water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. Also, communities in Central California interior face state mandated reductions in municipal water use.

The wildfire began approximately 1300CST and the wildfire consumed an estimated one thousand six hundred acres. There were four single engine air tankers, two from Abilene and two from Amarillo, that dropped retardant to suppress the flames. There was a fifth aircraft which supervised the four aircrafts as they battled the wildfire. The wildfire threatened homes and other structures in the Tierra Grande and Tascosa Hills area but those homes were saved. There were no reports of homes or other structures damaged or destroyed and there were also no reports of injuries or fatalities. The Texas Department of Transportation blocked off Farm to Market Road 1061 in two areas and southbound traffic was stopped at Farm to Market Road 2381 and northbound traffic was stopped at Loop 335 while crews work to contain the fire. Voluntary evacuations were started by the Amarillo/Potter/Randall Office of Emergency Management for residents in the Tierra Grande area. Fire departments and other fire agencies that responded to the wildfire included those from Amarillo, Canyon, Potter and Randall counties and also the Texas A&M Forest Service and the National Park Service at Lake Meredith. The wildfire was contained as of 0100CST Sunday morning of February 14.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Feb 22, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from February 22, 2016 to February 22, 2016. Affected areas: Hutchinson. Episode summary: The Gina 5 wildfire began around 1205CST about seven miles north northwest of Sanford Texas in Hutchinson county. The wildfire consumed approximately seven hundred acres and was determined to be caused by a cutting torch. There were no homes or other structures threatened and no homes or other structures were damaged or destroyed. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities. A total of seven fire departments or other fire agencies responded to the wildfire which was contained between 1600 to 1630CST.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Dec 10, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from December 10, 2015 to December 11, 2015. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Lassen/Eastern Plumas/Eastern Sierra. Episode summary: Cold low pressure from the North Pacific brought heavy snow to the northern Sierra and down to the lower valleys of northeast California on the 10th and 11th. Details: Heavy snow fell mainly south and west of Susanville on the 10th and early on the 11th, with valleys below 5000 feet starting as rain or a mix of rain and snow before changing over to all snow. Six and a half to 8 inches of snow fell between Sierraville and Lake Davis, including Portola. Ten inches of snow was estimated from the Independence Creek SNOTEL. A widespread 9 to 16 inches of snow fell around the Tahoe Basin on the 10th and 11th, including 12 to 13 inches in the Tahoe City area and 11 inches about 5 miles southwest of South Lake Tahoe.

title: Heavy Snow, High Wind: California, Dec 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, High Wind, from December 13, 2015 to December 13, 2015. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Lassen/Eastern Plumas/Eastern Sierra, Surprise Valley. Episode summary: Low pressure dropped from the northeast Pacific into California on the 13th, bringing high winds to the Surprise Valley and heavy snow to the northern Sierra and portions of northeast California, mainly above about 5000 feet. Details: Nine inches of snow fell in Loyalton, with 10 inches estimated from the Independence Creek SNOTEL (just east of Independence Lake). Ten to 20 inches of snow fell near the Sierra crest, with 7 to 9 inches around Lake Tahoe, in Woodfords, and on the slopes of the Verdi Range (west of Verdi). Wind gusts between 59 and 65 mph occurred at the Surprise Valley RAWS on the morning of the 13th.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Dec 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from December 21, 2015 to December 22, 2015. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area. Episode summary: A moist but relatively warm west to east flow across the Pacific brought very heavy high elevation snow to the Tahoe area on the 21st and 22nd. Details: Two to 4 feet of snow fell above 7000 feet around the Lake Tahoe Basin on the 21st and 22nd. There was a mix of rain and snow below 6500 to 7000 feet, with minimal snowfall at lake level (1 to 3.5 inches Tahoe City and 1/2 inch in South Lake Tahoe) with mainly rain.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Dec 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from December 23, 2015 to December 24, 2015. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Lassen/Eastern Plumas/Eastern Sierra, Surprise Valley. Episode summary: Several days of precipitation in northeast California with moist flow off the Pacific wrapped up with a final heavy snowfall event on the 24th. Details: An estimated 8 to 10 inches of snow fell southwest of Susanville in the higher elevations per SNOTEL and HADS sensors. In the lower elevations, 5 inches of snow was noted at the Portola CO-OP station. Five inches of snow fell in Cedarville between late evening on the 23rd and the morning of the 24th. Eighteen to 24 inches of snow fell at ski areas and along and west of highway 89 on the 24th. Elsewhere, a widespread 10 to 14 inches of snow fell around Lake Tahoe, in Truckee, and east to the foothills of the Verdi Range.

title: High Wind: California, Mar 09, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from March 09, 2016 to March 10, 2016. Affected areas: Modoc County. Episode summary: An incoming front brought high winds to some locations in northern California. Details: The Timber Mountain RAWS recorded wind gusts exceeding 58 mph continuously during this interval. The peak gust was 72 mph recorded at 10/0303 PST.

title: High Wind: California, Mar 13, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from March 13, 2016 to March 13, 2016. Affected areas: North Central & Southeast Siskiyou County. Episode summary: Another in a series of fronts brought high winds to isolated areas of northern California. Details: The Bolam RAWS recorded gusts exceeding 57 mph almost continuously during this interval. The peak gust was 63 mph at 13/0903 PST.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Snow: California, Jan 05, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Snow, from January 05, 2016 to January 07, 2016. Affected areas: Orange, Riverside, Riverside County Mountains, San Bernardino, San Bernardino County Mountains, San Diego, San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: A strong, low latitude jet stream brought a series of storms through Southern California with periods of moderate to heavy rain/snow, thunderstorms, gusty winds, and high surf. Three-day rainfall totals were around 2 to 7 inches for the coast/valley/foothill areas, and 1 to 3 inches for the deserts. The mountains received a wide range of snow amounts, ranging from 6 to 30 inches, most of which fell above 5000 feet. The highest amounts were in the San Bernardino and Riverside County Mountains, with 20 to 30 inches in several locations. Several trees, power lines and poles were downed from wind. A plane approaching San Diego International Airport was struck by lightning on the morning of the 7th, but no injuries or damage reported. Countless flooding reports also came out of the heavy rain accompanying this system, with southwestern San Diego County being hardest hit. Several reports of pea size hail came out of Carlsbad, Poway (accumulation of about 1 inch near I-15 and Carmel Mountain Road), and some in Orange County as well. Details: Snowfall began during the evening of the 5th, continued in a few main heavy periods, and wrapping up by the afternoon of the 7th. Criteria was met sometime in the evening of the 6th. Two-day snowfall totals for Riverside County mountain locations include: 14-16 inches at Pine Cove and Fern Valley near Idyllwild and 23 inches at the Long Valley Ranger Station in San Jacinto State Park. title: Flash Flood, Winter Storm: California, Jan 05, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Winter Storm, from January 05, 2016 to January 06, 2016. Affected areas: Los Angeles, Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Ventura, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: A powerful winter storm brought heavy rain and snow, flash flooding and gusty winds to the area. Rainfall totals from this storm generally ranged between 2 and 6 inches with locally higher amounts in some foothill areas. With such rainfall amounts, there was significant snowfall totals in the local mountains with up to 28 inches of snow reported at the resort level. Additionally, the heavy rain did generate several flash flooding events including several mud and debris flows. Details: Heavy rainfall over the Solimar burn scar resulted in a significant mud and debris flow. The southbound lanes of Highway 101 were closed due to water and debris across the roadway. Heavy rainfall over the Colby burn scar resulted in a significant mud and debris flow. On Rainbow Drive, 2-3 inches of water and debris was reported in a house. Additionally, Sierra Madre Road at Hicrest Road was closed due to water and debris. Heavy rainfall over the Calgrove burn scar generated a significant mud and debris flow. Mud and debris closed a mobile home park near the burn scar.

title: Flash Flood, High Wind, Winter Storm: California, Jan 31, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, High Wind, Winter Storm, from January 31, 2016 to January 31, 2016. Affected areas: Antelope Valley, Los Angeles, Los Angeles County Coasts Including Downtown Los Angeles, Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Barbara County Mountains, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: Another powerful winter storm took aim upon Southwestern California, bringing heavy rain and snow, thunderstorms, and gusty winds. Rainfall totals ranged from 0.50 to 1.50 inches across coastal and valley areas to up to 4.50 inches in the mountains. With such high rainfall totals, some significant snowfall was reported in the mountains with resort levels reporting up to 18 inches. Some severe thunderstorms developed with strong thunderstorm winds (in excess of 60 MPH) reported. Additionally, strong winds were reported across many areas. Details: Winter storm conditions developed across the mountains of Los Angeles county. Above 6000 feet, between 12 and 18 inches of snow was reported along with wind gusts between 65 and 75 MPH. Winter storm conditions developed across the mountains of Ventura county. Above 6000 feet, between 6 and 12 inches of snow was reported along with wind gusts between 65 and 75 MPH. The RAWS sensor at the Botanical Gardens in Santa Barbara reported a wind gust of 58 MPH.

title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Feb 19, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from February 19, 2016 to February 19, 2016. Affected areas: Crawford, Grant. Episode summary: Strong winds occurred across portions of southwest Wisconsin during the late morning and early afternoon of February 19th. A strong area of low pressure moved across the Upper Midwest with the wind occurring on the back side of the low. Gusts of 40 to 55 mph were reported with some minor tree damage occurring. Details: The automated weather observing equipment at the Platteville airport reported wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph during the late morning and early afternoon of February 19th. The highest reported wind gust was 54 mph. Wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph occurred across portions of Crawford County during the late morning and early afternoon of February 19th. A private weather station in Mount Sterling recorded a 54 mph gust. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Feb 19, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from February 19, 2016 to February 20, 2016. Affected areas: Grant. Episode summary: Temperatures warmed over the last half of February and allowed the ice on area rivers to break up and dissipate. This breakup led to an ice jam forming on the Grant River causing some minor river flooding near Burton (Grant County). Details: An ice jam pushed the Grant River out of its banks near Burton. The river crested a little over a foot above the flood stage at 19.12 feet.

title: High Wind: Texas, Mar 23, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from March 23, 2016 to March 23, 2016. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Hale, Lamb, Parmer, Swisher, Yoakum. Episode summary: Following a Pacific cold front early in the morning, a potent upper low in southeast Colorado spread a belt of very strong southwesterly winds over much of the South Plains and Texas Panhandle. Winds of 30 to 45 mph with some gusts of 58 mph or greater occurred for up to several hours. The most intense wind gusts were focused in the southern Texas Panhandle and resulted in some power outages in Tulia from downed lines. A cinder block fence in Plainview was also toppled from the high winds. Fortunately, the lack of severe drought conditions limited the extent and severity of blowing dust with most areas only seeing visibilities reduced to four or five miles during the peak of the high winds.||The maximum wind gusts of 67 mph were recorded by two Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet stations: Mackenzie Reservoir at 1205 CST and Silverton at 1300 CST. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 30, 2016 to January 31, 2016. Affected areas: Callahan. Episode summary: Plenty of dry grasses and trees, dry air and gusty southwest winds provided the conditions for the spread of a large wildfire near Eula. Details: The High Line Wildfire burned approximately 700 acres 2 miles north northeast of Dudley between County Roads 224 and 226 just east of Highway 36 in Callahan County. The wildfire spread north of County Road 230 but still west of FM 603. The fire was contained by the evening of January 31. Seven homes were burned near Eula. title: Cold/Wind Chill: Wisconsin, Jan 11, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Cold/Wind Chill, from January 11, 2016 to January 11, 2016. Affected areas: Kenosha. Episode summary: The Kenosha County Medical Examiner reported a death due to hypothermia. Details: The Kenosha County Medical Examiner reported the cause of death of a woman as hypothermia due to environmental cold exposure. The woman was found by a postal worker at 11:30 am. The low temperature earlier that morning in Kenosha was 4 below zero Fahrenheit.

title: Cold/Wind Chill: Wisconsin, Feb 28, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Cold/Wind Chill, from February 28, 2015 to February 28, 2015. Affected areas: Kenosha. Episode summary: The Kenosha County Medical Examiner reported a death due to hypothermia. Details: The Kenosha County Medical Examiner reported the death of an elderly man due to hypothermia. The temperatures were below zero during the early morning hours with high temperatures in the teens Fahrenheit.

title: High Wind: Texas, Mar 26, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from March 26, 2016 to March 26, 2016. Affected areas: Bailey, Parmer. Episode summary: On the heels of a strong cold front in the evening, northwest winds gusted to 72 mph and 59 mph at Muleshoe and Friona, respectively. No damage was reported. These wind gusts were measured by Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet stations. This same cold front helped support several inches of snow farther north across portions of the northern Texas Panhandle which came as a surprise to many on Easter morning.

title: High Wind: Texas, Mar 12, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from March 12, 2016 to March 13, 2016. Affected areas: Davis / Apache Mountains Area, Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: The passage of an upper trough and the associated cold front resulted in high winds over the Guadalupe Mountains. Details: McDonald Observatory recorded several gusts over 60 mph.

title: High Wind: Texas, Mar 13, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from March 13, 2016 to March 13, 2016. Affected areas: Davis / Apache Mountains Area, Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: Strong southwesterly flow aloft resulted in high winds in the Guadalupe and Davis Mountains. Details: McDonald Observatory recorded several gusts from the southwest over 60 mph.

title: High Wind: Texas, Mar 14, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from March 14, 2016 to March 14, 2016. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: Persistent, strong southwesterly flow aloft over the region resulted in high winds in the Guadalupe Mountains. Details: Strong west winds occurred in the higher elevations of the Guadalupe Mountains.

title: High Wind: Texas, Mar 18, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from March 18, 2016 to March 19, 2016. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: A cold front resulted in strong northeast gap winds through Guadalupe Pass. Details: Northeast winds of 40 mph or more occurred in Guadalupe Pass for four hours.

title: High Wind: Texas, Mar 22, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from March 22, 2016 to March 23, 2016. Affected areas: Davis / Apache Mountains Area, Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: The approach of a strong upper level trough resulted in high winds over the Guadalupe, Delaware, Apache and Davis Mountains, in addition to portions of the Permian Basin. Details: An extended period of high winds occurred in the higher elevations of the Guadalupe Mountains, punctuated by many gusts over 60 mph and a few gusts over 70 mph. McDonald Observatory recorded several gusts over 60 mph on March 23rd.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Jan 28, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from January 28, 2016 to January 28, 2016. Affected areas: Kenedy, Starr, Zapata. Episode summary: A cold front pushed across Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley during the first half of January 26th. A secondary surge of high pressure behind the front, combined with clearing skies and light winds to provide a good set up for a radiational cooling event that resulted in a short duration freeze for Zapata, Starr, and Kenedy counties. Temperatures across these counties dropped to or below freezing for several hours during the early morning hours of January 28th. Details: Temperatures fell to or below freezing for 4.5 hours on the morning of January 28th. The AWOS site in Zapata reported a low of 27 degrees. Temperatures fell to or below freezing across Starr County during the early morning hours of January 28th. The RAWS site at Falcon Dam reported a low of 27 degrees and the COOP site in Rio Grande City reported a low of 29 degrees. Temperatures fell to or below freezing across Kenedy County during the early morning hours of January. Both COOP sites in the county reporting temperatures below freezing, with the site in Armstrong reporting a low of 32 degrees and the site in Sarita reporting a low of 28 degrees.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Jan 29, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from January 29, 2016 to January 29, 2016. Affected areas: Kenedy, Starr, Zapata. Episode summary: Cold overnight temperatures continued in the wake of a cold front on January 26th. Clear skies, light northwesterly winds, and lowering dewpoints, combined to provide an excellent setup for radiational cooling. A short duration freeze occurred across Zapata, Kenedy, and Starr counties. Temperatures across these counties dropped to or below freezing for several hours during the early morning hours of January 29th. Details: Temperatures fell to or below freezing across Zapata County during the early morning hours of January 29th. The AWOS site in Zapata reported a low of 31 degrees. Temperatures fell to or below freezing across Starr County during the early morning hours of January 29th. The COOP site in Rio Grande City reported a low temperature of 29 degrees. Temperatures fell to or below freezing for several hours during the morning of January 29th. The COOP site in Armstrong reported a low of 25 degrees.

title: Strong Wind: Texas, Jan 16, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, from January 16, 2016 to January 16, 2016. Affected areas: Cameron, Hidalgo. Episode summary: The passage of a cold front along with deepening low pressure over the western Gulf of Mexico produced strong and gusty northwesterly winds across the Rio Grande Valley. Peak wind gusts in excess of 40 mph were measured across Cameron and Hidalgo counties, causing power outages that left almost 10,000 customers without power, grass fires, downing a tree and a traffic signal. Details: Strong winds took down a traffic light in Harlingen at the intersection of Business 77 and 1st Street. The nearby KHRL ASOS reported sustained winds of 36 to 41 mph with gusts to 50 mph. Public reported a large tree downed by winds near the intersection of 2 Mile N and 46th Street in McAllen. The nearby KMFE ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 48 mph. Reported property and crop damage: about $6,500.

title: Drought: California, Jan 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from January 01, 2016 to January 31, 2016. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continues in full force during the month of January, 2016. Fresno received 4.42 inch of rainfall while Bakersfield only received 1.95 of precipitation during the month. Even with these rainfall amount there has been little response in water storage across Central California. ||The U.S. Drought Monitor continued to report exceptional drought conditions across the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The general trend of below normal precipitation and above normal temperatures has continued this year. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, loss or reduction of ground water, wells drying up in several communities leaving them with no water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. Also, communities in Central California interior face state mandated reductions in municipal water use.

title: High Wind, Winter Storm: California, Jan 03, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Winter Storm, from January 03, 2016 to January 05, 2016. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Mtns, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: Beginning on the January 3rd a series of upper level systems moved through the area. On the 3rd the resultant pressure gradient lead to some severe wind gust across Kern County. Then by the 4th things transitioned to a winter storm event, with most of the higher elevations receiving snowfall. The series of storms continued to parade into the area until 8th. Details: Grapevine Peak RAWS reported a 82 MPH wind gust at 1132 PST. Bear Valley Springs station reported a 60 MPH wind gust. Yosemite Valley reported 17 inches of snowfall.

title: High Wind, Winter Storm: California, Jan 29, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Winter Storm, from January 29, 2016 to January 31, 2016. Affected areas: Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: A good fetch of tropical moisture surged into the area during the last weekend of January. Though, this was not the only impact during the later part of January as fog was also in play. In fact, the Thursday prior to the arrival of the moisture had enough of a break in activity for fog development. ||Then on Friday rain and snow showers began to fall, though snow levels where initially fairly high. The snow levels did fall throughout the event to nearly 3,000 feet above sea level. This first upper level system ejected out of the area early on Saturday morning, which resulted in severe wind gusts across Kern County.||Also on Saturday, due to a break in activity again the area experienced dense fog development. The showers resumed again on Sunday prior to the system ejecting out of the area. However, as the system ejected it increased the pressure gradient across Kern County, which resulted in severe wind gust into the evening Sunday. Details: Lodgepole reported 25 inches of snowfall. Lake Wishon reported 29 inches of snowfall. Lake Thomas reported 30 inches of snowfall.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Mar 08, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from March 08, 2016 to March 10, 2016. Affected areas: Bowie, Cass, Cherokee, Gregg, Harrison, Nacogdoches, Rusk, Sabine, Shelby, Smith. Episode summary: A strong upper level low pressure system settled over northern Mexico on March 8th, and became stationary through March 12th as it was cut off from the upper level jet stream, with a blocking upper ridge having developed over Florida and the western Atlantic. Meanwhile, a weak frontal boundary entered the region from the west on the 8th, and became stationary over Deep East Texas, Northwest Louisiana, and Southwest Arkansas. Upper level disturbances ejected northeast ahead of the Northern Mexico low pressure system, resulting in periods of showers and thunderstorms containing heavy rainfall to move repeatedly over these areas. The air mass was most unstable on the 8th, where several severe thunderstorms developed and produced wind damage across portions of Northwest and Northcentral Louisiana, as well as East Texas. However, widespread heavy rainfall was relentless along and ahead of the surface front over Deep East Texas, all of North Louisiana, and Southwest Arkansas where widespread flash flooding occurred. Numerous roads and bridges were flooded or washed out, homes were flooded, and many high water rescues were required as many drivers drove around barricades and into the flooded roadways. Widespread rainfall amounts of 5-10+ inches fell during the 4 day period across much of East Texas, with amounts of 12-16+ inches across Sabine County. Several structures suffered some sort of water damage along with numerous road surfaces as well. Many or those road surfaces, bridges and low water crossings were completely washed out. This resulted in many high water rescues of stranded motorists, especially during the very beginnings of the prolonged flooding event. Many motorists drove around barricades and into the

title: Drought: California, Jan 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from January 01, 2016 to January 31, 2016. Affected areas: Carquinez Strait And Delta, Central Sacramento Valley, Motherlode/Camptonville To Groveland, Northern Sacramento Valley, Northern San Joaquin Valley, Southern Sacramento Valley. title: Flood: California, Jan 23, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from January 23, 2016 to January 23, 2016. Affected areas: Tehama. Episode summary: Strong thunderstorms developed over the northern Sacramento Valley, dropping large hail, up to 3 inches in diameter. There was also large amounts of small hail, up to 5 inches deep, bringing slippery road conditions, clogging storm drains and causing vehicle accidents. Multiple funnel clouds were reported, but no tornado touchdowns were observed. Heavy showers and thunderstorms also brought locally heavy rains into the Valley and foothills. Details: Street flooding occurred on 10th street in Corning, with large amounts of 1/4 inch hail. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow: California, Jan 16, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, from January 16, 2016 to January 18, 2016. Affected areas: Shasta, West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Heavy rain fell, as much as 3 to 6 inches in the foothills, 1 to 2 inches in the Valley. Minor rises in foothill streams were observed. The Sacramento River at Tehama Bridge approached but did not reach flood stage. Details: There was 1.10 inches of rain that fell over 24 hours at Castella.
