title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 17, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 17, 2016 to April 18, 2016. Affected areas: Bandera, Bastrop, Bexar, Caldwell, Comal, Fayette, Gonzales, Kinney, Lee, Travis, Uvalde, Val Verde and 1 more areas. Episode summary: Persistent southeasterly flow in the low levels increased surface dewpoint temperatures to the middle 60s across South Central Texas. This allowed a deep upper level low and surface cold front to cause thunderstorms that produced locally heavy rainfall leading to flash flooding. A few storms also produced large hail. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing Hwy 71 at Kitchen Ln. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing Hwy 71 in several locations east of La Grange. Swift water rescues were performed and cars were under water. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing numerous roads in and around Del Rio including Cienegas Rd., Industrial Blvd., Kings Way, W. Academy St., 15th St., and Main St.

title: Frost/Freeze: California, May 28, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Frost/Freeze, from May 28, 2016 to May 28, 2016. Affected areas: Northeast Siskiyou And Northwest Modoc Counties. Episode summary: Clearing skies allowed nighttime temperatures to drop to around freezing over the Klamath Basin. Details: Tulelake reported a low temperature of 32 degrees.

title: High Wind: Texas, May 26, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from May 26, 2016 to May 26, 2016. Affected areas: Sabine. Episode summary: A complex of showers and embedded thunderstorms moved across East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana during the morning and afternoon hours on May 26th. As these showers and embedded thunderstorms diminished from west to east, strong, damaging winds with gusts up to 60 mph associated with a wake low over Deep East Texas during the late evening hours downed numerous trees and power lines over Sabine County Texas and across portions of Northcentral Louisiana. Details: Damaging wind gusts estimated to be near 60 mph from a strong wake low event snapped several trees on Highway 6 on the Texas Side of Toledo Bend Reservoir, with several additional trees downed along River Bend Drive in Eastern Sabine County.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 27, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 27, 2016 to May 27, 2016. Affected areas: Nacogdoches, Sabine, San Augustine. Episode summary: The second complex of showers and embedded thunderstorms in two days moved across East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana during the morning and afternoon hours on May 27th, bringing about widespread rains to the region. This complex developed well ahead of a closed upper level low pressure system over the Southern Rockies, which spread slowly east in the broad southwest flow aloft extending into the Lower Mississippi Valley. As it interacted with moderate instability and stronger shear over Southeast Texas, Southern and Central Louisiana, some of these storms became severe over portions of Deep East and Southeast Texas, as well as Northcentral and Southern Louisiana during the afternoon, producing numerous reports of downed trees and power lines. Given the already saturated grounds from rain that fell less than a day before, the heavy rainfall associated with these storms produced flash flooding over these areas as well. Details: TXDOT reported that Farm to Market Road 95 between Martinsville and Chireno was flooded and closed. County Road 384 about 3 miles southeast of Martinsville off of FM 95 was flooded and closed as well. Flash flooding was reported over Farm to Market Road 2866 northwest of Pineland, as well as Highway 83 East of Pineland. Flash flooding was reported on County Road 410 over Clear Branch Creek just west of Highway 96 south of San Augustine.

title: High Wind: California, May 19, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 19, 2016 to May 19, 2016. Affected areas: Owens Valley. Episode summary: A strong low pressure system moving through the Pacific Northwest produced high winds over portions of southeast California and southern Nevada. Details: The peak wind gust was measured 4 miles NW of Independence. Several trees were downed in the Owens Valley, some of which blocked roads, and at least one of which fell on a vehicle. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 22, 2015 to December 22, 2015. Affected areas: North Bay Mountains. Episode summary: Strong and gusty west to northwest winds developed behind the departing weather system during the early morning hours of Tuesday, December 22. Wind gusts of between 40 and 50 mph were common, especially along the coast and in the hills, and local wind gusts in excess of 60 mph occurred in the North Bay Mountains. Thousands of power outages were reported due to these strong winds. Details: Peak wind gusts at the Big Rock RAWS in Marin County. Peak wind gusts reported by the Atlas Peak RAWS in Napa County.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, May 31, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 31, 2016 to May 31, 2016. Affected areas: Chippewa, Dunn, Rusk. Episode summary: A line of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon along a cold front that extended from west central Wisconsin, southeast into north central Iowa. By 3 PM CST, strong storms developed southeast of Elk Mound and moved northeast across Dunn and Chippewa counties of west central Wisconsin. Several bands of torrential rainfall led to localized flash flooding, plus a few storms caused damage in Elk Mound and Albertville. One of the higher rainfall reports was 4.20 inches in the town of Ladysmith. Details: Two bands of torrential rainfall, with rainfall rates as high as 2 inches per hour, moved across far western Chippewa county between Albertville and Bloomer. The rainfall caused Highway 64 and County Road 40 near Bloomer to become impassable for a short period. A 3.00 inch rainfall report was measured by the local emergency manager. A 3.20 inch rainfall report was measured by the local emergency manager.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 15, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 15, 2016 to May 15, 2016. Affected areas: Brewster. Episode summary: There was an upper low over the northwest United States with plentiful moisture across West Texas. Upslope winds across the higher terrain of West Texas along with decent convective available potential energy and wind shear contributed in the development of thunderstorms with large hail and flash flooding. A couple of boundaries from convection the previous day may have aided in the development of the flash flooding. Details: A thunderstorm moved across Brewster County and produced heavy rain and minor flooding on Highway 385 in Marathon. A thunderstorm moved across Brewster County and produced flash flooding south of Marathon. Highway 385 was impassable south of Marathon. No damage was reported.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 04, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from June 04, 2016 to June 04, 2016. Affected areas: Shawano. Episode summary: A very weak tornado (waterspout) occurred on Loon Lake in northern Shawano County as a line of showers interacted with a surface boundary. Details: A very weak waterspout occurred on Loon Lake, about five miles northeast of the city of Shawano. The waterspout, which was photographed and recorded by law enforcement, remained nearly stationary for about a minute, causing no damage, before dissipating.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 22, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 22, 2016 to May 22, 2016. Affected areas: Glasscock, Howard. Episode summary: West Texas was under the backside of a ridge with a dryline across the area which provided lift. Good instability, moisture convergence, and high convective available potential energy was present along and to the east of the dryline. Wind shear was also high over the area, and a low level jet of high winds allowed for storms to continue into the late evening hours. These conditions contributed to thunderstorms that produced large hail, strong wind, flash flooding, and tornadoes across the Permian Basin. Details: Heavy rain fell across Howard County and produced flash flooding in Big Spring. People were trapped in a damaged building and rescue personnel had trouble getting them out due to flooded roads. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Howard County and produced flash flooding southwest of Big Spring. There was six to twelve inches of water flowing over the road. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate since no damage was reported. A thunderstorm moved across Howard County and produced a tornado near Big Spring. Eyewitness reports from storm chasers and spotters in the area indicate that the tornado began at 6:13 pm CDT just south of Texas State Highway 176, approximately 10 miles west of Big Spring. The tornado then moved southeastward over open fields, bounded by Natural Dam Lake to its west and Wilkinson Road just to it Reported property and crop damage: about $242,800.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 16, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from April 16, 2016 to April 17, 2016. Affected areas: Brown, Fisher, Runnels. Episode summary: A few supercells developed as an upper level disturbance interacted with a dryline. These supercells resulted in a funnel cloud report northwest of Sweetwater. As this supercell moved east and northeast, a storm chaser later photographed a tornado southwest of Roby in Fisher County. Details: Law Enforcement reported 8 to 10 inches of water over the road on Farm to Market 419. A trained spotter reported several low crossings flooded in Ballinger. In addition, a few vehicles were reported stalled near Bearcat Stadium. The Brownwood Emergency Manager reported several low water crossings barricaded due to high water. These included the Vine Street underpass, the intersection of Brady and Roggin Streets, and the low water crossing at Magnolia and 4th Street.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 19, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 19, 2016 to April 19, 2016. Affected areas: Menard. Episode summary: Several supercell storms formed in an unstable airmass on April 19, and resulted in large hail reports across the region. More severe storms developed on the 20th, in advance of a decaying cluster of thunderstorms. These storms resulted in more large hail reports. Details: The Menard County Sheriff's office reported U.S. Highway 83 in Menard flooded, with at least one motorist stranded due to flooding.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 26, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 26, 2016 to April 26, 2016. Affected areas: Haskell. Episode summary: The interaction of a dryline, a strong upper level disturbance and plenty of moisture resulted in an outbreak of severe thunderstorms across a large part of West Central Texas. An isolated tornado was also photographed just north of Stamford. A line of severe thunderstorms quickly formed and produced the vast majority of the large hail and wind reports. Details: A storm chaser photographed a tornado located just north of Stamford. The location of the tornado is estimated using radar and spotter information. The storm chaser took the picture from the golf course looking to the north and northwest. The tornado became quickly wrapped up in rain.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 14, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 14, 2016 to May 14, 2016. Affected areas: Harris. Episode summary: Afternoon thunderstorms developed and produced some hail, gusty winds and flash flooding. Details: Heavy rains produced flash flooding that lead to water rescues from vehicles in the Bellaire, Meyerland and Westbury areas. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Strong Wind: Texas, May 26, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, from May 26, 2016 to May 26, 2016. Affected areas: Ector, Midland. Episode summary: An upper low resided over the Arizona and New Mexico state line, and a dryline was present across the eastern Permian Basin and Lower Trans Pecos. An unstable moist air mass existed to the east of the dryline where increased dewpoints, steep mid-level lapse rates, and increased wind shear allowed for organized thunderstorms. Thunderstorms developed that produced large hail and severe wind gusts. Details: A shower produced a wind gust of 53 mph at the Odessa Airport. Media reported a telephone pole that was blown down in West Odessa. The cost of damage is a rough estimate. A shower produced a wind gust of 55 mph at the Midland International Airport. Media reported a tree blown down two miles northeast of Midland from the same shower. The cost of damage is a rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,100.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 31, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 31, 2016 to May 31, 2016. Affected areas: Ector, Midland. Episode summary: Intense heating and topography combined with outflow boundaries from prior storms aided in providing a focus for thunderstorms. Strong wind shear and high instability helped generate severe thunderstorms that produced large hail and strong winds. An advancing cold front and low level jet during the evening hours continued the thunderstorm threat. The heavy rains from these storms produced flash flooding. Details: Heavy rain fell across Midland County and produced flash flooding in the City of Midland. An NWS employee reported six inches of water running over Midland Drive in the northwest part of the City of Midland. Heavy rain fell across Ector County and produced flash flooding in Odessa, TX. Several roads were closed and seven water rescues were reported across the city. Damage costs are a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,200.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: California, Apr 08, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, from April 08, 2016 to April 11, 2016. Affected areas: San Bernardino, San Diego. Episode summary: A pair of upper level lows brought showers and thunderstorms to Southern California from the 7th to the 11th. Though they were relatively small, the thunderstorms that formed were slow moving, allowing them to produce a few areas of flooding. Details: The southbound onramp of Interstate 15 was flooded with 1 to 2 feet of stagnant water. A BMW stalled due to flooded waters in the right lane. The CHP reported several inches of water across all lanes of Highway 54. The CHP reported flooding on Highway 395 near Shadow Mountain Road. Vehicles were spinning out because of the water on the roadway. Reported property and crop damage: about $360,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 01, 2016 to June 02, 2016. Affected areas: Upton. Episode summary: An upper low over the region, outflow boundaries from thunderstorms the previous night, and a weak cold front that was moving slowly south across the area were the causes of thunderstorm activity across parts of West Texas. The strongest instability and wind shear were located in the Big Bend Region where thunderstorms produced large hail. Moisture content across the area was high and thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall, which added to the flash flood threat after a lot of areas had already seen heavy rains from the previous day. Details: Heavy rain fell across Upton County and produced flash flooding. State Highway 329 in Upton County was closed from the Crane County line to four miles east into Upton County due to flooding at low water crossings. Cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Upton County and produced flash flooding south of McCamey. The McCamey Sheriffs Department reported one foot of water running over Highway 1901 south of McCamey. Reported property and crop damage: about $300.

title: Strong Wind: California, Apr 22, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, from April 22, 2016 to April 23, 2016. Affected areas: Coachella Valley. Episode summary: A trough of low pressure brought strong winds to the desert slopes of the Riverside County mountains, impacting the Coachella Music Festival during the evening of the 22nd. Details: The Emergency Manager for the City of Indio reported strong winds at the Coachella Music Festival. The winds displaced numerous tents, causing damage to parked cars. Reported property and crop damage: about $30,000.

title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, Jun 10, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from June 10, 2016 to June 10, 2016. Affected areas: Jefferson. Episode summary: A surge of warm and moist air on a low level jet stream resulted in numerous thunderstorms over southern Wisconsin. Very heavy rain resulted in flash flooding, some street flooding; in addition to some hail with the storms. The roof of a home in Oconomowoc was struck by lightning with a resultant fire. Details: Up to 6.5 inches of rain in two hours brought flash flooding of creeks and fields in the Town of Sumner. Many roads were washed out including state highway 106 from Schwemmer Road to Kreutz Road with a foot drop off in some areas. The Becker Road bridge sustained excessive damage on the sidewalls due to large tree limbs blocking the middle of the bridge, thereby diverting water around the sides. U Reported property and crop damage: about $60,000.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 10, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from June 10, 2016 to June 10, 2016. Affected areas: Outagamie. Episode summary: A line of thunderstorms, from western Upper Michigan into southeast Minnesota, produced widespread damaging winds that downed a large number of trees and power lines as the storms moved into very warm and unstable air. A wind gust to 61 mph was measured at Marshfield Municipal Airport (Wood Co.) as the storms passed and a COOP observer in Plover (Portage Co.) measured a gust to 59 mph. Isolated quarter size hail fell at Hogarty (Marathon Co.) and southwest of Shawano (Shawano Co.), and a brief, weak tornado occurred near Mackville (Outagamie Co.) as the storms passed. Details: A weak tornado (EF0) developed about 1.3 miles southwest of Mackville and moved southeast before dissipating. Damage was limited to broken tree branches and limbs. Peak wind was estimated at 55 to 60 mph. The tornado was photographed by a storm spotter.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 30, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 30, 2016 to May 30, 2016. Affected areas: Glasscock, Howard, Midland, Scurry. Episode summary: An upper trough was off the Pacific coast and was moving inland over California and Arizona. This put West Texas and southeast New Mexico under southwest winds aloft. A dryline was backed up against the mountains leaving good moisture with 50 degree dewpoints off to the east. The dryline and boundaries across the area became the focus for thunderstorms. Lapse rates and instability were high, which aided in the development of severe storms with large hail, strong winds, and flash flooding. Details: Heavy rain fell across Midland County and produced flash flooding in and near Greenwood, TX. There was flooding along Highway 307 between FM 1379 and FM 1105 with an estimated six inches to a foot in depth. Heavy rain lead to flooding of low lying areas and minor street flooding in the City of Snyder. Heavy rain fell across Midland County and produced flash flooding in Spraberry. Highway 158 between Highway 137 and Interstate 20 was nearly underwater and impassable. Reported property and crop damage: about $500.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 15, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from June 15, 2016 to June 15, 2016. Affected areas: Calumet. Episode summary: Thunderstorms, a few with large hail, gusty winds, and heavy rain, moved through the area as a low pressure system slid southeast across Wisconsin. Golf ball size hail fell near Readfield (Waupaca Co.) and southwest of Coloma (Waushara Co.). A weak waterspout formed on Lake Winnebago west of Calumet County, but dissipated before reaching shore. A COOP observer near Rhinelander (Oneida Co.) measured 3.04 inches of rain from the storms, much of which fell in about an hour, and a COOP observer in Appleton (Outagamie Co.) had a one-hour rainfall total of 1.66 inches. Details: A weak waterspout formed northwest of Stockbridge on eastern Lake Winnebago and moved southeast before dissipating. No damage occurred.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 28, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 28, 2016 to May 29, 2016. Affected areas: Scurry. Episode summary: An upper trough was located over the Central Plains with another upper trough developing just off the southern coast of California. West Texas was under westerly winds aloft with a dryline present across the Lower Trans Pecos and eastern Permian Basin. Severe storms were able to develop along the dryline with the help of upper level lift in an environment with good instability, increased wind shear, and high lapse rates. Details: Heavy rain fell across Scurry County and produced flash flooding near Union, TX. A car was stranded in eight inches of water crossing over FM 1609. Several other low water crossings in the area were reported to be flooded. Damage costs are a rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 13, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 13, 2016 to June 13, 2016. Affected areas: Cherokee. Episode summary: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed during the overnight and early morning hours on June 13th across East Texas, near and east of a weakening upper level closed low and attendant trough over Central Texas. Showers and thunderstorms containing very heavy rainfall developed along a line from Waco to Mexia, Palestine, and Jacksonville, Texas, along a stationary surface boundary which was positioned on the south and east side of the weak closed low, resulting in showers and thunderstorms that repeatedly trained over the same areas. Given these surface and upper level features in place, in addition to daily record precipitable water values sampled in the early morning weather balloon data from Shreveport, LA, very heavy rainfall with rain rates of 2 to 3 inches per hour fell over these areas, resulting in widespread flash flooding between Waco and Jacksonville. This affected much of northern and central Cherokee County in East Texas, with numerous reports of roads closed due to flash flooding, and water entering businesses near Rusk. Widespread rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches fell within two to three hours time over these areas, before the showers and thunderstorms weakened by mid-morning and shifted east into extreme Eastern Texas and Northcentral Louisiana. Details: Multiple roads were closed due to flooding including Hwy. 69 between Rusk and Jacksonville, Hwy. 79 west of Jacksonville, Hwy. 84 at FM 1248, FM 347, FM 768 and FM 2138 outside of Jacksonville, Texas. Numerous other county roads were also underwater and closed. Highway 60 was closed in Rusk, Texas. Some businesses reported to have had water in them as well. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Mar 05, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from March 05, 2016 to March 07, 2016. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Mono. Episode summary: A deep moisture feed and cold front combined to bring heavy snow to the Sierra from late on the 5th through the morning of the 7th, mainly near and west of the crest. Details: One to 3 feet of snow fell near the crest above 7500 feet from the evening of the 5th through the morning of the 6th. Elsewhere, snowfall totals dropped off substantially, with 9 inches at the Mammoth Ranger Station, 3 to 6 inches in Lee Vining, and 1.5 inches in Bridgeport. Two rounds of snow brought between 2 and 4.5 feet of snow above 6500 feet, mainly west of highway 89. Below 6500 feet and farther east, considerably less snow fell with around a foot in the Tahoma and Tahoe City areas, with only 6 inches for the South Lake Tahoe and Truckee airports.

title: Heavy Snow, High Wind: California, Mar 12, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, High Wind, from March 12, 2016 to March 14, 2016. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Lassen/Eastern Plumas/Eastern Sierra, Mono. Episode summary: Strong, moist flow off the Pacific brought heavy snow to northeast California on the 12th and 13th followed by high winds for portions of Mono County on the 14th. Details: Between 18 and 30 inches of snow fell fell near the Sierra crest and in the higher elevations south of Lake Tahoe. At lake level, periods of rain or rain mixed with snow cut down totals greatly with only 9 inches of snow in Tahoma and just under 6 inches at the South Lake Tahoe airport and in Tahoe City. Southwest winds sustained between 40 and 54 mph with gusts 60 to 81 mph were recorded at the Mammoth-Yosemite airport and the Valentine Eastern Sierra Reserve (both near highway 395), with the higher end of the wind range at the latter location. Between 10 and 14 inches of snow fell on the shores of Lake Davis, with an estimated 14 to 24 inches near the Sierra crest and at around 7000 feet on Grizzly Ridge (northwest of Portola). Below 5000 feet, much less snowfall was reported with only 1 inch noted in Portola.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Jun 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from June 01, 2016 to June 02, 2016. Affected areas: Clay. Episode summary: With a front lingering in the region and a cut off low moving overhead, scattered to widespread showers formed across Oklahoma and north Texas the morning of the 1st and continued through the 2nd producing some flash flooding. Details: Highway 148 north was closed at Mayo road north of Henrietta. US 82 was impassable between Henrietta and Ringgold. US 287 S was impassable from Brown road to Klein road.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jun 15, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from June 15, 2016 to June 15, 2016. Affected areas: Castro, Childress, Garza. Episode summary: Very hot temperatures during the afternoon was enough to break an inversion that resulted in scattered thunderstorms within an unstable airmass. With a deeply mixed boundary layer, the primary hazard from these thunderstorms were microburst winds. However, very strong instability over the Rolling Plains did result in large hail. Furthermore, strong outflow winds well away from convective activity resulted in severe wind gusts.||High winds reports from the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet:||64 mph at Graham (Garza County), 62 mph at Dimmitt (Castro County), 60 mph at Hart (Castro County), and 59 mph at Childress (Childress County).

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Apr 17, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from April 17, 2016 to April 18, 2016. Affected areas: Bell, Bosque, Coryell, Jack, Johnson, Limestone, Milam, Palo Pinto, Wise. Episode summary: Another in a series of slow moving storms parked across North and Central Texas on the 17th, leading to heavy rain and localized flooding. The most significant flooding occurred in Palo Pinto, Jack, Johnson and Milam counties. Details: Several secondary roads remained flooded across the county after several inches of rain fell. U.S Highway 380/State Highway 199 was closed due to high water, just south of the city of Jacksboro. Palo Pinto Sheriff's deputies reported flooding along and near U.S. 281 near Mineral Wells. Reported property and crop damage: about $719,000.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Apr 22, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from April 22, 2016 to April 22, 2016. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area. Episode summary: Low pressure moved over northern California and brought a short period of heavy snow to the Lake Tahoe area on the 22nd. Details: Ten to 18 inches of snow fell near the Sierra crest above 6500-7000 feet and in the higher elevations south of Lake Tahoe, with 5 to 10 inches below 6500 feet and around the shores of Lake Tahoe.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 30, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 30, 2016 to April 30, 2016. Affected areas: Montgomery, Polk, San Jacinto. Episode summary: A weak disturbance passing ahead of a western upper level trough of low pressure moved through a regional unstable and moist environment. This initiated strong discrete thunderstorm cells that traveled across the northern half of the forecast area, producing flash flooding and wind damage. Details: High rainfall created countywide flooding. Sections of FM 350, FM 1988, FM 352, and FM 1276 between Livingston and Corrigan were flooded. Heavy rainfall caused the flooding, and the subsequent closure, of Rose Road. There was also flooded streets in the nearby Royal Forest subdivision. Roads were inundated with water around the towns of Onalaska and West Livingston. Water also covered FM 3126 between FM 2457 and Cedar Valley Road.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 18, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 18, 2016 to April 18, 2016. Affected areas: Hardin, Jefferson, Newton, Orange. Episode summary: A blocking pattern set up over the eastern sections of the country with a trough over Texas. Multiple upper level disturbances moved through Texas from the 18th to the 21st providing multiple rounds of thunderstorms. The first round produced flooding in Southeast Texas as is moved slowly across the area. Details: A couple of low water crossings near Batson flooded closing the roadways. Water also closed some roadways in Kountze and Silsbee. Cypress Bayou also went out of its banks. Water flooded Farm-to-Market 253 closing portions of the road. Media relayed a video of flooding along Cormier and Cherokee Streets in Vidor. Flooding was also reported along some streets in Pinehurst. Over 5 inches of rain was reported in Orange near the Sabine River.

title: Wildfire: California, Jun 07, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from June 07, 2016 to June 21, 2016. Affected areas: Western Siskiyou County. Episode summary: The Pony Wildfire was started by lightning around 0245 PDT on 06/07/16. As of the last report on 28/0430 PDT, the fire covered 2858 acres and was 63 percent contained. 17.5 million dollars were spent on firefighting efforts. Details: The Pony Wildfire was started by lightning around 0245 PDT on 06/07/16. As of the last report on 28/0430 PDT, the fire covered 2858 acres and was 63 percent contained. 17.5 million dollars were spent on firefighting efforts.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 26, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 26, 2016 to April 26, 2016. Affected areas: Grayson. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed along a dryline over the western and northern counties of the FWD CWA during the late afternoon and evening hours of Tuesday as an upper level disturbance moved overhead. Storms eventually organized into a line during the late evening hours, which moved east across the rest of the region. Damaging winds were the main severe threat that night but three tornadoes occurred in Grayson County. Details: Amateur radio spotters observed and reported a tornado which moved from southwest of Bells to just northwest of the Bells High School. This storm produced little damage other than tree damage near Bells. The only damage in town was to a recreational vehicle business near the intersection of US 82 and US 69. A National Weather Service storm survey crew determined a brief tornado produced EF-0 damage on the southeast side of Whitesboro. This tornado was embedded in a squall line and produced damage to four homes and two businesses. The most damage was done to a business, which took the brunt of a direct hit of a roof which was blown off of another house upstream. A National Weather Service damage survey team determined a tornado produced EF-0 and EF-1 damage to several homes, businesses, and one school on the evening of April 26th. The tornado occurred in Howe, just south of the Sherman city limits, beginning on the west side of US 75. The tornado damaged a mobile home business near the Howe High School, where superficial damage was done due to debris flyi Reported property and crop damage: about $730,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 27, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 27, 2016 to April 27, 2016. Affected areas: Jasper, Tyler. Episode summary: A strong upper level disturbance and a cold front moved through during the morning of the 27th. Widespread tree damage was associated with a bowing line segment in Southeast Texas along with 2 tornadoes. Details: The tornado began near FM 1005 just north of Magnolia Springs where it uprooted several pine trees. A home along FM 1005 was damaged when a tree fell on it. The path continued northeast and caused mostly tree damage with minor out building damage also noted. The tornado dissipated near Boggy Creek north of CR 317. The tornado touched down southeast of Woodville near highway 287 where tree fall displayed greater convergence and some roofing material was removed from a building. The tornado continued to the southeast snapping numerous softwood trees before dissipating just East of County Road 4250. Reported property and crop damage: about $17,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 30, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from April 30, 2016 to April 30, 2016. Affected areas: Hardin, Jasper, Newton. Episode summary: An upper low move across the plains with a divergent pattern aloft over Southeast Texas creating an atmosphere ripe for widespread storms. Flooding and a couple of severe storms developed. Details: Numerous streets were flooding around Silsbee and Kountze including Highway 92. A tornado developed approximately 10 miles southwest of call along county road 702 and moved northeast along county road 1004 snapping or uprooting numerous trees and power lines over a wide swath. The tornado destroyed a single wide trailer just west of us Highway 96. The trailer flipped over twice with three residents inside. One was person was transferred to the hospital to receive stitches. Th A tornado cut a path of over 9 miles through Jasper County before dissipating south of Call. Damage in Newton County was confined to minor tree damage along Holmes Road. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Drought: California, Apr 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from April 01, 2016 to April 30, 2016. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continues during the month of April, 2016. Fresno received 1.06 inches of rainfall while Bakersfield only received 0.97 inch of precipitation during the month. Increased precipitation earlier in the year and slightly below normal temperatures we received this month did allow for lower evaporation rates and soil moisture to maintain higher levels. Some snow melt did occur contributing to improved water storage levels. ||The U.S. Drought Monitor continued to report exceptional drought conditions across the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The general trend of below normal precipitation and above normal temperatures has continued this year. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, loss or reduction of ground water, wells drying up in several communities leaving them with no water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. Also, communities in Central California interior face state mandated reductions in municipal water use. Details: Persistent drought conditions continued to be reported.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 17, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 17, 2016 to April 17, 2016. Affected areas: La Salle. Episode summary: Isolated severe thunderstorms occurred over the western Brush Country during the late afternoon and evening hours. Details: Spotter reported a brief rain wrapped tornado.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 09, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 09, 2016 to May 10, 2016. Affected areas: Lamar. Episode summary: Isolated thunderstorms developed over North Texas during the evening hours of May 8 and May 9 along a dryline, which was able to surge east into the area each afternoon. Some of these storms produced damaging winds and large hail, along with a few instances of flash flooding. Activity on May 9 remained confined to the Red River counties, which were on the southern end of a more widespread event across Oklahoma. Details: Emergency management reported water up to the windows of a car at the 500 block of Lamar Avenue. Amateur radio reported water coming into homes on Clark Lane in southeast Paris, TX. A trained spotter reported multiple cars flooded approximately 1 mile north-northwest of Paris, TX with multiple high water rescues ongoing. Reported property and crop damage: about $70,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 10, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 10, 2016 to May 10, 2016. Affected areas: Mills. Episode summary: A weak cold front eased south to near the Red River area, and helped provide focus for thunderstorm development along with a continued active dryline. This ended up being more of a wind damage event, but several reports of hail were also received. Details: Highway 16, two miles south of Priddy was closed due to high water.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 20, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 20, 2016 to April 20, 2016. Affected areas: Zapata. Episode summary: As a weak midlevel disturbance moved across the region, convection developed across the mountains of northeast Mexico and moved east into Zapata County. Some of the thunderstorms became severe, with quarter sized hail reported in the city of Zapata. The storms became nearly stationary at times and produced heavy rainfall which led to falsh flooding in Zapata. Details: Zapata County Sheriff's Office reported several streets in the city of Zapata covered with one to two feet of water and that several motorists had been stranded on Highways 83 and 16 near Zapata. The AWOS site at the Zapata County Airport reported 1.26 inches of rainfall, with half an inch falling in a time span of twenty minutes.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 26, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 26, 2016 to May 27, 2016. Affected areas: Bosque, Comanche, Leon, Robertson. Episode summary: A series of upper level disturbances produced multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms across the region. A few storms became severe with large hail and damaging wind gusts, but storms training repeatedly over the same areas led to this being mostly a flood and flash flood event. Details: Several roads were closed due to flooding. In particular, CR 466 had 5-6 feet of water over it. Other closed roads included CR 456 and CR 229. Several FM and County Roads were closed due to flooding. Water was covering the road surfaces of CR 409, FM 587, CR 419, and FM 1689. Several roads across the county remained flooded. Reported property and crop damage: about $32,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 29, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 29, 2016 to May 31, 2016. Affected areas: Eastland, Erath, Fannin, Hood, Johnson, Kaufman, Palo Pinto, Somervell, Stephens, Tarrant, Young. Episode summary: Several disturbances in advance of a deepening upper level trough over the southwest states led to multiple rounds of showers and storms across North and Central TX. With wet soils already in place, flash flooding was the main weather concern during this time. However, with unstable air still in place, some storms were able to become severe with large hail and damaging winds. Details: Highway 183 between Rising Star and Cisco was flooded. Highway 183 south of Breckenridge was flooded. Water was across Highway 380 at Eastside Lake Road and Bryan Farm Road. Other county roads had minor flooding but no specific roads were given. Reported property and crop damage: about $509,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 15, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 15, 2016 to April 15, 2016. Affected areas: Oldham. Episode summary: A vigorous low pressure system produced supercell thunderstorms across the western Texas Panhandle during the afternoon and evening of April 15th. Several reports of large hail were received, including hail as large as tennis balls near Stratford and Dalhart. Two separate storms produced hail up to golf ball size in Dalhart. A brief tornado was observed over rural northern Oldham County. Details: Storm chasers reported a brief tornado over rural northern Oldham County. The tornado lasted for about one minute. This tornado was observed from Highway 385 just south of Boys Ranch.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 26, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from June 26, 2016 to June 26, 2016. Affected areas: Waupaca. Episode summary: Thunderstorms brought damaging winds, hail, very heavy rain, and a brief tornado, as they moved across central and east central Wisconsin starting in the late afternoon of June 25th, and continuing into the early morning hours of June 26th. The storms downed numerous trees and power lines at many locations as they passed. Thunderstorm winds also tore the roof from a silo and caused shingle and siding damage to a house and garage north of Black Creek (Outagamie Co.), knocked trees onto a house and a car near Seymour (Outagamie Co.), and produced a downburst wind of at least 75 mph that snapped and uprooted trees south of Nichols (Outagamie Co.).||A weak tornado that touched down east-southeast of Symco (Waupaca Co.) snapped and uprooted trees, and damaged several buildings at a farm. Details: A weak tornado formed 4.2 miles east-southeast of Symco and traveled east just under three miles. At least a half dozen pine trees were snapped along the path and several large trees were uprooted (DI 28, DOD 3,4). Several farm outbuildings were heavily damaged, with metal from the buildings strewn downwind hundreds of yards. A manufactured home was pushed off its block foundation (DI 3, DOD 3). T Reported property and crop damage: about $200,000.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Apr 07, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from April 07, 2016 to April 09, 2016. Affected areas: Ashland, Bayfield, Iron. Episode summary: A combination of synoptic and lake effect snow April 7th into the 8th brought heavy snow to parts of northern Wisconsin near Lake Superior. Snowfall reports included 16 near Bayfield, 14 near Cornucopia, 13 near Sand Bay, 11.6 in Gile, 11.2 near Washburn, and 8 near Herbster.

title: Heavy Rain: California, Apr 09, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, from April 09, 2016 to April 10, 2016. Affected areas: Kern. Episode summary: A slow moving moisture laden low pressure system moving across central California over the southern San Joaquin Valley produced thunderstorms and heavy rain. The slow movement of the parent system allowed for slow moving thunderstorms and heavy rain cells which created nuisance and street flooding in the southern San Joaquin Valley. Details: Reports of nuisance flooding and street ponding were submitted via Facebook of flooding in Shafter California in Kern County at approximately 2020 PST. Reports were submitted by California Highway Patrol of nuisance and street ponding northeast of Cawelo California near State Route 65 and Famoso Road at 2059 PST in Kern County. Numerous reports of nuisance flooding and street ponding were submitted by local law enforcement and California Highway Patrol in Bakersfield between April 9th at 2100 PST and April 10th 0000 PST.

title: High Wind: California, Apr 14, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 14, 2016 to April 14, 2016. Affected areas: Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: Low pressure system moving southeastward through northern California was accompanied by a cold front that moved southeastward through central California which produced an onshore flow with increased pressure gradients producing breezy to windy conditions for the Kern County Mountains. Details: Report received from Cache Creek APRS station of 34-41 mph sustained winds with peak wind gust of 59 mph at 0012 PST. Report received from Mojave NTPS station of peak wind gust of 64 mph at 0104 PST. Report received from Mojave ASOS of sustained winds of 38-43 mph between 0040 PST and 0120 PST with a peak wind gust of 69 mph at 0120 PST.

title: Tornado: California, Apr 27, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Tornado, from April 27, 2016 to April 27, 2016. Affected areas: Stanislaus. Episode summary: A weather system resulted in thunderstorms developing across the Southern Sacramento and Northern San Joaquin valley and adjacent foothills of the Sierra Nevada Mountains. The storms resulted in half inch hail deep enough to cause slick road conditions, and slight damage to a carport. Lightning struck a tree, causing a portion of it to split off. An EF0 tornado was also observed that uprooted a eucalyptus tree and moved a shed off it's foundation. Details: An EF0 tornado with swirling debris was observed near Hickman elementary school by a Sheriff's deputy and several members of the public. title: High Wind: California, Apr 25, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 25, 2016 to April 25, 2016. Affected areas: Se Kern Cty Desert. Details: Received report of road closures due to high winds at west bound California state route 58 and California state highway 14 near exit 167 both near Mojave California from 23ABC news in Bakersfield. title: High Wind: California, Apr 23, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 23, 2016 to April 23, 2016. Affected areas: Indian Wells Vly. title: Heavy Rain, High Wind, Strong Wind: Texas, Apr 18, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, High Wind, Strong Wind, from April 18, 2016 to April 19, 2016. Affected areas: Cameron. Episode summary: A broken line of thunderstorms marched across the Rio Grande Valley through the late afternoon and evening hours and combined with other development across Nuevo Leon and Tamaulipas, Mexico to form a convective system. This initially stabilized the atmosphere and held back development. However, the continued flow from the east/northeast ran into northward moving boundaries from storms in Tamaulipas/Nuevo Leon to form a severe storm over Port Isabel and South Padre Island, with the first report of large hail at 745 pm LST. Soon after, outflow from this storm would link up with others from the Mexico storms and a small but potent local convective system soon formed between Harlingen and Brownsville. Downburst winds, reached 58 mph at KHRL and knocked down a number of power lines, blew some shingles off one apartment complex, and blew off at least one poorly fastened carport on the east side of Harlingen. Strong winds from the south, once again, due to the sharp difference in high and low pressure within the region ��� propagated through the Lower Rio Grande Valley, producing a 60 mph gust at KHRL just after 12 am LST on the 19th and causing additional damage to at least one tin roof (Bass Boulevard, west side) and at least one fence in town. Additional minor damage may have occurred in Brownsville during the same period, as the peak wind at KBRO reached 54 mph at 1255 am LST on the 19th. In addition intense rains dropped generally 2 to 4 inches in Brownsville, with several known poor drainage intersections seeing nuisance flooding. Water was to the roof of cars in the low lying areas. About 20 units of the Treyway Terrace apartments were damaged by flooding. title: Drought: California, May 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from May 01, 2016 to May 31, 2016. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continues during the month of May, 2016. Fresno received 0.29 inches of rainfall while Bakersfield only received 0.55 inches of precipitation during the month. Increased precipitation earlier in the year and slightly below normal temperatures we received this month did allow for lower evaporation rates and soil moisture to maintain higher levels. Some snow melt did occur contributing to improved water storage levels. ||The U.S. Drought Monitor continued to report exceptional drought conditions across the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The general trend of below normal precipitation and above normal temperatures has continued this year. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, loss or reduction of ground water, wells drying up in several communities leaving them with no water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. Also, communities in Central California interior face state mandated reductions in municipal water use. Details: Persistent drought conditions continued to be reported.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 22, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 22, 2016 to May 22, 2016. Affected areas: Donley, Hansford, Ochiltree. Episode summary: One of the most significant severe weather events of the 2016 severe weather season occurred on the 22nd and brought large hail, damaging winds and tornadoes to mainly the eastern Texas Panhandle. A supercell thunderstorm produced at least 6 tornadoes in southern Ochiltree County on the evening of May 22, 2016. No damage was reported for the final two tornadoes east of Highway 70 in open country and these were not surveyed. Damage consisted of a destroyed barn, downed power lines, some tree damage, and several flipped pivot irrigation systems. Homes were narrowly missed on several occasions. the tornadoes exhibited odd motions that were not consistent with the motion of the storm which was turning right sharply during the event. Tow of the tornadoes were large and at least one large multivortex tornado occurred with this event. The storm's rear flank downdraft also produced significant damage across the area which included snapping numerous power poles along Highway 281. Details: Water was reported to be over the bridge on Highway 70 at Wolf Creek. A creek in the area overflowed its banks resulting in flooding of croplands and residential basements. Running water was reported along the sides of U.S. Highway 287. Local county roads were impassible due to flowing water. This occurred after an estimated 4 to 6 inches of rain fell in the area.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 16, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 16, 2016 to May 16, 2016. Affected areas: Dallam, Hemphill. Episode summary: A surface low pressure system over northeast New Mexico moved southeast during the late afternoon and evening hours. A cold front moved southeast across the panhandles from northwest to southeast behind the low pressure system. Severe thunderstorms developed across northeast New Mexico during the afternoon and then moved southeast across the panhandles. Low level shear helped to create an environment favorable for tornadic supercells in the Texas Panhandle. Tornadoes were well documented by spotters and storm chasers through photos and video, and four caused minor damage. Details: Damage from this short track, small tornado included a destroyed grain silo, tree damage, a flipped center pivot irrigation system and minor roof damage to a farm house. This resulted in EF-1 rating with estimated peak winds of 87 mph. This tornado resulted in flattened grass, a flipped center pivot irrigation system and a small trailer flipped over in a field. This was consistent with EF-0 damage and estimated peak winds of 80 mph. A brief tornado crossed Highway 60 about 3 miles south of Canadian. Minimal tree damage was found, consistent with EF-0 damage and estimated peak winds of 74 mph. A storm spotter witnessed this tornado.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 24, 2016 to May 24, 2016. Affected areas: Hutchinson. title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 26, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 26, 2016 to May 30, 2016. Affected areas: Callahan, Coleman, Kimble, Shackelford, Throckmorton. Episode summary: The dryline interacting with an unstable airmass, producing severe thunderstorms on May 26-27. As the airmass remained unstable, a dissipating front and dryline continued to produce rounds of severe thunderstorms on May 28 and 29. One of these supercell thunderstorms produced a strong tornado east southeast of Junction. Many reports of large hail and damaging winds were reported along with a few tornadoes and flash flooding. Details: Hardwood tree damage was the primary damage indicator used in the survey. A few hardwood trees were snapped at the trunk approximately 1 mile west southwest of Burkett, indicating max wind speeds of 90-95 mph. Most of the damage was EF0 as the tornado damaged many large tree limbs. A few outbuildings were completely destroyed at the beginning of the damage path. A community center Burkett had The Throckmorton Volunteer Fire Department trained spotters reported a tornado briefly touching down about 5 miles northwest of Elbert. This tornado snapped and also uprooted numerous oak tree trunks along its path. The tornado also destroyed a porch and carried it for a few miles. The strong winds lifted a portion of the roof off of the home. The tornado also uprooted large cedar trees. Storm chasers videotaped this tornado that was in the shape of a cone.

title: Flood: Texas, Jun 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from June 01, 2016 to June 01, 2016. Affected areas: Erath, Hood, Johnson, Kaufman, Palo Pinto, Somervell. Episode summary: Continued flooding from the end of May. Details: Persistent moderate to heavy rainfall that began on May 31st resulted in the flooding and closure of multiple roads in the county. Fm 2728 was closed during the early morning hours of the 1st. Several roads across the southern portions of the county remained closed due to flooding that began on May 31st. Areas affected included Mingus, Strawn, Gordon, and other areas along Palo Pinto Creek. House water rescues along the creek were still ongoing on the morning of June 1st. Several roads across the county remained barricaded due to flooding that began on May 31st.

title: Wildfire: California, Jun 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from June 01, 2016 to June 07, 2016. Affected areas: Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: The Chimney Fire started on June 1, 2016 on BLM land near the Chimney Peak Campground, 10 miles West of Pearsonville, CA in Tulare County. It was human caused. It burned 1324 acres before being contained on June 7, 2016. Coast of containment was $2.8 million.

title: Wildfire: California, Jun 23, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from June 23, 2016 to June 30, 2016. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns. Episode summary: The Erskine Fire began on June 23, 2016 along Erskine Creek Road, 1 mile southwest of Lake Isabella in Kern County. The fire spread rapidly due to strong, gusty winds, hot temperatures and dry conditions on June 23 through 25. The growth of the fire slowed as winds decreased by June 26, however the fire continued to burn through early July before being contained on July 9. It burned 48,019 acres. The fire closed Highway 178 east of Bakersfield for several days with evacuation of numerous small communities in the Lake Isabella area. The fire destroyed 285 residences and 1 commercial building as well as damaging 12 other residences. There were 2 fatalities as an elderly couple were unable to escape the rapidly moving fire. The cost of containment as of July 9, was $23 million.

title: Flood: Texas, May 19, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from May 19, 2016 to May 19, 2016. Affected areas: Bell, Milam. Episode summary: Persistent moderate to heavy rain caused flooding across Bell County including the southbound lanes of Interstate 35 under the overpass in Troy. Downstream locations across Milam County were also affected. Details: Persistent moderate to heavy rain caused flooding in the southbound lanes of Interstate 35 under the overpass in Troy. TXDoT reported the lanes were closed. The son of a volunteer firefighter was saved by helicopter during a high water rescue on Donahoe Creek at FM 402 near the town of Davilla, TX. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 31, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 31, 2016 to May 31, 2016. Affected areas: Mason, Taylor. Episode summary: Thunderstorms with very heavy rain caused flash flooding in portions of Mason and Taylor Counties. Details: A low water crossing was flooded causing water to flow over Highway 29. Flooding was reported along parts of FM 89 in Taylor County. The water level was one foot over the road in the vicinity of Lake Abilene State Park. Abilene State Park was evacuated. Water was over a part of U.S. Highway 83 and 84 south of Abilene in Central Taylor County.

title: Heavy Rain: California, May 05, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, from May 05, 2016 to May 06, 2016. Affected areas: Fresno, Kern, Kings, Merced. Episode summary: Slow moving upper level low pressure system just west of the coast of California allowed for a large influx of moisture to move into central California which set the stage for heavy rain bands and embedded thunderstorms to develop for two days in a row. Flooding was observed in many locations. Details: California Highway Patrol reported water covering northbound SR99 at the Belmont off-ramp in Fresno at 1710 PST. California Highway Patrol reported road flooding on SR152 at Rock Bridge west of Los Banos at 1822 PST. California Highway Patrol reported road closure due to road flooding south of Panoche Junction on Kamm Road just east of Interstate 5 to San Diego Road at 2259 PST.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, May 15, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from May 15, 2016 to May 15, 2016. Affected areas: Cameron. Episode summary: Convection initiated across the Rio Grande Valley as daytime heating combined with daytime heating of a moist atmosphere and a mid-level disturbance moving into the area. Slow moving thunderstorms dropped heavy rainfall across northwestern Cameron County resulting in urban nuisance flooding from heavy rainfall. Details: CoCoRaHS observer west of Harlingen reported 3.55 inches of rainfall in less than 2 hours. CoCoRaHS observer west of Harlingen reported 4.06 inches of rainfall in less than 2 hours.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Feb 24, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from February 24, 2016 to February 24, 2016. Affected areas: Hidalgo. Episode summary: The combination of rapidly drying fuels (grasses and brush) with very low afternoon humidity (below 15 percent) and frequent wind gusts between 20 and 25 mph allowed a grass fire to grow rapidly and burn nearly 700 acres of land near Sullivan City. Sparks from someone burning trash ignited the fire and strong winds fueled the fire. No injuries were reported. Details: Broadcast media reported a large grass fire near Sullivan City. Nearly 700 acres were burned, with no injuries or damaged structures reported.

title: Drought: California, May 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from May 01, 2016 to May 31, 2016. Affected areas: Carquinez Strait And Delta, Central Sacramento Valley, Motherlode/Camptonville To Groveland, Northern Sacramento Valley, Northern San Joaquin Valley, Southern Sacramento Valley. Episode summary: Long term drought impacts continued through the month of May, though the largest of the reservoirs in northern interior California were at or above normal levels due to a significant mountain snow pack melting. Lake Shasta was 107% of normal by the end of the month, Lake Oroville was 111%, Folsom Lake was 101%, and Don Pedro was 99%. New Melones continued to lag behind the other significant area reservoirs and was only 41% of normal.
