title: Tornado: Texas, May 30, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 30, 2016 to May 30, 2016. Affected areas: San Patricio. Episode summary: A weak tornado produced damage on the southwest side of the city of Taft as a thunderstorm moved through during the morning hours of the 30th. Details: Storm survey concluded a weak EF-0 tornado occurred on the southwest side of the city of Taft. The tornado touched down at the intersection of Wilburn and Mexico Streets and traveled east for about six tenths of a mile. The tornado snapped large trees at the base, lifted shingles from a few homes, and tossed outdoor furniture. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 31, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 31, 2016 to May 31, 2016. Affected areas: Jim Wells, Kleberg, Live Oak. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance moving across South Texas, combined with a very moist and unstable atmosphere, produced strong to severe thunderstorms across South Texas on May 31st. The strongest storms crossed Kleberg County and produced 3 tornadoes, very strong winds, large hail, and torrential rainfall. Details: An EF-0 tornado touched down in an open field southwest of Ricardo. The tornado was captured in a photo by a trained spotter. No visible damage was observed by NWS storm survey team. Vehicles were flooded near Texas A&M University at Kingsville and near Avenue G. Water approached homes and porches. A foot of water was on the roads. Several cars and trucks were stranded in high water. Roads were flooded on 17th Street, Caesar Avenue, and 14th through 16th Streets. Weak waterspout over northeast part of Choke Canyon Reservoir moved onshore. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,625,000.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, May 31, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from May 31, 2016 to May 31, 2016. Affected areas: Sawyer. Episode summary: Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused some flooding in the Winter, WI area. Details: A few roads were washed out due to heavy rain. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, May 27, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from May 27, 2016 to May 27, 2016. Affected areas: Fond Du Lac. Episode summary: A shortwave trough and warm front resulted in numerous thunderstorms over southern WI during the afternoon and early evening. One EF-1 tornado occurred in Fond du lac County. Details: An EF-1 tornado damaged the roofs of approximately 10 homes, 2 businesses, and 1 church. The roof damage covered less than 20 percent of the roof in most cases. The damage ranged from the removal of shingles to the entire removal of the roof material. Awnings and gutters were also damaged on the structures including a small number of windows. Numerous tree limbs were downed including some trees s Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: High Wind: California, May 14, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 14, 2016 to May 15, 2016. Affected areas: Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: Upper level trough and an associated cold front moved south and east into the central California interior and brought gusty winds to the Kern County desert areas. Details: Report received from Mojave ASOS of sustained winds of 43-50 mph between 1600 PST and 1700 PST with a peak wind gust of 60 mph at 1620 PST. Report received from Cache Creek APRS station of 32-44 mph sustained winds between 2129 PST and 0250 PST with a peak wind gust of 67 mph at 0045 PST.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 01, 2016 to June 07, 2016. Affected areas: Bexar, Blanco, Frio, Gonzales, Guadalupe, Hays, Kendall, Kinney, Llano, Uvalde, Williamson. Episode summary: A cold front moved into South Central Texas and encountered a very moist boundary layer. This front generated thunderstorms that produced large hail, damaging wind gusts, and heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing several streets in Pearsall. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing CR 140E at Hwy 85 west of Charlotte. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing Elm Creek Rd. southwest of Seguin.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 03, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 03, 2016 to June 04, 2016. Affected areas: Caldwell, Travis, Williamson. Episode summary: An upper level trough moved across Texas and interacted with a moist boundary layer to generate thunderstorms across South Central Texas. Some of these storms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding damaging the residential bridge on Silvermine Dr. at Williamson Creek near Hwy 71. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding requiring the Austin PD to respond to a call for flood assistance at N. Lamar Blvd. and W. 10th St. near Shoal Creek. The body of a man was discovered in Bull Creek just downstream from a low water crossing. A flooded pickup was found nearby. Time of the incident is estimated since there are no witnesses to the event. The cause of death was ruled drowning by the medical examiner.

title: Heavy Rain: California, May 05, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, from May 05, 2016 to May 05, 2016. Affected areas: El Dorado. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance brought early afternoon showers and a few strong thunderstorms, some of which had significant amounts of hail. Details: There was a 4 hour total of 1.17 inches of rain. There was also small hail around 1 pm.

title: Dust Storm: California, May 21, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, from May 21, 2016 to May 21, 2016. Affected areas: San Diego County Deserts. Episode summary: A trough of low pressure north of Southern California brought gusty winds to the mountains and deserts. Details: A spotter reported blowing dust with visibility of 1/4 to 1/8 of a mile, sustained winds to 39 mph and gusts to 50 mph.

title: Flood: Texas, May 23, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from May 23, 2016 to May 23, 2016. Affected areas: Milam. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms during the morning hours of May 23 produced mainly minor damage as they traversed the northern third of the region. Details: According to local news reports, a woman drove into high water on the Little River bridge in Cameron. While the heavy rain from the day before had ended hours before the incident, water remained over the roadway by 9 AM CDT on the 23rd. As the woman drove her car on the bridge, the water swept the car off of the bridge and into the river bank. The woman was rescued by Cameron Police Department and Reported property and crop damage: about $30,000.

title: Flood: Texas, May 14, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from May 14, 2016 to May 14, 2016. Affected areas: Denton. Episode summary: The remnants of a thunderstorm complex moved southeast from the Plains into North Texas overnight Friday Night. Storms were sub-severe, but created some problems with added minor flooding across the area Saturday Morning. One person drowned in the flooded Pecan Creek in Denton County. Details: Two homeless people were swept into a canal near Bell Place and McKinney Street around 5 AM Saturday May 14. A female adult was rescued about half a mile downstream. A male was found deceased another half a mile or so downstream near S Loop 288 and Shady Oaks at 10 AM.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 02, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 02, 2016 to June 02, 2016. Affected areas: Taylor, Tom Green. Episode summary: Thunderstorms with very heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in both Taylor and Tom Green Counties. Details: Water was reported up to the doors at Clack Street and Southwest Drive in Abilene, with high water rescues underway. Law enforcement officials reported many flooded streets across San Angelo and about a dozen of water rescues was reported.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Jun 27, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from June 27, 2016 to June 27, 2016. Affected areas: Crockett, Sutton, Tom Green. Episode summary: Rain and occasional heavy rain over a 24 hour period resulted in flooding of draws and low water crossings. Rainfall amounts averaged between 5 and 7 inches across parts of the area. Details: A water rescue at the intersection of Sunset Drive and College Hills Boulevard was reported by San Angelo Police. Sunset Drive was barricaded at the Red Arroyo, with a swath of water flowing over the road. Flooding was reported along the main draw which flows through Ozona. The roads passing through the draw were flooded. In addition, the Ozona Automated Weather Observing Station recorded 6.57 inches of rainfall between 6 PM on June 26 through|835 AM on June 27.

title: Drought: California, Jun 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from June 01, 2016 to June 30, 2016. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continues during the month of June, 2016. Entering the summer period which is usually quite dry for most areas, outside of a few summer thunderstorms, June was no exception. Fresno received 0.06 inches of rainfall while Bakersfield did not receive any precipitation during the month. ||The U.S. Drought Monitor continued to report exceptional drought conditions across the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The general trend of below normal precipitation and above normal temperatures has continued this year. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, loss or reduction of ground water, wells drying up in several communities leaving them with no water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. Also, communities in Central California interior face state mandated reductions in municipal water use. Details: Persistent drought conditions continued to be reported.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 15, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 15, 2016 to June 15, 2016. Affected areas: Midland. Episode summary: Weak upper level ridging was over Texas, and an upper disturbance moved over the region. This disturbance combined with intense afternoon heating to create instability for thunderstorms. A dryline/surface trough across the area provided a focus for storm development. Since the cloud bases were high and the air directly below the clouds was dry, strong winds resulted from the thunderstorms. There was plenty of low-level moisture so flash flooding also developed. Details: Heavy rain fell across Midland County and produced flash flooding in the City of Midland. Four high water rescues were reported in the City of Midland at 8:51 pm, 9:29 pm, 9:38 pm, and 11:31 pm. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Wisconsin, Jun 14, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Flood, from June 14, 2016 to June 14, 2016. Affected areas: Crawford, La Crosse. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed north of a warm front during the afternoon of June 14th. As these storms moved across southwest Wisconsin, they produced heavy rain that caused some flash flooding to occur in and near Prairie du Chien (Crawford County). Details: Heavy rain caused flooding to occur in Prairie du Chien and along State Highway 27 where it comes down off the ridge and into Prairie du Chien. Heavy rains caused street flooding to occur in the city of La Crosse. Some cars became stranded in the flooded streets.

title: Strong Wind: California, Jun 10, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, from June 10, 2016 to June 10, 2016. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area. Episode summary: A paddleboarder fell from his board into Lake Tahoe during rough waters and was lost. Details: Rough water due to gusty winds between 20 and 35 mph caused a paddleboarder to fall from his board into Lake Tahoe while seeking help for his companions who had also fallen from their boards. After the others were rescued by a marina crew, the rescue crew looked for the victim but he could not be found (although his board was found). The search for the victim was called off on June 15th.

title: Heat: California, Jun 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heat, from June 01, 2016 to June 09, 2016. Affected areas: Death Valley National Park. Episode summary: One person suffered heat stroke in Death Valley on June 1st (she survived), and another person was found dead, presumably from the heat, on June 9th. High temperatures at Furnace Creek during this period ranged from 115F to 120F. Details: Two people were stranded in the park when their car became stuck in loose sand. They walked for two miles before being found. One of them, described as an older woman, suffered from heat stroke. She recovered after a week in the hospital. Two park visitors found a dead motorcyclist on Harry Wade Road in the extreme southern end of the park June 9th. It is unknown when the man died.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jun 29, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from June 29, 2016 to June 30, 2016. Affected areas: Inyo, San Bernardino. Episode summary: The first monsoon moisture push of the season led to isolated thunderstorms on the 27th through the 29th, followed by a widespread severe weather and flash flooding outbreak on the 30th. The episode continued into July 2nd. Details: A debris flow covered Highway 168 with mud. Water and mud covered the intersection of Highway 95 and Goffs Road. 95 was eventually closed all the way to Interstate 40. Highway 190 was flooded from Daylight Pass Cutoff to Cow Creek. Reported property and crop damage: about $18,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Jun 12, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from June 12, 2016 to June 13, 2016. Affected areas: Anderson, Collin, Ellis, Freestone, Hill, Kaufman, Limestone, Mclennan, Navarro, Rains. Episode summary: An upper level low pressure center trekked east across the area, bringing with it 2 days of shower and thunderstorm activity to North and Central Texas. The heaviest rains occurred across the southeast portions of the region where several locations experienced significant flooding. Details: Several feet or water covered portions of HWY 22 between Blooming Grove and Frost. Heavy rain caused roads near Richland (including Interstate 45) to flood. Interstate 45 was shutdown between MM 210 and 218 just south of Richland due to flooding. Reported property and crop damage: about $51,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, May 05, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from May 05, 2016 to May 06, 2016. Affected areas: San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara. Episode summary: A moist and unstable atmosphere generated thunderstorms and flash flooding across inland sections of Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo counties. Due to flash flooding and mud and debris flows, sections of Highways 46 and 166 were closed. Details: California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding and mud and debris flows around the intersection of Highway2 33 and 166. Several vehicles were trapped in mud. California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding and mud and debris flows across sections of Highway 46, northeast of Shandon.

title: Wildfire: California, Jun 15, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from June 15, 2016 to June 30, 2016. Affected areas: Santa Barbara County Mountains, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: A hot and dry atmosphere, gusty winds and very dry vegetation lead to two significant wildfires across Southern California. The Sherpa fire and Pine fire burned over 7,500 acres total across the mountains of Santa Barbara and Ventura counties. Details: The Sherpa Fire burned 7,474 acres in the mountains of Santa Barbara county. The Pine Fire, which started in late June and burned into mid July, burned 2,304 acres in the mountains of Ventura county.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 02, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 02, 2016 to June 04, 2016. Affected areas: Hardin, Jasper, Jefferson, Orange. Episode summary: A ridge of high pressure and an area of low pressure pulled deep moisture across the region during the first 4 days of June. A slow moving upper low and multiple short waves also traversed the area creating lift. Widespread showers and storms was the result from the 2nd through the 5th. Details: Widespread street flooding was reported by the Hardin County Sheriff's Department. Flooding closed roads across a large portion of the county including in Lumberton and Silsbee. Texas Department of Transportation reported roads closed from flooding around Buna and Kirbyville including FM 777 and 1013. Beaumont Public Works reported multiple roadways flooded and closed around the city including Westgate Drive and Norwood Drive.

title: Tornado: Texas, Jun 13, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from June 13, 2016 to June 13, 2016. Affected areas: Carson, Moore, Potter. Episode summary: A weak upper disturbance moved across the region in advance of a vigorous upper trough which was moving across the southwest United States. Strong instability and moderate to strong low level wind shear provided a favorable environment for super cell thunderstorms to occur in advance of a developing line of thunderstorms which swept across the region during the evening hours. Storms produced large hail up to tennis ball size, wind gusts that were measured as high as 65 mph, and two tornadoes. The most significant damage form this event came from an EF2 tornado which rolled a well anchored double wide trailer onto it's roof in rural Carson County. Details: A brief tornado touched down in rural southeast Moore County just south of Highway 152. Tree damage was observed in a narrow path and included numerous broken limbs and one tree which was uprooted. This was consistent with EF-0 damage on the Fujita Tornado Damage Scale. The tornado began just west of Highway 136 in extreme eastern Potter County. Storm chasers witnessed the tornado form and cross the highway. One power pole was snapped along Highway 136 which was consistent with EF1 Damage. The tornado then continued into Carson County and produced damage just across the county line which was consistent with EF-2 on the Fujita Tornado Damage Scale. This damage occ

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Jun 01, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from June 01, 2016 to June 03, 2016. Affected areas: Bell, Cooke, Coryell, Eastland, Grayson, Hamilton, Hill, Hood, Johnson, Limestone, Mclennan, Montague and 1 more areas. Episode summary: An upper level low pressure center moved eastward into Central Texas late Wednesday June 1 and Thursday June 2, meandered over the area Friday June 3, then dropped southward to South Texas on Saturday June 4. Deep Gulf moisture contributed to the efficient rain producing thunderstorms associated with the system, creating flood and flash flood issues across mostly central and southern portions of the region. Details: BELL County Emergency Management reported that a few water rescues were ongoing in the city of Temple, TX. Bell County Emergency Management reported minor flash flooding of a few homes in Temple, and that several roads in the city of Belton, TX were closed due to flood waters. Hamilton County Sheriff's Department reported flash flooding along Pecan Creek, as well as along FM 221 and Hwy 281 southwest of Hamilton. Reported property and crop damage: about $241,000.

title: Heat: California, Jun 19, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heat, from June 19, 2016 to June 20, 2016. Affected areas: Coachella Valley, San Diego County Deserts, San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: A strong ridge of high pressure cranked up temperatures over the region. Daily high temperatures were 15 to 20 degrees above average on the 19th and 20th. Details: Three hikers were airlifted from 3 Sisters Falls Trail near Julian due to heat related illness. The Palm Springs ASOS reported a high temperature of 122 degrees, one shy of the all time record. Borrego Springs State Park reached 122 degrees, tying the all time record for the site.

title: Wildfire: California, Jun 19, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from June 19, 2016 to June 30, 2016. Affected areas: San Diego County Valleys. Episode summary: The Border Fire started June 19th, in the middle of a intense heatwave. The fire burned several thousand acres and multiple structures before it was contained. Details: The Border Fire began from unknown causes on the 19th of June. A local couple was killed on their property by the fire. Five structures and eleven outbuildings were destroyed, with one other home suffering damage. The fire also destroyed numerous power and phone lines. Firefighters acquired 100% containment on the fire June 30th, after 7,609 acres had been burned. Reported property and crop damage: about $4,000,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 27, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 27, 2016 to June 27, 2016. Affected areas: Terrell. Episode summary: An upper level ridge was centered over the Four Corners Region and an upper low was just west of the Pecos River. There was a lot of moisture in the atmosphere which contributed to heavy rain and flash flooding across West Texas. Details: Heavy rain fell across Terrell County and produced flash flooding fifteen miles south of Sheffield. Six to twelve inches of water was reported running over State Highway 349 at Independence Creek. No damage was reported.

title: High Wind: California, Jun 22, 2016
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from June 22, 2016 to June 24, 2016. Affected areas: Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: Low pressure moving southeastward from the Pacific Northwest moved into central California region creating gusty winds in the Kern County desert and mountain areas with highest winds across Kern County Desert. Details: Mojave AWOS (KMHV) reported sustained wind speed of 45 mph and a maximum wind gust of 62 mph on 6/22 at 2320 PST. Affected areas: Bowie, Camp, Cass, Franklin, Harrison, Marion, Morris, Red River, Rusk, Titus, Upshur, Wood. Episode summary: A significant winter storm affected the northern half of Northeast Texas on Sunday, January 9th. This storm system moved out of the Texas Hill Country late on January 8th and moved into the Southern Plains and Lower Mississippi Valley during the day Sunday, January 9th. An area of low pressure at the surface and in the lower levels of the atmosphere developed offshore the Southeast Texas Gulf Coast and remained offshore the Louisiana Gulf Coast during the day of the event. This low pressure system helped to feed moisture into the region from the south. Initially, the lower levels of the atmosphere were very dry, but lift provided by the storm system helped to moisten and cool the lower levels of the atmosphere such a combination of freezing rain, sleet and snow were the result across the northern half of Northeast Texas. The transition from freezing rain and sleet to all snow was fairly quick during the morning of January 9th across the region. The storm system exited the region late on January 9th but not before dumping some impressive freezing rain, sleet and snowfall totals across the southern half of the state. Generally, one quarter to one half inch of freezing rain and sleet was reported initially across the northern half of Northeast Texas with the snow being the predominant precipitation type during the afternoon and evening of January 9th. title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Jan 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from January 01, 2011 to January 01, 2011. Affected areas: Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green, Iowa, Jefferson, Kenosha, Milwaukee, Sheboygan, Walworth. Episode summary: Deep low pressure of 993 mb crossed Lake Superior into southeast Ontario, taking a cold front across southern Wisconsin. A combination of a tight pressure gradient around the low, with 3-hourly pressure rises of 2 to 3 mb, and clearing skies behind the front during the day, allowed for deep boundary layer mixing. This mixing tapped 30-40 knot (35 to 46 mph) winds just off the surface, which produced strong and gusty southwest winds. Sustained wind speeds reached 30 to 35 mph, with gusts between 35 and 45 mph during the morning and into the early afternoon hours. Scattered power outages were noted in newspapers due to wind-broken tree branches impacting power lines. Reported property and crop damage: about $38,000.

title: Frost/Freeze, Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow: California, Jan 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Frost/Freeze, Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, from January 01, 2011 to January 04, 2011. Affected areas: Monterey, North Bay Interior Valleys, North Bay Mountains, Santa Cruz. Episode summary: A strong storm system from the Gulf of Alaska affected the San Francisco and Monterey Bay areas from January 1st through January 4th. This system brought strong gusty winds and heavy rain to the area. Details: At approximately 3:30 a.m. PST on January 1, 2011 State Route 29 was closed from St. Helena (Napa County) to the Napa/Lake County line due to snow. The roadway reopened at 7:12 a.m. PST on January 1, 2011. A large tree fell on an occupied vehicle causing the closure of State Route 183 in the Monterey Area at approximately 9:21 p.m. PST. title: Drought: Texas, Feb 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from February 22, 2011 to February 28, 2011. Affected areas: Foard, Hardeman, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: Several months of below normal precipitation continued to wreak havoc on north Texas' agriculture. Summer and fall crops, hay forages, and alfalfa were hit hard by the lack of any significant precipitation. Farm pond water levels continued to decrease, or dry up altogether, which added insult to injury for area livestock. The extent of the damage was still undetermined monetary, but it was beginning to look like a total loss for many Texas farmers.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jan 02, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 02, 2011 to January 02, 2011. Affected areas: Kenedy. Episode summary: A very dry atmosphere, increasingly dry and somewhat cured fine fuels (grasses) which were in vast quantity due to the high growth through the first nine months of 2010, and moderate winds allowed a spark from a passing train to blossom into a large conflagration on the King Ranch in Kenedy County on January 2nd. Several smaller fires also started in the Lower Rio Grande Valley, with limited spread due to rapid containment and control. Details: Emergency Management called in from Willacy County were notified of a rapidly growing wildfire in south central Kenedy County just west of Highway 77 near Rudolph. Before it was over, more than 7,000 acres of ranchland burned. title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Jan 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from January 22, 2011 to January 22, 2011. Affected areas: Brooks, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Zapata. Episode summary: Canadian high pressure settling over the Rio Grande Valley overnight on the 21st and into the morning of the 22nd allowed maximum radiational cooling near the surface, dropping temperatures into the upper 20s to mid 30s across all of Deep South Texas. Several hours of freezing temperatures occurred from Zapata through Kenedy County during the early morning of the 22nd. Details: Temperatures fell to a morning low of 29 degrees on January 22nd in Sarita and Armstrong in Kenedy County. Based on similar observations from across Deep South Texas, most areas on the King Ranch were assumed to have five hours of freezing temperatures from 3 to 8 AM. Temperatures fell to a morning low of 29 degrees on January 22nd. Based on surrounding observations, most areas in Brooks County were assumed to have five hours of freezing temperatures from 3 to 8 AM. Temperatures fell to a morning low of 29 degrees on January 22nd in Falfurrias, 33 miles east but typically similar, if not warmer, than much of Jim Hogg County. Based on surrounding observations, most areas in Jim Hogg County were assumed to have five hours of freezing temperatures from 3 to 8 AM.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 08, 2011 to March 31, 2011. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Dickens, Garza, Hall, Kent, King, Motley, Stonewall and 2 more areas. Episode summary: An extended dry period over west Texas, as well as much of the state, resulted in the emergence of Severe (D2) to Extreme (D3) drought during the month of March. By the 8th, Severe (D2) drought had developed over portions of the southern Rolling Plains. The drought deepened and expanded over the region through the month, and by month's end Severe (D2) drought encompassed most of the western South Plains, the Rolling Plains and the extreme southeastern Panhandle, with Extreme (D3) drought developing over the southern Rolling Plains (including King and Stonewall Counties) by the 29th. ||Although the drought developed during the region's typical cool and dry season, rainfall for many areas of the South Plains region has barely approached one inch between October (2010) and March (2011). These totals amount to two to four inches below normal and rank as one of the driest October to March periods on record fro the region. Keetch-Byram Drought Index values ranged between 500 and 600 by the end of March. ||Through March, the impact of drought was already evidenced in increased wildfire activity. Impacts on agriculture, the area's primary economy, were minimal through March. However, area crops were beginning to show signs of stress as winter wheat crops were beginning to suffer. It was evident that if rain did not occur during April, wheat crops would be severely impacted and cotton planting would be delayed.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 13, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 13, 2011 to March 13, 2011. Affected areas: Floyd. Episode summary: A large wildfire ignited near Farm to Market Road 1065 in extreme northeastern Floyd County during the late evening hours of the 13th. The fire sparked, and spread rapidly, following the passage of a cold front which brought sustained northerly winds of 20 mph to 25 mph. The Texas Forest Service reported that 750 acres burned in the fire. No damages were reported.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 10, 2011 to March 10, 2011. Affected areas: Floyd, Motley. Episode summary: Warm, dry, and breezy weather contributed to the development of two large fires in Motley and Floyd Counties. The first fire developed around 12:30 CST near Flomot (Motley County). This fire grew to burn approximately 700 acres before it was contained around 15:00 CST. A second fire ignited southwest of Floydada around 13:30 CST and burned an estimated 300 acres. No significant damage was reported.

title: Drought: Texas, Jan 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from January 01, 2011 to January 31, 2011. Affected areas: Brown, Crockett, Irion, Kimble, Mason, Menard, San Saba, Schleicher, Sutton. Episode summary: A favorable La Nina Pattern resulted in severe drought conditions across portions of the Northwest Hill Country and the Northern Edwards Plateau. However, the drought improved across Brown, Irion, Mason, Menard, San Saba, and Schleicher Counties by early January as beneficial rainfall fell in December. According to the Texas crop weather report issued January 19 and 25 by the Texas A&M agriculture program, the following agricultural impacts were noted across the drought stricken counties of West Central Texas: extremely cold, dry and windy conditions continued. All counties needed rain to keep winter pastures and crops going. Extremely dry conditions continued to take a toll on wheat and oats. Small grain crops were complete failure in some areas. There was very little field activity due to dry soils. Producers increased Supplemental feeding of livestock as range land and pasture conditions continued to decline. Details: According to the US Drought Monitor, Crockett County experienced severe drought conditions. According to the US Drought Monitor, Sutton County experienced severe drought conditions. According to the US Drought Monitor, Kimble County experienced severe to moderate drought conditions.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jan 02, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 02, 2011 to January 02, 2011. Affected areas: Deaf Smith. Episode summary: The Pheasant Hunters 2 Wildfire began around 1313 CST about nine miles west of Hereford Texas in Deaf Smith county. The wildfire was reported to be under control around 1820 CST and was located near County Road 6 and County Road L. The wildfire consumed an estimated four hundred and fifty acres, and no structures were threatened or damaged. However, a 2003 Ford Expedition command vehicle including equipment were destroyed in the wildfire, and there was also one reported injury. Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jan 08, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 08, 2011 to January 08, 2011. Affected areas: Hutchinson. Episode summary: The Conoco Wildfire started around 1547 CST about six miles north northeast of Borger Texas in Hutchinson county. The wildfire was located just east of Plemmons Road and just southeast of the County Road V split and was contained by 2200 CST. The wildfire consumed three hundred and fifty-six acres. Although two homes and two other structures were threatened, there was no report of damages or injuries.

title: High Wind: California, Jan 14, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from January 14, 2011 to January 14, 2011. Affected areas: San Bernardino And Riverside County Valleys - The Inland Empire. Episode summary: A Santa Ana event caused areas of gusty winds in the mountains. Winds were blamed for playing a role in 3 fatalities. Details: Moderately high winds, estimated between 40 and 50 MPH, were blamed for downed power lines and a subsequent transformer explosion which killed three residents in the 5400 block of Acacia Avenue in San Bernardino, CA. The residents went outside to see what caused the explosion and a few small spot fires from sparks, and were electrocuted trying to extinguish the fires and help each other. title: High Wind: California, Jan 20, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from January 20, 2011 to January 20, 2011. Affected areas: Santa Ana Mountains And Foothills. Episode summary: A high pressure ridge built along the west coast, along with high pressure building over the great basin, set up a pattern favorable for moderate to strong Santa Ana winds across southwest California. Details: High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0830 and 0930 PST, during which time a peak gust of 74 MPH was measured. High winds ended between 1730 and 1830 PST.

title: High Wind: California, Jan 23, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from January 23, 2011 to January 23, 2011. Affected areas: San Diego County Mountains, Santa Ana Mountains And Foothills. Episode summary: North to Northeast winds behind a trough of low pressure over Arizona and surface high pressure over the Great Basin brought moderate to locally strong offshore winds through and below canyons and mountain passes. Details: High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0230 and 0330 PST, during which time a peak gust of 64 MPH was measured by the spotter. High winds ended between 0530 and 0630 PST. title: Tornado: Texas, Jan 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from January 09, 2011 to January 09, 2011. Affected areas: Jim Wells, Nueces. Damaging straight line winds affected most of the Coastal Bend and extended well into the Gulf of Mexico east of Rockport. Widespread wind damage was observed across the Coastal Bend as the storms moved quickly through the region. Approximately 30,000 customers lost power as a result of the storms. title: Drought: Texas, Feb 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from February 01, 2011 to February 28, 2011. Affected areas: Anderson, Comanche, Delta, Falls, Freestone, Hamilton, Henderson, Hopkins, Lamar, Leon, Milam, Rains and 2 more areas. Episode summary: Drought conditions improved during the early part of February due to precipitation from three winter storms, but then conditions deteriorated near the end of the month from lack of significant rainfall. During the latter half of the month, severe to extreme drought conditions began expanding. Drought conditions were the worse over the eastern and southeastern counties of north Texas during the month. Extreme drought (D3) as defined by the US Drought Monitor persisted across the southeast for much of the month. Twenty-five counties had Burn Bans during the month. The only portion of the county not classified in severe drought was the far western tip of the county. title: Cold/Wind Chill, Heavy Snow, Ice Storm, Strong Wind, Winter Storm: Texas, Feb 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Cold/Wind Chill, Heavy Snow, Ice Storm, Strong Wind, Winter Storm, from February 01, 2011 to February 04, 2011. Affected areas: Bell, Collin, Comanche, Cooke, Dallas, Delta, Denton, Eastland, Ellis, Erath, Fannin, Grayson and 18 more areas. The first winter storm began late on January 31st and ended during the morning hours of February 1st. A strong cold front blew through the region ushering in very cold air ahead of an approaching upper level system. Before the snow began, periods of rain, freezing rain, and sleet provided a sheet of ice underneath the snow. At times, thundersleet was observed. The highest snowfall totals fell across the northwestern counties of the CWA where 5-8 of snow was reported. Elsewhere, up to 3/4 of ice and 2 of sleet were reported in some counties. The combination of winter precipitation types resulted in hazardous conditions across much of the region. To make things worse, the cold air stayed in place for the next 3-4 days and another winter storm affected the region a few days later on the 3rd-4th. Schools and businesses were shut down for days and rolling blackouts were needed on the 2nd to account for the extreme demand on the state's electricity grids. The winter storm also affected airports across north Texas, and the economic toll from the winter storms and cold air was large due to the fact that this was the week leading up to Superbowl 45 in Arlington. title: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather, from February 03, 2011 to February 04, 2011. Affected areas: Anderson, Collin, Dallas, Delta, Denton, Ellis, Fannin, Henderson, Hopkins, Hunt, Kaufman, Lamar and 6 more areas. Episode summary: The second winter storm of the week brought heavy snow to most of the eastern and northeastern counties of north Texas. However, much of the area received at least some snow. The heaviest snowfall totals were measured in the far northeastern counties where 6-9 of snow was reported. North Texas was still crippled from the prolonged cold spell that had arrived earlier in the week, and therefore the impacts from this snow event were minimal. Details: Around 2 of snow and a little amount of sleet fell across the county. A one vehicle rollover accident on TX 19 between Montalba and Bois d'Arc due to the slick roads injured two people. Snowfall totals ranging from 4-7 fell across the county. The COOP Observer in Frisco reported a snowfall total of 5, but public reports of 6 in Wylie, Farmersville, and McKinney, and 7 in Anna and Melissa were also received. Six and a half inches of snow was also reported about 3 miles north of Princeton. An unknown number of injuries were reported due to broken bones from falling on ice. Snowfall totals of 5-8 were reported around the county. Up to 8 of snow was reported in the Cedar Creek Lake area. In Canton, a total of 7-8 of snow was reported. In Terrell and Mabank, over 6 of snow was reported. In Forney, about 5-6 of snow was reported. Many minor vehicle mishaps were reported on the snow covered roads. Reported property and crop damage: about $402,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Feb 28, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from February 28, 2011 to February 28, 2011. Affected areas: Grayson. Episode summary: A strong upper level disturbance combined with an advancing dryline/front to produce a line of storms across north Texas during the evening hours. Details: Slick roadways are believed to be the cause of a fatal accident on FM 1753. A man riding a motorcycle lost control on the wet road and slid off the road. He died while en route to the hospital.

title: Strong Wind: Texas, Jan 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, from January 09, 2011 to January 09, 2011. Affected areas: Hardin, Jefferson, Orange. Episode summary: A powerful low pressure system moved across the northwest Gulf of Mexico during the morning and early afternoon hours on January 9, producing numerous showers and thunderstorms across southeast Texas. After the precipitation moved east of the region, a wake low event caused strong east to southeast winds with measured wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph at many locations. Scattered reports of damage were received in Jefferson, Orange, and southern Hardin counties. Details: Entergy reported widespread power outages throughout the county. The KFDM-TV mesonet measured wind gusts of 45 mph or higher at many stations between 1200 PM CST and 100 PM CST, with a peak wind gust of 53 mph at Lamar University in Beaumont. A TCEQ monitoring station in Port Arthur measured a peak wind gust of 52 mph. The KBPT ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 49 mph at 1218 PM CST. Entergy stated up to 4000 customers lost power across Jefferson County, and th Entergy reported widespread power outages in and around Lumberton. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Heavy Rain, Tornado: Texas, Mar 19, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, Tornado, from March 19, 2011 to March 19, 2011. Affected areas: Hale, Lubbock. Episode summary: A series of three supercell thunderstorms impacted the central South Plains of west Texas during the late afternoon and evening hours of the 19th. The initial storm erupted near the intersection of a dryline and warm front over Hockley and Lubbock Counties shortly before 17:00 CST. This storm quickly became supercellular, and produced large hail and a brief tornado as it tracked east-northeastward over southern Hale and Floyd Counties. Additional supercells developed near the same surface features through the evening hours. One storm produced a swath of damaging hail over portions of Lubbock County, including near Shallowater where very large hail up to the size of baseballs was reported. Details: Storm spotters reported that locally heavy rainfall associated with the severe storms resulted in water which briefly covered portions of Farm to Market Road 597 west of Abernathy. Skywarn storm spotters and chasers observed a brief tornado northeast of Abernathy shortly after 18:00 CST. Witnesses described a funnel cloud that extended three-quarters of the way to the ground beneath a ragged wall cloud. Dust was seen rotating on the ground beneath the visible funnel. No damage was reported.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 23, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 23, 2011 to March 23, 2011. Affected areas: Hale. Episode summary: A wildfire ignited in heavy grassland fuels just east of Hale Center (Hale County) around 15:00 CST on the 23rd. Although winds were light, breezy and very dry conditions on the 22nd contributed to an enhanced curing of fuels on the 23rd. Relative humidity values around 10 percent and temperatures in the 70s helped to promote rapid fire spread in these fuels. The fire started when a resident attempted to burn a trash pile along Farm to Market Road 1914. The fire escaped in the parched fuels and destroyed two storage sheds when it ran more than 200 acres. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Blizzard: Wisconsin, Feb 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Blizzard, from February 01, 2011 to February 02, 2011. Affected areas: Green, Lafayette, Rock. Episode summary: A powerful low pressure center, passing south of Wisconsin, produced blizzard conditions across much of southern Wisconsin from the evening hours of Tuesday, February 1st into the early morning of Wednesday, February 2nd. Snow associated with the system began in the mid-afternoon hours of February 1st in far southern Wisconsin and became heavy as it pushed northward into the state through the evening. Very strong winds were associated with this storm for an extended period of time. Sustained winds of 30 to 40 mph were common through the event, with peak wind gusts between 45 and 55 mph. The combination of high winds and heavy snow created whiteout conditions with visibilities falling to near zero. Twenty-four hour snowfall totals were between 14 and 15 inches. In addition to the blizzard, several inches of snow fell on Jan 31. It's possible that some locations did not see a break in snowfall between the evening of January 31st and the morning of February 2nd. Many cooperative observer stations set records for multi-day snowfall totals. Beloit tied a record with a one-day (2/1) snowfall of 15 inches, is tied for second place with two-day (1/31-2/1) total of 17.0 inches and tied for fifth with a three-day (1/31-2/2) snowfall of 17.0 inches. Snow drifts of 3 to 8 feet were common, with reports of some drifts reaching 12 to 15 feet in open rural areas. Many area school districts dismissed classes early on February 1st, and remained closed on the 2nd and 3rd. A Civil Danger Warning was issued by Wisconsin Emergency Management concerning the dangerous driving conditions. Interstate 43 from Beloit to Mukwonago was closed, as well as portions of Interstate

title: Blizzard: Wisconsin, Feb 01, 2011
text: on February 1st, and remained closed on the 2nd and 3rd. A Civil Danger Warning was issued by Wisconsin Emergency Management concerning the dangerous driving conditions. Interstate 43 from Beloit to Mukwonago was closed, as well as portions of Interstate 90, with many stranded motorists having to be rescued from vehicles buried in the drifting snow. About 100 National Guardsman were mobilized statewide in response to Gov. Scott Walker's emergency declaration for 29 counties to help rescue motorists and run emergency shelters at armories. Rock County sheriff deputies had to abandoned their squad cars and jump into National Guard Humvees and Army trucks, which also got stuck in the deep drifts. Wisconsin DNR snowmobiles also became stuck in the deep snow. A 66-year old Janesville man was hospitalized for hypothermia after he fell and was subsequently buried by snow from a snow plow before being found by a neighbor a dug out of the snow bank 4 hours later. The blizzard conditions prevented firefighters from reaching a house fire in Gratiot (Lafayette County) until conditions improved enough for a plow to clear the road. The house was a total loss. Alliant energy reported 7,263 customers in the Milton-Edgerton area were without power at the height of the storm.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Feb 01, 2011

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Dust Storm, High Wind, Wildfire, from February 27, 2011 to February 28, 2011. Episode summary: Strong mid level winds at the base of a passing upper trough resulted in widespread windy conditions across the region, in addition to near 0 mile visibilities in blowing dust. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, from January 31, 2011 to January 31, 2011. Affected areas: Clay, Hardeman, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: A powerful winter storm began to take shape during the evening hours of the 31st and continued into the 1st of February. Most of the accumulating snow occurred on February 1, but thunder-sleet and snow did affect many locations in northern Texas after dark on the 31st, causing significant travel disruptions. Accumulations were minimal early on, but continued to deteriorate as the night progressed. A more thorough write-up is included in the February 2011 Storm Data entry. Details: Light thunder sleet, freezing rain, and snow developed over northern Texas during the mid evening hours. The winds increased to over 40 mph, creating hazardous driving conditions. The majority of the winter storm occurred on 2/1.

title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2011 to March 31, 2011. Affected areas: Hidalgo, Jim Hogg, Starr, Zapata. Episode summary: Dry conditions continued across portions of Deep South Texas in March. The dry conditions intensified to severe drought (D2) conditions across western and southwestern portions of the Rio Grande Valley in early March. A bout of showers and a few storms ahead of a cold front on the 5th would temporarily drop Jim Hogg and Zapata County out of D2 conditions by the 8th. Details: The dry conditions continued across Hidalgo County in March. Severe (D2) drought conditions developed across the southwestern one half of Hidalgo County the first week of March, then spread across all of Hidalgo County by the 22nd and begin intensifying at the end of the month. Dry conditions continued across Starr County in March. The severe (D2) drought conditions increased to include all of Starr County during the first week of March, would slip back to the eastern two thirds by the 15th after rains on the 5th, but recover to all of the county by the 22nd and intensify by the 31st as heat and wind continued to increase. Dry conditions across Zapata County continued in March. Severe (D2) drought conditions developed across all of Zapata County during the first week of March.

title: Drought: Texas, Mar 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 22, 2011 to March 31, 2011. Affected areas: Brooks, Jim Hogg, Zapata. Episode summary: A continued lack of significant rainfall resulted in the spread of the severe D2 drought conditions across the western and central portions of Deep South Texas the later portions of March. Details: A lack of rainfall across all of Deep South Texas increased the severity of the drought conditions across the western and central portions of the Rio Grande Valley during the latter half of March. Severe D2 drought conditions developed again across all of Zapata County by the 22nd, and would continue and intensify by the end of the month as heat and low humidity dominated. A lack of rainfall across Deep South Texas resulted in the Severe D2 drought conditions spreading across the Brush Country region during the latter half of March. Severe D2 drought conditions developed across all of Jim Hogg County beginning on the 22nd, and would continue/intensify through the end of the month. A lack of rainfall across Deep South Texas resulted in an increase in the areal coverage of the severe D2 drought conditions across the entire Brush Country region by the latter portion of March. Severe (D2) drought conditions developed across the western one tenth of Brooks County by the 22nd, and would spread through the western one-half of the county by month's end.

title: Flood, High Wind, Winter Storm: California, Jan 02, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, High Wind, Winter Storm, from January 02, 2011 to January 03, 2011. Affected areas: Fresno, Indian Wells Vly, Kern, Kern Cty Mtns, Madera, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Tulare, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: The new year (and decade) began with the latest in a series of Pacific storms that stretched back to December 17th, 2010. This storm brought strong, gusty winds to the region, especially to the base of the Grapevine, where gusts up to 89 mph were recorded on January 2nd. Snow fell on both the Grapevine and Tehachapi Pass, closing both routes between the San Joaquin Valley and southern California. Unlike the storms in December, this storm was focused more on Fresno, Kings, and Tulare counties, Fresno recorded 1.51 inch of rain on January 1st-2nd, while Bakersfield only received 0.16 inch. This was a cold storm, with the snow level falling to around 2500 feet. With the San Joaquin Valley floor and the lower foothills saturated from the record rains of the latter half of December, flood watches were posted for the New Year���s Day holiday weekend.||As the night of January 1st-2nd progressed, wind gusts to 50 mph were recorded in the far south end of the San Joaquin Valley, at the base of the Grapevine. Over an inch of snow had fallen in Squirrel Valley--at 2700 feet in the hills above Lake Isabella--by 9:45 PM. The winds at the base of the Grapevine continued through the 2nd, with a peak wind of 89 mph recorded during the afternoon. Several roads on the San Joaquin Valley floor flooded due to runoff from locally heavy rains onto the saturated ground. In the Tehachapi Mountains, heavy snow closed Interstate 5 over the Grapevine (a total of 8 inches of snow

title: Winter Weather: California, Jan 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from January 10, 2011 to January 10, 2011. Affected areas: S Sierra Foothills, Tulare Cty Foothills. Episode summary: Once the early January storm passed through the region, persistent high pressure, along with a fairly strong inversion layer above the area began to set up by the 3rd. This initially created foggy conditions by the evening of the 3rd throughout the central and southern San Joaquin Valley, albeit patchy in nature.||With abundant standing water on the San Joaquin Valley floor, dense fog developed during the night of January 4th-5th. The fog lifted into a stratus layer that blanketed the San Joaquin Valley during the afternoon of the 5th, with the stratus persisting through the night of the 8th-9th.||Locations in the mountains rose to above normal temperatures, while those in the San Joaquin Valley remained consistently below normal, or from the upper 30s to lower 40s, even into the daylight hours during the period from the 4th through the 9th.|An upper-level trough that moved through California, on the 8th-9th, had little impact on the stratus, other than to raise the bases of the clouds. This resulted in the stratus spreading into the Southern Sierra Nevada foothills, creating areas of fog. Temperatures in the foothills fell below freezing during the morning of January 10th, and moisture from the fog froze to create icy road surfaces.

title: Winter Weather: California, Jan 30, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from January 30, 2011 to January 30, 2011. Affected areas: S Sierra Mtns. Episode summary: The persistent ridge of high pressure finally gave way to a low pressure system that originated from the Gulf of Alaska by the early morning hours of the 30th, when snow began to fall on the higher elevations of the southern Sierra Nevada. Some locations received several inches of snow from the early morning until the following evening. A brief break from the generally warmer and dry conditions above the valley floor and the persistent fog and stratus over the San Joaquin Valley finally commenced. Windy conditions occurred in the desert areas in eastern Kern County, with reports of wind damage to power poles, as a result of this low on the 30th. This low trekked across central California during the afternoon and evening on the 30th, and instability was enough for a few afternoon thunderstorms to develop in areas of the southern San Joaquin Valley that briefly received sufficient solar radiation. As a result of this convection, some areas received over half an inch in a period of around an hour and a half. This low moved out of the area by the evening of the 30th, and a cooler airmass remained over the region into the last day of the month.||Prevailing high pressure during most of this month allowed the region to realize below normal precipitation throughout the central California interior and warmer than average temperatures above the persistent inversion layer, or above the valley floor. title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Apr 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from April 10, 2011 to April 10, 2011. Affected areas: Eau Claire. Episode summary: A strong early Spring cold front moved across eastern Minnesota during the afternoon of Sunday, April 10th. Ahead of this cold front, strong southerly winds and instability made for a moderate risk of severe weather based the Storm Prediction Center and atmospheric dynamics. After 2 pm, a few supercells developed rapidly from Red Wing, Minnesota, northward across Menomonie and Rice Lake, Wisconsin. These supercells rapidly became severe and started to produce large hail. One of the thunderstorms produced two EF-1 tornadoes near Augusta. These storms quickly moved out of west central Wisconsin by 6 pm. Details: An EF-1 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 95 to 105 mph occurred from approximately 5 miles southwest of Augusta, to 3.5 miles southwest of Augusta, Wisconsin. Two farmsteads were directly impacted with severe tree damage around the homes. One farmstead had their garage completely destroyed along with a barn heavily damaged. An EF-1 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 90 to 100 mph, occurred along a path from northwest of Augusta to north of Augusta, Wisconsin. Numerous trees and power poles were snapped, along with an outbuilding destroyed, and three other outbuildings significantly damaged. Reported property and crop damage: about $450,000.

title: Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind, Storm Surge/Tide, Strong Wind: California, Feb 15, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind, Storm Surge/Tide, Strong Wind, from February 15, 2011 to February 17, 2011. Affected areas: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, North Bay Interior Valleys, Northern Monterey Bay, San Francisco, San Francisco Bay Shoreline, Santa Cruz, Sonoma. Episode summary: After a prolonged warm and dry spell a strong low pressure trough made its way out of the Gulf of Alaska and into California. This trough began the series of cool weather systems that produced six consecutive days of precipitation in the San Francisco Bay Area and the central California coast. Damaging wind, locally flooding rain, intense hail and even moderate snowfall above 1500 feet were experienced during the first wave of this series. Details: Gusty wind caused a tree to fall onto the westbound connector of State Route 4 to westbound Interstate 80 at approximately 5:05 a.m. PST. The roadway reopened at 7:00 a.m. PST. After four days of rain with over seven inches falling in the higher terrain, the Willow Brook Creek swelled beyond its banks causing minor flooding along its channel. The stream gages at Old Redwood Highway and Penngrove Park went over their flood stages. Heavy rain drenched San Francisco causing storm drains to back up which resulted in minor flooding throughout the city. The Public Utilities Commission reported 25 minor floods at various locations. Nineteen of those floods occurred at intersections and six occurred at homes or businesses. Reported property and crop damage: about $610,000.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Feb 20, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from February 20, 2011 to February 20, 2011. Affected areas: Dane, Iowa, Jefferson, Milwaukee, Waukesha. Episode summary: Surface low pressure tracked from eastern Iowa to just south of Chicago producing a winter storm with a mixed-bag of precipitation types and wind gusts of 22 to 33 knots (25 to 34 mph) that affected South Central and Southeast Wisconsin from February 20th into early February 21st. Visibilities were reduced to around 1/2 mile. Only those counties bordering Illinois escaped the storm. The counties of Iowa, Dane, Jefferson, Waukesha, and Milwaukee picked up about 1/4 inch of ice due to freezing rain, and followed this with 1/2 to 1 inch of sleet and then light snow of 1/2 to 1.5 inches. Maximum sleet and snow accumulations were 2 inches in Mazomanie (Dane Co.), 3.0 inches in Watertown (Jefferson Co.), 5.4 inches in Merton (Waukesha Co.), and 7.2 inches in Brown Deer (Milwaukee Co.). The precipitation north of these counties was mostly snow.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, from February 03, 2011 to February 04, 2011. Episode summary: South Texas experienced frigid temperatures and prolonged hard freezes between Tuesday morning February 1st and Saturday morning February 5th, 2011. A large dome of arctic air plunged southward across South Texas on Tuesday morning February 1st behind a strong cold front. Arctic high pressure continued to push further south across South Texas between Wednesday February 2nd and Friday February 4th. As a result, widespread record low temperatures occurred between February 2nd and 5th. Most areas averaged between the middle 20s to middle 30s during this entire period. The duration of freezing temperatures for this event was quite remarkable. ||These very cold temperatures set the stage for one of the more significant ice storms to affect South Texas in recent history. A strong upper level disturbance approached South Texas on Thursday February 3rd. This disturbance along with increasing Gulf moisture above the cold arctic air helped to produce freezing drizzle by early Thursday evening. Freezing drizzle and light freezing rain then continued through all of Thursday night before ending Friday morning. A brief mix of sleet and snow did occur at times during this event across the Brush Country and northern Coastal Bend. However, little to no sleet or snow accumulation was observed during this event. Ice accumulations on the other hand were significant across much of South Texas. Generally 1/4 to 3/8 of ice accumulations occurred across the Coastal Bend and eastern Brush Country with up to 1/10 ice accumulation across the remainder of South Texas. This amount of ice produced very dangerous driving conditions. As a result, state and local

title: High Wind, Wildfire: Texas, Apr 29, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, Wildfire, from April 29, 2011 to April 29, 2011. Affected areas: Bailey, Garza, Hockley, Lubbock. Episode summary: A potent storm system lingered over the western U.S. on the 29th, but strong wind fields in advance of the system overspread west Texas during the afternoon hours. The strong downslope winds promoted hot and dry conditions and extremely critical fire weather. A few damaging wind gusts occurred during the late afternoon. At 15:33 CST the Preston Smith International Airport's Automated Surface Observing System near Lubbock recorded a peak gust of 68 mph. Several minutes later an intense wind gust caused damage to a Texas Forest Service greenhouse near Idalou (Lubbock County). A second severe gust of 62 mph was recorded by the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet near Muleshoe (Bailey County) at 15:40 CST. ||The winds and associated hot and dry conditions combined with the ongoing drought to result in several wind-driven wildfires. A fire sparked approximately four miles southwest of Justiceburg (Garza County) at around 10:30 CST and burned 750 acres before it was contained by 13:30 CST. Fire re-ignited at the site of a significant wildfire the previous evening (4/28) near Pep (Hockley County). This re-start burned an additional 3,000 acres (4,500 acre two-day total), but no additional property damage was reported. At approximately 14:30 CST a fire spread and consumed two trailer homes and two outbuildings near Idalou (Lubbock County). One man was left homeless and a firefighter suffered minor injuries battling the blaze. The fire developed as extremely critical fire weather interacted with a small burn area that was lit in violation of a burn ban the previous day (4/28). title: High Wind: California, Apr 25, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 25, 2011 to April 26, 2011. Affected areas: Antelope Valley, Santa Barbara County Mountains, Santa Barbara County South Coast. Episode summary: Strong and gusty northwest to north winds developed across sections of Southwestern California. The strongest northwest winds developed across the Antelope Valley with gusts at high as 67 MPH reported. Strong north winds developed across the Santa Ynez Range (in Santa Barbara County) with sustained winds of 40 MPH reported. Details: The RAWS sensor at Las Flores Canyon reported north winds with a sustained speed of 40 MPH. The ASOS sensor at Lancaster reported west to northwest winds with sustained speeds between 40 and 49 MPH and gusts between 58 and 67 MPH.

title: High Wind: California, Apr 29, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 29, 2011 to April 30, 2011. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Barbara County Mountains. Episode summary: Strong and gusty northerly winds developed across the Santa Ynez Range in Santa Barbara County and the Los Angeles County mountains. Sustained winds in excess of 40 MPH and gusts in excess of 65 MPH were reported. Details: Strong north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Los Angeles County. Mill Creek RAWS reported wind gusts between 58 and 60 MPH. the Chilao RAWS reported sustained winds 40-44 MPH with gusts 58-61 MPH. The Camp Nine RAWS sensor reported wind gusts between 58 and 71 MPH. Strong northerly winds developed through the Santa Ynez Range. The Montecito RAWS sensor reported sustained winds between 40 and 48 MPH with gusts between 59 and 72 MPH.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Mar 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from March 09, 2011 to March 09, 2011. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green Lake, Iowa, Marquette, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Sauk, Sheboygan, Washington and 1 more areas. Episode summary: Surface low pressure developed rapidly ahead of a strong short wave trough and moved south of Wisconsin from west central Illinois to just south of Chicago. A shield of precipitation spread over southern Wisconsin the night of March 8th with forcing from warm air advection ahead of the low, and continued through the morning of the 9th as the low crossed northern Illinois. The thermal structure associated with the storm was such that the rain/snow line bisected the Milwaukee/Sullivan County Warning Area. Locations along and northwest of a Fond Du Lac to Madison line saw snowfall accumulations of 3 to 5 inches, with isolated spots seeing more than 5 inches. To the east of this line, 2 to 4 inches of snow was common. The tier of counties right along the Illinois border only received 1 to 2 inches of snow, as most of the precipitation fell as rain. Details: A mix of rain and snow began around midnight on March 9th and changed over to all snow overnight. Snowfall totaled between 4 and 5 inches across the county. A cooperative observer near Holy Hill recorded 4.8 inches of snow. A mix of rain and snow began around midnight on March 9th gradually changed over to all snow overnight. Snowfall totaled between 3 and 4 inches across the county. A mix of rain and snow gradually changed over to all snow overnight on March 9th. Snowfall totaled between 2 and 4 inches across the county. A cooperative observer on the northwest side of MIlwaukee recorded 4.1 inches of snow.

title: Ice Storm: Texas, Feb 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, from February 09, 2011 to February 09, 2011. Affected areas: Victoria. Episode summary: Freezing rain was reported in several areas across Victoria County. Accumulations on some bridges reached 1/8.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Feb 25, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from February 25, 2011 to February 26, 2011. Affected areas: Jim Wells. Episode summary: A wildfire in Jim Wells County burned 4800 acres near Highway 281 and CR 418, forcing the evacuation of some residents near Premont. 45 homes were threatened and saved. Four outbuildings were destroyed.

title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2011 to March 31, 2011. Affected areas: Duval, La Salle, Mcmullen, Webb. Episode summary: Severe drought conditions across La Salle and Webb counties intensified to extreme drought conditions by the end of March. By the end of the month, severe drought conditions had expanded into portions of Duval and McMullen counties. No measurable rainfall had fallen in Laredo since January 15th. Fire danger and poor agriculture conditions continued to be the main impacts.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 17, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 17, 2011 to March 17, 2011. Affected areas: Jim Wells. Episode summary: A wildfire burned 300 acres in Jim Wells County, near U.S. 281 and CR 418. 12 homes were threatened and an additional 20 smaller structures, forcing the evacuation of residents. Two sheds were destroyed.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2011 to April 30, 2011. Affected areas: Bee, Calhoun, Duval, Goliad, Jim Wells, La Salle, Live Oak, Mcmullen, Victoria, Webb. Episode summary: Extreme drought conditions across La Salle and Webb counties continued through April, and expanded into McMullen and Duval counties. By mid-month, severe drought conditions had developed across Jim Wells, Live Oak, Bee, Goliad, Victoria and Calhoun counties.||No measurable rainfall had fallen in Laredo since January 15th. Only 0.01 fell at Corpus Christi and only 0.03 at Victoria. Fire danger and poor agriculture conditions continued to be the main impacts. Several wildfires and critical fire weather days occurred during April. Many crops were showing signs of stress. Planting of other crops continued to be delayed. Many farmers lost there first cutting of hay due to lack of rain. Rangeland and pastures further declined. Ponds continued to be very low. Livestock producers continued to supplement feed for cattle with hay. Cattle, swine, sheep and goat prices were at an all time high.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 04, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 04, 2011 to April 04, 2011. Affected areas: Webb. Episode summary: A wildfire on a critical fire weather day burned 27 acres. Seven homes and one business were destroyed in El Cenizo. 50 additional homes and one business were threatened. Around 150 people were evacuated. Winds were gusting to 45 mph and relative humidity values were around 13 percent at the time of the fire.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 06, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 06, 2011 to April 06, 2011. Affected areas: Duval. Episode summary: A wildfire burned 450 acres in Duval County near CR 263. No structures were threatened.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 27, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 27, 2011 to April 28, 2011. Affected areas: Duval. Episode summary: A wildfire burned 1500 acres in Duval county, near CR 266, on a critical fire weather day. Eight homes were threatened and saved. Four out buildings were destroyed.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind: California, Mar 24, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind, from March 24, 2011 to March 27, 2011. Affected areas: Monterey, North Bay Interior Valleys, Santa Cruz, Sonoma. Episode summary: A series of systems affected the San Francisco and Monterey Bay areas with heavy rain and strong winds. title: Flood: California, Mar 02, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from March 02, 2011 to March 02, 2011. Affected areas: Sonoma. Episode summary: A deep low pressure trough brought heavy rain to the area which led to flooding in Sonoma County. Strong orthogonal winds enhanced the precipitation over the mountainous areas. Details: Green Valley Road, west of Sullivan in the town of Graton was closed due to flooding. Mark West Station Road, at Starr Road in the town of Windsor was closed due to flooding.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 25, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from April 25, 2011 to April 25, 2011. Affected areas: Angelina, Bowie, Cherokee. Episode summary: A stationary frontal boundary remained anchored across north Texas into eastern Oklahoma during the morning hours and throughout the day of April 25th. The areas to the south and east of the frontal boundary remained moderately unstable with very strong shear in the lower levels of the atmosphere as well as the mid levels of the atmosphere. The combination of strong shear, good instability along with an upper level disturbance moving across the southern plains resulted in an outbreak of strong to severe thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced large hail, damaging thunderstorm wind gusts and isolated tornadoes. Details: An EF0 tornado touched down along Richardson Road northwest of Lufkin, Texas and moved eastward. Minor roof damage occurred to a mobile home at Royce Oliver Road and Richardson Road and several trees were blown down. Another home suffered minor roof damage and more trees were blown down at the FM 706/Hwy. 69 intersection. This tornado was a continuation of the tornado that moved out of Cherokee County, Texas. A high end EF1 tornado began in extreme southeast Cherokee County, Texas just north of the Neches River where it caused roof damage to a home along CR 2829 and blew down several trees.
