title: Flood, High Wind, Tornado: California, Mar 18, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, High Wind, Tornado, from March 18, 2011 to March 20, 2011. Affected areas: North Bay Interior Valleys, San Francisco Bay Shoreline, Sonoma. Episode summary: A series of weather systems bringing heavy rain, strong winds, high surf, and a tornado affected the District on March 16-21, 2011. Two deaths occurred during this time. Details: An EF1 tornado completely destroyed a metal building and severely bent a metal gate. Reports indicate that as many as fourteen sailboats and one houseboat floated free in Richardson Bay during the event with some becoming beached off Strawberry Point. At 10:20 pm Saturday night a huge oak tree, six feet in diameter, fell onto a SUV killing a 46 year-old man. Reported property and crop damage: about $185,000.

title: High Wind: Wisconsin, May 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: High Wind, from May 09, 2011 to May 09, 2011. Affected areas: Barron, Chippewa, Dunn, Eau Claire. Episode summary: A complex of thunderstorms developed across east-central South Dakota the early morning of May 9th, and moved eastward across southern Minnesota and into west-central Wisconsin by mid to late morning hours. A strong pressure gradient developed as the thunderstorm complex collapsed and created a wake low which produced damaging non-thunderstorm winds. Damage was confined to large trees near Rice Lake, Eau Clarie, and near Bloomer, Wisconsin. Details: One eight inch diameter pine tree, plus several large limbs were blown down due to strong post-thunderstorm winds. This occurred around the Sand Creek area. Time is approximate due to strong winds for several hours. Several large pine trees, up to 24 inches in diameter, were blown down in the wake of a large thunderstorm complex that moved across the area during the late morning. This occurred in the Rice Lake, Wisconsin area. Time is approximate due to strong winds for several hours. Several large white pines, up to 70 feet high, were blown down due to strong winds in the wake of a thunderstorm complex that moved across the area. This occurred around the Eau Claire, Wisconsin area. Time is approximate due to strong winds for several hours. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Mar 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from March 22, 2011 to March 22, 2011. Affected areas: Vernon. Episode summary: Rain fell across much of southwest Wisconsin during the evening of the 22nd and in some locations temperatures dipped below freezing to create icy roads. One fatality occurred on State Highway 27 in the southern part of Vernon County. A total of three accidents were reported across the county. Details: One person was killed in an accident on State Highway 27 in the southern part of the county when a car slid off an icy road. Rain fell across the region during the evening and in some locations the temperature dipped below freezing to create the icy conditions. A total of three accidents were reported across the county. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Mar 20, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from March 20, 2011 to March 28, 2011. Affected areas: Crawford, Jackson, Trempealeau, Vernon. Episode summary: The combination of melting snow and some rainfall helped to push some western Wisconsin rivers out of their banks during the latter part of the month. Details: The combination of rainfall and melting snow pushed the Trempealeau River at Dodge out of its banks. The river exceeded the flood stage from the 21st into the 27th. The river crested almost four feet over the flood stage at 12.75 feet. The combination of rainfall and melting snow pushed the Kickapoo River at Viola out of its banks. The river exceeded the flood stage from the 23rd into the 24th. The river crested over a foot above the flood stage at 15.24 feet. The combination of rainfall and melting snow pushed the Black River at Black River Falls out of its banks. The river exceeded the flood stage from the 20th into the 23rd. The river crested about a foot and a half over the flood stage at 48.35 feet.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 26, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 26, 2011 to April 26, 2011. Affected areas: Harrison, Panola, Rusk, Smith, Wood. Episode summary: A very volatile atmosphere developed during the late afternoon...evening and overnight hours of April 26th across the Four State Region. An area of low pressure moved from the Texas Hill Country into Northeast Texas during the afternoon. Meanwhile, a warm front had moved northward from central Louisiana and was oriented west to east near the Arkansas/Louisiana state line. A dry line had moved just east of the I-35 corridor of North Central Texas and a strong cold front trailed the dry line. Very strong speed and directional shear was noted in the low and mid levels of the atmosphere such that supercells developed. Many of these produced tornadoes across the region. Other storms produced strong straight line wind gusts with bowing segments and large hail. Details: This tornado was a continuation of the tornado that moved out of extreme northwestern Panola County and into extreme southern Harrison County. This tornado continued to snap several trees before lifting as it crossed Hwy. 43. Winds were estimated at 86-95 mph. A few trees were snapped at their base and had large limbs broken off with the initial touchdown along FM 2625 just west of Highway 59. The tornado continued northeast paralleling FM 2625 causing sporadic tree damage until it reached the intersection of FM 2625 and Taylor Road. title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Mar 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from March 22, 2011 to March 23, 2011. Affected areas: Ashland, Bayfield, Burnett, Douglas, Price, Sawyer, Washburn. Episode summary: Deepening low pressure over Colorado on the morning of March 22nd went straight east, reaching the Chicago area on the morning of March 23rd. Meanwhile, strong high pressure over southern Hudson Bay was feeding very dry, dense air from northern Ontario southward across Lake Superior into northwest Wisconsin. Substantial snow, accumulating 7 to 12 inches, remained south of the Lake Superior coast, south of a line from Dairyland, Cable, and Glidden. Strong winds, gusting to 50 mph, occurred across the the area during the afternoon and evening of March 22nd and into the early morning of the 23rd.

title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2011 to March 31, 2011. Affected areas: Archer, Baylor, Clay, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: The ongoing severe drought, D2, increased to D3, over northern Texas. Much of the state of Texas continued with another month of below normal precipitation. In some cases, only a few hundredths were recorded for the entire 31 days. Since Thanksgiving, much of northern Texas has seen its driest precipitation totals since the 1920s and 30s. Much of the wheat crop planted in the fall had all but been declared a total loss. In fact, the conditions have gotten worse with the emergence of the wheat crop. The lack of precipitation has made for low water levels on stock ponds for livestock, and the water level in irrigation reservoirs used for crops is falling. Fire weather has been a major concern, with thousands of acres burning throughout the month. The exact monetary number for the crop loss can not be determined, although it would probably be in the millions.

title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2011 to March 31, 2011. Affected areas: Brown, Crockett, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Kimble, Mason, Mcculloch, Menard, San Saba, Schleicher, Sterling and 2 more areas. Episode summary: A strong La Nina has caused the severe to extreme drought conditions to expand across West Central Texas through March. Precipitation estimates indicated that many locations across the area were approximately 6 to 12 inches below normal in rainfall since last October. ||As warm, dry and windy conditions continued to deplete soil moisture, wildfire was a big|concern in all areas. Dry land wheat remained in poor condition due to lack of moisture, but irrigated fields were doing well.

title: High Wind: Texas, Mar 07, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from March 07, 2011 to March 07, 2011. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: A broad area of zonal flow extended across the U.S. with an approaching shortwave trough moving out of Southern California and into Southern New Mexico. This trough combined with an associated cold front to bring strong winds to the eastern slopes and mountain passes of El Paso County. Details: The peak gust at Chapin High School in Northeast El Paso was 71 mph. Other reports included 70 mph at a National Weather Service employees residence in Northeast El Paso, and 66 mph at the El Paso International Airport.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Apr 19, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from April 19, 2011 to April 19, 2011. Affected areas: La Crosse, Monroe. Episode summary: An area of low pressure tracked from Kansas into lower Michigan from April 19th into the 20th. Enough cold air was in place across western Wisconsin for the precipitation from this system to fall as snow. Some of this snow was locally heavy with amounts in excess of 6 inches. The highest reported totals were 9 inches southwest of Warrens (Monroe County) and 8.3 inches at the La Crosse National Weather Service office (La Crosse County). Details: Snowfall amounts generally were in the 5 to 7 inch range. The highest reported total was 9 inches southwest of Warrens. Snowfall amounts ranged from 3 to 6 inches for locations in the river valleys. The highest reported total was 8.3 inches at the La Crosse National Weather Service office, which is located on a ridge top.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 07, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 07, 2011 to April 07, 2011. Affected areas: Hidalgo. Episode summary: Temperatures soaring to the upper 90s and humidity dropping to the mid to upper 30s combined with parched grass and brush, and sustained 20 foot winds near 20 mph with gusts between 25 and 30 mph to rapidly spread a small wildfire in Hidalgo County during the afternoon of April 7th. Details: A wildfire quickly spread to 35 acres in the Baullion area of Hidalgo County during the afternoon of the 7th, threatening four homes which were saved by local fire fighters. One firefighter was injured.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 11, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 11, 2011 to April 11, 2011. Affected areas: Hidalgo. Episode summary: A volatile combination of strong winds, extremely low humidity, illegal trash burning, and a stash of old tires produced a 10 acre fire in Alton, along Mile 8 1/2 North Road and Moorefield Road. The fire forced the evacuation of nearly 200 homes, damaged two structures, and produced acrid, pitch black smoke and fumes for several hours starting around noon on April 11th. Details: A 10 acre wildfire, known as the Alton-Moorefield Fire on Moorefield Road between Farm to Market (FM) 107 and FM 1925 in Alton, Hidalgo County, spread rapidly from grass and brush into a five-acre tire dump. At least 190,000 tires burned, with northerly winds of 20 to 30 mph, rapidly falling humidity below 15 percent, extremely dry grass and brush, and temperatures rising into the upper 90s durin Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: High Wind: California, Mar 07, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from March 07, 2011 to March 07, 2011. Affected areas: Coachella Valley. Episode summary: A strong westerly jet and associated shortwave trough moved quickly over the region accompanied by strong winds in the mountains and deserts, along with light rain over the coastal areas. Details: High winds began in the Coachella Valley between 0750 and 0850 PST, during which time a peak gust of 72 MPH was measured by the Whitewater RAWS. High winds ended between 1350 and 1450 PST. A downed power pole closed a portion of Indian Canyon Road and a tractor trailer overturned near the intersection of Interstate 10 and Highway 111, but no injuries reported. Reported property and crop damage: about $7,500.

title: Heavy Snow, High Wind: California, Mar 20, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, High Wind, from March 20, 2011 to March 21, 2011. Affected areas: Apple And Lucerne Valleys, Orange County Coastal Areas, San Bernardino County Mountains. Episode summary: A strong low pressure system dug through southern California, bringing very strong winds, heavy rain and heavy snow, with blizzard conditions in the mountains. Several inches of rain were reported at favored upslope locations. The strongest winds occurred over the high desert where winds exceeded 110 mph at times, causing considerable damage in the Apple Valley area. Behind the front, scattered thunderstorms dropped more rain, periods of hail, and a few waterspouts, but causing only minor urban flooding. Details: Snowfall began in most locations between 1500 and 1600 PST Sunday the 20th. A spotter in Wrightwood reported a storm total of 28 inches, with strong winds blowing all afternoon. A spotter in Running Springs reported a storm total of 20 inches. A spotter in Big Bear City reported a storm total of 15 inches at 6800 feet elevation, with a few inches more at the resorts. High winds began at the Hesperia South mesonet station between 1153 and 1253 PST. High winds ended between 1253 and 1353 PST. During this time, a wind gust of 62 MPH was recorded. A spotter measured a gust of 115 MPH on an anemometer. The gust damaged the anemometer shortly after. Several power poles and trees were knocked down, causing a blackout that lasted nearly 24 hours. Numerous houses sustained roof damage and at lease one house had its roof destroyed. title: Frost/Freeze: California, May 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Frost/Freeze, from May 10, 2011 to May 10, 2011. Affected areas: Central Siskiyou County. Episode summary: An unusually cold air mass combined with clearing skies to bring freezing temperatures to parts of northern California. Details: Reported low temperatures ranged from 24 to 31 degrees.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 04, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 04, 2011 to March 04, 2011. Affected areas: Carson. Episode summary: The Charless Ranch Wildfire began nine miles north of Pantex Texas in Carson County around 1500 CST. The wildfire caused no damages or injuries and consumed an estimated two thousand and five hundred acres. The fire was contained around 1700 CST and was caused by electrical failure.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 09, 2011 to March 09, 2011. Affected areas: Lipscomb. Episode summary: The Texas Forest Service reported that the Double D Wildfire began five miles north of Glazier Texas in Lipscomb County around 1440 CST. The wildfire caused the residents of thirty-five homes to be evacuated and fifty outbuildings were threatened. The wildfire consumed an estimated three hundred and thirty-one acres and was reported to have a one mile wide front. There were no reports of damages and no injuries. The wildfire was contained around 1853 CST. The wildfire was located near SR 305 and the Lipscomb County and Hemphill County lines.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 16, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 16, 2011 to March 16, 2011. Affected areas: Hutchinson. Episode summary: The Bugbee Creek Wildfire began two miles northwest of Sanford Texas in Hutchinson County around 1400 CST. The wildfire threatened three or four homes and also two oil and gas wells. There were no reports of damage or injuries. The wildfire consumed an estimated three hundred acres and is being investigated as arson. The wildfire started just before 1400 CST about two miles north of the Sanford Dam just off Farm to Market Road 687. The wildfire was contained around 1650 CST.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 17, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 17, 2011 to March 17, 2011. Affected areas: Lipscomb. Episode summary: The South of Higgins Wildfire began three miles south of Higgins Texas in Lipscomb County around 1630 CST and consumed an estimated six hundred and forty acres. The wildfire caused no damages or injuries and was contained around 1930 CST.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 19, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 19, 2011 to March 19, 2011. Affected areas: Collingsworth. Episode summary: The Texas Forest Service reported that the Elm Creek Wildfire began five miles south of Shamrock Texas in Collingsworth County around 1420 CST and was caused by lightning. The wildfire consumed an estimated three hundred acres and was contained around 1732 CST. There were no structures threatened or damaged and there were no reports of injuries.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Mar 18, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from March 18, 2011 to March 18, 2011. Affected areas: Howard. Episode summary: A cold front slowly drifting southward into the west Texas Permian Basin interacted with a diffuse dryline to produce slow moving supercells. Severe hail and flash flooding accompanied the storms during the evening hours. Details: At 8:55 PM CST, the broadcast media reported several cars were under water on the west side of Big Spring. About an hour later, the Big Spring Police Department reported several streets were closed due to high water crossing roadways.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, May 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from May 22, 2011 to May 22, 2011. Affected areas: Barron. Episode summary: During the early afternoon of Sunday May 22nd, a line of thunderstorms developed across south central Minnesota, and quickly moved north and northeast across east-central Minnesota, and into west-central Wisconsin. Several of the severe storms produced large hail and damaging winds across west central Wisconsin through the late afternoon hours. Details: An EF-1 tornado touched down just west of the intersection of 28th Avenue and 26th Street. It tracked northeast and dissipated at 30th Avenue. Damage was sporadic along this tornado path, with damages to roofs, a 12 foot house antenna, two seven foot tall horse enclosures, and numerous large trees uprooted and blown down. Reported property and crop damage: about $200,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 26, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 26, 2011 to March 31, 2011. Affected areas: Sutton. Episode summary: A large wildfire swept across Sutton County, south of interstate 10. Details: A wildfire burned 2439 acres. Although the fire threatened three homes, one bunkhouse, one large hunting lodge, six recreational vehicles, all of these structures were saved.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 10, 2011 to March 10, 2011. Affected areas: San Saba. Episode summary: A grassland wildfire developed as a result of very dry, warm air and plentiful fuels. Details: A wildfire burned 400 acres.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 16, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 16, 2011 to April 19, 2011. Affected areas: Garza, Motley. Episode summary: An extended period of critical fire weather persisted for several days following the high winds and Southern Plains wildfire outbreak on 14th and 15th. This episode of critical fire weather resulted in at least two significant fires near Matador (Motley County) during the afternoon of the 16th and in Garza County on the 19th.||A 400 acre wildfire ignited four miles north-northwest of Matador just before 15:00 CST on the 16th. The Texas Forest Service deployed air-attack to stop the blaze. ||On the 19th, a 2,000 acre fire threatened multiple homes near U.S. Highway 82 east of Post in Garza County.||No significant damages or injuries were reported with either incident.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 06, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 06, 2011 to April 21, 2011. Affected areas: King, Stonewall. Episode summary: The massive 'Swenson Fire' ignited during the afternoon hours of the 6th in Stonewall County, north of the Swenson community. The use of a cutting torch during critical fire weather conditions started the blaze, which consumed 122,500 acres before it was finally contained on the 21st. During the fire's 15-day run, it burned into grasslands of adjacent King and Knox Counties. At least nine structures were destroyed. Tragically, a 105-year old cowboy and his wife lost four ranch homes to the fire. The couple, who were uninjured, had lived in Stonewall County their entire lives and as patriarch to six generations of family cowboys on their ranch. The fire destroyed 155 utility poles in Stonewall County and 130 poles in King County. Dozens of cattle were reported killed. Total economic damages were estimated at $2.54 million. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,540,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 11, 2011

title: High Wind, Wildfire: Texas, Apr 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, Wildfire, from April 09, 2011 to April 14, 2011. Affected areas: Crosby, Garza, Hockley, Terry. Episode summary: A potent spring-time storm system impacted the western and central U.S. during the 9th and 10th of April. Strong wind through a deep layer of the atmosphere overspread the Southern Plains on the 9th as the parent storm system initially approached the southern Rockies. The strengthening wind fields overspread pronounced surface heating and drying over the Southern Plains. This resulted in an outbreak of wind-driven wildfires across portions of five states. ||Locally on the South Plains, winds that gusted upwards of 59 mph (Hockely County) contributed to two significant and damaging wildfires. The 'Prentice' Fire ignited in Terry County around midday on the 9th. The fire consumed 15,000 acres and destroyed three outbuildings and at least 50 utility poles. This fire quickly grew to become the massive and long-lived 'Killough' Fire, which eventually consumed 54,000 acres in northern Garza and southern Crosby County before it was contained on the 14th. The 'Killough' Fire destroyed one home and an oil field station. The development of additionally extremely critical fire weather on the 10th resulted in a 20-mile run of the 'Killough' Fire. By 20:30 CST on the 10th the fire threatened 60 homes near White River Lake in southeastern Crosby County and evacuation orders were issued. title: Strong Wind, Tornado: Texas, Apr 14, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, Tornado, from April 14, 2011 to April 14, 2011. Affected areas: Fannin, Tarrant. Episode summary: A powerful, negatively-tilted upper level trough moved into the Central Plains during the late afternoon hours which aided in the development of supercell thunderstorms near the intersection of a cold front and dryline in north central Texas. These storms developed near the Interstate 35 corridor and the Red River during the early evening hours, and then continued south-southeast through the Dallas/Fort Worth Metroplex. These storms primarily produced golfball sized hail, however several reports of damaging winds were reported in Dallas County, likely associated with a microburst in the northeastern portion of the county. Unfortunately, a 5-year old boy drowned on Lake Benbrook in Tarrant County when their boat capsized due to strong winds produced by a nearby thunderstorm. Details: A 5-year old boy drowned on Benbrook Lake after the boat he was in capsized due to strong winds gusting to around 35 mph. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 17, 2011 to April 30, 2011. Affected areas: Bosque, Ellis, Hill, Johnson, Tarrant. However, several rounds of severe weather during the latter half of the month damaged crops and fields. During the month, 33 counties had Burn Bans. title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, May 08, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from May 08, 2011 to May 09, 2011. Affected areas: Western Mojave Desert. Episode summary: A cold Pacific low pressure system brought high winds to the Mojave Desert, along with a few hail-producing thunderstorms. Details: Gusts of 58 mph or higher occurred at the Bicycle Lake (KBYS) ASOS on Fort Irwin from 1631 PST to 2009 PST, with a peak gust of 62 mph at 1921 PST. The California Highway Patrol also reported sand covering one and a half lanes of a road in the area. Strong winds in Barstow blew down a tree and two wooden fences. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,000.

title: Strong Wind: Texas, Apr 04, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, from April 04, 2011 to April 04, 2011. Affected areas: Hunt. Episode summary: A man was injured in Greenville when a metal gate flew open due to strong winds and hit him in the head. Details: A metal gate at an industrial business was flung open in strong winds and struck a vehicle as it was passing. The gate arms went through the front windshield, striking a man in the head and injuring him. Near the time, the local AWOS reported a wind gust of 37 MPH but gusts up to 40 MPH may have been occurring. Reported property and crop damage: about $7,000.

title: High Wind: California, May 25, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 25, 2011 to May 29, 2011. Affected areas: Owens Valley, Western Mojave Desert. Episode summary: A series of unseasonably strong Pacific storms produced spotty high winds in the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Details: The peak gust for this event was 59 mph 4 miles E of Independence. This gust occurred at the Bicycle Lake (KBYS) ASOS on Fort Irwin. The peak measured gust for this event was 63 mph 1 mile SSW of Independence. A helicopter parked in Independence was tossed by the wind late in the evening. Reported property and crop damage: about $250,000.

title: Tornado: California, Mar 21, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Tornado, from March 21, 2011 to March 21, 2011. Affected areas: Colusa. Episode summary: A brief tornado touched down near the town of Maxwell in Colusa County. Details: At approximately 3:05 pm an EF0 tornado touched down in a pasture about 2 miles west of downtown Maxwell. The pasture is located just north of Maxwell Sites Rd., between McDermott Rd. and Danley Rd. There was no damage observed, but several witnesses observed a brief touchdown in the grassy field, which is used as pasture for a herd of buffalo. There were no injuries nor fatalities.

Details: At approximately 3:00 pm an EF0 tornado touched down about a mile WSW of downtown Williams in Colusa County, near the intersection of Hwy 20 and Davis Road. The maximum wind speed of the tornado was estimated at 80 mph with a damage path of three quarters of a mile. The damage path was in an east-northeast direction. No injuries nor fatalities have been reported. The tornado damaged six homes, Reported property and crop damage: about $70,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 12, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 12, 2011 to May 12, 2011. Affected areas: Bexar, Travis, Val Verde. Episode summary: An upper level area of low pressure moved out of the southern Rockies into the plains and combined with a dryline to produce severe thunderstorms on successive days. On May 11th the storms were mainly in the northeastern part of the forecast area. On May 12th they were more widespread starting out west and moving to the east. There were several spottings of possible funnel clouds and even tornadoes near Uvalde and Hondo but a NWS damage survey could not find any tornadic damage. Several pictures and small cell phone videos were inconclusive. Large outflow in front of storms likely caused several small spinup gustnadoes which may explain some of the reports on the leading edge of the storms. Another possible tornado was reported 7 miles south of Giddings along Highway 77. Damage survey did find a damaged barn but no conclusive tornado damage. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain which caused road closures in the north and northeast parts of San Antonio. Episode summary: Low relative humidity values combined with breezy southwest surface winds above 20 mph to produce critical fire weather conditions across the Permian Basin of Texas. Details: Named the Bate's Field Fire, this fire burned 3200 acres and threatened 300 homes, a power plant and a water treatment plant.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 06, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 06, 2011 to April 06, 2011. Affected areas: Andrews. Episode summary: An upper level storm system over the western US helped to contribute to a hot, dry, and windy day across the Permian Basin of Texas. Temperatures were around 20 degrees above normal and relative humidities dropped into the 3-8% range. Winds speeds were above 20 MPH and the fire danger rating was extreme. Due to these factors, a Red Flag Warning was issued for the area. Details: A fire, known as the Texland Fire, occurred in Andrews County and burned 8,000 acres. title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 07, 2011

The winds combined with minimum relative humidity values of 10 percent or less and above normal temperatures, which resulted in the issuance of a Red Flag Warning for all of west Texas. Details: The fire, known as the Sanderson Fire, burned 3,590 acres in Terrell County. One Sheffield volunteer fire department firefighter was injured and 4 structures were threatened.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 12, 2011 to April 30, 2011. Affected areas: Pecos. This gradient allowed for strong southerly winds of 20 to 25 MPH to develop during the afternoon hours. Relative humidity values ranged from the low teens east of the Pecos River, to the single digits west of there. A Red Flag Warning was issued for the area. title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 14, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 14, 2011 to April 21, 2011. Affected areas: Andrews. Episode summary: An approaching upper level trough brought strong west winds across the area of 25 to 35 MPH with gusts of 40 to 50 MPH. Dry air was in place with minimum relative humidity values in the single digits. Critical to extremely critical fire weather conditions were present and a Red Flag Warning was issued for the area. Details: A fire, known as the Frying Pan Ranch, burned 80,907 acres in Andrews County. Numerous homes were threatened by this fire, but all structures were reportedly saved.

title: Strong Wind: Texas, May 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, from May 01, 2011 to May 01, 2011. Affected areas: Goliad. Episode summary: An area of low pressure over the southern plains provided strong south to southeast winds over the coastal plains on May 1st. The winds gusted to near 50 mph at times. Details: A strong wind gust snapped a medium sized tree and blew the roof off of a small shed near the community of Charco. Reported property and crop damage: about $500.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind, Strong Wind: Texas, May 12, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind, Strong Wind, from May 12, 2011 to May 12, 2011. Affected areas: Bee, Nueces, Webb. Episode summary: A large complex of thunderstorms, that developed during the early morning hours south of Del Rio, moved across the entire South Texas region during the afternoon of May 12th. There were several reports of strong winds with these storms and a few reports of small hail. An area of low pressure developed in the wake of the line of storms in the afternoon that produced strong winds over the Coastal Bend. Details: Wind gusts over 50 mph occurred in Corpus Christi in association with a wake low pressure area that developed behind the line of thunderstorms. Wind gusts to 58 and 51 mph occurred respectively at Corpus Christi Naval Air Station and Corpus Christi International Airport. Strong gusty winds, in association with a wake low pressure area that developed behind the line of thunderstorms, downed power lines in the city of Beeville. Spotter reported flooding near Inwood Road and Del Mar Boulevard in Laredo. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 26, 2011

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, May 20, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from May 20, 2011 to May 20, 2011. Affected areas: Brooks. Episode summary: Developing low pressure in the southern Plains helped import very unstable air into Texas, including the Rio Grande Valley and Deep South Texas where afternoon temperatures soared above 100 toward the coast, and heat index values exceeded 110 by late afternoon. Weak low level convergence and a possible afternoon sea breeze enhancement lifted the air mass into large thunderstorms, which developed initially just south of Hidalgo (northern Mexico) then re-formed in northern Hidalgo County. These storms intensified over the Encinitos Ranch (extreme northern Hidalgo into extreme southern Brooks) and continued forming from Encino to Falfurrias, ultimately producing locally heavy rainfall, large hail, and some wind damage across the Brush Country of Brooks County. Details: A re-forming strong to severe storm dropped several inches of rain in less than two hours in rural southern Brooks County, west of Federal Highway 281 and north of Farm to Market 755, west of Encino. title: Winter Storm: California, Feb 17, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Storm, from February 17, 2011 to February 19, 2011. Affected areas: Clear Lake/Southern Lake County, Motherlode/Camptonville To Groveland, Mt Shasta/Western Plumas County, Northeast Foothills/Sacramento Valley, Shasta Lake/North Shasta County, West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A cold winter storm brought additional heavy snow to areas still digging out from a storm that passed through the region just a day or two earlier. Traffic was impacted on major highways and power was lost in many foothill locations. Details: Three to four feet of snow fell at the highest elevations, more than two feet at 7000 feet, and eight to twelve inches fell down to 3000 feet. Five to eight inches of snow fell near 3000 feet with the snow level down to near 1000 feet in some locations. Up to a foot of snow fell near 3000 feet with the snow level as low as 1500 feet in some locations. Power was lost across many foothill locations for several days due to downed trees branches.

title: High Wind, Wildfire: Texas, Apr 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, Wildfire, from April 03, 2011 to April 04, 2011. Affected areas: Garza, Hockley, Terry. Episode summary: Strong southwest to westerly winds accompanied the passage of a strong upper air storm system on the 3rd. The winds combined with very dry air and deepening drought to contribute toward at least three significant wildfires on the South Plains of west Texas.||A 100 acre fire broke out just southwest of Denver City (Yoakum County) around 14:30 CST. The fire threatened at least 80 homes and 150 residents were |evacuated. No structural damages were reported.||By 18:00 CST a second fire had ignited near Justiceburg (Garza County). This fire quickly jumped U.S. Highway 84 and threatened some 400 recreational vehicles and trailer homes near Lake Alan Henry. Firefighters were able to save the properties, but suffered minor damages to several fire trucks. The fire burned approximately 5,000 acres before it was finally contained during the morning hours of the 4th.||Around 19:00 CST a fire began near two abandoned homes north of Smyer (Hockley County). The homes were destroyed, but firefighters were able to contain the blaze at 15 acres.||During the overnight hours, a localized but intense wind gust was observed by the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site near Post. The 68 mph gust recorded at 00:45 CST on the 5th resulted in no damage, and was likely enhanced as winds associated with a passing cold front interacted with local topographical features. ||Total economic losses due to wildfire on the 3rd were estimated at $325,000. Reported property and crop damage: about $325,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 02, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 02, 2011 to April 02, 2011. Affected areas: Yoakum. Episode summary: A wildfire ignited east-northeast of Denver City (Yoakum County) shortly after 16:00 CST on the 2nd. The fire burned 2,000 acreas before it was contained around 19:30 CST. No significant property damages were reported.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 24, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from April 24, 2011 to April 24, 2011. Affected areas: Callahan, Coleman, Shackelford, Taylor. Episode summary: The combination of a stationary east/west front intersecting with a dryline and favorable shear and instability caused severe thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon along mainly the I-20 corridor. The storms produced several tornadoes north of Baird and very large hail in Abilene. As the storms moved southeast into the Heartland, they produced more large hail. Details: A trained spotter reported this tornado briefly touched down. A storm chaser photographed this tornado. The twister broke some mesquite tree limbs. This tornado uprooted some trees.

title: Strong Wind: Texas, Apr 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, from April 03, 2011 to April 03, 2011. Affected areas: Tarrant. Episode summary: An elderly woman in Fort Worth died due to a power outage at her home that left her unable to receive the oxygen she needed to survive. The power outage occurred from a tree that was blown into the power line down the street by strong wind gusts up to 40 mph. Details: An elderly woman on oxygen died during a power outage that was caused by a tree that had blown into the power lines down the street. The woman lived in the west side of Fort Worth. Area automated weather stations recorded wind gusts up to 40 mph on this day.

title: Strong Wind, Wildfire: Texas, Apr 15, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, Wildfire, from April 15, 2011 to April 15, 2011. Affected areas: Grayson, Wise. Episode summary: Strong winds gusting up to 50 mph damaged a 100-year old store in Denison and ripped the roof off the gym at Bridgeport High School. The strong winds also fanned a fire that burned a 100 year-old home outside of Decatur. Details: The Hubbard's Furniture Store in Denison was damaged by strong winds. The winds ripped a 75 foot by 25 foot piece of metal from the front of the building, and sent it sailing into two trucks parked in front of the store. Minor damage was sustained to the trucks. The automated weather station nearby reported peak wind gusts up to 46 mph on this day. Strong winds ripped the roof off the Bridgeport High School gym. A grass fire, fanned by strong winds gusting up to 50 mph, destroyed a 100 year-old, two-story home northeast of Decatur. Reported property and crop damage: about $316,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 01, 2011 to June 30, 2011. Affected areas: Brooks, Cameron, Coastal Cameron, Coastal Willacy, Hidalgo, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Starr, Willacy, Zapata. title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, Jun 18, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from June 18, 2011 to June 18, 2011. Affected areas: Chippewa, Eau Claire. Episode summary: A weak frontal boundary remained nearly stationary across eastern Minnesota and western Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening of Saturday, June 18th. Due to the high water content in the atmosphere, and the relatively slow movement of the thunderstorms, torrential rainfall occurred, and a down burst created wind damage near Eau Claire, Wisconsin. A cluster of thunderstorms developed across western Eau Claire County, and remained nearly stationary with rounds of heavy downpours for nearly two hours. The Eau Claire airport recorded a rainfall amount of 4.74 inches which broke the previous day, monthly, and yearly one day total. A three foot mud slide occurred on the interstate near Eau Claire due to the extreme rainfall amounts in less than two hours. Details: Significant street flooding occurred around the city of Eau Claire, Wisconsin, due to rainfall amounts of four inches in less than two hours. In addition, a three-foot wide mud slide occurred near Mile Marker 63, on Interstate 94 near Eau Claire. It caused portions of the interstate to shut down until the debris was cleared. Roadways and a railroad track in southwest Chippewa County were flooded by torrential rains. Wheaton Township saw the most flooding during the evening.

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 07, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 07, 2011 to June 30, 2011. Affected areas: Brooks. Episode summary: Temperatures near or just above 100 degrees, frequent gusty winds, moderate to low relative humidity quickly erased any short term drought relief provided by mid May rainfall as conditions deteriorated from Severe to Extreme across all of Brooks County for the balance of June. Locally heavy rainfall the final week of the month would bring some relief as July arrived. Details: Severe (D2) Drought conditions deteriorated to Extreme (D3) in all of Brooks County on June 7th, and would continue through the end of the month. Rainfall of more than 2 inches across the southern half of the county would provide a bit of relief at month's end. title: High Wind: Wisconsin, May 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: High Wind, from May 09, 2011 to May 09, 2011. Affected areas: Clark. Episode summary: High winds produced by an outflow from a thunderstorm uprooted trees near Neillsville and Willard in Clark County. Details: Trees were uprooted in Neillsville. Trees were uprooted falling on power lines along County Road I. Reported property and crop damage: about $9,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 21, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 21, 2011 to April 21, 2011. Affected areas: Pecos, Terrell. Episode summary: Isolated thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front April 20, near the Lower Trans Pecos and Stockton Plateau. During the afternoon hours the next day, severe thunderstorms develop within significant low level moisture just ahead of a dryline over Terrell and Pecos Counties. Backed surface winds across Terrell County supported a low level shear near storm environment sufficient enough to produce brief tornadoes. One supercell produced at least 2 tornadoes as it moved across portions of south central Pecos County and into Terrell County. Details: Tornado damage was reported near Sanderson at approximately 17:45 CST. Several cedar trees were destroyed as the tornado tracked east southeast. A home and barn were also destroyed by the tornado. Spotter reports indicate the tornado was 1/2 mile wide and travelled approximately 9 miles. This event location was estimated based on public reports, photos, and radar data. CBS 7 has photos of this tornado available on their Facebook page. No damage was reported with this tornado. It is unclear whether or not this tornado continued its path into Terrell County, where another tornado was reported (with damage) a little over an hour later. The public reported a tornado approximately 20 miles south of Ft. Stockton, west of Highway 285. Photos of the tornado were sent to CBS 7 via Facebook. No damage was reported with this tornado. Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Apr 27, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from April 27, 2011 to April 27, 2011. Affected areas: Ashland, Bayfield, Douglas. Episode summary: Low pressure over Iowa early April 26th moved into the Ohio Valley that night. High pressure over James Bay supplied dry and cold air, causing a weak secondary low to develop along a cold front over the Ironwood MI area before dawn on the 27th. Falling temperatures caused rain to mix with and then change to snow over higher elevations overnight. Heavy wet snow was reported along and north of the first ridge south of the Wisconsin south shore of Lake Superior early on the 27th.

title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 06, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 06, 2011 to April 06, 2011. Affected areas: Lamb, Parmer. Episode summary: Scattered high-based virga showers spread over the extreme southwestern Panhandle and the northwestern South Plains during the late evening hours of the 6th. This weak convection resulted in localized severe wind gusts as measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas and KVII-TV Schoolnet mesonets near Lazbuddie (Parmer County) and Amherst (Lamb County). No damages were reported.

title: High Wind: California, May 29, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 29, 2011 to May 29, 2011. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range. Episode summary: A strong northwest pressure gradient produced some gusty northwest winds across the mountains of Los Angeles county. Northwest wind gusts to 64 MPH were reported. Details: The RAWS sensor at Camp Nine reported northwest wind gusts between 59 and 64 MPH.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2011 to May 31, 2011. Affected areas: Aransas, Bee, Calhoun, Duval, Goliad, Jim Wells, Kleberg, La Salle, Live Oak, Mcmullen, Nueces, Refugio and 3 more areas. Episode summary: Drought conditions became exceptional across La Salle and Webb Counties in May while extreme drought conditions expanded from Duval and McMullen Counties into Jim Wells, Live Oak, Bee, Goliad, Victoria and Calhoun Counties. Severe drought conditions developed over Aransas, Nueces, Kleberg, San Patricio, and Refugio Counties during the early part of the month. ||Although widespread 1 to 3 inches of rain occurred across South Texas on the 12th and alleviated the short term fire danger conditions, the rainfall was easily absorbed by the very dry soils. Overall, little change in the drought status was observed over the region with this rain event. Rainfall deficits for the month remained high with most areas receiving between 25 and 50 percent of normal rainfall for the month of May.||Hot, dry, and windy conditions further stressed crops in the region. Hay production was very limited with livestock producers reducing herds or liquidating herds completely. Rangeland and pastures did not improve significantly with the rainfall. Ponds were either very low or bone dry.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 25, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 25, 2011 to April 25, 2011. Affected areas: Houston, Polk, Trinity. Episode summary: Severe thunderstorms erupted along the dry line with the help of a shortwave aloft and produced large hail, strong damaging winds and tornadoes. Details: Tornado tracked through portions of Davy Crockett National Forest with extensive tree damage in the Moore Cemetery Road area. Damage appeared more concentrated in path described surrounded by area of more scattered wind damage. An EF0 tornado caused little damage at Walkers Waterfront. Tornado destroyed unoccupied mobile home and damaged several others along County Road 3015. Path continued across Route 21 with several large trees uprooted or snapped on a hillside east of Route 21. Reported property and crop damage: about $81,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 26, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 26, 2011 to April 26, 2011. Affected areas: Deaf Smith. Episode summary: Severe thunderstorms developed across the central Texas Panhandle during the mid afternoon and early evening hours. No damages or injuries were reported. Also, a non-thunderstorm wind gust was measured at the Hereford Texas AWOS station located at the Hereford Municipal Airport about five miles east northeast of Hereford Texas.

title: Flood, Winter Storm, Winter Weather: California, Apr 07, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, Winter Storm, Winter Weather, from April 07, 2011 to April 07, 2011. Affected areas: Kings, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: An upper-level trough dropped out of the Gulf of Alaska and approached the California coast on April 6th. This feature brought cooler temperatures, with Fresno down 6 degrees from the 5th, and Bakersfield down 4 degrees. The trough moved over interior central California the next day, bringing gusty winds, scattered mainly afternoon and evening thunderstorms, and much colder temperatures. The high at Fresno on April 7th was only 55 degrees, down 20 degrees from the previous day. Bakersfield had a high of 59 degrees, down 18 degrees from the 6th. There were several reports of one quarter to one half inch hail on the San Joaquin Valley floor. Several inches of snow fell in the Southern Sierra Nevada foothills fell as low as the communities of Bootjack, Oakhurst and Granite Station. Nineteen inches of snow fell at Lodgepole; this was the highest amount reported from either the Southern Sierra Nevada or the Tehachapi Mountains. In the Kern County deserts, winds gusted to 45-55 mph on April 7th behind the cold front. The upper-level low associated with the trough moved to near Point Conception during the afternoon of April 8th. This shifted the focus of precipitation westward, to over the west side of the San Joaquin Valley. Even so, precipitation was mostly light. A deep, cold airmass filled the San Joaquin Valley, and the high temperatures at Bakersfield and Fresno on the 8th were the same as the previous day. Details: Highway Patrol reported flooding on interstate 5 just north of Quebec Avenue. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Apr 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from April 10, 2011 to April 10, 2011. Affected areas: Green Lake. Episode summary: An outbreak of severe thunderstorms, caused by low pressure moving from southwest Minnesota across northwest Wisconsin, produced 10 tornadoes in Wisconsin, which tied a record for the largest number of tornadoes in one day in the month of April in the state. Southern Wisconsin was in the warm sector of the system for most of the day, with a capping inversion preventing thunderstorm development until early in the evening. The exit region of an upper jet helped break the cap, with severe super-cell thunderstorms rapidly developing in an unstable environment, with surface-based CAPE of 2000 J/kg and strong vertical shear. There was one tornado reported in the Milwaukee/Sullivan County Warning Area, an EF0 tornado that tracked across northeast Green Lake County just southeast of Berlin. Severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds in Waukesha and Milwaukee counties. Details: An EF0 tornado developed about 3.5 miles south-southeast of Berlin just south of the intersection of County Road F and County Road AA and traveled northeast about 1.8 miles before dissipating on Meadow Brook Road just east of County Trunk Highway V. title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Apr 15, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from April 15, 2011 to April 15, 2011. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green, Green Lake, Iowa, Jefferson, Kenosha, Lafayette, Marquette, Milwaukee and 8 more areas. Episode summary: Southern Wisconsin was situated between a polar high pressure area centered over southeast Canada and a strong low pressure that tracked from the central Plains toward northwest Illinois during the day on April 15th. The resulting tight surface pressure gradient over the region produced sustained east winds of 25 to 35 mph with peak gusts between 45 and 54 mph over a nearly 12-hour period. Scattered power outages were noted across southern Wisconsin due to broken tree branches falling on to power-lines. Details: Strong east to northeast gradient winds gusted to an estimated 45 mph (39 knots) as southern Wisconsin was between low pressure passing to the west and high pressure to the east. Strong east to northeast gradient winds gusted to 40 mph (35 knots) as southern Wisconsin was between low pressure passing to the west and high pressure to the east. Strong east to northeast gradient winds gusted to 44 mph (38 knots) as southern Wisconsin was between low pressure passing to the west and high pressure to the east. Reported property and crop damage: about $69,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 01, 2011 to April 08, 2011. Affected areas: Brown, Irion, Schleicher. Episode summary: Elevated fire weather conditions persisted April 1st and 2nd. Then on April 3rd, strong southwest winds developed behind the dryline and brought a very dry air mass into the area. This combination of very warm temperatures, very low relative humidities, and strong winds created critical fire weather conditions across a large part of West Central Texas. Details: The Camp Bowie wildfire burned approximately 2955 acres. It threatened 12 homes but none were destroyed. The wildfire burned 341 acres 13 miles north of Barnhart, on the Rocker B Ranch. Also, the fire threatened oil and gas wells in southern Irion County. The fire was 90 percent contained on April 6th. The Harkey Fire consumed 2713 acres in northwest Schleicher County. A welding machine sparked this fire.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 08, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 08, 2011 to April 30, 2011. Affected areas: Coke, Crockett, Menard, Tom Green. Episode summary: Critical Fire Weather Conditions persisted across West Central Texas from April 8 through the 11th with the combination of hot temperatures, dry air, and gusty southwest winds along and west of the dryline. The most critical fire weather conditions occurred on April 10 with strong gusty west winds and relative humidity values of 5 to 15 percent. Details: The Sutton Wildfire was started by arcing power lines. This wildfire burned nearly 31,000 acres. Lightning started a wildfire 7 miles south-southwest of Live Oak. The wildfire burned 581 acres. The Wildcat Fire burned approximately 159,308 acres and was 100 percent contained by the end of April. This fire was located just north of San Angelo and extended north into Coke County. More than 400 homes were saved. The communities of Grape Creek, Quail Valley, Bronte, Robert Lee and Tennyson were threatened. This wildfire caused many evacuations north of San Angelo and also near Robert Lee Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, May 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from May 01, 2011 to May 01, 2011. Affected areas: Tarrant. Episode summary: A prolonged severe weather event began during the early morning hours of May 1st and lasted into the overnight hours of May 2nd. A cold front moved through the northern sections of the Fort Worth County Warning Area, and the initial round of severe thunderstorms occurred north of this boundary during the morning hours of the 1st. These storms produced damaging winds and hail up to the size of baseballs. Additional rounds of severe storms developed north of the boundary during the afternoon and evening hours of the 1st. Little wind damage occurred from these storms but hail up to the size of golfballs were reported. The severe weather primarily affected locations north of a Mills to Ellis to Grayson County line. Details: A truck carrying eight people hit standing water on the eastbound lanes of I-30 and lost control. The vehicle flipped over the guardrail and traveled another 200 feet before stopping. A 20 year old male passenger was killed and 5 others were transported to the hospital. Reported property and crop damage: about $8,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 20, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 20, 2011 to May 20, 2011. Affected areas: Anderson, Fannin, Leon. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms developed across North Texas and primarily produced hail that was less than golfball sized in diameter. There were a couple of reported microbursts as well. Training thunderstorms led to heavy rainfall and isolated reports of flash flooding during the evening hours. Details: Street flooding was reported on Highway 56 just southwest of Bonham. There were several reports of flash flooding extending from the Telephone area southwest to Ivanhoe, and then south to Lake Bonham. Flash flooding was reported within the town of Buffalo and along Highway 75 south of town. Several County Roads also experienced flooding near Highway 75. FM 2539 south of Buffalo had to be closed for a few weeks because a culvert was washed out. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 21, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 21, 2011 to May 22, 2011. Affected areas: Coryell, Lampasas. Episode summary: Several supercell thunderstorms developed along a dryline in the southwestern portions of the Fort Worth County Warning Area. Locations in Mills, Hamilton, Coryell, and Lampasas County were primarily affected. Hail up to the size of grapefruits occurred from these severe thunderstorms. After several rounds of thunderstorms, flash flooding was reported in Lampasas County around Adamsville. Details: A brief tornado occurred approximately 6 miles east of Evant, just north of Highway 84. Some minor tree damage occurred. Several county roads near Adamsville were flooded after creeks exceeded their banks.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 22, 2011 to May 22, 2011. Affected areas: Jack. Episode summary: Numerous supercell thunderstorms developed along a dryline northwest of the Fort Worth County Warning Area and spread east through the evening. A brief tornado damaged trees in Jack County. Hail up to the size of golfballs fell and winds gusted in excess of 60 MPH from these thunderstorms. The severe weather primarily affected locations northwest of a Comanche to Dallas to Bonham line. Details: An EF-0 tornado occurred approximately 9 miles northeast of Jacksboro. This tornado damaged trees with maximum estimated winds around 80 MPH.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 23, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 23, 2011 to May 23, 2011. Affected areas: Dallas, Tarrant. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed near the Metroplex during the late morning hours. These storms produced hail that was mostly nickel to quarter sized in diameter. Heavy rainfall led to some localized flooding in the Metroplex. Details: Four to five inches of water was standing at the intersection of Marsh Ln and Northhaven Rd in Farmer's Branch. There was approximately a foot of water standing on two lanes at Interstate 30 and Green Oaks Blvd.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 24, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 24, 2011 to May 24, 2011. Affected areas: Cooke, Dallas, Denton, Kaufman, Montague, Parker, Tarrant, Wise. Episode summary: Three rounds of thunderstorms affected north Texas with 10 tornadoes confirmed. The atmosphere was highly unstable on this day and a High Risk was issued by the Storm Prediction Center for the northwestern counties of north Texas while a Moderate Risk covered much of the rest of north Texas. A strong upper level disturbance approaching from the west interacted with a dryline across the western portions of north Texas, and the first round of storms began to develop around 330 pm in the western counties. The first two rounds of storms remained along and north of Interstate 20 but the third round of storms later that night moved through most of the region as a line of storms. The most significant tornado occurred in the western limits of the city of Denton where EF-2 damage occurred. An EF-1 tornado also occurred in the city of Irving in Dallas County, and softball sized hail fell in the northern portions of the Metroplex. In the city of Dallas, one person died from electrocution after going outside around live, downed wires after a storm had passed. Details: A brief tornado touched down on the east side of Lake Nocona. No damage was reported with this tornado. Maximum winds were estimated to be 70 MPH with this tornado. A storm chaser videoed a tornado southwest of Gainesville for nearly 4 minutes. The tornado damaged some trees. A brief tornado was reported 2 miles southeast of St. Jo near Highway 82. Some tree damage was reported. This tornado was rated an EF-0 with maximum estimated winds of 70 MPH. Reported property and crop damage: about $913,000.

During the early part of the month, a total of 28 counties had burn bans, but many of the counties had removed the burn bans by the end of the month due to the several days of rainfall. title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 10, 2011 to April 10, 2011. Affected areas: Deaf Smith, Gray, Hutchinson, Potter, Roberts. Episode summary: A Pacific cold front moved across the southwest, central and eastern Texas Panhandle around midday to early afternoon which resulted in strong and gusty west to southwest winds. These high winds did cause some damage in the south central Texas Panhandle, however no injuries were reported. Details: There was a report of a few power poles being blown down near the intersection of Western Street and Olsen Boulevard in Amarillo Texas. No injuries were reported. Reported property and crop damage: about $4,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 14, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 14, 2011 to April 19, 2011. Affected areas: Callahan, Sutton. Episode summary: West winds of 20 to 30 mph with gusts to around 35 mph, combined with hot temperatures and relative humidity values in the single digits resulted in critical fire weather conditions on April 14 over a large part of West Central Texas. Dry and gusty northwest winds behind a cold front on April 15 reinforced the critical fire weather conditions as relative humidity values lowered to around 10 percent. Details: The McPherson fire located 21 miles southwest Sonora has burned approximately 2307 acres. The fire was 90 percent contained. The East Caddo fire located 7 miles south of Admiral burned 300 acres. The fire is 100 percent contained.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 20, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 20, 2011 to April 22, 2011. Affected areas: Mason. Episode summary: Elevated fire weather conditions occurred across the western portions of the Concho Valley and northern Edwards Plateau. The afternoon relative humidities were around 20 percent and the winds were light. Details: This wildfire started due to a lightning strike, 9 miles southwest of Mason. The Three Goat fire burned 453 acres. One home was threatend.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 15, 2011 to April 15, 2011. Affected areas: Donley, Gray, Hemphill, Hutchinson, Ochiltree, Potter, Roberts. Episode summary: A deepening surface low pressure system in eastern Kansas and high pressure building in from the west resulted in very strong and gusty northwest to northerly winds across the central and eastern Texas Panhandle. No damage or injuries were reported.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 25, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 25, 2011 to April 30, 2011. Affected areas: Brown, Concho, Crockett, Haskell, Irion, Kimble, Throckmorton. Episode summary: Critical Fire Weather Conditions occurred on April 25 across much of West Central Texas as a dryline brought southwest to west winds of 20 to 25 mph, relative humidity levels below 20 percent, and temperatures in the 90s. Isolated thunderstorms ignited a large wildfire in Kimble County on April 26. A few of these fires continued through the end of April. Details: The wildfire located 2 miles west of Zephyr burned 500 acres. Also, the fire was located near U.S. Highway 183 near Blanket Creek. The Oasis Pipeline Fire 11 miles south of Junction burned approximately 9445 acres and it was 80 percent contained. There were 11 structures destroyed, including 1 home. Also, 3 vehicles and 1 bulldozer were destroyed, along with numerous power poles and fence line. In addition, 20 head of cattle were lost. Commercial airtankers and four MAFFs tankers helped slow the spread of the fire that came This wildfire burned about 7,000 acres and it was 100 percent contained. Reported property and crop damage: about $350,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 03, 2011 to April 03, 2011. Affected areas: Gray, Hansford, Hartley, Moore. Episode summary: A tight pressure gradient from a surface trough of low pressure to the west of the Texas Panhandle resulted in strong and gusty gradient winds during the afternoon and evening hours across parts of the northwest, central and eastern Texas Panhandle. There were no reports of damages or injuries.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 03, 2011 to April 04, 2011. Affected areas: Ochiltree. Episode summary: The McCarter Wildfire began around 2021 CST about nine miles west southwest of Wolf Creek Park in Ochiltree County which is located off of Texas State Highway 70 and County Road Z. The wildfire consumed an estimated four hundred acres. There were no reports of damages or injuries and no structures were threatened. The wildfire was contained around 0200 CST on April 4.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 09, 2011 to April 10, 2011. Affected areas: Moore. Episode summary: The Crawford Ranch Wildfire began about two miles southeast of Masterson Texas near the Moore County and Potter County line around 1340 CST. The head of the wildfire was at Farm to Market Road 152 and Farm to Market Road 1913 and consumed a measured thirty-five thousand and ninety-seven acres which was mapped using GPS. The wildfire was sixteen miles long and one mile wide and damaged two fire engines and an outbuilding. Six homes were evacuated and six homes were saved. Also, multiple homes in front of the fire were evacuated and multiple oil tank batteries and oil pumps were threatened. The wildfire was contained on April 10 at 0040 CST. There were initially four firefighters injured; three of the firefighters, two from the Dumas Fire Department and one from the Cactus Fire Department, were taken to the Moore County Hospital where they were treated for smoke inhalation and were in good condition. The fourth firefighter, who was with the Cactus Fire Department, sustained third degree burns over more than sixty percent of his body and was airlifted to the burn center in Lubbock Texas. He later died from his injuries on April 20 at 0300 CST. The cause of the wildfire was related to electrical lines; either sparks from the power lines or downed power lines. Reported property and crop damage: about $155,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 09, 2011 to April 10, 2011. Affected areas: Hartley. Episode summary: Two wildfires in Hartley County merged into one wildfire and began around 1600 CST about fifteen miles west of Channing Texas. The wildfire was located near County Road 47 and Farm to Market Road 767 and consumed a measured twelve thousand four hundred and thirty-four acres which was mapped using GPS. There were no reports of damages or injuries and no structures were threatened. The wildfire was contained about approximately 0940 CST on April 10.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 10, 2011 to April 10, 2011. Affected areas: Moore. Episode summary: The Wind Mill Wildfire began around 1322 CST about thirteen miles east of Dumas Texas in Moore County. The wildfire consumed an estimated one thousand acres. The wildfire threatened one home and one other structure but both structures were saved. There were no reports of damages or injuries and the wildfire was contained around 1730 CST.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 10, 2011

Episode summary: The Glazier Wildfire began around 1458 CST about six miles east of Glazier Texas in Hemphill County. The wildfire consumed a measured five hundred and eight acres and was contained around 1800 CST. There were no reports of damages or injuries. Also, there were no structures reported threatened. The wildfire was caused by downed transmission lines.

The wildfire consumed fifty acres, but threatened and destroyed one structure which was an outbuilding. There were no injuries reported and was contained around 1630 CST. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 20, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 20, 2011 to April 20, 2011. Affected areas: Deaf Smith. Episode summary: The Adrian Wildfire began around 1227 CST about eight miles north of Simms Texas in Deaf Smith County. The wildfire threatened one home but that structure was saved. The wildfire did consume an estimated eight hundred acres, however no damages or injuries were reported. The cause of the wildfire was determined to be from transmission lines. The wildfire was contained around 1800 CST.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 26, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 26, 2011 to April 27, 2011. Affected areas: Potter. Episode summary: The Texas Forest Service reported that the Boys Ranch Wildfire began around 1455 CST about three miles northwest of Valley De Oro Texas in Potter County. The wildfire consumed an estimated five hundred acres which burned in tall grasses. There were no evacuations reported and there were no reports of damages or injuries. However, six homes were threatened but were saved. The wildfire was contained by 0900 CST on April 27.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Apr 26, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 26, 2011 to April 26, 2011. Affected areas: Armstrong. The wildfire was caused by lightning. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2011 to April 30, 2011. Affected areas: Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason and 12 more areas. Episode summary: The U.S. Drought Monitor placed most of West Central Texas in an extreme drought for April. According to the Texas Crop Weather Report issued by the Texas A&M Agriculture Program, the following impacts were noted across West Central Texas: hot, dry and windy conditions persisted, range land and pastures were in poor condition, stock water tank levels were critically low, livestock producers had to provide supplemental feeding due to poor foliage quality, and some producers sold livestock in order to decrease stocking rates. This extreme drought also resulted in an extremely high fire danger as soils were extremely dry. For the period from November 1, 2010 to April 30, San Angelo had received 1.83 inches (6.39 is normal), Junction received 1.5 inches (8.5 is normal), and Abilene received 5.69 inches (7.54 is normal). text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 01, 2011 to July 11, 2011. Extreme D3 drought conditions prevailed across all of Kenedy County through July 11th, with t Exceptional D4 drought conditions continued across all of Starr County at the beginning of July. At the beginning of May, Severe (D2) drought in Briscoe and Swisher counties further intensified to Extreme (D3). The remainder of the South Plains, Rolling Plains, and southern Texas Panhandle saw additional amplification of Extreme (D3) and Exceptional (D4) drought.||Moisture typically increases through May but May, 2011 saw continued insignificant rainfall for the region. Rainfall since November 2010 ranged from under one tenth of an inch at Plains (Yoakum County) to nearly two inches at Friona (Parmer County), Plainview (Hale County), Tulia (Swisher County) and Guthrie (King County). Most other locations around the region experienced close to an inch of rainfall during this period. These totals were about two to six inches below normal over the South Plains and six to eight inches below normal over the Rolling Plains. In addition, temperatures throughout the month of May ranged from five to eight degrees above normal. title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 01, 2011 to June 30, 2011. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Exceptional (D4) drought conditions continued to persist across the entire South Plains, Rolling Plains, and southern Texas Panhandle regions. June, on average, is among the wettest periods of the year for the Southern Plains. However, June 2011 saw deepening rainfall deficits with a spring thunderstorm season failing to develop. Zero percent of normal rainfall was observed over a large part of the region. Only a few stations have recorded over two inches of rainfall on the year with Paducah the only site recording over three inches of rainfall. No measurable rainfall fell at Lubbock International Airport which is only the second time in 100 years of record that has occurred. Most of the area measured between 10 and 25 percent of normal annual rainfall.||The historic drought was made worse by a June heat wave. A very strong upper level high settled over the region in early June resulting in record heat. Many cities around the region recorded the warmest month on record. Temperatures throughout the month of June averaged between 8 to 11 degrees above normal. The city of Paducah had a maximum temperature of 118 degrees on June 26th tying its all time record high. This was two degrees behind the all-time record high for the state of Texas. Childress also tied their all time record high temperature of 117 degrees on June 26th. Keetch-Byram Drought Index values ranged between 600 and 800 across the region by the end of June. title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2011
text: Keetch-Byram Drought Index values ranged between 600 and 800 across the region by the end of June. Strong winds with afternoon relative humidities often below 10 percent lead to many days with extreme fire weather concerns.||The drought's impact on wildfire activity continued into June with several wildfires initiated by dry high-based thunderstorms. This wildfire activity extended beyond the region's climatological wildfire season which typically subsides with seasonal green-up in April and May. Nearly 60,000 acres of land were burned by wildfires within the Lubbock CWA (County Warning Area) during the month of June. Agricultural impacts accelerated across the region as farmers struggled to irrigate dry fields. All crops were becoming a major loss by the end of June and were severely impacting the local economy. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from July 08, 2011 to July 08, 2011. Affected areas: Smith.
