Details: The Smith County fire department responded to a fire on County Road 272 in Chapel Hill that got out of control. The fire was started purposely as a burn pile in a resident's back yard. With the county suffering under extreme drought conditions, the fire quickly spread to other properties adjacent to the resident. The fire consumed 3 trailers, a vehicle and a boat. There were no report of inju Reported property and crop damage: about $120,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 15, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 15, 2011 to April 15, 2011. Affected areas: Hardeman, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: Strong, gusty winds developed during the afternoon hours over northern Texas on the 15th, as a strong low pressure moved into the southeast United States and a strong high pressure moved south through the Plains. No precipitation occurred with the gusts, with a couple of wind gusts exceeding 60 mph. Details: Sheppard Air Force Base measured a non-thunderstorm wind gust of 63 mph. The Goodlett Mesonet site measured a non-thunderstorm wind gust of 61 mph. Local media also estimated a wind gust of 60 mph in Quanah. The Vernon AWOS measured a non-thunderstorm wind gust of 59 mph.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 11, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado, from May 11, 2011 to May 12, 2011. Affected areas: Bell, Cooke, Coryell, Mclennan, Tarrant. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a dryline during the early afternoon hours. These storms consolidated into a couple of linear mesoscale convective systems that produced wind damage mainly north of the Interstate 20 corridor. During the evening hours, storms consolidated into a long quasi-linear convective system across the CWA. Isolated reports of large hail and wind damage occurred during the evening hours as well as heavy rainfall which led to localized flash flooding. Two EF-0 tornadoes also occurred on this day; one in Cooke County and the second in Tarrant County. Details: Fort Hood officials closed roads on base due to flood waters flowing over base roadways. Some of these locations were Tank Destroyer Blvd, West Range Road at Turkey Run Creek, House Creek, 37th Street at South Range Road, 68th St at Battalion Avenue and part of West Range Road. Also on the base, four homes in Comanche II housing experienced minor flooding. Residual flooding of several streets and areas on the Fort Hood Air Force Base continued for several hours after the storms had ended. Water was flowing up to 1 foot in depth over a few streets in Temple. Reported property and crop damage: about $323,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Jul 05, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 05, 2011 to July 31, 2011. Affected areas: Cameron, Coastal Cameron, Coastal Willacy, Hidalgo, Jim Hogg, Starr, Willacy, Zapata. Episode summary: Rainfall adding up to more than 8 inches in portions of southern Cameron, southwest Cameron/southeast Hidalgo, and pocket of Willacy County, as well as respectable rainfall totals between 2 and 6 inches across the remainder of the Rio Grande Valley and portions of the Brush Country and King Ranch of Deep South Texas continued to reduce the level of drought. Starting July 5th, all of Deep South Texas saw drought reduced by one to two categories, from Extreme/Exceptional (D3/D4) to Severe/Extreme (D2/D3). Details: The beneficial rains which moved across the Rio Grande Plains between June 30th and July 2nd, combined with other rains from June 22nd, finally improved the drought conditions a little bit across Zapata County the first full week in July. Extreme (D3) Drought conditions prevailed across all of Zapata County with the exception of the extreme northwestern tip of the county which still had Exception The beneficial rains which moved across the mid and upper Rio Grande Valley July 1st and 2nd, combined with rain on June 22nd, finally began miproving drought conditions in Starr County the first full week in July. Extreme (D3) Drought conditions replaced Exceptional (D4) conditions during the first full week of July. The beneficial rains which moved across the Deep South Texas Brush Country June 22nd, and again on July 1st and 2nd, finally helped improve drought conditions a little bit in Jim Hogg County. Extreme (D3) Drought conditions replaced Exceptional (D4) conditions which had plagued the County for most of June.

title: High Wind: California, May 08, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 08, 2011 to May 09, 2011. Affected areas: Coachella Valley. Episode summary: Deepening low pressure aloft and strong onshore flow brought gusty winds to southern California, mainly in the mountains and deserts. These winds toppled several trees and at least one power pole, which resulted in a small brush fire in Palm Springs. Details: Heavy winds knocked over a power pole around 1530 PST on the 9th near Stevens Road and Via Monte Vista, according to the Palm Springs Fire Department. Winds were gusting in the middle 50s at many nearby sensors during the day. The power pole fell into a vacant lot where it started a small brush fire, which was contained within a half hour and did not spread beyond that lot. Power was out for aroun Strong winds took down 35-40 trees at the Rancho Mirage Public library between late Sunday (8th) and early Monday (9th). The trees were mature, 15 to 20 foot tall mesquites and palo verdes. Nearby Thousand Palms recorded a wind gust of 40 MPH at 0300 PST Monday, while Thermal airport recorded a gust of 53 MPH at 2300 PST Sunday. No other damage was done to the library and no one was injured. Reported property and crop damage: about $30,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Cold/Wind Chill, from May 17, 2011 to May 19, 2011. Affected areas: Coachella Valley. Episode summary: A low pressure trough and associated front moved through southern California each morning of the 17th and 18th. Rainfall was fairly significant for these systems, bringing around a half inch of rain to areas west of the mountains and up to an inch on some coastal slopes. Light snow even fell at the highest mountain elevations above 5000 feet. Strong onshore flow with gusty winds also accompanied these storms, however there were only a few gusts that reached advisory criteria in the mid-50s MPH, and no damage was reported. With the frontal passages, however, came record low max and min temperatures for numerous Southern California stations, such as Oceanside, Palomar Mountain and El Cajon. A few single day precipitation records were also set. Details: On each of the 17th and 18th, numerous record low temperatures (both max and min) were set in the Coachella Valley. Palm Springs and Thermal both broke records on May 18, previously set in 1994 with high temperatures of 76 and 77 respectively. text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 28, 2011 to May 29, 2011. Affected areas: Apple And Lucerne Valleys. Strong onshore flow also brought gusty winds to most areas, especially the mountains and deserts. These winds were responsible for several downed trees and power poles/lines. The storms produced locally heavy rainfall, estimated by radar to be in excess of 1.5 inches. At 330 pm, Park and Forest service personnel reported flash flooding at Pinto Wye and near 49 Palm Oasis in the park. Flooding prompted the closure of the north entrance to the park.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jun 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from June 09, 2011 to June 09, 2011. Affected areas: Zapata. Episode summary: The combination of extremely dry soils, hot temperatures, locally gusty winds, and low humidity contributed to the rapid spread of two wildfires in Zapata County on June 9th. On the 9th, as with many days before and after, temperatures soared above 100 degrees, afternoon humidity fell below 20 percent, and winds gusted in excess of 25 mph, especially after 4 PM which is likely when each reported fire grew explosively. Details: A wildfire grew rapidly to 400 acres on the Henry Garza Ranch, 13 miles east of the City of Zapata, during the late afternoon of June 9th before being rapidly contained shortly after sunset. One house and three oil facilities were threatened and saved by Zapata County and City fire crews. Otherwise, the fire affected only grassland. A wildfire rapidly spread to 1,200 acres of range land, which burned from 4 PM until midnight at the Barberio Ranch and Loma Blanca Vela Ranch, 11 to 13 miles south of Zapata. Grasses and mesquite were blackened by the blaze, but no structures were threatened. Livestock damage information was unavailable at the time of this writing. title: Tornado: Texas, Jun 20, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from June 20, 2011 to June 20, 2011. Affected areas: Stephens. Episode summary: A strong summertime trough dug into the Plains with an attendant dryline and cold front moving into north Texas. Two rounds of storms affected north Texas beginning the evening of the 20th and continuing into the early morning hours of the 21st. The first round of storms developed in association with the dryline as it reached the western edges of the CWA. The second round of storms developed along the cold front as it also approached the western edges of the CWA. Nearly all of the storms and severe weather occurred along and north of Interstate 20. Hail and damaging winds were the main hazards with both lines of storms but a brief tornado did occur in Stephens County near Eliasville. Severe thunderstorm winds ripped roofs off buildings in Wise County and two people were injured in association with the roof damage. Most of the hail was golfball size or smaller but a few reports up to baseball size were received. Large amounts of hail up to the size of golfballs fell in Denton County damaging windows, buildings, and roofs in several cities across the southern half of the county. Details: A brief tornado touched down approximately 2 miles east of Eliasville in extreme northern Stephens County.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2011 to April 30, 2011. Affected areas: Archer, Baylor, Clay, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: North Texas continued to experience hot and dry conditions in April. D3 drought status (the 2nd worst) was already present over all 8 counties, but two counties worsened into D4 drought status by the end of the month. Normally a wetter month, most of the normal spring thunderstorm activity missed a large portion of Oklahoma. The dry April only compounded the very dry conditions seen over the region since the beginning of October 2010. In fact, this is the 3rd driest period statewide since October 1. Agricultural impacts were severe, as most the winter wheat crop was non-existent, as well as losses to other crops. The dry conditions also gave rise to enhanced fire weather concerns, with the normal increase in wind speeds during the spring months. Details: Baylor county remained in D3 drought status through the month. Clay county remained in D3 drought status through the month. Foard county remained in D3 drought status through the month.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from May 15, 2011 to May 15, 2011. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area. Episode summary: A large, cold, and slow moving system over the West brought a modest snowfall to the Sierra on the 15th. Details: Four to seven inches of snow fell from South Lake Tahoe north and west to the Sierra crest near Donner Summit. The morning snow and cold as well as wet roads later in the day forced the delay and eventual cancellation of the first leg of the Amgen Pro Cycling Tour.

title: High Wind: California, May 25, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 25, 2011 to May 25, 2011. Affected areas: Mono. Episode summary: A system off the northern California coast on the 25th moved into western Idaho by the 26th. This brought precipitation to northeast California with dry and windy conditions for Mono County on the 25th. Details: Wind gusts between 60 and 70 mph near the highway 395 corridor on the 25th. Specific high wind gusts include 73 mph at the Walker RAWS, 66 mph at the Mammoth airport AWOS, and 60 mph on the west side of Mammoth Lakes. Winds over Mammoth Mountain gusted between 100 and 140 mph.

title: Drought: Texas, Jul 12, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 12, 2011 to July 31, 2011. Affected areas: Brooks, Cameron, Coastal Willacy, Hidalgo, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Starr, Willacy, Zapata. Episode summary: Despite little to no rainfall from the second full week of July to the end of the month, impacts from the heavy rains of late June and early July manifest themselves in continued improvement in drought conditions across all of Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley from mid July the month's end. While a month earlier, all areas were in Extreme (D3) to Exceptional (D4) Drought, by July 12th, only the northern tier of the Deep South Country Brush Country/King Ranch and portions of the Upper Rio Grande Valley were in Extreme Drought; the Lower and Mid Valley had dropped to the Moderate and Severe (D1 and D2) categories. Details: Severe (D2) Drought conditions continued across all of Coastal Willacy County the second full week in July; isolated showers on July 10th allowed Drought conditions to subside to Moderate (D1) beginning on the 26th. Scattered showers with local downpours through July 2nd manifest themselves in slight improvement in drought moved across portions of Starr County the second full week in July. Extreme (D3) drought conditions prevailed across two thirds of Starr County, with Severe (D2) drought conditions prevailed across the remainder of Starr County encompassing the northwestern one third and extreme northeaste Scattered showers which ended in Zapata County by July 2nd manifest themselves in slightly improved drought conditions across portions of the county for the middle and latter part of the month. Extreme (D3) drought conditions prevailed across two thirds of Zapata County while Severe (D2) drought conditions prevailed across a northwest to southeast slot encompassing the central and southeastern one

title: High Wind: California, May 31, 2011

Winds also blew the roof off the Upside Down House in Lee Vining. The roof landed against the Old Schoolhouse Museum and broke through one wall of the museum. Here are some specific wind gusts: Lee Vining with 80 mph, Crowley Lake with 75 mph, Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, May 21, 2011

The wildfire consumed an estimated three hundred acres and was contained around 1900CST. The cause of the wildfire was still unknown at this time.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jul 16, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from July 16, 2011 to July 16, 2011. Affected areas: Barron, Chippewa, Polk. Episode summary: A small complex of thunderstorms developed across central Minnesota, and moved southeast across the northern Twin Cities Metro area and portions of west central Wisconsin, produced locally four to six inches of rainfall in less than 4 hours.||The worst areas were in the town of Woodmohr, and east of the city of Bloomer. A few roads were closed due to the flooding including;||The intersection of County Road GG & SS, |The intersection of Highway SS and 125th Street. |The 13000 block of 155th Avenue in Eagle Point. Details: The Wisconsin Highway Department had road repairs due to flash flooding around Turtle Lake and Almena. Some areas received between three and four inches during the morning. Several reports of excessive rainfall caused flooding in Bloomer, and a few roads that had significant flooding. In addition, water over-topped Highway SS at the intersection with Highway GG, and near the Highway SS intersection with 125th Street. A culvert washed out in the 13000 block of 155th Avenue. A measured report total of 4.50 inches in less than 4 hours.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jul 19, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from July 19, 2011 to July 19, 2011. Affected areas: Polk. Episode summary: Thunderstorms that developed across northern Minnesota during the afternoon of Tuesday, July 19th, moved southeast into west central Wisconsin by the early evening and produced numerous damaging wind reports and flash flooding. Details: A weak tornado knocked down several dozen trees before crossing Pipe Lake, and dissipated on the eastern shore of Pipe Lake. A damage survey revealed the tornadic winds were about 65 mph. Just to the west of the tornado was a strong rear flank downdraft, with winds just less than 80 mph, which knocked down at least 100 trees (see separate entry).

title: Frost/Freeze: Wisconsin, May 26, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Frost/Freeze, from May 26, 2011 to May 27, 2011. Affected areas: Ashland, Bayfield, Douglas, Iron, Price. Episode summary: High pressure built over southwest Ontario and northern Minnesota on the evening of May 26th, and over Lake Superior and northwest Wisconsin later that night. Clear skies and light winds allowed temperatures to fall below freezing in protected areas. The coastal counties and Price County were affected.

title: High Wind: Wisconsin, May 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: High Wind, from May 09, 2011 to May 09, 2011. Affected areas: Langlade, Marathon, Vilas. Episode summary: Strong and gusty winds developed as an area of weakening showers and thunderstorms moved away from the region. The high winds, a result of a wake low, downed numerous trees and power lines. Thousands of customers were without power across northern Wisconsin and nearly 9,000 customers lost power in Wausau (Marathon County). Trees on power lines caused some fires and an uprooted tree severed a gas line. Roofs were torn from two machine sheds near Antigo (Langlade County) and an unoccupied mobile home and a car were destroyed.||The highest measured wind gust was 65 mph in Weston (Marathon County), and a gust to 61 mph was recorded at Wausau Municipal Airport. The highest estimated gusts were 65 mph near Antigo and 60 mph near Sayner (Vilas County). Details: Estimated wind gusts to 60 mph near Sayner knocked down trees and power lines. Thousands in the area were left without power. Wind gusts as high as 65 mph in Weston and 61 mph at the Wausau Municipal Airport downed numerous trees and power lines in the area. Around 9,000 people in Wausau lost power. An uprooted tree broke a gas line and trees on power lines started some fires in the area. Wind gusts estimated to 65 mph downed trees and tore the roofs from two machine sheds northwest of Antigo. Trees fell on an unoccupied mobile home and a car, heavily damaging both. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, May 24, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 24, 2011 to May 25, 2011. Affected areas: Dallam. title: Wildfire: Texas, May 24, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 24, 2011 to May 27, 2011. Affected areas: Randall. Episode summary: The Texas Forest Service reported that the Canyon Wildfire, which is also known as the Cemetery Road Wildfire locally, began around 1600CST about five miles east southeast of Canyon Texas in Randall County. The wildfire started near the intersection of Interstate 27 and Cemetery Road. The wildfire initially threatened seven homes along with seven barns. There were two homes that were in immediate danger. A total of sixty homes were threatened. One abandoned older home was destroyed. The Palo Duro Canyon and Sunday Canyon and points east from there were under a voluntary evacuation. At least one hundred students from a youth camp had to be evacuated by bus. The Ceta Canyon Church Camp lost two cottages and also two multi-unit storage buildings. One home and one shelter building were heavily damaged and may be reclassified as lost. The Ceta Glen Church Camp lost two shower buildings and the Helen Tilger Hall received damage. There were unknown miles of fencing and utility poles which were lost. There were no injuries reported. The wildfire was mapped initially using a Texas Department of Public Safety helicopter along with a Global Positioning System at sixteen thousand three hundred and seventy-three acres and had a perimeter of fifty-three miles. However, approximately an additional one hundred and eighty acres were consumed on Palo Duro Canyon State Park land. It is estimated that a total of sixteen thousand eight hundred and three acres were consumed. Seven to eight ranches were immediately threatened by the wildfire, however an accurate count could not be completed due to the amount of smoke. It is believed that multiple ranches and homes were in the path of the wildfire. The wildfire

title: Wildfire: Texas, May 24, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 24, 2011 to May 24, 2011. Affected areas: Deaf Smith. Another thirty other structures were threatened with five of those structures destroyed. There were no reports of injuries. The wildfire was determined to have been caused by smoking materials. One wildland fire truck became burned over during structure protection, however the firefighters were not injured. The wildfire was contained around 2230CST. Reported property and crop damage: about $150,000.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2011 to May 31, 2011. Affected areas: El Paso, Hudspeth. Episode summary: Very little if any rain fell across Far West Texas since the beginning of the year which led to extreme to exceptional drought conditions across the area. Details: Through the month of May, the eastern half of Hudspeth County was in Exceptional(D4) drought. The remainder of Hudspeth County was in Extreme(D3) drought. No measurable precipitation was reported in most areas since early February, and in some cases since late October 2010. Through the month of May, all of El Paso County was in Extreme(D3) drought. No measurable precipitation was reported at the El Paso International Airport since early February when 0.11 inches was reported. Since October 5th, only 0.29 inches had been reported at the airport. This was the third driest October-May period on record.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, Wildfire, from May 24, 2011 to May 24, 2011. Affected areas: Castro, Garza, Lubbock, Swisher. In response, strong winds spread over the West Texas region during the afternoon hours on May 24. The strong winds lead to several wind-driven grass fires as well as a couple localized high wind gusts. Reduced visibilities were reported across the region with three-quarter mile visibility reported at Lubbock International Airport at 14:53 CST.||The first high wind gust was observed at a KVII-TV Schoolnet site in Hart (Castro County). The site recorded a measured gust of 58 mph at 13:48 CST. A second severe wind gust was observed from the Texas Tech University mesonet site at Reese Center (Lubbock County). The site measured a peak gust of 59 mph at 14:40 CST which was determined to be associated with the passage of a large wind-driven wildfire.||This wildfire at Reese Center destroyed the mesonet site causing $12,000 in damage. Additionally, as the fire passed through the mesonet site, a maximum temperature of 148 degrees Fahrenheit was recorded at 1.5 meters before the sensor failed. The fire also destroyed the anemometer at a height of 10 meters. The Lubbock County Sheriff's Office closed roads near this wildfire due to low visibility within the smoke along with evacuating 30 to 50 residences. This fire burned a total of 1200 acres before being contained at 17:00 CST.||Another wildfire started shortly after the Reese Center fire at 14:45 CST in Garza County ten miles northeast of Post. title: Wildfire: Texas, May 06, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 06, 2011 to May 11, 2011. Affected areas: Dickens, King. Another four homes were damaged by the wildfire. There were no reports of injuries. title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, May 15, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from May 15, 2011 to May 15, 2011. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green, Iowa, Jefferson, Kenosha, Lafayette, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Racine and 6 more areas. Episode summary: A tight pressure gradient between low pressure over Ohio and a ridge of high pressure extending from North Dakota into Ontario, Canada, produced strong north to northeast winds over most of South-Central Wisconsin and Southeast Wisconsin. Daytime heating of dry air that had spread into the region with the leading edge of the high allowed mixing up to 40 to 45 knot winds about 5,000 feet above ground level. This mixing resulted in sustained winds of 30 to 35 mph and wind gusts up to 45 mph at the surface. Scattered power-outages were reported due to broken tree branches falling on and snapping power-lines. Reported property and crop damage: about $90,000.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, May 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from May 22, 2011 to May 22, 2011. Affected areas: Green Lake. Episode summary: A deep 500 mb low and associated surface low pressure tracked from eastern South Dakota into central Minnesota, lifting a warm front into Wisconsin during the early afternoon of May 22nd. Cool 500 mb temperatures and moist surface dew points in the lower 60s produced sufficient instability for thunderstorm development, with mean-layer CAPE of 2000 to 2500 J/KG. A mid-level jet streak of 50-60 knots produced 40-50 knots of deep-layer wind shear for supercell thunderstorm development, with low-level shear of 30 to 40 knots in the 0-1 km layer as a low-level jet strengthened enhancing the tornado potential, especially near the warm front. Details: An EF0 tornado spun up about 2 miles south-southwest of Kingston about 900 ft southeast of the intersection of County Road H and State Highway 44 and traveled northeast approximately 1/3 mile before dissipating just south of State Highway 44. The tornado damaged a door on a shed, broke tree branches, and damaged a greenhouse. The EF-rating was based on DI 27(TH) DOD 2 with winds of 65 mph. The sta An EF0 tornado spun up about 0.3 miles northwest of downtown Markesan just west of State Highway 44 (Margaret Street) about 1/2 mile south of the intersection with County Road H and traveled east-northeast slightly over 4 miles before dissipating near Utley, about 1/4 mile west-northwest of the intersection of Utley Road and County Highway Q. The tornado broke tree branches, with some of them snap Reported property and crop damage: about $6,000.

The automated weather station at Decatur Municipal Airport (KLUD) measured a 52 mph wind gust. Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

Details: Local Law Enforcement Officials reported several water rescues in Brownwood caused by thunderstorms producing very heavy rain. As much as 3 to 4 inches of rain fell since 12 PM CDT.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2011 to May 31, 2011. Affected areas: Brown, Coke, Concho, Crockett, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason, Mcculloch, Menard and 8 more areas. Episode summary: The historic drought continued to plague much of West Central Texas. According to the Texas Crop Weather Report issued May 24 by the Texas A&M Agriculture Program and newspaper accounts, the region received some Rain but overall remained very dry, some producers received enough moisture to plant annual hay crops but much more rain will be needed to produce yields. Limited acreages of grain sorghum and cotton were planted. Cattle pens are twice as full this month as this time last year as ranchers sell off their livestock. Most ranchers remain uncertain whether and when to sell because of the markets. The dry, hot weather also resulted in intense, deep burning fires and significant downwind spotting.||Mostly dry conditions have continued through the spring with only a few scattered showers associated with thunderstorm activity. Over the last 238 days, from October 1 of 2010 through May 31 of 2011, Abilene had measurable rain on 22 days, while San Angelo had measureable rain on 12 days and Junction had 19 days of|measureable rain. This was also the driest period on record for the state. Details: The U.S. Drought Monitor placed Shackelford County in an extreme drought category. The U.S. Drought Monitor placed Concho County in a severe drought category. The U.S. Drought Monitor placed Sterling County in an exceptional drought category.

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 01, 2011 to June 30, 2011. Affected areas: Aransas, Bee, Calhoun, Duval, Goliad, Jim Wells, Kleberg, La Salle, Live Oak, Mcmullen, Nueces, Refugio and 3 more areas. Episode summary: Although most of South Texas received some rainfall during the month of June, the amounts remained well below normal. Rainfall deficits for the month ranged from 2.5 inches below normal for the southern portions of the Coastal Bend and Brush Country to 4 inches below normal for portions of the Victoria Crossroads and northern Coastal Bend. Along with the lack of rainfall, temperatures remained above normal across South Texas.||Exceptional drought conditions continued across La Salle and Webb Counties in June and advanced eastward into northeast Live Oak, Bee, Goliad, and Refugio Counties. Extreme drought conditions over Duval, McMullen, Jim Wells, southern Live Oak, Victoria, and Calhoun Counties expanded across the remainder of South Texas into Aransas, Nueces, Kleberg, and San Patricio Counties by the end of the month. ||Hay production was severely limited or insignificant. Livestock producers continued to provide supplemental feed to their reduced herds. Rangeland and pastures only improved slightly with the rainfall. Ponds remained either very low or dry.

title: Flood: California, Jun 24, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from June 24, 2011 to June 30, 2011. Affected areas: Mono. Episode summary: Much above average snowpack in the Sierra combined with warm to very warm temperatures to cause small stream flooding in Mono County late in June. Details: A bridge crossing McGee Creek was destroyed by flood waters. The location of the washed out bridge is approximate. The Lower Lee Vining, Moraine, Aspen, and Big Bend campgrounds are partially or completely closed due to snowmelt flooding from Lee Vining Creek. Monetary damages due to loss of income from the closed campsites and one culvert was washed out leading to higher water in campgrounds. California Land Management indicated that the Twin Lakes Campground (30 campsites) was completely shut down due to snowmelt flooding. No damage to campground property noted just the loss of income from the closed campsites. Reported property and crop damage: about $31,500.

title: Wildfire: Texas, May 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 01, 2011 to May 10, 2011. Affected areas: Irion, Kimble. Episode summary: Critical Fire Weather Conditions occurred on April 25 across much of West Central Texas as a dryline brought southwest to west winds of 20 to 25 mph, relative humidity levels below 20 percent, and temperatures in the 90s. Isolated thunderstorms ignited a large wildfire in Kimble County on April 26 called the Oasis Pipeline Wildfire. This wildfire continued into the month of May. The Scott Ranch Wildfire near Barnhart Texas also continued from late April into early May. Details: The Oasis Pipeline Fire 11 miles south of Junction burned approximately 9445 acres and it was 100 percent contained by midnight on May 10. There were 11 structures destroyed, including 1 home. Also, 3 vehicles and 1 bulldozer were destroyed, along with numerous power poles and fence line. In addition, 20 head of cattle were lost. Commercial airtankers and four MAFFs tankers helped slow the spread The Scott Ranch Fire located 13 miles west-northwest of Mertzon burned approximately 11,233 acres. The fire was started on April 26, when a chain swinging from a truck created sparks as it bounced on the road surface on a Scott Ranch road. Eight homes were threatened and saved. Oil and gas infrastructure were also threatened. Several utility poles were destroyed by the fire resulted in some power

title: Wildfire: Texas, May 08, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 08, 2011 to May 30, 2011. Affected areas: Fisher. Episode summary: This wildfire was ignited by lightning about 14 miles northwest of Sweetwater. Once the fire was ignited, it was fueled by critical fire weather conditions. Details: Thirty-two homes, oil infrastructure and wind turbines were threatened on this lightning-caused fire 13 miles northwest of Sweetwater. Two structures were lost but the type of structures were unknown.

title: Wildfire: Texas, May 17, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 17, 2011 to May 20, 2011. Affected areas: Sterling. Episode summary: The dryline brought elevated to critical fire weather conditions west of a line from Abilene to San Angelo. Details: The Price Fire began in western Sterling County and burned mesquite, grass and brush. One home and dozens of pump jacks were saved. Three heavy air tankers responded to the fire. The fire was declared controlled on May 20. The cause was unknown.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 19, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 19, 2011 to May 19, 2011. Affected areas: Wilbarger. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed early in the afternoon over the western portions of northern Texas. However, much of the early development moved northeast into Oklahoma. By later in the afternoon, more widespread thunderstorms developed east of the dry line. The northern tier of counties took the brunt of the active weather, with many areas reporting large hail. Vernon saw several rounds of hail, with training thunderstorms occurring for a couple of hours. Toward the end of the event, a brief tornado occurred over far northeast Wilbarger county, just south of the Red River. No damage occurred with the tornado. The severe activity had crossed into Oklahoma by mid evening. Details: A storm chaser east of Davidson OK observed and photographed a partially rain-wrapped tornado to his south-southwest, estimated to be just south of the Red River in far northeastern Wilbarger County Texas. This tornado produced no known damage.

title: Wildfire: Texas, May 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 10, 2011 to May 10, 2011. Affected areas: Ochiltree. Episode summary: The DeBall Wildfire began between 1330CST and 1338CST about six miles south southeast of Wolf Creek Park Texas in Ochiltree County. The wildfire did not cause any structural damages and there were no reports of injuries. The wildfire was contained around 1945CSTand consumed an estimated three hundred and fifty acres.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jun 18, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, from June 18, 2011 to June 22, 2011. Affected areas: Crawford, La Crosse, Vernon. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms developed well north of a warm front, that was across southern Iowa, during the evening of the June 18th. These storms were slow moving and produced some localized heavy rain and flash flooding across Crawford and Vernon Counties. The Viroqua Fire Department had to rescue a man trapped inside a pickup truck at the Sidie Hollow park. A group of Cub Scouts became stranded by rising waters in Eagles Park. After waiting almost 5 hours for flood waters to recede, they were led to safety by the Wheatland Fire Department with no injuries occurring. Some isolated wind damage also occurred in Onalaska (La Crosse County). Details: State Highway 56 was closed east of Viroqua due to flash flooding along Cook Creek. The flooding turned parts of the road into a lake and moved a log onto the road. A house that was built on a sunken lot had a basement wall collapse after four inches of rain fell on the area. In addition to the basement damage, the master bedroom and bathroom, laundry room and living room were ruined. Hornby Creek rose eight feet in a little over an hour stranding a Cub Scout Pack that was camping in Eagles Park. The scout leaders moved the Cub Scouts to higher ground and waited until the Wheatland Fire Department was able to rescue them around 6 a.m. Reported property and crop damage: about $74,000.

title: Winter Storm: California, May 14, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Storm, from May 14, 2011 to May 18, 2011. Affected areas: S Sierra Mtns, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: The next upper-level trough began moving into California on May 14th, bringing colder air and abundant mid and high clouds. Temperatures in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley only reached the mid 60s to mid 70s, down as much as 22 degrees from the 13th. During the morning of the 14th, a thin layer of cirrostratus covered the San Joaquin Valley. The layer of ice crystals aloft produced a prominent halo around the Sun that was visible from parts of the Valley.||The upper-level trough remained over the central California interior from May 15th through the 18th. Upper-level disturbances brought periods of showers to the region, as well as scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon of the 15th. Three funnel clouds were seen over the central San Joaquin Valley on May 15th (one in the morning near the foothills east of Fresno, and two in the afternoon near Kerman), and another funnel was observed on the 18th near Arvin in Kern County.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Storm, from May 28, 2011 to May 29, 2011. Affected areas: S Sierra Mtns. title: Dust Storm: Texas, Jun 12, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Dust Storm, from June 12, 2011 to June 12, 2011. Affected areas: Hockley, Lubbock, Lynn, Terry. Episode summary: On the evening of the 12th, isolated storms developed in the southwestern South Plains and tracked east-northeast. These storms produced severe wind gusts in Terry County. Additionally, a haboob was generated by the strong surface winds from the thunderstorms. A widespread area across Terry, Hockley, Lynn and Lubbock counties reported visibilities near zero at times due to blowing dust with the passage of the haboob.

title: High Wind, Wildfire: Texas, Jun 18, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, Wildfire, from June 18, 2011 to June 20, 2011. Affected areas: Cochran, Floyd, Hockley, Lamb, Stonewall, Yoakum. Episode summary: High based weak showers developed over the western South Plains during the evening hours of the 18th. These showers produced isolated severe wind gusts in Hockley and Floyd Counties. These high winds also sparked numerous wildfires across the region.||The first wildfire began on the 18th two miles southwest of Whiteface (Cochran County). Nearly 100 homes were threatened and evacuated in Whiteface and 2200 acres burned before being contained early on the 19th. A second wildfire on the 18th was started by downburst winds near Floydada (Floyd County). Strong winds downed a power line in a residential neighborhood causing two homes to be totally destroyed by a fire.||Lightning started two fires in Stonewall County early on the 19th which combined to burn 2000 acres. A wildfire in Lamb County started in the median along U.S. Highway 84 which prompted a closure of the highway near FM 1072 for two hours on the 19th. The wildfire burned a total of 350 acres. Reported property and crop damage: about $250,000.

title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, Aug 02, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from August 02, 2011 to August 02, 2011. Affected areas: Rusk. Episode summary: A complex of thunderstorms that developed across South Dakota early Tuesday morning, August 2nd, moved eastward into west-central, central and east-central Minnesota, then into west-central Wisconsin during the late morning. Brief severe wind gusts along a bow echo moved across the area, with mainly tree damage. In addition to the wind damage, two waves of thunderstorms that moved across portions of Rusk County, produced locally two to four inches of rain, and caused roads to washout near Hawkins. Details: Two county roads were washed out in far eastern Rusk County due to excessive rainfall of two to four inches in less than 2 hours. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from August 03, 2011 to August 03, 2011. Affected areas: Hidalgo. Episode summary: A suspected spark from a local utility vehicle caught grassland on fire during the afternoon of August 3rd, which quickly engulfed areas around the small community of Puerto Rico. The fire occurred in areas where Severe to nearly Extreme Drought continued, and was driven by the combination of the drought conditions and southeast winds gusting between 20 and 24 mph, relatively humidity falling to or just below 25 percent, and Dry fuels. Details: A grass fire rapidly spread to near 1,000 acres during the afternoon of August 3rd near Puerto Rico in northwest Hidalgo County. The fire started when a vehicle servicing local telephone poles sparked; the vehicle caught on fire and was heavily damaged. One barn and one home were saved by fire crews, which numbered up to 15 departments from at least Hidalgo and Starr Counties. The fire was report Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jun 11, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from June 11, 2011 to June 15, 2011. Affected areas: Cottle, Motley. Episode summary: A wildfire began 15 miles east-northeast of Matador (Motley County) late on the 10th and flared up during the daytime hours on the 11th. The fire rapidly spread across Motley County and into Cottle County on the 12th. The wildfire was contained late on the 14th after 30000 acres were burned.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jun 24, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from June 24, 2011 to June 25, 2011. Affected areas: Garza. Episode summary: A wildfire began during the afternoon of the 24th along U.S. Highway 84, 13 miles northwest of Post. The wildfire threatened 11 homes, destroyed 1000 railroad ties and burned 7000 acres. The wildfire became contained early in the morning on the 25th.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jun 28, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from June 28, 2011 to June 28, 2011. Affected areas: Bailey, Lamb. Episode summary: Lightning strikes from severe storms on the evening of the 27th started several wildfires. Three of these wildfires flared up during the afternoon hours of the 28th. One wildfire started in Lamb county and was known as the Tolk Plant Fire. An energy power plant was threatened but no damage was reported. This fire burned a total of 750 acres. Two additional wildfires flared up in Bailey County near the Lamb/Bailey County line near and north of of U.S. Highway 84. These two fires prompted the closure of U.S. Highway 84 between Muleshoe (Bailey County) and Sudan (Lamb County). Visibility was near zero on U.S. Highway 84 due to the smoke from the wildfire. These two fires burned a total of 5,900 acres.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jun 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from June 09, 2011 to June 11, 2011. Affected areas: Cottle. Episode summary: The Burdett Wildfire burned for two days in Cottle County and burned 6600 acres. No structures were threatened.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jun 13, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from June 13, 2011 to June 15, 2011. Affected areas: Stonewall. Episode summary: The Springer Wildfire began in Stonewall County on the 13th and was contained on the 15th after burning 2000 acres.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jun 16, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from June 16, 2011 to June 16, 2011. Affected areas: Lynn. Episode summary: High based weak showers developed over the South Plains during the evening hours on the 16th. These showers produced an isolated severe wind gust near Tahoka (Lynn County). The Texas Tech University mesonet site near Tahoka measured a wind gust to 60 mph. No damage was reported.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jun 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from June 10, 2011 to June 10, 2011. Affected areas: Garza. Episode summary: Evening severe thunderstorms on the 10th brought much needed rain to the South Plains and Rolling Plains but also produced damaging straight-line winds. Storms developed along a cold front stretched across the region with storms initially forming in the Permian Basin. As the storms moved into the South Plains they intensified. A strong gust front from the initial storms created a haboob that moved across several counties. There was no damage or injuries reported with the haboob. Lightning from these storms also started a wildfire in Motley county. The most significant damage was in King and Cottle Counties as a new complex of thunderstorms developed in Crosby and Dickens Counties and moved northeastward. Strong outflow winds caused damage from Dumont (King County) to Paducah (Cottle County). Paducah High School sustained significant damage from these straight-line winds. A wake low over Garza county created high wind gusts locally enhanced by the Caprock escarpment. These winds were measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.

title: High Wind: Wisconsin, May 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: High Wind, from May 09, 2011 to May 09, 2011. Affected areas: Ashland, Iron. Episode summary: As an area of rain and thunderstorms quickly dissipated on the morning of May 9th, a localized area of low pressure formed behind the precipitation. This rapid fluctuation in pressure, and local low pressure is referred to as a wake low. The wake low caused strong wind gusts across much of northwest Wisconsin and western Lake Superior, and resulted in sporadic tree damage in many locations. A few spots of more significant damage were observed in Ashland and Iron Counties. Measured wind gusts by weather stations were generally between 40 and 50 mph. Some of the more notable gusts included a 48 mph gust at the Hayward Airport (Sawyer County), a 47 mph gust at Barnes (Bayfield County), a 50 mph gust at Phillips (Price County), and a 50 mph gust 2 miles northwest of Maple (Douglas County). The private weather station northwest of Maple also measured a pressure drop of 4 millibars (0.12 inches of mercury) in 30 minutes. The strong winds also affected western Lake Superior, and a ship approaching Two Harbors reported a 40 knot gust at 80 feet above sea level, with developing 2 foot waves. Details: Strong winds uprooted trees, blew down some tree limbs and tree branches, and brought down a few power lines. This sporadic damage was confirmed from spotter and public reports, as well as local newspaper articles. The strong winds uprooted large pine trees at the Mellen Union Cemetery, and the root structures overturned some grave stones. title: Tornado: Wisconsin, May 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from May 22, 2011 to May 22, 2011. Affected areas: Price. Episode summary: A strong low pressure system deepened as it moved north into central Minnesota by the afternoon of May 22nd. A cold front extended to the south from the surface low, while a warm front slowly pushed north into far northern Wisconsin. Thunderstorms developed along and near both fronts and swept across far eastern Minnesota and much of Wisconsin. The combination of strong vertical wind shear and an unstable atmosphere contributed to supercell thunderstorms. The storms produced five tornadoes in Price County, and eleven total tornadoes across the entire state of Wisconsin. The 11 tornadoes was the 10th highest one-day tornado total for the state of Wisconsin on record. The storms also produced damaging winds and large hail across much of northwest Wisconsin. Details: A weak tornado developed and tracked roughly along Price Lakes Road for slightly over 3 miles, before dissipating near Le Tourneau Lake. The damage consisted of primarily trees and large tree limbs blown down or snapped in a convergent pattern along the road. Some large pine trees were snapped. Structural damage was very minor, with one house experiencing some roof damage and a blown in window. [D A weak tornado tracked for just over a mile around U.S. Highway 8 to the west of Prentice. The damage was primarily to trees, with a few 6-12 inch diameter pine trees snapped and blown in a convergent damage pattern. A metal barn also had some minor damage, mainly to eaves and siding. [DI 1 (SBO), DOD 1, EXP-UB, Est Gust 70 mph]. A brief, weak tornado occurred north-northwest of Prentice. Only tree damage was noted along the damage path. [DI 28 (TS), DOD 2, EXP, Est Gust 75 mph].

title: Tornado: Texas, Jul 19, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from July 19, 2011 to July 19, 2011. Affected areas: Medina. Details: A thunderstorm produced a brief, weak tornado west of Hondo. The tornado did not cause any damage and was rated EF0.

title: Excessive Heat: Texas, Aug 04, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Excessive Heat, from August 04, 2011 to August 04, 2011. Affected areas: Wood. Episode summary: Afternoon temperatures on August 4th were near 110 degrees about the time a 17 car train derailed near Mineola, Texas. The accident occurred near CR 2790 and FM 1804. Wood County officials blamed the heat for warping the metal train tracks. There were no report of injuries. Reported property and crop damage: about $200,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 06, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from August 06, 2011 to August 06, 2011. Affected areas: Bowie. Episode summary: Ambient temperatures near 107 degrees, relative humidity values near 20 percent and drought conditions were the ingredients needed for a grass fire which quickly burned out of control across Bowie County during the afternoon of August 6th. The wildfire...while only 50 acres in size, consumed two homes, a barn and a storage building. The fire started near County Road 2148. The United States Forest Service used helicopters to drop large containers of water on the fire. Reported property and crop damage: about $300,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from August 03, 2011 to August 05, 2011. Affected areas: Titus. Episode summary: Ambient temperatures near 110 degrees, very low relative humidity values, winds near 10 mph with higher gusts and drought conditions were the ingredients needed for a very large grass fire across Titus County in Northeast Texas. The fire, nearly 1058 acres in size, was located near the community of Talco, Texas. The Forest Service was called in to help control the fire. The fire threatened 17 homes and 75 outbuildings but only one small building was lost. One fire fighter was taken to a local hospital because of heat exhaustion. A heavy helicopter was brought in to drop water on the fire. Reported property and crop damage: about $500.

title: Drought: Texas, Jul 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 01, 2011 to July 31, 2011. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Exceptional (D4) drought continued across the entire area through the month of July. However, there was a brief reprieve into Extreme (D3) across portions of the southeastern Texas panhandle for the second half of the month due to abundant rainfall during the first half of the month. The remainder of the area received little to no beneficial rainfall during July.||The drought of 2011 clearly stands out as among the most extreme in this region in the past 100 years. Portions of Briscoe and Hall Counties experienced a heavy rain event on July 11. Otherwise, no area saw significant rainfall through the entire month. Annual rainfall totals at Lubbock and Childress were 1.13 inches and 3.64 inches, respectively. These were the lowest rainfall values ever recorded at Lubbock and Childress. Other annual rainfall totals include 2.35 at Morton (Cochran County), 2.23 inches at Silverton (Briscoe County), 1.37 inches at Friona (Parmer County) and 0.72 inches at Brownfield (Terry County). Keetch-Byram Drought Index values continued to range from 600 to 800 across the entire area. A heat wave from June continued to affect the area into the month of July. An upper high persisted over the area favoring very hot temperatures and the warmest July ever recorded for several areas. Many areas also saw temperature records broken with average temperatures between 8 and 11 degrees above normal.||Wildfire activity lessened through July due to the lack of dry high-based thunderstorms. Agricultural losses continued to mount with most crops failing. Aquifer draw-down greatly increased suggesting that irrigation may not be able to continue for a prolonged period of time.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jun 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from June 03, 2011 to June 16, 2011. Affected areas: Coke, Shackelford, Throckmorton. Episode summary: Persistent hot, dry, and windy weather continued to result in critical fire weather conditions throughout the month of June that featured numerous intense, deep burning fires resulting in significant downwind spotting that lasted for days and weeks. Details: This wildfire burned approximately 1300 acres about 5 miles south of Albany. About a hundred homes and one ranch were saved by the firefighters. The Lambs Head Wildfire was located just west of the intersection of U.S. Highways 283 and 183 or about 13 miles west of Woodson. The wildfire was started by an electrical short. The Dos Amigos Wildfire was located 15 miles west of Robert Lee and burned about 19,391 acres. One deer camp and numerous vehicles were destroyed. A nearby gas plant suffered minimal damage. The fire was 90% contained on June 15.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jun 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from June 10, 2011 to June 16, 2011. Affected areas: Nolan. Episode summary: Persistent hot, dry, and windy weather continued to result in critical fire weather conditions throughout the month of June. Details: The Camp Boothe Oaks Wildfire burned about 1,116 acres near the Camp Boothe Oaks Girl Scout Camp south of Interstate 20 between Sweetwater and Roscoe.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jun 16, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from June 16, 2011 to June 27, 2011. Affected areas: Brown, Crockett, Haskell, Jones, Sterling, Throckmorton, Tom Green. Episode summary: Persistent hot, dry, and windy weather continued to result in critical fire weather conditions throughout the month of June. Details: The Mitchell Ranch 2 Wildfire was located about 33 miles southwest of Ozona. The fire burned approximately 3,212 acres. Gas plants were threatened and saved. The Toenail Trail Wildfire was located about 4 miles southeast of Christoval. The fire burned approximately 1,000 acres. The Wilson Ranch Wildfire was located about 6 miles northeast of Water Valley. The fire burned approximately 4,300 acres.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jul 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from July 09, 2011 to July 09, 2011. Affected areas: Childress. Episode summary: A wildfire began near Kirkland (Childress County) around 1600 CST from lightning associated with isolated thunderstorm activity. The wildfire burned a total of 800 acres.

title: Drought: Texas, Aug 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from August 01, 2011 to August 31, 2011. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Severe (D3) drought conditions seen in Childress, Hall, Briscoe, Floyd, and Motley counties at the beginning of the month had returned to Exceptional (D4) drought conditions by the end of August. The exceptional drought was expected to continue well into the fall season with little to no relief.||Most areas saw little to no rain through the month. However, portions of the central and southern South Plains saw beneficial rainfall on August 11 with one to four inches recorded associated with slow moving thunderstorms. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heat, from July 01, 2011 to July 31, 2011. Affected areas: Dallas, Johnson, Mclennan, Rockwall, Wise, Young. Episode summary: Triple digit daytime temperatures and warm overnight lows gripped nearly all of north Texas for the entire month of July. A few records for daily high temperatures were set or tied, but several records for highest minimum temperatures were set. Dallas/Fort Worth set a new all-time record highest minimum temperature of 86 degrees on the 26th. The prolonged heat took its toll on North Texans and there were 15 heat related deaths; most of them occurring in Dallas County. There were many more heat related illnesses. A Heat Advisory was in effect from the 11th through the 18th, and then again from the 23rd through the end of the month. The triple digit heat this month began a streak that would challenge previous records for most consecutive 100 degree days and greatest annual 100 degree days. Details: Triple digit temperatures were recorded nearly every day during the month of July. title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2011 to May 31, 2011. Affected areas: Archer, Baylor, Clay, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: The severe drought continued over western north Texas during the month of May. By this time, farmers were beginning to think about what they could salvage with their winter wheat crop. Even though wheat prices were high, the yield over much of western north Texas was small. Precipitation-wise, most of the region remained well below normal. Even those that did get it were hampered by periods of hail and wind. Details: D4 drought status maintained itself through the month. D3 drought status at the beginning of the month quickly worsened to D4 by 5/10. D3/D4 drought status improved to D2/D3 status by 5/24.

title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, Jul 17, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from July 17, 2011 to July 17, 2011. Affected areas: Vilas. Episode summary: The passage of a weak upper level disturbance through a very unstable air mass created a bow echo line of severe thunderstorms during the evening hours. Details: A small section of Highway 70 was flooded in a low-lying area. In addition, a house had one basement wall caved in by high water. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Aug 19, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from August 19, 2011 to August 19, 2011. Affected areas: Marinette. Episode summary: A deadly tornado occurred in Marinette County in Wausaukee and isolated severe thunderstorms produced large hail and gusty winds across north-central Wisconsin. The storms knocked out electricity to 2,000 customers and caused at least $120,000 in damage. Details: A tornado quickly developed northwest of the city of Wausaukee during the late afternoon and moved southeast for nearly eight miles before dissipating. The twister touched down near Long Lake, snapping or uprooting hundreds of trees (DI 28, DOD 3, 4) as it moved toward Wausaukee. A mobile home near Long Lake was heavily damaged by fallen trees, but the occupants escaped without injury. As the t The thunderstorm that produced the tornado near Wausaukee re-entered Wisconsin from Menominee County, MI along the Menominee River. The tornado uprooted several trees and snapped numerous branches (DI 28, DOD 2, 3) as it continued to weaken along Highway 180. One tree fell onto the roof of a home near Deer Lane Road. Reported property and crop damage: about $120,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jun 19, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from June 19, 2011 to June 19, 2011. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: A deep, late-season upper trough was moving across the Rockies with a strong surface low located over far Southeastern Colorado providing a tight pressure gradient across the region. Details: An NWS Employee reported a peak gust of 60 mph located 3 miles northwest of Fort Bliss.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jun 12, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from June 12, 2011 to June 13, 2011. Affected areas: Oldham. Episode summary: The Texas Forest Service reported that the Gruhlkey Wildfire began in Oldham County about five miles west of Adrian Texas around 2047 CST. The wildfire was caused by lightning and consumed an estimated one thousand and two hundred acres. Although no damages were reported, two homes were threatened by the wildfire but were saved. There were no injuries reported. The wildfire was contained around 1208 CST on June 13.

The wildfire threatened gas and oil production along with cattle and the fire jumped Farm to Market Road 1913. There were no damages or injuries reported, however several homes were threatened but saved. The wildfire consumed an estimated five thousand acres and was reported to be six miles long and one mile wide. The wildfire was contained around 2013 CST.

Episode summary: A warm and humid air mass settled over southern Wisconsin, with high temperatures reaching the middle to upper 90s. Dew points initially were in the mid to upper 60s, and then fell into the upper 50s during the afternoon. The combination of the hot temperatures and moist dew points produced heat index values of 100 to 104 over southern portions of Iowa County and northern Lafayette County. Heat index values ranged between 92 and 98 across the remainder of southern Wisconsin.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 08, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from June 08, 2011 to June 08, 2011. Affected areas: Dane. Episode summary: Forcing along an advancing cold front moving into a warm, moist unstable air mass over the region produced severe thunderstorms with a tornado, damaging winds and large hail over south-central and southeast Wisconsin during the evening hours of June 8th. The combination of instability, with surface-based CAPE of 3000 J/kg, and 0 to 6 km bulk shear of 40 knots produced supercell thunderstorms, with one of the cells developing an EF1 tornado over central Dane County that uprooted trees, felled power-lines, damaged three vehicles and crushed a garage. A cluster of supercell thunderstorms from Lafayette into Dane County then congealed into a bowing line that moved due east and created damaging wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph across much of the area along and south of Interstate-94. At the height of the event, over 27,000 customers had no electric power in Southeast Wisconsin, and probably another 15 to 20,000 customers in south-central Wisconsin lost power. Details: This tornado spun up southwest of Verona about 1/2 mile southwest of the intersection of CTH G and Sugar River Road, and traveled east-northeast to about 3 miles northeast of McFarland about 1.5 miles east-northeast of the intersection of Interstate 39/90 and STH 12/18. The damage path was sporadic. On the south side of Verona, numerous trees were uprooted, a garage was crushed by a fallen tree, Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: High Wind: Wisconsin, Jun 15, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: High Wind, from June 15, 2011 to June 15, 2011. Affected areas: Kenosha. Episode summary: Focused warm air advection ahead of a short wave trough produced showers and thunderstorms that moved across southern Wisconsin early in the morning of June 15th. A wake low developed behind the departing line of showers and storms, creating damaging wind gusts between 40 and 70 mph (35 to 61 knots) in eastern Kenosha County within 2 to 3 miles of the Lake Michigan shore. The marine observation site at Kenosha Harbor clocked a 67 mph (58 knot) wind gust, while the Kenosha Municipal Airport recorded a gust of 45 mph (39 knots). The gusty winds blew down trees and a few power lines in the city of Kenosha, and felled trees that blocked some roads in Pleasant Prairie. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from June 19, 2011 to June 19, 2011. Affected areas: Dodge. While overall conditions were not favorable for supercell development, high 0 to 3km helicity and high 0-3km CAPE were sufficient to increase the stretching potential of any thunderstorm updraft to produce non-supercell tornadoes. A brief EF0 tornado touched down about 5 miles south of Theresa in Dodge County, breaking off small tree limbs and flattening tall grass in a swirl pattern. Details: A trained storm spotter witnessed a brief EF0 tornado that touched down about 2.7 miles northeast of Herman Center in Dodge County, just north of the intersection of County Road DW and Freedom Road. The tornado traveled less than one-tenth of a mile before dissipating. The maximum path width of the tornado was 20 yards with an average path width of 10 yards. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Tornado, from June 21, 2011 to June 21, 2011. Affected areas: Fond Du Lac, Green Lake, Milwaukee, Waukesha. title: Heavy Rain, Strong Wind: California, Jun 04, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, Strong Wind, from June 04, 2011 to June 04, 2011. Affected areas: Contra Costa, North Bay Interior Valleys, Sonoma. Episode summary: A late season cold front worked its way into Northern and Central California producing strong wind and heavy rain resulting in problems for the agricultural community. Details: Torrential rains over San Francisco's North Bay hit vineyards at a critical time of the growing season, when many vines had opened their flowers to begin the delicate process of self-fertilization. Around 10 to 15 percent of crops were lost equating to tens of millions of dollars to Sonoma County farmers. Heavy rain caused cherry crops in east Contra Costa County to absorb too much water resulting in splitting fruit. Split cherries are susceptible to bacteria and therefore can only be used in a limited capacity. Strong wind combined with saturated soil to knock a giant oak tree to the ground at the Sonoma Development Center. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,065,000.

Many cattle farmers had to sell their cows early because of the scarcity of grasses and hay. Corn farmers also witnessed poor corn production and had to try to grow other crops to salvage their growing season. The drought has also caused trees to suffer, with many trees dying or toppling due to weakened roots from little rainfall. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from July 01, 2011 to July 01, 2011. Affected areas: Douglas. Episode summary: A strong but nearly stationary cold front ran just inland from the Minnesota north shore of Lake Superior southwestward through the Sioux Falls SD area. A cluster of thunderstorms became severe just west of the upper St Croix river, in Pine County MN, and spread rapidly northeastward through northwest Wisconsin. Extensive straight-line wind damage occurred. In Burnett County 140,000 acres of trees were damaged or destroyed, which is estimated to be 1.5 million cords. Damage to public property, like roads and trails, was $1.8 million. Uninsured property damage was estimated at $350,000. The storm injured 39 people. Most injuries were minor. title: Wildfire: Texas, Sep 02, 2011

A wildfire started between Avinger and Jefferson, Texas and burned nearly 41,000 acres of timberland and grassland before it was declared contained on September 13th. A total of 91 structures were burned which included homes, outbuildings and vehicles. Hundreds of firefighters were called in to battle the 12 day wildfire which began when a limb hit a powerline causing sparks. Schools were closed for a few days in southern Cass and Marion Counties. There was one firefighter that was burned while battling the wildfire. This wildfire, which became known as the Bear Creek Fire, involved 17 different agencies including the Texas Forest Service, Texas Parks and Wildlife and fire departments from Florida, South Carolina and Alabama. The Texas Forest Service used helicopter drops from nearby Lake O The Pines to help battle the fire. A command center was set up to coordinate fire fighting efforts at the Pruitt Lake Missionary Baptist Church on Hwy. 155 in Avinger as well as the Pinecrest Baptist on Hwy. 59 in Linden, Texas. More than 8,000 cases of sports drinks and 10,000 cases of water were provided for all the fire fighters during the event. Reported property and crop damage: about $6,000,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from August 17, 2011 to August 17, 2011. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: A broad upper high was centered over New Mexico with weak flow throughout the atmosphere allowing for slow moving thunderstorms that produce heavy rain. A severe wind gust was reported in El Paso as well. Details: Heavy flooding was reported at the intersections of Wedgewood and McRae streets and also Montwood and Yarbrough streets in East El Paso.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Sep 29, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from September 29, 2011 to September 29, 2011. Affected areas: Zapata. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a weak upper level disturbance produced welcome, but locally heavy, rainfall in Zapata County, along with locally gusty winds across the Rio Grande Plains and Rio Grande Valley as drier, cooler air aloft mixed down to the surface in the form of outflows ahead of many of the storms. Wind gusts ranged from the upper 30s (mph) in Hidalgo County (37 mph, 215 PM) to the upper 40s to lower 50s in Jim Hogg (Hebbronville, 52 mph at 435 PM). Minor damage was reported in Zapata with the outflow, followed by nuisance flooding later that evening.||Earlier in the day, a locally strong storm dropped nearly 3/4 inch of rain at the Brownsville/SPI International Airport on the east side of town; lightning associated with the storm struck near or at the Public Utilities Board, causing minor damage. Details: The Zapata County Sheriff's Office reported minor flooding to curb level along State Highway 16 and Federal Highway 83, stretching south toward 9th Avenue. The emergency manager reported 1.75 inches at the fire station; other estimates suggested around 2 inches in less than an hour with the heavy thunderstorm which crossed the city between 8 and 9 PM that evening.

title: Heavy Rain: California, Aug 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, from August 01, 2011 to August 01, 2011. Affected areas: San Bernardino. Episode summary: A large area of upper-level high pressure was located over the south-central portion of the country supplying So Cal with some monsoonal moisture. Broad southwest flow in mid-levels was also present. Large, isolated, deep moist convection and overshooting tops within weak southwest flow aloft developed by 2 pm on the 1st over the San Diego County Mountains, Riverside Mountains, extreme northeast San Diego County and over Onyx Peak, drifting generally northward. Tuesday the 2nd was explosive between 2 and 3 pm over the Riverside Mountains and extreme northern San Diego County. Southwest flow aloft shunted low level convergence just off the crest and Tuesday storms drained towards the deserts. Flash flooding was observed in multiple locations due to heavy downpours. Details: Spotter reported 1.05 inches of rainfall in 30 minutes, causing 1-2 inches of mud and water on SR-247 near Blandford Land and Larrea Road.

title: Wildfire: California, Aug 06, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from August 06, 2011 to August 07, 2011. Affected areas: San Bernardino And Riverside County Valleys - The Inland Empire. Episode summary: The Gilman fire started around 1500 PST on August 6, along Gilman Springs Road east of Highway 60 near Moreno Valley. The fire burned rapidly though grass and brush to a total of 945 acres before it was finally contained around 1700 PST on the 7th. Highway 60 was closed from Gilman Springs Road to Jack Rabbit Trail and all trapped motorists were evacuated. No structured were damaged, but four hand crew members were treated for smoke inhalation, while battling the fire. The cause of the fire is unknown.

title: Wildfire: California, Aug 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from August 22, 2011 to August 24, 2011. Affected areas: San Bernardino County Mountains. Episode summary: The Ken fire started around 1200 PST on August 22, on the northbound side of I-15 just north of the Kenwood exit near Lytle Creek. Lane closures of I-15 were required for most of the day on the 22nd and finally reopened around 1200 PST on the 23rd. During its 300 acre burn, the Ken fire knocked down a power pole, one home, 2 shipping containers and 3 outbuildings (sheds) at Matthews Ranch. Two US Forest Service firefighters suffered injuries, one knee and one heat-related. The cause of the fire is unknown. The fire was fully contained around 1700 PST on the 24th. Reported property and crop damage: about $500,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Aug 27, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from August 27, 2011 to August 27, 2011. Affected areas: San Bernardino, San Diego. Episode summary: A surge of monsoonal moisture brought three days of significant thunderstorms from the 26th to the 28th. These storms brought more CG lightning, strong wind gusts in the low 50s mph, 1/2���-3/4��� hail and brief heavy downpours. Minor accumulation from small hail occurred with some of these storms. The rain produced some flash flooding at low water crossings in Chihuahua Valley. Street flooding and 1/2 hail was also reported near Big Bear in the San Bernardino Mountains. Lightning sparked several small fires in the Riverside and San Bernardino County mountains, including one that became the Oasis Fire. Details: Spotter reported street flooding on Big Bear Boulevard from the Stanfield cutoff to Pine Knot Avenue, as well as Rathbun Creek at Catalina Road. Water 6-12 inches deep covered the roadway. Chihuahua Valley Road was impassable due to fast-moving water over the roadway, up to 2 feet deep in places. Other roads were washed out nearby. Hail up to penny-sized (3/4) was also observed along Chihuahua Valley Road, with minor accumulation of the hail.

title: Wildfire: California, Aug 27, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from August 27, 2011 to August 30, 2011. Affected areas: San Bernardino County Mountains. Episode summary: The Oasis fire started around 1244 PST on August 27 off Oasis Road south of Highway 138 and Pinion Hills, near the LA/San Bernardino County line. The fire, sparked by lightning from a nearby thunderstorm, burned though a total of 355 acres before it was finally contained around 1730 PST on the 30th. Three firefighters were treated for minor injuries while fighting the blaze. No damage was reported with this fire.

title: Drought: Texas, Aug 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from August 01, 2011 to August 31, 2011. Affected areas: Anderson, Bell, Bosque, Collin, Comanche, Cooke, Coryell, Dallas, Delta, Denton, Eastland, Ellis and 34 more areas. Episode summary: Drought conditions continued to worsen across much of the Fort Worth County Warning Area (CWA) during the month of August due to very little rainfall. All 46 counties in the Fort Worth CWA were experiencing at least severe drought conditions (D2) throughout the entire month, and all but portions of Tarrant, Dallas, and Denton counties were in at least extreme drought (D3) by the end of the month. Also, all areas except locations along the Interstate 20/30 corridors experienced exceptional drought (D4) at some point in the month. Ranchers continued to sell some of their cattle because they did not have sufficient water or grass to survive. Farmers were forced to harvest cotton crops three weeks early due to the drought conditions, and the size of the cotton crop was much smaller than normal. Area lakes and reservoirs continued to experience well below normal pool levels which led to some communities issuing water conservation notices for residents and businesses. One to three inches of rain did fall in the western portions of the CWA, near Eastland and Palo Pinto Counties, and this area did see some improvement in the drought conditions because of the rain. Details: According to the US Drought Monitor, the county was classified as exceptional drought (D4) throughout the month. The county received very little rainfall and conditions did not improve. title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from August 01, 2011 to August 03, 2011. Affected areas: Hutchinson. Episode summary: The Texas Forest Service reported that the Turkey Track Wildfire began about seven miles east of Stinnett Texas in Hutchinson County around 1246 CST. The wildfire threatened three homes and four other structures along with oil wells, pipelines, and power lines. However, no damages were reported. There were also no reports of injuries. A measured three thousand and sixty-one acres were consumed by the wildfire. The cause of the wildfire was still under investigation. The wildfire was controlled on August 3 at 1900 CST.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 02, 2011

The wildfire threatened one residence, a garage, a barn house, storage bins, a radio tower, two grain silos, and propane tanks. There were no reports of damages or injuries, however there were two misses. The wildfire consumed a measured five hundred and seventy-four acres. The wildfire was contained on August 3 at 1900 CST.

The wildfire was contained around 1800 CST.

The wildfire was caused by lightning and consumed an estimated four hundred acres. There were no reports of damages or injuries. The wildfire occurred in rough brushy terrain and was contained on August 26 around 0000 CST.
