title: Wildfire: Texas, Oct 07, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from October 07, 2011 to October 08, 2011. Affected areas: Bowie. Episode summary: Very breezy conditions, warm temperatures and low humidity values were the ingredients needed for the rapid spread of a wildfire in Bowie County, Texas near the town of Dekalb. The fire was reportedly started by the use of a cutting torch near a heavily wooded area near Hwy. 259 and C.R. 2735. Strong winds caused the fire to spread rapidly with near 1000 acres of timberland and grassland consumed. Ten separate fire departments were called in to battle the blaze. There were reports of injuries to Texas Forest Service personnel who were burned while battling the fire.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from August 03, 2011 to August 07, 2011. Affected areas: Jones, Menard, Taylor. Episode summary: Plenty of fuels, extremely dry and hot weather and breezy south winds produced near critical fire weather conditions in early August. As a result of these weather conditions, a few smaller size wildfires erupted across West Central Texas. Details: The Whitehead Fire located near the Menard and Concho County Line burned approximately 451 acres. The wildfire threatened two homes but were saved by the fire fighters. The Wimberly Fire near Wimberly Road and Farm to Market Road 1235 burned 406 acres. The fire burned tall grass 4 miles north of Merkel. Single-engine airtankers from Mineral Wells responded to the blaze. The CR-3116 Fore was located about 3 miles east of Anson and this fire burned about 300 acres. Some structures were threatened but none were damaged.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 15, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from August 15, 2011 to August 18, 2011. Affected areas: Mason, Nolan, Sutton. As a result of these weather conditions, a few wildfires erupted across West Central Texas. Details: The M and M Fire in Southwestern Nolan County near Maryneal burned about 652 acres. The Allison 412 Fire burned about 836 acres north of Interstate 10 in Sutton County approximately 16 miles east of Sonora. A tire blowout caused the fire. The Blockhouse Wildfire was started by a bulldozer. This fire burned approximately 386 acres about 7 miles east northeast of Hext.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 30, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from August 30, 2011 to August 31, 2011. Affected areas: Kimble, Menard, Sutton. Episode summary: Plenty of fuels, extremely dry and hot weather and breezy north winds caused by Tropical Storm Lee produced near critical fire weather conditions in late August. The stronger winds resulted in larger wildfires across parts of West Central Texas. Details: The Big Draw Wildfire continued into September. This fire had 50 foot flame lengths and short distance spotting early in its lifetime. Numerous volunteer fire departments responded. The Double T Wildfire burned approximately 300 acres in northeast Menard County. It was approximately 95 percent contained. The Rick Ranch Wildfire in southeast Sutton County continued into September. The fire burned approximately 330 acres in late August.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Aug 08, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from August 08, 2011 to August 08, 2011. Affected areas: Dane. Episode summary: An unusual tornado event occurred during the early evening hours of August 8th. A vigorous short wave moved across the region in the early evening hours. While deep layer wind shear was weak, there was enough instability, with CAPE values around 700 J/Kg, to produce strong enough updrafts to ingest low-level vorticity and stretch it to produce non-supercell tornadoes (land-spout variety). A weak EF0 tornado formed as a shower moved over a weak, west to east orientated low-level atmospheric boundary over Lake Monona in Madison, southeast of the State Capitol. Details: Law enforcement officials, as well as many members of the general public, reported a tornado that formed and stayed over Lake Monona, about 1 mile east of Law Park in the City of Madison. The tornado tracked south, then southeast, over the lake before dissipating west of Squaw Bay, about 1/4 mile north of Waunona Park. No damage was reported. title: Drought: Texas, Oct 04, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from October 04, 2011 to October 31, 2011. Affected areas: Zapata. Episode summary: A few showers and thunderstorms moved across the Rio Grande Plains on September 29th and again on October 1st, improving long term drought conditions slightly across Zapata County. Additional rainfall on October 9th would lock in Extreme (D3) conditions through month's end, with the usual dry season underway. Details: Rainfall on October 1st, and again on October 9th across Zapata County removed the area of Exceptional (D4) Drought in the northwest corner, leaving the entire county at Extreme (D3) levels on the 11th - conditions which prevailed into early November.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Wisconsin, Aug 02, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Flood, from August 02, 2011 to August 04, 2011. Affected areas: Douglas, Sawyer. Episode summary: Heavy rains on August 2nd resulted in major flooding of the Nemadji River and the tributary Black River. Many roads were washed out, including Wisconsin State Route 35. Specifically, the Nemadji River Gage, near Superior, reached the flood stage of 20 feet at 1230 PM CDT August 2nd, crested at 27.37 feet at 200 AM CDT August 3rd, and returned back below flood stage at 300 PM CDT August 4th. The crest was the highest ever reported for that gage. Details: Heavy rains on August 2nd resulted in major flooding of the Nemadji River and the tributary Black River. Many roads were washed out, including Wisconsin State Route 35. title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Aug 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from August 01, 2011 to August 02, 2011. Affected areas: Douglas. Episode summary: A stationary front remained across central Minnesota and central Wisconsin early August 1st. Weak low pressure moved eastward along the front, bringing tropical moisture as it crossed the upper St Croix Valley early August 2nd, triggering severe thunderstorms with very heavy rain through August 2nd. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches was common. Flooding resulted in the Nemadji River basin. Details: Rainfall was 3.25 inches since 701 PM CDT the previous evening.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Aug 13, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from August 13, 2011 to August 14, 2011. Affected areas: Tom Green. Episode summary: An outflow boundary from convection across North Texas produced heavy rain as it moved south across the Big Country during the night time. During the morning hours on August 13, the outflow boundary went stationary around San Angelo. As a weaker boundary from the south collided with the aforementioned boundary in a very moist atmosphere, extremely heavy rainfall of 3 to 8 inches fell across the City of San Angelo and resulted in flash flooding. On the morning of the 14th, more heavy rain formed and caused some flash flooding just north of San Angelo. Details: Flooding was reported at Pierce and Colorado Streets in San Angelo. The water had risen above the tires of the vehicles. Two cars were stranded in water on Foster road which is located on the east side of San Angelo near the Department of Public Safety Office. More cars were reportedly stranded in deep water at College Hills and Sunset Avenue.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from August 01, 2011 to August 08, 2011. Affected areas: Bell, Jack, Kaufman, Lampasas, Mills. Episode summary: Elevated fire weather conditions persisted for most of the month due to the extreme heat and the ongoing historic drought. Many wildfires occurred during the month burning over 40,000 acres of land, several homes, and lots of personal property. From the 1st through the 5th, there were 6 grass fires that caused damage. The largest and most damaging of these fires was the 1701-acre Center City Fire that occurred in Mills County. Details: The Post Oak Fire began on August 1st, was contained on the 3rd, and fully controlled on the 4th. The fire started approximately 9 miles north of Jacksboro and burned 571 acres. A small acre fire just off Hwy 36 in Rogers destroyed a vacant mobile home. It was believed that a piece of farm equipment may have sparked the fire. A 30-acre fire on CR 3830 in Adamsville burned several metal barns, two cars, and some farm equipment. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,469,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 07, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from August 07, 2011 to August 15, 2011. Affected areas: Erath, Grayson, Jack, Lampasas, Mclennan. Many wildfires occurred during the month burning over 40,000 acres of land, several homes, and lots of personal property. From the 6th through the 10th, there were 5 grass fires that caused damage. The largest and most damaging of these fires was the 7328-acre Cherry Homes Fire in northern Jack County. A 3840-acre fire also occurred in northern Grayson County. Details: The Cherry Homes fire burned approximately 7328 acres of range land. It started approximately 13 miles northeast of Jacksboro at Cundiff Crafton Road. The fire started on the 7th from a campfire, was contained on the 10th, and controlled on the 14th. A travel trailer and a barn were destroyed in the fire. A small acre fire consumed two vacant mobile homes near FM 914 and FM 847, approximately 3.5 miles south of Stephenville. A 20-acre grass fire near CR 4820 in Kempner destroyed a mobile home. Reported property and crop damage: about $333,000.

Many wildfires occurred during the month burning over 40,000 acres of land, several homes, and lots of personal property. From the 11th through the 15th, there were 4 grass fires that caused damage. The largest of these fires was the 1320-acre Ranger Hill Fire in Eastland County. This fire did not damage any structures. Details: A tree limb fell on a power line and sparked a grass fire the burned 464 acres near Todd City. The Todd City fire was centered near the intersection of FM 19 and CR 335 in the northeastern part of the county. The fire began on the 15th, was contained on the 15th, and then fully controlled on the 20th. title: Wildfire: Texas, Aug 16, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from August 16, 2011 to August 31, 2011. Affected areas: Coryell, Dallas, Hunt, Johnson, Navarro, Robertson, Tarrant. Two large fires were started on the Fort Hood Military Base artillery training area. A grass fire in Hunt County burned a junkyard for boats and tires, and other fires burned homes in Dallas and Tarrant counties. Details: A grass fire damaged a group of vacant manufactured homes off Jimmy Lane in Combine. One home was destroyed and five others were badly damaged. Only one of the homes was occupied at the time. A few vehicles and some sheds were also burned in the fire. A small 2-acre grass fire near CRs 917 and 918 burned 62 round bales of hay. This fire was located just east of Cresson and was started by an electrical line. One firefighter had to be transported for heat exhaustion. A small fire near Hemphill Street and Loop 820 in southern Tarrant County burned a few bales of hay. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,708,500.

title: Drought: Texas, Aug 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from August 01, 2011 to August 31, 2011. Affected areas: Archer, Baylor, Clay, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: The exceptional drought maintained its cruel grip over western north Texas during the month of August. Beneficial rainfall that occurred north of the Red River amounted to at most an inch and the climbing precipitation deficits that began during the late summer and early autumn of 2010 continued. The agricultural industry has obviously taken a huge hit from their crops to their cattle. The shortage of hay this year has caused farmers to sell the majority of their cattle, with some of them selling off their entire herd. Farm ponds are down to their last puddle. Most water that remains is hot and stagnant, making it useless. The long-range forecast is for La Nina to establish itself once again by later this year, with below normal precipitation and above normal temperatures.

One secondary structure was lost in this complex. The fire complex was 100 percent contained. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from September 26, 2011 to September 30, 2011. Affected areas: Coleman, Crockett, Haskell, Shackelford. Episode summary: A cold front brought strong northeast winds and dry air to create ideal conditions for these wildifires to develop in late September. Details: The lightning induced Mitchell 3 Fire was located in the extreme part of southwest Crockett County. Several oil field structures were threatened and fire crews were working in rough terrain. The 700 acre Crooked River Ranch Wildfire started in Haskell County and burned south into extreme northern Shackelford County. One structure was threatened and saved. Three homes were threatened and saved but two outbuildings were lost in the fire. The fire was fully extinguished.

title: Flood, Wildfire: California, Sep 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, Wildfire, from September 10, 2011 to September 30, 2011. Affected areas: Kern, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Mtns, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: A dry southwest flow aloft set up over the area on the 6th along the leading edge of a upper level trough over the Pacific Northwest and northern California, bringing dry weather through the 8th. However, an upper level low moved from the Great Basin into central California on the 9th. This atypical movement of the low occurred because it was cut off from the prevailing westerly winds aloft. These systems usually move into the area from the Pacific Ocean. This low changed the flow aloft over the region to southeasterly, drawing moisture into central California from Arizona and northwestern Mexico. This warm, unstable airmass brought showers and thunderstorms to much of interior central California from the 9th through the 14th. Isolated thunderstorms continued over the Sierra Nevada crest on the 15th, as residual moisture remained over the area while the southeasterly flow transitioned to a more southwesterly direction. ||The low meandered across central and southern California during these several days. This low allowed for unstable conditions over the entire district; quite a few locations in the San Joaquin Valley received at least a trace of rain. On the 9th, thunderstorms produced little rainfall, but they did cause quite a few wildfires due to lightning over the mountains in Kern County (around Keene, Breckenridge, and just to the east of Arvin and Bakersfield). As for the 10th, numerous thunderstorms developed over Kern County and much of the southern San Joaquin Valley during the evening. Just above the ground, and in wind protected hollows, temperatures fell into the 20s; local hard freezes, defined as 2 or more hours with temperatures below 28 degrees, likely occurred. Agricultural damage was not known as of this writing. title: Strong Wind: Texas, Nov 26, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, from November 26, 2011 to November 27, 2011. Affected areas: Coastal Cameron. Episode summary: A strong cold front whipped across the Lower Rio Grande Valley late on November 26th and early on the 27th, followed by occasional Gale force wind gusts which continued into the morning hours. Gusts at the South Padre Island Coast Guard Station and Port Isabel C-MAN site ranged from 40 to 49 mph between 10 PM and 4 AM; Gusts exceeded 40 mph at the South Padre Island Heliport on the south side of the resort town. These gusts collapsed a protective awning at a car wash. Details: An off duty NWS Employee reported a collapsed awning over a car wash facility during the morning of November 27th, after a night of frequent wind gusts to or above 40 mph. Peak gusts at the South Padre Island Heliport reached 41 mph (1135 PM/26th), but the nearby U.S. Coast Guard station had a peak gust to 49 mph (10 PM/26th). title: Dust Storm: California, Jul 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, from July 03, 2011 to July 03, 2011. Affected areas: Imperial County Except The Lower Colorado River Valley. Episode summary: Isolated thunderstorms developed over portions of Imperial and Riverside counties during the early morning hours on July 3rd. Gusty thunderstorm outflow winds as high as 50 mph produced dense blowing sand and dust, especially across central Imperial county. Visibilities down to zero miles led to the issuance of multiple dust storm warnings. Details: Isolated thunderstorms developed across portions of Imperial county during the very early morning hours on July 3rd. The storms generated strong gusty outflow winds which led to dense blowing dust and sand in the area around Brawley. At 115 am, a trained weather spotter 3 miles southeast of Alamoria reported zero visibility in blowing dust. Winds were estimated to be between 40 and 50 mph.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Oct 05, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from October 05, 2011 to October 06, 2011. Affected areas: Apple And Lucerne Valleys, San Bernardino County Mountains, San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: A large upper-level low pressure system brought a strong cold front through southern California the 4th through the 6th, providing widespread moderate rain, well below normal temperatures and strong gusty winds. Most areas west of the mountains received 3/4 - 1 1/2 inches of rain, with higher amounts of 2 inches or more in the mountains and coastal slopes. This storm packed the highest rainfall totals for mountain locations like Idyllwild since 2004. Light amounts of snow were also seen at the highest elevations. Strong winds also led to downed power lines and overturned vehicles in Lucerne Valley. Details: Strong winds began at the Harrison Park RAWS between 1400 and 1500 PST and ended between 1700 and 1800 PST. During this time, high winds were reached with a gust of 59 mph between 1610 and 1620 PST. High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1000 and 1100 PST and ended between 2000 and 2100 PST. During this time, a wind gust of 65 mph was recorded between 1100 and 1200 PST and a gust of 68 mph was recorded between 1900 and 2000 PST. Strong winds forced a big rig with an empty trailer into oncoming traffic on Highway 18 near Rabbit Springs Road in Lucerne Valley, causing an accident involving three vehicles. Three people were injured in the accident. Exact wind speed at the time of the incident is unknown.||Strong winds also downed power lines in Lucerne Valley during this time. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Oct 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from October 01, 2011 to October 31, 2011. Affected areas: Atascosa, Bandera, Bastrop, Bexar, Blanco, Burnet, Caldwell, Comal, De Witt, Dimmit, Edwards, Fayette and 21 more areas. Episode summary: The La Nina event strengthened slightly during October according to the Climate Prediction Center, and the drought continued over South Central Texas. Most of the area remains in exceptional drought conditions (Stage D4). Some welcome rain during the 6th through the 8th brought some relief. Rainfall totals between one half and six inches moved Atascosa, Bexar, Dimmit, Uvalde, Val Verde, and Zavala counties into the extreme drought category (Stage D3). Kinney and Maverick counties remained in the extreme category at the end of the month, and all the other counties remain in exceptional drought. Fire danger in South Central Texas remained high to very high and burn bans continued for all of the counties. At the end of the month the seven day stream flow average remained in the below or much below normal range for basins across South Central Texas and the Rio Grande Plains. Area lakes and reservoirs remained well below normal pool elevations with Lake Travis around 54 feet below normal and Medina Lake near 47 feet below. The Edwards Aquifer rose slightly with the rains at the beginning of the month and was 20.1 feet below normal and 26.5 feet below the level from one year ago. The City of Kerrville remained in Stage 4 water restrictions, while the San Antonio Water System (SAWS), City of San Marcos, and City of Austin remained in Stage 2. Many other communities across South Central Texas continued with some level of water restrictions. title: Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 02, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from December 02, 2011 to December 03, 2011. Affected areas: Hale, Lubbock. Episode summary: An upper level storm system tracked over the South Plains of West Texas during the day on the second. This disturbance and abundant low level moisture created widespread freezing drizzle across region. Light ice accumulations were quickly observed after precipitation began. title: High Wind: Wisconsin, Oct 19, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: High Wind, from October 19, 2011 to October 20, 2011. Affected areas: Kenosha, Milwaukee, Racine. Episode summary: Rapidly developing low pressure moved across western Ohio and southeast Lower Michigan during the overnight period of October 19th and morning of October 20th. An associated strong pressure gradient and unstable conditions over the relatively warmer waters of Lake Michigan allowed strong gusty north to northeast winds to mix down to the lake surface and push inland from Milwaukee south to the Illinois border. Wind gusts reached 50 to 70 mph along the lake shore...and up to 51 mph inland. In downtown Milwaukee, wind and debris broke a few windows in the U.S. Bank tower. Elsewhere...some weak trees were uprooted and there were many reports of broken tree branches. This tree debris damaged at least a couple homes and resulted in scattered power outages as power-lines came down. The strong winds and high waves caused extensive damage to several boats and docks at the South Shore Yacht Club in Milwaukee. Refer to the separate Marine Strong Wind event within Storm Data for details. Details: A peak wind gust of 61 mph (53 knots) was measured at the Kenosha Harbor Great Lakes Observation System site. Details: Tornado touchdown near FM 163 and SH 321 was based on witness report. Damage was intermittent along a path from that point to near the intersection of FM 2286 and FM 2287 where a trailer was overturned and one woman was injured. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000.

title: Winter Storm: California, Nov 05, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Storm, from November 05, 2011 to November 06, 2011. Affected areas: Mt Shasta/Western Plumas County, West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A winter storm moved quickly across Northern California, bringing snow down to 4000 feet and a foot or more of snow to the Sierra Nevada passes. Details: Periods of heavy snow fell above 4000 feet and resulted in up to a foot of snow falling near 6000 feet and more than a foot of snow at the highest elevations. Eleven inches of snow fell at Kingvale on Interstate 80 and eight inches of snow fell over Echo Summit. Locally gusty winds resulted in poor visibilities in some areas but mostly at the pass level. Periods of heavy snow fell above 4000 feet and resulted in up to a foot of snow near 6000 feet and more than a foot of snow at the highest elevations. Nine inches of snow fell over the Yuba Pass. Locally gusty winds resulted in poor visibilities in some areas but mostly at the pass level.

title: High Wind: California, Nov 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from November 01, 2011 to November 02, 2011. Affected areas: San Bernardino And Riverside County Valleys - The Inland Empire, Santa Ana Mountains And Foothills. Episode summary: An inside slider upper-level low pressure system, passing just north of southern California and then across the Great Basin, resulted in strong sustained and gusty northerly winds across much of the Inland Empire and Santa Ana Mountains. Several sites recorded sustained winds of 40-50 mph with gusts over 60 mph. Minor wind damage was reported with this event. A traffic light was blown down in Rancho Cucamonga and a sign blown down onto the freeway near Yorba Linda. A few small brush fires also broke out near Rincon and along the 15 freeway in San Diego County. Details: High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 2230 and 2330 PST on the 1st and ended between 1030 and 1130 PST on the 2nd. During that time, a peak gust of 81 mph was measured between 0330 and 0430 PST on the 2nd.|Nearby, a large sign was blown down on the 91 freeway near Highway 55. High winds began at the Highland Springs RAWS between 0415 and 0515 PST and ended between 1015 and 1115 PST on the 2nd. Between 0815 and 0915 PST, a peak gust of 64 mph was measured. High winds began at the Tonner Canyon RAWS between 0600 and 0700 PST on the 2nd and ended between 1100 and 1200 PST. During that time, winds gusted consistently above 50 mph with a peak gust of 60 mph measured between 1000 and 1100 PST. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Winter Weather: California, Nov 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from November 03, 2011 to November 05, 2011. Affected areas: San Bernardino County Mountains. Episode summary: A strong upper-level low pressure system off coast of the Pacific Northwest trailed a cold front through Southern California, bringing 3 days of widespread moderate to heavy rainfall, along with gusty winds. Rainfall amounts over this three-day period were substantial, but did not cause significant flooding. Many areas west of the mountains received 1 to 2 inches of rain, and locally higher where thunderstorms occurred. The snow level, for this first significant snowfall of the season, lowered to between 3500 and 4000 feet, dropping 2 to 6 inches of snow to the mountains above that elevation. As a result, widespread chain control was put in place for these mountain locations. Cold, unstable air behind the front set off scattered thunderstorms as well. The storms near the Banning Pass had accumulations of several inches of pea-sized hail. Despite the high rainfall totals, no significant flooding occurred with this system. Details: This storm marked the first significant snow of the season for the San Bernardino County Mountains. A spotter in Running Springs reported 5 inches for the storm total, while another spotter in Forest Falls reported a storm total of 4 inches.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Nov 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from November 10, 2011 to November 12, 2011. Affected areas: San Diego County Valleys. Episode summary: A strong, cut-off low pressure system dropped south along the Southern California coast and moved directly across San Diego and northern Baja, bringing 2 days of widespread moderate to heavy rainfall, along with gusty winds, mostly on the 12th. Rainfall amounts over this two-day period were substantial, with locally heavy rainfall rates, providing northern areas west of the mountains with .25 to .50 inch of rain, and one to two inches over the vast majority of San Diego County, even spilling over into the deserts. Lindbergh Field had a peak rainfall rate of 0.40 inches per hour and nearly reached their daily rainfall record with a daily total of 1.4 inches. Urban-type street flooding occurred with this system, dumping up to 1000 cfs of water into the San Diego River on the 12th. Details: CBS 8 via Twitter reported a large tree down on power lines leaving 1500 customers without power. There were no nearby wind reports, but nearby gusts were measured around 40 mph out of the east. High winds began at the Otay Mountain SDGE mesonet site between 0910 and 0920 PST on the 10th and ended between 1030 and 1040 PST. During this time, several gusts over 58 mph were recorded with a peak gust of 63 mph measured between 0910 and 0920 PST. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Storm Surge/Tide: California, Nov 24, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Storm Surge/Tide, from November 24, 2011 to November 25, 2011. Affected areas: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore. Episode summary: Tidal flooding was reported in Marin County on both November 24 and November 25, 2011. Details: At approximately 0930PST on November 24, 2011 northbound US 101 connector to northbound SR 1 was closed due to flooding. The roadway reopened at 1346 hours. At approximately 1030PST on November 25, 2011 northbound US 101 connector to northbound SR 1 was closed due to flooding. The roadway reopened at 1316 hours.

title: Strong Wind: California, Nov 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, from November 01, 2011 to November 01, 2011. Affected areas: North Bay Interior Valleys. Episode summary: Strong winds during the evening of November 1, 2011 cut power, downed trees, and damaged a mobile home in Calistoga, CA. Details: In Calistoga, CA emergency officials responded to nine calls between 2200 and 2300PST for wind damage. Damage included fallen trees, large tree limbs, and a metal awning ripped from a home in Chateau Calistoga Mobile Home Park. Reported property and crop damage: about $17,000.

title: Strong Wind: California, Nov 18, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, from November 18, 2011 to November 18, 2011. Affected areas: East Bay Interior Valleys. Episode summary: Gusty winds during the late morning of Friday November 18, 2011 caused an injury. Details: A worker in a crane was burned around 1120PST Friday November 18, 2011 when a gust of wind blew him into a power line. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Nov 30, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from November 30, 2011 to November 30, 2011. Affected areas: North Bay Interior Valleys, Northern Monterey Bay, San Francisco Bay Shoreline, Santa Clara Valley Including San Jose, Santa Cruz Mountains, Santa Lucia Mountains And Los Padres National Forest. Episode summary: A wind event from November 30, 2011 to December 2, 2011 caused damage and one fatality across the San Francisco and Monterey Bay areas. The fatality occurred on November 30, 2011. Wind damage occurred from November 30, 2011 through December 2, 2011. Details: Strong winds knocked down trees and downed power lines in Corralitos between 1500 and 1900PST. Falling trees also took down a transmission line in the Scotts Valley area. About 190 customers lost power when strong winds knocked a wire down around 1840PST near Hagan Road and Olive Hill Lane in Napa. Wind gusted to 54 mph at Chabot and 51 mph at Pt. San Pablo. Reported property and crop damage: about $328,300.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Dec 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from December 01, 2011 to December 03, 2011. Affected areas: East Bay Hills And The Diablo Range, East Bay Interior Valleys, North Bay Interior Valleys, Northern Monterey Bay, San Francisco Bay Shoreline, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Santa Cruz Mountains, Santa Lucia Mountains And Los Padres National Forest. Episode summary: Strong winds affected the San Francisco Bay and Monterey Bay area causing damage and one fatality. The fatality occurred on November 30, 2011 and is in the November, 2011 StormData summary. Damages from November 30, 2011 are also in the November, 2011 StormData summary. Damages from December 1-3, 2011 will be in the December, 2011 StormData summary. Details: High winds were blamed for speeding a fire that destroyed two homes and damaged a third in North Livermore near May Nissen Park. Even though the fire's cause is under investigation high winds had a significant effect on this event. Numerous road closures occurred in the Santa Cruz Mountains due to numerous trees and power lines down. The Highland Peak RAWS, located at 2,490 feet, reported a peak wind gusts of 75 mph at 0020 PST. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,256,000.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Dec 31, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from December 31, 2011 to December 31, 2011. Affected areas: Barron, Polk, Rusk. Episode summary: A storm system developed across the Central Plains Saturday morning, December 31st, and quickly intensified and moved east across the Midwest by Sunday morning, January 1st. It created a large area of rain during the afternoon, and early evening across southern and eastern Minnesota, as well as west-central Wisconsin before quickly turning over to a period of heavy wet snow New Years Eve. Although snowfall amounts averaged between 3 and 5 inches, the quick nature of the turn over from rain to snow, the abnormally warm early Winter season over the Upper Midwest, and due to the holiday, a winter storm warning was issued for portions of west-central Wisconsin. Due to the intense and quick nature of the heavy wet snow, numerous accidents occurred during the height of the storm. Details: Four to five inches of heavy wet snow fell during the evening of Saturday, December 31st. The quick turnover to snow, the time of day, and the holiday celebration caused several accidents across the county. Four to five inches of heavy wet snow fell during the evening of Saturday, December 31st. The quick turnover to snow, the time of day, and the holiday celebration caused several accidents across the county. Most of the heavy snow fell before midnight, but an inch or two did occur past midnight.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 02, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 02, 2011 to November 02, 2011. Affected areas: Dallam, Hartley, Moore. Episode summary: A cold front pushed across the Texas Panhandle and produced strong gradient non-thunderstorm sustained winds, mainly across the northwest sections of the Texas Panhandle, during the afternoon hours. There were no reports of damage or injuries.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from December 31, 2011 to December 31, 2011. Affected areas: Childress, Hall. Strong pressure rises behind this front lead to high winds across the southeastern Texas panhandle. title: Drought: Texas, Jan 01, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from January 01, 2012 to January 31, 2012. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hockley and 11 more areas. Episode summary: All exceptional (D4) drought was absent from the area at the beginning of January. However, a very dry month lead to the reintroduction of exceptional conditions on the South Plains by the end of the month. Only two light precipitation events occurred during January and these two events did not bring much precipitation. Hall county remained in Abnormally Dry (D0) conditions.||Very warm and dry conditions persisted through the start of 2012. Temperatures averaged around four degrees above normal with only 5% of normal precipitation received. Lubbock Preston Smith International Airport recorded only 0.01 of precipitation while Childress Municipal Airport recorded 0.03. A few isolated areas received up to 0.3 liquid equivalent during the month. Significant weather systems did move across West Texas and brought record precipitation to areas south of the South Plains and Rolling Plains. Keetch-Byram Drought Index values had slightly increased across all areas. Values ranged from 500-600 across the western South Plains to 300-400 across the southern Rolling Plains.||Agricultural and livestock losses remained steady through the first month of the year. Soil moisture as a whole was depleted in January after repeated rounds of warm, dry and windy conditions. A severe wind and blowing dust event on January 22nd heavily damaged or destroyed many winter wheat crops. Most cotton farmers were beginning to prepare fields and reported very poor deep soil moisture below eight inches. Livestock was generally reported to be in fair condition.||Economic losses due to drought through January since the drought began were estimated near $2.4 billion. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000,000.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Nov 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from November 09, 2011 to November 09, 2011. Affected areas: Juneau, Monroe. Episode summary: Low pressure pushed into the Great Lakes region and spread a band of heavy snow over parts of central Wisconsin in the morning hours of November 9th. Volunteer snowfall observers estimated 6.5 inches near Wilton (Monroe County) and 8 inches near Mauston (Juneau County). There were many accidents across much of southwest into central Wisconsin, especially since the bulk of the snow fell during the morning commute time. Details: A volunteer observer estimated 6.5 inches of snow four miles east of Wilton. A volunteer observer estimated 8 inches of snow one mile south of Mauston.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Dec 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from December 03, 2011 to December 04, 2011. Affected areas: Trempealeau. Episode summary: Seven people were injured in two separate accidents as a result of slippery roads across Trempealeau County. One person was injured in the first accident near Whitehall. This accident occurred after light freezing rain fell in the morning hours of December 3rd. Six people were injured, two of them seriously, in the second accident near Arcadia. This occurred when 3 to 4 inches of snow created slippery roads during the evening of December 3rd. Details: A woman was injured in an early morning accident near Whitehall after she lost control of her vehicle on an ice covered road. Light freezing rain had occurred during the early morning hours of December 3rd. Six people were injured, two of them seriously, in a two vehicle accident south of Arcadia during the late afternoon of December 3rd. Three to four inches of snow had fallen creating slippery roads resulting in the accident. The two serious injuries were the result of the occupants being ejected from the vehicle. Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Nov 15, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from November 15, 2011 to November 15, 2011. Affected areas: San Jacinto. Episode summary: A thunderstorm produced a weak tornado that caused little damage. Details: A funnel cloud sighted by fire department and rescue people touched down twice in a pasture. Swirling dirt was evident near the intersection of FM 1725 and Tony Tap Road. There was little damage caused by this EF0 tornado.

title: High Wind: California, Nov 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from November 01, 2011 to November 02, 2011. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Clarita Valley, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area, Ventura County Coast, Ventura County Coastal Valleys, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: Strong surface high pressure in the Great Basin along with strong north to northeast flow aloft generated strong Santa Ana winds across Ventura and Los Angeles counties. North to northeast wind gusts up to 83 MPH were reported in the mountains while gusts to 59 MPH were reported across the coastal plain. Details: The Camarillo ASOS reported sustained northeast winds of 45 MPH with a gust to 59 MPH. The Wiley Ridge RAWS reported sustained northeast winds between 40 and 42 MPH and gusts as high as 65 MPH. The sensor at Laguna Peak reported northeast wind gusts between 72 and 83 MPH.

title: High Wind: California, Nov 30, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from November 30, 2011 to November 30, 2011. Affected areas: Los Angeles County San Fernando Valley. Episode summary: On the evening of 30th, a strong north to northeast wind event developed across sections of Southern California as a cold front swept across the area. Widespread wind gusts between 60 and 70 MPH were reported across the mountains of Ventura county as well as the mountains and valleys of Los Angeles county from the evening of the 30th through December 1st. Widespread power outages were reported, especially across the San Gabriel Valley where over 350,000 residents lost power. In the city of Pasadena, significant wind damage was reported with at least 42 buildings red-tagged due to wind damage. Along with the power outages, numerous trees were uprooted or severely damaged from La Canada-Flintridge to Monrovia. Strong northerly cross winds at Los Angeles International Airport resulted in 23 flights being diverted to Ontario International Airport. Details: A trained spotter in Glendale reported northerly wind gusts to 60 MPH.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 01, 2011 to December 02, 2011. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Los Angeles County San Fernando Valley, Los Angeles County San Gabriel Valley, Santa Clarita Valley, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: On December 1st, a strong north to northeast wind event, which developed on November 30th, continued across sections of Southern California. Widespread wind gusts between 60 and 70 MPH were reported across the mountains of Ventura county as well as the mountains and valleys of Los Angeles county through December 1st. Widespread power outages were reported, especially across the San Gabriel Valley where over 350,000 residents lost power. In the city of Pasadena, significant wind damage was reported with at least 42 buildings red-tagged due to wind damage. Along with the power outages, numerous trees were uprooted or severely damaged from La Canada-Flintridge to Monrovia. Strong northerly cross winds at Los Angeles International Airport resulted in 23 flights being diverted to Ontario International Airport. Details: Widespread strong north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Ventura County. Wind gusts between 60 and 70 MPH were reported. The San Rafael Hills RAWS sensor reported north to northeast wind gusts between 61 and 71 MPH. Additionally, trained weather spotters throughout the San Fernando Valley reported wind gusts in excess of 60 MPH. The Santa Fe Dam RAWS sensor reported north to northeast wind gusts between 58 and 68 MPH. Additionally, trained weather spotters in Pasadena reported wind gusts in excess of 60 MPH.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 05, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 05, 2011 to December 05, 2011. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: On December 5th, the second strong Santa Ana wind event brought strong and gusty north to northeast winds to the mountains of Ventura and Los Angeles counties. Wind gusts between 58 and 79 MPH were reported. Details: The sensor at Laguna Peak reported north to northeast wind gusts between 64 and 79 MPH. Strong and widespread north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Los Angeles County. Wind gusts between 58 and 62 MPH were reported by several RAWS sensors, including Acton, Camp Nine, Chilao, and Warm Springs. Strong and widespread north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Ventura County. Wind gusts in excess of 58 MPH were reported across sections of the mountains.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 16, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 16, 2011 to December 17, 2011. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Clarita Valley, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: Another round of strong and gusty north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Ventura and Los Angeles counties as well as the Santa Clarita Valley. Wind gusts between 58 and 78 MPH were reported. Details: Strong and gusty north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Los Angeles County. At the Camp Nine sensor, wind gusts between 58 and 78 MPH were reported. Additionally, wind gusts between 58 and 67 MPH were reported at the Mill Creek and Chilao RAWS sensors. Strong and gusty north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Ventura County. Wind gusts between 60 and 70 MPH were reported across the eastern half of the mountains. title: High Wind: California, Dec 22, 2011

Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area, Ventura County Coastal Valleys, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: In late December, a fourth round of strong and gusty north to northeast winds developed across sections of Ventura and Los Angeles Counties. In the mountain areas, wind gusts between 58 and 71 MPH were reported while some valley locations in Ventura County reported wind gusts between 58 and 65 MPH. Details: The Wiley Ridge RAWS sensor reported northeast wind gusts between 58 and 65 MPH. The Malibu Hills RAWS sensor reported north to northeast wind gusts of 64 MPH. Strong and gusty north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Los Angeles County. The strongest wind gusts were reported at the Chilao sensor (58 to 71 MPH) and the Warm Springs sensor (58 to 70 MPH). Additionally, the Camp Nine sensor reported wind gusts between 58 and 64 MPH.

title: High Wind: California, Jan 07, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from January 07, 2012 to January 08, 2012. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: In early January, the first significant Santa Ana wind event developed across the mountains of Ventura and Los Angeles Counties. North to northeast wind gusts between 58 and 83 MPH were reported. Details: The Topanga RAWS sensor reported north to northeast wind gusts of 63 MPH. Strong and gusty north to northeast wind developed across the mountains of Los Angeles County. The Camp Nine RAWS sensor reported the highest gusts between 58 and 83 MPH. Strong and gusty north to northeast wind developed across the mountains of Ventura County. Wind gusts in excess of 75 MPH were reported in some locations.

title: Winter Storm, Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 09, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, Winter Weather, from January 09, 2012 to January 09, 2012. Affected areas: Garza, Lubbock, Terry, Yoakum. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from November 07, 2011 to November 07, 2011. Affected areas: Wilbarger. The tornado was only briefly in the county before it crossed the river into Jackson county, Oklahoma. Details: This tornado began over far northern Wilbarger county before quickly moving into Jackson county, OK and continuing into Tillman county. No known damage occurred with this portion of the tornado.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Nov 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from November 09, 2011 to November 09, 2011. Affected areas: Florence, Forest, Langlade, Menominee, Northern Marinette, Northern Oconto, Oneida, Outagamie, Portage, Shawano, Waupaca, Waushara. Episode summary: The first winter storm of the season dumped heavy, wet snow across central and northeast Wisconsin as a low pressure system moved from Oklahoma to central Lake Michigan. A band of 6 to 9 inches of snow fell from the Waupaca area (Waupaca Co.) to the city of Florence (Florence Co.). There were brief bursts of heavy snow at Green Bay (Brown Co.), where thunder accompanied the snow around 2 pm CST.||Power outages occurred in Oneida, Marathon, Langlade, Waupaca and Shawano counties as the wet snow caused tree limbs to break. At the height of the storm, more than 15,000 customers were without power. Hundreds of vehicle accidents occurred on the slippery roads across the area.||Some of the highest snowfall totals included 9.2 inches at Long Lake (Forest Co.), 9.0 inches at Rhinelander (Oneida Co.), 8.3 inches at Laona (Forest Co.), 7.0 inches at Iola (Waupaca Co.) and 6.2 inches at Wild Rose (Waushara Co.).||Heavy rain preceded the snow in east central Wisconsin. In Green Bay, 2.20 inches of precipitation fell on the 8th and 9th, making it the third wettest November storm in over 100 years of record-keeping.

title: Lake-Effect Snow: Wisconsin, Nov 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Lake-Effect Snow, from November 10, 2011 to November 10, 2011. Affected areas: Vilas. Parts of northwest Vilas County received more than 8 inches of snow. The highest totals were 8.8 inches at Presque Isle, 8.4 inches two miles east of Presque Isle and 8.0 inches at Boulder Junction.

title: Drought: Texas, Dec 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from December 01, 2011 to December 31, 2011. Affected areas: Anderson, Bell, Bosque, Coryell, Delta, Ellis, Falls, Freestone, Hamilton, Henderson, Hill, Hopkins and 13 more areas. Episode summary: December was another wet month for North Texas and drought conditions continued to improve. Most counties received 3-6 inches of rainfall throughout the month which helped many southern counties be downgraded into extreme drought (D3). However, the ground was still dry and absorbed much of the rain, and the water did not run into area lakes. Many municipalities continued water restrictions due to the low lake levels. By the end of the month, only 21 out of the 46 counties in the Fort Worth County Warning Area remained in severe drought (D2) or worse and only 3 counties had burn bans in effect. Details: According to the US Drought Monitor, the county was classified as severe drought (D2) at the beginning of the month. The county received up to 6 inches of rainfall and was classified as moderate drought (D1) at the end of the month. According to the US Drought Monitor, the county was classified as exceptional drought (D4) at the beginning of the month. The county received up to 6 inches of rainfall and was classified as extreme drought (D3) at the end of the month. According to the US Drought Monitor, the county was classified as extreme drought (D3) throughout the month. The county received up to 6 inches of rainfall but drought conditions did not improve. Reported property and crop damage: about $194,000.

title: Heavy Rain, High Wind: California, Nov 19, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, High Wind, from November 19, 2011 to November 20, 2011. Affected areas: Coachella Valley, Riverside. Episode summary: A closed upper level low pressure system dropped south along the Southern California coast and moved inland across San Diego and northern Baja, bringing 2 days of widespread heavy rainfall, along with gusty winds ahead of the precipitation and mountain snow. Rainfall amounts from the 20th-21st were 1 to 1.5 inches west of the mountains and areas below the snow level of around 5000 feet, resulting in an Urban and Small Stream flood advisory due to minor flooding on freeway ramps and other streets in western San Diego County. The month of November also ended around 300% of normal for monthly rainfall at Lindbergh Field, due in part to this event. Above 5000 feet, many areas received significant snow amounts, the highest being above 7000 feet in the San Bernardino County Mountains. Above 7000 feet, the Mountain High ski resort received 10 inches of snow with this storm, while the Onyx Peak and Wrightwood areas received 4-6 inches of snow. Big Bear and other areas between 6000 and 7000 feet received 2-4 inches. All of the areas above the snow level had chain controls in place for this event. Details: The Weather Currents station at Beaumont-Calimesa received 1.17 inches of rain in the hour between 1900 and 2000 PST on the 20th and a total of 1.61 inches for the day. High winds began in the Coachella Valley between 0950 and 1050 PST and ended between 1250 and 1350 PST on the 19th. During that time, two gusts of 58 mph were measured at the Whitewater RAWS between 0950 and 1150 PST.

title: Drought: Texas, Nov 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from November 01, 2011 to November 30, 2011. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, from December 04, 2011 to December 05, 2011. Affected areas: Martin, Scurry. Lift was great enough for thundersnow, which likely contributed to a couple of areas receiving higher snowfall amounts. Details: Four inches of snowfall was reported in Lenorah, which is located approximately 6 miles east of Tarzan. Thunderstorms aided a rapid phase change to snow with the heaviest snowfall occurring after the precipitation changeover. Four inches of snowfall was reported 2 miles southwest of Knapp, which is approximately 14 miles west/southwest of Snyder.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from November 04, 2011 to November 04, 2011. Affected areas: Nueces. Episode summary: A wildfire spread across land north to northeast of Bishop. Episode summary: Much needed rainfall fell over western north Texas during parts of November, which did a little to alleviate the horrendous drought that had plagued the region for much of the year. title: Wildfire: Texas, Jan 16, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 16, 2012 to January 16, 2012. Affected areas: Hockley. Episode summary: Widespread strong winds developed over the South Plains during the morning and afternoon hours of the 16th. A utility line was blown down around 1145 CST along Texas Highway 114 west of Levelland (Hockley County). The start time of the fire was coincident with a wind gust to 57 mph at the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site near Levelland. The wildfire burned 681 acres of mostly grassland.

title: Strong Wind: Texas, Jan 16, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, from January 16, 2012 to January 16, 2012. Affected areas: Cherokee. Episode summary: Strong pressure gradient winds from the south resulted in sustained wind speeds near 20 mph with gusts as highs as 40 mph across all of Northeast Texas during the afternoon hours of January 16th. This made for very large swells on Lake Palestine in Northeast Texas. A man and his wife were out fishing on a boat when the boat capsized from the large wave action on the lake. The man drowned but his wife was later rescued.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 05, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 05, 2011 to November 05, 2011. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: An upper trough was moving through the Great Basin and into the Central Rockies with a strong cold front associated with it crossing Far West Texas. Wind gusts up to 69 mph were reported with this system. Details: A peak wind gust of 69 mph was recorded on the northeast side of El Paso 7 miles NNW of downtown.

title: Drought: Texas, Nov 01, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from November 01, 2011 to November 30, 2011. Affected areas: El Paso, Hudspeth. Episode summary: Severe(D2) to Exceptional(D4) drought continued across parts of Far West Texas through the month of November. Little change was noted during the month. Details: Severe(D2) drought was noted through the entire month over Far West El Paso County. The El Paso Airport received 0.23 inches of rain which was 0.26 inches below normal. A tight drought index gradient existed across Hudspeth County through the month of November. Far West Hudspeth County was only in Moderate(D1) drought but over the far eastern portion of the county it was up to Exceptional(D4). Little change was noted during the month.

title: Heavy Snow: Texas, Dec 22, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, from December 22, 2011 to December 24, 2011. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County, Van Horn & Hwy 54 Corridor. Episode summary: An upper level cutoff low pressure center moved slowly eastward over west Texas, creating a prolonged period of wintry precipitation. Although rain, sleet and snow occurred, the precipitation fell mainly as snow, with significant accumulations over west Texas. Details: Several hours of moderate snow fell before freezing rain mixed with the snow early on the 23rd. Since temperatures were in the 20s through the evening on the 22nd, and considering the moderate snowfall, several inches of snowfall were possible along with icy roads. Snow continued through the day and night on the 23rd and ended late in the morning on the 24th with 17 inches total. Considering Pine Springs in the Guadalupe Mountains had 17 inches of snowfall, northern portions of the Van Horn and Highway 54 corridor zone could have had 8-10 inches of snowfall.

title: Heavy Snow: Texas, Dec 23, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, from December 23, 2011 to December 25, 2011. Affected areas: Andrews, Ector, Gaines, Loving, Martin, Midland, Winkler. Episode summary: An upper level cutoff low pressure center moved slowly eastward over west Texas, creating a prolonged period of wintry precipitation. Although rain, sleet and snow occurred, the precipitation fell mainly as snow, with significant accumulations over west Texas. Details: Seminole spotter reported a total of 6 inches of snowfall. Storm total snowfall for Mentone was 6-8 inches. Andrews had a total of 5 inches of snowfall.

title: Tornado: Texas, Nov 08, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from November 08, 2011 to November 08, 2011. Affected areas: Galveston, Harris. Episode summary: Thunderstorms moved across Southeast Texas producing areas of damage and at least two tornadoes. Details: A tornado touched down at a industrial plant. It knocked over 10 empty trailers and did minor damage to plant. Extensive damage along Hidden Lakes Drive in Kingwood. Numerous trees were snapped our uprooted. Numerous homes had broken windows and partial roof damage. Tornado was rated EF1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale. Reported property and crop damage: about $150,000.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Jan 01, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from January 01, 2012 to January 02, 2012. Affected areas: Vilas. The snow tapered off as the low departed, but increased again as cold air flowing over the warmer waters of Lake Superior brought lake-effect snow showers to Upper Michigan and parts of northern Wisconsin.||Six to 11 inches of snow fell in northern Vilas County, most of which was lake-effect. title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Nov 09, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from November 09, 2011 to November 09, 2011. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Fond Du Lac, Green Lake, Iowa, Lafayette, Marquette, Sauk. Episode summary: Surface low pressure, tracking from northern Missouri across extreme northeast Illinois to northern Lower Michigan, was accompanied by a strong upper-level disturbance moving across the western Great Lakes region. These features combined with a favorable thermal profile to produce 3 to 6 inches of heavy, wet snow across northwest portions of South Central Wisconsin during the morning and early afternoon hours of November 9th. Power lines and tree limbs snapped under the weight of the heavy snow that had collected on them. Snowfall totals for the event included La Valle with 7.2 inches; Reedsburg with 6.4 inches; Baraboo with 6 inches; and Mineral Point with 5.5 inches of snow. The 7-inch amount was isolated and therefore prevented this event from being entered as a winter storm. In addition to the snow, the tight pressure gradient around the low produced sustained northeast to north winds of 15 to 25 mph, with gusts of 35 to 45 mph, reducing visibilities and adding to travel difficulties. Details: Snowfall totals of 3 to 5 inches made for slick roads and dangerous driving conditions. A street located on a hill in Ripon became impassible as cars stalled and slid back down the hill. A tree was set on fire when a live power line, weighted down by the heavy, wet snow, snapped and made contact with the tree.

title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Nov 13, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from November 13, 2011 to November 13, 2011. Affected areas: Kenosha, Milwaukee, Racine, Rock, Walworth, Waukesha. Episode summary: A strong low-level jet of 50 to 60 knots, ahead of a short wave trough approaching from the Central Plains, combined with steep lapse rates from the surface up to 800 mb to mix down strong wind gusts over Southeast Wisconsin during the afternoon of November 13th. Sustained winds of 30 mph, with gusts between 45 and 55 mph were measured over the southeast corner of the state. The highest reported gust was 54 mph (43 knots) in Kenosha. The strong winds snapped small tree branches and knocked down power lines. Reported property and crop damage: about $6,000.

title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Nov 29, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from November 29, 2011 to November 29, 2011. Affected areas: Kenosha, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Racine, Sheboygan. Episode summary: Strong low pressure tracked from the Ohio River Valley into the eastern Great Lakes with a tight pressure gradient developing over far eastern Wisconsin on November 29th. Strong north to northeast winds flowing over the low-friction surface of Lake Michigan allowed sustained winds to reach 30 to 35 mph, with wind gusts between 45 and 55 mph, to affect near shore locations from Sheboygan to Kenosha. The strongest wind gust was reported at the lake shore observation site near the Kenosha Harbor with a 55 mph (48 knot) wind gust, with a 53 mph (46 knot) gust at the John H. Batten Airport in Racine. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Dust Storm, Heavy Snow, High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Jan 21, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, Heavy Snow, High Wind, Strong Wind, from January 21, 2012 to January 21, 2012. Affected areas: Eastern Mojave Desert, Eastern Sierra Slopes Of Inyo County, Morongo Basin, Western Mojave Desert. Episode summary: A strong Pacific storm system brought high winds to much of the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Isolated heavy rain and snow also fell. Details: High winds blew parts of the roofs off two homes and blew over a flag pole in Morongo Valley, and blowing dust reduced visibility to zero and made travel impossible in Landers. The peak measured gust occurred at Twentynine Palms (KNXP). Thirteen inches of snow fell in Aspendell. Dust storm conditions reduced visibility to a quarter mile at Daggett, and blew so much sand onto Harvard Road that it had to be closed. A tree, sign, and power pole were also blown down in the Barstow area. The peak measured gust occurred at Bicycle Lake on Fort Irwin. Reported property and crop damage: about $55,000.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Jan 22, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from January 22, 2012 to January 23, 2012. Affected areas: Eastern Sierra Slopes Of Inyo County, Owens Valley. Episode summary: Another Pacific storm passed through the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin, bringing locally heavy snow. Details: Eight inches of snow fell in Bishop before changing to rain. The Aspendell observer measured 19.2 inches of snow.

title: Tornado: Texas, Jan 25, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from January 25, 2012 to January 25, 2012. Affected areas: Panola, Rusk. Episode summary: A vigorous upper level storm system moved out of west Texas and into central Texas during the morning of January 25th. An area of low pressure at the surface moved out of extreme southern Texas and into east central Texas during the late morning and afternoon hours. A warm front which was just off the southeast Texas/southwest Louisiana coast on the 24th, moved north during the morning and took a position along or just south of the interstate 20 corridor of northeast Texas and northern Louisiana. A moderately unstable airmass was noted in the warm sector south of the warm front with dewpoints in the middle 60s. A very strong low level and deep layer shear storm environment developed across the region and the result was strong to severe thunderstorms, some of which produced isolated tornadoes across the region. Details: The National Weather Service conducted a storm survey in Rusk County in the town of Mt. Enterprise and found evidence of an EF1 tornado. The tornado first touched down southwest of town along CR 3207 south of Gatlin Cemetery Road where several large trees were snapped and uprooted. title: High Wind, Strong Wind, Winter Weather: California, Nov 02, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, Winter Weather, from November 02, 2011 to November 04, 2011. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Mtns, Se S.J. Valley. title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Dec 03, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from December 03, 2011 to December 04, 2011. Affected areas: Ashland, Burnett, Iron, Sawyer, Washburn. Episode summary: Snow fell across northwest Wisconsin as weak low pressure over northwest Iowa early on the 3rd moved to the Green Bay area early on December 4th. Snow spread into northwest Wisconsin about 430 PM on December 3rd, then ended around daybreak on December 4th. Snowfall amounts ranged from 3 to 6 inches across northwest Wisconsin, south of a Minong to Ashland line. Lake Superior contributed moisture to areas east and south of Bayfield Peninsula. Snowfalls totaled 7 to 10 inches across Iron County, with snowfalls of 5 to 7 inches throughout surrounding counties. Details: The greatest snowfall was 7.00 inches at Sarona. The greatest snowfall was 6.50 inches at Clam Lake. More than 6 inches of snow fell across most of Iron County. The greatest reported snowfall was 9.6 inches seven miles east of Gurney.

title: Drought: Texas, Nov 01, 2011

Affected areas: Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Although some much needed rainfall fell across portions of West Central Texas, the rainfall was not enough to eliminate the year long drought. The highest rainfall amounts occurred across Throckmorton County and along and east of a line from Brownwood to Coleman to Junction where rainfall amounts in excess of an inch fell. Outside of this area, scattered showers produced lighter rainfall amounts. The cooler and wetter fall weather continued to reduce the wildfire threat. The U.S. Drought Monitor, issued through the National Mitigation Drought Center continued to depict extreme to exceptional drought over a large part of West Central Texas. title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Jan 24, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from January 24, 2012 to January 25, 2012. Affected areas: Bastrop, Bexar, Edwards, Travis. Episode summary: A deep upper level low pressure center brought a frontal system through Texas which caused thunderstorms across South Central Texas. These storms formed into a mesoscale convective system and produced several tornadoes, wind damage, large hail, and heavy rain that resulted in flash flooding. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain which caused flooding and closed the low water crossing on Wasson Road along Williamson Creek in Austin. Both Camp Mabry (3.14 inches) and Bergstrom International Airport (5.66 inches) reported record daily rainfall from these storms. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain which caused flooding in several subdivisions in and near Cedar Creek. A CoCoRAHS observer west-northwest of Bastrop reported 9.35 inches of rain from these storms. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain which caused flooding in Bastrop. People were rescued from a submerged car on Highway 71. A CoCoRAHS observer west-northwest of Bastrop reported 9.35 inches of rain from these storms. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Jan 13, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from January 13, 2012 to January 13, 2012. Affected areas: Brooks, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Starr, Zapata. Episode summary: A cold front pushed across the Rio Grande Valley and Deep South Texas on January 12th bringing chilly overnight temperatures on the 13th to the northern counties of the CWA. Readings fell well below freezing across much of the King Ranch (Brooks/Kenedy) where winds calmed. Colder pockets of the Rio Grande Plains and Brush Country (Zapata/Jim Hogg/Starr) also fell to or below freezing (32F) for several hours. Details: Temperatures fell to 32 degrees around midnight and continued falling to a low of 30 degrees across Zapata county before rising above 32 degrees after 8:15 AM. A citizen weather observer site also recorded a low of 30 degrees. Temperatures fell to 32 degrees between 6:15 AM and 8:15 AM at Brooks County Airport and across Brooks County before rising above freezing after 8:15 AM. A COOP site reported a low of 25 degrees in Falfurrias. Proxy observations from the Lower Rio Grande Valley NWR site at San Manuel (28) indicate up to five hours of freezing temperatures during the early morning hours. Temperatures fell below degrees between 6:15 AM and 8:15 AM across Kenedy before rising above freezing after 8:15 AM. A COOP site in Sarita reported a low of 28 degrees and a COOP site in Armstrong reported a low of 27 degrees. title: Dust Storm, High Wind: Texas, Jan 22, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Dust Storm, High Wind, from January 22, 2012 to January 22, 2012. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall, Hockley and 9 more areas. Episode summary: During the morning and afternoon of the 22nd, very strong winds and blowing dust covered much of the region as a powerful upper level storm system raced across the central High Plains. Winds initially increased early in the morning behind a Pacific type cold front. Wind speeds quickly increased behind this front and lifted considerable amounts of dust into the atmosphere. The blowing dust reduced visibilities to less than one half mile at many locations. Strong winds and low visibilities caused a tractor trailer to blow over on Interstate 27 north of Abernathy. A secondary surge of strong winds entered the southeastern Texas panhandle by the middle of the afternoon. This secondary surge was generated by showers in the eastern Texas panhandle. These intense winds caused much damage across the South Plains, Rolling Plains and extreme southern Texas Panhandle. Damage reports mostly included downed utility poles and broken tree limbs. Some of the most extensive damage occurred in Floyd County where over 2500 acres of winter wheat were sand blasted. Additionally, a large tree was uprooted in Lubbock and fell on a vehicle, motorcycle and roof of a home. title: Winter Weather: California, Nov 05, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from November 05, 2011 to November 06, 2011. Affected areas: S Sierra Mtns. Episode summary: Behind a fast moving cold front was an unseasonably cold airmass that plunged snow levels into the foothills. By the morning of November 6th, snow was falling down to 2700 feet near Lake Isabella (a half inch of snow was reported at Mountain Mesa), and up to 2 inches of snow fell at 4000 feet. Further north, Tuolumne Meadows received another 8 inches of snow during the night of November 5th-6th.||The San Joaquin Valley saw temperatures fall to well below normal. The high temperature at Bakersfield on November 4th was only 56 degrees, just 1 degree above the record low maximum temperature for that date (55 in 1996). The next day, Fresno did break its record low maximum temperature for the 5th with a high of 57 degrees; the old record was 58, set in 1996. Two days later, Bakersfield tied its record low maximum temperature for November 7th of 58 degrees, last set in 1963.||In the cold, unstable air behind the front, scattered showers developed across interior central California, and even isolated thunderstorms. The airmass over the San Joaquin Valley stabilized as an upper-level ridge built into California behind the trough. With ground moisture from the showers of November 6th, conditions were right for the development of patchy fog the following morning. Fog was not the only concern for interior central California, however. The unseasonably cold airmass also brought sub-freezing temperatures to parts of the Kern County deserts.

title: High Wind, Winter Weather: California, Nov 10, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Winter Weather, from November 10, 2011 to November 12, 2011. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: A low pressure trough moved into California on November 10th. Ahead of the trough, a strong offshore flow brought southeast winds to the region. As these winds downsloped through the Tejon and Tehachapi Passes, very warm and above-normal temperatures occurred in the south end of the San Joaquin Valley. Bakersfield had a high of 78 on November 10th, and 76 the next day. Winds gusted at the base of the Grapevine as well, reaching 61 mph during the afternoon of November 10th, and 73 mph before sunrise the following morning.||This storm also brought snow across the Southern Sierra and Kern County Mountains. Snowfall reports included 7 inches of new snow at Ponderosa and 2th. Snow fell at Pine Mountain Club (at 6100 feet in the western Tehachapi Mountains) during the evening of November 11th, and winds gusted to 56 mph at the base of the Grapevine during the morning g hours of the 12th. A high pressure ridge built over the east Pacific, setting up a dry northwest wind flow over California.

title: Winter Weather: California, Nov 20, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from November 20, 2011 to November 20, 2011. Affected areas: S Sierra Mtns, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: The next in the series of storms arrived two days later. The storm brought a reinforcing push of cold air into the San Joaquin Valley, plunging high temperatures into the 50s. The high temperature at Bakersfield on November 20th was only 53 degrees, only 4 degrees warmer than the record low maximum temperature for the date of 49 degrees, set in 1922. Fresno had a high of 55 on the 20th, again only 4 degrees warmer than the record low maximum of 51 degrees, set in 1972. For both cities, this was the coldest high temperature for the month.||The upper-level low stayed off the California coast, spinning moisture into the state from the south. As a result, this storm brought more rain to the Southern San Joaquin Valley than to the central Valley. Even so, there was sufficient rain over most of the Valley floor to recharge the ground moisture. Areas of dense fog developed over the central and southern San Joaquin Valley during the morning of November 21st, persisting into the late morning hours in some locations. Morning fog also developed the next two mornings. Fog also developed in the Kern County deserts during the night of November 20th-21st, with the visibility at Edwards Air Force Base falling to less than a quarter mile shortly after midnight. ||Snowfall in the mountains was moderate with this storm. The heaviest snow totals were reported at Agnew Pass, Tamarack Summit, Quacking Aspen, and Blackcap Basin, where around 10 inches accumulated.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Nov 30, 2011
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from November 30, 2011 to November 30, 2011. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: A low pressure trough moved into California on November 24th. This system brought some light rain to the region, but the main impact was from the mid and high clouds ahead of the cold front. These clouds inhibited fog development, resulting in a mostly fog-free Thanksgiving Day morning. Dense fog returned the next morning, mainly over the east side of the San Joaquin Valley and persisting into the late morning hours. The dense night and morning fog became more widespread over the central and southern San Joaquin Valley from November 26th through the 28th as a stagnant weather pattern lingered over central California. ||A strong upper-level trough approached the central California interior on November 29th, destabilizing the airmass and reducing the San Joaquin Valley fog. A tight surface pressure gradient developed over California, resulting in northeast winds gusting over 60 mph across the Southern Sierra Nevada. High winds developed on November 30th which is a relatively rare phenomenon known as a Mono Wind Event across the Sierra Nevada. This event continued into the first two days of December and caused extensive tree damage across much of the Southern Sierra Nevada. Please see the December, 2011 storm data report for more detailed storm reports from this event! ||At the lower elevations, a cold front moved through the San Joaquin Valley on November 30th, bringing northwest winds gusting to near 50 mph.
