title: High Wind, Strong Wind, Winter Weather: California, Mar 13, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, Winter Weather, from March 13, 2012 to March 15, 2012. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Lassen/Eastern Plumas/Eastern Sierra, Surprise Valley. Episode summary: Low pressure moving through the Pacific Northwest brought a modest higher-elevation snowfall and strong, gusty winds to northeast California on the 13th on the 14th. Details: The Surprise Valley RAWS reported winds gusting to between 68 and 73 mph. Areas of heavy snow fell near the Sierra crest with much less snowfall elsewhere along and west of highway 89 on the 13th and 14th. East of highway 89, very little snow fell during the same period with rain or a mixture of rain and snow below 7000 feet limiting accumulations. Snowfall totals include: 12-20 inches (locally 2 feet) near the crest with 6-8 inches elsewhere near and west of highway 89 Widespread wind gusts between 40 and 50 mph were reported on the 13th. However, local areas along highway 395 just south of Janesville recorded winds gusts up to 65 mph with 2 tractor trailer trucks and several trees blown over/down. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 10, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 10, 2012 to May 10, 2012. Affected areas: Ector, Howard, Midland, Pecos, Scurry. Episode summary: An upper level low moved into West Texas from Mexico. This low provided strong lift with cold air aloft and plenty of moisture contributing to heavy convective rainfall. Since the upper low was slow to move out of the area, areas across West Texas received a lot of rain in a short amount of time which resulted in flash flooding. Details: A thunderstorm with heavy rain moved over Howard County and produced flash flooding in Big Spring. East Sixth Street in Big Spring was under about three feet of water in some places. No reports of damage were received, so the damage estimate is assumed to be zero. A thunderstorm with heavy rain moved over Pecos County and produced flash flooding in Iraan. One and a half feet of running water was reported at Tenth and Eleventh Streets in Iraan. No reports of damage were received, so the damage cost will be estimated at zero. A thunderstorm that produced heavy rain moved over Ector County and produced flash flooding on the east side of Odessa. Two feet of moving water was reported along Highway 80 and Country Club Road in Odessa. The cost of damage is estimated at zero dollars since no damage was reported. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Mar 16, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from March 16, 2012 to March 17, 2012. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Lassen/Eastern Plumas/Eastern Sierra, Mono. Episode summary: Strong, cold low pressure dropped south from the Gulf of Alaska on the 16th and 17th and brought heavy snow to the Sierra and portions of northeast California. Details: An estimated 12 to 16 inches of snow fell in the higher terrain of eastern Plumas and Sierra Counties with this system. Below 5000 feet, little snowfall was noted except in the Feather River Basin along highways 70 and 89. This includes 4 inches in Portola. Eighteen to 36 inches of snow fell for ski areas west of highway 89 on the 16th and 17th, with local amounts of 3 to 4 feet near the crest. Elsewhere, the main snowfall fell overnight from the 16th into the 17th with a widespread 8 to 13 inches reported per SNOTEL and CO-OP data. An estimated 12 to 20 inches of snow fell west of highway 395 (except 20-24 inches Mammoth Lakes and 39 inches Mammoth Mountain Ski area) from the evening of the 16th through early morning on the 17th. Elsewhere, 10-12 inches fell in Lee Vining with 6 inches for Bodie and Tom's Place. Meanwhile, Bridgeport only saw a very light accumulation (specific amounts missing).

title: Heavy Snow, High Wind, Winter Weather: California, Mar 31, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, High Wind, Winter Weather, from March 31, 2012 to March 31, 2012. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Lassen/Eastern Plumas/Eastern Sierra, Mono. Episode summary: Strong low pressure moved across the North Pacific and into the West by early on April 1st bringing areas of heavy snow and strong winds to the Sierra and eastern California on the 31st. Details: Eight to 13 inches of snow fell on the west side of Lake Tahoe while ski areas received 12 to 18 inches of snowfall. Meanwhile, areas east of highway 89 only received 4 to 8 inches of snow although much of the snow was in a 4-hr period (heavy snowfall rate). Winds were sustained at 40-50 mph on Lake Tahoe during the morning of the 31st. According to the Coast Guard, these winds generated 4-foot waves on the north shore of the lake. The Truckee Airport reported sustained winds of 35-45 mph with gusts between 58-70 mph. Elsewhere, widespread gusts 40-50 mph were reported. High winds were reported along highway 395 north of Bridgeport with gusts 61-76 mph at the Walker RAWS and gusts up to 64 mph at the Bridgeport RAWS. High winds also may have occurred east of Mono Lake as winds were gusting 70-75 mph at Brawley Peak and along highway 359 just over the state line in Nevada.

title: Frost/Freeze: Wisconsin, Apr 10, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Frost/Freeze, from April 10, 2012 to April 12, 2012. Affected areas: Clark, Crawford, Jackson, La Crosse, Trempealeau. Episode summary: With the unseasonably warm temperatures over the latter half of March, fruit crops across western Wisconsin got an early start on the growing season. Unfortunately, several nights of temperatures near or below the freezing mark throughout the month of April caused considerable damage to these fruit crops. Most of the damage likely occurred from April 10th through the 12th when low temperatures dipped into the middle to upper 20s. It is estimated that apple orchards lost between 20 and 100 percent of the crop, pears and plums were hit hard, some tart cherry orchards had losses up to 80 percent, and the first picking of strawberries was completely lost. Exact crop losses will likely not be known until the fall harvest. Details: Apple orchards across Clark County estimated losses up to 100 percent from freezing temperatures that occurred after the start of the growing season. Exact crop damage numbers will not be known until the fall harvest. Apple orchards across Crawford County estimated losses of 20 to 25 percent from freezing temperatures that occurred after the start of the growing season. Pear and plum crops were also hit hard while damages to tart cherry orchards ranged from little loss up to 80 percent. The first blooming of strawberries were completely loss but subsequent bloomings are doing fine. Exact crop damage numbers wil Apple orchards across La Crosse County estimated losses up to 80 percent from freezing temperatures that occurred after the start of the growing season. Exact crop damage numbers will not be known until the fall harvest.

title: Heavy Rain, High Wind: Texas, Jun 02, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, High Wind, from June 02, 2012 to June 02, 2012. Affected areas: Bailey, Lamb. Episode summary: Isolated high-based severe storms developed late this afternoon over the northwestern South Plains. In spite of weak vertical wind shear, one of these storms evolved into a slow-moving supercell over western Lamb County and only moved roughly 15 miles in the span of two hours. This supercell produced large hail to golf ball size in Needmore along with torrential rains that resulted in localized flooding of one rural road. Additional storms later this evening produced two instances of high winds as measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station near Olton. Details: A NWS employee observed localized flooding from persistent heavy rains over FM 298 four miles east of Needmore. Bar ditches adjacent to a playa lake swelled over a 100-foot stretch of the roadway to a depth of a few inches. A Texas Tech West Texas mesonet station measured a wind gust to 58 mph. The wind was associated with an apparent wake low that developed behind decaying showers and thunderstorms. No damage was reported.

title: Winter Storm: California, Mar 25, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Storm, from March 25, 2012 to March 26, 2012. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Mtns, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: By the 20th, high pressure began to strengthen and allowed temperatures to recover; they rose to a few degrees above seasonal averages by the 21st. This pattern continued for the next couple of days until another low pressure system arrived on the 24th.||An upper-level low moved over interior central California on the 24th and 25th, bringing rain and mountain snow to much of the region during that weekend. Snow levels were much higher with this system than the one that moved through the area during the previous weekend; snow fell mainly above the pass levels in Kern County and remained above 5000 feet in most areas throughout the southern Sierra Nevada. Nearly a foot of new snow fell on the Southern Sierra Nevada, and rainfall amounts in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley were up to a quarter inch.

title: Winter Storm: California, Mar 31, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Storm, from March 31, 2012 to March 31, 2012. Affected areas: S Sierra Mtns, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: The next upper level low arrived to the region on the night of March 27th-28th after a brief dry period between storm systems. This storm stayed mainly over northern California, and brought only light precipitation to the region. A stronger storm arrived on the last day of the month, bringing heavier precipitation to the region. Rainfall amounts for March 31st-April 1st were between a quarter and a half inch of rain for the central San Joaquin Valley, and between a tenth and a quarter of an inch for the south Valley. text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, Heavy Snow, High Wind, from April 10, 2012 to April 14, 2012. Affected areas: Apple And Lucerne Valleys, Coachella Valley, Riverside County Mountains, San Bernardino, San Bernardino County Mountains. Mountain locations received between one-quarter and three-quarters of an inch of rain. Above 6000 feet, a trace to 2 inches of snow was observed in the San Bernardino Mountains. A couple thunderstorms with damaging winds also occurred near Hemet in Riverside County. ||A deeper upper low developed right behind the last and closed off before diving inland over southern California on the 13th. title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 03, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 03, 2012 to June 03, 2012. Affected areas: Briscoe. Episode summary: Scattered high-based and nearly stationary thunderstorms developed in Briscoe County late this afternoon. As early evening approached, these storms intensified and moved east accompanied by localized instances of large hail up to ping-pong ball size and high winds in portions of Hall and Childress Counties. Details: Heavy rains from a slow-moving severe thunderstorm created several swift-moving mud flows in open ranch land along Texas Highway 256 in far eastern Briscoe County. No property damage such as washed-out fences or side roads was observed.

title: Tornado: Texas, Jun 04, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from June 04, 2012 to June 04, 2012. Affected areas: Crosby. Episode summary: Moisture trapped beneath a developing ridge of upper high pressure combined with strong daytime heating to fuel the development of numerous thunderstorms. Although wind shear was minimal, very strong instability led to several of these storms becoming strong while growing into multicellular clusters and lines. Some of these storms produced large hail, high winds and even one very brief EF0 tornado. The large coverage of these slow-moving storms proved very beneficial to South Plains residents and farmers as a widespread rain event had not occurred since early spring. Details: A brief tornado located about two miles southwest of Crosbyton was photographed by a storm chaser. NWS radar indicated a short-lived, low-level mesocyclone that developed along the northwest edge of an apparent surging gust front. The increased cyclonic shear to the left of the gust front's motion was likely stretched vertically and produced the brief EF0 tornado. No damage survey was conducted as

title: Flood: Texas, Jun 06, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from June 06, 2012 to June 06, 2012. Affected areas: Garza, Hale, Lubbock. Episode summary: Early this morning, a slow-moving upper level low that originated from a complex of thunderstorms over the South Plains on June 4th had moved over the southeast Texas Panhandle. During the pre-dawn hours, a very narrow band of elevated showers and thunderstorms developed on the southwest edge of the upper low and proceeded to move repeatedly over portions of southeast Castro, southwest Swisher, Hale, southwest Floyd, eastern Lubbock, Crosby, and Garza Counties. Rainfall rates near two inches per hour were common with some of these storms and at least one storm in southwest Hale County produced marginally severe hail. Bias-corrected NEXRAD rainfall totals indicated several swaths of 2 to 4 inches of rainfall from just east of Hart southeast to Edmonson, with another from Hale Center south-southeast to Idalou and Caprock, and more scattered instances near White River Lake and also in northwest Garza County. Heavy rains as recorded by Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet stations included 4.42 inches 5ENE Abernathy (Hale County) and 3.74 inches 6NW White River Lake (Crosby County). Similar rains forced the closure of Interstate 27 at the Hale Center underpass for a few hours and flooded Highway 62/82 just east of Idalou until late morning. Water was also reported over Highway 380/399 about 7 miles west of Post. Precipitation diminished greatly in intensity and coverage by 1000 CST. title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Apr 08, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from April 08, 2012 to April 08, 2012. Affected areas: Dodge, Marquette, Washington. Episode summary: Widespread wind gusts up to 40 mph...with a few peak gusts of 45 to 55 mph...affected portions of Southcentral and Southeast Wisconsin during the late afternoon of April 8th. These strong winds were due to the tight pressure gradient between high pressure centered over the Plains and low pressure accompanying a short wave trough into southern Canada. A dry air mass over southern Wisconsin produced deep mixing up to strong winds aloft, with steep lapse rates allowing these winds to translate down to the surface. The strongest wind gusts were associated with very light showers and sprinkles that evaporated as they fell into the drier air. The evaporative cooling of the air moving downward with the showers increased the momentum of the air, producing the stronger gusts. Reported property and crop damage: about $4,000.

title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Apr 15, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from April 15, 2012 to April 16, 2012. Affected areas: Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green, Iowa, Jefferson, Kenosha, Milwaukee, Racine, Rock, Sauk, Sheboygan and 1 more areas. Episode summary: Two periods of strong winds affected Southcentral and Southeast Wisconsin as a deep surface low tracked from southern Minnesota into northern Wisconsin during the overnight hours of April 15th to 16th. Southerly winds gusting to between 45 mph and 54 mph (39 knots to 47 knots) affected South Central Wisconsin on the night of the 15th with the tightening pressure gradient ahead of the low. The winds were enhanced with strong low-level jet winds mixing down to the surface. Cold-air advection, behind a cold front trailing the low, crossed the region during the day on the 16th and brought sustained winds between 20 mph and 30 mph (17 knots to 26 knots) and gusts up to 49 mph (43 knots) to much of South Central and Southeast Wisconsin. There were multiple reports of downed power lines, trees and tree branches. Reported property and crop damage: about $28,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 23, 2012 to April 26, 2012. Affected areas: Coachella Valley. Episode summary: Gusty southwesterly occurred over the mountains and desert slopes ahead of a low pressure system that moved through southern California and northern Baja on the 24th/25th. No damage was reported with these winds. Details: High winds began at the Sky Valley mesonet station between 1445 and 1545 PST on the 23rd and occurred off and on through on the 26th. Several gusts over 58 mph were recorded between 1500 PST on the 23rd through 0000 PST on the 24th. A peak gust of 69 mph was measured between 2244 and 2344 PST on the 23rd. High winds occurred again late evening on the 25th with a peak gust of 73 mph around 2200 PST

title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, May 24, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from May 24, 2012 to May 24, 2012. Affected areas: Clark, Monroe. Episode summary: Small lines of severe thunderstorms formed along a fast moving cold front during the afternoon of May 24th. These thunderstorms caused sporadic wind damage starting near Arcadia (Trempealeau County) and continued toward Longwood and Dorchester (Clark County). Most of the damage was limited to trees and power poles blown down. Before the cold front moved through, a strong gradient was in place. This produced wind gusts of 40 to 45 mph that blew down a cluster of maple trees near Wilton (Monroe County). Details: A cluster of maple trees near Wilton was blown down from strong gradient winds. Several trees across Clark County were blown down from strong gradient winds. A home sustained roof damage northwest of Spencer and at least one tree was blown down onto power lines in the Greenwood area. Reported property and crop damage: about $7,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 11, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 11, 2012 to May 11, 2012. Affected areas: Hunt. Episode summary: As an upper level low moved across the region, bands of moderate to heavy rainfall moved east across the region. During the afternoon hours on May 11th, a few strong and severe thunderstorms developed near the core of the upper level low; producing ping pong and golf ball sized hail and winds to 65 mph in Tarrant County. Details: Several street in Commerce were closed due to several hours of moderate to heavy rainfall but conditions were improving at the time the report was received.

title: High Wind: Texas, May 05, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from May 05, 2012 to May 05, 2012. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: An upper trough passing by to the north of the region resulted in high winds in the Guadalupe Mountains. Details: Sustained westerly winds of 40 mph or greater occurred through Guadalupe Pass for 2-3 hours.

title: High Wind: Texas, May 23, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from May 23, 2012 to May 24, 2012. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: Increased mid level westerly winds at the base of an upper trough which passed through the northern Rocky Mountains resulted in high winds in the Guadalupe Mountains. Details: Sporadic high winds occurred at the Pinery RAWS site in the Guadalupe Mountains. Many hours of high winds occurred through Guadalupe Pass with gusts varying between 58 and 66 mph. Many hours of high winds occurred at the Guadalupe Peak RAWS site in the higher elevations of the Guadalupe Mountains, with gusts varying between 58 and 76 mph.

title: Heavy Rain, Tornado: Texas, Apr 16, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, Tornado, from April 16, 2012 to April 16, 2012. Affected areas: Cameron, Kenedy. Episode summary: A slow moving front, prior boundaries from evening storms on the 15th, and a warm humid air mass in place across the Rio Grande Valley activated numerous afternoon and early evening thunderstorms on April 16th. Early morning showers produced a funnel cloud in Donna; the tail of stronger storms which produced flooding, tornadoes, and hail across the Coastal Bend from mid-morning through mid-afternoon produced a small tornado on the Kenedy Ranch along the Kenedy/Kleberg County line. By afternoon, temperatures warming into the mid and upper 80s were sufficient to trigger rapid development of thunderstorms in eastern Starr County; these would slide into Hidalgo County during the afternoon and produce a combination of torrential rains, frequent lightning, and hail mainly between pea and dime size with a few nickel and quarter size reports in the Edinburg/Pharr/McAllen area. More than 2 inches of welcome rain fell in Edinburg. By late afternoon, inflow of deep moisture along the Highway 77 corridor filled in thunderstorms between the Cameron/Willacy county line and the south end of the King Ranch. One storm grew very robust and slowly drifted in between Rio Hondo, Harlingen, San Benito, and Los Fresnos. An assumed large hail core centered over rural locations; others observed wind gusts to 55 mph and rainfall as much as 3.7 inches in Rio Hondo.||The outflow associated with the large storm in north central Cameron County outran its updraft support, and much of the action calmed by the time the remnants reached Brownsville between 5 and 545pm. The outflow combined with other boundaries from storms sliding along the Rio Grande River into southwest Cameron County to flare up a small but potent storm just

title: Heavy Rain, Tornado: Texas, Apr 16, 2012
text: action calmed by the time the remnants reached Brownsville between 5 and 545pm. The outflow combined with other boundaries from storms sliding along the Rio Grande River into southwest Cameron County to flare up a small but potent storm just west of Port Isabel just before 6 pm. As the storm raced east onto South Padre Island, a downburst developed which produced winds up to 57 mph at the Port Isabel Coast Guard station (along Laguna Vista Bay) and a half mile swath of estimated 70 to 75 mph winds across the central portion of the resort area of South Padre Island, all occurring roughly between 622 and 628 pm CDT. Reports from residents indicated two small boats sank at a bayside dock, two windows blown out of shuttle buses, a restaurant awning blown down, a utility pole knocked down at service station, and lawn furniture strewn around one resident's yard. Details: A tornado was reported on the Kenedy Ranch, approximately 3 miles south of Rivera (Kleberg County). This storm would later produce a damaging tornado near Kingsville. The National Weather Service Office in Corpus Christi relayed the report to from the general public. An off-duty NWS employee reported an estimated 3 to 4 inches of rain along FM 510 near Bayview, with several inches of water flooding nearby roads.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2012 to April 09, 2012. Affected areas: Brooks, Cameron, Coastal Cameron, Coastal Willacy, Hidalgo, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Willacy, Zapata. Episode summary: Strong thunderstorms that moved across Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley at the end of March provided plenty of beneficial rain to the region. This rainfall allowed for drought conditions to begin to improve across much of the region. Details: Hidalgo County saw improvement in drought conditions. The western two thirds of the county improved to D2 drought, with the eastern third remaining in D3 drought conditions. Brooks County saw overall improvement in drought conditions with most of the county in D2 drought conditions, with the far SE corner in D3 drought conditions. Jim Hogg County saw improvement in drought conditions for much of the county. The central portion of the county was in D2 drought, with a sliver of D1 drought on the southern edge of the county and D3 drought along the northern county line.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 10, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 10, 2012 to April 16, 2012. Affected areas: Brooks, Cameron, Coastal Cameron, Coastal Willacy, Hidalgo, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Willacy, Zapata. Episode summary: Thunderstorms on April 15th and April 16th provided plenty of beneficial rainfall to the region. Thunderstorms on the evening of April 15th had rainfall rates in excess of 3 inches an hour over portions of Zapata and Jim Hogg counties, while thunderstorms on April 16th provided rain for much of the eastern half of the region. McAllen received 1.76 inches of rain, Harlingen received 1.04 inches of rain, and Rio Hondo received as much as 3.7 inches of rain. Details: Willacy County continued to see improvement in drought conditions over much of the county. The western two thirds of the county entered into D2 drought, while the eastern third remained in D3 drought conditions. Cameron County continued to see improvement in drought conditions over much of the county. The western two thirds of the county entered into D2 drought, while the eastern third remained in D3 drought conditions. Coastal Willacy County saw no improvement in drought conditions and remained in D3 drought.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 17, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 17, 2012 to April 30, 2012. Affected areas: Brooks, Cameron, Coastal Cameron, Coastal Willacy, Hidalgo, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Willacy, Zapata. Episode summary: Severe thunderstorms impacted the Rio Grande Valley once again on March 20th, bringing well needed rain across the region. These thunderstorms were fast moving, but still dropped .35 inches of rain in McAllen, .2 inches in Brownsville and 1 inch in Harlingen. Details: Hidalgo County continued to see improvement in drought conditions. D2 drought remained only in a sliver on the far eastern boundary of the county, while the rest of the county was in D1 and D0 drought conditions. Jim Hogg County continued to see improvement in drought conditions. Much of the county improved to D1 and D0 drought, with only the far NW corner in D2 drought. Brooks County saw no change in drought conditions. The western half of the county remained in D1 drought, while the eastern half of the county was in D2 drought conditions.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, May 26, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from May 26, 2012 to May 26, 2012. Affected areas: La Crosse. Episode summary: Thunderstorms that developed over South Dakota during the early morning hours of May 26th held together past sunrise and intensified over southeast Minnesota during the late morning. These storms then produced large hail and locally heavy rain over portions of western Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening. Golf ball sized hail fell near Tell (Buffalo County) and some street flooding occurred in La Crosse (La Crosse County). Details: Locally heavy rain produced some street flooding in the city of La Crosse that included the intersection of U.S. Highways 14/61 (Mormon Coulee Road) and Losey Boulevard.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 08, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 08, 2012 to May 08, 2012. Affected areas: Hidalgo, Zapata. Episode summary: The leading edge of a slow moving upper level disturbance across the southwest U.S. induced thunderstorms across the Sierra Madre Oriental during the early morning hours of May 8th. These storms moved into the Rio Grande Plains toward noon, then linked up with additional lift from an approaching wind shift line drifting south from the South Texas Plains. Feeding on a very unstable atmosphere - cold and dry air well above the earth���s surface - initial storms would slam Zapata County during lunchtime with damaging wind, large hail, flooding rain, and frequent lightning. As the afternoon progressed, increasing contrast between cooler air across the South Texas Plains (60s and 70s) with the last of the early May heat in the Rio Grande Valley (90s) set the stage for additional storms with damaging winds and flooding rain in Zapata, and culminated with a monster supercell thunderstorm which cruised from southwest Brooks County through Raymondville before weakening.||This impressive supercell storm dominated the episode, and produced a measured instantaneous wind gust over 100 mph in rural Hidalgo County. Fortunately for the populated middle Valley, where more than 700,000 persons are at risk, this cell slid through northern Hidalgo County north of the SR 186 and U.S. 281 interchange, and accelerated through the Lower Rio Grande Valley National Wildlife Refuge northeast of Linn and San Manuel before reaching Raymondville (Willacy County). The cell quickly weakened by the end of dinner hour (6 to 7 PM CDT) before reaching the Laguna Madre and Gulf of Mexico. Details: The Hidalgo County Precinct #4 Constable recorded 4 to 4.5 inches of rainfall across his ranch to the northwest of U.S. Highway 281, approximately

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 08, 2012
text: hour (6 to 7 PM CDT) before reaching the Laguna Madre and Gulf of Mexico. Details: The Hidalgo County Precinct #4 Constable recorded 4 to 4.5 inches of rainfall across his ranch to the northwest of U.S. Highway 281, approximately 6 miles north of Linn. High standing water of unknown depth was reported on unpaved roads and in some of the fields. Street flooding with briefly up to 3 feet of moving water near the intersection of Irene and US 83. Photos also showed urban type flooding at a local park in the city of Zapata, with an estimated 1 foot of water depth.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Jun 12, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from June 12, 2012 to June 12, 2012. Affected areas: Andrews, Ector. Episode summary: A flat upper ridge was over the Southern Plains with a stationary cold front across the Permian Basin and Southeast New Mexico. An unstable air mass was across the region with very moist air and hot temperatures. Outflow boundaries which provided a focus for thunderstorm development were present across the Permian Basin, Trans Pecos, and Southeast New Mexico from convection to the north. Details: A thunderstorm moved over Odessa and produced heavy rain. Dixie Street in Odessa was flooded as a result of this heavy rain. The cost of damage is estimated to be zero since no damage was reported. A severe thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced a tornado about an eighth of a mile east of Frankle City, TX. A National Weather Service employee spotted the damage at about 9:30 PM CDT. The damage consisted of one power pole bent at a 60 degree angle to the south of FM1967 with power lines about ten feet above the road. A power pole to the north of the first one was snapped, and Reported property and crop damage: about $6,000.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado: Texas, May 10, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado, from May 10, 2012 to May 11, 2012. Affected areas: Cameron, Jim Hogg, Zapata. Episode summary: Vigorous energy cycling around a seasonally strong upper level disturbance crashing into Texas brought a final round of potent thunderstorms through much of the Rio Grande Valley during the late night hours of May 10th into daybreak on May 11th. Initial severe thunderstorms and isolated tornadoes pummeled the Coastal Bend and South Texas Plains from Corpus Christi to near Laredo during the evening of the 10th. As night progressed, pockets of colder air behind the initial line pushed its west end southward; just before midnight, this end would link up with individual cells moving off the Sierra Madre west of Zapata County and form a separate, smaller line from Jim Hogg to Zapata County. This line quickly intensified and dumped heavy rain, high winds some large hail, and one confirmed tornado. As the line marched from the Ranchlands into the Rio Grande Valley, it weakened a bit; as the remnants neared the coast before daybreak, individual small rotating storms developed and redeveloped in Cameron County, with several reports of funnel clouds and at least one confirmed tornado in San Benito (just after 3 AM) from a few hours prior to until just after daybreak on the 11th.||While minor flooding was reported across some of the hilly terrain of the Rio Grande Plains, rainfall was more welcome in the Lower and Mid Valley, with many locations between San Benito, Harlingen, and McAllen receiving 1 to 2 inches of soaking. Frequent to excessive lightning strikes knocked out power to portions of the Rio Grande Valley as the intense storms passed; the lightning caused one structure fire in Pharr. Details: Heavy rainfall of unknown amount caused

text: to 2 inches of soaking. Frequent to excessive lightning strikes knocked out power to portions of the Rio Grande Valley as the intense storms passed; the lightning caused one structure fire in Pharr. Details: Heavy rainfall of unknown amount caused minor flooding in the Medina Addition section of the City of Zapata. The Zapata County Sheriff's Office reported 3 feet of flowing water along U.S. Highway 83 in the vicinity of El Clareno Ranch, about 7 miles south-southeast of the City of Zapata. The highway was closed from 1140 PM on the 10th until 130 AM on the 11th. No damage, injuries, or deaths were reported. A mini-supercell thunderstorms dropped a very brief tornado, containing estimated 80 mph winds (high end EF0 on the Fujita Scale) on top of a single family home, causing considerable damage to property at the well built structure. Damage included: four sections of cyclone fence bent in different directions around the home; a boat and trailer flipped over, numerous snapped tree limbs in different Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

title: High Wind, Winter Weather: California, Apr 01, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Winter Weather, from April 01, 2012 to April 01, 2012. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: April began midway through the storm that arrived on the last day of March. As mentioned in the weather summary for March, two-day storm totals (March 31st-April 1st) were between a quarter and a half inch of rain for the central San Joaquin Valley, and between a tenth and a quarter of an inch for the south Valley. The exception was the southwest part of the San Joaquin Valley, which was rain-shadowed and received only a few hundredths of an inch of rain. In the Southern Sierra Nevada, snowfall amounts over the high country generally were between 5 and 9 inches, although a couple of sites in Tulare County had around a foot of new snow. In the western Tehachapi Mountains, cars were stuck in the snow on the Mil Potrero Highway. Gusty southeast winds developed ahead of the cold front, with gusts of 35 to 45 mph in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley, and 58 to 62 mph in the Kern County deserts; a tree was blown down in Mojave.||As the storm moved east of California, an upper-level ridge moved into the state. High temperatures in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley on April 2nd were as much as 7 degrees warmer than on the 1st, and the desert saw even stronger warming in some locations. This warming continued on the 3rd, and then the ridge gave way to an approaching upper-level trough. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Frost/Freeze: California, Apr 06, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Frost/Freeze, from April 06, 2012 to April 06, 2012. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: A dry cold front moved through interior central California on April 4th. This front triggered gusty winds across the central and southern San Joaquin Valley and over the mountains and deserts. Winds gusted to 45-50 mph over parts of the San Joaquin Valley and the Kern County deserts. Winds also gusted to over 45 mph in the Kern River Canyon, and to 66 mph at Bird Spring Pass in the far south end of the Sierra Nevada.||An unseasonably cold airmass moved into the San Joaquin Valley behind the cold front. Morning low temperatures on April 6th fell as low as 28 degrees, and the lows at Bakersfield and Fresno of 38 degrees were 2 and 3 degrees off the record lows for the date, respectively. Lows during the next morning were only a degree or two warmer.||An upper-level ridge then moved over California, warming temperatures briefly to above normal. Fresno finally had its first 80-degree day of the year on April 8th; the last time Fresno had seen 80 was on October 30th, 2011.

title: Flood, High Wind, Winter Storm: California, Apr 12, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, High Wind, Winter Storm, from April 12, 2012 to April 14, 2012. Affected areas: Fresno, Kern, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Tulare, Tulare Cty Mtns. title: Strong Wind: California, Apr 26, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, from April 26, 2012 to April 26, 2012. Affected areas: Indian Wells Vly. Episode summary: An upper-level ridge built into California behind the departing trough. Temperatures warmed to near normal by April 16th, then above normal the next day. An upper-level trough moved through the Pacific Northwest on the 18th, briefly flattening the ridge, but the ridge rebounded on April 19th for a sharp warming trend. High temperatures in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley on April 20th were 7-10 degrees warmer than the previous day. Temperatures on the 21st continued to warm, and highs were 4-7 degrees warmer than on the 20th. Both Bakersfield and Fresno had their first 90-degree days of the year, with highs of 94 and 93 degrees, respectively. ||Temperatures warmed even further on the 22nd; record high maximum and minimum temperatures were either tied or broken at both Fresno and Bakersfield.||The ridge began to weaken by the following evening, with an upper level trough over northern California. This trough ushered in cooler marine air into the San Joaquin Valley and much of interior central California so that temperatures cooled several degrees by the 23rd. (This pattern was similar to what occurs during the summer months.) Temperatures mainly reached the 80s on the 23rd and 24th in the San Joaquin Valley; however, they remained as high as the 90s during these days in the Kern County desert areas where there was little influence from the marine air.|Another low pressure trough approached central California by April 25th, bringing strong thunderstorms to the southern San Joaquin Valley, including Bakersfield and Delano during the afternoon. These storms continued to develop and intensify as they moved northward into Tulare County. The main threat these storms produced was heavy rain; this caused

text: strong thunderstorms to the southern San Joaquin Valley, including Bakersfield and Delano during the afternoon. These storms continued to develop and intensify as they moved northward into Tulare County. The main threat these storms produced was heavy rain; this caused street flooding throughout much of the San Joaquin Valley portion in Tulare County, including Visalia, Tulare, and Porterville. Temperatures on April 28th were several degrees warmer than during the previous day and returned to near seasonal averages.||On the afternoon of the 26th, gusty winds developed in the Ridgecrest area. title: Wildfire: California, May 24, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from May 24, 2012 to May 28, 2012. Affected areas: San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: The Banner fire started around 1315 PST on the 24th, near the intersection of Highway 78 and S-2, east of Julian near Shelter Valley. No structures or homes were damaged or destroyed, but at one point, 50 residences and one commercial building were threatened. Three firefighters were also injured during the incident, although details of those injuries are unknown. The fire burned a total of 5,321 acres before being fully contained on the 28th.

title: Drought: Texas, Jul 01, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 01, 2012 to July 31, 2012. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Dickens, Floyd, Hale, Hall, Hockley, Kent, King and 9 more areas. Episode summary: Drought conditions across the South Plains, Rolling Plains and extreme southern Texas Panhandle worsened during the month of July. Childress and Hall Counties returned to Severe (D2) drought conditions while Extreme (D3) conditions expanded. Castro, Crosby and Garza Counties remained in Moderate (D1) drought conditions.||Temperatures were observed to be above normal with precipitation well below normal for most areas. There were only a few days that saw thunderstorm activity and this activity was only isolated. Year to date precipitation values were between 50 and 90 percent of normal for most of the region. A small part of the region consisting of southern Lubbock County, Lynn County, and western Garza County was between 100 and 150 percent of normal. July was 1.7 degrees and 3.3 degrees above seasonal averages for Lubbock and Childress respectively. Through the month of July, 2012 ties as the warmest year on record. Although maximum temperatures have been lower than 2011, minimum temperatures have been higher. Keetch-Byram Drought Index values worsened during July. Values between 600 and 700 were observed over the western South Plains and Rolling Plains with values of 500 to 600 elsewhere.||Irrigated crops struggled to keep up with water demands due to the lack of precipitation. Dryland crops were also struggling and were likely to fail within the next month. Pastures and rangelands were deteriorating rapidly with little to no grazing land left for cattle. Although wildfire activity was low, fuels were dry enough to sustain wildfires from lightning starts in July.||Economic losses due to drought through July since the drought began were estimated near $2.4 billion.

title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, May 24, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from May 24, 2012 to May 24, 2012. Affected areas: Douglas. Episode summary: A cold front drifted east into the Superior WI area. Some thunderstorms associated with the front resulted in nearby rainfall reports as high as 3 to 4 1/2 inches. Some street flooding resulted in Superior WI. Details: County Road UU and Papano Road were both under water.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, May 26, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from May 26, 2012 to May 27, 2012. Affected areas: Lincoln. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed in an unstable air mass north of a warm front. Some of the storms became quite strong as they moved through central and east central Wisconsin, producing hail up to nickel size, heavy rainfall and isolated wind damage. Details: A weather observer north of Tomahawk, near Rice Reservoir, measured 3.55 inches of rain from storms that moved through the area between about 9:30 PM CDT on the 26th and 2:00 AM CDT on the 27th. A spotter measured 2.60 inches of rain from thunderstorms that moved through the Heafford Junction area between about 10:00 PM CDT on the 26th and 2:18 AM CDT on the 27th.

title: High Wind: California, Jun 04, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from June 04, 2012 to June 04, 2012. Affected areas: Owens Valley. Episode summary: An unseasonably strong low pressure system brought isolated high winds to the Owens Valley and the Mojave Desert. Details: High winds blew a large tree as well as large branches across Old Sherwin Grade Road northwest of Bishop. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, May 03, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 03, 2012 to May 03, 2012. Affected areas: Calumet, Manitowoc, Outagamie, Winnebago. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed over northeast Iowa Wednesday evening before tracking over east central Wisconsin overnight on May 2nd into the morning of May 3rd. Rainfall measurements for the 24 hour period ending around 7 am CDT indicated a widespread 2 to 4.5 inches of rain over east central Wisconsin. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 30, 2012 to May 30, 2012. Affected areas: Concho, Runnels. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 30, 2012 to May 30, 2012. Affected areas: Foard. Details: A storm chaser reported a large rain-wrapped tornado estimated to be about 10 miles northwest of Truscott. This tornado occurred in open country and no damage was reported. The strong outflow winds spread to the north into the southern portions of Imperial county, and they generated dense blowing dust and sand, creating dust storm conditions in towns such as Calexico, Holtville and Seeley. Some of these storms produced heavy rain leading to flash flooding along with large hail and strong winds. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding on Flores St requiring a high water rescue by law enforcement personnel.

title: Flash Flood: California, Aug 11, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from August 11, 2012 to August 13, 2012. Affected areas: Inyo, San Bernardino. Episode summary: Monsoon moisture fueled another round of thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Several storms produced severe weather and flash flooding. Details: Six inches of water flowed down Buena Vista Drive. Six inches of water along with rocks and debris flowed across Avalon Avenue between Winters and Aberdeen. Eight to 10 inches of swiftly flowing water covered the intersection of Yucca Mesa Road and Buena Vista Drive. Reported property and crop damage: about $28,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Aug 18, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from August 18, 2012 to August 18, 2012. Affected areas: Inyo. Details: Highway 190 was washed out and closed at mile marker 79. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Aug 22, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from August 22, 2012 to August 22, 2012. Affected areas: Inyo, San Bernardino. Details: Several unpaved roads were closed due to flooding in the southeast part of the Mojave National Preserve. Sections of paved roads were covered with debris and grapefruit sized rocks. title: Heat: Wisconsin, Jul 02, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heat, from July 02, 2012 to July 07, 2012. Affected areas: Adams, Buffalo, Clark, Crawford, Grant, Jackson, Juneau, La Crosse, Monroe, Richland, Taylor, Trempealeau and 1 more areas. Episode summary: Five people died from the effects of a long duration heatwave that gripped western Wisconsin from July 2nd through July 7th. Two of the deaths occurred in La Crosse County with one each in Juneau, Richland and Vernon Counties. Numerous people were also treated for heat related illnesses. The highest apparent temperatures during the heatwave ranged from 100 to 110 each day. Two record daily high temperatures were set at La Crosse (La Crosse County). Other impacts from the heat included stimulating algae growth on area waterways which depleted oxygen levels leading to fish kills. Milk production was down during the heat as well, as cows starting drinking more water and ate less feed leading to the drop. Campgrounds also reported a downturn in business as potential campers remained at home and numerous roads buckled and had to be repaired. Details: One person died from heat related causes but additional details were not available from county officials. The Viroqua automated weather observing system recorded maximum apparent temperatures of 100 to 103 each day but conditions may have been warmer in surrounding areas. title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 06, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from July 06, 2012 to July 06, 2012. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: A deep southerly flow of monsoon moisture remained over the region. The presence of an inverted upper trough led to the development of slow moving storms that produced locally heavy rainfall resulting in flash flooding. Details: A slow moving thunderstorm developed over eastern portions of the city of El Paso. Heavy rainfall from the storm caused water to flow over the curbs along a long stretch of Lee Trevino boulevard. Two cars were reported stalled out in the rising water. A local media website showed photos of water 1.5 feet deep flowing across the intersection of Eads and Pebble Hills drive. A weather spotter reported a total of .61 inches of rainfall in 23 minutes. This resulted in some minor street flooding in the area.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 09, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from July 09, 2012 to July 09, 2012. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: A back door cold front moved into the region and combined with monsoon moisture that was lingering in the region to produce thunderstorms. A weak disturbance embedded in the northwest flow aloft added to the instability across the region. Details: A weather spotter reported .65 inches of rain in 45 minutes from thunderstorm that moved across the area. Curb to curb minor street flooding was reported along Hondo Pass in northeast El Paso.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 23, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from July 23, 2012 to July 23, 2012. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: Southeasterly flow around a high pressure ridge over the central plains allowed for a return of deeper moisture into the area. Afternoon heating led to an unstable atmosphere and several slow moving thunderstorms developed late in the afternoon. These slow moving storms resulted in localized minor flooding across the region. Details: A local weather spotter reported minor flooding along Mesa Hills drive near Sunland Park Mall. Water reached the height of the curb in some spots. A public report of .55 inches of rain in less than one hours time was reported at the same time near Putnam School in the same area.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 30, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 30, 2012 to July 31, 2012. Affected areas: Riverside, San Diego. Episode summary: A large moisture surge moved over the area as monsoon flow rotated around the western edge of an upper high over the southern plains and into southern California. Daytime heating, along with a low to mid-level circulation coming up from the south, was sufficient to create the instability needed for thunderstorms over the mountains and deserts during the two-day period of the 30th and 31st. Heavy rain was the main threat from these storms and resulted in several instances of flash flooding, most notably in the San Diego County deserts and the Coachella Valley. Details: La Posta road flooded near Interstate 8. A nearby mesonet station recorded 1.66 inches of rain in the past hour from 1300 to 1400 PST. Heavy rain caused a 15-foot wall of water to rush through a slot canyon near the Silent Caves and Split Mountain Road. Two hikers, a man and his son, were caught in the canyon, but were able to get to higher ground in the caves and were unharmed. Their pickup truck, however, was washed 1.5 miles down the canyon and destroyed. Flooding reported on Split Mountain Road near Highway 78 in Ocotillo Wells. Source unknown. title: Drought: Wisconsin, Jul 01, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Drought, from July 01, 2012 to July 31, 2012. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green, Green Lake, Iowa, Jefferson, Kenosha, Lafayette, Marquette, Milwaukee and 6 more areas. Episode summary: The extremely dry conditions that began in June continued in July across southern Wisconsin. Many locations did not see any precipitation until several rounds of thunderstorms moved through the region during the middle and end of the month. While these thunderstorm events held monthly precipitation deficits to between 0.10 and 0.20 of an inch below normal, the modest monthly deficits still increased the yearly precipitation deficits to between 3 and 5 inches. In addition to the continued below normal precipitation, there were several periods of extreme heat that increased the damaging effects on already stressed crops. The rain that did fall came too late for much of the corn crop, as it fell after the critical pollination stage. Details: The drought designation for Sauk County was raised from Abnormally Dry (D0) over the northern 2/3 of the county with Moderate Drought (D1) over the southern 1/3 on July 3rd, to Extreme (D3) with Severe (D2) over the far northwest corner on July 17th. Late month rains brought only minimal improvement to Severe (D2) for the entire county by July 31st. The drought designation for Washington County was raised from Moderate Drought (D1) on July 3rd, to Extreme (D3) on July 17th. Late month rains brought only minimal improvement to Severe (D2) for the entire county by July 31st. The drought designation for Green County was raised from Moderate (D1) on July 3rd, to Extreme (D3) on July 17th. Late month rains did little to improve the precipitation deficits, keeping the designation at Extreme (D3) county-wide through July 31st.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, from August 09, 2012 to August 09, 2012. Affected areas: San Bernardino. title: Flood, Wildfire: California, Aug 09, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, Wildfire, from August 09, 2012 to August 12, 2012. Affected areas: San Diego, San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: The Chihuahua fire was started by lightning around 1213 PST on the 9th, along Chihuahua Valley Road near Sunshine Summit, northwest of Warner Springs. There were 250 residences and 100 other structures threatened by the fire, leading to mandatory evacuations of the residences and a Boy Scout camp along Chihuahua Valley Road. The fire burned a total of 2007 acres before being fully contained around 1730 PST on the 12th. Details: Rich Thompson, the IMET at the Chihuahua Fire heard reports of flooding on a few roads in and around the fire on the fire radios. A few crews were stranded temporarily, but no one was injured. He estimates approximately 0.26 to 0.50 inches of rain in less than one hour at the base camp and up to one inch in one hour over the fire itself.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Aug 31, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from August 31, 2012 to August 31, 2012. Affected areas: Angelina. Episode summary: Hurricane Isaac made its second landfall during the predawn hours of August 29th across Southeast Louisiana. This hurricane moved very slowly north and east and was downgraded to a tropical storm later that same afternoon but due to its slow northeast movement...tropical storm force winds were not felt across portions of East Central and Northeast Louisiana until the early morning hours of August 30th. These winds estimated to be sustained at 35 to 50 mph with gusts as high as 70 mph produced winds that downed multiple trees across a few parishes. While the remnants of Isaac moved north into Arkansas on August 30th and 31st, feeder bands extended well south into Northeast Texas and some of these produced severe thunderstorms across Angelina County in Northeast Texas. Details: Excessive heavy rainfall resulted in a creek overflowing its bank and flooding pastureland with rapid moving water near a home along Old Diboll Highway in Burke, Texas.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Aug 17, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from August 17, 2012 to August 17, 2012. Affected areas: Smith. Episode summary: A weak stationary frontal boundary across Northeast Texas and Northwest Louisiana served as a focus for showers and thunderstorms, some of which produced strong and damaging wind gusts. Isolated flash flood producing storms were also reported across portions of Smith County, Texas. Details: Flooding was reported on Interstate 20 and FM. 14 near Lindale, Texas.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Jul 11, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from July 11, 2012 to July 11, 2012. Affected areas: Calhoun. Episode summary: A slow moving upper level disturbance interacted with deep tropical moisture to produce numerous showers and thunderstorms over the Victoria Crossroads and Mid-Coast regions during the day. The showers and thunderstorms began in the early morning hours and persisted through the afternoon. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 4 inches occurred over the Victoria Crossroads and Mid-Coast regions with higher amounts between 6 to 8 inches over Calhoun County. This heavy rain caused flooding of roadways across Calhoun County from the late morning through the afternoon hours. Details: Flooding occurred over a wooden bridge over the Chocolate Bayou near the Matson addition, southwest of Port Lavaca. Roadways were closed due to flooding along Farm to Market Road 1090 northwest of Port Lavaca between Maxwell Ditch Road and Royal Road, and the bridges intersecting Oakglen Drive and Sweetwater Road near the Chocolate Bayou southwest of Port Lavaca. Heavy rains produced flooding near Chocolate Bayou with water over the roadway on Highway 35 between Farm to Market Roads 2433 and 2541 southwest of Port Lavaca. Reported property and crop damage: about $110,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jul 14, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from July 14, 2012 to July 17, 2012. Affected areas: Kleberg. Episode summary: Lightning started a wildfire on the Padre Island National Seashore about 6 miles south of the Visitors Center on July 14th. The fire burned for over 2 days and consumed roughly 13000 acres. There were no structures lost or injuries reported. The fire primarily burned grasses on the uninhabited part of the federally owned park. Details: A lightning strike on the afternoon of July 14th started a wildfire on the Padre Island National Seashore about 6 miles south of the Visitors Center. The fire spread during the next two days consuming roughly 13000 acres before the fire was extinguished.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 18, 2012

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jul 27, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from July 27, 2012 to July 27, 2012. Affected areas: Webb. Episode summary: A nighttime core rain event occurred in the Laredo vicinity during the early morning hours of July 27th. A weak upper level low pressure area moved across the western Brush Country during the night and interacted with deep tropical moisture over the area. Thunderstorms developed over the eastern part of Webb County and slowly moved toward Laredo a few hours after midnight. Very heavy rainfall of 5 to 8 inches occurred within a 3 hour time period over the northeast portion of Laredo. This produced flooding in a residential area on the northeast side of Laredo. Several high water rescues were performed with motorists stranded from Interstate 35 to Loop 20 on the northeast side of Laredo. One person was evacuated from her home due to rising water. Around 100 homes received damage from flood waters in northeast Laredo. Details: Flooding was reported on the far north side of Laredo in the San Isidro subdivision. These treated people were considered injured and a broad estimate of 300 was assigned to south-central and southeast Wisconsin.||The counties surrounding Dane had 4 days of 100 degrees or higher, while counties toward Lake Michigan had 2 or 3 days. The cites of Janesville, Kenosha, Middleton, Sullivan, and Paddock Lake topped out at 106 degrees, which was Wisconsin's highest temperature for the 2012 summer season. Numerous new daily record highs were set as well as record high minimums. The long duration of this excessive heat period makes this probably one of the four most dangerous heat waves to strike southern Wisconsin in recorded history.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 13, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from July 13, 2012 to July 13, 2012. Affected areas: Jim Hogg. Episode summary: Broad high pressure over the Gulf of Mexico kept a conveyor belt of moisture moving north into the region, while midlevel high pressure centers over the plains and the southeast US resulted in disturbances aloft and unsettled weather across the Rio Grande Valley and Deep South Texas on July 13th. Large scale lift and upper diffluence combined with a light to moderate southeast wind, and abundant moisture, allowed for seabreeze convection. The convection initiated along the coastal counties earlier in the afternoon and continued to march across the region through the evening hours. Rainfall amounts ranged from around 3/10 inch in the south-central area to around 3 inches in the city of Sheboygan. This translated to monthly deficits ranging from around 4 inches to 1 inch. Sufficient soil moisture allowed for crops to grow normally, however, by the end of June it became apparent higher parts of farm fields were drying out and corn and soybean crops were showing signs of stress. Farther north, a slow-moving supercell developed in western Briscoe County and drifted southeast directly over Caprock Canyons State Park accompanied by torrential rain rates of three inches per hour. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from October 12, 2012 to October 12, 2012. Affected areas: Hale. Episode summary: Unusually moist air for mid-October was carried into the Texas South Plains on the 11th ahead of a vigorous upper low in the four corners region. By the afternoon of the 12th, this upper low tracked into Colorado accompanied by a strong subtropical jet that overspread the South Plains. With surface dewpoints in the mid to upper 60s and diminishing stratocumulus clouds, strong instability developed by late afternoon over the central South Plains. Very strong wind shear already in place was made even stronger near a warm front that began lifting slowly north between Lubbock and Plainview. By 1700 CST, a pair of strong and severe storms erupted near Shallowater and began moving north-northeast. One of these storms developed strong low-level rotation as it crossed the warm front near Hale Center and assumed an easterly motion. This rotation culminated in two tornadoes over open land in eastern Hale County. Earlier, this same storm produced very large hail up to baseball size that damaged several vehicle windows at a rest stop on I-27. Also, large hail up to golf ball size accompanied a left-moving supercell that raced northward near I-27. Both of these supercells decayed around 1900 CST before a third supercell late this evening entered Yoakum County from neighboring Lea County, NM. Although NWS Lubbock Doppler Radar indicated the likelihood of large hail west and northwest of Plains, this final supercell did not produce any known severe weather before it evolved into a line of strong thunderstorms while overspreading much of the South Plains before midnight. Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms, mainly during the early part of the month, brought between 0.5 inch and 3 inches of rain to southern Wisconsin for the month, but monthly deficits ranged from around 0.5 inch to between 2 and 3 inches. This increased the yearly precipitation deficits to between 5 and 9 inches. By the end of September a slight improvement in the drought was observed over the southeastern counties which went from D2 (severe) down to D1 (moderate), or from D3 (extreme) down to D2 (severe). This trend is reflected in the attached image. The extreme heat from earlier in the summer did not continue into September, with monthly average temperatures at or a bit below normal. title: Heat: California, Sep 15, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heat, from September 15, 2012 to September 15, 2012. Affected areas: Orange County Coastal Areas, San Diego County Coastal Areas, San Diego County Valleys. Episode summary: Strong high pressure over California resulted in very hot and dry conditions around the 15th, up to 15 degrees warmer than seasonal averages. By 0900 PST, temperatures were already pushing 100 degrees in many inland valley locations and even closer to the coast. Two separate running events were held that day, sending several people to the hospital for heat exhaustion. Lindbergh Field broke their record high temperature on the 15th, coming in at 101 degrees F. Due to the heat, officials did shorten the length of one of the races, while the Orange Coast College delayed their afternoon football game until later in the evening. Details: There were 11 heat-related injuries requiring hospitalization between 0800 and 1000 PST at a 5K run in Balboa Park. Temperatures ranged between 92 and 99 degrees during that time. The ages of the injured ranged from 15 to 17 years old. A 45 year old woman apparently suffered heat exhaustion and was airlifted from a hiking trail near Lake Hodges in Rancho Bernardo. Temperatures in the area were in the 90s at the time. High temperatures resulted in heat exhaustion and dehydration of 8 runners participating in a cross country track meet at Fairview Park. Six were transported to hospitals; two were treated locally and released. Approximate ages of the injured were 17 to 20.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from September 06, 2012 to September 06, 2012. Affected areas: San Bernardino And Riverside County Valleys - The Inland Empire. Episode summary: The Canyon fire started around 1052 PST on the 6th as three separate fires, near the intersection of Lambs Canyon Road and Gilman Springs Road near Beaumont in Riverside County. One firefighter received minor fire-related injuries and was transported by paramedics for treatment. The fire burned a total of 3 acres before being fully contained around 1150 PST the same day. The cause of the fire is unknown. CHP closed the #2 lane on northbound Highway 79 for a time.

title: Wildfire: California, Sep 23, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from September 23, 2012 to September 26, 2012. Affected areas: San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: The Shockey fire started around 1114 PST on the 23rd, near the intersection of the Shockey Truck Trail and Highway 94, east of Campo in San Diego County. As the fire burned rapidly, approximately 25 structures were threatened. Two residences were damaged, 11 other residences destroyed along with 14 outbuildings and 11 vehicles. Mandatory evacuations were in place for approximately 125 residents in the communities of Tierra del Sol, Boulevard and Jewell Valley. Shelters were opened at Mountain Empire High School (animal sheltering as well) and the Campo Tribal Shelter. Three child care facilities voluntarily evacuated as well. Highway 94 was closed from the Shockey Truck Trail east to Jewell Valley and the Mexican border. Three firefighters received unknown injuries. A 69-year old male was found dead in his home due to burn injuries and smoke inhalation. The fire burned a total of 2556 acres before being fully contained around 1900 PST on the 26th. The fire started in an area where target shooting occurs, but the exact cause of the fire is still unknown. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,670,000.

The ridge began to retrograde west towards Baja California. Despite the necessary ingredients being in place (lifting of warm and humid low and mid level air, a favorable upper level jet pattern, and an area of surface low pressure) widespread rain did not occur. ||Only splotchy heavy rainfall fell, with the heaviest rain falling on Friday September 14th across the Valley. Another weak frontal boundary and more seabreeze activity on the 18th and 19th provided spotty, but much needed, rainfall across the Lower and Mid Valley. Tropical cyclones were non existent for the Texas coast through September, held off by very dry air associated with the ridge and its frequent extension into the southern and central Plains states. title: Drought: Wisconsin, Nov 01, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Drought, from November 01, 2012 to November 30, 2012. Affected areas: Buffalo, Clark, Crawford, Grant, Jackson, La Crosse, Monroe, Taylor, Trempealeau. Episode summary: Precipitation amounts across western Wisconsin averaged a half to 1.5 inches during the month of November. The drought conditions showed some improvement during the first half of the month with Clark, Jackson, La Crosse and Monroe Counties no longer classified as being in a severe drought. Conditions also temporarily improved over portions of Taylor and Trempealeau Counties, but by the end of the month, the severe drought covered the northern half of both counties along with all of Buffalo County. Dairy farmers were impacted by the drought during the latter half of the year because of higher feed costs. Milk production increased during the first part of the year leading to lower milk prices. title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Oct 30, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from October 30, 2012 to October 30, 2012. Affected areas: Kenosha, Sheboygan. Episode summary: Deep surface low pressure associated with the remains of Hurricane Sandy, and Canadian high pressure building into the Northern Plains, created a tight surface pressure gradient over southern Wisconsin. Some minor beach erosion was reported in Kenosha County due to the high waves that were the result of the strong winds. Estimated waves heights along the Kenosha County shoreline ranged up to 8 to 10 feet. Wave heights diminished to 4 to 7 feet as one went north. title: High Wind: Texas, Dec 14, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from December 14, 2012 to December 14, 2012. Affected areas: Parmer. Episode summary: After the South Plains saw its first snow of the season earlier this week, a powerful and fast-moving line of thunderstorms plowed across the South Plains this afternoon ahead of a vigorous upper storm system. The day began with abundant low clouds and moisture from the Gulf of Mexico on stiff southerly winds. These clouds parted by late morning followed by even stronger southerly winds with frequent gusts over 40 mph, areas of blowing dust, and abundant sunshine that would further destabilize the atmosphere. As a negatively-tilted upper trough and Pacific cold front began exiting eastern New Mexico shortly after 1300 CST, showers expanded in coverage near the state line and rapidly intensified into thunderstorms as they encountered an increasingly moist and unstable airmass. These storms solidified into a narrow, but intense squall line that raced eastward at highway speeds for the next four hours accompanied by several severe wind gusts measured between 58 and 77 mph. Scattered wind damage was reported throughout the South Plains and in some instances commercial power was disrupted. Well behind the thunderstorms, very strong winds developed a few thousand feet above the ground. Near Friona, these winds briefly mixed to the surface behind the cold front and produced a severe, non-convective wind gust. Details: Following a strong Pacific cold front and an earlier thunderstorm squall line, a non-convective wind gust of 61 mph was measured by a Texas Tech West Texas mesonet. Winds a few thousand feet above the ground behind the front were determined to be nearly 50 knots.

October 18th was the hottest October day all time across many locations across the Rio Grande Valley; high temperatures away from the coast soared above 100, including a blistering 108 at La Joya. Details: Little to no rain fell across Zapata County during October. title: Dust Storm, High Wind: Texas, Dec 19, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Dust Storm, High Wind, from December 19, 2012 to December 19, 2012. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Crosby, Floyd, Hale, Hall, Hockley, Lamb, Lubbock, Lynn, Motley and 4 more areas. Episode summary: A historic dust storm engulfed much of the South Plains this afternoon resulting in dust storm conditions (visibilities at or below 1/2 mile in blowing dust) at the Lubbock International Airport for the longest duration since December 16, 1977. The culprit for this exceptional dust storm was a surface cyclone rapidly deepening in far southwest Kansas ahead of a vigorous upper level trough exiting the southern Rockies. Along the southern periphery of this trough, a deep layer wind maximum overspread the Texas South Plains during the afternoon behind a Pacific cold front. Initially, a layer of thick high clouds prevented these winds from mixing to the surface behind the front, but as the late morning and afternoon wore on, these clouds departed and allowed high winds with frequent gusts around 60 mph to stir up extensive blowing dust on the Caprock. The highest wind gusts as measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet developed in Lubbock and Floyd Counties where peak wind gusts of 66 and 72 mph were recorded, respectively. Visibilities fell abruptly to 1/2 mile or less in many rural areas, with near-zero visibility at times as documented by TV news reporters along Interstate 27 in southern Hale and northern Lubbock Counties. These conditions contributed to a deadly 25-vehicle pileup on I-27 just south of New Deal. One man was fatally injured and at least 17 others suffered injuries of varying severity. Law enforcement promptly closed the interstate in both directions for several hours. Also, a mobile triage unit from UMC Hospital was dispatched for the first time

title: Strong Wind, Wildfire: Texas, Dec 19, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, Wildfire, from December 19, 2012 to December 20, 2012. Affected areas: Bell, Collin, Henderson, Mclennan, Wise. Episode summary: A line of thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front that was moving across the region. These thunderstorms produced mostly wind damage across the eastern half of the CWA. The most significant damage was reported in Collin County where a mobile home was rolled onto its top. In addition to the thunderstorm winds, very strong winds behind the front continued into the following day. Sustained winds of 20 to 30 mph were common with wind gusts over 50 mph in some locations. These winds caused many power outages across the region and some additional minor damage. Also, the strong winds fueled 2 grass fires which caused some property damage in Bell and McLennan Counties. Details: Strong winds fueled a grass fire which spread to a mobile home in the town of Gholson. The home was destroyed and one resident suffered smoke inhalation. A grass fire fueled by gusty winds spread to a barn filled with scrap metal. The barn and much of its contents were destroyed. Strong northwest winds behind a cold front blew the roof off a pump house located approximately 4 miles south-southwest of Decatur. The nearest AWOS reported winds over 45 mph around this time. Reported property and crop damage: about $121,500.

The greatest concentration of heavy snow was in western Denton County and Collin County where 4-6 of snow fell. There were also isolated locations that received 4-6 of snow in Parker, Grayson, Fannin, Hunt, and Emory counties. Details: An average of 3-5 inches of snow fell across Collin County with some isolated totals near 6 inches. In Plano, the local police department reported 51 vehicle accidents; with a possible 13 minor injuries due to the accidents but only one requiring transport to a hospital. An average of 4-5 inches of snow fell across the eastern half of Denton County. Temperatures that night fell into the upper teens and 20s which resulted in icy conditions on many roadways. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Drought, from October 01, 2012 to October 31, 2012. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green, Green Lake, Iowa, Jefferson, Kenosha, Lafayette, Marquette, Milwaukee and 8 more areas. Episode summary: Above normal precipitation at many locations in October helped to ease the drought across southern Wisconsin. Several rounds of steady rain, as well as showers and a few thunderstorms, brought between 2.3 inches and 5.5 inches of rain to southern Wisconsin for the month. Monthly surpluses ranged from around 0.25 inch to nearly 2.5 inches above normal, though locations in far southern Wisconsin still saw deficits between 0.02 of an inch and 0.43 of an inch. The yearly precipitation deficits were still running between 4 and 8 inches below normal. By the end of October improvement in the drought was observed over all of southern Wisconsin. The far southern counties went from D3 (Extreme) down to D2 (Severe), with much of the South-central Wisconsin going from D2 (Severe) down to D1 (Moderate). Much of Southeast Wisconsin, which generally saw the highest amounts of precipitation for the month, went from D1 (Moderate) to either D0 (Abnormally Dry) or out of a drought category all together. This trend is reflected in the attached image which addresses all of Wisconsin. Monthly average temperatures for October were 1 to 2 degrees below normal. Agricultural experts indicated that crop yields would be reduced.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Nov 22, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from November 22, 2012 to November 23, 2012. Affected areas: Ashland, Bayfield, Douglas, Iron. The combination of the system's synoptic snow and subsequent lake effect snow in the wake of the cold front resulted in up to a foot of snow in parts of northwestern Wisconsin. The greatest snowfall amounts, about 8 to 12 inches, stretched from east central Douglas County through the northern tier of Bayfield, Ashland, and Iron Counties. Several locations in northwestern Wisconsin measured 12.0 inches of snow, including Gile (Iron County), Cornucopia (Bayfield County), and Hawthorne (Douglas County). title: Heat: California, Oct 02, 2012
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heat, from October 02, 2012 to October 02, 2012. Affected areas: Northern Salinas Valley / Hollister Valley / Carmel Valley. Episode summary: An unseasonable heat wave gripped the area on the first two days of October 2012. High temperatures soared well into the 90s and 100s across the area, which was well above normal and resulted in several record high temperatures as well as all-time October record high temperatures. October 1 and 2 had high temperatures of 91 and 93 degrees in San Francisco and 100 and 101 in Salinas. Farm workers who were picking in the fields near Salinas on both days were negatively impacted by the excessive heat, which lead to a fatality of a farm worker on October 2 near Salinas. By the 3rd, cooler weather returned and the heat wave came to an end. Details: A farm worker picking crops in the fields near Salinas, California died as a result of excessive heat and heat stroke which lead to his having a heart attack.
