title: Wildfire: California, May 02, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from May 02, 2013 to May 02, 2013. Affected areas: San Bernardino And Riverside County Valleys - The Inland Empire. Episode summary: The Van Buren wildfire started around 0724 PST on the 2nd in the median of Van Buren Boulevard at Jurupa Road in Jurupa Valley (Riverside County). Jurupa Rd was closed from Van Buren to Rutile and Van Buren closed from Jurupa to Rutile. Evacuations were ordered for a few hours. The fire burned 12 acres, but destroyed two homes, an RV and 5 out buildings, with damage to two additional residences. No injuries were reported. The fire was fully contained around 1330 PST on the 2nd. The cause of the fire is likely a discarded cigarette. Reported property and crop damage: about $550,000.

title: High Wind: California, May 02, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 02, 2013 to May 02, 2013. Affected areas: San Bernardino And Riverside County Valleys - The Inland Empire, Santa Ana Mountains And Foothills. Episode summary: Surface high pressure built into the Great Basin, bringing strong and gusty northeast winds through and below passes and canyons during the morning of the 2nd. Winds temporarily decreased that night, before increasing again, somewhat, the morning of the 3rd. Details: High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0451 and 0551 PST on the 2nd and ended between 0951 and 1051 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained 30 to 45 mph with gusts mostly above 60 mph, including the peak gust of 70 mph measured between 0651 and 0751 PST. Winds gusted 35-40 mph with gusts above 55 mph between 0500 and 1000 PST on the 2nd. During this time, a peak gust of 62 mph was measured between 0816 and 0916 PST.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, May 22, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from May 22, 2013 to May 24, 2013. Affected areas: Trempealeau. Episode summary: Several rounds of thunderstorms rolled across western Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening of May 19th. The first round of storms produced wind damage across Buffalo County during the afternoon. The second round of storms in the evening produced additional severe wind gusts in Vernon, Grant and Richland Counties. The most significant damage occurred in Gilmanton (Buffalo County) were a dozen power poles were blown down. Details: Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Trempealeau River out of its banks at Dodge. The river crested over a foot above the flood stage at 10.34 feet.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 23, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 23, 2013 to May 23, 2013. Affected areas: Borden, Brewster, Howard, Scurry. Episode summary: A dryline was located across the Permian Basin and the Trans Pecos, and a cold front was in the Texas panhandle. Good lower level moisture was present to the east of the dryline, and there was plentiful upper level moisture available. The atmosphere was very unstable. Mid-level lift was present with an upper level disturbance that moved over the area. This combination of moisture, lift, and instability helped to create several severe thunderstorms that produced large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding across West Texas. Details: Thunderstorms moved over Howard County and produced flash flooding in Big Spring. The 1300 block of Sixth Street, portions of Third Street, and the intersection of Alamesa and Parkway were all flooded. A taxi cab was reported to be pushed off the road in Big Spring. The cost of damage is a rough estimate. A thunderstorm moved over Brewster County and produced heavy rain in Alpine. A thunderstorm moved over Howard County and produced heavy rain over southeast Big Spring. Reported property and crop damage: about $7,500.

title: Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 10, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 10, 2013 to May 10, 2013. Affected areas: Harris. Episode summary: Clusters and lines of storms produced hail and flooding. In addition several homes and one individual were struck by lightning. Details: There were numerous reports of flooding around the greater Houston metropolitan area. There was curb high street flooding at the intersection of Gessner and Hammerly Streets. There was also high water causing flooding at the West Sam Houston Tollway southbound at U.S. Highway 59 southwest. Frontage road flooding was reported at the 610 West Loop northbound at U.S. Highway 59 southwest. There was a Heavy rains weakened the root system of a large tree causing it to collapse. Reported property and crop damage: about $751,500.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado: Wisconsin, May 29, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado, from May 29, 2013 to May 29, 2013. Affected areas: Grant, La Crosse. Episode summary: A small tornado crossed the Mississippi River from Iowa hitting a campground just north of Bagley (Grant County). This tornado was part of a larger severe weather outbreak that occurred across much of western Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening of May 29th. These storms developed in a warm and moist airmass behind a warm front that was moving north across the Upper Midwest. In addition to the tornado, a pole barn and other structures were damaged near Whitehall (Trempealeau County) and structural damage to buildings also occurred near Richland Center (Richland County). Details: Heavy rain caused water to spread over several roads in Bagley as the drainage system was not able to keep up the rain. Streams in the area were running very high. Heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in the city of La Crosse and also caused some manhole covers to pop off. A small tornado crossed the Mississippi River from Clayton County going through a campground north of Bagley before dissipating.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Apr 10, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from April 10, 2013 to April 10, 2013. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green Lake, Marquette, Sheboygan. Episode summary: Ice accumulations of 1/10 to 2/10 of an inch brought down tree limbs and power lines causing scattered power outages. Some trees were felled by the weight of the accumulated ice combined with strong northeast winds gusting to around 35 mph. The freezing rain and sleet were on the northern edge of a large precipitation shield associated with persistent warm air advection aloft, with the rain falling into a sub-freezing layer near the ground. Details: Emergency management officials reported ice accumulations of 1/16 to 1/8 of an inch.

title: High Wind: Wisconsin, Apr 10, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: High Wind, from April 10, 2013 to April 11, 2013. Affected areas: Dane, Green, Iowa, Lafayette, Rock, Sauk. Episode summary: A wake low developed behind an area of rain showers as a dry slot around surface low pressure moved through the region in the early morning hours of April 11th. There were reports of downed tree branches and scattered power outages due to downed power lines, as well as entire trees being downed by the powerful wind gusts that reached as high as 63 mph (55 knots) at a mesonet site at Madison's Capital Square and 60 mph (52 knots) at Lone Rock Airport.

title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Apr 11, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from April 11, 2013 to April 11, 2013. Affected areas: Columbia, Dodge, Jefferson, Kenosha, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Racine, Walworth, Washington, Waukesha. Episode summary: A wake low developed behind an area of rain showers that moved through the region in the early morning hours of April 11th. There were reports of downed tree branches and scattered power outages due to downed power lines, as well as entire trees being downed by the powerful wind gusts that reached as high as 52 mph (45 knots) at Watertown Airport. Details: A measured gust to 52 mph (45 knots) was reported by the AWOS at Watertown Airport. The NWS office in Sullivan recorded a peak gust of 51 mph (44 knots). Reported property and crop damage: about $73,000.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, May 30, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from May 30, 2013 to May 31, 2013. Affected areas: Jackson. Episode summary: For the second straight day, thunderstorms developed during the afternoon across western Wisconsin. Some of these storms produced damaging winds from central Grant County northeast into Adams County. A wind gust of 70 mph occurred near Lancaster (Grant County). Details: Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Black River out of its banks in Black River Falls. The river crested over two feet above the flood stage at 49.31 feet.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Apr 08, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from April 08, 2013 to April 30, 2013. Affected areas: Green, Jefferson, Kenosha, Ozaukee, Rock, Sheboygan. Episode summary: The second week of April saw rainfall totals between 2 inches and 5 inches across southern Wisconsin. These totals represented 300 percent to 600 percent of the amount normally seen from April 7th through the 14th. This pushed several of the rivers into minor to moderate flooding, with major flooding at several locations on the Rock River, and on the Fox River at New Munster, inundating nearby land areas and roads. Rivers crested between 1 foot and 4.5 feet above flood stage. Runoff was enhanced by a lingering deep frost layer. While the top 4 or 5 inches of soil had thawed, there was still a foot or more of frost below the top-most unfrozen layer, preventing much of the rain from percolating into the ground. Some of the fast-responding rivers and streams fell back within their banks in a day or two, while others remained above flood stage through the end of the month and into May as rain totals for the entire month ranged between 5 and 8 inches, or between 150 percent and 200 percent of normal. The Milwaukee River near Cedarburg experienced minor flooding, cresting at 12.44 feet, or 1.44 feet over the flood stage of 11 feet, at 419 AM CDT on April 14th. title: Flood: Wisconsin, Apr 18, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from April 18, 2013 to April 24, 2013. Affected areas: Green, Racine, Rock. Episode summary: Repeated rounds of showers and some thunderstorms during the second half of April brought rain totals for the entire month to between 5 and 8 inches, or between 150 percent and 200 percent of normal across southern Wisconsin. With some rivers already in flood from the 2 inches to 5 inches of rain that had fallen across southern Wisconsin earlier in the month, additional minor to moderate flooding occurred at locations that had either just fallen below flood stage from the early month rain, or went into flood with the added amounts in the second half of the month. Rivers crested between 1 and 2 feet above flood stage, inundating nearby land areas and roads. Some of the fast-responding rivers and streams fell back within their banks in a day or two, while others remained above flood stage for almost a week. Details: The East Branch of the Pecatonica River near Martintown crested at 15.11 feet, or 1.61 feet above the flood stage of 13.5 feet at 1145 PM on April 21st. Turtle Creek in Beloit experienced minor flooding as it crested at 10.44 feet, or 1.44 feet above the flood stage of 9 feet at 832 AM on April 19th. The Sugar River at Brodhead went back into minor flooding as it crested at 6.64 feet, or 1.64 feet above the flood stage of 5 feet at 145 AM on April 20th. Reported property and crop damage: about $27,000.

title: Flood: Texas, May 09, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from May 09, 2013 to May 09, 2013. Affected areas: Brazos. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance coupled with a moist environment, led to late afternoon thunderstorms across central Texas. These storms produced wind damage, hail and flooding. Details: A foot of water covered the intersection of Deacon Drive and Rio Grande Street in College Station. Flash flooding was also reported on Old San Antonio Road as a creek was overrunning its banks. Minor street flooding was reported at the intersection of George Bush Drive and University Oaks Drive. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, Jun 26, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from June 26, 2013 to June 26, 2013. Affected areas: Eau Claire. Episode summary: Thunderstorms began to develop during the afternoon of Wednesday, June 26th. These storms developed from the Twin Cities, northeast across east central Minnesota, and west central Wisconsin and moved slowly southeast. The storms became severe along the Mississippi River Valley from the area around Red Wing Minnesota, east to River Falls and Ellsworth, Wisconsin. Details: Very heavy rainfall in a short period of time caused a mudslide on Highway 53 just south of the Eau Claire/Chippewa county line. The southbound lanes were closed for about three hours as crews removed more than 30 truckloads of soil. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Jun 19, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from June 19, 2013 to June 19, 2013. Affected areas: Hockley. Episode summary: After the morning complex of storms and associated flash flooding northeast of the South Plains, an outflow boundary from these storms surged west onto the Caprock ahead of strong easterly winds and widespread blowing dust. This dust became thick enough to reduce visibilities occasionally below 1/4 mile in some areas. By mid-afternoon, a lone supercell storm developed along this boundary in southeast Cochran County and later produced a 20-minute EF-2 tornado in southwest Hockley County. Although this tornado remained over mostly undeveloped land, some oil field equipment, metal buildings, and power poles were heavily damaged or destroyed. The parent supercell also produced very large hail slightly larger than three inches in diameter that damaged some homes and vehicles. Farther west, scattered storms exited east-central New Mexico and produced a few instances of sub-severe wind gusts in Parmer and Bailey Counties along with marginally severe hail near Muleshoe. As these storms continued east and moved into more stable air behind the outflow boundary, they quickly weakened but still managed to generate locally heavy rainfall. Details: A supercell thunderstorm spawned an EF-2 tornado in far southwest Hockley County resulting in damage to oil field equipment, outbuildings, power poles, and storage tanks. Although the parent storm moved very slowly east throughout the tornado's life, a strong rear flank downdraft and occluding mesocyclone caused the tornado to veer sharply northward early in its life. title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 10, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 10, 2013 to May 10, 2013. Affected areas: Hardin, Jefferson, Orange. Episode summary: A north to northwest flow with multiple short waves traveling across the area kicked off severe weather in Southeast Texas. High winds, hail, and heavy rain was reported during the event. Details: Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall caused saturated ground that gave way to flash flooding. Streets and cars were flooded in the north end of Beaumont. Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall caused saturated ground that gave way to flash flooding. A neighborhood flooded in Lumberton with 2 homes taking on water. Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall caused saturated ground that gave way to flash flooding. Several roads were flooded and closed around Bridge City and Vidor. Reported property and crop damage: about $150,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, May 23, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from May 23, 2013 to May 23, 2013. Affected areas: Wilbarger. Episode summary: Strong outflow winds emanated from the north side a thunderstorm complex moving through the Abilene to Throckmorton region, resulting in severe gusts farther north. Details: Relayed by Wilbarger County EM.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jun 06, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from June 06, 2013 to June 06, 2013. Affected areas: Henderson. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a late Spring cold front as it pushed southeast across north Texas. Isolated minor wind damage occurred around the area late Wednesday night and Thursday morning associated with the storms. Details: Heavy rainfall contributed to a collission of a tractor trailer rig and a pickup truck on Loop 7 in Athens. A passenger in the pickup was killed in the accident.

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 01, 2013 to June 17, 2013. Affected areas: Cooke, Denton, Montague, Wise. Episode summary: A few of the northern counties beginning the month of June in severe drought received some beneficial rains during the first week or so, and were subsequently upgraded to moderate drought around the middle of the month. Details: D2 / Severe drought conditions in place at the beginning of June improved to D1/moderate by June 18th, and remained as such through the end of the month. D2/severe drought conditions in place at the beginning of June were upgraded to D1/moderate around the middle of the month. Moderate/D1 conditions remained in place through the end of the month. D2/severe drought conditions in place at the beginning of June were upgraded to D1/moderate around the middle of June, and remained as such through the end of the month. Reported property and crop damage: about $6,000.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, May 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from May 01, 2013 to May 16, 2013. Affected areas: Jackson. Episode summary: Township roads across Jackson County that were covered with flood waters starting in April, opened up by the middle of May as the waters receded. Details: Stetzer Road in the Town of Melrose was closed starting in April until May 16th due to flooding and high water on the Black River and Germann Valley Creek. Hawk Island Road in the Town of Manchester was closed starting in April until May 9th due to flooding and high water on the Black River.

title: Wildfire: Texas, May 13, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 13, 2013 to May 14, 2013. Affected areas: Lampasas, Palo Pinto. Episode summary: After some recent rainfall, conditions became extremely dry on the afternoon of Monday, May 13th. Low relative humidity and 10 to 20 mph winds allowed fires which started as controlled burns to quickly become uncontrolled. Details: Lometa Volunteer Fire Department fought and contained a 74 acre brush fire on Monday and Tuesday May 13-14. Ranch land was burned, but no structures caught fire. However, the forcing was not sufficient for this convection to overcome the strong nocturnal inversion and tap into the marginal elevated instability. The strong deep layer shear easily toppled developing thunderstorms which led to brief periods of heavy rain. The water quickly receded once showers and thunderstorms ended over the city. The shortwave quickly moved to the east, shifting the favorable environment for development out of the Texas Panhandle by the late morning hours. Details: Brief heavy rain caused water to cover one lane of Osage Road south of Interstate 40 in Amarillo (Potter County), as reported by an off duty National Weather Service Employee. The KVII schoolnet site at Cornado Elementary School (Potter County) reported 0.83 inches of heavy rain in association with these thunderstorms. No reports of street flooding accompanied this report.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado: Texas, May 25, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado, from May 25, 2013 to May 25, 2013. Affected areas: Bee, Goliad, Live Oak, Victoria. Episode summary: Deep atmospheric moisture was in place over South Texas during the morning hours on May 25th. A slow moving upper level disturbance moved into the area from the west producing scattered to numerous thunderstorms over the northern Coastal Bend into the Victoria Crossroads. Showers and thunderstorms trained over the same areas into the early afternoon hours. Rain amounts between 7 and 9 inches caused flash flooding from Three Rivers to Beeville to Goliad to Victoria. The most significant flooding occurred near the community of Pettus. Atmospheric shear profile was relatively weak and funnel clouds and a weak tornado occurred in the near-tropical air mass. Details: Interstate 37 was closed due to high water near the community of Oakville. Heavy rainfall between 7 to 9 inches occurred over northern Bee County causing significant flooding along Medio Creek. Flood waters from Medio Creek caused road closures along U. S. Highway 181 at the intersections with Farm to Market Road 623 in Pettus and with Farm to Market Road 798 in Tulsita. Flood waters reached a depth of 1 to 2 feet in homes and businesses in the city of Pettus, including Interstate 37 was closed due to 4 feet of water over the road near mile marker 74. Reported property and crop damage: about $620,000.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2013 to May 31, 2013. Affected areas: Armstrong, Carson, Collingsworth, Dallam, Deaf Smith, Donley, Gray, Hansford, Hartley, Hemphill, Hutchinson, Lipscomb and 8 more areas. Episode summary: Drought conditions worsened during the month of May despite a few precipitation events during the latter half of the month. Exceptional (D4) drought encompasses the northern and western portions of the Texas Panhandle with Extreme (D3) drought affecting the southeastern portion of the Texas Panhandle. Severe (D2) drought only affects Gray County.| |May brought many late freezes and several opportunities for precipitation. Amarillo recorded 2.80 inches of precipitation for May (0.51 above normal), Dalhart recorded 0.44 inches of precipitation (1.80 inches below normal), and Borger recorded 1.08 inches of precipitation (1.81 inches below normal). This May was the 32nd warmest and 5th driest May on records for the Texas High Plains Region. ||The scattered precipitation during the month of May has helped improve some of the dormant fuels across the Panhandle. The Keetch-Byram Drought Index showed marginal improvement from April. The northwestern potion of the Texas Panhandle falls within the 600 to 800 range while the majority of the area stayed within the 400 to 600 range. The 200 to 400 range now encompasses Roberts County, Hutchinson County, and Gray County. Countywide burn bans remain in effect for all of the Texas Panhandle except for Hansford, Roberts, Hemphill, Oldham, Gray, Donley, Collingsworth and Deaf Smith Counties. ||The sparse precipitation for the month and several freezes severely impacted developing crops. Irrigated crops remain in fair conditions however; it is not the peak water demand period for these crops. Rangeland and pastures across the Texas Panhandle have remained in poor to very poor condition as observed by the Texas Crop and Weather Report. The Palmer Drought

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Wisconsin, Jun 21, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Flood, from June 21, 2013 to June 21, 2013. Affected areas: Crawford, Grant, La Crosse, Vernon. Episode summary: Thunderstorms that developed over northwest Minnesota during the evening of June 20th, moved across western Wisconsin during the early morning hours of the 21st. These storms produced large hail and winds strong enough to cause damage. Trees were blown down in the city of La Crosse (La Crosse County) and a pontoon boat was flipped by the high winds on Lake Onalaska (La Crosse County). Most of the hail that fell was penny to nickel sized. Locally heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in the city of La Crosse and a minor mud slide south of Genoa (Vernon County) that covered part of State Highway 35. Details: Locally heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in several locations across the city of La Crosse. Roads in Prairie du Chien were closed as runoff from locally heavy rains produced flooding. Locally heavy rain produced street flooding in Chaseburg, Westby and Viroqua. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 23, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 23, 2013 to May 24, 2013. Affected areas: Fisher, Kimble, Menard, Tom Green. Episode summary: A complex of thunderstorms produced very heavy rain and reports of flash flooding across the Concho Valley and Northwest Hill Country during the late night of May 23 and into the early morning of May 24. Also, the Lower Colorado River Authority gauges reported around 5 inches of rain in Concho, Menard and Kimble Counties. Details: Roads were flooded in Rotan with a depth of 1 to 2 feet of water. Southwest Boulevard was flooded near Loop 306. The flood gauge showed a depth of 1.5 feet. A high water rescue occurred at South Taylor Street and Concho Street.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2013 to May 31, 2013. Affected areas: Aransas, Bee, Calhoun, Duval, Goliad, Jim Wells, Kleberg, La Salle, Live Oak, Mcmullen, Nueces, Refugio and 3 more areas. Episode summary: Temperatures were near or slightly below normal again for the month of May. Several beneficial rain events occurred across portions of South Texas during the month of May. Significant rainfall was received in the Victoria Crossroads, inland portions of the Coastal Bend, and most of the Brush Country. Only the northern Coastal Bend and Mid-Coast regions did not receive much rainfall. Several areas received rainfall amounts over 6 inches during the month from the Victoria Crossroads to the northern Brush Country as well as over inland sections for the southern Coastal Bend westward into the southern Brush Country. The highest amounts above 10 inches occurred over northern portions of Live Oak, Goliad, and Bee Counties.||Exceptional drought continued over portions of the southern Coastal Bend. The size of the severe to extreme drought area was reduced but still remained over portions of the Brush Country eastward into the northern Coastal Bend with severe drought developing over Aransas County by the end of the month.||Mandatory water restrictions continued during the month for the city of Corpus Christi as the combined lake capacity levels remained below 40 percent. The city of Portland continued under mandatory water restrictions. The cities of Victoria and Laredo remained under voluntary water restrictions. Different stages of water restrictions continued for Beeville, Point Comfort, Alice, Kingsville, Taft, and Odem during the month. Details: Extreme drought continued over the southern portion of the county. Exceptional drought continued over the western portion of the county. Extreme drought continued over the northeastern portion of the county.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2013 to May 31, 2013. Affected areas: Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason and 12 more areas. Episode summary: The drought continues to impact much of West Central Texas. The U.S. Drought Monitor rated Haskell, Throckmorton, Fisher, Jones and and Shackelford Counties in the exceptional category, while the Drought Monitor placed Coke, Nolan and Schleicher Counties in the extreme drought category. The rest of the region was placed in the severe drought category.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2013 to May 31, 2013. Affected areas: Bandera, Bastrop, De Witt, Dimmit, Edwards, Frio, Gillespie, Kerr, Kinney, Lee, Llano, Maverick and 6 more areas. Episode summary: May brought some much needed rain to South Central Texas. Much of the area received above normal rainfall and 14 counties moved to better than severe (Stage D2) drought. In addition, Bandera, Kerr, Medina, Real, Uvalde, and Williamson Counties improved a category to stage D2. All the other counties stayed the same with Kinney, Maverick, and Val Verde in exceptional (Stage D4) drought category, Dimmit, Edwards, and Zavala in extreme (Stage D3), and Bastrop, De Witt, Frio, Gillespie, Lee, and Llano in severe (Stage D2) category. Fire danger at the end of the month was low to moderate. Of the counties in D2 or worse drought seven had outdoor burn bans in effect at the end of the month. These were Dimmit, Edwards, Frio, Kinney, Maverick, Medina, and Val Verde. The seven day stream flow averages were much below normal (less than 10 percent) across the Colorado River basin. The Guadalupe, Nueces, Rio Grande, and Frio River basins were reporting below normal (10 to 24 percent) flow. Area lakes and reservoirs continued below normal pool elevations. Lake Amistad was around 61 feet below normal at 1056.3 feet which is a new record low for the lake. Lake Travis was 52 feet below normal and Medina Lake near 82 feet below normal which left it at 5.5 percent of capacity. The Edwards Aquifer saw some improvement from the rain in May, but was still 8 feet below normal, and 4.2 feet below the level at the end of May 2012. Uvalde was in stage 5 water restrictions and Kerrville was in stage 1. Details: May

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jul 22, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from July 22, 2013 to July 22, 2013. Affected areas: Trempealeau. Episode summary: A cold front triggered a broken line of severe thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours of July 22nd. A small tornado touched down in the Mississippi River and moved onshore into the Trempealeau National Wildlife Refuge (Trempealeau County) before dissipating. The only damage from the tornado was to hundreds of trees in the refuge. Otherwise, the storms produced a few more funnel clouds and some large hail. The largest hail reported was golf ball sized in Centerville (Trempealeau County). Details: The tornado began as a waterspout in the marsh waters just off the main channel of the Mississippi River southeast of Winona, Minnesota, but on the Wisconsin side. White spray could be seen for some distance as the waterspout pulled up water into the funnel. The tornado then moved onshore in the Trempealeau Wildlife Refuge and knocked down numerous trees for nearly a half mile. Water plants wer Reported property and crop damage: about $22,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, May 11, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from May 11, 2013 to May 11, 2013. Affected areas: Cameron, Willacy. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance acted on unstable air across the Lower Rio Grande Valley, and resulted in redevelopment of a cluster of thunderstorms which earlier had dropped more than 1.5 inches of rain across the Rio Grande Plains. Between approximately 4 and 6 AM on May 11th, nearly 2.5 inches of rain fell near Raymondville, and nearly 3 inches fell on the west side of Harlingen. Details: Between 2.3 and 2.77 inches of rain fell in less than two hours on the west side of Harlingen, leaving ponded water in streets and fields and some nuisance urban flooding behind. The event, which occurred very early on a Saturday morning, had little impact with few people out. Around 2.5 inches of rain fell in less than two hours just southwest of Raymondville, leaving ponded water in streets and fields and some nuisance urban flooding behind. The event, which occurred very early on a Saturday morning, had little impact with few people out.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jun 21, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from June 21, 2013 to June 22, 2013. Affected areas: Crawford, Grant, Richland. Episode summary: A nearly stationary band of thunderstorms developed across southwest Wisconsin during the evening of June 21st. These storms remained in place until another line of storms pushed in from the west during the early morning hours of the 22nd. Rainfall amounts exceeded six inches with flash flooding reported in parts of Crawford, Grant and Richland Counties. The area in and around Boscobel (Grant County) was hit extremely hard by the flooding. 650 homes were impacted by the flooding with two dozen families displaced, most homes had basements full of water with some having the water reach the first level. Roads in the region had numerous washouts and some bridges were blown out. Rescue crews had to save 54 canoeists who became stranded on the Wisconsin River due to rising waters. Details: Locally heavy rain produced flash flooding across mainly the far southwest part of Richland County. Knapp Creek and numerous other small streams were out of their banks with County Road F flooded south of Excelsior. South of Muscoda, 5.4 inches of rain was reported. In Mt. Zion, 3 inches of rain was reported. Reported property and crop damage: about $11,400,000.

title: Flood, Heavy Rain, Strong Wind, Tornado: California, May 04, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, Heavy Rain, Strong Wind, Tornado, from May 04, 2013 to May 09, 2013. Affected areas: Kern, Mariposa, Sw S.J. Valley. Episode summary: May began warm and dry. Humidities were in the teens across the mountains of Kern and Tulare Counties on May 1st through the 3rd, and as highs in the southern San Joaquin Valley climbed into the mid 90s on the 2nd, relative humidities in the south end of the Valley fell to 10 percent or lower for several hours.||An upper-level low approached central California on May 4th. The southerly flow ahead of the low funneled through the passes and canyons of the Temblors, Diablo Range and the Tehachapi Mountains. This created gusty winds along the west side of the San Joaquin Valley that persisted from the afternoon of the 4th through the evening of 5th. Winds gusted to 51 mph at Sunflower Valley, and to 50 mph at Panoche Road. A gust to 59 mph was measured at the California Highway Patrol Weigh Station at the base of the Grapevine during the late afternoon of May 5th.|Winds also gusted to 45 mph at Meadows Field, Bakersfield during this time. The gust at Meadows Field tied the highest gust on record at Bakersfield for May, last occurring on May 23rd, 1990.||The upper-level low moved to off Monterey Bay on the evening of May 5th. In addition to the gusty winds generated by the cyclonic circulation, the low also spun subtropical moisture into central California, and as a series of upper-level disturbances rotated around the low, they triggered showers and thunderstorms across the region on the 6th. One of the thunderstorms spawned a tornado that touched down at 7:10 PM on May 6th in the dry riverbed of the Kern River near the

One thunderstorm generated an outflow wind that was measured at 40 mph at the Edwards AFB North Base Auxiliary Field. Winds also gusted to 55 mph in the Indian Wells Valley. title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jun 21, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, from June 21, 2013 to June 29, 2013. Affected areas: Crawford, Richland, Trempealeau, Vernon. Episode summary: For the second night in a row, thunderstorms with very heavy rain rolled across southwest Wisconsin producing widespread flash flooding during the evening of June 22nd. At least three rounds of thunderstorms moved across the area dumping another 3 to 4 inches of rain on ground that was saturated from heavy rains that fell less than 24 hours before. Numerous mud slides occurred in Richland and Crawford Counties causing state and county highways to be closed. The Governor of Wisconsin declared a state of emergency following the flooding in Crawford, Grant and Richland Counties. FEMA declared a federal disaster area for the following counties: Crawford, Grant, Richland and Vernon. Details: The COOP observer at the Genoa Lock and Dam reported 3.2 inches of rain. The COOP observer in Soldiers Grove reported 3.93 inches of rain. The COOP observer near De Soto reported 3.62 inches of rain. Reported property and crop damage: about $791,000.

title: Excessive Heat: California, Jun 28, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Excessive Heat, from June 28, 2013 to June 30, 2013. Affected areas: Death Valley National Park. Episode summary: A large area of high pressure brought record-breaking temperatures to much of the Desert Southwest. Several people died from the heat, many more were injured, and some infrastructure was damaged. Details: Excessive Heat Warning criteria were reached each day from June 28th through 30th, and continued into July. Two people were overcome by heat in Death Valley on the 28th.

title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, Jun 24, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from June 24, 2013 to June 25, 2013. Affected areas: Crawford, Grant. Episode summary: More thunderstorms with heavy rain moved across southwest Wisconsin during the evening of June 24th into the early morning hours of June 25th. The heavy rain produced yet more flash flooding that led to the evacuation of a trailer home near Bagley (Grant County). Many roads became covered with water in Crawford and Grant Counties. Details: Heavy rain produced rapidly rising water in the Bagley area that forced the evacuation of one trailer home and caused water to go over County Highway X. Water also covered State Highway 35 in Patch Grove. Heavy rain produced street flooding in Prairie du Chien that caused some vehicles to become stalled. The automated weather observing equipment at the Prairie du Chien airport measured 1.71 inches of rain in less than two hours. A mudslide in the southern part of the county closed U.S. Highway 61 between State Highway 60 and Boscobel in Grant County. The slide was estimated to be 200 yards long.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jun 15, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from June 15, 2013 to June 15, 2013. Affected areas: Portage, Winnebago. Episode summary: Thunderstorms moved into western Wisconsin during the afternoon and increased in intensity and coverage across central and northern Wisconsin as they encountered a more unstable air mass. The storms produced heavy rainfall and hail to nickel size as they moved eastward across the state. Street flooding occurred in Neenah (Winnebago Co.), Clintonville (Waupaca Co.), and Stevens Point (Portage Co.) as a result of the heavy rain. Details: Thunderstorms produced 2.72 inches of rain in Plover in less than 90 minutes, including 0.62 inch in the first 10 minutes. Thunderstorms produced 1.5 to 2 inches of rain in Neenah over a two-hour period, resulting in some street flooding.

title: Drought: Texas, Aug 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from August 01, 2013 to August 31, 2013. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Drought conditions generally improved one level through the month of August. This was due to widespread rainfall around the middle of the month which brought several inches of rainfall. Bailey, Hall, and Parmer Counties dropped down to moderate (D1) drought levels. Only a small strip of exceptional (D4) drought remained mostly across Floyd County.||Much of the month of August saw fairly consistent temperatures with the end result being slightly above seasonal average. The first and last part of the month were generally warmer than normal with a reprieve in temperatures coming during the middle of the month. This was mostly due to repeated widespread rainfall events. Much of the region observed between one to three inches of rainfall during this period with much of it falling from the 14th through the 16th. Despite the rainfall, Keetch-Byram Drought Index values increased from the beginning to the end of the month. Most areas saw values between 500 and 600 with values between 300 and 500 across the southwestern Texas Panhandle.||Rainfall during the middle of the month greatly improved crops, rangelands and pastures. Although, area lakes, ponds, and stock tanks remained low due to long term drought conditions. Warmer and drier conditions toward the end of the month began to increase crop stress. Fire weather activity remained low as it typically does in late summer with relatively little cured fuel.||Economic losses due to drought through August since the drought began were estimated near $2.8 billion. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Aug 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from August 01, 2013 to August 01, 2013. Affected areas: Lubbock. Episode summary: On the afternoon of the first, scattered thunderstorms developed across the South Plains. The most concentrated area of storms was located over Lubbock County. Several outflow boundaries from convection collided near Lubbock Preston Smith International Airport which created two brief landspout tornadoes in close proximity to each other. Details: The first of two brief landspout tornadoes occurred near Lubbock Preston Smith International Airport. The tornado began around 1542 CDT and lasted until 1547 CDT. No damage was reported. The second of two brief landspout tornadoes occurred near Lubbock Preston Smith International Airport began around 1546 CDT and lasted until 1553 CDT. No damage was reported.

title: Drought: Texas, Jul 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 01, 2013 to July 31, 2013. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Drought conditions across the region slightly lessened through the month of July with an unusual weather pattern emerging toward the end of the month. Almost all areas remained within severe (D3) to exceptional (D4) drought. However, an extremely small pocket of moderate (D1) drought was observed over the northern Rolling Plains.||Much of the month of July saw typical hot and dry conditions with an upper level high pressure system controlling the southwestern United States. This upper level ridge brought hot temperatures and little rainfall. However, in the second half of the month, an unusual upper level low pressure system moved from east to west. This system brought cooler than seasonal average temperatures and much needed rainfall, and in some areas, excessive rainfall. In fact, Lubbock observed a record minimum high temperature for three consecutive days as well as daily rainfall records. Many areas received one to three inches of rainfall with some pockets observing four to six inches. Some selected sites recorded four day totals of 6.41 inches at Plainview (Hale County), 5.26 inches at Amherst (Lamb County), 5.09 inches at Denver City (Yoakum County), 4.55 inches at Sundown (Hockley County), and 3.13 inches at Lubbock Preston Smith International Airport (Lubbock County). Due to these excessively cool July temperatures, the mean temperature at the end of the month was below average by 1.1 degrees at Lubbock and 1.5 degrees at Childress. Keetch-Byram Drought Index values improved through the month because of the abundant rainfall. Values between 200 and 400 were observed over the southern Rolling Plains and southwest Texas Panhandle. Elsewhere across the South Plains

text: Lubbock and 1.5 degrees at Childress. Keetch-Byram Drought Index values improved through the month because of the abundant rainfall. Values between 200 and 400 were observed over the southern Rolling Plains and southwest Texas Panhandle. Abnormally high dew point temperatures served to further reduce fire weather potential. Rainfall also produced modest greening across much of the region. The beginning of the month saw crops becoming stressed due to excessively hot temperatures. However, the copious rainfall allowed crops to progress during the second half of the month. title: Drought: Texas, Jun 18, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 18, 2013 to June 30, 2013. Affected areas: Ellis, Milam, Robertson. Episode summary: A few of the south-central locations beginning the month of June in Moderate/D1 drought were downgraded to Severe/D2 drought around the middle of the month, due to below-normal June rainfall. Details: Moderate/D1 drought during the first half of June deteriorated to Severe/D2 conditions around the middle of the month over the western third of Ellis County. These conditions spread east across the rest of the county by June 25 and remained in place county-wide through the end of the month. Moderate/D1 drought in place during the first half of June deteriorated to Severe/D2 conditions by June 18. Conditions continued to deteriorate, becoming Extreme/D3 by June 25 across the western half of the county. These conditions persisted, along with moderate/D2 conditions over the eastern half of the county, through the end of the month. Moderate/D1 drought conditions in place across Robertson County during the first half of June deteriorated to Severe/D2 by the 18th of the month, due to continued below-normal precipitation. Conditions worsened to D3/Extreme drought over far northern portions of the county by June 25th. These conditions, along with Severe/D2 conditions across the rest of the county, remained in place through the e Reported property and crop damage: about $9,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 01, 2013 to June 30, 2013. Affected areas: Anderson, Bell, Bosque, Comanche, Coryell, Eastland, Erath, Falls, Freestone, Hamilton, Hill, Hood and 13 more areas. Episode summary: Drought conditions continued across a good portion of north Texas during June of 2013, particularly over the western-most counties where the least amount of rain occurred. Details: Exceptional/D4 drought severity plagued most of Young County at the beginning of June 2013. By June 18, conditions were upgraded to Extreme/D3 over all but the extreme western portions of the county. These conditions remained in place through the end of the month. After spending the first week and a half in Moderate/D1 drought, conditions were downgraded to Severe/D2 county-wide by June 11. Severe/D2 drought conditions remained in place through the end of the month. Jack County spent most of June with Extreme/D3 drought over the western half of the county and Severe/D2 over the eastern half. Some improvement occurred during the second half of the month as conditions were upgraded to moderate over the far eastern reaches of the county, but overall Jack County was one of the drier north Texas counties. Reported property and crop damage: about $88,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 25, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 25, 2013 to June 30, 2013. Affected areas: Dallas, Navarro. Episode summary: Dallas and Navarro Counties experienced moderate drought up until the last week of the month, when Severe drought conditions crept into portions of these two counties. Details: Dallas County experienced Moderate/D1 drought severity up until June 25th, when Severe/D2 conditions crept into the southwestern corner of the county. Navarro County began June of 2013 with Moderate/D1 drought conditions in place county-wide. Due to below-normal rain during the month, conditions were downgraded to Severe/D2 across most of the county on June 25. These conditions continued through the end of the month. Reported property and crop damage: about $4,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jun 02, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from June 02, 2013 to June 02, 2013. Affected areas: Trinity. Episode summary: Clusters of thunderstorms passing across Trinity County created minor flooding issues. Details: Heavy rain caused water to run over FM 1280.

title: High Wind: Wisconsin, Jun 21, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: High Wind, from June 21, 2013 to June 21, 2013. Affected areas: Oneida. Episode summary: The remnants of a thunderstorm complex moved into central Wisconsin during the morning hours causing isolated wind damage, heavy rainfall and a funnel cloud.||A wake low developed behind the departing area of showers. High wind gusts from the wake low, estimated at 60 mph, downed trees and power lines in Oneida County near Sugar Camp. title: Heavy Rain: Texas, May 28, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from May 28, 2013 to May 28, 2013. Affected areas: Deaf Smith. Episode summary: During the late evening of the 28th, a dryline retreated westward across Deaf Smith County as the nocturnal low level jet transported moisture from the Gulf of Mexico northwestward. A near stationary discrete supercell formed along this retreating dryline and produced copious amounts of large hail and brief periods of heavy rain. The large hail clogged drainage systems which caused localized flooding in Deaf Smith County. Flooded areas were contained to low lying areas and did not affect roadways. The flood waters quickly receded once the supercell moved northeast out of the area and the drainage systems became unclogged. No injuries, high water rescues, or fatalities were associated with this localized flooding. Details: The Emergency Manager for Deaf Smith County reported that hail up to the size of tennis balls (2.00 inches) was covering the ground and roadways. The hail clogged drainage systems which caused fields along the road to become flooded. The flood waters did not impact the roads and quickly receded once the drainage systems unclogged.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from June 07, 2013 to June 07, 2013. Affected areas: Hansford, Hutchinson, Potter, Randall, Roberts. Episode summary: The Texas Panhandle was firmly locked in northwest flow aloft on the 7th. This type of weather pattern favors the development of precipitation across the Panhandle as it allows weak shortwave troughs to dive southeastward from the Continental Divide into the Southern Plains. The large scale lift provided by one such shortwave during the afternoon hours of the 7th worked in tandem with weak steering flow during the afternoon and increasing PWAT values during the evening hours to produce localized heavy rain across the Texas Panhandle. Scattered, near stationary, discrete thunderstorms developed over the northern Texas Panhandle due to weak steering flow during the afternoon hours of the 7th. These storms were able to generate moderate rain amounts due to being over the same location for an extended period of time. As the hours progressed into the evening, low level winds transported gulf moisture into the southern Texas Panhandle which fueled, in the form of increased PWAT values, a line of thunderstorms moving south-southeastward across the western half of the Panhandle. While these storms moved quickly across the area, the ample supply of moisture allowed these thunderstorms to efficiently produce heavy rain. All precipitation ended across the Texas Panhandle by 10 PM due to the upper level support for these storms moving into central Texas. Details: Merging thunderstorms moved over the town of Spearman (Hansford County) during the afternoon hours of the 7th. The heavy rain produced from these storms caused minor street flooding across the town. No reports of swift water rescues or stranded vehicles were reported in association with this flooding. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the New Mexico Eastern Plains during the evening hours of the 17th. These thunderstorms moved eastward and entered the western Texas Panhandle around the 7 PM CST hour. The thunderstorms over the southwestern Texas Panhandle began merging and moving to the southeast. The storm mergers caused brief intensifications before diminishing. As these thunderstorms diminished, localized heavy rain was reported in Deaf Smith County. The heavy rain caused brief minor flooding which receded quickly once thunderstorms moved out of the area. Details: Diminishing thunderstorms over Deaf Smith County produced locally heavy rain during the evening hours of the 17th. A member of the public 2 miles west of Bootleg (Deaf Smith County) reported 4 inches of rain and minor flooding of roads. title: Tornado: Texas, Aug 14, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from August 14, 2013 to August 14, 2013. Affected areas: Hale. Episode summary: Isolated storms moved south out of the Texas Panhandle, with an isolated supercell developing downstream across Hale County. This storm produced severe wind gusts and hail, along with a brief tornado west of Interstate 27 which damaged several center pivot irrigation systems. The storms also produced severe winds near Ropesville into the early morning hours. Details: A fire department official reported a brief tornado touchdown west of Interstate 27 and north of Farm to Market Road 54 northwest of Abernathy. Several center pivot irrigation systems were damaged before the tornado lifted. Reported property and crop damage: about $250,000.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Jun 22, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from June 22, 2013 to June 30, 2013. Affected areas: Green, Kenosha, Lafayette, Rock. Episode summary: During the period of June 20th to June 28th, portions of southern Wisconsin experienced repeated rounds of thunderstorms, with rainfall of 1 inch to as much as 6 inches per round. The run-off from these heavy rain events caused area rivers and streams to flood. Flooding levels ranged from minor to moderate, with the Yahara River at Fulton in far northern Rock County going into major flood for a time. River stages climbed to between 2 feet to nearly 5 feet over flood stage. WHile most of the rivers fell back below flood stage by the end of the month, some rivers remained in flood into July. Details: The river gauge on the Pecatonica River near Martintown remained above flood stage from the morning of June 25th into early July. The river experienced minor flooding, cresting at 15.56 feet at 10:15 AM CDT on June 28th, which is 2.06 feet above flood stage. The river gauge on Turtle Creek near Clinton remained above flood stage from the morning of June 25th to the late afternoon of June 27th. The creek experienced moderate flooding, cresting at 11.76 feet at 4:15 PM CDT on June 26th, which is 3.76 feet above flood stage. The river gauge on the Sugar River in Brodhead remained above flood stage from the afternoon of June 24th into early July. The creek experienced moderate flooding, cresting at 8.86 feet at 2:00 AM CDT on June 28th, which is 3.86 feet above flood stage. Reported property and crop damage: about $72,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Jul 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 01, 2013 to July 30, 2013. Affected areas: Salt Basin, Southern Hudspeth Highlands. Episode summary: Another wet month helped all of Far West Texas get out of any kind of significant drought conditions. Details: The eastern half of the zone started out in Severe(D2) drought but by the end of the month the entire zone was in Abnormally Dry(D0) drought conditions. The Dell City Cooperative Observer reported 2.91 inches of rain which was 1.35 inches above normal. The far eastern areas of the zone started out in Severe(D2) drought but by the end of the month had transitioned to Abnormally Dry(D0) drought conditions.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jul 08, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from July 08, 2013 to July 08, 2013. Affected areas: Calumet, Outagamie. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed in a very moist and unstable air mass ahead of an approaching cold front and low pressure system. The storms produced wind damage from a wet microburst, penny to nickel size hail, and heavy rainfall. The microburst downed about 30 trees and dropped penny size hail in Forest County, between Crandon and Wabeno. Numerous locations received more than 2 inches of rain in a 3 to 4 hour period, and the roof of a building in Appleton (Outagamie Co.) collapsed from the weight of the rain. Details: Heavy rain during the early morning hours of July 8th resulted in minor street flooding in the southwest part of Forest Junction. Heavy rain fell in Appleton during the early morning of June 8th, mainly between 0315CST and 0700CST. The 24-hour rainfall total ending at 0600CST was 2.35 inches. The weight of the rainwater caused the roof of a building to collapse around 0900CST. The collapse caused a gas leak, and the Appleton building inspector declared 3 buildings uninhabitable while contractors examined the damage. Reported property and crop damage: about $98,500.

title: Drought: Texas, Sep 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from September 01, 2013 to September 30, 2013. Affected areas: Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hockley, Kent and 10 more areas. Episode summary: Drought levels generally improved one drought category level through the month of September. Several non-severe thunderstorm events contributed to rainfall across a wide portion of the most severe drought areas. Parmer County returned to severe (D2) drought while Bailey and Hall Counties remained in moderate (D1) drought conditions.||September saw a mix of localized heavy rainfall rainfall events along with very warm temperatures. An upper level ridge remained in control of the weather pattern for much of the month leading to temperatures 3.4 degrees and 3.1 degrees above normal at Lubbock and Childress, respectively. By the end of the month, the ridge was beginning to loosen its grip on the West Texas region allowing for several localized heavy rainfall events. The area that saw the most precipitation was the southeastern Texas Panhandle. On the 13th of September, Caprock Canyons State Park measured 3.88 inches. Keetch-Byram Drought Index values generally remained the same or worsened throughout the month. Levels were as high as 600-700 over the southwestern South Plains with readings as low as 200-300 over the southeastern Texas Panhandle.||Rain through the summer was enough to make area grasses grow and irrigated crops fill many fields. White River Lake was at an all time low, reporting zero percent of conservation capacity. Fuel moisture values remained near normal across the area. Some drying of fuels was beginning to occur on the South Plains. The warm conditions contributed to crop maturation after beneficial rains in August.||Economic losses due to drought through September since the drought began were estimated near $2.8 billion.

title: Wildfire: California, Aug 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from August 01, 2013 to August 31, 2013. Affected areas: Western Siskiyou County. Episode summary: This fire was human caused. It started around 10:30 PM on 07/31/2013. Details: The Butler wildfire burned all month. Initially it was part of the Orleans Complex. At the beginning of September, it was combined with the Forks Fire, becoming part of the Forks Complex. At that time, the fire covered 21230 acres. It was 45% contained and 27.2 million dollars had been expended on firefighting efforts.

title: Wildfire: California, Sep 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from September 01, 2013 to September 23, 2013. Affected areas: Western Siskiyou County. Episode summary: This fire was human caused. It started around 10:30 PM on 07/31/2013. At the beginning of September, the Forks fire (formerly part of the Salmon Complex) was grouped with the Butler Fire (formerly part of the Orleans Complex). The new grouping was named the Forks Complex. Details: The last report on the Forks Complex stated that it was 37246 acres in size and was 90% contained. The estimated containment date was 10/1/13, and 59.8 million dollars was expended in fire fighting efforts.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Sep 02, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from September 02, 2013 to September 02, 2013. Affected areas: Gregg. Episode summary: A disturbance aloft moved south towards the Interstate 20 corridor of Northeast Texas during the predawn hours and morning hours of September 2nd. These storms were prolific rainfall producers with hourly rainfall rates approaching three inches per hour. Some of these storms began to train across Gregg County Texas producing isolated reports of flash flooding in the town of Longview, Texas. Details: Excessive heavy rainfall resulted in two cars being stranded at the intersection of High Street and Common Street. The intersection of Nelson and Green Streets was also closed due to high water. Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Aug 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from August 01, 2013 to August 31, 2013. Affected areas: Archer, Baylor, Clay, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: With precipitation amounts near to slightly above average for August, the ongoing severe drought eased slightly over western north Texas. Details: D3 (extreme) drought was present at the beginning of the month, but had improved slightly to D2 (severe) drought by the end of the month. D4 (exceptional) drought was present at the beginning of the month, but had improved slightly to D3 (extreme) drought by the end of the month. D1 (moderate) drought continued with persistent dry conditions.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 21, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 21, 2013 to July 22, 2013. Affected areas: Inyo, San Bernardino. Episode summary: A large push of monsoon moisture triggered an extended period of thunderstorms across the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Many storms produced flash flooding and severe weather. Details: A mud and debris flow trapped vehicles near the intersection of Highway 395 and Haiwee Canyon Road. One vehicle was carried a mile and a half by the flow. Deep water flowing on Highway 247 south of Barstow caused two cars to get stuck. Highway 190 was closed at the intersection of Panamint Valley Road due to flash flooding and debris. Debris was also reported on 190 at Townes Pass. Reported property and crop damage: about $95,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 23, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 23, 2013 to July 23, 2013. Affected areas: Inyo. Episode summary: Remnant monsoon moisture continued to fuel scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin, with isolated flash flooding. Details: Highway 168 was closed from Highway 395 across the White Mountains due to flash flooding depositing boulders on the road. Mud washed over Highway 395 at Haiwee Road, closing the highway. Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

title: Dust Storm, Flash Flood: California, Jul 28, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, Flash Flood, from July 28, 2013 to July 28, 2013. Affected areas: Eastern Mojave Desert, Inyo, San Bernardino. Episode summary: Mid level dry air pushed in above low level monsoon moisture, triggering widespread thunderstorms with flash flooding and severe weather. Details: Mud and rocks washed across Highway 95. Mud and rocks washed onto Highway 395. Mud, rocks and sand washed over Kelso Cima Road at several low water crossings. Reported property and crop damage: about $114,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 17, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from July 17, 2013 to July 17, 2013. Affected areas: Ector. Episode summary: An upper low was over eastern New Mexico with upper level disturbances which rotated around the low and provided lift. In addition to the lift, abundant moisture was across the area. This resulted in flash flooding across Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. Details: Heavy rain was reported in Odessa with water up to the curb at the intersection of Laredo and Dixie.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jul 15, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from July 15, 2013 to July 15, 2013. Affected areas: Waukesha. Episode summary: Slow-moving thunderstorms developed over northwest Waukesha County and then repeatedly tracked from southwest to northeast across the City of Oconomowoc during the late afternoon hours of July 15th. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain fell in a 2-hour period, closing several roads due to standing water and clogged storm drains in a construction zone. Several parked vehicles were damaged by the rising water in the flooded streets. Reported property and crop damage: about $34,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 22, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 22, 2013 to July 22, 2013. Affected areas: Los Angeles, Ventura. Episode summary: A push of monsoonal moisture from northern Mexico brought thunderstorms to the mountains and deserts of Ventura and Los Angeles counties. Some of the thunderstorms producing heavy rain and flash flooding. Details: Strong thunderstorms produced heavy rain and flash flooding in the mountains of Ventura county. The California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding along the intersection of Highway 33 and Apache Canyon Road. Strong thunderstorms produced heavy rain and flash flooding across the Antelope Valley between the communities of Llano and Pearblossom. California Highway Patrol reported numerous vehicles stuck in flood waters at the intersection of Highway 138 and 165th Street East. Also Avenue T between Pearblossom and Llano was closed due to flooding.

title: Flash Flood: California, Aug 26, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from August 26, 2013 to August 26, 2013. Affected areas: Los Angeles. Episode summary: A surge of monsoonal moisture brought another round of strong thunderstorms and flash flooding to the Antelope Valley. Heavy rain and flash flooding was reported across Leona Valley and near Quartz Hill High School. Details: Trained spotters reported widespread flash flooding across the communities of Quartz Hill and Leona Valley. The area around 60th Street and Quartz Hill High School experienced flash flooding as well as the area around 90th Street West and Elizabeth Lake Road in Leona Valley.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 31, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from July 31, 2013 to July 31, 2013. Affected areas: Moore. Episode summary: The Texas Panhandle was firmly locked in northwest flow aloft during the evening hours of the 31st. A weak shortwave trough used this northwest flow to move out of the Continental Divide and towards the Southern Plains. The large scale lift provided by this shortwave allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop across the Central Plains and Eastern Plains of New Mexico. These thunderstorms would move to the south-southeast and pass through the Southern Plains. Slow storm motions and higher values of precipitable water lead to periods of heavy rain while traversing the Texas Panhandle. Thunderstorms both diminished and moved south of the Southern Plains by midnight of August 1st. Details: Scattered discrete thunderstorms slowly moved across Moore County during the late night hours of the 31st. These slow moving storms allowed heavy rain to accumulate across the city of Dumas (Moore County) that lead to minor flooding. A trained storm spotter in Dumas (Moore County) reported about a foot of water in their backyard and reported that near 4 inches of rain fell in 2 hours. text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 03, 2013 to July 03, 2013. Affected areas: Mono. Episode summary: Hot temperatures and plenty of moisture combined to bring strong thunderstorms with hail and heavy rain on the 2nd and 3rd. A slow-moving thunderstorm with very heavy rain was responsible for a large debris flow onto Interstate 80 which closed the freeway on the 2nd. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from September 08, 2013 to September 09, 2013. Affected areas: Smith. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from September 09, 2013 to September 09, 2013. Affected areas: Panola. Episode summary: Severe drought conditions, triple digit temperatures and strong southeast winds resulted in a fire that quickly burned out of control during the late afternoon hours of September 9th. title: Drought: Texas, Aug 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from August 01, 2013 to August 31, 2013. Affected areas: Brooks, Cameron, Coastal Cameron, Coastal Willacy, Hidalgo, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Starr, Willacy, Zapata. Episode summary: The first week of August picked up where the last week of July left off for the Rio Grande Valley and Deep South Texas. With high pressure ridging across the southern Plains and northern Mexico, La Canicula was in full swing. This pattern suppressed precipitation and allowed for abundant sunshine and above average hot temperatures, with daytime temperatures 3 to 5 degrees above normal for the period. Details: Hot, dry, and breezy conditions ensured that Jim Hogg saw no improvements in drought conditions during the first week of August. The eastern two thirds of the county in remained in Extreme (D3) drought conditions, while the western third of the county remained in Severe (D2) drought conditions. Hot, dry, and breezy conditions ensured that Zapata County saw no improvements in drought conditions during the first week of August. The eastern half of the county remained in Severe (D2) drought conditions, while the western half of the county remained in Moderate (D1) drought conditions. Hot, dry, and breezy conditions ensured that Starr saw no improvements in drought conditions during the first week of August. Starr County remained split with the far southeastern corner of the county in Exceptional (D4) drought conditions, the western third of the county in Severe (D2) drought conditions, and the remainder of the county in Extreme (D3) drought conditions.

title: Drought: Texas, Jul 23, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 23, 2013 to July 31, 2013. Affected areas: Cameron, Coastal Cameron, Coastal Willacy, Kenedy, Zapata. Episode summary: The coastal counties and Zapata County saw a brief respite and temporary improvement in drought conditions, as the effects from rains during the middle the month, courtesy of a southwest moving upper level disturbance that originated in the Ohio Valley and ended up in northwest Mexico. The disturbance ultimately brought a several day period of locally unsettled weather mainly between the 16th and 20th, began to be felt. Where rainfall was much more sparse, drought conditions continued to hold steady or worsen. The high pressure ridge aloft quickly returned and brought back summer time heat and dry conditions across the area the last week of the month. Details: Drought conditions improved across all of Coastal Cameron County, as the effects from rain earlier in the month began to be felt. The entire area improved from Exceptional (D4) drought conditions to Extreme (D3) drought. Drought conditions improved across all of Coastal Willacy County, as the effects from rain earlier in the month began to be felt. The entire area improved from Exceptional (D4) drought conditions to Extreme (D3) drought. Thanks to rain earlier in the month, drought conditions improved across Cameron County, with the Exceptional (D4) drought conditions over the eastern half of the county, being replaced by Extreme (D3) drought conditions, resulting in the entire county experiencing Extreme (D3) drought.

title: Dust Storm: California, Aug 22, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, from August 22, 2013 to August 22, 2013. Affected areas: Imperial County Except The Lower Colorado River Valley. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed across portions of far southwest Arizona and southeast California during the afternoon hours on August 22nd, and they produced strong and gusty outflow winds in excess of 40 mph. The winds were sufficient to generate dense blowing sand and dust, lowering visibilities to below one quarter mile across portions of Imperial county. As a result, dust storm conditions developed which led to the issuance of both Blowing Dust Advisories and Dust Storm Warnings for portions of Imperial county. No accidents or injuries were reported as a result of the dense blowing sand and dust. Details: Thunderstorms developed across portions of far southwest Arizona and southeast California during the afternoon hours on August 22nd, and they generated strong gusty outflow winds in excess of 50 mph. The gusty winds produced dense blowing sand and dust across portions of Imperial county, affecting communities such as Imperial and Holtville, as well as motorists on area roads such as Interstate 8.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 24, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from July 24, 2013 to July 25, 2013. Affected areas: Armstrong, Deaf Smith, Donley, Gray, Randall. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed along both storm outflows moving across the southwestern Texas Panhandle from New Mexico and a modifying surface front across Northwestern Texas. The weak steering winds caused these storms to slowly move eastward along these boundaries over the same area from the evening hours of the 24th and into the morning hours of the 25th. These storms had access to climatologically high Precipitable Water Values of 1.3 inches to 1.5 inches. The ample atmospheric moisture and training of storms lead to periods of heavy rain resulting in localized flooding of flood prone areas across the southern Texas Panhandle. This localized flooding diminished as storms moved out of the area by 10 AM on the 25th. Details: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the southwestern Texas Panhandle during the evening hours of the 24th. title: Flash Flood: California, Aug 25, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from August 25, 2013 to August 25, 2013. Affected areas: Riverside. Episode summary: Tropical moisture from former tropical storm Ivo lingered across southeast California on August 25th, and as a result the airmass was very moist and unstable. Due to the very moist nature of the atmosphere, a Flash Flood Watch was in effect. During the late afternoon hours, scattered thunderstorms developed across central Riverside county, including parts of Joshua Tree National Park, and they produced locally heavy rain which led to flash flooding. Flash Flood Warning were then issued beginning at 430 pm; some of the most significant flooding in the park occurred at the Cottonwood Visitor's Center near the south entrance. Multiple roads were closed or washed out, and park rangers assisted several stranded motorists who were attempting to leave the park. Details: The atmosphere across central Riverside county, including Joshua Tree National Park, remained very moist and unstable on August 25th, due in part to lingering moisture from former tropical storm Ivo. Scattered thunderstorms developed across the park during the afternoon hours, primarily affecting the southern portion from the Cottonwood Visitor's Center south to the park exit along Interstate 10. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 20, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from July 20, 2013 to July 20, 2013. Affected areas: Potter. Episode summary: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along a surface trough across the western Oklahoma Panhandle during the early morning hours of the 20th. These storms produced an outflow boundary which moved southward across the Texas Panhandle. Isolated showers developed along this outflow boundary. As these storms moved into the southern Texas Panhandle, they gained access to climatologically high Precipitable Water values. This high water content allowed the storms to produce quick half to near an inch accumulations in Potter County. The outflow continued to move southward and exited the Texas Panhandle by 4 AM CST. Details: An isolated thunderstorm moved over the northern half of Amarillo (Potter County). The high water content in the atmosphere allowed this storm to quickly produce 0.60 inch of rain. No flooding was reported in association with this heavy rain.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from July 30, 2013 to July 30, 2013. Affected areas: Ector. Episode summary: A record-setting ridge of high pressure (600 dm over northern New Mexico) built in over the Great Basin and desert Southwest, beginning around June 29th, lasting through approximately July 7, when it hit another peak in temperatures. This resulted in extreme high temperatures, well above normal across the region during this period. The hottest days in July were the 1st through the 3rd, during which several record high minimums were set, as well as highs well over 100 degrees. Prolonged heat in the higher terrain was a significant impact, like in San Diego County. Details: The El Mirage mesonet station reached a high of 110 degrees.
