title: Wildfire: California, Jul 15, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from July 15, 2013 to July 30, 2013. Affected areas: Riverside County Mountains. Episode summary: The Mountain Fire started around 1243 PST on July 15, near the junction of Highway 243 and Highway 74. It burned east of Mountain Center, through the Apple Canyon and Bonita Vista areas, and then along the Desert Divide and southern portion of the San Jacinto Wilderness. CAL FIRE Investigators have determined the cause of the Mountain Fire to be an electrical equipment failure on private property. Mandatory evacuations were ordered for the Idyllwild and Fern Valley areas, including the San Jacinto State Park Wilderness, Forest Service Wilderness and Forest Service campgrounds. Other evacuations include the Trails End Community at the top of Morris Ranch Road, the Andreas Canyon Club, south of Palm Canyon Drive in Palm Springs, Bonita Vista, Pine Springs and the Zen Mountain Center off Apple Canyon Road. Portions of Highways 74 and 243 were closed in this area. Several trails and campgrounds were closed as well. The Palm Springs Tram was shut down for the duration of the fire. The fire destroyed 3 mobile homes and 3 residences and damaged one other residence in Bonita Vista. In Pine Springs, 1 commercial building, a workshop, garage and cabin were destroyed. In addition, 11 other outbuildings and 4-6 vehicles were destroyed. Any possible injuries are unknown. The fire burned 27,531 acres before being fully contained around 1700 PST on July 30th. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000,000.

title: Wildfire: California, Jul 06, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from July 06, 2013 to July 15, 2013. Affected areas: San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: The Chariot Fire started around 1155 PST on July 6, near Chariot Canyon Road at Oriflamme Canyon Road in Vallecito, San Diego County. The location is east of Sunrise Highway and about 9 miles southeast of Julian. The rugged terrain and poor access hindered control efforts. The cause of the fire is still unknown. Laguna, El Prado, Fosters and Horsehaven Campgrounds were evacuated of an unknown number of campers. Twenty campers were evacuated from Shriners Camp to a shelter in Alpine. Sunrise Highway/County Road 1 was closed from SR-79 to Old Highway 80. The fire threatened 120 residential structures and destroyed 118 structures, of undetermined type, plus 2 commercial buildings. The communication site on Monument Peak, as well as other nearby campgrounds in the Cleveland National Forest were threatened as well. Approximately 7 firefighters sustained unknown injuries. The fire burned 7,055 acres before being fully contained around 1700 PST on July 15. Reported property and crop damage: about $7,240,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Sep 20, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from September 20, 2013 to September 20, 2013. Affected areas: Camp, Gregg, Harrison, Smith, Upshur. Episode summary: A long wave trough moved into the Southern Plains during the afternoon, evening and overnight hours of September 20th. This trough was able to tap not only Gulf Of Mexico Moisture, but Eastern Pacific Moisture as well due to moisture associated with Hurricane Manuel off the coast of Baja California. Disturbances rotated out of the Mexican Plateau and into the region from the south and west, providing the lift needed for widespread showers and thunderstorms across the region. Some of this activity trained over the same general area during the overnight hours and produced very heavy rainfall rates. Widespread 2-4 inches of rainfall were the result with isolated higher amounts approaching 8 inches. Despite drought conditions across the region, rates were such that the water produced strong runoff and some flooding was noted. Details: County Road 474 gave way with a car stuck nose first in the water. The intersection of Hwy. 59 and Hwy. 80 in Marshall, Texas was underwater. High water entered a home in Ore City, Texas. Details: The Palm Springs ASOS recorded a high temperature of 118 degrees, which tied the previous record set on the 28th in 1979. The Indio mesonet station set a record high of 121, breaking their old record of 117, set also in 1994. The Campo COOP station recorded a high temperature of 106 degrees, which broke their previous record of 103, set in 1972.

title: Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Oct 13, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, Heavy Rain, from October 13, 2013 to October 13, 2013. Affected areas: Hall. Episode summary: Widespread moderate to heavy rainfall developed over much of the South Plains late this morning and afternoon ahead of a slow moving warm front. Aloft, an unsettled southwesterly flow combined with exceptionally moist air to produce multiple rounds of elevated showers and thunderstorms. Wind shear and instability were favorable enough for a few of these storms to acquire rotation from South Plains (Floyd County) to Turkey (Hall County). One of these rotating storms produced torrential rainfall and two inches worth of pea size hail in Turkey. Although localized, flooding affected much of Turkey and adjacent sections of Highway 86. Elsewhere, widespread soaking rains impacted all but the extreme southwest Texas Panhandle and southern Rolling Plains where on average around one inch of rain was measured. Following the rain, several days of cool temperatures proved detrimental to farmers as many fields remained too wet for harvesting. Cotton bolls suffered some degradation in quality, but monetary losses were expected to be minimal. Details: The public reported standing water of unknown depth covering all of Highway 86 in and around Turkey. An NWS COOP observer in Turkey measured 7.15 inches of rain. The majority of this rain fell within one hour from a nearly stationary thunderstorm. This same storm also produced pea size hail up to two inches deep in Turkey, but no damage was reported. Reported property and crop damage: about $500.

title: Tornado: Texas, Aug 14, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from August 14, 2013 to August 14, 2013. Affected areas: Hutchinson, Sherman. Episode summary: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over the eastern Colorado Plains during the early afternoon hours of the 14th. These storms formed along a stalled frontal boundary that had moved across the Southern Plains the previous day. A strengthening jet streak moving across western Kansas provided the large scale forcing needed to initiate storms along the stalled front. After a brief track east of the front the storms turned to the right and began moving due south. As they moved southward one of the storms became a dominate supercell among a couple weaker storms and intensified significantly as it moved across the Oklahoma Panhandle. This supercell ingested weaker storms as it moved southward which allowed it to sustain a discrete appearance as it moved into the northern Texas Panhandle. While over the northern Texas Panhandle, this supercell produced two brief tornadoes over undeveloped land. As this storm moved across the central and southern Texas Panhandle, the storm structure took on a more multi-cell linear appearance. These storms moved quickly south of the Texas Panhandle by 9 PM CST. Details: A weak and brief tornado was photographed by spotters near Pringle (Hutchinson County). The tornado lasted 20 seconds and no damage was reported. The maximum wind speed was estimated at 65 mph. At 4:45 PM CST, a brief and weak tornado was observed by the public 14 miles east of Stratford near Texas Highway 15 (Sherman County). Witnesses accounts indicate the tornado appeared as a dust whirl associated with a rotating wall cloud. The tornado remained over open country for three minutes and resulted in no damage. The maximum wind speed for this tornado was 65 mph.

title: Wildfire: California, Aug 22, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from August 22, 2013 to August 26, 2013. Affected areas: Santa Lucia Mountains And Los Padres National Forest. title: Drought: Wisconsin, Oct 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Drought, from October 01, 2013 to October 31, 2013. Affected areas: Adams, Buffalo, Clark, Jackson, Juneau, La Crosse, Monroe, Trempealeau, Vernon. Episode summary: The severe drought that developed across western Wisconsin in early September, shrunk in size during the first week in October. Between 1.5 and 5 inches of rain fell across the region, which allowed the drought to be downgraded to moderate across all of Adams, La Crosse and Vernon Counties. During the second week of October, another half to one inch of rain fell, which allowed the drought to be downgraded even more. The severe drought continued in parts of Buffalo, Jackson, Juneau, Monroe and Trempealeau Counties, but was smaller in areal coverage. Some soybean fields in the same counties had plants half their normal height. The severe drought area across Tempealeau County shrunk in size after 2 to 5 inches of rain fell during the first week of October. Another half to one inch of rain fell during the second week of October which confined the severe drought area to the northern half of the county.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 31, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 31, 2013 to October 31, 2013. Affected areas: Angelina, Cherokee, Nacogdoches, Rusk, San Augustine, Smith. Episode summary: A deep upper level trough moved out of the Inter-Mountain West and into the Southern Plains on October 31st. This resulted in strong southwest flow aloft which opened up the Lower Mississippi River Valley for deep tropical moisture from not only the Gulf of Mexico but also the Eastern Pacific. Precipitable Water values for the region were above the 99th percentile value for late October. The end result was very heavy rainfall with widespread rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches across Northeast Texas with isolated amounts upwards of 8 to 10 inches for the entire event. This resulted in widespread flooding...especially south of the Interstate 20 corridor of Northeast Texas. Details: Numerous roads were flooded and closed throughout the county. FM 3053 was flooded with 3-5 feet of water across it. Industrial Drive near Hwy. 79 was flooded with 4 feet of water. Flooding was also resulted in a sinkhole on CR 379D south of Henderson. FM. 855 between Hwy. 175 and FM. 3198 was closed due to flash flooding. A car was stalled in high water on FM. 2868 near the Flint community. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

Most counties remained anywhere between severe (D2) to exceptional (D4) drought conditions. Lamb County dropped from severe (D2) to moderate (D1) conditions.||Temperatures in November saw a reversal from previous months and were below averages by several degrees. Lubbock's monthly average was 1.3 degrees below normal while Childress was 2.3 degrees below normal. Temperatures remained below freezing for 80 continuous hours or more for many locations on the South Plains. This was mainly due to a significant winter storm that affected the region from the 22nd through 24th. This winter storm resulted in a large swath of sleet, freezing rain, and snow. Areas across the southwestern Texas panhandle into the northwestern South Plains saw the highest snowfall totals. A maximum of 10.5 inches was reported at Happy (Swisher County). Between one tenth and three tenths of an inch of ice was reported from the southern South Plains through the Southern Rolling Plains. Similar to drought levels, Keetch-Byram Drought Index values were nearly unchanged. Values between 400 and 500 were observed on the South Plains with 500 to 600 over the Rolling Plains.||All locations across the South Plains and Rolling Plains have now experienced a killing frost. No significant wildfires were reported despite most vegetation in a dormant state. Harvesting was nearly complete with estimates of nearly a 30% reduction of crops from the 10-year average.||Economic losses due to drought through November since the drought began were estimated near $3.0 billion. Reported property and crop damage: about $200,000,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Sep 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from September 01, 2013 to September 23, 2013. Affected areas: Bell, Comanche, Coryell, Hamilton, Lampasas, Mills. Episode summary: Severe drought conditions during the summer months were alleviated around the time of the autumnal equinox over the southwestern counties; due mostly to the beneficial rain received during the third week of the month. Details: Severe/D2 drought over the northern tip of Comanche County at the beginning of September expanded to cover all of the county by the 10th of the month. Conditions were upgraded to Moderate/D1 by September 24 due to rainfall received during the preceding week. Severe/D2 drought over the southern tip of Hamilton County at the beginning of September expanded to cover all of the county by the 10th of the month. title: Flash Flood: Texas, Sep 12, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from September 12, 2013 to September 12, 2013. Affected areas: El Paso, Hudspeth. Episode summary: A deep south to southwest flow aloft continued to tap moisture from the Baja region while low level flow was tapping Gulf of Mexico moisture. Precipitable water values across the region were running over 150 percent of normal. Training storms developed over Far West Texas and produced record rainfall amounts. Details: A trained spotter reported massive flooding across rural Hudspeth County. Area roadways had water at jeep hood level. Rainfall amounts of between 2 to 4 inches were reported from CoCoRaHS observers. Significant flooding issues were reported across Far Northeast El Paso. Total rainfall amounts were between 3 to 4.5 inches in 6 to 8 hours. Almost 4 inches of rain fell in the Horizon City, Tornillo and Socorro areas overnight and into the morning of September 12th. Water levels in Tornillo were up to the hoods of some cars. Homes and neighborhoods in Socorro flooded with at least 15 families needing to be evacuated. In San Elizario TX serious flooding damaged the historic Old County Jail and La Portales Museum along with some homes. Reported property and crop damage: about $4,000,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Oct 10, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from October 10, 2013 to October 10, 2013. Affected areas: Hartley. Episode summary: A combination of factors led to a brief window of high wind gusts in Hartley County during the evening hours of the 10th. A 60 mph low level jet set up across the Texas Panhandle during the evening hours as a surface low pressure system moved into southeastern Colorado which tightened the surface pressure gradient across the county. As virga showers moved out of eastern New Mexico and into Hartley County, the additional downward motion below these storms combined with the low level jet and tight surface pressure gradient to produce high wind gusts at the surface. The Dalhart (Hartley County) ASOS reported a 63 mph non-thunderstorm wind gust at 4:20 PM. High wind gust potential ended as the line of virga showers moved into the central Texas Panhandle. Details: Dalhart ASOS reported a 63 mph gust.

title: Cold/Wind Chill: Texas, Nov 06, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Cold/Wind Chill, from November 06, 2013 to November 06, 2013. Affected areas: Armstrong, Carson, Gray. Episode summary: A cold front moved through the Texas Panhandle during the early morning hours of the 6th. The cooler post frontal airmass allowed temperatures to reach freezing prior to sunrise on the 6th. These subfreezing temperatures threatened sensitive vegetation during the growing season. Overnight low temperatures ranged from 29 degrees at McLean (Gray County) to 31 degrees at Panhandle (Carson County). After sunrise on the 6th, temperatures quickly warmed above freezing by 8:00 AM CST. Details: Overnight low of 29 at McLean. Overnight low of 30 at Claude. Overnight low of 31 at Panhandle.

title: Drought: Texas, Oct 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from October 01, 2013 to October 31, 2013. Affected areas: Bandera, Edwards, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Real, Val Verde. Episode summary: Despite several significant rain events during October, there was little change in the ongoing drought as most of this rain fell in counties where the drought conditions had previously improved. The only counties remaining in severe (Stage D2) or worse category were Val Verde (Stage D3), Bandera, Edwards, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, and Real (all in Stage D2). None of these counties saw any change in their drought category during October. Fire danger at the end of the month was low to moderate. None of the counties in D2 or worse drought had outdoor burn bans in effect at the end of the month. The seven day stream flow averages were below normal (10 to 24 percent) across the Upper Nueces and Medina River basins. Area lakes and reservoirs continued well below normal pool elevations. Lake Amistad showed slight improvement from September, but was still near 37 feet below normal. Lake Travis rose nearly five feet, but was still more than 55 feet below normal. Medina Lake saw almost no rain and continued to be the most affected lake at 87 feet below normal which left it at 4 percent of capacity. The Edwards Aquifer rose during the month and was up to 26 feet below normal, and 7 feet below the level at the end of October 2012. This allowed the Edwards Aquifer Authority to ease water restrictions to stage 2 requiring large water users to reduce pumping by 30%. Fredericksburg remained in stage 4 water restrictions and Kerrville was able to improve to stage 1. title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 12, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 12, 2013 to October 13, 2013. Affected areas: Caldwell, Dimmit, Hays, Maverick, Travis, Uvalde, Zavala. Episode summary: An upper level trough caused southwesterly winds aloft that transported tropical moisture from the Pacific across Mexico into Texas. Surface flow from the southeast brought in low level Gulf moisture. A cold front dropped through central Texas and provided a focus for showers and thunderstorms that produced heavy rainfall leading to flash flooding. Significant flash flooding was seen across portions of South Austin where rainfall totals exceeded 10 inches. Down over the Rio Grande Plains, the same system produced a rain area that exceeded 17 inches near the towns of Crystal City and Carrizo Springs. This flooding rain went into the Nueces watershed and led to major flooding along the Nueces from Asherton all the way down to Lake Corpus Christi. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding in Dimmit County. Nearly all major roads in the county were closed due to high water including Highway 83 between Carrizo Springs and Asherton, FM1433, FM1407, FM1556, and FM468. A CoCoRaHS observer 3.0 miles NNE of Carrizo Springs reported a rainfall total of 17.67 inches of rain during this event. Several other rainfall totals of 11 Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding in Dimmit County. Highway 85 was closed between Carrizo Springs and Dilley and a few stranded motorists needed assistance. There was flooding reported along Barton Creek and water rescues along Bee Cave Road. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000,000.

title: Drought: Wisconsin, Nov 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Drought, from November 01, 2013 to November 30, 2013. Affected areas: Buffalo, Jackson, Juneau, Monroe, Trempealeau. Episode summary: During the first week of November, 1 to 2 inches of rain fell across western into central Wisconsin. This helped the lingering drought, lowering the drought status to moderate across all of Juneau and Monroe Counties. However, this was not enough rain to have a significant impact in other parts of western Wisconsin and the severe drought continued across the northern halves of Buffalo and Trempealeau Counties into the northwest corner of Jackson County. Details: The drought status across Juneau County was changed from severe to moderate after 1 to 2 inches of rain fell in the first week of November. The drought status across Monroe County was changed from severe to moderate after 1 to 2 inches of rain fell in the first week of November. The northern sections of Buffalo County only received between 1 and 1.5 inches of liquid precipitation during November. This was not enough to change the soil moisture conditions and a severe drought remained across the northern half of the county.

title: Dust Storm: Texas, Nov 16, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Dust Storm, from November 16, 2013 to November 16, 2013. Affected areas: Hockley, Lubbock, Terry. Episode summary: In advance of a large upper trough, southwesterly winds increased to 30 to 40 mph over much of the South Plains with gusts measured as high as 55 mph at the Lubbock International Airport. title: Drought: Texas, Sep 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from September 01, 2013 to September 30, 2013. Affected areas: Brooks, Cameron, Coastal Cameron, Coastal Willacy, Hidalgo, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Starr, Willacy, Zapata. Episode summary: By the end of the first week of September, the benefits from rains that fell during the latter part of August and the first week of September began to be felt. A continued surge of deep tropical moisture, allowed for shower and thunderstorm activity to develop across portions of Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley. The eastern sections of the region received between one and three inches of rain fall during early September, with the central and western counties averaging between one and two inches. A few isolated areas received heavier rains, especially over Cameron County. The shower and thunderstorm activity allowed for some improvements in areas where the heaviest rains occurred. Exceptional (D4) drought conditions covered most of Hidalgo County and extended into Starr, Jim Hogg, Brooks, and Willacy counties. The rest of the region was under Severe (D2) to Extreme (D3) drought conditions, with the exception of Zapata County, which was under Moderate (D1) to severe (D2) conditions. Details: Rain fell nearly every day during the first week of September across Cameron County. Total accumulations varied across the county, the ASOS at the Brownsville/South Padre Island International Airport recorded 3.9 inches of rain, while the ASOS at Valley International Airport in Harlingen measured only 1.61 inches. Regardless, this beneficial rainfall allowed for improvement in drought conditions. title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 21, 2013

title: Ice Storm: Texas, Nov 22, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, from November 22, 2013 to November 24, 2013. Affected areas: Andrews, Big Bend Area, Borden, Crane, Davis / Apache Mountains Area, Dawson, Ector, Gaines, Glasscock, Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County, Howard, Loving and 13 more areas. Episode summary: An arctic airmass moved into the region with well below normal temperatures in it's wake. An upper trough was situated over the western Conus, and stayed there for several days. An extended period of wintry precipitation resulted over West Texas. Details: Light freezing rain and sleet fell from the morning of 11/22 until the afternoon of 11/23. However, heavier freezing rain fell the evening of 11/23 with a 1/4 inch of ice accumulation by 953 pm CST. Over 60 car wrecks were reported in Midland from the morning of 11/22 to the morning of 11/24. Numerous roads closed, particularly Loop 250 in Midland. There were no fatalities, and several injurie The Winkler County S.O. reported 1/4 inch to 1 inch ice accumulation due to freezing rain. A little sleet and snow mixed in at times. The Crane County S.O. reported 1/4 to 1/2 inch ice accumulation due to a mix of freezing rain, sleet and snow. Roads are icy. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Dec 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from December 01, 2013 to December 31, 2013. Arctic outbreaks occurred over much of the eastern U.S. with some of this frigid air spilling into West Texas. By the end of the month, Lubbock was 1.9 degrees below normal while Childress was 2.5 degrees below normal. This marks the second consecutive month of below normal temperatures. Precipitation was spotty through the first half of the month with a more widespread precipitation event occurring on the 20th and 21st. While the central Texas Panhandle saw several inches of snow, the extreme southern Texas Panhandle into the Rolling Plains saw freezing rain and rain. title: Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 08, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from December 08, 2013 to December 08, 2013. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Cochran, Crosby, Floyd, Hale, Hockley, Lamb, Lubbock, Lynn, Parmer and 3 more areas. Episode summary: Freezing drizzle developed across portions of the Caprock during the evening of the 7th and lasting into the early morning of the 8th. This was due to very warm and moist air advecting from the southwest and overrunning subfreezing air at the ground. Multiple traffic accidents were reported in Plainview and Lubbock as a thin icy glaze developed on roadways. Conditions improved by early to mid morning on the 8th as the warm layer of air deepened and eroded the remaining shallow layer of arctic air. Following 84 consecutive hours of temperatures at or below 32 degrees, the Lubbock airport rose to above freezing around 1100 CST on the 8th. This was an impressive feat considering Lubbock achieved record cold the day prior, only to rocket to 58 degrees by the afternoon of the 8th.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado: Texas, Oct 30, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado, from October 30, 2013 to October 31, 2013. Affected areas: Hardin, Jasper, Jefferson, Newton, Orange, Tyler. Episode summary: A strong and very wet system moved across the region. Flooding began during the 30th with a pair of tornadoes occurring during Halloween in Southeast Texas. Details: Heavy rain from training thunderstorms fell across Jasper County and neighboring Tyler County for multiple hours. This produce flooding across the region as near 6 inches of rain fell. The high rainfall rates caused flooding around the city of Jasper closing streets, flooding of at least one car, and flooding a couple of houses. Heavy rain across the Beaumont area produced flooding along Eastex Freeway from near the Highway 287/69/Interstate 10 spilt to Highway 105 in Beaumont. Flooding caused the exit ramps and frontage roads to be impassable to some cars with lower sitting vehicles flooding. Heavy rain caused minor flooding of FM 1745 at Russel Creek and at Billiums Creek in the Chester area. Reported property and crop damage: about $290,000.

title: Drought: Wisconsin, Oct 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Drought, from October 01, 2013 to October 06, 2013. Affected areas: Wood. Episode summary: Severe drought (D2) conditions, that developed in far southwest Wood County in September 2013, improved to moderate drought (D1) conditions after a period of significant rainfall across central Wisconsin between October 3rd and October 5th. Details: Severe drought (D2) conditions that developed across far southwest Wood County in September 2013 came to an end in early October 2013.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Nov 24, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from November 24, 2013 to November 25, 2013. Affected areas: Bowie, Camp, Cass, Franklin, Gregg, Harrison, Marion, Morris, Red River, Smith, Titus, Upshur and 1 more areas. Episode summary: A shallow cold layer of air moved out of the Southern Plains and into the Lower Mississippi Valley on the 24th of November. The flow aloft across the southern portion of the country was from the southwest. This resulted in an overrunning pattern of warm and moist air overrunning the cold shallow subfreezing air. The end result was a period of freezing rain and sleet across portions of Northeast Texas. Ice accumulation was mostly less than one quarter of an inch and mainly just north of the Interstate 20 corridor of Northeast Texas. Temperatures were well above normal before this airmass settled into the region so the ice accumulation was mainly on elevated objects such as bridges, overpasses, trees, powerlines and car tops.

title: Strong Wind, Winter Storm: California, Oct 27, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, Winter Storm, from October 27, 2013 to October 28, 2013. Affected areas: Northern San Joaquin Valley, Southern Sacramento Valley, West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: Ahead of a low pressure system, strong onshore winds caused for travel disruption for Northern California. The system then dropped over a foot of snow for the Sierra at higher elevations as it passed through the region. Details: The low pressure system brought the first significant snows of the winter season. The snow was confined to the higher terrain (mainly above 6500 ft), but did impact Interstate 80 and Donner Pass. Snow amounts reported by spotters include 9 at Kingvale, 14 at Soda Springs, 15 at Sugarbowl Peak, 12 at Sugarbowl base, 8.9 at Forni Ridge, 11.6 at 5 ENE of Kyburz, and 5.8 at 5 ENE Pinecrest. Strong onshore winds brought down large trees for the Southern Sacramento Valley. Sacramento Executive AP peaked at 41mph, Sacramento International AP peaked at 46mph, and Vacaville/Nut Tree peaked at 36mph. Broadcast media reported several large trees down in Sacramento which hit houses, powerlines, and cars. A tree fell on a home near Sac State that caused significant roof damage. Onshore winds increased in the afternoon Oct. 27th ahead of the strong trough. Winds in Tracy measured 44mph, Stockton measured 44mph, and Campo Seco measured 49mph. Blowing dust greatly restricted visibility and brought traffic to a slow crawl on highly traveled roads (I-5 and I-580) in the late afternoon and evening hours. The California Highway Patrol reported that six big rigs on I-580 were kn Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 05, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from December 05, 2013 to December 06, 2013. Affected areas: Bowie, Camp, Cass, Franklin, Morris, Red River, Smith, Titus, Upshur, Wood. Episode summary: Another cold shallow arctic airmass moved southeast out of the Southern Plains and into the Lower Mississippi Valley the first week of December. The shallow subfreezing airmass was overridden with a very warm and moist airmass such that freezing rain and sleet fell across the region. Ice accumulation was mainly less than one quarter of an inch but resulted in accumulation on bridges and overpasses, trees and powerlines. Some traffic accidents were noted across Northeast Texas during the height of the winter weather along with a few power outages.

title: Winter Storm: California, Dec 06, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Storm, from December 06, 2013 to December 07, 2013. Affected areas: Upper Trinity River. Episode summary: The first snowstorm of the season dropped snowfall over parts of Northwest California. Snow levels were low. This resulted in chain restrictions on the higher elevation roads. Details: There were a few reports of snowfall meeting warning criteria, especially at lower elevations. Chain restrictions were required on some of the main roads and numerous traffic accidents were reported on these roads.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 09, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 09, 2013 to December 09, 2013. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Clarita Valley, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: The combination of strong surface high pressure in the Great Basin and a passing upper level low produced strong and gusty northeast winds across sections of Ventura and Los Angeles counties. In the mountains, wind gusts as high as 92 MPH were reported while wind gusts in excess of 60 MPH were reported in some valley areas. Details: Strong and gusty north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Los Angeles county. Some wind reports from local RAWS stations include: Chilao (sustained winds 42-54 MPH and gusts 60-69 MPH), Warm Springs (gusts 59-62 MPH), and Camp Nine (gusts 60-77 MPH). Strong and gusty north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Ventura county. North to northeast wind gusts in excess of 70 MPH were reported across the area. Strong and gusty north to northeast winds developed across the Santa Clarita Valley. The Newhall Pass RAWS sensor reported wind gusts as high as 62 MPH.

title: Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Oct 13, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, Heavy Rain, from October 13, 2013 to October 13, 2013. Affected areas: Tom Green. Episode summary: Warm moist air from the gulf and a stationary boundary resulted in isolated severe thunderstorms. An isolated severe thunderstorm produced damaging winds and very heavy rainfall across the town of Wall on October 13. On October 12, strong thunderstorm winds knocked down a couple of old rotten trees onto vehicles and resulted in a couple of injuries. Details: Very heavy rain of 5 to 6 inches fell over a short time and flooded many roads in the town of Wall. A National Weather Service Cooperative Observer measured 5.30 inches of rain since 7 AM. The heavy rain resulted in widespread flooding throughout the town of Wall.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 15, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 15, 2013 to October 15, 2013. Affected areas: Brown. Episode summary: A strong thunderstorm flooded low water crossings across the City of Brownwood. Details: The City of Brownwood barricaded the flooded Vine Street underpass. Other streets were closed because of flooding.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Dec 02, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from December 02, 2013 to December 04, 2013. Affected areas: Barron, Polk, Rusk. Episode summary: The Upper Midwest had a long duration winter storm event that developed Monday morning, December 2nd, and eventually evolved into a large storm system that moved from the Plains, northeast across the Upper Midwest and western Great Lakes region by late Wednesday night. ||A weak disturbance produced locally two to five inches across Polk, Rusk and Barron Counties of west central Wisconsin from Monday morning to Tuesday morning. A few locations in Barron County near Rice Lake and Cumberland received locally six inches from Monday's storm. ||By Tuesday, much warmer air from the southern United States produced precipitation in the form of sleet, rain and snow that fell through part of Wednesday afternoon as the surface low moved across west central Wisconsin. The mixture of precipitation eventually changed over to all snow Wednesday evening. However, the mixture of sleet and snow added up to locally 4 to 7 inches across portions of west central Wisconsin. Details: Storm totals by Wednesday evening ranged from 4 to 7 inches snow and sleet across the county.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Oct 30, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from October 30, 2013 to October 31, 2013. Affected areas: Anderson, Bell, Falls, Freestone, Limestone, Milam. Episode summary: Significant flooding occurred in the south and southeastern counties when up to 11 of rain fell during the late evening and overnight hours. The flooding rains were caused by large scale lift occurring over a moist but cool boundary layer. Training of showers and thunderstorms occurred throughout the event. Details: Heavy rain and flash flooding led to the closure of Wedel Cemetery Road. The road was damaged by the flood waters. One to two feet of water was flowing over the intersection of FM 436 and Old TX 95 in Little River. Heavy thunderstorms produced nearly 8 of rain in just a few hours resulting in flash flooding. Heavy thunderstorms produced flash flooding in southern Falls County. FM 1373 was underwater between FM 413 and HWY 6. High water was reported on HWY 6 where it crosses Little Brazos River. Water was also reported on FM 2413 and FM 46. Nearly 8-10 of rain fell over the area in just a few hours. Reported property and crop damage: about $560,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Oct 14, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from October 14, 2013 to October 14, 2013. Affected areas: Eastland, Falls, Tarrant, Wise, Young. Episode summary: A 43 year old male was killed in Wise County when a semi jackknifed on a wet road and hit the oncoming car the male was driving. A 26 year old male was killed in Falls County when his car lost control on a curve in a heavy downpour and slid into an oncoming tractor-trailor. A 65 year old female was killed in Tarrant County when her car lost control on a rain-slick bridge and fell onto the riverbank below. A 24 year old female was killed in a chain reaction accident in Eastland County on Ranger Hill in rainy conditions. Details: A 43 year old male was killed when a semi jackknifed on a wet road and hit the oncoming car the male was driving. The accident occurred near the intersection of TX 101 and FM 1786. A 26 year old male was killed when his car lost control on a curve in a heavy downpour and slid into an oncoming tractor-trailor. The accident occurred on Highway 7 about 3 miles west of Chilton. A 24 year old female was killed in a chain reaction accident on Ranger Hill in rainy conditions. Reported property and crop damage: about $150,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Oct 03, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from October 03, 2013 to October 03, 2013. Affected areas: Columbia, Sauk. Episode summary: Strong to severe thunderstorms including heavy rain occurred along a stationary front over southern Wisconsin. Details: An old and weak stone and mortar wall collapsed on one side of the house when high water from heavy rain impacted it. Street flooding resulted in some cars stalling in the high water, mainly on the east side of town. Hourly radar rainfall rates were 1-1.5 inches. High standing water on some streets.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Nov 25, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from November 25, 2013 to November 25, 2013. Affected areas: Carson, Potter, Randall. Episode summary: Localized wintry precipitation moved across portions of the southern Texas Panhandle during the evening hours of the 25th. Low level moisture curved around a southeastward traveling surface low as an upper level low dove southward across the Panhandle. As the forcing mechanisms aligned light drizzle initiated, and froze on contact with elevated surfaces such as windshields and overpasses due to surface temperatures in the mid-20s. Freezing drizzle lasted for a brief period as the surface low quickly moved southeast of the Panhandle by 7 Pm CST, but was sufficient to impact local roadways. A trained spotter in Amarillo reported that freezing drizzle was making roads slick on Soncy Road, Loop 335, and Hillside Road (Randall County) which caused several vehicles to skid. The same spotter reported that his windshield had accumulated a tenth of an inch of ice. An NWS employee reported a vehicle accident at the intersection of Interstate 40 and Lakeside Drive (Potter County) which caused traffic to back up for two miles. A member of the public also reported slick conditions on US Highway 60 near Pantex (Carson County). No further reports of slick conditions or vehicle accidents were reported in association to this freezing drizzle. Details: Slick conditions on Highway 60 near Pantex. Slick conditions led to a wreck at Lakeside and I-40. Slick conditions across the SW side of Amarillo with 0.10 inch of ice on windshield.

title: Ice Storm: Texas, Dec 05, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, from December 05, 2013 to December 06, 2013. Affected areas: Andrews, Borden, Ector, Howard, Midland, Scurry, Winkler. Episode summary: A strong arctic cold front moved south into the region with light precipitation breaking out behind it. Wintry precipitation increased in intensity as a mid level shortwave trough and entrance region of an upper jet combined to increase lift over the region. A mix of sleet and freezing rain resulted. Details: One quarter inch of ice accumulation was reported in Andrews. The freezing rain on the 5th was followed by sleet overnight. One inch of ice accumulation was reported in Midland. Precipitation began as freezing rain, then transitioned to sleet during the afternoon and evening. One inch of ice accumulation was reported in Odessa. Ice accumulated more rapidly when precipitation transitioned from freezing rain to sleet the afternoon and evening of the 5th.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Oct 31, 2013

Episode summary: A slow moving storm system and associated frontal boundary generated heavy rainfall that led to flooding across portions of southeast Texas, especially in and around the Houston and Galveston areas. Details: Heavy rain caused road flooding around the city of Houston. High water at intersection of Robinson Creek Rd and Bowden Rd. High water on roads in and around Bonney. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Oct 01, 2013

Affected areas: Brown, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Fisher, Haskell, Jones, San Saba, Shackelford, Throckmorton. Episode summary: Beneficial rainfall during the fall continued to diminish the severity of the three year drought, agriculturally, across a large part of West Central Texas. Spence to Lake Ivie to beyond San Saba in a severe drought because of very low lake levels. Details: The U.S. Drought Monitor placed the extreme northern portion of Fisher County in a severe drought. title: Ice Storm, Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 20, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, Winter Weather, from December 20, 2013 to December 21, 2013. Affected areas: Castro, Childress, Cottle, Dickens, Swisher. Episode summary: In advance of an upper low in the Desert Southwest, a very rich feed of subtropical and Gulf moisture overspread much of west and northwest Texas by the afternoon of the 20th resulting in a widespread rain event. In Childress County and into parts of the Rolling Plains, marginally freezing temperatures following a weak cold front from earlier in the day resulted in several hours of light to moderate freezing rain. Roughly 16 hours of freezing rain fell in Childress from the afternoon of the 20th before ending late in the morning on the 21st. Although ground temperatures remained above freezing through the event, exposed objects such as trees, power lines and fences in Childress County ended up with 0.1 to nearly 0.3 inches of ice. The ice buildup on power lines resulted in over 700 residents in Childress losing power, but fortunately area roads remained warm enough through the event and Christmas travel was not seriously impacted. ||Light freezing rain was also observed farther south in Cottle and Dickens counties, and the wintry precipitation was able to form a light accumulation on trees, power lines, and vehicles. Near the end of the event, precipitation fell as snow across the extreme south-central Texas Panhandle. A cooperative weather observer reported 2.0 inches of snow in Dimmitt (Castro County) and law enforcement reported 3.0 inches in Happy (Swisher County). One motorist fatality was reported due to slick roads on Interstate 27 near Tulia. Reported property and crop damage: about $55,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 13, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 13, 2013 to October 14, 2013. Affected areas: Duval, La Salle, Webb. Episode summary: On the morning of October 13th, 2013, a complex of showers and thunderstorms developed between Eagle Pass and Cotulla. These showers and thunderstorms continued to form and move over nearly the same area throughout the afternoon and evening hours on the 13th into the early morning hours on the 14th. The combination of a slow-moving outflow boundary, a deep layer of very moist air from both the Gulf of Mexico and the Pacific Ocean, and upper level forcing from a weak disturbance resulted in 6 to 8 inches of rainfall occurring in western portions of La Salle, northwest Duval, and western Webb Counties. Further west across Dimmit and Zavala counties, rainfall amounts exceeded 10 inches in some locations. Details: Road closures along portions of Texas Highway 97 and Farm to Market Road 624 in Cotulla with 2 feet of water moving over the roads. The Duval County Sheriff's Office reported flooding on a bridge along Texas Highway 16 about 10 miles north of Freer. Heavy rainfall produced flooding in Cotulla and across La Salle County. Rising creeks and water over the roads caused road closure across many Farm to Market roads including FM 468 and FM 469. Reported property and crop damage: about $240,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 16, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 16, 2013 to November 16, 2013. Affected areas: Hartley, Moore, Ochiltree, Sherman. Episode summary: The Texas Panhandle experienced a windy day with some locations reaching high wind criteria during the early afternoon hours of the 16th. The surface pressure gradient across the Texas Panhandle increased through the morning hours of the 16th in response to a closed surface low over northeastern Iowa. This strengthening pressure gradient increased sustained surface winds across the Panhandles into the 35 mph to 40 mph range. Sherman, Ochiltree, Hartley, and Moore counties saw sustained surface wind of 40 mph for 2 to 3 hours due to a slightly stronger pressure gradient across those counties. Strong 60 mph to 70 mph winds aloft also managed to mix to the surface which caused localized high wind gusts. The Dumas AWOS reported a 58 mph wind gust at 1:55 PM CST, and the Dalhart ASOS reported a 62 mph gust at 1:28 PM CST. By 3 PM CST, the surface pressure gradient across the Texas Panhandle weakened as a closed surface low moved into southeastern Colorado. Details: Sustained wind of 44 mph at Dumas with a gusts of 58 mph. Sustained wind of 40 mph at Perryton. Sustained wind of 44 mph at Dalhart with a gust of 62 mph.

title: Dust Storm: Texas, Nov 16, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Dust Storm, from November 16, 2013 to November 16, 2013. Affected areas: Sherman. Episode summary: The Texas Panhandle experienced a windy day with some locations reaching high wind criteria during the early afternoon hours of the 16th. The surface pressure gradient across the Texas Panhandle increased through the morning hours of the 16th in response to a closed surface low over northeastern Iowa. This strengthening pressure gradient increased sustained surface winds across the Panhandles into the 35 mph to 40 mph range. Sherman, Ochiltree, Hartley, and Moore counties saw sustained surface wind of 40 mph for 2 to 3 hours due to a slightly stronger pressure gradient across those counties. These high winds picked up dust and dirt which caused near zero visibility on U.S Highway 287 south of the town of Stratford (Sherman County). The low visibility led to a multiple-car pile-up involving 5 cars and two tractor trailers around 2:00 PM CST. Seven of the 14 people involved were taken to the hospital with only one being listed in serious condition. By 3 PM CST, the surface pressure gradient across the Texas Panhandle weakened as a closed surface low moved into southeastern Colorado which brought an end to the lower visibilities. Details: Lower visibilities led to a multiple car pile up on US Highway 287. Seven people were taken to the hospital with one listed in serious condition.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Oct 27, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from October 27, 2013 to October 27, 2013. Affected areas: East Bay Hills And The Diablo Range, East Bay Interior Valleys, Mountains Of San Benito County And Interior Monterey County Including Pinnacles National Park, San Francisco, San Francisco Bay Shoreline. Episode summary: Strong and gusty west-northwest winds impacted much of the Bay Area resulting in downed trees, downed power lines, toppled scaffolding, and blown over tractor trailers. An unseasonably cold and rapidly developing low pressure system moved through the Bay Area during the afternoon hours of October 27 and the early morning hours of October 28th. As the surface low rapdily deepened a tight pressure gradient developed across the Bay Area, most notably the East Bay. The dropping surface pressures and rather strong onshore pressure gradient helped to produce widespread wind gusts in excess of 35 mph with a few locations over 60 mph. As the strong onshore winds were squeezed through the East Bay hills winds were enhanced knocking over tractor trailers on Altamont Pass. Details: Wind gusts of 75 MPH measured on a mesonet site in Altamont Pass. Tractor trailers were blown over on the highway through Altamont Pass. A wind gust of 69 MPH was measured at the Santa Rita Mesonet Site in San Benito County at an elevation of 5000 feet. A wind gust of 62 MPH was measured on the Los Vaqueros RAWS at elevation 1100 feet. Reported property and crop damage: about $45,000.

title: Flood: Texas, Oct 17, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from October 17, 2013 to October 22, 2013. Affected areas: La Salle, Live Oak, Mcmullen. Episode summary: Due to the very heavy rains which fell across the upper reaches of the Nueces River watershed, major river flooding was the result between Asherton and the headwaters of Lake Corpus Christi. The Nueces River at Asherton recorded a crest of 29.70 feet on the 14th. This is the 5th highest all-time crest on record for Asherton. The Nueces River at Cotulla recorded a crest of 22.81 feet on the 17th. This is the 4th highest all-time crest on record for Cotulla. South of Tilden on the Nueces River, a crest of 23.50 feet on the 17th was measured. This is the 3rd highest all-time crest for South of Tilden on the Nueces River. The Nueces River at Three Rivers recorded a crest of 38.95 feet on the 21st. This is the 10th highest all-time crest for Three Rivers. ||Widespread lowland flooding several miles from the main Nueces River channel occurred along the Nueces River between Asherton and the headwaters of Lake Corpus Christi. Many homes, roads, farm and oil field equipment, and cattle were flooded and cut off due to the major flooding. Details: Farm and ranch equipment were inundated by major flooding along the Nueces River. Some oil field equipment were flooded also. Major flooding along the Nueces River occurred near Cotulla. Some farm and ranch equipment were flooded. Cattle were cut off by the flood waters also. County Road 365 in River Creek Acres flooded and closed due to major flooding on the Nueces River. title: Drought: Texas, Jan 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from January 01, 2014 to January 31, 2014. Affected areas: Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hockley, Kent and 10 more areas. Episode summary: January saw nearly stagnant drought conditions with only a slight expansion. The entire area remained in severe (D2) drought or worse except for Hall and Bailey Counties.||The month of January saw unusually cool temperatures on average across the entire region. Most of the month was characterized by a blocking upper ridge over the West Coast preventing most arctic air intrusions. However, when arctic air did make it as far south as West Texas, temperatures were well below seasonal averages. This marks the third consecutive month of below normal temperatures. Because of the blocking ridge, almost no precipitation was measured during the month with several sites not even measuring a trace of precipitation. January is normally a dry month with precipitation averages ranging from 0.50 to 0.75 inches. With dry but cool conditions, Keetch-Byram Drought Index Values remained unchanged. Values were generally between 400 and 500.||Of the few days during January that were above normal on temperatures, fire weather conditions reached critical levels. Fuels considerably dried out through the month with Energy Release Component (ERC) values exceeding the 90th percentile for this time of year. The region is entering the peak of the wildfire season in the upcoming months. Dry land crops struggled through January with no precipitation. Irrigated crops were in good condition. The unusually cold weather stressed livestock and supplemental feed was expected to be needed into the summer months.||Economic losses due to drought through January since the drought began were estimated near $3.0 billion.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Jan 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from January 14, 2014 to January 14, 2014. Affected areas: Chippewa, Dunn, Eau Claire, Pepin, Pierce, Polk, St. Croix. Episode summary: A storm system moved across the Upper Midwest the morning of Tuesday, January 14th. Initially this storm system was weak as it produced one to two inches of snow across portions of central and east central Minnesota prior to sunrise. After 6 am, the storm quickly intensified and produced snowfall rates of 1 to 1.5 inches per hour across far east central Minnesota, and into west central Wisconsin. By the early afternoon, snowfall amounts ranged from 6 to 10 inches across west central Wisconsin from near Osceola to Chippewa Falls and Eau Claire. Details: Several snowfall reports of 6 to 8 inches occurred across Polk County in a 10 hour period Tuesday. Several snowfall reports of 6 to 9 inches occurred across Chippewa County in a 10 hour period Tuesday. Several snowfall reports of 7 to 10 inches occurred across Eau Claire County in a 10 hour period Tuesday.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Nov 22, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from November 22, 2013 to November 26, 2013. Affected areas: Bandera, Blanco, Burnet, Edwards, Gillespie, Hays, Kendall, Kerr, Llano, Williamson. Episode summary: An arctic airmass settled over South Central Texas and then south to southeasterly low level flow developed setting up on overrunning pattern. A series of upper level shortwave troughs moved across the region producing winter precipitation over several days. A mix of freezing rain, freezing drizzle, sleet, and rain fell at various times from November 22nd through the 25th. There was some light ice accumulation on exposed surfaces including trees, fences, and railings. On November 26th, precipitation fell as snow with no accumulation. Details: There was a mix of sleet and freezing rain with light accumulation on exposed surfaces. A mix of freezing rain and freezing drizzle produced light accumulation on exposed surfaces. A mix of sleet, freezing rain, and rain produced light ice accumulation on exposed surfaces.

title: Cold/Wind Chill: Texas, Jan 05, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Cold/Wind Chill, from January 05, 2014 to January 07, 2014. Affected areas: Angelina, Bowie, Camp, Cass, Cherokee, Franklin, Gregg, Harrison, Marion, Morris, Nacogdoches, Panola and 9 more areas. Episode summary: An arctic airmass infiltrated the region early on Sunday, January 5th with falling temperatures and strong northwest winds. Temperatures fell through much of the day on January 5th behind the front with winds approaching 30 mph at times, making it feel much colder with very cold wind chills. Skies cleared the evening of the 5th but the strong northwest winds continued with wind chill values near zero to ten degrees above zero witnessed the night of the 5th. Low temperatures the morning of the 6th and the morning of the 7th were some of the coldest temperatures Northeast Texas had seen since February 3 through the 5th of 1996. The extreme cold resulted in many underground water lines freezing and bursting. Below are some low temperatures recorded at various locations for the mornings of the 6th and 7th of January. title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Nov 25, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from November 25, 2013 to November 25, 2013. Affected areas: Dane, Dodge, Green, Iowa, Jefferson, Kenosha, Lafayette, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Racine, Walworth, Washington and 1 more areas. Episode summary: A surge of relatively warm and moist air aloft led to the development of light to moderate snow during the morning rush hour with 1-3 inches accumulating. Roads became snow covered and numerous slide-offs and accidents occurred, especially in the Madison area and the Milwaukee Metropolitan area. Two indirect deaths occurred with vehicle mishaps in Dane County. Since this was the first snow event for the season, motorists may not have been cautious enough. Details: A trained spotter reported 2.0 inches of snow in Cedarburg. A Cooperative Observer reported 1.1 inches of snow in Milwaukee. The Public reported around one half inch to one inch across Racine County.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from November 17, 2013 to November 18, 2013. Affected areas: Kenosha, Racine. Strong west winds along and behind a cold front gusted to 35 to 55 mph across southern Wisconsin. A man was killed in Kenosha County when a strong wind gust forced him to lose control of his motorcycle. Also a brick facade from an old and weakened building in the city of Racine collapsed onto a car and sidewalk. No one was injured. title: Drought: Texas, Dec 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from December 01, 2013 to December 31, 2013. Affected areas: Bandera, De Witt, Edwards, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Real, Val Verde. Episode summary: December was a dry month across South Central Texas with most of the region receiving less than normal rainfall. Fortunately, this had little effect on the drought. De Witt County was the only county that changed into a worse drought category moving into severe drought (Stage D2). The rest of the area remained unchanged with Val Verde County in extreme (Stage D3) drought category and Bandera, Edwards, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, and Real Counties in severe (Stage D2) drought category. The seven day stream flow averages at the end of the month were much below normal (less than 10 percent) across the Frio, Lower San Antonio, and Guadalupe River basins and below normal (10 to 24 percent) across the Medina, Nueces, Lower Colorado, and Upper San Antonio River basins. Area lakes and reservoirs continued well below normal pool elevations. Lake Amistad showed slight improvement from November, but was still near 36 feet below normal. Lake Travis continued to see improvement, but was near 53 feet below normal. Medina Lake was again the most affected lake at 88.3 feet below normal which left it at 4 percent of capacity. The Edwards Aquifer rose slightly during the month and was 27 feet below normal, and 11 feet below the level at the end of December 2012. The Edwards Aquifer Authority remained in stage 2 water restrictions requiring large water users to reduce pumping by 30%. Fredericksburg remained in stage 4 water restrictions and Kerrville in stage 1. title: Winter Weather: Texas, Nov 23, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from November 23, 2013 to November 24, 2013. Affected areas: Carson, Dallam, Gray, Hansford, Hartley, Hemphill, Hutchinson, Lipscomb, Moore, Ochiltree, Oldham, Potter and 2 more areas. Episode summary: A slow moving upper level low brought several inches of snow to the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandle from the 23rd to the 24th of November. As the upper low moved over New Mexico, the associated jet streak provided large scale lift sufficient to produce scattered snow bands across the southern Texas Panhandle during the early evening hours of the 23rd. Moisture deficiency in the snow growth region of the atmosphere had been a hindrance for efficient snow production earlier in the week, but the 6 PM CST upper air sounding from Amarillo showed saturated conditions in the snow growth region. These scattered snow bands were able to quickly generate one to two inches of snow across the southern Texas Panhandle due the higher moisture availability. This snow band would move to the northwest before diminishing over the northeastern Texas Panhandle. After a brief lull, another snow band developed across the Eastern Plains of New Mexico and moved northeastward into the southwestern Texas Panhandle. The 6 AM CST upper air sounding from Amarillo on the 24th showed that drier air was beginning to work its way into the Texas Panhandle. However, the extreme northern portion of the snow bands reached the Oklahoma Panhandle. As this band reached the Oklahoma Panhandle, the influence of the drier air infiltrating the Southern Plains became more evident. The main snow band diminished and all further snow showers that developed through midday on the 24th became isolated in coverage. title: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 02, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather, from February 02, 2014 to February 02, 2014. Affected areas: Briscoe, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall, Kent, King and 6 more areas. Episode summary: Late in the evening of February 1st, an open trough approached West Texas from far northern Mexico. Unseasonably deep moisture and strong lift ahead of this trough resulted in a nearly stationary band of moderate to heavy snow from near O'Donnell (Lynn County) northeast to Paducah (Cottle County) shortly after midnight on February 2nd. Lift and instability were so great at times that several cloud-to-ground lightning strikes accompanied this intense band of snow. Snowfall rates in this thundersnow were estimated to be between two and three inches per hour. By 0200 CST, the Sheriff's Office in Post reported treacherous roads and several vehicles in the ditch along Highway 84 from intense snow with visibilities of 50 to 75 feet. This heavy snow band slowly exited the Rolling Plains shortly after daybreak, but not before producing a large snow swath measured between six and ten inches deep. Occasionally gusty north winds during the storm produced some snow drifts up to a couple feet. Dozens of minor vehicle accidents were reported, particularly in Garza, Crosby and Dickens Counties. title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from February 03, 2014 to February 04, 2014. Affected areas: Garza. Episode summary: Light snow and freezing drizzle occurred on the evening of the third into the morning of the fourth ahead of an upper level trough moving northeast out of northern Mexico. Abundant low level and near surface moisture contributed to freezing drizzle as well as some very light snow amounts from the far southern panhandle into the South Plains and Rolling Plains. Icy roads in Garza County caused a multiple vehicle accident on the northbound side of US Highway 84 at the intersection of FM 399 northwest of Post. One fatality was reported while four others were injured.

title: Drought: Texas, Feb 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from February 01, 2014 to February 28, 2014. Affected areas: Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall, Hockley and 11 more areas. Episode summary: February saw little changes in long term drought conditions with only one major winter storm as the only precipitation event and wildly varying temperatures. Hall County, which has remained in moderate (D1) drought conditions since July 2013 was degraded to severe (D2) drought. Bailey County remained in D1 conditions and Garza county dropped to D1 due to the winter storm. Elsewhere, conditions ranged from D2 to exceptional (D4) drought conditions.||The month of February saw wild temperature swings as well as a major winter storm. This winter storm was the only precipitation across the region during the entire month. Up to one foot of snow in a 24-hour period was observed across the southern Rolling Plains and southeastern South Plains on February 2nd. The lack of measurable precipitation throughout the rest of the month prevented the region from realizing any major improvements to drought conditions. Although temperatures actively varied throughout the month between very warm periods and arctic cold fronts, the average monthly temperatures were below seasonal averages. Temperatures at Lubbock and Childress were -2.0 and -5.6 degrees, respectively. Both the Lubbock and Childress stations recorded one daily record maximum and a record minimum, further indicative of the variable temperatures. title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 09, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from February 09, 2014 to February 10, 2014. Affected areas: Cottle. Episode summary: On the afternoon of the ninth, a slow moving cold front moved into the Rolling Plains bringing significant low level moisture behind the front. During the evening hours, light freezing drizzle and freezing fog began to form creating patchy black ice on area roadways. At around 0100 CST on the tenth, a van traveling through Cottle County, a few miles west of Paducah, encountered black ice which resulted in the van overturning and ejecting several individuals. There were no fatalities but several injuries reported with the traffic accident.

title: Extreme Cold/Wind Chill: Wisconsin, Jan 27, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Extreme Cold/Wind Chill, from January 27, 2014 to January 28, 2014. Affected areas: Adams, Buffalo, Clark, Crawford, Grant, Jackson, Juneau, La Crosse, Monroe, Richland, Taylor, Trempealeau and 1 more areas. Episode summary: Wind chills of 35 to 45 below were common across western Wisconsin on the mornings of January 27th and 28th. These dangerous wind chills occurred behind a strong cold front that moved across the region on January 26th. As temperatures fell behind the front, strong northwest winds starting pushing the wind chills to 35 below or colder during the early morning of the 27th. Most locations then had wind chills of 35 below or colder into the morning of the 28th, which was when warmer air started to spread back across the area. The lowest recorded wind chill was 46 below from the automated weather observing equipment at the Black River Falls airport (Jackson County). All the schools across western Wisconsin were closed on both January 27th and 28th. Details: Wind chills of 35 below or colder occurred across Monroe County from the morning of January 27th into the morning of the 28th. The lowest recorded wind chill was 35 below from the automated weather observing equipment at the Sparta airport and a mesonet reporting station near Tomah. Wind chills of 35 below or colder occurred across Juneau County from the morning of January 27th into the morning of the 28th. The lowest recorded wind chill was 38 below from the automated weather observing equipment at Volk Field. Wind chills of 35 below or colder occurred across Trempealeau County from the early morning of January 27th into the morning of the 28th.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 29, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from December 29, 2013 to December 29, 2013. Affected areas: Parker. Episode summary: A female died in a car crash near Weatherford that was likely caused by an icy patch. Five other passengers were seriously injured in the crash. Five other passengers involved in the accident were seriously injured. The accident occurred on Farm Road 1885 near Farm Road 920 north of Weatherford. Light freezing rain was occurring around the time of the accident. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Dec 21, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from December 21, 2013 to December 21, 2013. Affected areas: Dallas. Weather played a role in the death of a person who crashed their truck in the 4500 block of Davis Street near Cockrell Hill Rd. The roads were slick due to rain at the time of the accident. title: Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from January 23, 2014 to January 24, 2014. Affected areas: Angelina, Cherokee, Nacogdoches, Panola, Rusk, Sabine, San Augustine, Shelby. Episode summary: A strong ridge of arctic high pressure moved southward into the Southern Plains on Thursday, January 23rd. Light rain began during the morning hours on Thursday as moisture began to override the shallow cold airmass closer to the surface. As the day continued, the depth of the cold air became deeper and deeper with some sleet and snow flurries reported near the Interstate 20 corridor of Northeast Texas and Northern Louisiana. By late afternoon, the change over from light rain to brief periods of sleet and eventually all snow began across the southern half of Northeast Texas into West Central and East Central Louisiana. Snow came down moderately heavy at times reducing visibilities to near one mile, especially across the lower Toledo Bend and Sam Rayburn Country of Deep East Texas into West Central Louisiana. The precipitation ended during the predawn hours Friday, January 24th but not before some impressive snow totals were reported across the region. Below are some snow totals for selected cities across Northeast Texas with the snow having begun during the late afternoon or early evening on Thursday, January 23rd and ending during the predawn hours of Friday, January 24th. Broaddus: 4 inches, Pineland: 4 inches, Etoile: 3 inches, Lufkin: 3 inches, Hemphill: 3 inches, Toledo Bend Dam: 3 inches, Center: 2 inches, Wells: 2 inches, San Augustine: 2 inches, Rusk: 1 inch, Mount Enterprise: 1 inch, Carthage: 1 inch, Nacogdoches: 1 inch.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from December 04, 2013 to December 04, 2013. Affected areas: Eastern/Central El Paso County. Episode summary: An 150kt jet streak was located near Albuquerque at 12z on the 4th with a broad upper trough over the Western United States. Deep west to southwest flow was in place across the region with strong winds occurring ahead of an approaching cold front. A peak gust of 66 mph was reported at in Northeast El Paso. Details: An NWS Employee reported a peak gust of 66 mph in Northeast El Paso near Kenworthy and Trans-Mountain Road. Other peak gusts reported include 60 mph at Fort Bliss, 58 mph 10 miles north-northeast of El Paso and 65 mph 1 mile north of Horizon City.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 28, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from January 28, 2014 to January 28, 2014. Affected areas: Angelina, Nacogdoches, Sabine, San Augustine, Shelby. Episode summary: Another arctic cold front moved into the region Monday, January 27th, resulting in very cold and much below normal temperatures across the region. An upper level disturbance moving atop this very cold air mass resulted in areas of snow, sleet and freezing rain across Deep East Texas and the southern sections of North Central Louisiana early Tuesday morning for the second time in less than a week. The wintry mix was more predominant over Deep East Texas, with the snow the more dominant precipitation type across the southern sections of North Central Louisiana. The precipitation ended around mid morning on the 27th, resulting in mainly light snowfall accumulations across the region. Below are some snow totals for selected cities across Northeast Texas. Etoile: 1.00 inch, San Augustine: 1.00 inch, Hemphill 1.00 inch, Lufkin: 0.30 inches, Center: 0.30 inches.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 07, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from December 07, 2013 to December 07, 2013. Affected areas: Austin, Brazos, Burleson, Colorado, Washington. Episode summary: Light freezing drizzle developed in the late afternoon through early evening hours. There were light accumulations on area bridges and overpasses. Details: Light freezing drizzle was reported in the Brenham area. There was a light glaze on area roads and the windshields of automobiles. Light freeing drizzle and sleet was reported near Bellville. There was ice on a bridge in the area on Highway 36. Light freezing drizzle was reported across portions of Brazos County. Numerous roads were closed due to accumulation of ice, especially in and around Highway 21 from the Bryan area westward to the Brazos River near the Caldwell county line. Several accidents were reported.

title: Winter Storm, Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 05, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, Winter Weather, from December 05, 2013 to December 06, 2013. Affected areas: Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Mcculloch, Menard and 10 more areas. Episode summary: A strong upper level disturbance and an arctic cold front brought periods of freezing rain, sleet and light snow to much of West Central Texas. Sleet was the dominant mode of frozen precipitation as a half to an inch of sleet was reported across much of the area along and north of Interstate 10 and east of a line from Robert Lee to Sonora. The icy roads and very cold temperatures resulted in the closing of schools, universities and colleges. City state and federal offices also closed for the day. Details: A National Weather Service employee reported one half inch of sleet 4 miles west south west of San Angelo. Law enforcement officials reported a tenth of an inch of freezing rain about 10 miles northwest of Sterling City. The sheriff's office reported between one quarter and just under one half inch of sleet on area roads at 12:10 AM. As of 10 AM on December 6th, a total of one inch of sleet was reported in Eldorado.

title: Drought: Texas, Dec 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from December 01, 2013 to December 31, 2013. Affected areas: Armstrong, Carson, Dallam, Deaf Smith, Hansford, Hartley, Moore, Oldham, Potter, Sherman. Episode summary: The month of December was another dry month for most of the Texas Panhandle, with most precipitation being observed late in the month in a single snowstorm that brought 6 to 10 inches of snow to the northwest Texas Panhandle. This led to a general degradation of drought conditions across the Panhandle and an expansion of drought into areas which were drought-free after summer 2013. Exceptional (D4) Drought conditions returned to portions of the northwest Texas Panhandle while Extreme (D3) Drought conditions also expanded in that area. The remainder of the western half of the Texas Panhandle remains at Moderate (D1) to Severe (D2) Drought rating. The eastern half of the Texas Panhandle remains below Severe (D2) Drought rating, but most of the Abnormally Dry (D0) conditions there degraded to Moderate Drought by the end of December. Amarillo recorded 0.32 inches of precipitation for the month (0.39 inches below normal), Dalhart recorded 0.21 inches of precipitation (0.33 inches below normal), and Borger recorded 0.27 inches of precipitation (0.50 inches below normal).||Winter wheat was in need of moisture, but most winter wheat was in fair to good condition during the month according to reports received by the Texas A&M Agrilife Program. Upper soil zones remained drier than normal in most of the Texas Panhandle, but moisture levels were near normal in areas having received snowfall during the month. Deeper soil zones ranged from less than 30 to around 50 percent of normal in the western Texas Panhandle, but values of greater than 150 percent of normal were reported in the northeastern Texas Panhandle.
