title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 04, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from February 04, 2014 to February 04, 2014. Affected areas: Bowie. Episode summary: Vigorous upper level trough moved out of the Southwest United States and into the Texas Hill Country during the morning hours of the 4th. Upper forcing was felt well in advance of the trough across Southeast Oklahoma, the northern third of Northeast Texas into Southwest Arkansas with widespread precipitation breaking out. Temperatures quickly dropped below freezing during the late night hours of the 3rd into the predawn hours of the 4th and as a result, the light rain became mostly freezing rain with a mix of sleet and light snow. The temperatures did not climb above freezing until the mid morning hours of February 4th. Freezing rain accumulations across portions of Bowie County were mostly near one tenth of an inch. This resulted in ice accumulation on elevated objects only, including bridges, overpasses and powerlines. There were a few automobile accidents along with a few power outages.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 07, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from February 07, 2014 to February 07, 2014. Affected areas: Bowie, Camp, Cass, Franklin, Morris, Red River, Titus. Episode summary: Another upper level disturbance moved across the Middle Red River Valley of Southeast Oklahoma, the northern half of Northeast Texas and Southwest Arkansas as well as portions of North Central Louisiana during the afternoon and evening hours of February 7th. This system overran an cold airmass at the surface and as a result, some snow was reported across the region. The snow across the northern half of Northeast Texas was mainly near one inch in accumulation. The snow caused some slick spots across some locations, mainly across elevated bridges and overpasses.

title: Winter Storm, Winter Weather: California, Dec 06, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Storm, Winter Weather, from December 06, 2013 to December 07, 2013. Affected areas: Burney Basin/Eastern Shasta County, Motherlode/Camptonville To Groveland, Mountains Southwest Shasta County To Northern Lake County, Mt Shasta/Western Plumas County, Northeast Foothills/Sacramento Valley, Northern Sacramento Valley, Shasta Lake/North Shasta County, West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A cold snap across the area kept much of the valley overnight temperatures below freezing for the first week of December. This was followed by a low pressure system that brought additional cold weather, with very low elevation snow (300-500ft). The snow was significant due to its rarity at the lower elevations, as well as a temporary closures of I-5 in Shasta County and trans-Sierra I-80. Details: The cold, low elevation snow system brought 4 to 12 inches of snow to the foothills. Shingletown received 5-8 inches of snow, and near Brush Creek received 12 inches. Magalia received around 7 inches. The cold, low elevation snow system brought snow to western Plumas and Lassen Park area for several hours. The slopes received approximately 6 to 10 inches of snow, with highest amounts over the Lassen Peak region (18-22). Quincy and Chester received 4-6 inches of snow along the east side of the crest. The cold, low elevation snow system only brought around 4 inches to the city of Burney, with locally higher amounts for the higher elevations, as the system spread from northwest to southeast across interior northern California.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Dec 16, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from December 16, 2013 to December 16, 2013. Affected areas: Brooks, Kenedy. Episode summary: Clear, calm, and dry conditions set the state for radiational cooling of the ground and surfaces just above the ground overnight and through the early morning hours of Monday, December 16th. A cold front came through the region on December 14th. Afternoon humidity around 20 to 25 percent on December 15th with dew points in the low to mid 20s combined with the calm winds to allow temperatures to plummet after sunset; reading were in the mid to highs 30s at or before midnight. After midnight, temperatures dropped to or below freezing across large portions of Kenedy and Brooks counties. The Falfurrias COOP site in Brooks County reported a low of 26 degrees, while in Kenedy County, the Sarita COOP site reported a low of 28 degrees and the Armstrong COOP site reported a low of 29 degrees. Decent moisture still near the top of the soil, left behind from the rains of November and held in place by a cool second week of December, aided frost development. Episode summary: With a very cold atmosphere already in place, an upper level storm system moved out of the Texas Hill Country and into Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas and Northwest Louisiana during the afternoon hours of February 11th. Precipitation became widespread across the region late in the afternoon and especially during the overnight hours of February 11th and the 12th. During the onset of precipitation, a mixture of rain and sleet was the predominant precipitation type with some sleet accumulations near one quarter of an inch across portions of Northeast Texas. During the evening and overnight hours of the event, the transition turned to predominantly freezing rain with ice accumulations mainly less than one quarter of an inch across Northeast Texas. Impacts included several automobile accidents that occurred from icing in elevated bridges and overpasses as well as isolated power outages from ice accumulating on limbs which fell across powerlines.

The large wildfire consumed an estimated six hundred acres which threatened four homes and ten other structures. However, no structures were damaged or lost. There were also no reports of injuries or fatalities but there was one near miss. The cause of the wildfire was determined to be from downed power lines. A total of thirteen fire departments and other fire agencies responded to the wildfire including the National Park Service, personnel from the Crutch Ranch and the Big Creek Ranch, a Texas Department of Public Safety helicopter, a privately owned helicopter which spotted for the fire fighters and a third helicopter which performed water drops along with crews from Spearman, Gruver, Skellytown, Stinnett, Fritch and Borger. The wildfire was contained around 2000CST.

In Lubbock, light freezing rain resulted in some hazardous travel. Several mostly minor vehicle accidents occurred along access ramps to Interstate 27, especially near 19th Street. One of these accidents resulted in two serious injuries. Farther northwest, colder air aloft resulted in light snow accumulations of 1 to 1.5 inches in parts of Bailey, Parmer, Castro, Lamb, and Swisher Counties. In parts of Cottle County, elevated instability created a few thunderstorms with freezing rain before noon CST; however, area roads were not adversely affected. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Winter Storm: Texas, Mar 02, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, from March 02, 2014 to March 02, 2014. Affected areas: Bowie, Camp, Franklin, Gregg, Morris, Red River, Smith, Titus, Upshur, Wood. Episode summary: An arctic cold front moved through the region during the morning hours of March 2nd. An upper level disturbance trailed the cold front and as a result, strong lift resulted in the development of post frontal convection. Surface temperatures slowly fell throughout the day with temperatures reaching the freezing mark by early afternoon across portions of the region. Temperatures cooled enough in the lower levels of the atmosphere such that freezing rain transitioned over to sleet across much of the area. Given the convective nature of some of the precipitation, widespread sleet accumulations of one half to one inch were reported. There were some isolated areas with total sleet accumulations near 2 inches. Further east where temperatures were not cold enough aloft for sleet, freezing rain was the dominant precipitation type accumulations near one quarter to one half inch. The freezing rain and sleet accumulations resulted in numerous automobile accidents along with power outages from falling limbs and trees throughout the northern half of Northeast Texas.

title: Coastal Flood, High Wind: California, Jan 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Coastal Flood, High Wind, from January 30, 2014 to January 30, 2014. Affected areas: Apple And Lucerne Valleys, Coachella Valley, San Diego County Coastal Areas. Episode summary: A trough of low pressure moving across central California brought strong west winds to the mountains and deserts from the evening of the 30th through the morning of the 31st. Sustained winds of 25 to 35 mph and gusts to 60 mph...locally higher were observed. Burns Canyon in the upper desert and Sky Valley in the Coachella Valley were the big hot spots. In addition, high astronomical tides and elevated surf due to the storm resulted in minor coastal flooding near Imperial Beach in San Diego County, closing a couple streets. Details: High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 0851-0951 PST on the 30th and ended between 1851-1951 PST that evening. During this period, winds were sustained over 40 mph with gusts over 65 mph, and several in the 80s. A peak gust of 85 mph was recorded between 1751-1851 PST. High winds began at the Sky Valley mesonet between 1611-1616 PST on the 30th and ended between 2026-2031 PST that evening. During this period, winds were sustained over 40 mph with gusts over 65 mph, and several in the 70s. A peak gust of 88 mph was recorded twice between 1906-1906 PST. Minor coastal flooding occurred due to a combination of high astronomical tides and elevated surf. This resulted in Descanso street at South Seacoast Drive being shut down. Cortez Avenue and Palm Avenue also had minor flooding. Tides peaked at 7.7 feet at 0800 PST on the 30th, according to the San Diego tide gauge.

title: Drought: Texas, Jan 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from January 01, 2014 to January 31, 2014. Episode summary: The month of January was another dry month for most of the Texas Panhandle, with only 2 or 3 light snowfalls being reported across the far northern parts of the Panhandle. As short term precipitation deficits worsened, drought conditions returned to the eastern Texas Panhandle. Severe (D2) to Exceptional (D4) Drought conditions continued in the western Texas Panhandle. The eastern half of the Texas Panhandle remained below Severe (D2) Drought rating. Winter wheat was in mostly fair to good condition during the month according to reports received by the Texas A&M Agrilife Program, but dryland planted wheat had very poor growth. Upper soil zones remained drier than normal in the Texas Panhandle but were driest across the southern and eastern parts. Deeper soil zones ranged from less than 30 to around 50 percent of normal in the western Texas Panhandle, but values of 110 to 150 percent of normal were scattered across the Texas Panhandle. The Palmer Drought Severity Index worsened to a rating of Severe Drought conditions for the Texas Panhandle. text: conditions for the Texas Panhandle. title: Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from January 23, 2014 to January 24, 2014. Affected areas: Kimble, Mason, Mcculloch, Menard, San Saba. Episode summary: Some light wintry precipitation occurred on January 23. A mix of light sleet and snow occurred across the area southeast of a Menard to Brady to Junction line, with less than a tenth of an inch of accumulation. Details: Light sleet was reported in Brady at 333 PM CST and by 554 PM CST, numerous accidents were reported in Brady. A trained spotter estimated an 1/8 inch of sleet about 7 miles north of Brady at 555 PM CST. Light sleet was reported one mile south of San Saba at 335 PM CST and by 558 PM CST, sleet and snow covered grassy areas and sidewalks. By 808 PM, a National Weather Service Cooperative Observer located 7 miles northwest of San Saba measured half an inch of snow. Light sleet was reported in Mason at 558 PM CST and about a tenth of an inch sleet and snow was estimated by 340 AM CST. Roads were also slippery.

title: Drought: Texas, Jan 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from January 01, 2014 to January 31, 2014. Affected areas: Archer, Baylor, Clay, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: With little to no precipitation through the month, the long term drought kept its grip on western north Texas. Details: With little to no rainfall during the unusually cool month of January, D3(extreme) to D4(Exceptional) drought prevailed across the county. With little to no rainfall during the unusually cool month of January, D2(severe) drought prevailed over much of the county, with D3(extreme) to D4(exceptional) drought over the northern third of the county. title: Winter Weather: California, Jan 29, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from January 29, 2014 to January 31, 2014. Affected areas: West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A Pacific storm brought the first significant precipitation across the area since early December. Main precipitation fell Wednesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon. Details: A Pacific storm brought snowfall to the Sierra Nevada Wednesday morning through Friday morning. By Thursday morning, ski resorts (7000-8500 ft elevation) reported 4 to 6 inches of snow, with locally higher amounts on their peaks up to 8 inches. By Friday morning, the ski resorts reported 8 to 16 inches of snow from the entire storm total.

title: Heavy Snow: Texas, Mar 16, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, from March 16, 2014 to March 16, 2014. Affected areas: Davis / Apache Mountains Area. Episode summary: A shortwave trough closed off as it translated southward over New Mexico and resulted in snowfall in the higher elevations of the Davis Mountains in West Texas. Details: A trained spotter reported 7.5 inches of snowfall at McDonald Observatory. A trained spotter reported 3 inches of snowfall at the Davis Mountains Resort, 11 miles west of Fort Davis. Elevation is 5985 feet.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 06, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from February 06, 2014 to February 06, 2014. Affected areas: Bastrop, Fayette, Guadalupe. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance moved across South Central Texas during the morning hours of February 6. Isentropic upglide of warm moist air over a cold airmass at the surface led to freezing drizzle, light freezing rain, sleet, and snow flurries across the area. The first report of sleet was at 3:15 am in Bexar county. Winter weather spread across central and eastern portions of the region through the morning hours. Icy conditions on roadways caused accidents near Smithville. Icy conditions were also observed on bridges, overpasses, and intersections elsewhere in Bastrop County, along I-10 near Flatonia in Fayette County, and on the bridges over the Guadalupe River in Guadalupe County. The last report of winter weather was of snow flurries at 10:49 am in Burnet. Details: Icy conditions on roadways caused accidents near Smithville. Icy conditions were also observed on bridges, overpasses, and intersections elsewhere in Bastrop county. There were icy conditions at I-10 near Flatonia. There were icy bridges over the Guadalupe River.

title: Winter Storm: Texas, Jan 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, from January 23, 2014 to January 24, 2014. Affected areas: Austin, Fort Bend, Grimes, Harris, Houston, Liberty, Madison, Montgomery, Polk, San Jacinto, Trinity, Walker and 2 more areas. Episode summary: Snow totals between 1 and 4 inches and some freezing rain was produced by a storm system that moved across the area during the late night and morning hours. Freezing rain produced significant icing on bridges and overpasses with several road closures in and around the Houston area and numerous accidents. Details: Around a tenth of an inch of ice formed on bridges and overpasses from freezing rain and some sleet. The icing caused numerous accidents. Many major routes around Houston were closed due to icy conditions. Around a tenth of an inch of ice formed on bridges and overpasses from freezing rain and some sleet. Between 2 and 4 inches of snow across the county, especially from Livingston to Onalaska.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Jan 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from January 03, 2014 to January 03, 2014. Affected areas: Brooks, Hidalgo, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Zapata. Episode summary: A cold front pushed across the Rio Grande Valley and Deep South Texas on the morning of January 2nd. Behind the front, drier and much colder air filtered into the region. The combination of a surface ridge overhead, combined with light winds and clear skies allowed for good radiational cooling to occur, resulting in a light freeze across the northern and western ranchlands early on January 3rd. Details: After 1 am, temperatures dropped below freezing across Hidalgo County and remained at or below freezing for nearly 7 hours. The RAWS site at the Santa Ana Wildlife Refuge reported a low of 30 degrees, while the RAWS site at Linn/San Manuel reported a low of 31 degrees. The Co-Op observers in San Manuel and McCook both reported lows of 32 degrees. Temperatures dropped to or just below freezing across Kenedy County during the early morning and remained there for several hours. A Co-Op observer in Armstrong recorded a low of 31 degrees. Temperatures dropped to or just below freezing across Brooks County during the early morning and remained there for several hours. A Co-Op observer in Falfurrias recorded a low of 31 degrees.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Jan 06, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from January 06, 2014 to January 07, 2014. Affected areas: Brooks, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Zapata. Episode summary: A cold front surged across the Rio Grande Valley and Deep South Texas late January 5th and early January 6th, bringing the tail of a frigid air mass nudged into the area. A weakening upper level disturbance approached the region as cold air funneled into the Valley and produced a thick cloud layer that kept daytime temperatures in the 30s and 40s. Temperatures fell to or just below freezing across the ranchlands during the late night and early morning hours of January 7th. Details: Around 1 am, temperatures dropped to freezing across Zapata County for around 7 hours. A low of 32 degrees was recorded at the Co-Op site in Escobas. Temperatures dropped to or just below freezing across Jim Hogg County late in the evening on January 6th and remained there until the morning of January 7th, for a total of nearly 13 hours. The Hebbronville RAWS site recorded a low of 30 degrees and the Hebbronville AWOS site reported a low of 31 degrees. Around 1 am,temperatures dropped to or below freezing across Brooks County for almost 7 hours. A Co-Op observer in Falfurrias recorded a low of 31 degrees.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Jan 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from January 14, 2014 to January 14, 2014. Affected areas: Starr, Zapata. Episode summary: A Pacific cold front pushed across the Rio Grande Valley and Deep South Texas during the day, January 13th. Behind the front, drier and colder air filtered into the region. Light winds and clear skies allowed for good radiational cooling to occur, resulting in a light freeze across Zapata and Starr counties early on January 14th. Details: During the early morning hours of January 14th, temperatures dropped to freezing across Zapata County for around 3 hours. A low of 32 degrees was recorded at the AWOS site in Zapata. During the early morning hours of January 14th, temperatures dropped to or just below freezing across Starr County for approximately 3 hours. The Falcon Dam Co-Op site recorded a low of 30 degrees.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Jan 22, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from January 22, 2014 to January 22, 2014. Affected areas: Brooks, Hidalgo, Kenedy, Starr, Willacy, Zapata. Episode summary: A cold front pushed across Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley during the early morning hours of January 21st. High pressure in the wake of the front, combined with mostly clear skies and light overnight winds to allow for good radiational cooling on the morning of January 22nd. A large portion of the region had temperatures fall to or below freezing for a number of hours. Details: During the early morning hours of January 22nd, temperatures dropped to or just below freezing across Starr County for 5 hours. The Falcon Lake RAWS site recorded a low of 29 degrees. After midnight, temperatures dropped to or just below freezing across northern Hidalgo County for 8 hours. The Linn/San Manuel RAWS site recorded a low of 31 degrees. Sheltered locations within the more populated sections of the county, including Weslaco/Donna, San Juan, and Edinburg (among others), had several hours of frost that required scraping of the windshield according to several visitors During the early morning, temperatures dropped to or below freezing across Brooks County for nearly 4 hours. A Co-Op observer in Falfurrias recorded a low of 26 degrees.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Jan 24, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from January 24, 2014 to January 24, 2014. Affected areas: Brooks, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Willacy, Zapata. Episode summary: An arctic front sliced across the Deep South Texas ranchlands and the Rio Grande Valley during the evening of January 23rd, sending temperatures plummeting from the upper 70s into the lower 40s in a matter of 3 to 4 hours after sunset. By midnight, temperatures had fallen into the 30s and would result in a light freeze across the ranchlands a few hours later, starting generally around 3 AM on the 24th. Details: Temperatures dropped to or just below freezing across Brooks County during the early morning hours. A Co-Op observer in Falfurrias recorded a low of 31 degrees. After 5 am, temperatures dropped to or below freezing across Zapata County for around six and a half hours. A low of 32 degrees was recorded at the AWOS site in Zapata and a low of 31 degrees was reported by the Co-Op observer in Escobas. Temperatures dropped to or just below freezing across Jim Hogg County for over 15 hours. The Hebbronville RAWS site recorded a low of 29 degrees and the Hebbronville AWOS site reported a low of 30 degrees.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Jan 25, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from January 25, 2014 to January 25, 2014. Affected areas: Brooks, Jim Hogg, Kenedy, Zapata. Episode summary: Surface high pressure behind the front on the 24th settled over the Rio Grande Valley and Deep South Texas decreasing winds allowing drier air to filter into the area. The cirrus deck in place over the region slowly eroded away during the night from the west to the east and allowing temperatures to fall to or below freezing on the 25th once the skies cleared. Details: Temperatures dropped to or below freezing across Zapata County for approximately 7 hours. A low of 29 degrees was recorded at the AWOS site in Zapata and a low of 30 degrees was reported by the Co-Op observer in Escobas. Temperatures dropped to or below freezing across Brooks County for over 8 hours. A Co-Op observer in Falfurrias recorded a low of 30 degrees.

title: Strong Wind: Texas, Jan 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, from January 23, 2014 to January 24, 2014. Affected areas: Coastal Cameron, Hidalgo. Episode summary: The combination of a sharp surge of cold air and a trough of low pressure across the western Gulf of Mexico brought strong and gusty winds across the Lower and Mid Rio Grande Valley during the evening of January 23rd in Hidalgo County, and during the morning of January 24th close to the Cameron County coast. title: High Wind: California, Jan 09, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from January 09, 2014 to January 10, 2014. Affected areas: Santa Barbara County Mountains, Santa Barbara County South Coast. Episode summary: A strong northerly pressure gradient generated gusty Sundowner winds across southern sections of Santa Barbara county. The strongest winds were reported around the community of Montecito. Details: Strong northerly winds developed across southern Santa Barbara county. The RAWS sensor at Montecito reported sustained winds between 40 and 51 MPH with gusts between 59 and 66 MPH.

title: High Wind: California, Jan 13, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from January 13, 2014 to January 15, 2014. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: Strong surface high pressure over the Great Basin generated gusty Santa Ana winds across sections of Ventura and Los Angeles counties. The strongest winds were reported in the mountains with gusts in excess of 65 MPH. Details: Strong northeasterly winds developed across the mountains of Los Angeles county. The RAWS sensor at Camp Nine reported gusts between 60 and 66 MPH while the RAWS sensor at Chilao reported gusts between 59 and 69 MPH. Strong northeasterly winds developed across the mountains of Ventura county. Wind gusts in excess of 60 MPH were reported in some areas. Strong northeast winds developed across the Santa Monica Mountains. An automated sensor at Laguna Peak reported wind gusts as high as 75 MPH. The RAWS sensor at Malibu Hills reported wind gusts between 58 and 65 MPH.

title: Wildfire: California, Jan 16, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from January 16, 2014 to January 25, 2014. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Los Angeles County San Gabriel Valley. Episode summary: The Colby Wildfire started in the hills above the San Gabriel Valley. The fire was fueled by the combination of an extended period of dry, northeast winds and very dry vegetation. The fire destroyed 5 homes and burned 1,952 acres. Details: The Colby Wildfire burned 1,952 acres of land in the hills above the San Gabriel Valley. The fire was started by an illegal campfire and it destroyed 5 homes.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 28, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from January 28, 2014 to January 28, 2014. Affected areas: Brazoria, Brazos, Burleson, Harris, Montgomery, Polk, Walker, Waller. Episode summary: The second winter weather event in four days was felt across almost all of southeast Texas except along the coast as an upper level disturbance moved across the area with temperatures near freezing. Although some light icing was observed across the area, there was little accumulation. Details: Across the county, light sleet was observed with glaze accumulation on vehicles. A mix of light snow, sleet and freezing rain with little accumulation was observed across the county. There was some ice on vehicles, and only a couple of bridges and roads were briefly closed due to their higher elevation. Freezing rain was observed across the county, especially in and around the Conroe area, but there were no reported road closures due to little accumulation.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from January 23, 2014 to January 24, 2014. Affected areas: Bell. Episode summary: Cold arctic air and modest amounts of moisture resulted in light freezing rain, sleet and snow over southern portions of North Texas. Slick roads resulting from the wintry precipitation caused several accidents. Details: Several vehicles became stuck on icy roads and bridges. Northbound I-35 traffic came to a stop where tractor trailers could not make it up the incline.

title: Strong Wind: California, Jan 05, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, from January 05, 2014 to January 08, 2014. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns, Se S.J. Valley. Episode summary: January began with an upper-level ridge of high pressure over the central California interior. This ridge persisted over the region for much of the first two-thirds of the month, with high temperatures several degrees above normal. The ridge kept a dry airmass in place, resulting in very low relative humidities in the mountains and foothills. For the first time in memory, Red Flag Warnings were issued for the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains in January.||An offshore wind pattern developed over the central California interior on January 5th. Gusty southeast winds funneled through the Grapevine into the far south end of the San Joaquin Valley on the 5th, and again on the 8th of January. A gust to 57 mph was recorded at the base of the Grapevine on January 5th. Gusts to around 45 mph were reported at Bird Spring Pass and near Mojave during the early morning hours of January 8th. Reported property and crop damage: about $4,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, High Wind, from January 23, 2014 to January 24, 2014. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley. Episode summary: One consequence of the dry airmass was that despite the unseasonably warm afternoon high temperatures, strong radiational cooling allowed overnight lows to fall to near normal. title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 10, 2014 to March 10, 2014. Affected areas: Randall. Episode summary: The East Complex Wildfire began around 1326CST in Randall county about twelve miles south southeast of Canyon Texas near Farm to Market Road 285 (Wayside Road) and between U.S. Highway 87 and Interstate 27. The wildfire consumed an estimated six hundred and forty acres and was caused by burning debris. There were no structures damaged or lost and there were no reports of injuries or fatalities. The wildfire was contained around 1600CST and a total of three fire departments responded to the wildfire including the Texas Forest Service.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 18, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 18, 2014 to March 19, 2014. Affected areas: Lipscomb. Episode summary: The Higgins Wildfire began around 1230CST around 7 miles west southwest of Higgins Texas or between Higgins and Glazier off of U.S. Highway 60 in Lipscomb county and spread eastward into Oklahoma. The wildfire consumed an estimated twenty-nine thousand six hundred and eleven acres. There were two homes and four outbuildings which were destroyed. However, there were no reports of injuries or fatalities. The two homes destroyed were not occupied and one of the houses was apparently abandoned and the other had just been renovated. There were also fifteen rural homes which were evacuated during the wildfire. The exact cause of the wildfire remains under investigation and the wildfire was contained around 0100CST on March 19th. There were close to thirty fire departments responded to the wildfire. Reported property and crop damage: about $190,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Mar 29, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from March 29, 2014 to March 29, 2014. Affected areas: Dallam. Episode summary: The Kerrick Wildfire began approximately 1418CST about ten miles southwest of Griggs Oklahoma in extreme northeastern Dallam county Texas. The wildfire started just west of U.S. Highway 287 near Farm to Market Road 807 and consumed an estimated five acres. The wildfire destroyed two homes and three outbuildings. There was one home which was damaged. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities. The cause of the wildfire was determined to be from burning tumbleweeds in some horse pens that got out of control. There were a total of twelve fire departments or other fire agencies that responded to the wildfire including the Stratford Volunteer Fire Department, the Boise City Fire Department, Griggs Fire Department, and the Keyes Fire Department. The wildfire was contained around 1930CST to 20000CST. Reported property and crop damage: about $340,000.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Apr 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from April 03, 2014 to April 04, 2014. Affected areas: Barron, Polk, Rusk, St. Croix. Episode summary: A winter storm developed across the Central Plains Thursday morning, April 3rd. Initially, warm air brought areas of light rain, sleet, and snow across portions of east central Minnesota and west central Wisconsin during the morning and early afternoon. This area of precipitation quickly moved northward into Lake Superior, and another area of precipitation developed across northwest Iowa, spread northeast across southwest and south central Minnesota during the afternoon hours, then encompassed most of west central Wisconsin by the evening. The precipitation quickly became more sleet and snow as colder air moved into the region. Eventually all of the precipitation moved east of the area by the afternoon of Friday, April 4th. ||Some of the higher snowfall totals from Wisconsin include;|10.0 inches in Haugen, in Barron County. |9.0 inches in Baldwin, in St. Croix County. |9.0 inches in Cumberland, in Barron County. Episode summary: The last in a series of cold fronts drove shallow, Canadian air into the region February 11th. Skies cleared across portions of the Valley early on the 12th. Temperatures dropped a few degrees from their overnight values in the upper 30s to around 40 and slipped to or below freezing across ranchlands and brush country. Details: Temperatures fell below freezing during the early morning hours of February 12th. The COOP observer in Sarita reported a low of 29 degrees and the COOP observer in Armstrong reported a low of 31 degrees. Temperatures fell below freezing during the early morning hours of February 12th. The RAWS site in Hebbronville reported a low of 32 degrees. Temperatures fell below freezing across Zapata County during the early morning hours of February 12th. The ASOS site in Zapata recorded a low of 30 degrees and the COOP observer in Escobas reported a low of 29 degrees.

title: Ice Storm, Winter Weather: Texas, Mar 04, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, Winter Weather, from March 04, 2014 to March 04, 2014. Affected areas: Hardin, Jefferson, Northern Jasper, Northern Newton, Orange, Southern Jasper, Southern Newton, Tyler. Episode summary: A cold air mass swept back into Southeast Texas early in March. While the cold Canadian air was in place an upper level disturbance moved across the region causing yet another round of wintery precipitation that began early in the morning on the 4th. Temperatures warmed during the mid day to early afternoon hours as rain moved out of the region. Details: Temperatures slowly fell to freezing across most of Orange County before sunrise while rain was occurring. This produced around one tenth of an inch of ice accumulation over most of the county except for along Sabine Lake were temperatures just briefly touched freezing. No ice related closures were reported. Freezing rain began early in the morning of the 4th with around one quarter of an inch of ice accumulating around sunrise. Travel was not greatly impacted, however several trees were reported down across the county with some falling onto roadways. Freezing rain began early in the morning of the 4th with around one quarter of an inch to three tenths of ice accumulating around sunrise or shortly after. Travel was not greatly impacted, however several trees were reported down. Ice melted during the afternoon as temperature rose above freezing. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, High Wind: California, Feb 28, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, High Wind, from February 28, 2014 to February 28, 2014. Affected areas: Apple And Lucerne Valleys, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Bernardino And Riverside County Valleys - The Inland Empire, San Diego, San Diego County Mountains, Santa Ana Mountains And Foothills. Episode summary: A weak, upper-level trough moved through California overnight on February 26th, into the morning of the 27th, increasing gusty west winds and bringing a round of light to moderate showers over and west of the mountains. A much stronger, Pacific low pressure system took aim at southern California late on the 27th, bringing periods of heavy rain and high-elevation mountain snow through the 28th (with additional heavy rain through March 1). Most of the upslope rain and convective showers occurred on the 28th. Strong, long-duration upslope flow enhanced rainfall on southwest-facing coastal slopes. The four-day, storm total precipitation amounts were significant. Costal locations ranged from 1 to 3 inches of rain, with the valleys recording up to 4.5 inches toward the coastal slopes. Mountain locations varied widely depending on slope aspect, but most recorded between 3 and 8 inches of rain. The upper deserts recorded between one-tenth and one-half inch, while the lower deserts measured generally less than one-tenth of an inch. The notable exceptions were Palm Springs, Desert Hot Springs in the Coachella Valley and San Felipe in San Diego County, all of which measured between one-half of an inch and one inch. The big rainfall winners were along the southern slopes of the San Bernardino County mountains, with Yucaipa Ridge coming in at 11.11 inches, Lytle Creek with 9.67 inches and Cedar Glen with 9.10 inches. The snow level remained fairly high, around 6000 feet. Most locations saw between 2 and 7 inches of snow, with

title: Drought: Texas, Feb 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from February 01, 2014 to February 28, 2014. Affected areas: Palo Pinto, Young. Episode summary: Young and Palo Pinto County began and ended the month in severe drought (D2). Very little rain fell across North Texas during the month of February which allowed for no improvement in drought conditions. Surrounding areas were in moderate drought (D1) throughout the month. Details: According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, the county remained in severe drought (D2) throughout the month. Less than an inch of rain fell during February and there were no improvements. Reported property and crop damage: about $4,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Feb 25, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from February 25, 2014 to February 28, 2014. Affected areas: Bell, Coryell, Dallas, Fannin, Hood, Hunt, Johnson, Lamar, Lampasas, Somervell, Tarrant. Episode summary: Very little rain fell during the month of February and many counties in North Texas experienced worsening drought conditions. Moderate drought (D1) deteriorated to severe drought (D2) by the 25th of the month across the central portions of the Fort Worth County Warning Area. Details: According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, the county began the month in moderate drought (D1) but ended the month in severe drought (D2). Less than an inch of rain fell during February and which allowed for the drought conditions to deteriorate. Reported property and crop damage: about $11,000.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Apr 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from April 14, 2014 to April 15, 2014. Affected areas: Milwaukee, Waukesha. Episode summary: A Polar trough brought a narrow north to south band of light snow that slowly moved east across southeast Wisconsin. The air and road temperatures, which were above freezing during the day and early evening, cooled below freezing with icy roads quickly developing. Dozens of slide-offs and accidents occurred including a 30-vehicle pileup on highway 45 in Wauwatosa. This was the last winter weather event that occurred in spring. Due to the very cold and snowy cold season, the Wisconsin Department of Transportation is requesting $27.3 million from the state legislature to cover the counties costs of additional salt and plowing. The $27.3 million is the total for the entire state of Wisconsin. Details: Air and road temperatures cooled below freezing during the evening as light snow was occurring. Wet roads quickly become icy and dozens of slide-offs and accidents occurred. Portions of I-43 and I-94 were shut down due to the accidents. No serious injuries were reported. Air and road temperatures cooled below freezing during the evening as light snow was occurring. Wet roads quickly become icy and dozens of slide-offs and accidents occurred. A 30 car pileup, which included two trucks and two buses, occurred on highway 45 in Wauwatosa. Only one injury was reported.

title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, Apr 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from April 12, 2014 to April 13, 2014. Affected areas: Sauk. Episode summary: A strong stationary front with a 40 degree temperature gradient setup along the Wisconsin and Illinois border. Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms developed and moved east to northeast across southern Wisconsin. Dozens of hail reports were received with only a couple wind damage reports. Heavy rain lead to flash flooding of small creeks in southern Sauk County. Details: Numerous roads were closed over southern Sauk County due to flash flooding of small creeks and streams. Estimated rainfall amounts ranged from 4-7 inches. Some of the known creeks that flooded were Otter Creek, Honey Creek, North Branch of Honey Creek, and Pine Creek. title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 06, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 06, 2014 to April 06, 2014. Affected areas: Gregg, Smith. Episode summary: A deep upper level trough located across New Mexico and the Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles slowly moved northeast towards the region on April 6th. Southwest flow dominated the region ahead of the upper level trough which allowed for copious amounts of Pacific and Gulf of Mexico Moisture to ride up and over a stalled frontal boundary along the Southeast Texas and the Southern Louisiana Gulf Coast. Elevated instability and strong lapse rates aloft resulted in the development of large hail initially on the 6th but as the day went on, training of cells resulted in some wind damage with widespread flooding noted across portions of the region as well. Heavy rainfall of 4 to near 6 inches was reported in portions of Gregg and Smith Counties in Northeast Texas with this event. Details: Excessive heavy rainfall resulted in the closure of Hwy. 80 between Ward and Rockwall Streets from flash flooding. Excessive heavy rainfall resulted in several street closures in the south portion of Tyler, Texas. Widespread street flooding reported at New Copeland Road on the south side of Tyler. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Feb 17, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from February 17, 2014 to February 17, 2014. Affected areas: Brown, Calumet, Door, Kewaunee, Manitowoc, Outagamie, Portage, Waupaca, Waushara, Winnebago, Wood. Episode summary: A fast-moving weather system dropped 5 to 7 inches of snow in 12 hours across central and east central Wisconsin as it moved across the state. The highest snowfall totals included 7.8 inches in Chilton (Calumet Co.), 7.5 inches in Ephraim (Door Co.), and 7.2 inches in Cleveland (Manitowoc Co.). Details: Snowfall totals across Wood County were mostly around 6 inches. The highest total was 6.3 inches at Wisconsin Rapids. Snowfall totals across Portage County were mostly in the 4 to 6 inch range. The highest total was 6.1 inches at Amherst. The highest reported snowfall total in Waupaca County was 6.5 inches at Clintonville.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Feb 20, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from February 20, 2014 to February 21, 2014. Affected areas: Forest, Langlade, Lincoln, Marathon, Oneida, Vilas. Episode summary: Low pressure moved across Wisconsin and rapidly deepened. Heavy snow and high winds, accompanied by thunderstorms at times, affected much of northwest and north central Wisconsin. The snow combined with the high winds to cause considerable blowing and drifting snow. The heaviest snowfall totals in north central Wisconsin included 13.0 inches at Winchester (Vilas Co.) and 8.0 inches at Minocqua (Oneida Co.). Details: The heaviest snowfall in Vilas County was in the far northwest where Winchester received a storm total of 13.0 inches. The highest reported snowfall total in Oneida County was 8.0 inches at Minocqua. Snowfall estimated in the 6 to 8 inch range fell across parts of the county.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 20, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 20, 2014 to April 20, 2014. Affected areas: Childress. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms ignited early on the afternoon of the 20th across the southern Texas Panhandle as a slow-moving upper trough encountered moderate instability east of a weak dryline. The most intense thunderstorms, including a few supercells, developed in Hall and Childress Counties. These supercells produced several reports of large hail, some up to baseball size in the city of Childress where numerous vehicles and buildings suffered various degrees of damage. One of these supercells produced a very brief and small tornado east of Childress over open land. Additionally, these slow-moving storms dropped torrential rain that at one point was measured as great as 6 inches per hour by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet station. Minor flooding was common in and around Childress where up to 3.25 inches of rain fell. By early evening, additional supercells developed south into the Rolling Plains near Paducah and Guthrie, but reports of severe weather were unavailable in these remote areas. Details: Storm chasers observed a brief tornado over open land.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 13, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 13, 2014 to April 13, 2014. Affected areas: Camp. Episode summary: An upper level trough moved out of the Texas Hill Country and towards the region during the afternoon hours of April 13th. Thunderstorms developed well in advance of the trough across the region and these thunderstorms developed under the influence of relatively weak instability but strong low level and deep layer shear. The result was a small, yet potent tornado that touched down just north of Pittsburg, Texas in Camp County. Details: NWS conducted a storm survey in Camp County and determined that a weak EF0 tornado touched down just north of Pittsburg, Texas. This storm damaged a few businesses along Hwy. 271. A number of billboard signs were damaged and a few businesses sustained roof damage and wall damage. A local bank was able to capture video of the small tornado with its outside security camera. title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2014 to March 11, 2014. Affected areas: Aransas, Bee, Calhoun, Goliad, Jim Wells, Live Oak, Nueces, Refugio, San Patricio, Victoria. Episode summary: Above to well above normal rainfall occurred across all of South Texas during the month of March. Rainfall amounts were 2 to 3 inches above normal from the eastern Brush Country into the Coastal Bend and Victoria Crossroads. Some areas in Jim Wells, Duval, and Live Oak Counties received between 4 and 5 inches during the month. Rainfall amounts were 1 to 2 inches above normal over the western Brush Country also. This beneficial rainfall improved the soil moisture conditions over South Texas. The severe to extreme drought conditions over the coastal plains improved to moderate by the middle of the month. Details: Drought conditions improved to moderate levels.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from February 10, 2014 to February 10, 2014. Affected areas: Carson, Hutchinson, Potter, Randall. Episode summary: A very rare weather phenomenon occurred during the day of the 10th and brought one to four inches of snow to the south central Texas Panhandle. A cold and saturated air mass was already in place, with freezing fog and light flurries ongoing. Steam being released from several local industrial power plants provided additional moisture and condensation nuclei which enhanced snowfall. Narrow bands of enhanced snow production produced 3 to 4 inches of snow across and south of the city of Borger (Hutchinson and Carson counties) and 1 to 2 inches across the city of Amarillo (Randall and Potter counties). The enhanced snowfall ended by the early afternoon as steam production at the power plants diminished. Details: One to two inches of snow at NWS Office. One to two inches of snow on southwest side of town. Three to four inches of snow on southwest side of Borger.

title: Cold/Wind Chill: Texas, Feb 06, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Cold/Wind Chill, from February 06, 2014 to February 07, 2014. Affected areas: Armstrong, Carson, Collingsworth, Donley, Gray, Hansford, Hemphill, Hutchinson, Lipscomb, Moore, Ochiltree, Potter and 4 more areas. Episode summary: Surface temperatures dropped into the single digits across most of the Texas Panhandle during the early evening hours of the 6th and persisted until the late morning hours of the 7th. These sub-freezing temperatures coupled with southerly winds of 15 to 20 mph to drop wind chill values into the minus 5 degrees to minus 12 degrees. These dangerous wind chill values improved during the late morning hours of the 7th as ambient temperatures warmed into the lower 20s. title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 07, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from February 07, 2014 to February 07, 2014. Affected areas: Bandera, Bexar, Gillespie, Uvalde, Williamson. Episode summary: Southerly low level winds and an approaching upper level trough allowed warm and moist air to move over a cold airmass at the surface. This lead to freezing drizzle and light freezing rain developing during the early morning hours on February 7. The first report of freezing drizzle was at 2:50 am in Kerr County. Icy roads were reported in several counties. Highway 46 was closed in Bandera County from Highway 16 to I-10. There were numerous accidents in and around Fredericksburg in Gillespie County. In Uvalde County most of the bridges were closed due to ice and an accident was reported on the Highway 90 bridge over the Nueces River. The Shin Oak Dr. bridge over I-35 was closed in Live Oak as were the flyover ramps connecting Highway 281 and Loop 1604 in San Antonio, both of these in Bexar County. There were some accidents on icy bridges around Jarrell in Williamson County. The precipitation transitioned from freezing to liquid during the late morning hours as temperatures warmed above freezing. Details: Texas Department of Transportation reported the closure of TX Highway 46 from Highway 16 to Interstate 10 due to icing. Numerous vehicle accidents were reported in and around Fredericksburg due to ice on roads. Uvalde County Emergency Manager reported that most of the bridges in Uvalde county are iced over.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from February 10, 2014 to February 11, 2014. Affected areas: Dallas, Denton, Tarrant. Episode summary: Freezing drizzle resulted in icy road conditions across the DFW Metroplex. Three people in the region died. Details: A male was killed on Cattlebaron Drive in northwest Tarrant County when he lost control of his vehicle on crashed into a tree. Also, a chain-reaction crash at Collins Street and Green Oaks Blvd involved up to 20 cars. Hundreds of car accidents were reported in the county by the local police and several required medical attention. Many school districts closed or started late on Tuesday the 11th. A high school student was killed in a vehicle crash due to icy roads from freezing drizzle. The accident occurred on FM 156 near Highway 114. Another female student in the car was seriously injured. Parts of University Drive in Denton, Loop 288, Nottingham Drive were closed for sanding Monday evening. A firefighter fell to his death off an icy overpass along Walton Walker Boulevard in southwest Dallas. He was attending responding to a wreck on the bridge and was hit by an oncoming car that was also sliding on the icy bridge. Reported property and crop damage: about $330,000.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 07, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from February 07, 2014 to February 07, 2014. Affected areas: Bell. Episode summary: A teenager died in a vehicle crash on I-35 near Salado caused by icy roads due to freezing drizzle. Details: Icy roads resulted in a vehicle crash that killed a girl along I-35 near mile marker 279 south of Salado. Several icy bridges were reported across the county and at least 55 vehicle wrecks were reported. Some bridges around Temple and Killeen were closed due to icing. Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: Winter Storm: Texas, Feb 02, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, from February 02, 2014 to February 02, 2014. Affected areas: Cooke, Jack, Montague, Young. Episode summary: A mix of freezing rain, sleet, and snow fell across mainly the northwestern counties of the CWA. Locations along and north of a Breckenridge to DFW line received from a Trace to 4 of ice, sleet, and snow accumulations. Other selected totals include 6.25 inches at Ralls (Crosby County), 6.07 inches at Slaton (Lubbock County), 5.80 inches at Floydada (Floyd County), 5.46 inches at Northfield (Motley County), and 5.23 inches at Lubbock Preston Smith International Airport (Lubbock County). The annual total at Lubbock Preston Smith International Airport was only 0.90 inches before Memorial Day weekend. By the end of May, Lubbock was only -0.08 inches below the annual average. Above average temperatures at the beginning of the month nearly evened out with cooler temperatures at the end of the month. The abundant rainfall kept temperatures well below seasonal averages after its occurrence. Lubbock was only 0.4 degrees above normal while Childress was 1.3 degrees above normal. Severe (D2) to Extreme (D3) Drought conditions continued in the western Texas Panhandle. The poor health of range and pasture land lead to concerns for blowing dust if strong winds occurred. title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Apr 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from April 03, 2014 to April 04, 2014. Affected areas: Clark. Episode summary: A late season winter storm hit portions of north central Wisconsin with ice. The coating of ice, up to a quarter of an inch thick, mainly coated elevated exposed surfaces. The icing did create some power outages in Thorp (Clark County). After the freezing rain ended, a period of snow occurred with accumulations of 1 to 2 inches. The highest reported snow total was 1.7 inches near Owen (Clark County). Details: Freezing rain coated elevated, exposed surfaces with up to a quarter inch of ice causing power outages in Thorp. title: Dust Storm: Texas, Mar 27, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Dust Storm, from March 27, 2014 to March 27, 2014. Affected areas: Deaf Smith, Moore, Randall. Episode summary: The combination of persistent drought and gusty southwesterly winds caused isolated dust storm conditions across the southwestern Texas Panhandle during the midday hours of the 27th. Sustained winds of 25 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph followed a surface through which moved across the Texas Panhandle during the late morning hours. By midday reports of less than a quarter mile visibilities were coming in across the southwestern Texas Panhandle. Visibilities were reported as low as an eight of a mile 8 miles west of Hereford (Deaf Smith County), and one mile south of Cactus (Moore County). Visibilities were reduced to a quarter mile near the intersection of 45th Ave and Soncy Road on the southwest side of Amarillo (Randall County). These lowered visibilities caused traffic to slow down; however no reports of vehicle accidents were reported in relation to the dust storm. Details: Visibility reduced to less than a quarter mile one mile south of Cactus. Visibility reduced to less than a quarter mile 8 miles west of Hereford. Visibility reduced to less than a quarter mile at 45th Ave and Soncy Road on the southwest side of Amarillo.

Behind the cold front strong surface winds picked up dust causing lowered visibilities across the Panhandle. Visibilities degraded to less than a quarter mile at: Dalhart (Dallam and County); Stratford (Sherman County); Spearman (Hansford County); Perryton (Ochiltree County); Dumas (Moore County); Borger (Hutchinson County); Miami (Roberts County); Panhandle (Carson County); Pampa (Gray County); Wheeler (Wheeler County); and Amarillo (Potter County). By 6:30 PM CST, the strong winds across the Texas Panhandle weakened and brought an end to dust storm conditions. Details: Less than a quarter mile visibility 11 miles east of Dalhart. Less than a quarter mile visibility in Spearman. Less than a quarter mile visibility 10 miles north Panhandle.

title: Dust Storm: Texas, Mar 15, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Dust Storm, from March 15, 2014 to March 15, 2014. Affected areas: Carson, Hansford, Moore, Ochiltree, Oldham, Potter. Episode summary: A cold front moved through the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandle during the late afternoon hours of the 15th. Many reports of near zero visibility were received from the southwest side of Dumas (Moore County), Perryton (Ochiltree County), Gruver (Hansford County), Pantex (Carson County), and on the north-northwest side of Amarillo (Potter County). These lowered visibilities also caused numerous traffic issues including the closure of State Highway 354 between US Highways 87 and 385 (Moore County), and caused multiple vehicle accidents along Farm to Market Road 1061 near Vega (Oldham County). Visibility improved shortly after 10 PM CST as strong surface winds subsided. Details: Near zero visibility across the county. Quarter mile visibility reported near Pantex. Quarter mile visibility led to multiple vehicle accidents along Farm to Market Road 1061 near Vega. Reported property and crop damage: about $40,000.

title: Flood: California, Mar 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from March 01, 2014 to March 01, 2014. Affected areas: Riverside, San Diego. Episode summary: The strong upper level low pressure system that brought damaging wind and flooding on February 28, continued to produce bands of rain and snow, along with gusty winds through March 1. The majority of the flooding occurred on February 28th, but minor street flooding was still being reported from continued rain on March 1 from Riverside to Vista and San Diego as areas of heavy rain occurred during the morning of March 1st and then was followed by a continuous line of heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms late in the afternoon. Additional rain on March 1 resulted in flooding in Oceanside, Temecula, Sea World San Diego, as well as minor street flooding in Mission Viejo and a few other locations. Road closures remained in effect near Forest Falls due to a major debris flow that occurred the afternoon and evening of February 28th. Numerous power outages continued into the 1st for many residents in the San Bernardino County mountains as well. Up to 8 inches of snow was reported in the San Bernardino County mountains as well. Strong onshore winds combined with a large west-southwest swell to generate high surf along the San Diego and Orange County beaches with strong rip currents on the 1st as well. Details: CHP reported one lane of Interstate 5 had a couple feet of water on the road near the Oceanside Harbor bridge. CHP reports Bridge Street at Gillman Springs Road closed due to flooding from heavy rain.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 09, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 09, 2014 to May 09, 2014. Affected areas: San Augustine. Episode summary: A strong upper level trough moved out of the Texas Hill Country...towards the region during the late morning, afternoon and evening hours of May 9th. Strong instability developed across the region with peak heating and a strong capping inversion initially during the morning broke during the day. Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed in the unstable airmass with large hail and damaging thunderstorm wind gusts the primary result. Some of these storms trained across the same general area...producing copious amounts of rainfall. A Flash Flood Warning was prompted for San Augustine County as a result. title: Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 26, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, Tornado, from May 26, 2014 to May 26, 2014. Affected areas: Crosby, Floyd, Hockley, Lubbock. Episode summary: A slow-moving upper low moved across the Texas Panhandle this afternoon accompanied by a cold pocket aloft. After a fourth consecutive morning of heavy rains across the region, a few hours of clearing in the afternoon resulted in a final bout of thunderstorms; some of which became severe. The strongest of these storms moved from near Levelland and Lubbock east into the southern Rolling Plains accompanied by a downburst and marginally severe hail. A seven-minute EF0 tornado was also spotted by storm chasers in southeast Hockley County this evening. Other than removing a roof extension from a small rural shed, this tornado produced no other damage. The greatest impact by far was more torrential rainfall on top of already saturated soils. The result was widespread flooding of many roads and streets across southern Lubbock, Crosby, Hockley and Floyd Counties. To underscore the intensity of these rains, a Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station near Wolfforth measured an instantaneous hourly rainfall rate of a whopping 10.3 inches. Details: Storm spotters and an off-duty NWS employee observed a seven minute tornado over rural land about seven miles southeast of Levelland. Although this tornado did destroy a small roof extension attached to an outbuilding, the construction of the roof was of low quality and therefore the tornado was assigned an EF0 rating. Reported property and crop damage: about $500.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from April 03, 2014 to April 03, 2014. Affected areas: Collin, Denton, Hopkins, Hunt. Episode summary: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of a dryline moving across the region. These storms were hail producers and mainly affected areas primarily along and north of US 380 from Decatur to Sulphur Springs. The worst damage was done in Denton where hail up to the size of softballs caused close to $5 billion in damage. Three tornadoes also occurred with this system; an EF-0 in Collin County, an EF-0 in Hopkins County, and an EF-1 in Hunt County. Details: A National Weather Service storm survey crew determined a tornado caused EF0 damage to a subdivision in Princeton. The tornado produced damage to a number of homes, along with several fences which were blown down. A National Weather Service storm survey crew determined a long track tornado produced EF1 damage in several spots in Hunt County. The hardest hit home was a ranch for exotic birds and chickens. This tornado produced a non continuous path for nearly 12 miles, producing several pockets of tree and fence damage. A National Weather Service damage survey crew determined a tornado produced EF1 damage in northern Hopkins County, near the city of Birthright. This tornado caused damage to several homes and businesses, including the Birthright Volunteer Fire Department building. A total of 76 houses or businesses were damaged in this tornado. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,815,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, May 11, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 11, 2014 to May 11, 2014. Affected areas: Hutchinson. Episode summary: The North 136 Wildfire began around 0734CST in Hutchinson county about four miles northwest of Stinnett Texas. The wildfire consumed an estimated four hundred and twenty and was caused by downed power lines. There was one home that was threatened but saved and there were no homes or other structures lost. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities. The wildfire was contained around 1330CST and a total of six fire departments and other agencies responded to the wildfire including the Texas A&M Forest Service.

title: Wildfire: Texas, May 11, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 11, 2014 to May 14, 2014. Affected areas: Hutchinson. Episode summary: The Double Diamond Wildfire began around 1520CST in Hutchinson county about two miles northwest of Fritch near the Harbor Bay area of Lake Meredith National Recreational Area. The wildfire consumed an estimated two thousand five hundred and eighty-three acres and was caused by a child playing with matches in an abandoned shed. A total of three hundred and sixty-eight structures were damaged or lost including two hundred and twenty-five homes that were destroyed along with one hundred and forty-three other structures. Also, a total of one hundred and forty-seven vehicles were destroyed. There was one report of a fatality from a heart attack that was indirectly related to the wildfire, however there were no reports of any injuries. The wildfire reportedly cased an estimated ten million or more dollars in property losses. The wildfire was finally contained between 1000CST to 1100CST on May 14. There were a total of thirty-seven fire departments that responded to the wildfire including the Texas A&M Forest Service. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2014 to March 31, 2014. Affected areas: Bandera, Burnet, Edwards, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Llano, Medina, Val Verde. Episode summary: Some of South Central Texas experienced a wet March. Across the southern portion of the region they received above normal rainfall with some places getting 150 to 200 percent of normal. Unfortunately, the north central and northwestern areas had less than 25 percent of normal for the month. With the lack of rainfall Bandera, Burnet, Kerr and Llano Counties worsened to extreme drought category (Stage D3). The rest of the area remained unchanged with Gillespie County in extreme (Stage D3) drought category and Edwards, Kendall, Medina and Val Verde Counties in severe (Stage D2) drought category. Fire danger was moderate to high across the area at the end of March. Of the counties in D2 or worse drought Burnet, Kendall, Kerr, Llano, and Val Verde had burn bans in effect. The seven day stream flow averages at the end of the month were much below normal (less than 10 percent) across the Frio, Medina, Nueces, Colorado, and Guadalupe River basins and below normal (10 to 24 percent) across the San Antonio and Rio Grande River basins. Area lakes and reservoirs continued well below normal pool elevations. Lake Amistad remained near 35 feet below normal and Lake Travis dropped slightly to near 54 feet below normal. Medina Lake was again the most affected at 90 feet below. The Edwards Aquifer dropped again during the month and was 28 feet below normal, and 6 feet below the level at the end of March 2013. The Edwards Aquifer Authority remained in stage 2 water restrictions requiring large water users to reduce pumping by 30%. title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2014 to March 31, 2014. Affected areas: Armstrong, Carson, Collingsworth, Dallam, Deaf Smith, Donley, Gray, Hansford, Hartley, Hemphill, Hutchinson, Lipscomb and 8 more areas. Episode summary: The month of March was another dry month for the Texas Panhandle, with most areas receiving less than one quarter inch of precipitation during the month. Short-term precipitation deficits worsened especially in the eastern Panhandle. Extreme (D3) to Exceptional (D4) Drought conditions expanded to cover all of the Texas Panhandle by the end of March. The worst conditions were located in the central Panhandle from approximately Hartley County to Carson County. Amarillo recorded 0.20 inches of precipitation for the month (1.19 inches below normal), Dalhart recorded 0.09 inches of precipitation (1.08 inches below normal), and Borger recorded 0.07 inches of precipitation (1.34 inches below normal).||Soil moisture was rated mostly very short by month's end. High winds dried out soils and caused some areas of blowing dust problems, which limited farmers preparing for the upcoming summer season. Winter wheat under irrigation was progressing well, with growers running center pivots more frequently as days warmed. Dryland winter wheat declined in many areas. Rangeland remained dormant, and producers were still supplementing cattle. Stocker cattle were placed on graze-out wheat or moved to feed yards. Upper soil zones remained at extremely dry levels in the southeastern and western parts of the Panhandle, while slightly less dry in the central Panhandle. Deeper soil moisture was less than 30 percent of normal in most of the Panhandle, but values of 70 to 90 percent of normal were scattered across the eastern Texas Panhandle. title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 19, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 19, 2014 to April 19, 2014. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: An upper low was located over Arizona which was able to tap into some mid level Baja moisture. At the same time, southeast surface winds brought in Gulf of Mexico moisture at the low levels. Good shear and instability allowed for hail, strong winds and heavy rain to occur over El Paso County, with one hail/flash flood event leading to a fatality. Details: Three people were rescued from a drainage canal near Valero gas station at Loop 375 and Gateway North. One lady was rescued from under 3 feet of hail and treated for hypothermia, but later died. Additional flooding was reported near Kenworthy and Salem Dr. with cars stalled out.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, May 21, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from May 21, 2014 to May 21, 2014. Affected areas: Brewster. Episode summary: An upper level low pressure area was over Nevada and was moving eastward toward West Texas. There was good moisture, lift, and instability in the atmosphere so thunderstorms developed along and to the east of the dryline. Details: Heavy rain moved across Brewster County with 0.75 - 0.99 inches of rain reported within two hours at Panther Junction.

A jet streak of almost 100kts was also approaching Southern New Mexico ahead of this system. A peak gust of 76 mph was reported with this system. title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2014 to March 31, 2014. Affected areas: Archer, Baylor, Clay, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: With little to no precipitation and warming temperatures, drought conditions persisted across all of western north Texas. Details: Extreme (D3) to exceptional (D4) drought persisted through the month. Extreme (D3) to exceptional (D4) drought across the county worsened through the month, with exceptional (D4) drought becoming more prevalent. Severe (D2) to extreme (D3) drought was present at the beginning of the month. By month's end, most of the county had worsened to extreme (D3) to exceptional (D4) drought.

title: Wildfire: California, Mar 15, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from March 15, 2014 to March 15, 2014. Affected areas: Coachella Valley. Episode summary: The Pierce Fire began around 1537 PST on the 15th near the intersection of Avenue 66 and Pierce Street in Thermal. Initially reported at 10 acres, the fire burned at a moderate rate of spread through medium to heavy brush, increasing rapidly to 200 acres over just a few hours. Road closures were in effect along north and southbound Highway 86 between Avenue 86 and Avenue 80, as well as Avenue 66 from Avenue 86 to Pierce Street. The fire burned a total of 350 acres before being fully contained at 2234 PST on the 15th. The fire downed power lines in the area and destroyed one outbuilding. No injuries to firefighters or civilians were reported. Reported property and crop damage: about $35,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 23, 2014 to May 23, 2014. Affected areas: Scurry. Episode summary: An upper level low was over southern Arizona with upper level disturbances moving over New Mexico and the Big Bend region. Residual outflow boundaries from thunderstorms the previous day were present across the area helping to provide additional lift. There was a lot of moisture in the air so this aided in heavy rainfall. The atmosphere became very unstable with an increase in heating, especially in the higher terrain. This allowed for severe thunderstorms to develop across West Texas and southeast New Mexico with hail, flash flooding, and a tornado. Details: Heavy rain moved across Scurry County and produced flash flooding in Snyder. Low-lying areas were flooded with six to eight inches of water covering the roads. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,000.

title: Drought: California, Feb 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from February 01, 2014 to February 28, 2014. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continued in full force during the month of February, 2014. Extreme drought was detected by the U.S. Drought Monitor for much of the region, with exceptional drought detected along the west side of the San Joaquin Valley. For California as a whole, 2013 was the driest year on record. As the 2013-2014 winter progresses, little rain has fallen across California. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, a decrease in the snow-related tourism activity in the Southern Sierra Nevada, reduction in air quality due to persistent stagnant air, loss or reduction of ground water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. For the first time on record, red flag warnings were issued in January for not only the Southern Sierra Nevada and the Tehachapi Mountains but also the south end of the San Joaquin Valley.

This was a signal of an approaching storm system.|| A cold front brought colder weather to the region on December 3rd, followed by a stronger system on December 6th and 7th. The first storm brought gusty winds to the mountains and desert, as well as light rain and drizzle over the San Joaquin Valley. Some light snow fell in Yosemite and other parts of the Sierra Nevada. Daytime high temperatures cooled to below normal in quite a few locations, especially north of Kern County, due to increased cloud cover and light precipitation.||Behind the cold front, an arctic airmass brought freezing temperatures to the central and southern San Joaquin Valley. Well below normal minimum temperatures commenced on December 4th and continued until the 6th as a modified Arctic airmass was entrenched in the region. Low temperatures dropped below 20 degrees in some San Joaquin Valley locations during the mornings of the 5th and 6th, such as Madera, where the low reached 19 degrees. Daytime high temperatures were generally a few degrees below average until the

title: Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind: California, Nov 20, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind, from November 20, 2013 to November 23, 2013. Affected areas: Kern, Merced, S Sierra Mtns, Tulare. Episode summary: A stronger Pacific storm moved into northern California on the 19th, with precipitation spreading southward into the central California interior that evening. This was the first storm to bring significant precipitation to the central California interior and reached the region during the afternoon of November 20th, with the heaviest rain falling on the central and southern San Joaquin Valley during the early evening. Several Valley and foothill stations reported rainfall amounts in excess of a half inch from the storm and a few sites had an inch or more of rain. Flooding was reported in Atwater (Merced County) near the Castle Air Museum and Airpark. The rain gauge at the nearby Merced Regional Airport recorded 0.58 inch of rain.||Rain continued overnight and into the 21st. Runoff accumulated in low-lying roadways, and leaves clogging storm drains exacerbated the problem. Flooding was reported on southbound Highway 99 near Pixley (in Tulare County) during the morning commute. ||In the Southern Sierra Nevada, estimates of new snow ranged as high as nine inches. Precipitation fell over the entire central California interior, including the desert of Kern County where Edwards AFB reported 0.35 inch of rain|The storm packed a 1-2 punch, as a second cold front intensified as it moved into central California on the 21st. This time, the heaviest precipitation was over the south end of the San Joaquin Valley. Heavy rains caused street flooding north of Bakersfield during the late afternoon. At Meadows Field, 0.45 inch of rain fell in a two-hour period (from 6 to 8 PM). Hail up to a half-inch in diameter fell on Rosamond shortly after sunset.||The upper-level low moved

title: Wildfire: California, Sep 01, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from September 01, 2013 to September 30, 2013. Affected areas: S Sierra Mtns. Episode summary: The Rim Fire was partly in Stanislaus NF and Partly in Yosemite National Park. The ignition date was 8/17/13 at 1525 PDT. The cause was human and the location was 2 Miles Northeast of Buck Meadows. The size was 257,135 acres and containment was reached on 10/6/13 (92% contained as of 9/30/13).
