title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind: California, Aug 18, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind, from August 18, 2013 to August 19, 2013. Affected areas: Kern, Tulare Cty Foothills. Episode summary: High pressure had strengthened by the third week of August and lasted for the remainder of the month over much of the western states and even into the Midwest. August 18th saw the return of monsoonal moisture to the region as a warm, moist airmass wrapped around the upper-level ridge. This airmass brought thunderstorms to the mountains and deserts, especially in Kern and southern Tulare Counties. A strong thunderstorm near Boron produced ��-inch hail during the afternoon of the 18th, and caused flooding near the Boron rest area on Highway 58.||An upper-level low approached the California coast on the 19th, drawing very warm air into the central California interior from the south. Temperatures climbed to their highest readings of the month, with Fresno reaching 110 degrees, and Bakersfield hitting 108. Thunderstorms developed over the mountains and deserts, with some drifting into the San Joaquin Valley during the afternoon and evening hours. Garlock and Red-Rock-Randsburg Road in the eastern Kern County desert was closed due to flooding around sunrise, with flooding on U.S. 395 reported a couple of hours later. Quarter-inch hail fell near Lake Isabella during the early afternoon, and mud and debris flows blocked Highway 178 in the Kern River Canyon. There was a media report of a 1.90 inch storm total rainfall in the Lake Isabella area.||An early evening thunderstorm on the 19th dropped quarter-inch hail on Fresno. Outflow winds from collapsing thunderstorms caused roof damage east-southeast of Lemon Cove, and a 30-foot flag pole was blown over. Trees and utility lines were downed in Woodlake. title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 22, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 22, 2013 to July 22, 2013. Affected areas: Kern, Tulare. Episode summary: The high pressure ridge over the region began to rebuild once again by July 17th. The flow aloft remained southwesterly, and skies remained generally clear until the 18th. Some development of convective clouds (i.e., mainly in the form of cumulus clouds) returned to the higher elevations of the southern Sierra Nevada by July 19th, then began to increase the 20th as the flow aloft turned more southerly and brought more moisture over the central California interior. By the 21st, the mountains and desert were once again under the influence of southeasterly monsoonal flow, and showers and thunderstorms returned. One thunderstorm that moved through Grant Grove knocked down a few trees and power lines.||Even more active weather occurred in the Kern and Tulare County mountains, as well as the Kern County desert on July 22nd. During this time, monsoonal moisture was abundant with increased atmospheric instability which led to the issuance of some flash flood warnings in the Kern and Tulare County mountains and even a flash flood and severe thunderstorm warning in the Kern County desert. Flash flooding due to slow moving thunderstorms occurred at several locations, including Pine Mountain Club, Johnsondale (in the Tulare County mountains), and in the Kern County desert south of Ridgecrest, along Red Rock-Randsburg Road, a favored locale for flash flooding due to the topography in this area. This desert road was shut down during the late afternoon and evening hours due to both flooding and debris flow. Garlock Road near Randsburg also flooded, just west of the junction with U.S. 395, and U.S. 395 was closed north of Johannesburg due to flooding. Around one inch to one and a half inches of

title: High Wind: California, May 18, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 18, 2013 to May 19, 2013. Affected areas: Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: Behind the low, an upper-level ridge that had been over the Pacific Northwest dropped south into California, warming temperatures well above normal. Bakersfield had its first 100-degree day of the year on May 11th, with Fresno hitting triple digits for the first time on the next day. A strong upper-level disturbance moved through Tulare County during the afternoon of the 11th, triggering a few thunderstorms over the Southern Sierra Nevada in Kern and Tulare Counties.||Several high and high minimum temperature records were set between May 11th and the 13th. |Fresno set both record high and record high minimum temperatures on May 12th, and Bakersfield tied its record high minimum temperature for the date. The next day, Fresno tied its record high minimum temperature.||An upper-level low approached Monterey Bay on May 14th, deepening the marine layer and allowing cooler marine air to spill into the San Joaquin Valley. This ended the four-day stretch of near-record heat across much of the central California interior. The low also triggered thunderstorms over the Southern Sierra Nevada on the 14th, and Yosemite Valley measured 0.55 inch of rain during the afternoon. Winds funneled through the passes and canyons of the Kern County from the evening of the 14th through the early morning of the 16th. Gusts to as high as 58 mph were measured at the Mojave Air and Space Port, and gusts to 45-55 mph were common in the Mojave Desert below the Tehachapi Pass.||Clouds from this system kept overnight lows in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley warm, and Fresno set a record high minimum temperature for May 15th.||A stronger upper-level low reached California on May 16th. Winds also gusted to 44 mph at NAS Lemoore. Strong winds also developed across the mountains and deserts of Kern County on the 22nd, with gusts to 56 mph recorded.||An upper-level low over the Pacific Northwest brought another dry trough into the northern half of California on May 24th. As the upper-level jet stream dove around the base of the trough, it brought gusty winds to the Cache Creek area where gusts to 49 mph were recorded. The trough also deepened the marine layer, and marine air spilling through Pacheco Pass caused gusts to 35 mph as far east as Los Banos during the night of May 24th-25th and into the morning of the 25th.||The upper-level trough lingered over the state through the 28th, and then moved east of the region the next day. The trough kept gusty winds over the mountains and deserts, and the central

title: High Wind: California, Apr 05, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 05, 2013 to April 08, 2013. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: April began with an upper-level low tracking eastward across the central California interior. This system, which brought thunderstorms to the region the last two days of March, kept temperatures near average on April 1st. Showers developed over the Temblors and Diablo Range, bringing light rain to parts of the west side of the San Joaquin Valley, and showers also developed along the Southern Sierra Nevada. A tenth of an inch of rain fell at Bodfish, southwest of Lake Isabella, while well to the north, 0.06 inch of rain fell at Ponderosa Basin in Mariposa County.||As the low moved into the Great Basin, an upper-level ridge moved onshore, bringing a short-lived warming trend. Temperatures warmed over the northern parts of the San Joaquin Valley on the 2nd, then over the whole region of the 3rd. However, this was the last day of above-normal temperatures as the next Pacific storm rode over the ridge, pushing the ridge back over the Pacific Ocean.||The night of April 3rd-4th saw an upper-level trough along the California coast. A fetch of subtropical moisture pushed north along the leading edge of the trough and into the west side of the central California interior. Moderate showers developed over the northern half of the San Joaquin Valley, with a sharp fall-off in rain from Madera to Fresno. The Madera Municipal Airport recorded 0.55 inch of rain, while the Fresno-Yosemite International Airport only recorded 0.06 inch of rain.||This moisture moved east across the region as the low pressure system tracked toward the coast, with light showers reaching the Southern Sierra Nevada by the afternoon of the 4th. Clouds associated with this moisture, as

text: recorded 0.06 inch of rain.||This moisture moved east across the region as the low pressure system tracked toward the coast, with light showers reaching the Southern Sierra Nevada by the afternoon of the 4th. Clouds associated with this moisture, as well as the subtropical nature of the airmass, kept overnight temperatures well above normal. Fresno tied its record high minimum temperature for April 4th of 57 degrees.||Gusty winds developed across the Kern County mountains and deserts in the wake of the low. Winds gusted as high as 65 mph at Mojave, and the strongest winds of the event were from Jawbone Canyon to the Mojave area. A series of upper-level disturbances riding a westerly flow aloft kept these gusty winds going afternoons and evenings through April 7th.||Another storm system moved into northern California on April 7th, and dropped south during the day and evening. Precipitation was light, with 0.03 inch of rain falling at the Fresno-Yosemite International Airport, and 0.02 inch at the Madera Municipal and Merced Regional Airports. In contrast to the storm of April 4th which left the south end of the San Joaquin Valley dry, this storm brought measurable rain throughout the Valley. Of the major cities, Bakersfield had the highest rainfall, with 0.05 inch falling at Meadows Field.||The highest rainfall amounts were in the Southern Sierra Nevada. Yosemite Village had 0.71 inch of rain, and Isabella Dam had 0.57 inch. Ponderosa Basin had 0.29 inch of rain, Mountain Mesa reported 0.21 inch, and 0.39 inch fell at Glennville. Snow fell on the higher elevations, with an inch of new snow falling on Ponderosa (elevation 7200 feet in Tulare County). A couple of thunderstorms developed over the Southern Sierra Nevada during the morning of the 8th.||The storm brought very strong winds to the central California interior. Winds

text: inch of new snow falling on Ponderosa (elevation 7200 feet in Tulare County). Winds gusted to 75 mph at Mojave, 66 mph at Rosamond, 46 mph at Naval Air Station Lemoore and 39 mph at Fresno.||A cold airmass associated with the storm dropped high temperatures in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley into the mid 60s to around 70 on April 8th.||A high pressure ridge built into California from the Pacific Ocean beginning on April 9th. This high brought several degrees of warming to the region, with the warmest temperatures on the 12th and 13th. Bakersfield saw its high temperatures rise from 64 on April 8th to 84 on the 12th, and a degree warmer the next day. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: High Wind: California, Apr 13, 2013
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 13, 2013 to April 14, 2013. Affected areas: Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: An east Pacific storm approached California on April 14th, weakening the ridge and cooling temperatures several degrees. Winds increased during the day as a cooler airmass pushed into the San Joaquin Valley and the upper-level jet stream aligned with the passes and canyons of the Kern County mountains. Winds gusted to 80 mph at Bird Springs Pass in the Kern County Sierra Nevada, and to 62 mph at North Edwards Auxiliary Airfield, Edwards AFB. Elsewhere in the mountains and deserts, several wind gusts were in the 45-55 mph range, and gusty winds persisted into the 15th. With dry conditions, blowing dust proved to be a problem in the Kern County deserts. In the San Joaquin Valley, winds gusted to 25-30 mph at several sites, mainly in the central and southwestern San Joaquin Valley.||Gusty winds continued on April 16th as a low-level jet stream moved into the state along the back side of the storm. The jet stream was oriented mainly north-south, and funneled through the mountain passes and canyons. Winds gusted to 45-55 mph in the Kern County mountains and deserts, and to 35-40 mph in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley. The 16th also saw precipitation falling in the mountains. Snow levels were low, around 3600 feet. Snow fell at Ponderosa Basin (elevation 3600 feet), and the California Highway Patrol reported light snow falling, but not sticking, at Lebec (elevation 3585 feet). On the morning of April 17th, Ponderosa reported a 24-hour total of an inch of new snow. In addition to being cold, the airmass was unstable and a few thunderstorms developed near Bass Lake on the 16th.||An upper-level ridge began building into

title: High Wind: California, Apr 13, 2013
text: morning of April 17th, Ponderosa reported a 24-hour total of an inch of new snow. In addition to being cold, the airmass was unstable and a few thunderstorms developed near Bass Lake on the 16th.||An upper-level ridge began building into California on April 18th, and temperatures warmed to near normal on the 18th, then well above normal from the 19th through the 27th. High temperatures in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley reached the mid 80s to around 90 on April 21st, and the warmest locations in the Kern County deserts reached the lower 90s. High temperatures were a couple of degrees warmer on the 22nd, with both Bakersfield and Fresno reaching the 90-degree mark for the first time since October 18th, 2012. The high at Fresno was 91 degrees, and Bakersfield was a degree cooler.||A weak cold front dropped into the Great Basin on April 23rd, bringing a push of colder air into the deserts. Temperatures fell as much as 10 degrees from the 22nd to the 23rd at some desert sites. A weaker influx of cool air into the San Joaquin Valley dropped temperatures in the central Valley by a few degrees on the 23rd, with highs falling back into the mid 80s. The cool air did not penetrate as far as the south end of the San Joaquin Valley, and Bakersfield had a second consecutive day with a high of 90 degrees.||Ahead of the cold front, winds increased in the Kern County mountains and deserts during the evening of April 22nd. Gusts were as high as 49 mph, but were not persistent. Wind speeds would jump to over 40 mph, then drop down to 20-25 mph the next observation before increasing again.||April 24th saw the central California interior between two weather features���an upper-level low southwest of

title: High Wind: California, Apr 13, 2013
text: 49 mph, but were not persistent. Wind speeds would jump to over 40 mph, then drop down to 20-25 mph the next observation before increasing again.||April 24th saw the central California interior between two weather features���an upper-level low southwest of the Channel Islands and a short-wave moving through northern California. Mid-level moisture wrapping around the low moved into the region from the east, while the flow down the back of the short-wave was from the northeast. The two flows collided over Madera County, setting up a convergence zone that supported isolated late afternoon convection over the high country of the Southern Sierra Nevada in northeastern Madera County. At the same time, the aforementioned features allowed the coastal marine layer to deepen. The marine layer was over 4300 feet deep at Fort Ord during the afternoon of the 24th, and marine air spilling through the passes and canyons of the Temblors and Diablo Range triggered 35-40 mph gusts along the west side of the San Joaquin Valley during the late afternoon and evening.||The influx of cool air into the San Joaquin Valley produced a noticeable drop in temperatures on the 25th. The high at Bakersfield only reached 79 degrees, the first time since April 18th that the high at Meadows Field did not reach 80 degrees. Fresno was slightly warmer with a high of 81 degrees, down 10 degrees from the previous day. (Bakersfield���s high was down 9 degrees from the 24th.)||High pressure rebuilt into California beginning on April 26th, with temperatures warming through the 29th. A mainly dry upper-level short-wave dropped through California on the 28th, triggering a thunderstorm over the Sierra Nevada crest in Tulare County, and bringing breezy conditions to the west side of the San Joaquin Valley as well as through and below the passes of the

title: High Wind: California, Apr 13, 2013
text: dropped through California on the 28th, triggering a thunderstorm over the Sierra Nevada crest in Tulare County, and bringing breezy conditions to the west side of the San Joaquin Valley as well as through and below the passes of the Kern County mountains. Winds gusted up to 42 mph at both Cache Creek and Mojave, and to 37 mph at Ridgecrest.||A stronger upper-level trough moved through northern California on April 30th. Short-waves moving along the periphery of the trough brought narrow bands of high clouds that pushed south across the central California interior. The short-waves also brought gusty winds to the region. Gusts reached 35-40 mph on the west side of the San Joaquin Valley, and 45-50 mph below favorably oriented passes and canyons of the Kern County mountains.||Although the trough brought a cooler airmass to the region, April ended on a warm note as Fresno set a record high minimum temperature on the 30th. Despite only setting two temperature records for the month���both high minimums and one being a tie���Fresno had its warmest April on record. (Fresno temperature records go back to 1887; rainfall records go back further, to 1878.) Bakersfield set no temperature records during April, but did tie its 14th warmest April on record (since 1889).

title: High Wind, Winter Storm, Winter Weather: California, Apr 25, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Winter Storm, Winter Weather, from April 25, 2014 to April 26, 2014. Affected areas: Indian Wells Vly, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: The storm that moved into northern California during the evening of April 24th brought thunderstorms to the northern part of the state. This was an indicator of the highly unstable airmass accompanying the storm. Thunderstorms developed over central California around midday and had strengthened to near severe levels by the middle of the afternoon. Three Severe Thunderstorm Warnings were issued by WFO Hanford on the 25th, two of which were for a particularly long-lasting storm. Eleven Significant Weather Advisories were issued for non-severe thunderstorms due to the threats of hail and strong outflow winds. Hail estimated at al least a half inch in diameter was reported from these storms, as were wind damage and at least two funnel clouds. The thunderstorms brought appreciable rains to Fresno, giving the city its fourth wettest April 25th on record (0.55 inch; wettest is 0.93 inch in 1952). Bakersfield had a storm total of 0.36 inch. This brought its monthly total to 0.50 inch, just under the average rainfall for April of 0.52 inch. The rainfall from this storm ensured that neither Bakersfield nor Fresno would have its driest rain season on record, although conditions for the season remained much below normal.||A very cold airmass moved into central California behind the cold front. By late on April 25th, snow was being reported down to the 3800-foot elevation, and storm-total snow estimates were as high as 25 inches in the high country of the Southern Sierra Nevada, and up to 3.5 inches in the Tehachapi Mountains. High temperatures in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley on the 26th

title: High Wind, Winter Storm, Winter Weather: California, Apr 25, 2014
text: storm-total snow estimates were as high as 25 inches in the high country of the Southern Sierra Nevada, and up to 3.5 inches in the Tehachapi Mountains. For Bakersfield, April tied for the 14th warmest April on record; one of the Aprils it tied with was from last year. Reported property and crop damage: about $600,000.

title: Strong Wind, Winter Storm, Winter Weather: California, May 05, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, Winter Storm, Winter Weather, from May 05, 2014 to May 06, 2014. Affected areas: Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Tulare Cty Mtns. Episode summary: A late season cold winter like storm system swept into Central California beginning on May 5th. This storm brought heavy snowfall to the Southern Sierra Nevada with snowfall amounts over 1 foot in the high Sierra. Snowfall also occurred in eastern Tulare County with close to 1 foot in some spots. This storm also brought strong to severe wind gusts to much of Kern County, although the Tehachapi Mountains saw little in the way of snowfall. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: High Wind: California, May 09, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 09, 2014 to May 10, 2014. Affected areas: Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: A fast moving trough of low pressure brought very strong winds to much of Central California between May 9th to 11th.

title: Winter Storm: California, May 20, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Storm, from May 20, 2014 to May 20, 2014. Affected areas: S Sierra Mtns. Episode summary: Towards the end of the month another cold, wintry like storm approached Central California. Heavy snow occurred in and around Yosemite NP. 8 inches of new snow fell on Tioga Pass Rd. (Hwy 120) forcing a closure of the road to clear the snowfall for several days on May 20th. Strong winds also occurred in the San Joaquin Valley, and in the Kern County Mountains and Deserts.

title: Wildfire: California, May 26, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from May 26, 2014 to May 31, 2014. Affected areas: S Sierra Foothills. Episode summary: The Hunters wildfire was managed by CalFire. Ignition was 5/26/14 and the cause was unknown. The location was 5 miles south of Coulterville, CA (Mariposa County) and the size was 677 acres. Containment was reached on 6/2 and the cost to containment was $4.4 Million. There were two residences lost and one outbuilding. There were no fatalities and unknown injuries. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jun 05, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from June 05, 2014 to June 05, 2014. Affected areas: Terry. Episode summary: Late this evening, the remnants of a high-based thunderstorm tracked across southern Terry County and produced damaging winds with a heat burst. An employee with Lyntegar Electric Cooperative reported at least 16 power poles were toppled from near Wellman northeast toward Brownfield. A Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station located two miles south of Brownfield recorded a ten-minute period of severe wind gusts as high as 77 mph. The heat burst that accompanied these damaging winds pushed the temperature from 88 to 96 degrees in the span of ten minutes. Reported property and crop damage: about $32,000.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, May 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 12, 2014 to May 12, 2014. Affected areas: Jefferson, Kenosha, Milwaukee, Racine, Walworth, Waukesha. Episode summary: A warm front had stalled over southern Wisconsin with repeated rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms and heavy rainfall. There was some flash flooding in southeast Wisconsin. Details: General street flooding throughout the city of Waukesha. Minor road flooding. Sewer overflows and street flooding in Fort Atkinson and Jefferson. Low lying streets flooded as well as runoff from farm fields flowing over roadways in rural areas. Numerous garbage cans were overturned in Fort Atkinson resulting in bags of trash floating in the water. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Flood: Texas, Jun 06, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from June 06, 2014 to June 06, 2014. Affected areas: Castro. Episode summary: A complex of severe thunderstorms developed in eastern New Mexico ahead of an upper level disturbance and along a surface front. As these storms moved across the Texas and New Mexico state line during the evening hours, several severe wind gusts and subsequent reports of damage were received in the far southern Texas panhandle into the South Plains. In addition, hail as large as golf balls was reported in the far southwestern panhandle. Details: The Dimmitt Sheriff's Office reported extensive flooding of streets and roads in and around Dimmitt.

title: Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Apr 13, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, Heavy Rain, from April 13, 2014 to April 15, 2014. Affected areas: Crawford, Grant, Richland, Vernon. Episode summary: Thunderstorms with locally heavy rain, moved across portions of southwest Wisconsin for the second day in a row on April 13th. After receiving 1 to 3 inches of rain on the 12th, another 1.5 to 2.5 inches fell on the 13th. This was enough to produce some minor mudslides across the extreme southern portions of Crawford and Richland Counties. Details: Minor mudslides occurred across the extreme southern part of Crawford County north of Boscobel. A minor mudslide occurred in the southern part of Richland County at the intersection of State Highways 80 and 193. Near Boscobel, 2.26 inches of rain fell. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Apr 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from April 01, 2014 to April 03, 2014. Affected areas: Trempealeau. Episode summary: Flooding along the Trempealeau River near Dodge (Trempealeau County) occurred in early April due to run off from snow melt and ice on the river breaking up. Details: Runoff from snow melt along with the ice breaking up, caused the Trempealeau River in Dodge to go out of its banks. The river crested less than a half foot above the flood stage at 9.33 feet.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Apr 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from April 30, 2014 to April 30, 2014. Affected areas: Jackson. Episode summary: Minor flooding occurred along the Black River in Black River Falls (Jackson County) due to run off from heavy rain. Details: Run off from heavy rains pushed the Black River out of its banks in Black River Falls. The river crested around a quarter of a foot above the flood stage at 47.22 feet.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2014 to April 30, 2014. Affected areas: Archer, Baylor, Clay, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: With little to no precipitation, drought conditions worsened over much of northern Texas. This was exacerbated by unseasonably warm conditions. Details: Extreme (D3) to exceptional (D4) drought persisted through the month. Severe (D2) to Extreme (D3) drought worsened, with extreme to exceptional (D4) drought covering the county by the end of the month. Exceptional (D4) drought persisted through the month.

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 01, 2014 to June 30, 2014. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Repeated widespread rainfall events through June further alleviated short and long term drought conditions across the South Plains, Rolling Plains, and extreme southern Texas Panhandle. Almost all of the South Plains was in severe (D2) drought conditions while the Rolling Plains was mostly in extreme (D3) drought conditions. A portion of Cottle and King Counties remained in exceptional (D4) drought conditions.||A significant rainfall event occurred at the end of May over Memorial Day weekend and this trend continued through the month of June. Much of the region saw at least two inches of rainfall with some locations observing greater than seven inches. By the end of the month, most areas were at or around the average annual rainfall to date. Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet stations near Wolfforth (Lubbock County), Hart (Briscoe County), and Roaring Springs (Motley County) recorded monthly precipitation measurements of 5.65 in., 5.33 in., and 5.25 in., respectively. A cooperative weather observer in Vigo Park (Swisher County) recorded 6.64 inches. The abundant rainfall kept temperatures near seasonal averages through June. Lubbock and Childress were 0.9 and 0.6 degrees above normal, respectively. Lubbock International Airport recorded four days at or above 100 degrees while Childress Municipal Airport observed only two days at or above 100 degrees. Keetch-Byram Drought Index Values markedly improved as well through June. Widespread values between 200 and 400 were observed over much of the area with values between 400 and 500 over the southern South Plains. There were also isolated pockets in the southern Texas Panhandle of less than 200.||Fire weather impacts continued to be low as they

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2014
text: were observed over much of the area with values between 400 and 500 over the southern South Plains. There were also isolated pockets in the southern Texas Panhandle of less than 200.||Fire weather impacts continued to be low as they normally are going into summer. The beneficial rains have resulted in improvement of farming and ranching conditions across the entire region. Rainfall has eased the need for supplemental irrigation and further need for irrigation is not expected until at least August. Some area farmers reported moisture to a depth of four feet. Area lake levels also improved but still needed a tremendous amount of water to be filled to capacity.||Economic losses due to drought through June since the drought began were estimated near $3 billion.

title: Flood: Texas, Jun 07, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from June 07, 2014 to June 08, 2014. Affected areas: Bailey, Lubbock. Episode summary: An outbreak of severe storms affected many locations on the Caprock late this day and through the overnight hours resulting in numerous instances of hail damage, destructive winds and flooding. Several of these storms were supercells and a few even developed organized low level rotation. However, official NWS storm surveys did not find conclusive evidence of tornadic activity, but instead discovered several swaths of intense rear flank downdraft winds that at one point were measured as high as 96 mph. Preliminary estimates indicate that several thousand acres of newly planted cotton and grain crops throughout portions of the South Plains would require replanting following torrential rains and soil erosion. Total property and agricultural losses from this event will likely approach $250 million. Details: Many streets in Muleshoe were reported to be covered in water. Torrential rains resulted in widespread flooding of playa lakes, streets and roads throughout far southwest Lubbock County, or generally from Wolfforth and points south. Roads such as Brownfield Highway and County Roads 179 and 41 had several sections that at times became impassable by car. One sedan was disabled by floodwaters near Farm-to-Market Road 1585 and Brownfield Highway shortly after m Reported property and crop damage: about $100,015,000.

title: Cold/Wind Chill: Texas, Apr 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Cold/Wind Chill, from April 14, 2014 to April 15, 2014. Affected areas: Armstrong, Carson, Collingsworth, Dallam, Deaf Smith, Donley, Gray, Hansford, Hartley, Hemphill, Hutchinson, Lipscomb and 8 more areas. Episode summary: A cold front moved through the Texas Panhandle during the late night hours of the 14th. The cooler post frontal airmass allowed temperatures to drop well below freezing by the early morning hours of the 15th. These subfreezing temperatures threatened sensitive vegetation during the growing season. Overnight low temperatures ranged from 20 degrees at Amarillo (Potter and Randall County) to 27 at Borger (Hutchinson County). Temperatures warmed above freezing by 8:00 AM CST.| |The following is a listing of low temperatures per county: 24 degrees at Dalhart (Dallam and Hartley County); 23 degrees at Stratford (Sherman County); 23 degrees at Gruver (Hansford County); 21 degrees at Perryton (Ochiltree County); 23 degrees at Lipscomb (Lipscomb County); 25 degrees at Dumas (Moore County); 27 degrees at Borger (Hutchinson County); 27 degrees at Mesa Vista (Roberts County); 23 degrees at Canadian (Hemphill County); 26 degrees at Boys Ranch (Oldham County); 20 degrees at Amarillo (Potter and Randall County); 25 degrees at Panhandle (Carson County); 25 degrees at McLean (Gray County); 27 degrees at Wheeler (Wheeler County); 21 degrees at Hereford (Deaf Smith County); 24 degrees at Claude (Armstrong County); 21 degrees at Clarendon (Donley County); and 24 degrees at Wellington (Collingsworth County). Details: Overnight low of 23 degrees at Lipscomb. Overnight low of 25 degrees at Dumas. Overnight low of 24 degrees at Dalhart.

title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 24, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 24, 2014 to April 24, 2014. Affected areas: Hemphill. Episode summary: A cold front moved through the Texas Panhandle during the early morning hours of the 24th. The increased surface pressure gradient behind the front allowed strong winds aloft mix to the surface to cause a high wind gust at the West Texas Mesonet site 6 miles east of Canadian (Hemphill County). This high wind gust was brief and no other high wind reports were received. Details: High wind gust of 59 mph at Canadian.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jun 09, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from June 09, 2014 to June 09, 2014. Affected areas: Cochran, Garza, Hockley. Episode summary: A quasi-linear convective system developed this evening across Eastern New Mexico and pushed into the Texas Panhandle before moving across the Rolling Plains. Later into the night, an additional line of thunderstorms developed across Eastern New Mexico and the Southern Texas Panhandle and subsequently merged with the existing line. A preceding gust front developed ahead of this system, producing isolated high wind gusts across portions of the South Plains. Details: The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station in Morton recorded a 69 mph wind gust. The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site in Graham recorded a 59 mph wind gust. The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site in Levelland measured a 58 mph wind gust.

title: Wildfire: California, Apr 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from April 30, 2014 to April 30, 2014. Affected areas: San Bernardino And Riverside County Valleys - The Inland Empire. Episode summary: The Etiwanda fire began on April 30th around 0700 PST in the San Bernardino National Forest near Rancho Cucamonga in San Bernardino County. The fire was due to an escaped illegal campfire a few days prior, when strong winds blew embers that ignited in Day Canyon. A mandatory evacuation order was issued for Rancho Cucamonga residents from Haven Avenue to Carnelian Street, north of Hillside Road, as well as the area West of Etiwanda, North of Wilson and East of Day Creek Wash. Schools evacuated included Day Creek Intermediate School, Los Osos High School, Heritage Intermediate School and Caryn Elementary. The fire burned rapidly south, threatening 600-800 structures. 2143 acres before being fully contained on May 6. Three firefighters sustained unknown minor injuries and one structure was damaged. Reported property and crop damage: about $6,000.

title: Ice Storm, Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Apr 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Ice Storm, Winter Storm, from April 03, 2014 to April 04, 2014. Affected areas: Florence, Forest, Langlade, Lincoln, Marathon, Menominee, Northern Marinette, Northern Oconto, Oneida, Shawano, Southern Marinette, Southern Oconto and 1 more areas. Episode summary: Low pressure moved from the central Plains into southern Wisconsin. The storm produced a swath of heavy, wet snow across northwest and north central Wisconsin and freezing rain across central and far northeast Wisconsin.||The heaviest snowfall was 14.5 inches a few miles southwest of Lac du Flambeau (Vilas Co.) and in Presque Isle (Vilas Co.). Most locations in north central Wisconsin received 6 to 9 inches of snow. Freezing rain accumulations of 0.25 to 0.40 were reported across central Wisconsin.||Despite the heavy, wet snow and ice accumulation, there was only isolated damage to trees and power lines. Details: The highest snowfall total from the storm was 14.5 inches at Lac du Flambeau and Presque Isle. WSAW-TV in Wausau measured 0.4 inches of freezing rain during the night of April 3rd into the morning hours of the 4th. A storm total of 9.6 inches of snow fell at WJFW-TV in Rhinelander, and an estimated 9.5 inches of snow fell 3 miles west of Minocqua.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Apr 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from April 12, 2014 to April 12, 2014. Affected areas: Winnebago. Episode summary: Thunderstorms that developed north of a warm front that was across southern Wisconsin, produced heavy rainfall, isolated wind damage and large hail. The heavy rain caused urban and small stream flooding in Winnebago County, around Oshkosh and Neenah. Details: Heavy rainfall caused widespread urban flooding in Oshkosh which requiring some streets to be closed. Thunderstorms with heavy rainfall caused small stream flooding around the intersection of CH-JJ and SH-76 southwest of Neenah.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Apr 16, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from April 16, 2014 to April 17, 2014. Affected areas: Florence, Forest, Oneida, Vilas. Episode summary: Low pressure from the Plains moved across Wisconsin and produced a swath of heavy, wet snow over the northern part of the state. Six to sixteen inches of snow fell, with the heaviest across Vilas County, where 16.0 inches fell near Phelps and at Conover, and 15.0 inches fell at Boulder Junction.||The heavy snow caused scattered power outages. Details: The highest snowfall totals in Forest County included 14.0 inches at Alvin, and 12.5 inches 4 miles northwest of Alvin. The highest snowfall totals in Florence County included 9.0 inches 3 miles north of Spread Eagle. The highest snowfall totals in Vilas County included 16.0 inches near Phelps and at Conover, 15.0 inches at Boulder Junction, 14.4 inches at St. Germain.

title: Frost/Freeze: California, Jun 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Frost/Freeze, from June 14, 2014 to June 14, 2014. Affected areas: Modoc County. Episode summary: An unseasonably cold air mass and clearing skies allowed temperatures to drop below freezing over many areas in northeast California. Details: Reported low temperatures ranged from 30 to 31 degrees.

title: Frost/Freeze: California, Jun 17, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Frost/Freeze, from June 17, 2014 to June 17, 2014. Affected areas: Northeast Siskiyou And Northwest Modoc Counties. Episode summary: An unseasonably cold air mass and clearing skies allowed temperatures to drop below freezing over some parts of northeast California. Details: Reported low temperatures ranged from 30 to 36 degrees.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado: Texas, May 25, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado, from May 25, 2014 to May 25, 2014. Affected areas: Ector, Martin, Midland, Pecos. Episode summary: An upper low was located along the Arizona/New Mexico border progressing slowly eastward into the northern Texas Panhandle with associated upper-level disturbances rotating around the base of the upper trough. Outflow boundaries from convection the previous day were the focus for thunderstorm development across the Trans Pecos and Permian Basin along with strong heating in the higher terrain. Moist and unstable atmospheric conditions were conducive for potential flooding and supercell development. Also, winds were changing direction and speed with increasing elevation in the atmosphere to support tornado development. Details: Heavy rain fell across Midland County and produced flash flooding near Midland International Airport. Cars were reported to be stalled on Business 20 under the Farm to Market road 1788 bridge. Two to three feet of water was covering the road. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Midland County and produced flash flooding in Midland. Street flooding was reported on Ward Street south of Neely. No damage was reported so the cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Pecos County and produced flash flooding near Bakersfield. Several spots on Farm to Market Road 1901 between Bakersfield and McCamey were reported to be flooded with over six inches of water. Since no damage was reported, the cost of damage is a rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $17,300.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2014 to April 30, 2014. Affected areas: Bell, Bosque, Collin, Comanche, Cooke, Coryell, Dallas, Denton, Eastland, Ellis, Erath, Fannin and 19 more areas. Episode summary: Drought conditions became worse over several counties in the western and northwestern portions of North Texas. Little change in drought conditions occurred over the rest of the region. Details: Eastland County spent all of April 2014 in Severe/D2 drought. Erath County spent most of April 2014 split between Extreme/D3 drought across the southern half of the county and Severe/D2 conditions across the northern half. By the end of the month, all of Erath County was classified in the Extreme/D3 category. Johnson County spent the majority of April 2014 split between Extreme/D3 conditions over the western two-thirds of the county and Severe/D2 across the eastern third. On April 29, all of Johnson county was classified under the Extreme/D3 category. Reported property and crop damage: about $88,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2014 to April 07, 2014. Affected areas: Anderson, Freestone, Henderson, Limestone. Episode summary: A few counties in the southeastern part of North Texas received enough rain early in the month to eliminate their D2/Severe drought status by April 8th. Details: Severe/D2 drought conditions over southern portions of Henderson County improved to Moderate/D1 by April 8, due to beneficial rainfall received during the first week of the month. Severe/D2 conditions over the northern half of Anderson County during the first week of April improved to Moderate/D1 county-wide by April 8, and remained as such through the end of the month. Severe/D2 conditions over southeastern portions of Limestone County improved to Moderate/D1 county-wide by April 8, and remained as such through the end of the month. Reported property and crop damage: about $4,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from April 28, 2014 to April 28, 2014. Affected areas: Bexar. title: Flood, High Wind: Texas, Jun 19, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, High Wind, from June 19, 2014 to June 20, 2014. Affected areas: Briscoe, Castro, Hockley, Lubbock, Swisher. Episode summary: By late this afternoon, scattered slow moving thunderstorms exited far eastern New Mexico and resulted in a few severe wind and hail reports across portions of the South Plains. As these storms consolidated into a squall line over the central South Plains by early evening, torrential rainfall rates produced some instances of areal flooding. This line of storms quickly decayed east of the Caprock Escarpment, but still managed to produce some severe wind gusts. During the overnight hours, a lone rain shower produced a high wind gust near Silverton. Details: A trained spotter reported water covering several sections of County Road 303 south of Pep. A NWS Cooperative observer reported streets in Hart were covered by several inches of water. NWS radar indicated nearly four inches of rain fell between Hart and Nazareth. A NWS employee reported flooding of some streets in Shallowater.

title: Flood: Texas, Jun 18, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from June 18, 2014 to June 18, 2014. Affected areas: Bailey. Episode summary: Following an early morning high wind gust from a decaying shower in Castro County, thunderstorms erupted across the eastern plains of New Mexico this afternoon and produced some instances of severe hail and flooding as they overspread the western South Plains. One of these storms was particularly intense while in Cochran County and may have contributed to a fatal plane mishap near Lehman. Hail as large as ping pong ball size accompanied this storm. All of these storms dissipated by late evening, but one final severe storm developed late in the overnight hours and resulted in a severe wind gust in Cochran County. Details: Law enforcement reported curb to curb flooding in Muleshoe. An eastbound lane of Highway 84 also had one lane under water two miles southeast of the city.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2014 to April 30, 2014. Affected areas: Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Very little rainfall for the month of April caused the drought to intensify across much of West Central Texas. Abilene experienced the fourth driest period on record with 1.77 inches of rainfall measured from January 1 through April 30. San Angelo experienced the second driest period on record with 0.52 inches of rainfall recorded from January 1 through the end of April. A large part of the area was upgraded to extreme drought while Sutton and Kimble Counties were upgraded to exceptional drought by the U.S. Drought Monitor. According to the Texas Crop Report and the Texas Forest Service, the drought resulted in larger wildfires, poor wheat conditions, and low stock tank water levels. Details: All of Mason County was in an extreme drought. Most of Irion County was in an extreme drought. Most of Kimble County was in an exceptional drought.

title: Winter Weather: California, Apr 25, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from April 25, 2014 to April 25, 2014. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Mono. Episode summary: Low pressure moved into the West on the 25th, bringing heavy snow to the high Sierra with light accumulations for the Sierra valleys. Details: A wide range of snowfall fell with this system on the 25th. Areas below 6500 feet east of highway 89 in the Tahoe Basin generally received only up to 3 inches of snowfall. Meanwhile, areas west of highway 89 below 7000 feet saw 5-9 inches of snow, with areas near the crest receiving upwards of 18 inches. This event was mainly restricted to the high Sierra west of highway 395 where up to around 2 feet of snow fell near Mammoth Mountain. Areas near and east of highway 395 received much less with only up to 3 inches observed.

title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Apr 15, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from April 15, 2014 to April 15, 2014. Affected areas: Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason, Mcculloch and 10 more areas. Episode summary: A large cold high pressure system brought freezing temperatures on the morning of April 15. Temperatures dropped into the lower and mid 20s for several hours across a large part of the area. There were a few readings around 30 degrees near Mason, San Saba, Coleman and Sonora. These freezing temperatures damaged a significant amount of winter wheat across the area.

title: High Wind: California, Apr 26, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 26, 2014 to April 26, 2014. Affected areas: Antelope Valley. Episode summary: Strong onshore pressure gradients generated gusty southwesterly winds across the Antelope Valley. Sustained winds in excess of 40 MPH and gusts in excess of 60 MPH were reported. Details: Strong and gusty southwest winds developed across the Antelope Valley. The ASOS at Palmdale Airport reported sustained winds of 46 MPH with gusts to 63 MPH.

title: High Wind: California, Apr 29, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 29, 2014 to April 30, 2014. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Los Angeles County San Fernando Valley, Santa Clarita Valley, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area, Ventura County Coastal Valleys, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: Surface high pressure, building into the Great Basin, generated a strong late-season Santa Ana wind event across Ventura and Los Angeles counties. In the mountains, northeast wind gusts in excess of 70 MPH were reported while northeast wind gusts in excess of 60 MPH were reported in some valley areas. As the winds developed, a couple of small wildfires occurred across the mountains of Ventura and Los Angeles counties, but did not grow to any significant levels. Details: Strong north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Los Angeles county. The Chilao RAWS sensor reported the strongest gusts (up to 78 MPH). Other RAWS stations (Camp Nine, Mill Creek, and Warm Springs) reported wind gusts between 58 and 72 MPH. Strong north to northeast winds developed across the Santa Clarita Valley. Various RAWS stations (Newhall Pass, Del Valle, and Saugus) reported wind gusts between 58 and 60 MPH. Strong north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Ventura county. Wind gusts between 60 and 70 MPH were reported across eastern sections of the mountains.

title: High Wind: California, May 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 10, 2014 to May 11, 2014. Affected areas: Antelope Valley, Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: A strong west to northwest wind event developed across the mountains of Ventura and Los Angeles counties as well as the Antelope Valley. In the mountains, northwesterly wind gusts up to 60 MPH were reported. Across the Antelope Valley, sustained winds up to 40 MPH were reported along with gusts in excess of 50 MPH. Details: The ASOS at Palmdale Airport reported sustained winds of 40 MPH. The RAWS sensor at Camp Nine reported northerly wind gusts up to 60 MPH. Strong and gusty northerly winds, up to 60 MPH, were reported across eastern sections of the Ventura county mountains.

title: Flash Flood: California, May 22, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from May 22, 2014 to May 22, 2014. Affected areas: Los Angeles. Episode summary: Strong thunderstorms developed across the Antelope Valley. Some storms were strong enough to produce flash flooding across the community of Palmdale. In addition, one thunderstorm generated nickel-size hail in Palmdale which was just below severe levels. Details: A weather spotter in the Palmdale area reported a strong thunderstorm (with heavy rain) that produced flash flooding near the intersection of 47th Street East and East Avenue South. Elsewhere across the Antelope Valley, reports of flooding due to heavy rain were reported.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jun 24, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from June 24, 2014 to June 24, 2014. Affected areas: Calumet, Winnebago. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed along a weak front in a very moist atmosphere and produced heavy rain in Calumet County and Winnebago County. Details: Thunderstorms produced 1.16 inches of rain in 40 minutes on the northeast side of Oshkosh causing street flooding. The storm also dropped pea size hail. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain in parts of central and southern Calumet County. 3.38 of rain fell near Stockbridge in less than three hours. The heavy rain caused fields to flood and washed out culverts of several area roads. Several houses had water in their basements. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 03, 2014 to April 03, 2014. Affected areas: Potter. Episode summary: A cold front moved through the Texas Panhandle during the midday hours of the 3rd. The combination of a tight surface pressure gradient and strong winds aloft mixing to the surface led to a 60 mph high wind gust at the Amarillo (Potter County) ASOS at 1:27 PM CST. This was an isolated gust and no further gusts were observed. Details: Measured at the Amarillo ASOS.

title: Dust Storm: Texas, Apr 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Dust Storm, from April 03, 2014 to April 03, 2014. Affected areas: Carson, Potter, Randall. Episode summary: A cold front moved through the Texas Panhandle during the midday hours of the 3rd. The combination of a tight surface pressure gradient and strong winds aloft mixing to the surface led strong surface winds of 35 MPH to 38 MPH. These strong winds lofted loose dirt into the air and reduced surface visibility to less than a quarter mile in Skellytown (Carson County), and Amarillo (Potter and Randall Counties). Less than a quarter mile visibility was reported at 1:22 PM CST by a trained spotter traveling State Highway 152 near Skellytown. Less than a quarter mile visibility was observed by the NWS office in Amarillo (Potter County), and off duty NWS Meteorologist at Soncy Street and 34th Ave (Randall County) between 1:00 PM CST and 2:00 PM CST. Winds decreased after 2:00 PM CST and brought an end to dust storm conditions. Details: Less than a quarter mile visibility observed at the NWS office. Less than a quarter mile visibility observed at Soncy and 34th Ave. Less than a quarter mile visibility observed on State Highway 152 near Skellytown.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Apr 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from April 12, 2014 to April 17, 2014. Affected areas: Columbia, Ozaukee. Episode summary: Heavy rainfall of 3-5 inches from April 12-14 resulted in minor river flooding of the Milwaukee and Wisconsin rivers. The flooding closed roads and did flood some homes near the Wisconsin river. Details: The Wisconsin river crested at 17.84 feet in Portage. Long Lake which is near the Wisconsin river also flooded. Several roads were closed in the Black Hawk Park area with up to 4 feet of water over the roads. Several homes and out buildings had water in the first floor in the town of Dekorra. Some people had to use boats for transportation to and from their home. The Milwaukee river crested at 11.4 feet in Cedarburg and was experiencing minor flooding throughout Ozaukee County. Several roads were closed due to the flooding. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 26, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 26, 2014 to May 26, 2014. Affected areas: Glasscock, Howard, Martin. Episode summary: An upper-level low was centered over northern New Mexico. The atmosphere was very unstable with cooling occurring in the middle levels. A very moist air mass was in place, and the ground was already saturated from recent rainfall making conditions ideal for flash flooding. An upper-level disturbance that was rotating around the upper low moved over West Texas which increased the lift over the area. There was also an increase of wind speed and change of wind direction with height in the atmosphere which allowed for storms to rotate easier. These conditions combined to produce tornadoes, hail, high winds, and flash flooding in West Texas. Details: Heavy rain moved across Howard County and produced flash flooding near Big Spring. title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2014 to April 30, 2014. Episode summary: A dry spring pattern continued through April for the Texas Panhandle, with most areas receiving less than one inch of precipitation during the month. Short-term deficits worsened especially in the western Panhandle, where less than one quarter of an inch fell. In what should have been the start to the growing season, precipitation ranged from less than 5% to near 50% of normal through the month. Long-term precipitation deficits going back to October 2010 matched or were worse than similar periods in the 1930s and 1950s droughts of record. By the end of April, Exceptional (D4) Drought conditions expanded to cover all of the Texas Panhandle. Farmers prepared for spring planting while much of the winter wheat crop was zeroed out by crop insurance adjusters. Winter wheat under irrigation did well and was used as a forage for cattle where available. Rangeland remained dormant, and producers were still supplementing cattle or reducing herd sizes. Upper soil zones remained at extremely dry levels in the Panhandle, ranging from less than 1 percent full in parts of the western Panhandle to between 5 and 10 percent full in parts of the eastern Panhandle. Episode summary: Overall drought conditions continued to improve over the area with many areas continuing the wet period from May and June. However, the second half of the month saw drier conditions. A cooperative weather observer in Hart (Castro County) observed 5.35 inches. This is where the greatest improvement to the drought was realized. Elsewhere, scattered rainfall throughout the month kept monthly precipitation values near or above normal with the exception of the southern South Plains. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from June 27, 2014 to June 27, 2014. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: A passing upper level trough resulted in high winds in the lower elevations of the Guadalupe Mountains.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jul 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from July 01, 2014 to July 01, 2014. Affected areas: Swisher. Episode summary: A wake low followed a cold front moving through the Texas Panhandle into the South Plains and Rolling Plains this morning, producing a wind gust to 59 mph near Tulia.

title: Flood: Texas, Jul 02, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from July 02, 2014 to July 02, 2014. Affected areas: Parmer, Yoakum. Episode summary: An early morning upper level disturbance combined with moist upslope flow, aided by a nearby frontal boundary, to produce showers and thunderstorms. Portions of Parmer County in and around Bovina received between 4 to 6 inches of rainfall, with locally higher amounts estimated by radar. High water plagued area roadways causing multiple reports of traffic related issues. Showers and thunderstorms regenerated during the late afternoon and early evening hours, mainly across portions of Yoakum County, in association with a mesoscale convective vortex in eastern New Mexico. Consistent moderate to heavy rainfall from Plains to Denver City caused street flooding and road closures. Details: Local law enforcement officials and trained spotters reported submerged roadways between Plains and Denver City, including Highway 214. A storm spotter measured 4.30 inches of rainfall in just a few hours near Plains. Law enforcement officials reported standing water over Highways 60 and 86 in the vicinity of Bovina causing multiple vehicles to hydroplane off the road. One car was stranded in high water as rainfall amounts of 4 to 6 inches fell across much of town, with locally higher amounts.

title: Flood: Texas, Jul 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from July 03, 2014 to July 03, 2014. Affected areas: Hockley. Episode summary: A moist and unstable environment led to the development of an isolated storm in northeastern Hockley County. This storm persisted for several hours through the mid to late afternoon and early evening, causing a brief stint of severe winds southwest of Anton as well as flooding issues from Anton to east of Levelland. Details: Fire department officials observed flooding near and around Anton, including Farm to Market Road 1294 to 168 as 3 to 5 inches of rain fell over the area. Areas east of Levelland to Opdyke West also reported minor flooding on area roadways, including Highway 114.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jun 02, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from June 02, 2014 to June 02, 2014. Affected areas: Dodge. Episode summary: A line of showers and thunderstorms move east across southern Wisconsin during the morning and produced wind damage and heavy rainfall in Dodge County. Details: An estimated one inch of rain in 20 minutes resulted in urban street flooding with some street closures. A shallow layer of mud flowing across the road due to an estimated one inch of rain in 20 minutes and a plugged culvert.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 27, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from June 27, 2014 to June 27, 2014. Affected areas: Dunn. Episode summary: A line of thunderstorms moved northward across west central Wisconsin during the afternoon of Friday, June 27th. One of the storms produced a tornado around Colfax that had a damage track of 7 miles. The worst damage was at the local high school where damage to the school HVAC units on the roof occurred, plus several storage sheds and an athletic metal building were completely destroyed. Lightning also struck during the Cadott Country Fest, with minor injuries to two people. Details: A storm survey indicated that most of the damage was rated EF-0 with winds up to 85 mph. However, the tornado did briefly strengthen to EF-1 on the northeast side of Colfax, at the local high school where a shed was destroyed and two HVAC units where blown off the roof. This is where the winds may have reached 90 mph. The tornado was often less than 25 yards wide but it did widen to a maximum of 1 Reported property and crop damage: about $1,200,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 23, 2014 to May 23, 2014. Affected areas: Maverick. Episode summary: A mesoscale convective system developed over the mountains in northern Mexico and moved across the plains into Texas. This system produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding in Maverick County. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing FM 1021 in Eagle Pass and US Highway 277 near Elm Creek.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 25, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 25, 2014 to May 26, 2014. Affected areas: Bandera, Bastrop, Bexar, Karnes, Uvalde. Episode summary: A late season mid to upper level low moved through the southern plains. Jet streaks around this low provided enough lift to produce thunderstorms across South Central Texas. Surface flow off the Gulf of Mexico produced a very moist environment which led to heavy rainfall and flash flooding. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding. FM187 was closed due to a flooded low water crossing. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing Whartons Dock Rd. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding. Flood waters, filled with debris, closed numerous roads in Medina. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 27, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 27, 2014 to May 27, 2014. Affected areas: Caldwell, Comal, Hays, Travis. Episode summary: A late season mid to upper level low moved through the southern plains. Jet streaks around this low provided enough lift to produce thunderstorms across South Central Texas. Some thunderstorms produced severe size hail. Surface flow off the Gulf of Mexico produced a very moist environment which led to heavy rainfall and flash flooding. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing many low water crossings in eastern Hays County. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing many low water crossings in eastern Comal County. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing many low water crossings in eastern Travis County.

title: High Wind: California, Jun 26, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from June 26, 2014 to June 27, 2014. Affected areas: Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: A strong post-frontal pressure gradient produced high winds in the southeastern Kern County Desert. The California Highway Patrol Weigh Station at Cache Creek reported a peak gust of 78 mph at 141 am PDT. The peak wind at the Mojave Test Pilot School was 69 mph at 141 pm PDT. The peak wind at the Mojave AWOS (KMHV) was 63 mph at 1015 pm PDT.

title: Drought: California, Jun 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from June 01, 2014 to June 30, 2014. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continued in full force during the month of June, 2014. Exceptional drought was detected by the U.S. Drought Monitor for almost the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The 2013-2014 water year (July 1 - June 30) concluded with Fresno setting its second driest on record (4.81 inches) and Bakersfield setting its third driest (2.41 inches). ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, a decrease in the snow-related tourism activity in the Southern Sierra Nevada, reduction in air quality due to persistent stagnant air, loss or reduction of ground water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. For the first time on record, red flag warnings were issued in January for not only the Southern Sierra Nevada and the Tehachapi Mountains but also the south end of the San Joaquin Valley.

title: Wildfire: California, Jun 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from June 01, 2014 to June 02, 2014. Affected areas: S Sierra Foothills. Episode summary: The Hunters wildfire was managed by CalFire. Ignition was 5/26/14 and the cause was unknown. The location was 5 miles south of Coulterville, CA (Mariposa County) and the size was 677 acres. Containment was reached on 6/2 and the cost to containment was $4.4 Million. There were two residences lost and one outbuilding. There were no fatalities and unknown injuries. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000,000.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jul 07, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from July 07, 2014 to July 07, 2014. Affected areas: Pierce. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of Monday, July 7th. These storms became severe as they moved from central to east central Minnesota, and into portions of west central Wisconsin. There was a brief tornado touchdown in southern Washington County at the St. Croix Bluffs Regional Park, and it moved eastward across the St. Croix River and caused minor damage to trees before lifting about a mile into Pierce County. Details: An EF0 tornado continued to move eastward from Washington County, into Pierce County, Wisconsin, where most of the damage was large tree limbs blown down from mature hardwood trees.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 12, 2014 to May 13, 2014. Affected areas: Colorado, Washington. Episode summary: Thunderstorm clusters developed ahead of a slow-moving cold frontal boundary. Details: High rainfall rates with training thunderstorm cells produced street flooding in an around the town of Columbus. There were reports of flooding on numerous county roadways including Schobel Road, FM 2434, and Schulenburg Lane. Power lines were also reported down over Interstate 10 near Columbus. Eight county roads were closed due to high water. FM Road 1155 was closed due to flooding between FM Road 2193 and Chappell Hill. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 26, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 26, 2014 to May 27, 2014. Affected areas: Fort Bend, Harris. Episode summary: A shortwave disturbance produced slow moving clusters of thunderstorms that tracked north and east from the Gulf Coast the afternoon of May 26th and 27th. Details: There was water inundating the roadways around the Grand Parkway and Westpark tollway intersection. There were numerous flooded roadways with water over adjacent sidewalks. Heavy rain caused flash flooding that allowed overflowing water to inundate Telge Road in Tomball.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jun 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, from June 01, 2014 to June 01, 2014. Affected areas: La Crosse, Vernon. Episode summary: During the afternoon and evening of June 1st, thunderstorms with very heavy rain rolled across western Wisconsin. Some of these storms dumped over 3 inches of rain which caused streams in the vicinity of Westby (Vernon County) to rapidly come out of their banks spilling water over some roads. Details: Flooding of low lying agricultural land occurred southwest of Westby after 3 to 5 inches of rain fell in the area. Runoff from heavy rain caused the headwaters of the North Fork of the Bad Axe River to go out of its banks and over Natwick Road. The road had to be closed until the flood waters receded. Flooding occurred along State Higway 56 west of Viola as heavy rains pushed the Bishop Branch of the Cooks Creek and the West Fork of the Kickapoo River out of their banks. Reported property and crop damage: about $11,000.

title: Flood, Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 16, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, Tornado, from June 16, 2014 to June 16, 2014. Affected areas: Grant. Episode summary: A line of severe thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon of June 16th across Minnesota and Iowa. As the storms rolled across western Wisconsin they produced sporadic wind damage and at least 2 tornadoes in Platteville (Grant County) where 5 injuries occurred. The tornadoes caused extensive damage to the University of Wisconsin - Platteville campus and to numerous homes and business near the campus. Damage estimates to the campus alone were near $10 million. The Governor of Wisconsin declared a state of emergency for three southern Wisconsin counties, including Grant. The U.S. Small Business Administration approved a request for a disaster declaration in Grant County. The disaster declaration allows homeowners and businesses to obtain loans to repair or replace damaged or destroyed property. Details: A tornado formed along a squall line west of Platteville, just south of County Road B, and traveled through Memorial Park on to the Univ. of Wisconsin - Platteville campus. Five people were injured, one of them seriously. There was extensive damage done to five buildings and the stadium on campus. Roofs of two new residential halls were partially destroyed and a third residential hall was also da A second tornado (EF1) hit the northeast corner of Platteville, near the Golf and Country Club. The track was about 1/2 mile long with a 50 yard width. Damage included some trees knocked down and a roof off an apartment building. Heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in Boscobel. Reported property and crop damage: about $21,043,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 29, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado, from June 29, 2014 to June 29, 2014. Affected areas: Crawford, Grant, Richland. Episode summary: A cluster of severe thunderstorms developed ahead of an advancing cold front over northeast Iowa during the evening of June 29th. As these storms moved across southwest Wisconsin they produced a tornado near Fennimore (Grant County) that produced considerable tree damage, destroyed several farm outbuildings and damaged three homes. The storms also produced damaging winds that blew over vehicles near Mt. Hope (Grant County) and Fennimore. Barns were blown down near Sinsinawa (Grant County) and Louisburg (Grant County). Details: Runoff from heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in Prairie du Chien. Runoff from heavy rain pushed small streams out of their banks with water over County Highway TB near the intersection with County Highway O south of Richland Center. Runoff from heavy rain overwhelmed culverts and drainage ditches sending water over roads northeast of Eagle Corners. Along State Highway 60 east of the Eagle Corners boat landing, water and small rocks were flowing over the road. Reported property and crop damage: about $466,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Jun 09, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from June 09, 2014 to June 09, 2014. Affected areas: Bowie, Red River. Episode summary: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms redeveloped early Monday morning, June 9th across extreme Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, and Southwest Arkansas, as the nocturnal low level jet interacted with the retreating surface front. While these storms were not severe, they did produce an extended period of locally heavy rainfall especially across northern Bowie County Texas, as well as Little River, northern Miller, and southern Hempstead counties in Southwest Arkansas, where surface gauge and radar estimated determined that widespread 3-6+ inches of rain had fallen in 2-3 hours. As a result, flash flooding was observed just west of Texarkana, TX as well as across much of Little River County Arkansas. A tornado was also produced from these storms in Red River County, Texas. Details: Seventh Street near the Railroad Bridge was flooded and closed in Texarkana. The NWS conducted a storm survey in Red River County, Texas in the town of Avery and determined that the damage was consistent with that of a weak tornado. An EF0 tornado began along CR. 3326 where it snapped numerous trees, damaged the roof of the school gym and a dugout at the baseball field before lifting on the east side of town. Winds were estimated to be near 85 mph. High water was reported on Hwy. 82 between Kings Highway and the Wal-Mart in Nash, Texas. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flood: Texas, May 13, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from May 13, 2014 to May 13, 2014. Affected areas: Nueces. Episode summary: Storms associated with a cold front moved through the Coastal Bend during the early morning hours of May 13th. Rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches in an hour caused flooding of low lying areas in the community of Bishop. Details: KIII-TV sent pictures of flooding of streets in the southeast portion of the community of Bishop. Rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches within an hour caused water to pond in low lying areas. Pictures indicated up to a foot of water standing in the streets.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 26, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 26, 2014 to May 26, 2014. Affected areas: San Patricio, Victoria. Episode summary: As a strong upper level low pressure system settled into New Mexico early on the morning of May 26th, a region of strong upper level divergence between two jet streams aloft was focused over the Victoria Crossroads area. Abundant moisture flowed into the region with a strong southerly low level flow. An area of intense thunderstorms formed over the Victoria area during the morning hours. The storms essentially were stationary for several hours over the northern portion of the city of Victoria and northern Victoria County. Rainfall amounts of 4 to 7 inches of rain fell across northern Victoria County. Flash flooding occurred from Nursery and Mission Valley to the northern portions of the city of Victoria. ||Additional thunderstorms formed over the Coastal Bend in the afternoon. A weak and brief tornado formed west of Sinton. Details: Numerous roadways and subdivisions were flooded from near the community of Nursery to the northern portions of the city of Victoria. Water was as deep as a foot to a foot and a half in these areas. A few of the roads were closed between Victoria and Nursery for a couple of hours. Several cars were stranded in high water in Victoria. NWS storm survey revealed a brief EF-0 tornado touched down in the middle of a farm field with no significant damage. The tornado occurred near the intersection of Highway 188 and County Road 29. A photo from storm spotters in the area confirmed the brief tornado. Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 27, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 27, 2014 to May 27, 2014. Affected areas: Jim Wells. Episode summary: A mesoscale convective system moved into southeast Texas during the morning hours on May 27th. This left an outflow boundary located over south-central Texas by the afternoon. A strong upper level low pressure system was moving across north Texas during the day and a strong upper level jet streak enhanced the low to mid level shear in the atmosphere during the afternoon. A supercell developed south of San Antonio near a merger between the outflow boundary and sea-breeze boundary. The supercell moved to the south-southeast and then south along Highway 281 from Pleasanton down through Alice. The supercell produced large hail at times over Live Oak County. The storm intensified as it approached Alice, causing damage due to large hail and high winds. An EF1 tornado moved across the southeast side of Alice. The storm weakened briefly after leaving Alice but again organized as it moved toward the community of Premont in southern Jim Wells County. Another EF1 tornado occurred near Premont. Details: An EF0 tornado touched down in the city of Premont near the intersection of Northwest 3rd Street and South Cora Street. The tornado traveled south and briefly produced EF1 damage near Southeast 5th Street and Southern Bernice Street. Partial roof damage was observed to a few homes, numerous large tree limbs were snapped, and one tree was completely uprooted.
