title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2014 to May 31, 2014. Affected areas: Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason and 12 more areas. Episode summary: The drought intensified during May across West Central Texas as much of the area experienced extreme to exceptional drought conditions. The exceptional drought conditions included Sutton and Kimble Counties. The impacts from exceptional drought conditions included widespread crop and pasture losses and water emergencies from shortages in reservoirs, streams and wells. Much of the remainder of West Central Texas had extreme drought conditions. The impacts of extreme drought included major crop and pasture losses and widespread water shortages or restrictions. Heavy rainfall occurred across a large part of West Central Texas during the last week of May, with average amounts of 5 to 10 inches. Details: The US Drought Monitor indicated extreme drought conditions across Tom Green County during May. The US Drought Monitor indicated extreme drought conditions across Sterling County during May. The US Drought Monitor indicated exceptional drought conditions across Sutton County during May.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 10, 2014 to May 11, 2014. Affected areas: Coachella Valley, San Diego County Mountains, Santa Ana Mountains And Foothills. title: High Wind: Texas, Jun 09, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from June 09, 2014 to June 09, 2014. Affected areas: Moore. Episode summary: A cold front moved through the Texas Panhandle during the early morning hours of the 9th. The stronger surface pressure gradient and a well-mixed boundary layer allowed strong winds aloft reach the ground around midday. The AWOS near the town of Dumas (Moore County) reported sustained winds of 40 to 42 mph from 11:55 AM CST until 1:55 PM CST. By the early afternoon, the surface pressure gradient decreased sufficiently to prevent any further high winds. Details: Sustained high winds of 40-42 mph at Dumas.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 08, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 08, 2014 to June 08, 2014. Affected areas: Collingsworth. Episode summary: The combination of isentropic lift over a stalled front south of the Texas Panhandle, PWAT values nearing 1.50 inches, and a shortwave propagating eastward proved sufficient to produce heavy rain thunderstorms during the late night hours of the 7th. A cluster of thunderstorms developed across the southern Texas Panhandle and moved eastward. These storms produced sub-severe hail before transitioning to pure heavy rain over the southeastern Texas Panhandle. The heavy rain led to flash flooding in Collingsworth County before the storms exited the Panhandle by 3:30 AM on the 8th. Details: A cluster of thunderstorms brought heavy rain to Collingsworth County during the late night hours of the 7th and early morning hours of the 8th. This heavy rain led to the development of flash flooding across the city of Dodson (Collingsworth County). A law enforcement officer reported a vehicle stalled in flood waters in town. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from May 01, 2014 to May 09, 2014. Affected areas: Val Verde. The news media reported that fire crews were able to successfully defend other structures on several ranch residences in the area. Residents of Pandale were forced to evacuate, but no damage was reported. Details: The Malone Fire in northwestern Val Verde County was brought under control on May 9. title: Tornado: Texas, May 07, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 07, 2014 to May 07, 2014. Affected areas: Wichita. Episode summary: A large upper level trough became established over the western U.S. bringing strong southwest flow across the Southern Plains. At the surface, a north to south oriented dryline became well established across western north Texas. This dryline served as a focus for several rounds of supercell thunderstorms. Sporadic severe wind and hail occurred, along with a couple of brief tornadoes. Details: Storm spotters and chasers observed a brief tornado southwest of Burkburnett. No damage is known to have occurred and the location of the tornado is estimated.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado, from May 23, 2014 to May 27, 2014. Affected areas: Crockett, San Saba, Sterling, Tom Green. Episode summary: A slow moving large upper level low pressure center approached West Central Texas through the period. Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms developed across the area and resulted in damaging winds, hail, and flash flooding. Details: A resident in close proximity saw the tornado as it briefly touched down on top of a nearby ridge. A storm chaser videotaped this tornado. He was located at the intersection of State Highway 163 and FM 2139 as he was looking to the west southwest. He said it only lasted for 90 seconds before it transitioned into the rope stage. Law enforcement reported State Highway 163 was flooded about 4 to 6 miles south of Sterling City.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jul 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from July 14, 2014 to July 14, 2014. Affected areas: Randall. Episode summary: The southern Texas Panhandle saw a round of intense rainfall during the afternoon hours of the 14th. A cold front slowly moving southwestward into the Panhandle combined with a shortwave trough rounding the base of a closed low over the Great Lakes set the stage for convection to develop. The 6 PM CST upper air sounding out of Amarillo (Potter County) showed moderate CAPE of 2673 J/kg, 1.30 inches of PWAT, and weak deep layer shear in place across the Panhandle. As storms approached the southern Texas Panhandle from the north, they encountered an outflow from convection over Northwest Texas. The combined forcing of the outflows allowed storms to intensify and slowed the storm motions. The heavier rainfall and increase residence time over the area lead to widespread flash flooding. This flash flooding dissipated quickly once convection moved into Northwest Texas by 10 PM CST. Details: The convergence of two outflow boundaries over the city of Amarillo (Potter and Randall County) produced thunderstorms capable of producing very intense rainfall. These storms also moved very slowly to the south after developing which allowed for a longer residency time over the city. The intense rainfall caused flash flooding to occur across the southwest side of town. title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, May 26, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from May 26, 2014 to May 26, 2014. Affected areas: Marathon, Marinette. Episode summary: Slow-moving thunderstorms developed in a warm, humid air mass ahead of a cold front. The storms produced as much as 4.75 inches of rain near Porterfield (Marinette Co.). Farm fields were flooded and low-lying roads were covered by water. Heavy rainfall also caused flooding of low-lying areas west of Marathon City (Marathon Co.).||In addition to the heavy rainfall, the storms produced small hail, and winds of 50 mph that uprooted a few trees in the wet soil. Details: Thunderstorms produced small hail and two periods of heavy rainfall with up to 4.75 inches of rain in the Porterfield area. Runoff from the heavy rain caused lowland flooding in the Townships of Porterfield, Lake and Grover. Wind gusts to 50 mph uprooted some trees in the saturated soil. Runoff from heavy rainfall caused flooding of lowland areas just west of Marathon City. A car traveling at a high rate of speed had its bumper removed after the vehicle hit water on the road.

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 01, 2014 to June 30, 2014. Affected areas: Bandera, Edwards, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Llano, Medina, Val Verde. Episode summary: June brought beneficial rain to much of South Central Texas with the Rio Grande Plains experiencing a near record rainfall event near the end of the month. With the wet weather, no county worsened during the month and Val Verde (Extreme Category (D3)), Bandera, Edwards, Kerr, Llano, and Medina (all Severe (D2)) Counties improved. Episode summary: During the early afternoon hours of July 23rd, a complex of showers and thunderstorms moved southeast into Eastern Oklahoma and Northwest Arkansas, after originally developing early that morning across portions of Nebraska and central Kansas. This complex encountered a very unstable air mass near a weak surface trough over Northern and Eastern Oklahoma and Northern Arkansas as it continued southeastward. At the same time, other scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over Central and Eastern Arkansas near this surface trough, while also aided by a weak upper level disturbance sinking south across Arkansas and the Mid-Mississippi Valley. The Eastern Oklahoma storm complex absorbed the growing storm complex over Central Arkansas, resulting in a large mesoscale convective system (MCS) intensifying and surging south into Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas during the mid and late afternoon hours. Widespread wind damage was reported across much of Central and Southern Arkansas as well as Southeast Oklahoma, with a large cold pool of air surging south into Northeast Texas and North Louisiana by late afternoon and early evening. Wind gusts ranged from 50-70 mph with this MCS as it surged south across much of the Ark-La-Tex, resulting in numerous downed trees, power lines, and structural damage. This storm complex weakened during the early evening hours, although the resultant cold pool still produced 40-45 mph wind gusts which produced minor tree damage over portions of Deep East Texas that did not see showers or thunderstorms. Prior to the start of the rainy weather, many locations across the Texas Panhandle were experiencing 3 to 4 year precipitation deficits rivaling those of the worst periods during the 1930s Dust Bowl and 1950s droughts of record. By the end of May though, some areas recorded greater than 150 percent of normal precipitation for the month. Short-term dryness continued in the northern and eastern Texas Panhandle. Widespread Exceptional (D4) Drought conditions at the start of May improved to a mix of Extreme (D3) and Exceptional Drought conditions at the end of the month. Farmers were rushing to plant summer crops, while most winter wheat had either been lost due to spring dryness or was being harvested. Rangeland quickly greened up following the rain, though range and pastures continued to be rated mostly in poor condition following several years of drought. Episode summary: During a rather dry April and first week of May, little to no rainfall was recorded over the center of the Rio Grande Valley and Deep South Texas. The lack of rain, combined with temperatures in the 90s and lower 100s and afternoon humidity in the teens and twenties, as well as periods of gusty north winds up to 25 mph, allowed the return of Severe (D2) drought conditions to return to the region to start May. The remainder of the region remained dry with D1 and D0 conditions expanding in area. ||The severe D2 drought conditions were short lived as rain fell across the region on May 9th and 10th, eliminating the D2 conditions by the 13th. Details: Dry conditions throughout April and the first week of May, allowed for Severe (D2) drought conditions to develop over southern Brooks County. Dry conditions throughout April and the first week of May, allowed for Severe (D2) drought conditions to develop over southeastern Jim Hogg County. Dry conditions throughout April and the first week of May, allowed for Severe (D2) drought conditions to develop over northern Starr County.

title: Heat: Wisconsin, Jul 22, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heat, from July 22, 2014 to July 22, 2014. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Green, Green Lake, Iowa, Jefferson, Lafayette, Marquette, Rock, Sauk. Episode summary: Gusty west to southwest winds brought a hot and very humid airmass into southern Wisconsin just ahead of an approaching cold front. High temperatures in the upper 80s to lower 90s and dewpoints in the middle to upper 70s resulted in heat index values in the lower 100s for portions of southern Wisconsin. Details: Heat Index values in the lower 100s. Heat Index values in the lower to middle 100s.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2014 to May 31, 2014. Affected areas: Aransas, Calhoun, Goliad, Refugio, Victoria. Episode summary: Above normal rainfall occurred over most of South Texas during the month of May. Below normal rainfall occurred in eastern Calhoun County and northern La Salle County. Rainfall amounts of 5 to 6 inches occurred over portions of the Brush Country, Coastal Bend, and western Victoria Crossroads. Higher amounts of 8 to 10 inches occurred over Goliad and Victoria Counties. This rainfall reduced the area of severe drought over the Victoria Crossroads by the end of the month. Details: Severe drought remained over the northern half of the county. Severe drought remained over the extreme southeast part of the county. Severe drought ended over the county by the latter part of the month.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jul 27, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from July 27, 2014 to July 27, 2014. Affected areas: Winnebago. Episode summary: A very weak and brief waterspout formed under a rain shower over southern Lake Winnebago. The shower developed as a result of an upper level low pressure system that was over Wisconsin. Details: A very weak and brief waterspout formed under a rain shower over southern Lake Winnebago, about 5 miles southeast of Oshkosh. The waterspout, which was photographed, was on the water for just a few seconds then dissipated. The parent funnel was seen by hundreds of people across the area. No damage occurred.

title: Drought: Texas, Aug 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from August 01, 2014 to August 31, 2014. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall and 12 more areas. Episode summary: A mix of improved and worsened drought conditions occurred across the area throughout August. Scattered thunderstorm activity brought bouts of heavy rain for some areas, but others unfortunately missed out. Minor improvement took place in the far southwest Panhandle and northern South Plains, going from moderate (D1) drought to abnormally dry (D0) conditions. Portions of the South Plains, south and west of Lubbock, saw deterioration back into extreme (D3) conditions. Severe (D2) drought encompassed the remainder of the South Plains with mainly extreme (D3) conditions remaining in the Rolling Plains. A portion of Cottle into extreme Northeast King County continued to experience exceptional (D4) drought conditions.||Warmer and drier than average weather plagued the region through much of August, with only scattered thunderstorm activity occurring on select days. Lubbock and Childress experienced monthly average temperatures of 1.9 and 1.3 degrees above average, respectively. The most significant rainfall event took place on the 28th as a complex of thunderstorms developed, but this was mainly confined to areas east of the Caprock Escarpment where 1 to 2 inches of rainfall fell thus contributing to much if not all of the monthly rainfall total for many locations. Widespread Keetch-Byram Drought Index Values of 400-500 were in place by month's end with portions of the Southern South Plains and Rolling Plains approaching the 500-600 range. An area of 300-400 was in place in the Northern South Plains with locales in the Far Southwestern Panhandle near the 200-300 category.||Green fuels and normal to slightly above normal moisture values kept fire concerns low for the most part, although a few locations that

title: Drought: Texas, Aug 01, 2014
text: in place in the Northern South Plains with locales in the Far Southwestern Panhandle near the 200-300 category.||Green fuels and normal to slightly above normal moisture values kept fire concerns low for the most part, although a few locations that missed out on any rainfall saw modest curing of grasses. The increased heat units this month helped cotton farmers and peanut producers, but dryland farmers relied heavily on irrigation with the lack of rainfall. An increase in lightning-induced wildfires occurred as well with the deteriorating rangeland. title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 12, 2014 to June 13, 2014. Affected areas: Mclennan. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours on Thursday, generally south of an outflow boundary which stretched roughly along Interstate 20. Several storms became severe, producing mostly large hail. Thunderstorms continued into the overnight hours producing locally heavy rain and some flash flooding in the Waco area. An 18 year old male was killed in Waco when his vehicle was swept away by flood waters. Details: Flat Creek near the intersection of Hewitt Drive and Mars Drive, behind Midway High School, flooded over the roadway. The creek also overflowed near the intersection of Panther Way and Panther Run. It was reported that the creek overflowed by at least half a mile, was up to 2 feet over at least one road, and the water was swiftly flowing over the road; like a river. Several cars were stuck in the Waco police department was closing I-35 South at New Road due to flooding. Castleman Creek in Hewitt overflowed its banks due to heavy rainfall and flooded Hewitt Park. It was reported that the water was as high as the 4-foot-tall disc golf baskets in some areas. The flood waters flooded the park restrooms. A 40-foot-long section of Earle Street near the creek had to be replaced after the flood waters ripped up the road and moved it about 100 feet. Reported property and crop damage: about $230,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Jun 22, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from June 22, 2014 to June 22, 2014. Affected areas: Bosque, Hill, Hood, Johnson, Mclennan, Parker. Episode summary: An upper level low pressure system worked its way slowly east across Texas the weekend of June 21-22. A combination of abundant moisture and the slow movement of the system generated localized areas of heavy rain and flash flooding. Significant flash flooding occurred in southern Parker County and in Hood County. Several people had to be rescued from their homes in Hood County and at least 7 homes were destroyed by flood waters in Hood County. Details: County Road 1116, located southwest of Cleburne, was being closed due to high water. Over 4 inches of rain was estimated in the area. Water was reported over CR 1121 just to the east of FM 2331. Over 3 inches of rain was estimated in the area. Timber Wild Drive in Brock was being barricaded due to an estimated 10 of water over the road. Ox Mill Creek Road was also being barricaded. Water was also reported over Old Dennis Road and Daniel Road. A vehicle became trapped in high water on Old Brock Road. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,080,000.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Jun 24, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from June 24, 2014 to June 24, 2014. Affected areas: Mclennan, Tarrant. Episode summary: A stationary front draped across central portions of North Texas served as a focus for thunderstorm development on Tuesday afternoon. Meanwhile a second thunderstorm complex advanced from the northwest. Several thunderstorms became severe, namely in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, with damaging winds being the primary occurrence. Flash flooding also occurred in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. Much of the western portions of Fort Worth were flooded by flash flood waters. Details: Significant urban flash flood occurred as 2-3 inches of rain in less than 2 hours fell over the western half of Tarrant County. Social media reports showed significant flooding near Hulen and Bryce Streets in Fort Worth. Some roads in downtown Fort Worth were impassable and blocked by the fire department. In the West 7th district, the water was reported to be several feet deep. Many vehicles were A few roads in Bellmead were under water due to heavy rainfall over a 1-2 hour period. A few roads in Robinson were under water due to heavy rainfall over a 1-2 hour period. Reported property and crop damage: about $595,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Jun 25, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from June 25, 2014 to June 25, 2014. Affected areas: Denton, Ellis, Navarro, Tarrant. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms developed Wednesday and moved slowly from south to north, once again producing urban flash flooding in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex. Details: Water was flowing over the Interstate 45 access road in Palmer. High water rescues were being conducted in Arlington near North Cooper Street and West Randol Mill Road. Several homes along the creek in Trophy Club had 4-6 of water inside of them. Reported property and crop damage: about $200,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Jun 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from June 30, 2014 to June 30, 2014. Affected areas: Gray, Hutchinson. Episode summary: Outflow from severe thunderstorms led to brief high wind conditions for isolated locations in the Texas Panhandle during the late night hours of the 30th. This outflow led to the Borger (Hutchinson County) ASOS to reported sustained 41 mph winds for one hour ending at 11 PM CST. This outflow also caused a 66 mph high wind gust at the TXDOT AWOS site 2 miles east-southeast of Pampa (Gray County) at 10:55 PM CST. Details: High wind gust of 66 mph at Pampa. Sustained 41 mph wind at Borger.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 17, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 17, 2014 to June 17, 2014. Affected areas: Gaines. Episode summary: Good moisture was present across the area, and there was intense heating which helped to increase the instability. Upper level disturbances moved over the area which helped to increase lift. These conditions combined to produce flash flooding and severe wind gusts across the northwest Permian Basin. Details: Heavy rain moved across Gaines County and produced flash flooding south of Seminole. One to one and a half feet of water was reported to be running over Highway 385. No damage was reported so the cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 18, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 18, 2014 to June 18, 2014. Affected areas: Midland. Episode summary: Upper level disturbances were moving over the region which provided a source of upper lift. There was a dryline present which provided a focus for thunderstorms to develop, and there was plentiful moisture available east of the dryline. Winds were increasing and turning with height which allowed for more organized storms to develop. These conditions resulted in large hail, severe wind gusts, and flash flooding across the Permian Basin. Details: Heavy rain moved across Midland County and produced flash flooding in Midland. Water rose to the doors of Fannin Elementary School. Portions of Wadley Avenue were flooded curb to curb and at one to one and a half feet deep. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate since no damage was reported. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jun 18, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from June 18, 2014 to June 18, 2014. Affected areas: Portage. Episode summary: Thunderstorms formed north of a stationary front, that was over southern Wisconsin, and produced heavy rainfall, isolated large hail and wind damage. Large hail fell for more than 20 minutes at Plover (Portage Co.). Heavy rain from the storms caused minor urban flooding in Stevens Point (Portage Co.). Some of the highest measured 24-hour rainfall totals, ending around 0700 CST, included 3.80 inches at Babcock (Wood Co.), 3.45 inches near Vesper (Wood Co.), 2.46 inches at Pittsville (Wood Co.), 2.41 inches northeast of Wild Rose (Waushara Co.), 2.32 inches at Almond (Portage Co.), and 2.23 inches at Plover. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall that caused minor urban flooding in Stevens Point.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jul 06, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from July 06, 2014 to July 06, 2014. Affected areas: Oneida. Episode summary: A cold front moved into a moderately unstable airmass and produced thunderstorms over north-central Wisconsin. Some of the storms produced penny to nickel size hail, wind damage, and heavy rain that caused urban flooding. Details: A line of thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall in the Rhinelander area as it slowly moved to the south. The rain caused street flooding in downtown Rhinelander. A few miles west of downtown Rhinelander, the automated weather observation system at Rhinelander Airport recorded 1.55 inches of rain in 19 minutes, including 0.81 inch in just five minutes between 7:02 PM and 7:07 PM CDT.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Jun 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from June 23, 2014 to June 30, 2014. Affected areas: La Crosse. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the early evening hours of June 23rd across western Wisconsin. Some of these storms produced funnel clouds over the northern sections of the city of La Crosse (La Crosse County). Details: Runoff from heavy rain and inflow from tributary streams pushed the Mississippi River out of its banks in La Crosse. The flooding continued into July with the crest occurring in July as well. The flooding closed 130 of the 400 campsites at Goose Island County Park and all 300 of the campsites at Pettibone Campground.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Jun 25, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from June 25, 2014 to June 25, 2014. Affected areas: Refugio. Episode summary: A weak upper level disturbance moved into South Texas and interacted with deep tropical moisture over the region. Scattered thunderstorms developed over the Brush Country to the coastal plains. A strong storm formed over Refugio County and produced a weak tornado. The slow moving storm produced very heavy rainfall that led to flooding over rural northeast portions of the county. Details: NWS storm survey and local video concluded an EF0 tornado, with winds estimated at 65 MPH briefly touched down in north Refugio. It touched down near the intersection of west Heard Street and north Alamo Street. The tornado removed the roof and collapsed the north facing exterior wall of one mobile home. Minor shingle damage was observed on a couple of homes along east Houston Street. Several larg Public reported county roads covered with a foot of water in places to the northeast of Refugio. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Dust Storm: California, Jul 06, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, from July 06, 2014 to July 06, 2014. Affected areas: Lower Colorado River Valley, Riverside County Eastern Deserts. Episode summary: Late afternoon and evening thunderstorms generated strong gusty outflow winds which moved into the deserts of eastern Riverside county and created dust storm conditions. Gusty east winds in excess of 40 mph were sufficient to drop visibilities to one quarter mile or below in dense blowing dust and sand, creating very hazardous driving conditions along the Interstate 10 corridor from Blythe westward to Eagle Mountain. Details: Strong thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon hours across southwest Arizona, and they generated strong gusty easterly outflow winds in excess of 40 mph. The gusty winds spread into portions of the lower Colorado River valley, including Blythe, and created dust storm conditions. At 1716MST a trained spotter 2 miles west of Blythe reported a dust storm at the Blythe airport. title: Flood: Wisconsin, Jun 28, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from June 28, 2014 to June 28, 2014. Affected areas: La Crosse. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed across western Wisconsin during the evening hours of June 28th ahead of a trough of low pressure. Several of these storms produced high winds that caused considerable damage in the city of La Crosse north into Holmen (La Crosse County). Numerous trees and power lines were blown down by winds that gusted to at least 60 mph. At least 7,000 customers in the La Crosse area were without power. The power outage took out street lights and stop lights across much of the city. Details: Runoff from heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in the city of La Crosse. The heavy rain also flooded the building of a local food pantry destroying some of the food that was stored in the building. Reported property and crop damage: about $40,000.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Jun 21, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from June 21, 2014 to June 22, 2014. Affected areas: Brewster, Midland. Episode summary: Upper level disturbances moved over the region which provided lift. There was a plentiful supply of continuous moisture that came into the area, and there was good instability especially across the higher terrain. These conditions allowed for flash flooding to develop across the Permian Basin and Davis Mountains. Details: Heavy rain moved across Midland County and produced flash flooding near Greenwood. There was one and a half feet of water over the intersection of Highway 307 and Farm to Market Road 1090. Cars were stalled as a result of this flooding. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain moved across Brewster County and produced flash flooding near Alpine. A pasture was flooded. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. There was heavy rain near Alpine and one to one and a quarter of an inch of rain fell in 50 minutes. Reported property and crop damage: about $6,500.

title: Flood: Texas, Jun 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from June 23, 2014 to June 23, 2014. Affected areas: Hemphill. Episode summary: A slow moving supercell thunderstorm produced periods of heavy rain over Hemphill County during the afternoon hours of the 22nd. This heavy rain led to the Canadian River to rise above banks at the town of Canadian (Hemphill County) by 7:30 AM on the 23rd. Details: Reports state two female horseback riders (one 24 years old the other 6 years old) traveling along the banks went missing prior to noon on Monday June 23rd. By 7 PM that day, search and rescue crews located the still saddled horse the females were last seen riding downstream of the US 60 bridge spanning the Canadian River. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from June 22, 2014 to June 22, 2014. Affected areas: Hemphill, Lipscomb, Roberts. A discrete supercell developed over the Oklahoma Panhandle during the early afternoon hours of the 22nd. The outflow from this tornadic supercell interacted with discrete storms developing along a southward moving cold front over western Kansas, and caused the storms to transition into a linear structure. This line would enter the central Oklahoma Panhandle and north central Texas Panhandle around 8 PM CST. Both the line of thunderstorms and the tornadic supercell moved southward across the Texas Panhandle before the tornadic supercell joined with line around 11 PM CST. The combined line moved southward and exited the southern Texas Panhandle around 1 AM CST on the 23rd. Details: A slow moving supercell thunderstorm moved southward across the eastern Texas Panhandle during the evening hours of the 22nd. This supercell produced multiple brief tornadoes over the course of several hours. This tornado began in extreme eastern Roberts County where it produced light damage at a ranch house. title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jun 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from June 23, 2014 to June 24, 2014. Affected areas: Brewster. Episode summary: The edge of an upper ridge was over southeast New Mexico and West Texas as an upper level disturbance moved over the area. Several outflow boundaries were across the area which provided a focus for thunderstorms to develop. There was good low level moisture present and the atmosphere was unstable. These conditions resulted in high wind gusts and heavy rain. Details: Heavy rain fell across Brewster County near Alpine. Almost one inch of rain fell in fifteen minutes. This rain caused minor street flooding.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jun 24, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from June 24, 2014 to June 25, 2014. Affected areas: Ector, Jeff Davis. Episode summary: Upper level disturbances moved over the region, and there was plentiful moisture and instability present. Lift was also enhanced by upslope winds coming into the higher terrain. These conditions contributed to large hail and severe winds across West Texas. Details: Heavy rain fell in Odessa with a quarter to a half an inch falling in 20 minutes. Heavy rain fell across Jeff Davis County and produced minor flooding across low water crossings near Fort Davis.

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 01, 2014 to June 30, 2014. Affected areas: Anderson, Bell, Bosque, Collin, Comanche, Cooke, Coryell, Dallas, Denton, Eastland, Ellis, Erath and 20 more areas. Episode summary: A slight improvement in drought conditions occurred over the south-central and southeastern counties, while the rest of the region remained mostly unchanged in the Severe and Extreme drought categories. Details: Extreme/D3 conditions affected all of Cooke County for the entire month of June 2014. Extreme/D3 conditions affected all of Grayson County for the entire month of June 2014. Extreme/D3 conditions affected all of Wise County for the entire month of June 2014. Reported property and crop damage: about $55,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Jul 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 01, 2014 to July 31, 2014. Affected areas: Hidalgo, Starr. Episode summary: Less than half an inch of rain was reported by a CoCoRaHS observer W of Rio Grande City during all of June, with all of it falling on one day. Overall dry conditions and little rain led to the development of Severe (D2) drought conditions developing across the Upper Valley by the beginning of July. Details: A general lack of rainfall and hot conditions allowed for Severe (D2) drought conditions to return to the eastern half of Starr County by the beginning of July. The remainder of the county continued to experience Moderate (D1) drought conditions. A stripe of Severe (D2) drought conditions developed by the beginning of July, along the far western county border and would remain through the remainder of the month. The far SE corner of the county experienced abnormally dry (D0) conditions, with the remainder of the county in Moderate (D1) drought conditions.

title: Drought: Texas, Jul 09, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 09, 2014 to July 31, 2014. Affected areas: Starr. Episode summary: While some welcome rain did fall over the area during the first half of July, it would not be enough to prevent the spread of intensifying drought conditions. By the end of the first full week of July, the area of Severe (D2) drought conditions had grown larger, as drier conditions spread further west across the Upper Valley. Details: Nearly all of Starr County was covered in Severe (D2) drought conditions by the end of the first full week of July. Only a tiny sliver of Moderate (D1) drought conditions remained along the far northern county border. Drought conditions would hold steady through the remainder of the month.

title: Drought: Texas, Jun 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 01, 2014 to June 17, 2014. Affected areas: Rains, Van Zandt. Episode summary: Drought conditions improved over several locations across the central and eastern portions of the region due to beneficial rains received during June of 2014. Details: Severe/D2 conditions improved to D1/moderate during the second week of June. Severe/D2 conditions in place over Van Zandt County improved to Moderate/D1 during the second week of June, 2014. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Aug 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from August 03, 2014 to August 03, 2014. Affected areas: Riverside. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed across portions of central Riverside county during the late morning hours on August 3rd, and they intensified into the early afternoon, producing very heavy rainfall. Rain rates were in excess of 2 inches per hour at times, and the heavy rain produced flash flooding affecting towns such as Eagle Mountain, Desert Center, Cottonwood Visitor's Center and Chiriaco Summit. Flash Flooding was also observed along the Interstate 10 corridor from Desert Center westward past Chiriaco Summit. Locally heavy rain flooded roads, spread dirt and debris onto area highways and led to road closures. Eagle Mountain road was closed as the heavy rain raised up asphalt and washed it away near mile marker 192. Multiple Flash Flood Warnings were issued for central Riverside county due to the heavy rain and observed flooding. Details: Thunderstorms developed across portions of central Riverside county during the late morning hours on August 3rd, and they produced locally heavy rainfall which led to flash flooding. Some of the more significant flooding occurred along the Interstate 10 corridor to the south of the Cottonwood Visitor's Center. According to the California Department of Highways, at approximately 1327PST, flash floo Thunderstorms developed across portions of central Riverside county during the late morning hours on August 3rd, and they intensified into the early afternoon. The storms produced heavy rains which led to flash flooding; the most significant flooding affected the Interstate 10 corridor in the area around Desert Center. Flash Flood Warnings were issued for a substantial portion of central Riverside Reported property and crop damage: about $60,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Jun 06, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from June 06, 2014 to June 06, 2014. Affected areas: Hartley, Ochiltree. Episode summary: The combination of a stationary front, upper level shortwave, and an unstable environment helped to initiate thunderstorms across the Texas Panhandle during the evening hours of the 6th and into the early morning hours of the 7th. The stationary front provided a focusing mechanism for discrete thunderstorms to develop across the western and northern Texas Panhandle around 5 PM CST. The SPC Mesoanalysis page showed roughly 3000 J/kg of CAPE and 40-50kts (46-60mph) of deep layer shear across the Panhandle. Within this environment the storms quickly became severe producing large hail and damaging wind. Low level helicity also allowed two storms to produce brief tornadoes. Given the high amount of deep layer shear the discrete cells developed into a broken line of storms as they moved across the Texas Panhandle. The broken line was completely into western Oklahoma by 10 PM CST. Residual boundaries and another shortwave allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop during the early morning hours of the 7th with a few becoming severe. All convection diminished by daybreak on the 7th. Details: A discrete supercell developed during the evening hours of the 6th. As the storm intensified it produced a brief tornado over the rural portions of Hartley County. Due to the location of the tornado, minimal damage was located however multiple eye witnesses reported the tornado. The winds were estimated at 65 mph. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from July 16, 2014 to July 16, 2014. Affected areas: Moore, Sherman. As the evening progressed, the outflows from storms pushed the warm front southward across the Panhandle. Severe convection ended around 9 PM CST as storms transitioned to heavy rain production. title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jul 16, 2014

title: Tornado: Texas, Jun 11, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from June 11, 2014 to June 11, 2014. Affected areas: Tom Green. Episode summary: A surface trough and dryline combined with a very unstable airmass and produced bow echo type severe thunderstorms across West Central Texas. A damaging macroburst formed as the storms interacted with a hot and dry sub cloud layer. The downburst winds extended from 1 mile northwest of Carlsbad to 3 miles east northeast of Wall and damaged the north half of the City of San Angelo with thunderstorm winds gusting to around 95 mph. A couple of weak tornadoes formed on the leading edge of the damaging winds or the bow echo. The downburst was approximately 7 miles wide by 22 miles long. A severe thunderstorm with damaging thunderstorm winds also produced a haboob or a wall of dust as it impacted Rotan. Details: The twister damaged roof coverings, road signs, fences and trees. There was evidence of cyclonic circulation superimposed on the large scale damaging winds that affected much of northern San Angelo. The wind speed was estimated to be near 85 mph. A tornado was observed and videotaped just north of FM 388 and just west of Loop 306. The tornado moved east southeast across Loop 306 before dissipating.

Episode summary: The California drought continued in full force during the month of July, 2014. Exceptional drought was detected by the U.S. Drought Monitor for almost the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The 2013-2014 water year (July 1 - June 30) concluded with Fresno setting its second driest on record (4.81 inches) and Bakersfield setting its third driest (2.41 inches). ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, a decrease in the snow-related tourism activity in the Southern Sierra Nevada, reduction in air quality due to persistent stagnant air, loss or reduction of ground water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. For the first time on record, red flag warnings were issued in January for not only the Southern Sierra Nevada and the Tehachapi Mountains but also the south end of the San Joaquin Valley.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from June 01, 2014 to June 30, 2014. Episode summary: The wet summer pattern continued through June for most of the Texas Panhandle, with most locations measuring at least 3 to 4 inches of rain for the month. Some parts of the Panhandle received greater than 6 inches of rain, or greater than twice the monthly average for June. A mix of Extreme (D3) to Exceptional (D4) Drought conditions at the start of June improved to mostly Severe (D2) and Extreme (D3)Drought conditions at the end of the month. A band of Exceptional (D4) Drought remained from Gray County northwestward to Dallam County. Amarillo recorded 5.40 inches of precipitation for the month (2.24 inches above normal), Dalhart recorded 3.77 inches of precipitation (1.47 inches above normal), and Borger recorded 3.17 inches of precipitation (0.55 inches above normal).||Soil moisture was rated from short to adequate during the month. Crops were mostly benefiting from the rains, but were running behind in areas that were too wet or too dry. title: Heavy Rain, Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 29, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, Tornado, from June 29, 2014 to June 29, 2014. Affected areas: Dane, Iowa, Sauk. Episode summary: A cluster of supercellular storms caused 3 tornadoes, and downburst wind damage over south central WI during the late evening. Details: The typical street flooding and standing water occurred in Baraboo with heavy rainfall. A sporadic path of EF-2 tornado damage. Up to six power poles snapped. A large camper-trailer destroyed and tossed 100 yards. A well-built metal building significantly damaged, with debris landing on cars. Other smaller sheds destroyed. A swath of sporadic to continuous tornado damage. There was extensive tree damage including numerous large pine trees snapped. Half of a roof was torn off of a large barn and half a roof torn off a pole barn. A grain elevator was blown off of a silo. A six inch diameter tree landed on a car. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,950,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jun 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from June 30, 2014 to June 30, 2014. Affected areas: Dane. Episode summary: A large scale bow echo raced east to northeast across southern WI, causing straight line wind damage in many areas. We Energies reported a maximum power outage of 110000 homes which has not happened since 2005. The outages were due to straight line winds and lightning impacting the power lines. Details: Many side streets in downtown Madison and near east side with standing or rushing water. 2.25-2.49 inches of rain in 30 minutes.

title: Flood, Heavy Rain: California, Aug 21, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, Heavy Rain, from August 21, 2014 to August 21, 2014. Affected areas: Imperial. Episode summary: A line of thunderstorms developed across south central Imperial county during the early afternoon hours on August 21st and they affected communities such as Imperial and El Centro. The stronger storms produced damaging microburst winds estimated to be in excess of 60 mph. The peak thunderstorm wind gusts were sufficient to blow down numerous power poles as well as overturn semi-trailer trucks on area highways such as Interstate 8. In addition to the strong winds, some storms produced large hail as well as locally heavy rainfall. The heavy rainfall led to episodes of both flash flooding and flooding which covered much of central and eastern Imperial county. Numerous roads were closed during the afternoon and evening hours due to the flooding. No injuries were reported due to the strong winds or flooding. Details: Thunderstorms developed across portions of south central Imperial county during the afternoon hours on August 21st, and some of them affected the communities of Imperial and El Centro. The stronger storms produced locally heavy rain with rain rates approaching 2 inches per hour. The storms led to significant urban flooding as well as the issuance of Flash Flood Warnings. According to the Imperial Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across much of Imperial county during the afternoon hours, and they persisted into the evening on August 21st. The storms produced locally heavy rainfall with peak rain rates well in excess of one inch per hour. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from September 04, 2014 to September 04, 2014. Affected areas: Dane. Episode summary: A cluster of strong and slow moving thunderstorms moved across southern WI during the morning hours due to the passage of a warm front. Details: A few flooded streets or standing water on streets in the low lying areas of Madison.

title: Wildfire: California, Jul 25, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from July 25, 2014 to July 31, 2014. Affected areas: Motherlode/Camptonville To Groveland. Weather conditions combined with very dry fuels allowed Sand Fire incident to grow into 4,240 acres in Amador and El Dorado Counties. Details: The Sand Fire began east of Highway 49, 5 miles north of Plymouth (south of Placerville) on the afternoon of July 25th. The fire was caused by a vehicle driving into dry vegetation, and was considered a CalFire incident. text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from July 11, 2014 to July 26, 2014. Affected areas: Mountains Southwest Shasta County To Northern Lake County. Episode summary: A warming trend developed Friday, July 11th and into the weekend from a warm high pressure system building westward over California. This resulted in temperatures in the 90s to low 100s with dry weather. Weather conditions combined with very dry fuels allowed the ignited Bully Fire to grow rapidly over several days. Details: The Bully Fire in Shasta County began on the afternoon of July 11th as weather conditions were becoming drier and warmer. The fire started near Plantina Road at Bland Road west of Igo and Ono communities, caused by a vehicle driving over dry vegetation. By the time it was contained, the fire grew 12,661 acres, destroyed 20 structures, injured 21 people, and resulted in 1 death. The fire was estima

title: Wildfire: California, Jul 04, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from July 04, 2014 to July 04, 2014. Affected areas: Carquinez Strait And Delta. Episode summary: Dry and warm weather conditions with gusty west-southwest winds of 10 to 20 mph gusts to 25mph helped to fan the flame of a fire in Collinsville, CA. Details: A wildfire broke out in the town of Collinsville around 2pm on July 4th, which destroyed 8 homes, damaged 3 more homes, burned boats and vehicles. The fire displaced 25 residents and caused an estimated 2.5 million dollars in damage. The cause of the fire was unknown, though the dry and windy conditions (20-25mph gusts) along with 4th of July celebrations may have been a factor. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,500,000.

title: Drought: California, Aug 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from August 01, 2014 to August 31, 2014. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continued in full force during the month of August, 2014. Exceptional drought was detected by the U.S. Drought Monitor for almost the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The 2013-2014 water year (July 1 - June 30) concluded with Fresno setting its second driest on record (4.81 inches) and Bakersfield setting its third driest (2.41 inches). ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, a decrease in the snow-related tourism activity in the Southern Sierra Nevada, reduction in air quality due to persistent stagnant air, loss or reduction of ground water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. For the first time on record, red flag warnings were issued in January for not only the Southern Sierra Nevada and the Tehachapi Mountains but also the south end of the San Joaquin Valley.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 07, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from July 07, 2014 to July 07, 2014. Affected areas: Harris. Episode summary: A funnel cloud developed early in the morning, then isolated severe thunderstorms formed in the early evening hours. Details: Heavy rain (an estimated three inches) from a slow moving thunderstorm produced localized street flooding. There was up to two feet of water over the road along Avenue D in Katy.

title: Wildfire: California, Aug 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from August 01, 2014 to August 04, 2014. Affected areas: S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns. The fire burned 4689 acres, of which 1092 acres were in Yosemite National Park and 3597 acres in Stanislaus National Forest. The cause is under investigation. There were 2 structures lost and no fatalities. Cost of containment was $10.6 million.

There were no structures lost and no fatalities. Cost of containment was $21.4 million.

title: Wildfire: California, Aug 18, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from August 18, 2014 to August 27, 2014. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns. The cause is under investigation. There were 12 structures lost and no fatalities. Cost of containment was $6.9 million.

title: Wildfire: California, Aug 18, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from August 18, 2014 to August 25, 2014. Affected areas: S Sierra Foothills. Episode summary: The Junction wildfire started on August 18, 2014 and was contained on August 25, 2014. The fire was located 1 mile northwest of Oakhurst in Madera County. It burned 612 acres. There were 47 structures destroyed and 6 damaged. Many of the structures were outbuildings, motor homes and storage containers. There were no fatalities. The cost of containment was $4.9 million.

It was being managed for resource benefit, but began being actively contained after the El Portal fire started nearby on July 26, 2014. It was fully contained on August 19, 2014. title: Tornado: Texas, Jul 21, 2014

Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jul 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from July 03, 2014 to July 03, 2014. Affected areas: Harris. Episode summary: Atmospheric conditions, with the collision of outflow boundaries originating from previous storms, created an environment conducive to the formation of slow-moving clusters of thunderstorms. Heavy rainfall from this activity caused street flooding on the west side of Houston. Details: Heavy rain caused several streets to flood in and around the Spring Branch area. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jul 17, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from July 17, 2014 to July 18, 2014. Affected areas: Brazos, Trinity, Walker. Episode summary: A southern plains shortwave disturbance moving into a very moistened central and eastern Texas environment allowed clusters of central Texas thunderstorms to form and move eastward. These storms produced locally heavy rainfall that caused flash flooding across portions of southeast Texas. Details: Heavy rains caused area roads to flood in and around the College Station area, including portions of SH 6 and Tauber Road. Some water rescues were reported along with water in some cars and homes. High water on roads SW of Huntsville. Public report of 7.99 inches of rain was received. Heavy rain caused flash flooding between Groveton and Apple Springs. Sections of FM 94 were under water, and some flooding was reported in and around the Apple Springs area. Reported property and crop damage: about $55,000.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Jul 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from July 01, 2014 to July 07, 2014. Affected areas: La Crosse. Episode summary: Rivers that went over flood stage in late June from excessive runoff, remained in flood to begin July. The flooding subsided in the first week of the month along the Mississippi River. Details: Flooding that began in late June on the Mississippi River in La Crosse ended in the first week of July when the river went below the flood stage. The river crested 1.5 feet above the flood stage at 13.48 feet. The high water caused officials to close two public beaches in the city of La Crosse, a campground and to cancel several water events during the city's Riverfest festival.

title: Drought: Texas, Jul 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from July 01, 2014 to July 31, 2014. Affected areas: Eastern/Central El Paso County, Western El Paso County. Episode summary: Most of El Paso County was put into Severe(D2) drought the beginning of July, but some decent rainfall across the east brought some improvement by the middle of the month. Details: The entire zone was in Severe(D2) drought during the entire month. The entire zone was put into Severe(D2) drought at the beginning of the month, but by July 8th, the southeast portion of the zone was put back into Moderate(D1) drought. The El Paso Airport reported 0.69 inches of precipitation which was 0.98 inches below normal.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jul 22, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from July 22, 2014 to July 22, 2014. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: An upper ridge was centered over the El Paso area with low and mid level flow out of the southeast providing plenty of moisture for heavy rains to occur. Over an inch of rain fell quickly around Socorro, TX which resulted in some localized flash flooding. Details: KFOX reported flooding in the Socorro area near Thunder and Rio Vista Drive. Streets near the intersection had to be blocked off. Some people had to wait for the water to recede to get to their homes.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Jul 31, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from July 31, 2014 to July 31, 2014. Affected areas: Harris, San Jacinto. Episode summary: Thunderstorms formed ahead of an approaching summer cold frontal boundary. Storms were enhanced by passing shortwave disturbances while interacting with outflow boundaries from sea breeze-initiated thunderstorms. Details: There was high water observed near the intersection of Beltway 8 and JFK Boulevard. A grocery store's roof collapsed due to heavy rainfall. Poor drainage flooding also reported on portions of route 59 feeder road. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Sep 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from September 12, 2014 to September 12, 2014. Affected areas: Brazos. Episode summary: Deep tropical moisture in combination with a slowly southward moving cold front helped to generate numerous showers and thunderstorms that produced heavy rainfall and flooding in and around the Bryan and College Station areas. A record rainfall total of 4.26 inches was set for the date at KCLL. Details: Flash flooding occurred in and around the Bryan and College Station areas. Water reached up to cars near the intersection of East Villa Maria Road and Rustling Oaks Drive, and there was high water near the intersection of South College Avenue and Davis Street. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,000.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Aug 11, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from August 11, 2014 to August 11, 2014. Affected areas: Ashland. Episode summary: A few storms formed over the southern end of Chequamegon Bay just to the west Ashland, WI on during the early afternoon of August 11th. At least two witnesses saw a waterspout form over the Bay and then briefly move inland as a tornado with the storms moving to the south-southwest. Pictures were taken of the waterspout. One witness described the tornado moved inland for about 10 seconds before dissipating near the median on Highway 2. Details: At least two witnesses saw a waterspout form over Chequamegon Bay and then briefly move inland as a tornado with the storms moving to the south-southwest. Pictures were taken of the waterspout. One witness described the tornado moved inland for about 10 seconds before dissipating near the median on Highway 2.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Jul 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from July 30, 2014 to July 31, 2014. Affected areas: Collin, Cooke, Denton, Grayson, Hunt. Episode summary: An upper level system moving across the region brought a MCS across the northeastern half of the CWA and then another round of heavy rain developed in the wake of the MCS. Heavy rain from both complexes resulted in flash flooding, mainly to the north and northeast of the DFW Metroplex. A few reports of wind damage were also documented. Details: One foot of water was reported over the Interstate 35 access road in Sanger, south of FM 455. Interstate 35 in and just north of Sanger also had to be closed two times due to high water. Up to 4 of rain was reported in Sanger in just a few hours. The east side of Quail Run Circle was washed out by heavy rainfall. 2-4 inches of rain fell in the area in just a few hours. Significant flooding was reported in Gunter and flood waters reached the edges of a few homes and businesses in the city. Parts of Highway 289 were closed due to high water. Several residents were trapped in their homes until the waters receded. 3-5 of rain fell in the area in just a few hours. Reported property and crop damage: about $30,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 04, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 04, 2014 to July 05, 2014. Affected areas: San Bernardino. Episode summary: An inverted upper-level trough lifted north from Baja, Mexico, and along with significant moisture flux (PW of 1.8 inches) helped initiate thunderstorms in easterly steering flow along and just west of the mountain ridgeline. An upper-level trough enhanced thunderstorm intensity and coverage on the afternoon of the 4th and morning of the 5th. Subsidence behind the upper-level wave acted to suppress convection for the latter half of the 5th. Rainfall on the 4th was mainly confined to the Riverside and San Diego County mountains, with amounts of one-tenth to one-half inch in general, and up to 1.5 inches under the heaviest cells in San Diego County. Flooding was reported along Interstate 15 north of Victorville and along National Trails Highway, as well SR 247 washed out at Reche Road, north of Yucca Valley. Activity on the 5th was concentrated farther north in the San Bernardino County mountains, upper deserts and Coachella Valley. Cells in these areas generally produced amounts of one-third of an inch, to just over one inch of rain, with locally higher amounts in the higher mountain locations. Over the two days, a spotter in Onyx Peak reported over 3 inches of rain and damage to dirt roads on their property. Thunderstorm winds also damaged two structures near Yucaipa, damaging the roof of one and collapsing the other completely. Details: California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding on I-15 and Wild Wash Road. A transient was rescued from flowing water in the flood control channel at 11th and D Streets in Yucaipa. CHP reported flash flooding at Highway 66 (National Trails Highway.) and Hodge Road.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 27, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 27, 2014 to July 27, 2014. Affected areas: San Diego. Episode summary: Residual instability left over from nocturnal convection over Arizona and southeast California moved through southwestern California, helping to initiate showers and thunderstorms over portions of the San Diego County mountains. A separate upper-level low disturbance helped to trigger thunderstorms all the way to the coast and coastal waters during the morning hours. A lightning strike near Encinitas burned the side of a home. Most coastal and valley locations received one-tenth of an inch or less, though a few locations received significantly more, such as 0.57 inch in Del Mar. This disturbance continued to provide enough instability for thunderstorms over the high desert and San Bernardino County mountains, generating up to 0.87 inch. CHP reported flash flooding on Highway 79 at Fink Road and closed the highway at mile marker 46. Details: CHP reported flash flooding on Highway 79 at Fink Road. The water was very muddy, fast-flowing and several feet deep in places. CHP closed the highway at mile marker 46. A downpour at La Jolla Shores caused quite significant water flow through the Boat Launch at the foot of Avenida de la Playa. Part of the HPS chain link fence in front of the outfall structure washed down into the Boat Launch area posing a significant hazard. Significant sand erosion occurred at the area as well. Reported property and crop damage: about $300.

title: Wildfire: California, Jul 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from July 03, 2014 to July 06, 2014. Affected areas: San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: The Banner Fire started around 0930 PST on July 3 in the Banner, California area, near Route 78 in San Diego County. It quickly spread westward and expanded to 150 acres, threatening the town of Julian. Portions of Route 78 were closed, and mandatory evacuation was ordered for 200 homes; however, the evacuation order was lifted later that evening, as the containment increased. Two homes were destroyed. On July 4, four injuries were reported. On July 6, at 0815 PST, the Banner Fire was 100% contained. However, the road closures still remained in effect through the day, as the firefighting crews continued to monitor the burn areas for potential flare-ups. The cause of the fire is still under investigation. Reported property and crop damage: about $900,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Aug 04, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, from August 04, 2014 to August 04, 2014. Affected areas: Clark. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed along a slow moving cold front across western Wisconsin during the late morning of August 4th. These storms produced some locally heavy rains that caused some flash flooding to occur near Granton (Clark County). The storms also dropped some hail around Neillsville (Clark County) where nickel sized hail was reported. Details: Flash flooding along the South Branch of O'Neill Creek partially washed out a culvert on Meridian Road northeast of Granton. In addition, the flooding eroded between 300 and 350 feet along the side of the road adjacent to the culvert. Runoff from heavy rain caused water from Jack Creek to partially cover U.S. Highway 10 south of Granton, temporarily reducing the road to one lane. The heavy rain also caused erosion to occur along the sides of Pelsdorf Avenue, Starr Road and Catlin Avenue. In Neillsville, 2.35 inches of rain was measured. Reported property and crop damage: about $37,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Aug 18, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from August 18, 2014 to August 18, 2014. Affected areas: Trempealeau. Once these storms reached the South Plains, they lost much of their vigor as they consolidated into a large line that only produced two known instances of severe weather. However, this line became more efficient at producing torrential rainfall rates and flooding throughout the South Plains with some locations recording one inch of rain in 15 minutes or less. Parts of Lubbock experienced significant flooding that left at least two dozen cars stranded in high waters. Frequent cloud-to-ground lightning and power outages added to the drama as up to 8,000 Lubbock residents were without power during the height of the storm. Details: A swath of intense rainfall moved south directly over Interstate 27 from Abernathy, through downtown Lubbock, and south to Woodrow. The most extreme areas extended from the southeastern Texas Panhandle through the northern Rolling Plains.||The Rolling Plains and extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle continued to be abnormally warm and dry through October. Keetch-Byram Drought Index values worsened across the Rolling Plains. Observed values ranged from 400-500 over the northern portion of the Rolling Plains worsening to 500-600 by the end of the month. The southern Rolling Plains saw values between 200-300 worsening to 300-400 by the end of October. Fire weather concerns through October remained low but were expected to worsen through the winter.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Aug 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from August 12, 2014 to August 12, 2014. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: An upper ridge was located over the Rockies with southeast low level flow returning deep moisture to the region. Diurnally driven slow-moving thunderstorms developed around El Paso and caused flash flooding just east of Downtown El Paso. Details: Numerous reports via Twitter and media showed Interstate 10 near Raynolds and the Spaghetti Bowl flooded with traffic at a standstill. A trained spotter reported 1.75 inches of rain near this area.

title: Flash Flood: California, Aug 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from August 12, 2014 to August 13, 2014. Affected areas: San Bernardino. Episode summary: A push of monsoon moisture fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Some storms produced severe weather and flash flooding. Details: Nipton Road was washed out, and a big rig was stuck in the wash. A series of thunderstorms caused street flooding in Needles. The first storm in the series caused the wind damage documented in a separate entry. Highway 95 was closed from 5 Mile Road to Interstate 40 due to flood damage. One swift water rescue occurred at mile marker 56. Reported property and crop damage: about $24,000.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: California, Aug 18, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from August 18, 2014 to August 21, 2014. Affected areas: Inyo, San Bernardino. Episode summary: A significant push of monsoon moisture fueled an outbreak of thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Many storms produced severe weather and flash flooding. Details: A spotter measured 1.72 inches of rain, and reported that all road within about three square miles were closed due to flooding. Water six to seven inches deep flowed over Highway 127. Highway 95 was closed from Goffs Road to about 12 miles south of the Nevada state line due to flooding. Twelve vehicles were stranded between two washouts. Reported property and crop damage: about $23,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Aug 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from August 30, 2014 to August 30, 2014. Affected areas: Gillespie. Episode summary: An upper level trough of low pressure moved across the southern plains and interacted with deep tropical moisture to produce thunderstorms over South Central Texas. Some of these storms developed heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding. A low water crossing on Ranch Rd. 783 had approximately 1.5 feet of water over the roadway between Doss and Harper.

title: Flash Flood: California, Sep 07, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from September 07, 2014 to September 09, 2014. Affected areas: San Bernardino. Episode summary: A major surge of monsoon moisture aided by Hurricane Norbert just west of Baja California fueled an outbreak of thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Widespread flash flooding occurred. Details: Up to six inches of water flowed over low spots on Newberry Road, including the intersection with Route 66. Kelso Cima Road was flooded near Kelso Depot. Mud and debris up to a foot deep covered a 200 foot long stretch of road near the intersection of National Trails Highway and Danby Road. Reported property and crop damage: about $695,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: California, Aug 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, from August 01, 2014 to August 03, 2014. Affected areas: Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego. Episode summary: An upper-level low from Baja cut underneath a large area of seasonably strong high pressure aloft, tapping into lingering monsoonal moisture to produce showers and thunderstorms over the mountains and deserts, as well as a few along the coastal areas, with heavy rain at times. The activity on the 2nd consisted of elevated thunderstorms with lightning along the coast during the morning and a few thunderstorms over the San Bernardino County mountains. Rain and rapid cooling in one of these storms resulted in several bicyclists being treated for hypothermia during the Tour de Big Bear race. This elevated convection became intense and transitioned into numerous strong thunderstorms on the 3rd, focusing more on the mountains and deserts and closing several roadways due to flooding. Rainfall of 2 to 4 inches occurred in less than 3 hours across steep terrain in the San Bernardino County mountains. The hardest hit areas were Mt Baldy, Forest Falls and Oak Glen where numerous debris flows occurred causing road damage and closures. Incident Command Posts were set up at both Mt Baldy and Valley of the Falls. A weather station in Mt Baldy reported 4 inches of rain in less than 2 hours. Swift water rescues were performed in Mt Baldy along the LA County line. There was also a large area of 1 to 2.5 inches of rain in low-lying areas and deserts, including 2.73 inches in one hour at the Borrego ALERT gage. The Fish Creek RAWS in the San Diego County desert recorded 2.77 inches of rain in one hour, resulting in moderate flooding and the subsequent closure of Fish Creek Road through August 8th. Heavy

CHP reported water over the highway near the intersection of Highway 79 and Chihuahua Valley Road with traffic stopped in both directions. title: Dust Storm, Flash Flood, Flood: California, Aug 21, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, Flash Flood, Flood, from August 21, 2014 to August 21, 2014. Affected areas: Coachella Valley, San Diego. Episode summary: A line of elevated thunderstorms developed during the morning of the 20th over the ocean and along the coast ahead of an approaching upper-level low. Dynamic lift and monsoonal moisture led to further destabilization and increasing storm intensity with time. The initial band moved inland and organized thunderstorms with prolific lightning persisted over the Inland Empire and Riverside County mountains. The coastal and valley locations of San Diego and Riverside Counties received anywhere from a few hundredths of an inch of rain to one-half of an inch, with the greatest amounts in the Inland Empire and northern San Diego County valleys. The upper low moved across San Diego and Imperial Counties on the 21st, producing intense thunderstorms over the mountains and deserts, as well as a significant dust storm that moved up the Coachella Valley. The mountain locations of San Diego and Riverside Counties received up to one-half of an inch of rain, while the San Diego County deserts received up to 1.30 inches. One-inch hail was reported with thunderstorms in Nuevo and Mount Laguna/Pine Valley. Details: A spotter in Campo reported flash flooding and pea size hail at CA Highway 94 and Shookey road. A ham radio spotter is reporting up to 6 inches of water on the road in the 35000 block of Highway 79 near Warner Springs. A spotter reports a dust storm producing quarter mile visibility in Cathedral City, with winds estimated at 15-20 mph. A haboob in Palm Springs felled a tree onto a pickup truck containing a man who was injured and taken to the hospital. Peak wind speeds at the nearby Palm Springs ASOS were 40

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Sep 21, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from September 21, 2014 to September 22, 2014. Affected areas: Reeves. Episode summary: Moisture from the remnants of Tropical Storm Odile continue to rotate around the area under an upper level ridge stretching over the region. The main focus for rainfall was more concentrated over the Trans Pecos and Southeast New Mexico at this time. Easterly low level upslope flow favored areas west of the Pecos and especially the Guadalupe Mountains in western Eddy County. The high moisture allowed for any shower or thunderstorm to produce 1-3 inches of rainfall. Details: Heavy rains across Reeves County produced flash flooding 9 miles south of Toyah on FM 2903 with water over the road along Nine Mile Draw. Damage estimates are very rough. Heavy rains occurred along the Pecos River which flowed towards the city of Pecos causing nearby draws to flow out of their banks. This contributed to water ponding over the roads and low lying areas about one to three miles north of Pecos on FM 1216. This section of the road was closed due to the flooding. Damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Reeves County and produced flooding along the Pecos River. Local emergency management officials were continuing to report flooding along the Pecos River from Orla to the city of Pecos. Mandatory evacuations were issued from the Pecos River to U.S. Highway 285. Emergency management in Loving County reported minor flooding on the western side of Mentone. The cost of damage Reported property and crop damage: about $501,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from October 14, 2014 to October 14, 2014. Affected areas: Modoc County. Episode summary: An incoming cold front brought strong winds to parts of northeast California. Details: A gust to 61 mph was recorded at the Timber Mountain RAWS.
