title: Coastal Flood: California, Aug 26, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Coastal Flood, from August 26, 2014 to August 27, 2014. Affected areas: Orange County Coastal Areas. Episode summary: A large southerly swell around 10 feet, generated by Hurricane Marie, moved through the coastal waters from the 25th through the 28th. This swell resulted in very large surf and dangerous rip currents during this time. Coastal flooding due to the high surf was observed at Seal Beach on the 26th, and reached into some homes. The direction of the swell kept the vast majority of the surf and coastal flooding in Orange County, and largest surf on the 27th and 28th. Surf heights from 15 to 18 feet were reported near Newport Beach and northward to Huntington Beach. The Wedge at Newport Beach had sets of 25 to 30 feet. This high surf not seen since May 2011. South Laguna Beach reported major beach erosion. Details: Local TV media reported significant coastal flooding of Seal Beach, specifically along East Seal Way, where many homes experienced a few inches to 1 foot of water rushing into them after 12 to 14 foot waves cleared the 2 and a half foot protective sea wall. Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

title: Drought: California, Sep 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from September 01, 2014 to September 30, 2014. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continued in full force during the month of August, 2014. Exceptional drought was detected by the U.S. Drought Monitor for almost the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The 2013-2014 water year (July 1 - June 30) concluded with Fresno setting its second driest on record (4.81 inches) and Bakersfield setting its third driest (2.41 inches). ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, a decrease in the snow-related tourism activity in the Southern Sierra Nevada, reduction in air quality due to persistent stagnant air, loss or reduction of ground water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. For the first time on record, red flag warnings were issued in January for not only the Southern Sierra Nevada and the Tehachapi Mountains but also the south end of the San Joaquin Valley.

title: Wildfire: California, Sep 07, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from September 07, 2014 to September 29, 2014. Affected areas: S Sierra Mtns. Episode summary: The Meadow fire was located in Yosemite National Park, 5 miles East of Yosemite Valley, east of Half Dome in the Little Yosemite Valley. It was started by lightning on July 19, 2014, but was not discovered until August 15, 2014. The fire only grew to 10 acres and was being managed for resource objectives until September 7, 2014 when strong winds developed and began to rapidly spread the fire. The fire grew to 4772 acres before being contained on September 29, 2014. There were no fatalities and no structures lost. However, access to Half Dome was closed for several days. Cost of containment was $4.9 million.

title: Wildfire: California, Sep 05, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from September 05, 2014 to September 12, 2014. Affected areas: S Sierra Foothills. Episode summary: The Bridge Fire was located 10 miles East of Mariposa in Mariposa County. It began on September 5, 2014 and grew to 300 acres before being contained on September 12, 2014. There were no fatalities, 3 injuries to fire fighters, and no structures lost. Cost of containment was $5.4 million.

title: Wildfire: California, Sep 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from September 14, 2014 to September 22, 2014. Affected areas: S Sierra Foothills. Episode summary: The Courtney fire was located 3 miles East of Oakhurst in Madera County and burned toward the community of Bass Lake. The fire began on September 14, 2014 and burned 320 acres before being contained on September 22, 2014. The cause of the fire was under investigation, but is believed to be human caused. The fire resulted in evacuations of several hundred residents and visitors for several days. There were 30 residences, 19 outbuildings, 13 vehicles, and 4 recreational vehicles destroyed as well as 4 residences, 3 outbuildings and 2 vehicles damaged. Cost of containment was $4.4 million.

title: High Wind: Texas, Oct 13, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from October 13, 2014 to October 13, 2014. Affected areas: Crosby. Episode summary: A strong upper level low pressure system moving out of the Rockies onto the Southern High Plains brought widespread strong winds to the region late on the 12th into the afternoon of the 13th. Winds briefly reached severe criteria at a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near White River Lake (Crosby County). Winds were measured at 58 mph at this location early in the morning on the 13th. This same system brought thunderstorms on the 12th with one storm briefly becoming severe near Aspermont (Stonewall County).

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Sep 17, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from September 17, 2014 to September 18, 2014. Affected areas: Andrews, Borden, Culberson, Ector, Howard, Midland. Episode summary: There was moisture coming into the region from Tropical Storm Odile over northern Mexico/southern New Mexico. This made the air mass very moist. Upper level disturbances were moving over the area from Odile which increased atmospheric lift. The air was also unstable, especially for areas that received sunshine during the day. These conditions allowed for rain and thunderstorms to develop across areas that had already received good rainfall allowing for flash flooding. Details: Heavy rain moved across Culberson County and produced flash flooding in the Guadalupe Mountains. This flash flooding resulted in mud and rocks falling onto Highway 62/180 through Guadalupe Pass. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Borden County and produced flash flooding on Farm to Market Road 1054. No damage was reported so the cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Andrews County and produced flash flooding southeast of Andrews. Portions of Farm to Market Road 1788 were closed due to two and a half feet of water over the road about eleven miles south of State Highway 176. A vehicle accident was reported at this location. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $18,200.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Aug 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from August 10, 2014 to August 10, 2014. Affected areas: El Paso. Episode summary: A moderately moist atmosphere was in place with a weak upper disturbance crossing the region. Weak low and mid level flow kept storm motion very slow allowing for locally heavy rain to develop over West El Paso. Details: About 1 inch of rain fell in less than an hour causing curb to curb water running on Mesa Street in West EL Paso.

title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Aug 29, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from August 29, 2014 to August 29, 2014. Affected areas: Waupaca. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed in unstable air ahead of a cold front and produced heavy rain that caused minor flooding. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that flooded farm fields and partially flooded a basement northeast of Iola. A storm spotter four miles northeast of Iola measured 3.25 inches of rain in a 24-hour period.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Aug 28, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from August 28, 2014 to August 28, 2014. Affected areas: Donley. Episode summary: The combination of an upper level disturbance, a surface trough situated over the south-central Texas Panhandle, and above normal precipitable water resulted in intense rain producing thunderstorms during the afternoon hours of the 28th. The intense rainfall from these storms led to the development of localized flash flooding in Donley County. This flash flooding quickly diminished once convection moved east of the Panhandle. Details: A cluster of thunderstorms developed over Donley County during the afternoon hours of the 28th. These thunderstorms produced intense rainfall which led to the development of flash flooding in rural areas northwest of the town of Clarendon (Donley County). A local law enforcement officer reported that a foot of flowing water was covering a low water crossing 3 miles northwest of Clarendon (Donley C

title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Oct 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from October 14, 2014 to October 14, 2014. Affected areas: Sheboygan. Episode summary: A gravity wave occurred around the back edge of a diminishing stratiform precipitation area. This gravity wave caused strong winds over Sheboygan County. Details: Several trees reported blown down in Sheboygan and Plymouth. Strong winds were observed throughout the county. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Aug 17, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from August 17, 2014 to August 17, 2014. Affected areas: Denton. Episode summary: Widespread showers and thunderstorms developed in an environment aided by diffluence aloft. Although they did not produce severe weather on the 17th, they did produce minor flash flooding along Interstate 35E in the Lewisville area in Denton County. Details: The right lane of I35E in Lewisville was closed due to water on the roadway.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Sep 19, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from September 19, 2014 to September 20, 2014. Affected areas: Ector, Loving, Reeves, Ward, Winkler. Episode summary: The remains of Tropical Storm Odile were moving across the region as they rotated around the circulation of an upper ridge. A circulation was also located over the central Permian Basin which was allowing rain to move across the same areas. There was plentiful moisture across the area from Odile as well as from tropical storm Polo. Good upper level lift was also present from Odile. Heating from breaks in the cloud cover allowed for instability to increase. This moisture, lift and instability allowed for rain and thunderstorms to continue moving over the same areas leading to more flash flooding for West Texas and southeast New Mexico. Details: Heavy rain moved across Reeves County and produced flash flooding in Orla. Roads in Orla were damaged from the flowing water. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Ector County and produced flash flooding in Odessa. Several roads in southern portions of Odessa had two to three feet of water over them. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Winkler County and produced flash flooding south of Kermit. There was water running across Highway 18. No damage was reported so the cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $13,900.

These storms also produced intense rainfall across the southern portion of Randall County which led to the development of flash flooding. Once the storms moved out of the Southern Plains this flash flooding was able to recede. Details: Intense rainfall from a line of thunderstorms which moved through Randall County during the early afternoon hours of the 24th led to the development of Flash Flooding in Palo Duro Canyon State Park. title: Frost/Freeze: Texas, Oct 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from October 14, 2014 to October 14, 2014. Affected areas: Deaf Smith. Episode summary: The combination of light winds and clear skies led to the development of frost in Hereford (Deaf Smith County) during the early morning hours of the 14th. This frost threatened sensitive crops during the growing season. By 8 AM CST, temperatures rose above 36 degrees to bring an end to frost conditions. title: High Wind: Texas, Oct 13, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from October 13, 2014 to October 13, 2014. Affected areas: Gray. Episode summary: A strong surface pressure gradient and strong winds aloft mixing to the surface led to the occurrence of a high wind gust at McLean (Gray County) just before the noon hour on the 13th. The West Texas Mesonet site one mile east-northeast of McLean reported a 58 mph high wind gust at 11:30 AM CST. No further high wind gust was reported due to the surface pressure gradient weakening. Details: High wind gust of 58 mph at McLean.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Sep 20, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from September 20, 2014 to September 20, 2014. Affected areas: Andrews, Borden, Howard, Loving, Martin. Episode summary: Remains of Tropical Storm Odile were over the region. The atmosphere was very moist and there was a mid-level circulation over northern portions of the area. There were nocturnal low level winds that produced additional lift which aided in more rain and thunderstorms developing. The saturated ground from previous rains allowed for flash flooding to develop across West Texas and southeast New Mexico when additional rain moved over these same locations. Details: Heavy rain fell across Loving County and produced flash flooding near Mentone. There was water flowing eight inches over State Highway 302. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Andrews County and produced flash flooding southeast of Andrews. There was water over Farm to Market road 1788 and traffic was diverted off this road. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Howard County and produced flash flooding in Vincent. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $27,800.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Aug 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from August 01, 2014 to August 01, 2014. Affected areas: Harris. Episode summary: Thunderstorms formed ahead of a weak cold frontal boundary. Storm motion was very slow as convection was enhanced by passing shortwave disturbances, while interacting with outflow boundaries from sea breeze initiated thunderstorms. Details: Heavy rain caused flooding to enter homes in the Aldine Bender area. There were several flooded roadways in and around the northern Houston area, generally located inside the Sam Houston Beltway. Some notable one hour rainfall rates were 4.16 inches at Greens Bayou and Highway 59 and 3.96 inches at Jefferson and Highway 59. Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Oct 09, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from October 09, 2014 to October 09, 2014. Affected areas: Gray. Episode summary: Two stalled baroclinic zones from earlier convection and a cold front laid across the Panhandles in the afternoon hours of the 9th. Up to 1500 J/Kg mlcape developed in the southern Texas Panhandle with lesser amounts further north. Straight long hodographs favored splitting supercells and favorably oriented boundaries gave right movers something to latch onto. One dominate right moving supercell formed in eastern Oldham County and rode an east-west oriented boundary all the way through Wheeler County. This storm exhibited signs of rotation and twice tightened to the point of necessitating tornado warnings. Hail up to tennis ball size hail was reported sporadically throughout the event. Another storm near Dalhart later in the night formed along the other boundary and became supercellular producing a very intense low level couplet and baseball size hail. Storms finally decreased in intensity around midnight. Details: A supercell thunderstorms produced a weak EF-1 tornado which caused intermittent damage along a 7 mile path from 4.2 miles south of Kingsmill (Gray County) to 3.8 miles south-southeast of Pampa (Gray County). The tornado snapped several wooden utility poles along Farm-to-Market Road 2300 between the intersection of County Roads L and N. This disrupted electrical service to several hundred customer

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from September 21, 2014 to September 21, 2014. Affected areas: Andrews, Borden, Gaines, Loving, Martin, Midland, Reeves. Episode summary: The remnants of Tropical Storm Odile and an associated mid-level circulation were still over the region. The airmass was very moist, and lift was enhanced by upslope low-level winds across southeast New Mexico and the higher terrain of West Texas. These conditions resulted in rain and thunderstorms across the area, and flash flooding continued as moderate to heavy rain moved over areas with previously saturated soils. Details: Heavy rain fell across Midland County and produced flash flooding. Water up to six feet deep was covering low water crossings along Scharbauer Road in Midland. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Martin County and produced flash flooding. A truck driver reported that water was so high on State Highway 137 just north of Farm to Market Road 846 in Martin County that he was barely able to make it through the water. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Borden County and produced flash flooding. Most of the farm to market roads across eastern Borden County had flooding. Farm to Market roads 1610, 1205 and 669 were closed due to flooding. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $509,900.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Sep 04, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from September 04, 2014 to September 04, 2014. Affected areas: Clark. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed along a warm front during the morning hours of September 4th. These storms produced high winds and large hail as they moved across portions of north central Wisconsin. All of the reports came from Taylor County where a 60 mph wind gust and quarter sized hail occurred near Jump River while trees were blown down in Gilman and west of Medford. Additional thunderstorms developed during the afternoon as a cold front moved across the region. These storms primarily produced locally heavy rain that caused some street flooding to occur in and south of Abbottsford (Clark County). Details: Locally heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in Unity which sent water over State Highway 13. Locally heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in Abbottsford.

title: Flash Flood: California, Sep 06, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from September 06, 2014 to September 08, 2014. Affected areas: Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego. Episode summary: Weakening Hurricane Norbert helped draw significant moisture into southwest California on the 7th. Daytime heating utilized this moisture to set off scattered thunderstorms with heavy rain at times, mainly in Riverside and San Diego Counties. Local rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches fell over the city of Riverside, San Bernardino and Hemet, while the mountains in that county saw up to six tenths of an inch, near Sky Valley. Early morning thunderstorms on the 8th drenched parts of the the Coachella Valley which received one-third of an inch up to just over 3 inches near the lower foothill in Thousand Palms, and Bear Creek in La Quinta. Rainfall rates were up to 2 inches per hour at times, producing widespread flash flooding, most notably in the Coachella Valley on September 8th. Mud and water closed several roads and stranded countless vehicles in La Quinta, Palm Desert, and Thousand Palms. Homes in La Quinta were surrounded by water. The worse hit areas were Washington Street in La Quinta and Varner Road in Thousand Palms. Moving water was a deep as 3 feet on roads and 4 to 5 feet of standing water submerged vehicles and mud was several feet high on Varner Road. A complete storm survey was done in Riverside City and in the Coachella Valley. Details: CHP reported road washing out at Cedar Avenue in Hemet, as well as flooding along Highway 74 at 1st Street across all lanes of 74. Also flooding was reported at Palm and 1st, with knee-deep water. The Hemet Valle Vista alert gage recorded 2.06 inches of rain over the past hour. A few miles east on Highway

A particularly strong storm dumped just over an inch of rain, causing flooding along Balboa Avenue, near Scripps Ranch and Kearny Mesa. The City of San Diego reported 30 buildings damaged and the American Red Cross in Kearny Mesa had significant damage including partial roof collapse. title: Dust Storm, High Wind: California, Oct 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, High Wind, from October 14, 2014 to October 14, 2014. Affected areas: Sw S.J. Valley, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: A trough of low pressure moving into northern California brought no rain to central California, but did increase the westerly winds across the coastal mountains and into the west side of the San Joaquin Valley. These winds increased in the late afternoon and continued through the evening with gusts to 40 to 60 mph common through and below the passes and gaps in the coastal mountains, especially through and below Cottonwood Pass along Highway 41. Sunflower Valley APRS reported a peak wind gust of 59 mph at 1906 PST. Panoche Road RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph at 1907 PST. These strong winds were blowing across Interstate 5 and highway 41. Due to the extended period of drought across the San Joaquin Valley, the winds caused blowing dust across most of the west side of the valley. Visibility was reduced to near zero in blowing dust, resulting in stopped traffic along Interstate 5 and highway 41 and other county roads between Avenal and Lost Hills. There were at least 7 accidents reported and highway 41 was closed from near Avenal to where it intersects highway 46 in San Luis Obispo county for at least 3 hours.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from October 31, 2014 to October 31, 2014. Affected areas: Racine. title: Flood: Wisconsin, Sep 05, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from September 05, 2014 to September 07, 2014. Affected areas: Sawyer. Episode summary: The Hayward area experienced a very wet period in late August and early September which brought about 4 to 7 inches of rain to the area. However, all the rain over the past days caused Smith Lake, which is north of Hayward, to flood. The rising waters of Smith Lake gradually overtopped the earthen dam that feeds into Smith Creek, which in turn runs through Hayward proper and feeds into Hayward Lake. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from November 16, 2014 to November 16, 2014. Episode summary: A cold front moved across the Texas Panhandle during the evening hours of the 15th. The post frontal airmass cooled the lowest layers of the atmosphere during the overnight hours of the 15th and into the early morning hours of the 16th. title: Tornado: Texas, Oct 13, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from October 13, 2014 to October 13, 2014. Affected areas: Upshur. Episode summary: An upper level trough moved quickly into the Central and Southern Plains providing the necessary lift for scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across Northwest Texas and Western Oklahoma during the evening hours of Sunday, Oct. 12th. At the surface, a warm front was rapidly moving northward across East Texas and North Louisiana with low level moisture returning quickly in the wake of the northward moving warm front. A cold front in association with the upper level trough was rapidly moving eastward through Western Oklahoma and Texas. Overnight across Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas, Northeast Texas and Northwest Louisiana, moderate instability was in place with increasing low and mid-level shear as the upper trough approached from the west. Storms eventually erupted ahead of the cold front across Central Oklahoma and Northern Texas, maturing into a squall line as it approached the region during the predawn hours of Monday, Oct. 13th. As the squall line traversed through the region, widespread wind damage was reported associated with straight line winds. Several short track, intense tornadoes developed along the leading edge of the squall line as well across portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas and Northern Louisiana. The storms finally exited the region during the afternoon hours of Oct. 13th. Post-event Storm Surveys determined that 6 tornadoes occurred with this severe weather outbreak, one of which produced 1 fatality and 4 injuries in Little River County, Arkansas. Another tornado produced widespread damage across Ouachita Parish in Monroe, Louisiana. Details: An National Weather Storm Survey team determined that the damage in Upshur County, Texas was consistent with that of a tornado. title: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather: Texas, Nov 16, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather, from November 16, 2014 to November 16, 2014. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Following maximum temperatures in the 60s and 70s on the 15th, a strong cold front and upper trough brought a wintry blast to the entire South Plains region by the morning of the 16th. Initially, freezing drizzle developed over the extreme southeast Texas Panhandle before expanding to the south and west. A thin glaze of ice was deposited on many exposed surfaces but most roads fared well until the freezing drizzle changed over to snow in the following hours. The heaviest snow, up to four inches, fell at Memphis (Hall County) with generally two to four inches elsewhere in the southern Texas Panhandle. Lesser amounts were observed farther south including one inch at Lubbock's Preston Smith International airport. With temperatures well below freezing all day, road conditions quickly deteriorated and nearly 120 accidents were reported in the city of Lubbock alone with 11 confirmed injuries. Accidents were noted elsewhere including three fatalities from two separate motor vehicle accidents attributed to icy roads. Two brothers died after their truck rolled multiple times while traveling on US Highway 84 just south of Slaton (Lubbock County). A third vehicle fatality occurred northwest of Hale Center (Hale County) Saturday night on Farm to Market Road 179 near Farm to Market Road 1914.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Sep 27, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from September 27, 2014 to September 28, 2014. Affected areas: Cameron, Hidalgo. Episode summary: Showers and thunderstorms would continue to plague the region on the 27th. By noon, a slow moving band of blinding rains developed in rural northeast Starr and northwest Hidalgo counties, and would soon link up with other cells forming from Reynosa/Tamaulipas into the Mcallen, Edinburg, San Juan, and Pharr area early in the afternoon. Poor drainage areas were unable to keep up with the rainfall rates, and water up to 3 feet deep piled up in a few areas until a little while after the rain moved east. Farther north, in rural central and northern Hidalgo County, rains continued well after they had cleared out from the larger population centers. Nearly 4 and a half inches fell in San Manuel during the afternoon. Further east in Cameron County an evening round of rain dropped 4 to 6 additional inches and flooded areas from the La Tina Ranch to Holly Beach and the Laguna Atascosa National Wildlife Refuge. Details: Broadcast media reported flash flooding in rural Hidalgo County. Flood waters damaged property and several feet of standing water remained. title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Nov 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from November 10, 2014 to November 11, 2014. Affected areas: Taylor. Episode summary: Parts of north central Wisconsin received up to ten inches of snow from the first winter storm of the season. Two rounds of snow impacted the region as an area of low pressure moved from Nebraska into lower Michigan from November 10th into the 11th. The first round of snow moved over the region during the morning of the 10th with the second round falling during the late afternoon of the 10th into the early afternoon of the 11th. Between these two rounds of snow, Taylor County was hit the hardest with accumulations around 6 inches in the southwest part of the county up to 10 inches in the northeast corner. Emergency management officials reported several vehicle accidents occurred because of the snowy conditions with only one serious injury. The driver of a vehicle that was attempting to pull out a stuck vehicle, sustained a head injury when the ball hitch on the stuck vehicle broke loose, flew threw the back window of other vehicle, striking the driver in the head. Details: COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that 6 to 10 inches of snow fell across Taylor County. One person was seriously injured when the ball hitch of a stuck vehicle broke loose, flew threw the window of another vehicle and struck the driver of the second vehicle in the head. Reported property and crop damage: about $500.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Sep 05, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from September 05, 2014 to September 05, 2014. Affected areas: San Patricio. Episode summary: Localized band of tropical showers and thunderstorms persisted over the community of Odem. Heavy rainfall amounts up to 5 inches occurred. This produced flooding of streets within the community. Details: Heavy rainfall up to 5 inches caused flooding of streets in the community of Odem. Water depth reached up to a foot in places.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Sep 27, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from September 27, 2014 to September 27, 2014. Affected areas: Kleberg, Nueces. Episode summary: A coastal trough along with a favorable upper level pattern resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms over the Coastal Bend. Showers and thunderstorms trained over the same region over Kleberg County producing very heavy rainfall. Rainfall amounts between 5 and 7 inches occurred over western Kleberg County led to major flooding in the city of Kingsville. Water was 1 to 1 and 1/2 feet deep in some areas of Kingsville. Cars were stranded in high water. Heavy rain occurred in Corpus Christi producing isolated reports of street flooding. Details: Tenth Street between Nettie Avenue and Avenue A in Kingsville was closed due to low water crossings being flooded. High water made roads impassable on Morgan Street between Alameda Street and 15th Street in Corpus Christi. Rainfall amounts between 5 and 7 inches occurred over western Kleberg County. This produced major flooding in the city of Kingsville. Water was 1 to 1 and 1/2 feet deep in some areas of Kingsville. Several cars were stranded in high water. Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Sep 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from September 01, 2014 to September 30, 2014. Affected areas: Calhoun, Goliad, Kleberg, Nueces, Victoria. Episode summary: Abundant rainfall occurred over the Coastal Bend, Brush Country, and portions of the Mid-Coast regions through the month of September. This alleviated the severe drought conditions over parts of South Texas. Below normal rainfall occurred over the Victoria Crossroads where severe drought conditions lingered through the month. Details: Severe drought continued over all of the county through the month. Severe drought continued over the eastern portion of the county through the month. Severe drought ended over the county by the end of the month.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Sep 16, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from September 16, 2014 to September 16, 2014. Affected areas: Starr. Episode summary: The remains of a weak upper level disturbance and surface trough triggered more slow moving thunderstorms on September 16, 2014, that exacerbated runoff across arroyos of the Upper Rio Grande Valley early that afternoon - runoff that likely began after locally heavy rainfall on the 13th. Details: The Arroyo Roma was reportedly in minor flood (bank full) after slow moving thunderstorms likely produced sufficient runoff into the waterway near Roma during the late morning and early afternoon of September 16th. Rainfall amounts in the area were unknown.

title: Drought: Texas, Dec 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from December 01, 2014 to December 31, 2014. Affected areas: Briscoe, Childress, Cottle, Floyd, Hall, King, Motley. Episode summary: Drought conditions remained nearly unchanged throughout the month of December. Severe (D2) to exceptional (D4) drought categories remained over the Rolling Plains and extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle. Exceptional drought persisted over eastern Cottle County connected to a larger exceptional drought region along the Red River to the east.||December began and ended on an extreme cold note but ended up being above seasonal average for the month due to very warm temperatures mid-month. Temperatures at Childress were 2.4 degrees above seasonal averages. Monthly rain totals generally ranged from one tenth to one quarter inch which were well shy of normal, averaging from three quarters of an inch to one inch. Keetch-Byram Drought Index Values ranged from 400 to 600 which were unchanged. Precipitation over the past year was adequate to generate normal to above normal grass and shrub coverage. Furthermore, less grazing than in past year may have contributed to an abnormally high fuel load for the beginning of the dry season.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 07, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 07, 2014 to November 08, 2014. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: Northeast winds behind a strong cold front resulted in high winds through Guadalupe Pass.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 10, 2014 to November 10, 2014. Affected areas: Davis / Apache Mountains Area, Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: Strong mid level winds ahead of an approaching upper trough resulted in high winds in the Guadalupe Mountains. Details: McDonald Observatory reported gusts as high as 61 mph behind a strong cold front.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 23, 2014 to November 23, 2014. Affected areas: Davis / Apache Mountains Area, Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: A shortwave trough moving over the region resulted in high winds in the Guadalupe and Davis Mountains. Details: McDonald Observatory reported several gusts over 60 mph.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 12, 2014 to November 12, 2014. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: Northeast winds behind a strong cold front resulted in high winds through Guadalupe Pass.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 15, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 15, 2014 to November 16, 2014. Affected areas: Guadalupe Mountains Of Culberson County. Episode summary: A passing shortwave trough imparted strong westerly winds to the higher elevations of the Guadalupe Mountains.

title: High Wind: California, Nov 16, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from November 16, 2014 to November 16, 2014. Affected areas: Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: Strong surface high pressure across the Great Basin generated strong and gusty Santa Ana winds across Ventura and Los Angeles counties. The strongest winds (gusts up to 74 MPH) occurred in the mountains. Details: Strong north to northeast winds developed across the Santa Monica Mountains. The RAWS sensor at Malibu Hills reported wind gusts between 58 and 74 MPH. Strong north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Los Angeles county. Some peak gusts from local RAWS stations include: Mill Creek (gusts 58 to 62 MPH), Camp Nine (gusts 58-65 MPH) and Chilao (gusts 58 to 72 MPH). Strong north to northeast winds developed across the mountains of Ventura county. Wind gusts up to 65 MPH were observed.

title: Flash Flood: California, Nov 21, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from November 21, 2014 to November 21, 2014. Affected areas: Los Angeles. Episode summary: An isolated strong thunderstorm produced heavy rain, flash flooding and a mud/debris flow in the city of Glendora near the Colby Fire burn scar. One home and several vehicles were damaged by over four feet of mud. Details: An isolated thunderstorm developed over the Colby Fire burn scar. Heavy rain from the thunderstorm produced flash flooding and a mud/debris flow on the 1100 block of Easley Canyon Road in the community of Glendora. One home and several vehicles were damaged by over four feet of mud and debris.

title: Heat: California, Oct 04, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heat, from October 04, 2014 to October 04, 2014. Affected areas: San Diego County Valleys. Episode summary: The month of October began with a strong ridge of high pressure over the southwestern United States, as well as offshore flow due to surface high pressure over the Great Basin. This resulted in an extended heat wave through the 5th. This had impacts on the largely-attended Miramar Air Show, where dozens of people were treated for heat-related illness/injury. Details: One of the local television stations and San Diego County Health Department reported 50-75 people were treated for heat-related injuries at the Miramar air show.

title: Coastal Flood: California, Oct 09, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Coastal Flood, from October 09, 2014 to October 09, 2014. Affected areas: Orange County Coastal Areas. Episode summary: A 5 to 6-foot south-southeast swell generated by former Hurricane Simon brought high surf and strong rip and longshore currents on the 6th and 7th to Orange County beaches. On the 9th, the astronomical tides rose to near 7 feet, resulting in minor coastal overflow flooding in Orange County. Details: Minor tidal overflow resulted in flooding along the Pacific Coast Highway at Anderson in Sunset Beach. The curb lane on the beach side was under a few inches of water.

title: High Wind: California, Oct 31, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from October 31, 2014 to October 31, 2014. Affected areas: San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: A trough of low pressure deepened along the West Coast deepened the marine layer, with precipitation beginning late evening on the 31st, continuing into November 1. Gusty west winds also affected the mountains and deserts, with a few reaching high wind criteria. Details: High winds occurred at the Volcan Mountain mesonet station between 2200-2300 PST. During this time, winds were sustained out of the west-southwest between 35 -45 mph, with a peak gust of 63 mph.

title: High Wind: Texas, Nov 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from November 10, 2014 to November 10, 2014. Affected areas: Oldham. Episode summary: An arctic front moved across the Texas Panhandle during the evening hours of the 10th. This front caused sustained winds to increase into the 35 mph range with gusts ranging from 45 to 55 mph. One gust was able to reach 58 mph at the West Texas Mesonet site 1 miles west-southwest of Boys Ranch (Oldham County). This was an isolated report and no other high wind gusts were reported. Details: High wind gust of 58 mph reported at 1WSW Boys Ranch WTM.

title: Drought: Texas, Oct 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from October 01, 2014 to October 13, 2014. Affected areas: Coryell, Hunt, Mclennan, Mills, Navarro, Rains. Episode summary: Drought conditions persisted across much of of north Texas during October 2014 as the overall rainfall deficit continued across the region. Details: Upwards of 3 inches of rain fell across Navarro County during the first half of October, leading to an upgrade from D2/Severe drought to D1/Moderate by Oct 14. D1/Moderate drought conditions remained in place through the end of the month. Mclennan County began October of 2014 with Severe/D2 drought conditions in place across the northern half of the county. After four inches of rain fell during the first half of the month, conditions were upgraded to Moderate/D1 by Oct 14, and remained as such through the end of the month. Coryell County began October of 2014 with Severe/D2 drought conditions in place across the northern half of the county. After two to three inches of rain fell during the first half of the month, conditions were upgraded to Moderate/D1 by Oct 14, and remained as such through the end of the month. Reported property and crop damage: about $4,000.

title: Strong Wind: Wisconsin, Oct 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, from October 14, 2014 to October 14, 2014. Affected areas: Brown, Calumet, Outagamie, Shawano, Waupaca, Winnebago. Episode summary: Strong winds blew across east central Wisconsin, producing several measured gusts to around 50 mph, as low pressure passed east of the state. The winds associated with the low may have been enhanced by a gravity wave. The strong winds downed numerous trees, branches, and power lines. More than 14,000 customers were without power at the height of the event.||Some of the strongest measured wind gusts included: 53 mph at Austin Straubel International Airport (Brown Co.), 52 mph at Shawano Municipal Airport (Shawano Co.), and 51 mph at Outagamie County Regional Airport. Details: A wind gust to 52 mph was measured at Shawano Municipal Airport. Strong winds downed numerous trees (especially in about a 10 mile stretch north of Iola), branches, and power lines across Waupaca County. A wind gust of 48 mph was measured at Clintonville Municipal Airport, and a gust to 40 mph was measured at Waupaca Municipal Airport. A wind gust of 51 mph was measured at Outagamie County Regional Airport. Reported property and crop damage: about $45,000.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 11, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 11, 2014 to December 11, 2014. Affected areas: North Coast Interior. Episode summary: A strong storm system brought high winds to parts of Northwest California. This resulted in numerous power outages and trees blown down. Details: RAWS on the highest mountain peaks reported gusts over 70 MPH. There were numerous power outages and trees blown down.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 11, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 11, 2014 to December 11, 2014. Affected areas: Central Siskiyou County, Modoc County. Episode summary: An incoming front on 12/10/14 brought strong winds to many parts of southern Oregon and northern California. A rapidly developing low pressure system behind the first front brought another round of high winds on 12/11/14. Both of these events were covered by a long duration High Wind Warning, but high winds occurred in northern California only during the second event. Details: The ASOS at Montague airport (KSIY) recorded a gust to 67 mph at 11/0453 PST. The Weed RAWS recorded a gust to 59 mph at 11/0448 PST. The Rush Creek RAWS recorded a gust to 69 mph at 11/0903 PST.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Dec 02, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from December 02, 2014 to December 02, 2014. Affected areas: Eastern Sierra Slopes Of Inyo County. Episode summary: A storm system brought rain and snow to much of the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin on the 2nd. The leftover moisture and colder air in the wake of the storm produced patchy dense fog on the 3rd and 4th. Details: A spotter measured eight inches in Aspendell before the snow changed to rain. Several SNOTELs in the area estimated between seven and 10 inches of snow.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Dec 11, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from December 11, 2014 to December 11, 2014. Affected areas: Eastern Sierra Slopes Of Inyo County, Owens Valley. Episode summary: Another storm system brought locally high winds, rain and snow, and patchy dense fog to the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Details: These winds were measured at an elevation of 10,300 feet 3 miles west of Aspendell. The duration of high winds is unknown - the 110 mph was the peak measured gust. Strong winds in the Bishop area blew down one set of power lines and several trees, one of which landed on a house. The event time is estimated. The Bishop ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 48 mph. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Dec 14, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from December 14, 2014 to December 14, 2014. Affected areas: Castro, Parmer. Episode summary: A strong surface low pressure system lifted northeast across the northwest Texas Panhandle early this afternoon and generated strong winds over much of the South Plains with some high winds measured in parts of Parmer and Castro Counties. A gust to 58 mph was measured near Hart by a Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet station. Fortunately, blowing dust was not a significant issue; although numerous tumbleweed piled up to depths of several feet against homes in cities such as Muleshoe and Farwell.

title: Drought: Texas, Oct 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from October 01, 2014 to October 31, 2014. Affected areas: Callahan, Fisher, Haskell, Jones, Kimble, Mason, Nolan, Shackelford, Taylor, Throckmorton. Episode summary: According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, extreme drought conditions were reported across Haskell, Shackelford and Jones counties. Impacts of extreme drought included major crop failures, pasture losses and widespread water shortages or restrictions. Severe drought conditions existed north of Interstate 20 and across the Hill Country counties of Kimble and Mason. Impacts from severe drought included crop and pasture losses, water shortages and water restrictions. Details: The U.S. Drought Monitor indicated severe drought conditions across Callahan County during October. The U.S. Drought Monitor indicated severe drought conditions across Fisher County during October. The U.S. Drought Monitor indicated extreme drought conditions across Haskell County during October.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Nov 21, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from November 21, 2014 to November 22, 2014. Affected areas: Dane, Green, Iowa, Jefferson, Kenosha, Lafayette, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Racine, Rock, Walworth, Waukesha. Episode summary: A push of relatively mild and moist air aloft flowing over below freezing temperatures at the surface resulted in light freezing rain from late evening on November 21st to just beyond sunrise on November 22nd. A light coating of ice formed on untreated roads and sidewalks with vehicle slide-offs, accidents, and falls. Details: A light coating of ice accumulation on roads and sidewalks from freezing rain.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Nov 24, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from November 24, 2014 to November 25, 2014. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green, Green Lake, Iowa, Jefferson, Lafayette, Marquette, Rock, Sauk and 4 more areas. Episode summary: An upper trough brought rain changing to snow over southern Wisconsin from late morning on November 24th through the night. 3 to 6 inches of snow accumulated causing some slide-offs and accidents. Details: Three to four inches of snow. Three to five inches of snow.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Nov 28, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from November 28, 2014 to November 28, 2014. Affected areas: Columbia, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green Lake, Jefferson, Marquette, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Sauk, Sheboygan, Washington, Waukesha. Episode summary: The push of relatively mild and moist air aloft over below freezing temperatures at the surface resulted in a brief period of freezing rain. A thin layer of ice accumulation on roads resulted in some slide-offs and accidents. Details: A light coating of ice accumulation on roadways from freezing rain.

title: Drought: Texas, Oct 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from October 01, 2014 to October 31, 2014. Affected areas: Bandera, Bexar, Blanco, Burnet, Comal, De Witt, Edwards, Gillespie, Karnes, Kendall, Kerr, Lavaca and 4 more areas. Episode summary: October was another dry month across South Central Texas. Most of the region had less than 50 percent of normal rainfall. The lack of rain had only minor impact on the drought with only Karnes and Lavaca Counties changing to worse category, both to Severe (Stage D2). The rest of our counties remained the same with Medina in Extreme (Stage D3) and Bandera, Bexar, Blanco, Burnet, Comal, De Witt, Edwards, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Llano, Real, and Val Verde in D2. Fire danger was low to moderate across the area at the end of the month. Of the counties in D2 or worse drought Bexar, Comal, De Witt, Kerr, Medina, and Val Verde had burn bans remaining in effect. The seven day stream flow averages at the end of the month were below normal (10-24 percent) for the Upper Colorado, Upper Guadalupe, and San Antonio River basins. The Lower Colorado, Lower Guadalupe, Medina, Frio, and Nueces River Basins were much below normal (less than 10 percent). Area lakes and reservoirs continued well below normal pool elevations. Lake Amistad was 32.8 feet below normal. Lake Travis was down slightly at 57.6 feet below normal. Medina Lake dropped again and was 88.6 feet below normal. The Edwards Aquifer rose slightly during the month and was at 629.3 feet. This was 10.7 feet lower than at the end of October 2013 and 34.5 feet below average. The Edwards Aquifer Authority continued stage 4 water restrictions requiring large water users to reduce pumping by 40%. The Barton Springs Edwards Aquifer Conservation District continued stage 2 alarm drought status requiring

The Barton Springs Edwards Aquifer Conservation District continued stage 2 alarm drought status requiring a 20% reduction in pumping. title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Dec 08, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from December 08, 2014 to December 08, 2014. Affected areas: Columbia, Dane, Dodge, Fond Du Lac, Green, Green Lake, Iowa, Jefferson, Lafayette, Marquette, Rock, Sauk and 4 more areas. Episode summary: A surge of relatively mild and moist air aloft over below freezing temperatures at the surface resulted in freezing rain and some sleet. A thin layer of ice on roads and sidewalks led to numerous slide-offs and accidents. Numerous schools were delayed mainly over south central Wisconsin with a few school closings. Details: A thin layer of ice accumulation on roads and sidewalks from freezing rain.

title: Strong Wind, Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Oct 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Strong Wind, Winter Storm, from October 30, 2014 to October 31, 2014. Affected areas: Door, Vilas. Episode summary: A vigorous upper level storm system moved across northern Wisconsin and produced locally heavy snow across Vilas County. The snow was enhanced by lake effect as cold air poured across Lake Superior. Twelve-hour snowfall totals were in the 6 to 9 inch range.||North winds were 20 to 30 mph across the region, with gusts in excess of 50 mph in Door County. Several trees were downed by the strong winds across northeast Wisconsin, causing sporadic power outages. Details: A wind gust of 56 mph was measured at Northport Pier at Death's Door. Sustained winds there were in the 35 to 45 mph range from 1:40 AM CST to 3:30 AM CST. A gust to 50 mph was measured on Washington Island. Snow totals included 6.5 inches at Presque Isle to 9.0 inches near Winchester. Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Dec 18, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from December 18, 2014 to December 18, 2014. Affected areas: Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Washington, Waukesha. Episode summary: Freezing drizzle developed along a weak surface trough resulting in a coating of ice on roadways. Numerous slide-offs and accidents occurred especially in northern Milwaukee, southern Ozaukee, southern Washington, and northeast Waukesha counties. Details: A coating of ice on roadways from freezing drizzle.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Nov 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from November 10, 2014 to November 13, 2014. Affected areas: Ashland, Bayfield, Burnett, Douglas, Iron, Price, Sawyer, Washburn. Episode summary: A low pressure area moved from central Nebraska and through Wisconsin. The low brought widespread snowfall of 8 to 16 inches to northwest Wisconsin with higher amounts in the snowbelt areas. Off-lake winds provided lake-induced snow to the snowbelt areas. The snow tapered off for some areas in the afternoon and evening of the 11th, but winds blowing over the Lake resulted in lingering snow through the 12th and 13th. Snowfall totals included 49 inches at Gile, 38 inches in Hurley, 22.5 near Mellen, 20 near Iron River, 18 near Butternut, 17 in Ashland, 17 near Clam Lake, 16 in Sarona, 16 near Stone Lake, 15 in Grantsburg, 15 near Spooner, 14 near Seeley, 13 near Hayward, 12.5 near Bayfield, 12 near Phillips, 12 in Poplar and Foxboro, 12 on Madeline Island, and about 9.5 inches near Superior.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, Oct 18, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from October 18, 2014 to October 18, 2014. Affected areas: Cameron. Episode summary: Rapidly deepening tropical moisture combined with the convergence of low level southerly with easterly flow along and near the coast to produce scattered showers and thunderstorms. The precipitation began just before dawn and persisted through the early afternoon; when finished, between 2 and nearly 4 inches had fallen between Brownsville and Rio Hondo. The on again, off again rain produced nuisance minor flooding. Details: Heavy rain fell across central and northern Cameron County during the morning hours, with several CoCoRaHS observers reporting rainfall totals between 2 and nearly 4 inches. 3.75 inches was reported just east of Rio Hondo. Scattered showers and thunderstorms brought heavy rainfall to southern Cameron County and the city of Brownsville. CoCoRaHS observers reported between 2 and 3.16 inches of rainfall across western and downtown Brownsville north to Cameron Park. Minor street flooding was reported near Price Road and Frontage Road and at the intersection of East 12th Street and East Elizabeth Street.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Oct 22, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from October 22, 2014 to October 22, 2014. Affected areas: Cameron. Episode summary: During the early morning commute and school trip, a band of very heavy rain developed along the Rio Grande east of Brownsville, and spread across the city from the Sabal Palm Sanctuary through Southmost and into downtown between 630 and 830 am. Soon after the torrents began, poor drainage and rainfall rates of 2 inches per hour overwhelmed many areas, with nuisance flooding (up to 2 feet) in numerous locations and more life/property threatening flash flooding (3 feet or more, water into property) in some of the worst draining areas as well as locations where 3 inches fell in an hour or less. More than 3.5 inches fell near downtown during the event, which matched closely with known flash flood areas. Details: Numerous reports of heavy rainfall was reported by CoCoRaHS observers. Totals ranged from 2 inches to 4.15 inches. The heavy rainfall brought widespread nuisance flooding, especially in poor drainage and low lying areas. Numerous roads and intersections were impacted. Emergency management, local law enforcement, and members of the public reported flash flooding across portions of Brownsville, especially the western and downtown areas. There were several reports of 3 feet or more of water into properties.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Nov 24, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from November 24, 2014 to November 24, 2014. Affected areas: Buffalo. Episode summary: A man was killed when his truck slid into the path of a freight train while snow was falling across western Wisconsin. According to official reports, heavy, wet snow was falling as the driver approached a rail crossing north of Fountain City (Buffalo County). He was unable to stop when the crossing arm closed and slid into the path of the train. Details: The driver of a vehicle was killed when he slid into the path of an oncoming freight train north of Fountain City. The accident occurred on slippery roads created by the heavy, wet snow that was falling. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,500.

title: Drought: California, Nov 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from November 01, 2014 to November 30, 2014. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continued in full force during the month of November, 2014. Exceptional drought was detected by the U.S. Drought Monitor for almost the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The 2013-2014 water year (July 1 - June 30) concluded with Fresno setting its second driest on record (4.81 inches) and Bakersfield setting its third driest (2.41 inches). ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, a decrease in the snow-related tourism activity in the Southern Sierra Nevada, reduction in air quality due to persistent stagnant air, loss or reduction of ground water, wells drying up in several communities leaving them with no water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains. For the first time on record, red flag warnings were issued in January for not only the Southern Sierra Nevada and the Tehachapi Mountains but also the south end of the San Joaquin Valley.

title: Strong Wind: California, Nov 15, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, from November 15, 2014 to November 16, 2014. Affected areas: Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: A weak disturbance moved through across southern California on November 13 and 14 but brought only mid and high clouds across central California with some virga. Despite this disturbance, dense fog formed in the San Joaquin Valley during the morning hours of the 14th. Visibility was less than 1/4 mile at many locations including Madera, Fresno, Visalia, Hanford, and Lemoore. At times visibility was less than 200 feet. ||A ridge of high pressure followed the weak disturbance, with the axis over the coast of California on the 15th. The resulting northwesterly flow brought gusty winds to the Kern County desert, mainly below the passes of the Tehachapi mountains. ||Surface high pressure strengthened in the Great Basin by Sunday, November 16th. This turned the flow offshore and brought gusty easterly winds along with very dry conditions across the Kern County Mountains. The winds followed the terrain and became southeasterly and gusted 35 to 45 mph at times. Humidity also fell to less than 10 percent for 20 to 34 hours on November 16th to the 18th. Red flag warnings were in effect for that time period, but no significant fire activity was reported. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Nov 22, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from November 22, 2014 to November 22, 2014. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: A series of weak storm systems moved through central California on November 19-22. Although these storms did not bring much precipitation, they did bring gusty winds over the Kern County mountains and desert areas with gusts over 45 mph. ||The storms also brought enough moisture for areas of dense fog to develop in the San Joaquin Valley during the early morning hours of the 21st. Visibility lowered to less than 1/4 mile with a few areas reporting visibility less than 500 feet. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Winter Weather: California, Oct 31, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from October 31, 2014 to October 31, 2014. Affected areas: West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: An unseasonably cold system brought several inches of snow to the northern Sierra, impacting traffic on roads above 6000 feet. Details: There was 5 inches of new snow reported at Kingvale 6100 feet and at Soda Springs 6700 feet, along with gusty winds. Chain controls were required, and traffic slow downs were reported on Interstate 80.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Nov 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from November 10, 2014 to November 10, 2014. Affected areas: Wheeler. Episode summary: A large wildfire began about six miles west of Wheeler, Texas in Wheeler county around 1245CST off of Farm to Market Road 2473. The wildfire consumed approximately six hundred acres and there were no structures damaged or lost. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities and the wildfire was brought under control around 1600CST. A total of five fire departments or agencies responded to the wildfire.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Oct 11, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 11, 2014 to October 11, 2014. Affected areas: Nueces. Episode summary: A band of showers and thunderstorms were localized over the downtown and bay front areas of Corpus Christi on the evening of October 11th. Heavy rainfall amounts between 3 to 5 inches occurred. This produced flooding of roads in the downtown area with water depth up to a foot in places. Some damage occurred to motorcycles at the American Bank Center where Bike Fest was being held. Details: Public reported flooding occurred near American Bank Center where Bike Fest was being held. Flood waters were deep enough to cause some damage to motorcycles outside. Public reported flood waters were deep enough to prevent fire trucks from reaching the downtown area at Crosstown Expressway and Leopard Street. Spotter reported very heavy rain in the downtown area near Concrete Street. Water was up to 1 foot in depth at Interstate 37 and downtown with cars stalled. Reported property and crop damage: about $350,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from October 18, 2014 to October 18, 2014. Affected areas: Nueces. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches produced flooding of roads on the south and west side of the city of Corpus Christi. Details: Flood waters made Interstate 37 impassable near Corn Products Road. Flood waters made the westbound lanes of Interstate 37 impassable near Clarkwood Road. Some roads within a mile radius of Staples Street and Saratoga Street were impassable with water depth up to a foot and a half.

title: Drought: Texas, Oct 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from October 01, 2014 to October 31, 2014. Affected areas: Armstrong, Carson, Collingsworth, Dallam, Donley, Gray, Hansford, Hartley, Hemphill, Hutchinson, Lipscomb, Moore and 4 more areas. Episode summary: October saw below normal precipitation for much of the Texas Panhandle, though several episodes of rainfall did keep moisture in the Panhandle throughout the month. Most areas measured at least half an inch during the month, with scattered areas measuring as much as 4 to 5 inches. Extreme (D3) Drought remained along a line from east of Dalhart to near Clarendon and in the extreme northeastern Panhandle. The southwestern Texas Panhandle remained a mix of Abnormally Dry (D0) to Moderate (D1) Drought conditions following rain from September and October, and areas surrounding Perryton improved to Moderate (D1) Drought conditions during October. Otherwise, the remainder of the Panhandles were rated at Severe (D2) Drought conditions. Amarillo recorded 1.08 inches of precipitation for the month (0.58 inches below normal), Dalhart recorded 1.01 inches of precipitation (0.46 inches below normal), and Borger recorded 0.85 inches of precipitation (0.87 inches below normal).||Soil moisture was rated mostly short to adequate during the month. Crops fared well during the month, and some development was even limited by too much rain and cloudiness. Rangeland and pasture continued to improve in some areas, but cattle herd sizes remained limited due to prolonged drought. Upper soil zones were mostly in the 10 to 30 percent full range, with locations in the western Panhandle generally drier. Deeper soil moisture was still below normal in much of the Texas Panhandle, but values were estimated to be greater than 150 percent of normal where rainfall had been most frequent over the previous few months. The Palmer Drought Severity Index indicated a rating of Moderate Drought to Near

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Nov 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from November 10, 2014 to November 12, 2014. Affected areas: Florence, Forest, Langlade, Lincoln, Northern Marinette, Oneida, Vilas. Episode summary: A complex storm system affected the region November 10-11, 2014, bringing a swath of heavy snow to parts of northern Wisconsin. The main storm hit in two phases. The first phase was in the form of a long west to east band of snow which set up across Minnesota and northern Wisconsin early on November 10th. Low pressure then moved across far southern Wisconsin and produced another round of snow late on November 10th and into the 11th across central and northern Wisconsin.||In addition to the long-duration storm, additional lake effect snow from Lake Superior pushed totals over 20 inches in some locations in the snowbelt. The highest reported snowfall total was 23.7 inches at Lac du Flambeau (Vilas Co.). Some of the highest snow totals outside the snowbelt included 15.2 inches near Alvin (Forest Co.), 12.5 inches at Florence (Florence Co.), 12.0 inches at Lake Tomahawk (Oneida Co.), and 11 inches at Pearson (Langlade Co.). Details: A storm total of 23.7 inches of snow was measured at Lac du Flambeau. A storm total of 12.0 inches of snow was measured at Lake Tomahawk. A storm total of 15.2 inches of snow was measured 4 miles northwest of Alvin.

title: Drought: Texas, Jan 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from January 01, 2015 to January 31, 2015. Affected areas: Briscoe, Childress, Cottle, Dickens, Floyd, Hall, King, Motley, Stonewall, Swisher. Episode summary: Since late December 2014, drought conditions expanded by a small margin across the southeast Texas Panhandle and portions of the Rolling Plains. Severe (D2) levels grew south to northern Stonewall County and also west to include portions of King and Swisher counties. Extreme (D3) drought categories remained confined to Childress and Cottle Counties.||Episodes of rain and snow in early to mid January tended to drop reduced precipitation amounts over the drought stricken areas compared to locations farther west; however, a large storm system by January 31st did bring much needed moisture to the southeast Panhandle and Rolling Plains where rainfall totaled between 1/2 inch to nearly 1 inch. Additional rainfall events of this magnitude were still needed to reduce drought levels appreciably and improve area water supplies.||In mid January, a spell of unseasonable warmth and breezy conditions led to an uptick of wildfire concerns especially in the southeast Panhandle. One grass fire about two miles south of Memphis (Hall County) consumed several hundred acres of tall grass on the 15th. Area fuel loads were at or above normal with energy release component values generally at normal, however surpluses in topsoil moisture by the final day of January greatly alleviated the short term wildfire concerns.||Fortunately, agricultural drought impacts in January were negligible thanks to the aforementioned precipitation. Winter wheat and area livestock were noted to be in fair to good condition.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Dec 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from December 30, 2014 to December 31, 2014. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Cochran, Crosby, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hockley, Lamb, Lubbock, Lynn and 4 more areas. Episode summary: Following an arctic front the night prior, widespread freezing drizzle developed early on the morning of the 31st throughout much of the region before mixing with and changing to very light snow. East of the Caprock Escarpment, the duration of freezing drizzle was limited to just a couple of hours compared to nearly 30 hours on the Caprock where the worst impacts were felt. With temperatures in the teens and 20s, many roads and streets developed a thin glaze of ice that later became coated with light snow up to one inch. Treacherous road conditions led to hundreds of vehicle accidents across the South Plains with some serious injuries noted northwest of Post (Garza County) and also near Muleshoe (Bailey County). Conditions at Lubbock Preston Smith Airport were so bad that the airport officially shut down at 2300 CST on the 30th before re-opening for limited flights by the afternoon of the 31st. Combined with the closure, dozens of canceled flights earlier in the day stranded some flyers at the airport for nearly 24 hours. The precipitation gradually dissipated in coverage by late afternoon on New Year's Eve, however temperatures remained well below freezing all day prolonging hazardous travel for holiday revelers - many of whom opted against traveling for festivities. Damage and economic losses from this event were not available at the time of this writing. Muleshoe (Bailey County) was the only location to receive greater than one inch of snow totaling 1.1 inches.

title: Heavy Snow, Ice Storm, Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 02, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, Ice Storm, Winter Weather, from January 02, 2015 to January 03, 2015. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hockley, Kent and 9 more areas. Episode summary: Following occasional light snow and freezing drizzle on New Year's Day (only trace accumulations), a potent storm system approached the region on January 2nd from southern New Mexico before exiting the Rolling Plains on January 3rd. Ahead of this storm, an influx of moisture and lift bolstered wintry precipitation throughout the region on the 2nd. This precipitation fell mainly in the form of freezing rain in the Rolling Plains, snow in the far western South Plains and southwest Texas Panhandle, with a combination of freezing rain, sleet and snow in between. As the storm system passed overhead on the night of the 2nd, snow became the dominant precipitation type before ending by the morning of the 3rd. The greatest swath of snow between four and nine inches deep fell across the far southwest Texas Panhandle. Locations in the far southeast Texas Panhandle, including Childress (Childress County), were spared the impacts of this winter storm as precipitation there was simply too light and brief in duration.||The worst impacts by far were dealt to portions of the southeast South Plains into the Rolling Plains where freezing rain produced ice between 1/4 and 1/2 inch thick. In addition to downing some trees and limbs, the ice damaged about 100 miles in total of power lines and caused numerous power outages. The heaviest swath of ice fell in an area from Tahoka (Lynn County) east to Post (Garza County) and Clairemont (Kent County) where Highway 380 was closed for about eight hours until utility crews could fully remove all downed power lines. At the

title: Heavy Snow, Ice Storm, Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 02, 2015
text: of ice fell in an area from Tahoka (Lynn County) east to Post (Garza County) and Clairemont (Kent County) where Highway 380 was closed for about eight hours until utility crews could fully remove all downed power lines. At the height of the storm, Lyntegar Electric COOP reported 10,117 customers without power across the far southern South Plains. Fortunately, most roads in the Rolling Plains remained wet due to ground temperatures hovering just above freezing, but colder temperatures farther west and northwest created such hazardous conditions that regional travel became nearly impossible at times; especially on US Highway 84 from near Progress (Bailey County) to Farwell (Parmer County) where several inches of wet snow accumulated. This stretch of roadway remained hard-packed in snow and ice until the afternoon of the 5th when temperatures finally warmed above freezing. text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Coastal Flood, Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind, Strong Wind, from December 11, 2014 to December 11, 2014. Episode summary: An Atmospheric River event brought heavy rain and gusty winds with a strong winter storm that impacted the Bay Area for several days in mid-December. On December 11, the intense surface low moved up the coast and drug a narrow cold frontal rainband (NCFR) through the Bay Area that morning and early afternoon. NCFRs are rapidly moving fronts that are notorious for intense rainfall and gusty winds despite having limited instability. ||The NCFR wasn't a major wind producer, but the rainfall rates were impressive. Instantaneous rainfall rates of 1.5-2 inches/hr were reported. Observational data from the Big Sur Coast were also impressive with Big Sur receiving 4.43 in 2 hours and Flores Camp receiving 3 in 1 hour. It wasn't so much the total amount of rainfall for many locations, but the intensity and how much was received in a short amount of time. ||Many locations around the entire Bay Area had flooding: urban flooding of streets and highways, flooding of creeks and even one large river in the North Bay. Eventually the NCFR slowed around the Big Sur Coast. The stalling was likely due to another 'wave' in the atmosphere, farther to the southwest, riding along the boundary. title: Winter Weather: California, Nov 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from November 01, 2014 to November 01, 2014. Affected areas: West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A cold system brought accumulating snow down to around 5000 feet, with light amounts down to around 4000 feet. There were periods of moderate rain (up to 1-3 inches storm total) in the Central Valley, foothills and lower mountains. This storm began on October 31st and peaked overnight. Details: A cold system brought light snow as low as 4100 feet (Kyburz), with accumulating snow above 5000 feet. Five inches of snowfall was reported at Kingvale at 6100 feet. This brought traffic slowdowns on I-80 and Highway 50.

title: Winter Storm: California, Nov 29, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Storm, from November 29, 2014 to November 30, 2014. Affected areas: West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: Snow caused travel difficulties in the Sierra above 6000 feet. Moderate rain of 1/2 to 2 inches fell in the foothills and lower mountains. Details: Snowfall amounts near 6000 feet were around 6 inches, with up to a foot at Donner Summit at 7200 feet. The slippery roads caused travel difficulties and delays over Sierra passes, aggravated by increased traffic due to the holiday weekend.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: California, Dec 03, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, from December 03, 2014 to December 04, 2014. Affected areas: El Dorado, Placer, Sacramento, Tehama. Episode summary: Heavy rain showers and thunderstorms brought record rainfall and flooding issues to portions of the Central Valley and foothills. There were 2 berm levees which failed in Tehama County, flooding over 200 homes and damaging farms and orchards. Significant traffic delays were caused by road flooding across interior Northern California. Snow levels remained above 7500 feet, so snowfall was limited to higher Sierra peaks and Lassen Peak. Details: Roadway at Coleman Fish Hatchery Rd. and Gover Rd completely flooded and impassable. Flooding in North Highlands on 3617 Quinn Way due to leaves in the storm drain. The street was flooded. Roadway flooding in Vina at Squaw Hill Rd. and South Ave. Reported property and crop damage: about $6,804,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Nov 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from November 01, 2014 to November 30, 2014. Affected areas: Bosque, Collin, Comanche, Cooke, Dallas, Denton, Eastland, Ellis, Erath, Grayson, Hill, Hood and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Precipitation was below normal for most locations across north Texas during the month of November, leading to a continuation of the persistent drought conditions across the region. Details: D2/Severe drought conditions were in place county-wide at the beginning of the month. Conditions were upgraded to Moderate/D1 across the northern half of the county by week two of November due to nearly 2 inches of rain which fell early in the month. D2/Severe drought conditions covered Montague County for all of November, 2014. Severe/D2 drought conditions were in place county-wide at the beginning of the month. Conditions were upgraded to Moderate/D1 by week two across all but the southern third of the county due to nearly an inch and a half of rain which fell during the first week of the month. Reported property and crop damage: about $44,000.

Conditions deteriorated to Severe/D2 during the last week of the month due to below normal precipitation. Reported property and crop damage: about $500.
