title: Drought: California, Dec 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from December 01, 2014 to December 31, 2014. Affected areas: Northern San Joaquin Valley. Episode summary: On January 17th, 2014, Governor Jerry Brown declared a drought emergency for the entire state of California. The drought continued through the year 2014 with well below normal precipitation, though there were brief periods of relief in February/March and December from heavy rains. Exceptional drought was reported by the U.S. Drought Monitor by the end of July for all of Interior Northern California, with the most impacted area being the Northern San Joaquin Valley. Details: Impacts to the region included: Reservoirs dropped to low levels (record lows in some cases), farmers limited plantings of some crops and allowed areas of land to go fallow, increased agricultural unemployment and poverty, strong conservation efforts within many communities, increased reliance on shrinking groundwater resources, a decrease in snow-related tourism activity in the Northern Sierra Ne Reported property and crop damage: about $1,500,000,000.

title: Flood, Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, High Wind, Strong Wind, Winter Storm: California, Dec 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, High Wind, Strong Wind, Winter Storm, from December 10, 2014 to December 12, 2014. Affected areas: Burney Basin/Eastern Shasta County, Butte, Carquinez Strait And Delta, Glenn, Lake, Mt Shasta/Western Plumas County, San Joaquin, Shasta, Southern Sacramento Valley, Tehama, West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada, Yolo. Episode summary: An atmospheric river event beginning early December 11th brought periods of heavy rainfall, flooding from overly saturated grounds and high river/stream water levels, and heavy snow above 7000 ft. Windy conditions persisted through the event, causing trees and tree branches to fall down and localized power outages affecting hundreds of thousands of homes across Northern California. Snowfall of 1 to 2 feet caused travel problems at Sierra passes. Winds were reported to reach as high as 50-60 mph in the valley/foothill region, and over 100 mph in the mountains. |On December 22, Governor Brown declared a state of emergency for heavy rain, flooding and wind damage in counties including Tehama, Lake, Shasta, and Yolo. Details: Two apartment buildings suffered flooding as a creek behind the buildings over topped. Residents were forced to evacuate. Highway 99 was down to one lane due to flooding. Heavy rain caused closures on Highway 99W between CR 33 and 48, and portions of County Roads 33, 35, 48, Rd D just north of Willows. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,640,000.

title: Flood, Heavy Rain, Sleet: Texas, Nov 22, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, Heavy Rain, Sleet, from November 22, 2014 to November 23, 2014. Affected areas: Anderson, Hopkins, Jack, Palo Pinto, Wise. Episode summary: An upper level storm system moved across north Texas on the 21st and 22nd of the month. Cold air filtered in on the 21st, while moisture returned on the 22nd. A few areas reported sleet and freezing rain, with minimal impacts. While the main focus was light accumulations of sleet, most areas in north Texas also received rainfall. Some of the rain led to traffic accidents due to hydroplaning. Details: The Gordon fire department reported sleet accumulations affected travel in the city. Accumulations of less than one tenth of an inch were reported. The Decatur fire department reported sleet accumulations in the city of Decatur. The accumulations were mainly on grassy areas and rooftops, but a few roadways had icy spots. There were several social media reports on light accumulations of sleet in Jacksboro. The sleet was slowly accumulating and there were several wrecks in the area. Reported property and crop damage: about $205,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from November 04, 2014 to November 04, 2014. Affected areas: Mclennan. Episode summary: Localized thunderstorms occurred across central Texas during the late afternoon and evening of November 4th. Most of the storms produced very little impacts, but there were a few accidents that resulted from heavy rain in Waco. Details: An inmate was injured in a one vehicle accident while being transported by police to the McLennan County jail on Monday, November 4th. The accident occurred at mile marker 326 on I-35 near the Moonlight Drive exit. A Moody police officer was driving the inmate to the jail after arresting him on a warrant when the police car hydroplaned in the rain. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Ice Storm, Winter Weather, from December 30, 2014 to December 31, 2014. title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Nov 24, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from November 24, 2014 to November 25, 2014. Affected areas: Door, Langlade, Menominee, Oneida, Portage, Shawano, Southern Marinette, Southern Oconto, Waupaca, Waushara. Episode summary: Rain changed to snow as a low pressure system intensified northeast of Wisconsin. Five to seven inches of snow fell in 12 hours across parts of northeast Wisconsin. Winds gusted to more than 30 mph at times causing blowing and drifting of the new snow. The highest snowfall totals included 7.6 inches at Stevens Point (Portage Co.), 7.4 inches at Polonia (Portage Co.), 7.3 inches near Amherst (Portage Co.), 7.2 inches near Rhinelander (Oneida Co.), 7.1 inches at Lena (Oconto Co.), and 7.0 inches at High Falls Reservoir (southern Marinette Co.) and Oconto Falls (southern Oconto Co.). Details: Heavy snow fell across the northwest Waushara County. A total of 6.5 inches of snow was measured at New London. A total of 7.2 inches of snow was measured 5 miles north of Rhinelander.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from November 22, 2014 to November 25, 2014. title: Drought: Texas, Nov 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from November 01, 2014 to November 30, 2014. Affected areas: Bandera, De Witt, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Medina. Episode summary: November was a wet month across South Central Texas with nearly all of the area receiving greater than normal rainfall. Most the region had more than 150 percent of normal and a few spots along the Rio Grande River, northern Bexar County, and southern Comal County receiving above 300 percent of normal. Ten counties improved out of Severe Drought category (Stage D2). Despite the rainfall Medina County remained in Extreme Drought category (Stage D3) and Bandera, De Witt, Gillespie, Kendall, and Kerr remained in D2. Fire danger was low to moderate across the area at the end of the month. Of the counties in D2 or worse drought only De Witt and Medina had burn bans remaining in effect. The seven day stream flow average at the end of the month was below normal (10-24 percent) for Nueces River basin. The Guadalupe, Upper and Lower San Antonio, Medina, and Frio River Basins were much below normal (less than 10 percent). Area lakes and reservoirs continued well below normal pool elevations. With all the rain over the Rio Grande River Basin Lake Amistad rose during the month but was still 30.1 feet below normal. Lake Travis was down slightly at 58.0 feet below normal. Medina Lake dropped again and was 89.1 feet below normal. The Edwards Aquifer rose slightly during the month and was at 636.2 feet. This was 5.8 feet lower than at the end of November 2013 and 32.2 feet below average. The Barton Springs Edwards Aquifer Conservation District continued stage 2 alarm drought status requiring a 20% reduction in pumping. title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jan 02, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from January 02, 2015 to January 03, 2015. Affected areas: Red River. Episode summary: An upper level low pressure system across Southern New Mexico/Northern Mexico began opening up and moved into the Texas Hill Country late on the 2nd and during the early morning hours of the 3rd. A strong upper level jet streak rounded the base of this trough from old Mexico into Southern Texas and into the Lower Mississippi Valley early on the 3rd as well. At the surface, a low pressure system formed off the Southeast Texas coast and moved North Northeast from Southeast Texas into Northwest Louisiana with a returning warm front from the coastal parishes of Louisiana. Heavy rainfall developed along and north of the Interstate 30 corridor of Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas while strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of East Central Texas and Northern Louisiana along and in the wake of the returning warm front. The result was wind damage from these thunderstorms in addition to some flash flooding north and west of the Interstate 30 corridor. Details: Bridges were flooded east of Clarksville, Texas including 114 near English and 1158 near Whiterock.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 11, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from January 11, 2015 to January 11, 2015. Affected areas: Bowie, Camp, Cass, Franklin, Morris, Red River, Titus. Episode summary: A cold arctic airmass filtered into the region in the preceding days of January 11th with temperatures mostly in the lower 30s. An overrunning moist airmass resulted in the development of mostly light rain across Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas and the Northern third of Northeast Texas. After midnight on the 11th, this precipitation became light freezing rain but due to the temperature being at or just below freezing, ice accumulation was relegated to trees and elevated exposed objects including powerlines and some bridge surfaces. Ice accumulations were mostly near one tenth of an inch across the region.

title: Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, High Wind: California, Dec 02, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, Heavy Snow, High Wind, from December 02, 2014 to December 03, 2014. Affected areas: Fresno, Kern, Kern Cty Mtns, Mariposa, S Sierra Mtns, Tulare. Episode summary: An upper level low and associated atmospheric river moved across central California December 2-3, 2014. This storm generated significant rainfall across the lower elevations. One-third to three-quarters of an inch of rain fell in the San Joaquin Valley and adjacent foothills, with 1 to 3 inches of rain along the west slopes of the Sierra Nevada below the snow line, which was generally above 8000 feet. Heaviest rain fell across Tulare County and Kern County in and around the Lake Isabella area. Up to two feet of snow fell in the high elevations of the Sierra Nevada. While there was significant concern about debris flows on burn scars due to the heavy rain, no problems were noted as rainfall intensity was not great enough. Strong winds were also observed at the base of the Grapevine along I-5. Details: Snowfall amounts of 22.8 inches at West Woodchuck Meadow and 24.5 inches at Agnew Pass. Mesonet station Wishon Dam /WSHC1/ rainfall 1.83 inches. Mesonet station Wofford Heights /WFHC1/ rainfall 1.98 inches.

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Jan 20, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from January 20, 2015 to January 20, 2015. Affected areas: Columbia, Dodge. Episode summary: The passing of a weak area of low pressure resulted in areas of freezing drizzle and light snow over portions of south central and southeast WI. There were some slide-offs and accidents, including an indirect fatality in Columbia County. Details: An icy roadway from freezing drizzle led to a fatal car accident around 5:45 am in the Town of Leeds. The man was killed when his car slid into an oncoming pickup truck. Freezing drizzle resulted in a light coating of ice on roadways, mainly in southern Dodge County.

Episode summary: The California drought continued in full force during the month of December, 2014. Although there was heavy rain and snowfall across central California in early December, the later part of December was mainly dry. The U.S. Drought Monitor continued to report exceptional drought conditions across the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The 2013-2014 water year (July 1 - June 30) concluded with Fresno setting its second driest on record (4.81 inches) and Bakersfield setting its third driest (2.41 inches). For the calendar year, 2014 was the warmest year on record for Fresno and Bakersfield. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, a decrease in the snow-related tourism activity in the Southern Sierra Nevada, reduction in air quality due to persistent stagnant air, loss or reduction of ground water, wells drying up in several communities leaving them with no water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains.

title: Drought: Texas, Feb 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from February 01, 2015 to February 27, 2015. Affected areas: Briscoe, Childress, Cottle, Hall, King, Motley, Stonewall. Episode summary: Following periodic rounds of mostly light precipitation, severe (D2) to extreme (D3) drought conditions remained unchanged across the far southeast Texas Panhandle and portions of the Rolling Plains by the end of February. Agricultural interests still fared well given decent topsoil moisture. Winter wheat, pastures and rangelands were reported in fair to good condition. However, deep soil moisture was generally below average throughout Childress and Cottle Counties where the long-term drought has been less reluctant to ease its grip compared to locations farther south and west. Fire weather concerns were low this month thanks in large part to very few breezy or windy days coinciding with periods of above normal warmth and low relative humidities.

Episode summary: Cold air that moved into the San Joaquin Valley at the end of December continued to bring below freezing temperatures on the 1st of January. Kern, Tulare, Kings, Fresno, Madera and Merced counties all experienced temperatures dropping below 32 degrees with many areas dropping to 26-28 degrees in areas without protection for and hour or two. A few locations had minimum temperatures of 24-25 degrees for a brief period. According to Citrus Mutual, utilization of wind machines and water raised grove temperatures on average by three to four degrees thereby assuring no significant fruit damage for any of the major varieties, navel oranges, lemons and mandarins. Details: Widespread temperatures below 32 degrees for several hours. Temperatures dropped to a minimum of 24-25 degrees. No crop damage reported. Widespread temperatures below 32 degrees for several hours. Temperatures dropped to a minimum of 25-27 degrees. No crop damage reported. Widespread temperatures below 32 degrees for several hours. Temperatures dropped to a minimum of 24-26 degrees. No crop damage reported.

title: Coastal Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, Strong Wind: California, Dec 02, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Coastal Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, Strong Wind, from December 02, 2014 to December 03, 2014. Affected areas: Alameda, Marin, North Bay Interior Valleys, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, Santa Cruz Mountains, Sonoma, Southern Monterey Bay And Big Sur Coast. Episode summary: A winter storm impacted the Bay Area with rain and wind, bringing some flooding issues as well as downed trees and power lines across the area. Details: Flooding blocking three lanes of freeway in Yerba Buena Island Tunnel on the Bay Bridge. Intersection of Highways 12 and 121 closed due to flooding. Trees down in Saratoga due to the heavy rainfall weakening the ground. Reported property and crop damage: about $76,000.

title: Heavy Rain: California, Jan 11, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, from January 11, 2015 to January 11, 2015. Affected areas: Kern. Episode summary: A series of disturbances moved into Southern California on January 10 and 11, 2015, and brushed across Kern county and the Tulare county portion of the Sierra Nevada. Only light precipitation occurred on January 10, but the system that moved through on the 11th was stronger and produced locally heavy rain. This resulted in some street flooding in the Bakersfield area along with some rock slides along Highway 178 in the Kern county mountains, and along Redrock-Randsburg Road in the Kern county desert. Details: Heavy rain resulted in a rock slide on the eastbound side of Highway 178 near the mouth of the Kern Canyon. The road was blocked by baseball sized rocks. Heavy rain contributed to rocks sliding across the roadway. Rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch in 24 hours over the Kern county produced ponding of water/flooding on roadways in the south end of the San Joaquin Valley, in and south of Bakersfield. The flooded areas included part of Highway 99 between Rosedale Highway and Olive Drive in Bakersfield and Highway 119 near Buena Vista.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 24, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 24, 2014 to December 24, 2014. Affected areas: Owens Valley. Episode summary: A Pacific storm system and associated cold front brought isolated high winds to the Owens Valley. Details: The Bishop (KBIH) ASOS recorded high winds for 30 minutes, with the peak gust occurring at 2217 PST. A tree blew into the roadway on the northwest side of town. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather: California, Dec 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather, from December 30, 2014 to December 31, 2014. Affected areas: Eastern Mojave Desert, Morongo Basin, San Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley. Episode summary: A very cold storm system brought rare low elevation snow to the Mojave Desert. Details: Two inches of snow fell in Yucca Valley. Three vehicle crashes in the Morongo Basin resulted in five (indirect) injuries. Very light snow fell as low as Kelso and Nipton, with two to three inches in the higher elevations of the Mojave National Preserve. At least three vehicle accidents were reported due to slick roads. Highway 95 was also closed from Interstate 40 to the Nevada state line for about three hours due to snow. About half an inch of snow accumulated in Needles. Approximately one sixth of the customers in town lost power. Reported property and crop damage: about $60,000.

title: High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Dec 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Strong Wind, from December 30, 2014 to December 31, 2014. Affected areas: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, East Bay Hills And The Diablo Range, East Bay Interior Valleys, North Bay Interior Valleys, Northern Monterey Bay, San Francisco, San Francisco Bay Shoreline, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Santa Clara Valley Including San Jose, Santa Cruz Mountains, Southern Monterey Bay And Big Sur Coast. Episode summary: A strong wind storm struck the Bay Area on December 30 during the afternoon and evening hours. Strong winds brought down numerous trees and power lines across the area. The combination of recent heavy rains earlier in the month brought weakened ground conditions and then there were numerous dead trees across the area from years of ongoing drought. Major disruptions to the evening commute due to downed trees and the accidents they caused were observed. Wind gusts of 40-55 MPH were widespread across the area. Despite most areas not reaching 60 MPH, there was widespread wind damage and impacts due to the reasons above. Details: A tree blown down blocking the Interstate 880 South off ramp onto East Brokaw near Milpitas. A wind gust of 64 MPH was measured atop Mt. Diablo. A four foot diameter tree was blown down blocking both lanes of Empire Grade Road and resulting in a closure of the road. Reported property and crop damage: about $207,200.

title: Flood: California, Feb 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from February 07, 2015 to February 08, 2015. Affected areas: Siskiyou. Episode summary: Heavy rains caused flooding along the Scott River. Details: The Scott River at Fort Jones exceeded the flood stage of 15.0 feet at 07/0100 PST. The stream crested at 17.25 feet at 07/1100 PST. The stream dropped below flood stage at 08/0045 PST.

title: Flood: California, Feb 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from February 07, 2015 to February 07, 2015. Affected areas: Siskiyou. Episode summary: Heavy rains caused flooding along the Klamath River. Details: The Klamath River at Seiad Valley exceeded the flood stage of 15.0 feet at 07/0700 PST. The stream crested at 16.29 feet at 07/1515 PST. The stream dropped below flood stage at 07/2115 PST.

title: Flood: California, Feb 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from February 06, 2015 to February 08, 2015. Affected areas: Siskiyou. Episode summary: Heavy rains brought flooding to streams and some urban areas in Siskiyou County. Details: Flooding was reported along the Scott River near Callahan and near Kidder Creek. There were also reports of farmland flooding along the Shasta River.

title: Winter Storm: Wisconsin, Jan 31, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Storm, from January 31, 2015 to January 31, 2015. Affected areas: Crawford, Grant. Episode summary: Parts of southwest Wisconsin received heavy snow on the last day of January. The area was set up to for heavy snow after a cold front moved through the region on the 30th. This front was not very far south of the region as an area of low pressure moved along it, throwing moisture from the Gulf of Mexico into the cold air. As a result, heavy snow started falling during the evening of the 31st. This heavy snow continued into February 1st with two day totals of 6 to 10 inches common. The highest reported total was 10.5 inches near Eastman (Crawford County). In addition to the snow, the area of low pressure also produced winds of 20 to 40 mph that caused considerable drifting to occur. Details: COOP and volunteer snow observers reported heavy snow across Crawford County during the evening of January 31st. The heavy snow continued into February 1st. COOP and volunteer snow observers reported heavy snow across Grant County during the evening of January 31st. The heavy snow continued into February 1st.

title: Flood: California, Feb 08, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from February 08, 2015 to February 09, 2015. Affected areas: Siskiyou. Episode summary: A line of heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms dropped an estimated 1-4 inches of rain in south central Siskiyou county from Dunsmuir north to the Weed area. There was some flooding as a result of this. Details: Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms dropped an estimated 1-4 inches of rain in 12-18 hours from Dunsmuir north to the Weed area. An underground culvert was overwhelmed and water backed up into several buildings and over roads in Weed. An emergency manager reported that the Sacramento River was beginning to overrun its banks near Dunsmuir. Some flooding was also reported near burn scars in

title: Heavy Rain: California, Jan 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, from January 26, 2015 to January 27, 2015. Affected areas: San Bernardino. Episode summary: Cooling temperatures overnight after light rain the previous evening led to isolated dense fog over the Mojave Desert. Details: Rain, low clouds, and fog led to four car crashes in the Morongo Basin with two (indirect) injuries. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Strong Wind: California, Feb 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, from February 06, 2015 to February 06, 2015. Affected areas: Owens Valley. Episode summary: A Pacific storm system and strong jet stream brought gusty winds to the Owens Valley. Isolated damage occurred west-northwest of Bishop. Details: A large cottonwood tree blew down 13 miles WNW of Bishop, blocking Round Valley Road at Boundary Road. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: High Wind: California, Feb 05, 2015

title: Flash Flood, Flood: California, Dec 02, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, from December 02, 2014 to December 04, 2014. Affected areas: Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego. Episode summary: A Pacific storm brought moderate to heavy rain and flash flooding to the region from the 2nd through the 4th. Two-day rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches were recorded west of the mountains, while the southern slopes of the San Bernardino County mountains saw up to 5 inches of rain (isolated amount of 14.5 inches at Yucaipa Ridge). The heavy rain caused countless instances of flooding, with mud, debris and water closing several roadways and stranding vehicles. Snow levels remained above 8000 feet, so no snow accumulation was observed. Details: Valley of the Falls Road reported open, but minor flooding as Mill Creek was running full. Yucaipa Ridge reported 4 inches of rain in 6 hours. CHP reported flooding and mud at San Timoteo Canyon Road and Live Oak Canyon Road. CHP reported Duncan road in Phelan closed due to flooding between Sheepcreek and Buckwheat roads and minor street flooding at Main St. and I Ave near Hesperia. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jan 02, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from January 02, 2015 to January 02, 2015. Affected areas: Ector. Episode summary: There was a strong upper low over Arizona and New Mexico that was slowly moving toward West Texas. Good moisture was across the area and lift increased as the upper low approached the region. These conditions contributed to precipitation developing across much of West Texas. Due to the cold air that was in place, the precipitation was a wintry mix across most of the area. Moderate to heavy rainfall coupled with ice impeding drainage of water as temperatures warmed up above freezing allowed for flash flooding to develop across parts of the Permian Basin. Details: The combination of moderate to heavy rainfall, melting of snow and ice, and ice blocking the drainage of water contributed to flash flooding in Odessa. There were multiple high water rescues as a result of these conditions. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $6,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, High Wind: California, Dec 12, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Flood, High Wind, from December 12, 2014 to December 12, 2014. Affected areas: Apple And Lucerne Valleys, Orange, San Diego. Episode summary: A strong Pacific low pressure system brought increasing wind and precipitation with a period of heavy rain the morning of the 12th and showers continued into the following morning. Significant post-frontal showers occurred in San Diego County, as well as local convergence of air around coastal islands, producing a narrow band of showers. Widespread rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches were recorded in the coast and valley areas. The snow level dropped to around 6000 feet, with 2 to 5 inches of snow above 6000 feet and 6 to 8 inches above 7000 feet. Mountain locations below 6000 feet saw up to around 4 inches of rain. River rises in the San Diego River at Fashion Valley resulted in a levee breach which flooded the parking lot of Qualcomm Stadium. Several other roadways in San Diego County were closed due to flooding with mud and debris in the road, especially near the Tijuana River Valley. Most wind gusts were below 58 mph, with the exception of Burns Canyon in the upper desert. High Surf was also generated along west facing Orange and San Diego County beaches by the storm that moved through. Details: KOGO radio reported flooding along Highway 78 and El Camino Real. An NWS employee reported around an inch of standing water on Interstate 5 stretching from Camp Pendleton, south to Highway 78. KOGO radio reported a flooded ramp onto Interstate 5 near National City. News10 reported a levee breech along the San Diego River near Qualcomm stadium, releasing large amounts of water into the parking area. At the time, the San Diego River stage was at

title: Flood: California, Dec 16, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, from December 16, 2014 to December 17, 2014. Affected areas: San Diego. Episode summary: A weak, upper-level trough of low pressure moved through the West on the 16th, with scattered showers and high elevation snow. Showers lingered through the night, before a second, stronger trough moved through the region on the 17th. Showers increased in coverage and intensity with the second trough, behind a leading line of strong thunderstorms, with scattered thunderstorms behind it. Significant lightning activity occurred with this initial, organized line of thunderstorms between approximately 2200 PST on the 16th and 0400 PST on the 17th. Post-frontal showers continued, with a few reports of small hail, and a funnel cloud at Riverside March Field. Two-day rainfall totals varied widely with the coast and valley locations receiving between one-tenth and almost one inch of rain, but most saw between one-quarter and three-quarters of an inch. Coastal mountain slope locations received up to 1.3 inches of rain, while the deserts ranged from a few hundredths of an inch to one-third of an inch (highest amounts in the upper deserts). Several roads were closed due to flooding in San Marcos, Spring Valley and a mud/debris flow along Highway 91 in Corona. The snow level lowered to 4500-5000 feet, with two-day accumulations of up to 4 inches below 6000 feet and up to 10 inches between 6000-8000 feet. Details: CHP reported the roadway completely flooded at the I-805 and Highway 94 interchange where a vehicle hydroplaned and overturned. Nearby stations reported instantaneous rainfall rates of 0.25 to 0.40 per hour. Road closed due to flowing water in Escondido Creek over Country Club Drive on low lying crossing. Webcams from SD county flood control confirmed flooding. News 10 reported roadway flooding Along Bent Avenue at Discover

title: Coastal Flood: California, Dec 20, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Coastal Flood, from December 20, 2014 to December 20, 2014. Affected areas: San Diego County Coastal Areas. Episode summary: A long-period, west-northwest swell generated elevated surf along exposed west-facing beaches in San Diego and Orange Counties for the 20th through the 24th. Astronomical high tides above 7 feet each morning, combined with the elevated surf, caused minor tidal overflow in low-lying beach areas in San Diego County on the 20th. Strong rip currents were also observed through the period. Details: Minor tidal overflow was observed along the strand south from Oceanside Pier to Wisconsin Street between 0700-0800 PST on the 20th.

title: Winter Storm: Texas, Dec 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, from December 30, 2014 to December 31, 2014. Affected areas: Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mcculloch, Menard and 9 more areas. Episode summary: A high impact winter storm event affected most of West Central Texas during the period from January 30, 2014 through noon on January 2, 2015. The winter storm continued into the midnight hours of January 3rd. The freezing rain and sleet formed an icy glaze on area roads that either slowed or shut down ground travel, air travel and commerce across much of the region by the morning of December 31st. There were numerous accidents in the cities of Abilene and San Angelo. A hospital in San Angelo had to divert patients as it ran out of room. An arctic cold front caused temperatures to drop below freezing across much the region by the afternoon and the evening of the 30th and continued through New Years Eve and New Years Day. Details: About 0.39 inches of ice and sleet was reported 1 mile north northwest of Roby. About half an inch of ice and sleet was reported in Anson. A quarter inch of sleet and freezing rain was reported in Sterling City. Law enforcement officials reported dangerous driving conditions and several accidents in the county. They also reported it was difficult for emergency personnel to reach these accidents.

title: Flood: Wisconsin, Dec 10, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flood, from December 10, 2014 to December 19, 2014. Affected areas: Menominee (C). Episode summary: Three separate ice jams along the Wolf River about 0.75 mile south of Keshena lead to flooding in the Keshena area. Details: Ice jams, comprised of frazil ice, caused low-land flooding along the Wolf River in Keshena. An excavator was used in an attempt to open up a channel that would allow water to bypass the jam, but those efforts were unsuccessful. About a dozen structures were affected by the high waters, and some homes had flooding in their basements. The intersection of State Highways 47/55 and County Trunk VV Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 11, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 11, 2014 to December 11, 2014. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Mono. Episode summary: Strong low pressure approaching the northern California coast brought widespread wind damage to the Lake Tahoe area and to parts of Mono County on the 11th. Details: Winds gusted to 60 and 70 mph at the Truckee and South Lake Tahoe airports, respectively, on the morning of the 11th. Over the Sierra ridges, winds gusted as high as 135 mph. Numerous trees and power lines were downed, along with damage to several homes and vehicles due to fallen trees. The power outages, some lasting up to 2 days, caused South Lake Tahoe schools to be closed through the 12th. Fin Downslope winds gusted to between 65 and 80 mph near the highway 395 corridor. Locally higher winds to over 100 mph occurred near the highway 395 and state route 167 junction (near Mono City) shortly after 1100PST, with reports of windows shattered and roof shingles blown off. Also, a roof blew off a home and serious damage was noted at a gas station awning in Lee Vining. Reported property and crop damage: about $250,000.

title: High Wind: California, Dec 23, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from December 23, 2014 to December 25, 2014. Affected areas: Apple And Lucerne Valleys, Coachella Valley, San Diego County Mountains, Santa Ana Mountains And Foothills. Episode summary: Surface pressure strengthened to a 1035 mb high over the Great Basin on the 22nd, resulting in gusty Santa Ana winds through the 23rd, strongest in the early mornings of the 23rd. Winds remained strong through the 25th, but shifted around to the northwest (onshore) on the 24th ahead of an approaching low pressure system passing to the north of the area. No significant damage was reported as a result of these winds. Details: High winds occurred at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0051-0551 PST on the 23rd. During this time, winds were sustained out of the ENE at 30-40 mph with gusts in the 60s, including the peak gust of 67 mph, recorded between 0151-0251 PST. High winds occurred at the Pleasants Peak mesonet station between 0059-0229 PST on the 23rd. During this time, winds were sustained out of the east at 45-50 mph High winds occurred at the Whitewater RAWS between 2200 PST on the 24th and 0400 PST on the 25th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the WNW at 30-40 mph with gusts in the upper 50s, with a peak gust of 61 mph, recorded between 2150-2250 PST. High winds occurred at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1751 PST on the 24th and 0051 PST on the 25th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the WSW at 35-50 mph with gusts 60-75 mph. A peak gust of 90 mph, recorded between 2151-2251 PST.

title: Drought: Texas, Dec 01, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from December 01, 2014 to December 31, 2014. Affected areas: Bandera, Caldwell, De Witt, Edwards, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Medina, Val Verde. Episode summary: December was a dry month across South Central Texas with nearly all of the area receiving less than normal rainfall. Only four of the southeastern counties had above normal. With the lack of rainfall Caldwell, Edwards, and Val Verde Counties moved into Severe Drought category (Stage D2). Medina County remained in Extreme Drought category (Stage D3) and Bandera, De Witt, Gillespie, Kendall, and Kerr remained in D2. Fire danger was low across the area at the end of the month and of the counties in D2 or worse drought only De Witt, Medina, and Val Verde had burn bans in effect. The seven day stream flow average at the end of the month was below normal (10-24 percent) for the Medina, Lower San Antonio, and Frio River basins. The Guadalupe and Nueces River Basins were much below normal (less than 10 percent). Area lakes and reservoirs continued well below normal pool elevations. Lake Amistad rose slightly during the month but was still 29.9 feet below normal. Lake Travis was also up slightly at 57.7 feet below normal. Medina Lake dropped again and was 89.7 feet below normal. The Edwards Aquifer dropped slightly during the month and was at 636.0 feet. This was 4.9 feet lower than at the end of December 2013 and 33.2 feet below average. The Barton Springs Edwards Aquifer Conservation District continued stage 2 alarm drought status requiring a 20% reduction in pumping. Fredericksburg remained in stage 3 water restrictions and Kerrville remained in stage 2. Details: December was a dry month across South Central Texas with nearly all of the area receiving less than normal rainfall.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from December 31, 2014 to December 31, 2014. Affected areas: Bandera, Edwards, Kerr, Real, Uvalde. title: Heavy Snow, High Wind, Winter Storm, Winter Weather: California, Dec 30, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, High Wind, Winter Storm, Winter Weather, from December 30, 2014 to December 31, 2014. Affected areas: Coachella Valley, Orange County Coastal Areas, Riverside County Mountains, San Bernardino And Riverside County Valleys - The Inland Empire, San Bernardino County Mountains, San Diego County Mountains, San Diego County Valleys, Santa Ana Mountains And Foothills. Episode summary: A very cold and potent low pressure system approached southern California on the 30th with showers increasing through the day and night with a shot of very low-elevation snow. The brunt of the storm occurred during the night of the 30th and morning of the 31st. Snow levels dropped rapidly overnight down to 1500-2000 feet, with some light accumulations even down to 1000 feet. The southern Inland Empire was hardest hit with the unusually low snow, covering areas like Temecula, Lake Elsinore, and Wildomar, which caused issues all along Interstate 15 down through Valley Center. Several inches were also reported in Ranchita and Julian in San Diego County. Overall, the snow totals went as follows: 10 to 18 inches across Palomar Mountain to Julian, 6 to 9 inches from Warner Springs to Julian in San Diego County, 2 to 4 inches from Temecula to Wildomar and Lake Elsinore in the southern Inland Empire, and 4 to 8 inches across Highway 74 and Horsethief canyon in the Santa Ana Mountains. The snow resulted in several road closures, including Highway 74 and Highway 18, stranded vehicles and chain controls on the roads that remained open. Rainfall totals below the snow level generally ranged from .25-1.25 inches, with no significant flooding reported. Thunderstorms also occurred with the leading edge of the cold front from Oceanside and Carlsbad to La Mesa with hail up to one-half inch diameter. Strong winds also accompanied

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from February 22, 2015 to February 23, 2015. Affected areas: Bailey, Briscoe, Castro, Childress, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hall and 12 more areas. Episode summary: Following an arctic front on the morning of the 22nd, periods of freezing drizzle and sleet created icy stretches mainly across the South Plains and Rolling Plains. Enough moisture and lift in the Rolling Plains even led to the development of several elevated thunderstorms this morning. During the overnight of the 22nd into the 23rd, a deeper fetch of subtropical moisture arrived and produced a second round of wintry precipitation mostly in the form of light snow and some sleet. Although most snow accumulations were generally light and at or below 1 inch, roads became hazardous for Monday morning commuters. Following at least two dozen vehicle accidents on Sunday in Lubbock County alone (one fatal accident occurred in Hale County), a surge of accidents occurred from Sunday night through Monday morning with 84 wrecks reported. The majority of these accidents occurred in the Lubbock area with at least two serious injuries reported by the Lubbock Police Department. Reported property and crop damage: about $500,000.

Episode summary: The California drought continued in full force during the month of January, 2015. Precipitation fell on only a few days of the month, and mostly across Kern County. Snowfall in the Sierra Nevada was limited to the highest elevations due to the warm nature of the storms that did move through. Temperatures remained well above normal throughout central California. ||The U.S. Drought Monitor continued to report exceptional drought conditions across the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The 2013-2014 water year (July 1 - June 30) concluded with Fresno setting its second driest on record (4.81 inches) and Bakersfield setting its third driest (2.41 inches). For the calendar year, 2014 was the warmest year on record for Fresno and Bakersfield. The trend of below normal precipitation and above normal temperatures continued into 2015. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, a decrease in the snow-related tourism activity in the Southern Sierra Nevada, reduction in air quality due to persistent stagnant air, loss or reduction of ground water, wells drying up in several communities leaving them with no water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains.

title: Flash Flood, High Wind, Tornado: California, Dec 11, 2014
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, High Wind, Tornado, from December 11, 2014 to December 12, 2014. Affected areas: Los Angeles, Los Angeles County Mountains Excluding The Santa Monica Range, San Luis Obispo County Mountains, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara County Central Coast, Santa Barbara County Mountains, Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area, Santa Ynez Valley, Ventura, Ventura County Mountains. Episode summary: A strong winter storm moved across Southwestern California, bringing strong winds and significant flooding to the area. Southerly wind gusts between 60 and 80 MPH were reported in the mountains as well as the Central Coast of Santa Barbara county. Due to heavy and intense rainfall, there were numerous reports of flash flooding. The most significant flooding event occurred in the Camarillo Springs area of Ventura county, near the Springs Fire burn scar. Details: The Branch Mountain sensor reported a southerly wind gust of 58 MPH. Strong southerly winds developed in the mountains of Santa Barbara county. The sensor at La Cumbre Peak reported wind gusts between 60 and 70 MPH. The sensor at Las Flores Canyon reported sustained winds between 40 and 42 MPH. Strong southerly winds developed in the mountains of Los Angeles county. Some wind gust reports from the local RAWS network include Camp Nine (gusts 59 to 84 MPH), Chilao (gusts 58 to 64 MPH) and Mill Creek (gusts 62 to 74 MPH).

title: Winter Weather: Wisconsin, Feb 25, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Winter Weather, from February 25, 2015 to February 26, 2015. Affected areas: Kenosha, Milwaukee, Racine. Episode summary: The northern fringes of a light snow area, from low pressure tracking southeast along the Missouri River Valley, overspread southern WI for the afternoon and early evening of February 25th. The winds also turned onshore from Lake MI resulting in lake effect snow from the late afternoon of February 25th, and for much of the morning of February 26th. The combination of lake effect snow and system snow produced snowfall of 3 to 6 inches over Milwaukee County and the eastern portions of Racine and Kenosha Counties. More than half of the snow accumulation was due to moderate to heavy bursts of lake effect snow. Numerous slide-offs and accidents occurred during the morning rush hour. Details: Powdery snow accumulations of 3-6 inches with the highest totals over southeast Milwaukee County. Powdery snow accumulations of 3-6 inches with the highest totals over eastern Racine County. Powdery snow accumulations of 3-5 inches with the highest totals over eastern Kenosha County.

Another person was found dead, floating in the water. Strong north to northeast winds impacted the Santa Monica Mountains. The RAWS sensor at Malibu Hills reported wind gusts between 59 and 78 MPH. title: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather, from February 27, 2015 to February 27, 2015. Affected areas: Bailey, Castro, Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Hall, Hockley, Lamb, Lubbock, Motley, Parmer and 3 more areas. Episode summary: Following a modified arctic cold front the evening prior, an approaching trough aloft generated two separate bands of heavy snow shortly after midnight CST. The first band fell over the far northwest South Plains and southwest Texas Panhandle with a second and narrower band that impacted parts of the South Plains east into the northern Rolling Plains. The latter of these mesoscale snow bands proved quite intense at times and produced snow burst rates measured at 1.6 inches per hour by on-duty NWS employees in south Lubbock. This intense snowfall shifted east of the Lubbock metro area well before the brunt of morning commuters hit the roads, although a few dozen minor vehicle accidents were still noted in Lubbock alone. Fortunately, this number could have been much higher had many area schools and businesses not closed for the day.||List of notable snow measurements from this event:||5.0 inches at Lubbock Int'l Airport (Lubbock County), Lubbock NWS Office (Lubbock County), Matador (Motley County), Muleshoe (Bailey County), and Roaring Springs (Motley County),|4.8 inches at Levelland (Hockley County),|4.5 inches at Shallowater (Lubbock County) and Crosbyton (Crosby County),|4.0 inches at Friona (Parmer County), Hart (Castro County), Paducah (Cottle County), Spur (Dickens County), and 6NNW Ropesville (Hockley County),|3.0 inches at Plains (Yoakum County), Olton (Lamb County), Tulia (Swisher County), Denver City (Yoakum County), and Turkey (Hall County),|2.5 inches at Aspermont (Stonewall County).

title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2015 to March 31, 2015. Affected areas: Briscoe, Childress, Cottle, Hall, King, Motley, Stonewall. Episode summary: Drought conditions worsened from extreme (D3) to exceptional (D4) levels across the eastern half of Childress County, but remained unchanged since February over the remainder of the far southeast Texas Panhandle south into portions of the Rolling Plains where D2 (severe) and D3 conditions persisted. Although monthly precipitation was near normal just west of these drought stricken areas, precipitation was below normal for much of the southeast Texas Panhandle with monthly deficits in excess of one inch. Fortunately, agricultural drought impacts were low with area livestock still able to forage on winter wheat stands that benefited from precipitation earlier in the year. However, farmers already preparing fields for spring planting will be in great need of deep soil moisture. Fire weather impacts remained unusually low in spite of above normal fuel loads. Much of this was attributed to a relative lack of windy, dry and warm weather patterns.

title: Winter Storm: Texas, Feb 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, from February 23, 2015 to February 23, 2015. Affected areas: Bowie, Camp, Cass, Franklin, Gregg, Harrison, Marion, Morris, Red River, Smith, Titus, Upshur and 1 more areas. Episode summary: A cold dome of arctic air spilled southward out of the Central and Southern Plains, into the Lower Mississippi Valley ahead of the Winter Storm event. The flow aloft was from the west southwest with embedded disturbances moving towards the region from West Texas. These disturbances provided the necessary lift to generate widespread winter precipitation across the region in the form of freezing rain and sleet. Temperatures during the predawn hours of February 23rd were mostly just above freezing but once the precipitation moved in from the west, the precipitation quickly changed over to freezing rain mixed with sleet as the temperatures fell during the day. Freezing rain accumulations across Northeast Texas, mainly along and north of the Interstate 20 corridor were near one tenth of an inch or less. Sleet accumulations along and north of the Interstate 20 corridor ranged from near one half inch to near one and one half inch.

title: Winter Storm: Texas, Feb 25, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, from February 25, 2015 to February 25, 2015. Affected areas: Bowie, Camp, Cass, Franklin, Gregg, Harrison, Marion, Morris, Panola, Red River, Smith, Titus and 2 more areas. Episode summary: Cold arctic air remained in place across the region and there was already ice on the ground across some locations that observed a Winter Storm from sleet accumulation on Monday, February 23rd. An upper level trough exited the Four Corners region of the country and moved into the Texas Hill Country during the predawn hours of Wednesday, February 25th. Widespread precipitation developed ahead of the trough across Texas and moved into the region shortly after midnight on the 25th. The precipitation began as a mixture of light rain or freezing rain after midnight towards the predawn hours on Wednesday. As the trough moved closer into the region from the west, the precipitation quickly transitioned over to sleet and eventually moderate to heavy snow across a good portion of the region after sunrise on the 25th. The mixed winter precipitation moved out of the region during the late afternoon or early evening hours of the 25th. Snowfall totals across Northeast Texas along and north of the Interstate 20 corridor ranged from 1 inch to near 7 inches. Some of the greatest snowfall accumulations were found at the following locations: Longview: 7 inches, Domino: 7 inches, Avery: 5 inches, Texarkana: 4 inches, Mount Pleasant: 4 inches, Clarksville: 4 inches, Talco: 4 inches, Hallsville: 4 inches, Gladewater: 4 inches.

title: Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind, Strong Wind: California, Feb 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flood, Heavy Rain, High Wind, Strong Wind, from February 06, 2015 to February 09, 2015. Affected areas: Alameda, Contra Costa, East Bay Hills And The Diablo Range, East Bay Interior Valleys, Marin, Monterey, Napa, North Bay Interior Valleys, North Bay Mountains, San Benito, San Francisco, San Francisco Bay Shoreline and 7 more areas. Episode summary: A strong winter storm finally impacted California following up on nearly a month and a half of no rain and the driest January on record. The storm brought heavy rain, gusty winds, and damage to trees and power lines along with some minor flooding of urban areas. Rainfall amounts were heaviest in the mountains with 5-10 inches or more occurring. Generally 1-3.5 inches fell in low elevation areas and urban spots, with less than an inch in Southern Monterey County. Winds gusted 50-70 MPH with the highest gusts in the mountains of the region. Several small mudslides were reported with the largest occurring in the Santa Cruz Mountains north of Boulder Creek on Highway 9. Details: A fuel tanker crashed in heavy rain on Highway 1 North of Jenner in Sonoma County. The tanker leaked about 9,000 gallons of diesel into the ocean. A gust of 59 MPH measured on the Calaveras Road RAWS at elevation 1230 ft. A wind gust of 70 MPH measured on Mt. Diablo at elevation 3849 feet. Reported property and crop damage: about $114,300.

title: High Wind: California, Feb 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from February 06, 2015 to February 09, 2015. Affected areas: Mendocino Coast, Mendocino Interior, North Coast Interior, Redwood Coast. Episode summary: A strong storm system brought several cold fronts to Northwest California over a few days in early February. Each cold front brought high winds to parts of Northwest California. This resulted in numerous power outages and trees blown down. Details: The Crescent City ASOS reported a gust to 64 mph. Law enforcement reported a large limb of a Redwood tree fell on a Humboldt State University residence hall. This caused damage to the third floor of the building. They also reported numerous trees were blown down. The Crescent City ASOS reported a gust to 66 mph. Law enforcement reported a few 3-4 foot diameter Redwood trees were blown down across Highway 199. They also reported that several other trees nearby were blown down. RAWS on the highest mountain peaks reported gusts up to 75-85 mph.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Jan 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from January 17, 2015 to January 17, 2015. Affected areas: Gray. Episode summary: The large wildfire began about one mile north of McLean around 1230CST and consumed approximately six hundred and forty acres. One vacant home and one shed were completely destroyed, however there were no reports of injuries or fatalities. The wildfire was brought under control around 1430CST which was caused by high winds striking a power line. Reported property and crop damage: about $100,000.

title: Wildfire: Texas, Feb 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Wildfire, from February 14, 2015 to February 14, 2015. Affected areas: Potter. Episode summary: The 2381 or Bushland Wildfire began about two miles north of Bushland around 1430CST and consumed roughly nine hundred and sixteen acres. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities and there were also no reports of any homes or other structures damaged or destroyed by the wildfire. The fire spread north to near Farm to Market Road 1061 and Farm to Market Road 2381 where it was stopped from spreading any further. Farm to Market Road 2381 was closed and a part of Farm to Market Road 1061 was closed during the late afternoon and early evening hours. The cause of the wildfire has not yet been determined but may have been accidental. The fire was contained by 1900CST and the Texas Forest Service, Potter County Fire Department, the Randall County Fire Department along with a few other fire departments responded to the wildfire.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from January 10, 2015 to January 10, 2015. Affected areas: Bell, Coryell, Lampasas. This resulted in some light accumulations of sleet and freezing rain over some of the southern counties of North Texas as temperatures dropped below freezing by early Saturday. Details: Minor icing was reported near the town of Troy by the Bell County Sheriff's Department. Patchy icing was reported on roads and bridges by the Sheriff's Department with no major issues. title: Drought: Texas, Jan 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from January 01, 2015 to January 31, 2015. Affected areas: Bosque, Collin, Comanche, Coryell, Dallas, Delta, Denton, Eastland, Ellis, Erath, Fannin, Grayson and 16 more areas. Episode summary: Severe or greater drought conditions continued to plague central and western portions of north Texas during January of 2015. Details: Severe/D2 drought conditions covered all of Bosque County at the beginning of January, with some of the far northern locations even being classified under Extreme/D3. By the end of the month, only the northern half of the county was listed under Severe/D2 drought, with the southern half having improved to D1/Moderate Drought. Hill County spent all of January, 2015 with Severe/D2 drought conditions in place, though the far southern reaches were classified as merely D1/Moderate, and the northern-most locations were listed as Extreme/D3. Navarro County was affected by Severe/D2 Drought across the northwestern quarter of the county for all of January, 2015. The rest of the county was listed as Moderate drought or better. Reported property and crop damage: about $42,500.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Mar 09, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from March 09, 2015 to March 09, 2015. Affected areas: Cherokee, Gregg, Harrison, Panola, Rusk, Smith. Episode summary: A deep upper level trough was anchored across northern Mexico into the Texas Hill Country on March 9th which allowed for deep Pacific and Gulf of Mexico moisture to infiltrate the region. Embedded disturbances moved into the Southern Plains and Lower Mississippi Valley and produced the necessary lift for widespread and excessive heavy rainfall. Details: FM 2868 was flooded and closed near the community of Flint, Texas. Several city and secondary roads were closed due to excessive heavy rainfall. Excessive heavy rainfall forced the closure of County Road 2217 near Tatum, Texas.

title: Winter Storm: Texas, Jan 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, from January 01, 2015 to January 03, 2015. Affected areas: Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher, Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mcculloch, Menard and 9 more areas. Episode summary: A high impact winter storm event affected much of West Central Texas during the period from January 30, 2014 through noon on January 2, 2015. The winter storm continued through midnight on January 3rd for areas north of Interstate 20. The freezing rain and sleet formed an icy glaze on area roads that either slowed or shut down ground travel, air travel and commerce across much of the region by the morning of December 31st. There were numerous accidents in the cities of Abilene and San Angelo. A hospital in San Angelo had to divert patients as it ran out of room. An arctic cold front caused temperatures to drop below freezing across much the region by the afternoon and the evening of the 30th. And these freezing temperatures remained through New Years Eve and New Years Day. Details: A half an inch of sleet and freezing rain was reported in Sweetwater along with numerous accidents. A quarter inch of ice and sleet was reported at Abilene State Park. Over 100 accidents were reported from the night of the 30th through New Years Day. The Abilene Airport was closed. A trained spotter estimated about four tenths of an inch of ice and sleet in Baird.

This was a prolonged snow event that began by early afternoon on March 22nd and ended the morning of March 23rd. title: Extreme Cold/Wind Chill: Wisconsin, Jan 04, 2015

Wind chills dropped as low as 37 below zero at Manitowish Waters (Vilas Co.) and Marshfield (Wood Co.). Details: The coldest wind chill recorded in Marathon County was 36 below zero at Mosinee. The coldest wind chill recorded in Wood County was 37 below zero at Marshfield. The coldest wind chill recorded in Vilas County was 37 below zero at Manitowish Waters.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Jan 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from January 13, 2015 to January 13, 2015. Affected areas: Crockett, Irion. This frozen precipitation resulted in two fatalities. Details: At 628 AM CST, law enforcement reported two rollover accidents on Interstate 10 overpasses, resulting in two fatalities at mile markers 343 and 369. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from March 21, 2015 to March 21, 2015. Affected areas: Chambers, Galveston, Washington. A swath of four and seven inches of rain fell from Brazoria County to Chambers County. Details: There were flooded and impassable roadways, with a few flooded vehicles, around town. A local rain gauge at Spindletop Bayou near Winnie reported 6.89 inches of rainfall. High water was observed near the intersection of FM 1155 and South Meyersville Road. title: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather: Texas, Mar 04, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather, from March 04, 2015 to March 04, 2015. title: Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Apr 09, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, from April 09, 2015 to April 09, 2015. Affected areas: Ozaukee. Episode summary: The approach of a warm front brought numerous showers and thunderstorms, and heavy rain to southern WI the night of April 8th into the morning of April 9th. Low pressure then tracked along the warm front that was located along the WI and IL border in the evening. Numerous thunderstorms developed over southern WI and northern IL from the late afternoon and evening hours. Several of the thunderstorms produced severe hail in southern WI. Details: A 100 yard stretch of southbound I-43 became flooded resulting in two vehicles mostly submerged in standing water. The flooding was under the overpass and a clogged drain significantly contributed to the flooding. Approximately 2-3 inches of rain had fallen during the overnight period. Reported property and crop damage: about $35,000.

title: Flood: Texas, Apr 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from April 13, 2015 to April 13, 2015. Affected areas: Terry, Yoakum. Episode summary: Numerous slow moving showers and thunderstorms developed this morning north of an upper low located over the western Permian Basin. One particularly intense band of rainfall trained northwestward across western Terry and eastern Yoakum Counties late this morning for nearly three hours. Rainfall totals underneath this band measured as great as seven inches at the Tokio (Terry County) COOP gin. The NWS Lubbock regional hydrologist surveyed much of the area later that afternoon and documented widespread flooding of playa lakes, fields and some roads. Farm-to-Market Road 1780 south of the town of Tokio was closed at the Sulphur Springs Creek crossing due to water estimated up to three feet deep. Asphalt along this creek crossing was peeled away. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 16, 2015 to April 17, 2015. Affected areas: Harris, Liberty, Walker. title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 09, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from April 09, 2015 to April 09, 2015. Affected areas: Cherokee, Gregg, Harrison, Rusk. Episode summary: A potent upper level storm system ejected into the Central Plains on April 9th. An attendant developing cold front moved southeastward into the region during the late afternoon hours. A warm prefrontal airmass was noted across all of Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas and Northwest Louisiana during the late afternoon and evening hours which meant that strong instability was present. Deep layer shear was supportive of supercell and multicell thunderstorms. Low level storm relative helicity was also supportive of tornadoes, at least initially across Northeast Texas. title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 13, 2015 to April 13, 2015. Affected areas: Titus. Episode summary: With the aid of afternoon heating, moderate instability developed during the afternoon hours of April 13th across portions of Northeast Texas. A weak surface boundary moved into the region from the west with forcing noted along the boundary. Strong low level shear was noted during the afternoon along this boundary as well. The result was widely scattered storms and one of which produced a tornado in Titus County, Texas. Details: A brief but potent EF-2 tornado touched down east of Winfield, Texas during the afternoon of April 13th. This tornado struck the Mid America Pet Food Plant and damage consisted of tossing cars, trucks and trash dumpsters. title: Strong Wind: Texas, Apr 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Strong Wind, from April 16, 2015 to April 16, 2015. Affected areas: Bowie. Episode summary: A large complex of strong to severe thunderstorms moved out of Central Texas and into Northeast Texas during the early evening hours of April 16th. These storms encountered a moderately unstable airmass with strong deep layer shear. The result was scattered to numerous multicell thunderstorms and a few supercell thunderstorms that produced large hail and wind damage. Details: Strong non-thunderstorm wind gusts downed a few large trees in the Simms, Texas community. These winds were able to down the trees because of very saturated soils. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 18, 2015 to April 18, 2015. Affected areas: Rusk, Smith. Episode summary: Discrete supercell thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon hours across North Central Texas. These storms moved eastward into Northeast Texas during the late evening and overnight hours of the 18th. By the time the storms moved into Northeast Texas, the storms had evolved into a broken line of storms...producing damaging wind gusts and large hail. Despite relatively weak instability, the storms propagated eastward along a cold pool the developed out ahead of the storms. Details: County Road 111 was washed out in the New London community. A vehicle fell into the washout area of the roadway but they were evacuated from their vehicle. Numerous county roads were flooded in and around the Flint community. Greenbriar Road was flooded and closed as well. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 17, 2015 to April 17, 2015. Affected areas: Brazoria, Galveston, Harris, Wharton. Episode summary: An approaching broad upper low east of the Four Corners region placed eastern Texas in a favorable upper air pattern conducive to sustaining either a mesoscale storm complex or an organized linear storm system. Daytime heating, within a highly moist environment and a passing shortwave disturbance, allowed a south central Texas originating derecho to pass through within the southwest flow and cause severe weather damage across the Houston, Texas area. Details: County Road 215 was impassable due to flood waters. There were numerous reports of flooded roadways and stranded vehicles in high water in and around the city of Houston, Bellaire, Pasadena, La Porte and the Clear Lake/Webster areas. There were fire department high water rescues over the southeastern sector of the county. Impassable roads due to high flood waters include, but are not limited to, South Shepard Street, West Alabama Street, Westheimer Street flooding in the town of Richwood. Reported property and crop damage: about $316,000.

title: Drought: Texas, Feb 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from February 01, 2015 to February 28, 2015. Affected areas: Bandera, De Witt, Edwards, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Llano, Medina, Real, Val Verde. The seven day stream flow average at the end of the month was below normal (10-24 percent) for the Colorado River Basin. The Guadalupe, Medina, Frio, and Nueces River Basins were much below normal (less than 10 percent). Area lakes and reservoirs continued well below normal pool elevations. Lake Amistad remained 29.1 feet below normal. Lake Travis was up slightly at 55.2 feet below normal. Medina Lake dropped slightly and was 89.7 feet below normal. The Edwards Aquifer dropped during the month and was at 644.2 feet. This was actually 2.6 feet higher than at the end of February 2014 but still 24.4 feet below average. Fredericksburg remained in stage 3 water restrictions and Kerrville remained in stage 2. title: Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, Tornado, from April 22, 2015 to April 22, 2015. Affected areas: Briscoe, Floyd, Motley. Episode summary: Early this morning, a series of outflow boundaries moved south across the southern Texas Panhandle and much of the Rolling Plains. The most organized of these boundaries would eventually retreat north before stalling from near Hereford (Deaf Smith County, WFO AMA) southeast to Paducah (Cottle County). This boundary provided the focus for an intense and long-lived supercell that developed west of Hereford by mid-afternoon. This supercell proceeded to move southeast and impact areas from Happy and Tulia (Swisher County) southeast to Silverton (Briscoe County), Matador (Motley County) and Grow (King County) with destructive hail, downburst winds and torrential rainfall rates of one half inch in five minutes. By early evening, a second supercell developed west of Plainview (Hale County) and crawled eastward accompanied by hail up to golf ball size and a brief tornado over open land near Lockney (Floyd County). Details: Several storm spotters observed a brief tornado over open land about two miles west of Lockney. Detailed video from a storm chaser indicated this tornado was preceded by a well-defined rotating wall cloud. No damage survey was conducted as this tornado remained over open land. The Motley County emergency manager reported water over State Highway 70 north of Matador with several secondary roads impassable from high water. The NWS Lubbock regional hydrologist conducted a flood survey from torrential rains that fell across Briscoe, Floyd and Motley Counties. title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 24, 2015 to April 24, 2015. Affected areas: Lynn, Yoakum. Episode summary: Late this morning, scattered to numerous thunderstorms erupted over the central South Plains ahead of a vigorous mid-level dry slot. After producing pea size hail and minor street flooding in southwest Lubbock, these storms marched into the Rolling Plains and the far southeast Texas Panhandle. Shortly after 1200 CST, the northern end of these storms intensified into a small bow echo near Northfield (Motley County) where a severe wind gust to 59 mph occurred. This bow echo raced northeast at 50 mph and produced scattered damage to roofs and trees in the city of Childress. Farther west, very dry air and deep mixing west of a dryline helped carry some high winds to the surface over portions of the southern South Plains. No wind damage was reported with any of these high wind gusts, however sustained winds around 30 mph did result in some blowing dirt and minor visibility reductions. The overall lack of drought conditions and a healthy green-up of grasses helped mitigate both blowing dirt and wildfire impacts.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from March 17, 2015 to March 18, 2015. Affected areas: Duval, Jim Wells, Live Oak. Episode summary: A strong upper level storm system moving out of the Texas Big Bend interacted with unusually deep moisture over South Texas during the early morning hours of March 18th. Widespread heavy rainfall occurred over the eastern Brush Country to the Victoria Crossroads with rainfall amounts between 2 and 3 inches. Locally higher amounts between 3 and 5 inches occurred over Duval, Jim Wells, and Live Oak Counties. This led to flooding of low lying areas around Benavides, Orange Grove, and George West. title: High Wind, Wildfire: California, Feb 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, Wildfire, from February 06, 2015 to February 12, 2015. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area, Lassen/Eastern Plumas/Eastern Sierra, Mono, Surprise Valley. Episode summary: A strong front pushed into the West on the 6th, bringing widespread high winds along with areas of enhanced downslope winds in the lee of the Sierra. Details: Widespread wind gusts between 63 and 82 mph were noted near highway 395. However, the Bridgeport RAWS measured a wind gust to 91 mph. Numerous trees (up to 18 in diameter) were downed near Mono City, with some broken windows and roof damage noted as well. According to the Mammoth Times, power lines were downed which caused widespread power outages north of Mammoth for at least a day. Extreme downslope winds in the lee of the Sierra prompted rapid spread of the Round Fire, which raced up a drainage and burned 40 homes in Swall Meadows. The size of the fire was 6,537 acres according to CalOES. Precipitation arrived early in the morning on the 7th which dramatically slowed the fire, although the fire was not completely contained until the 12th. Wind gusts of 61 to 70 mph were recorded at the Surprise Valley RAWS.

title: Drought: Texas, Feb 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from February 01, 2015 to February 28, 2015. The drought became more intense by the second week of February for areas near and northeast of the DFW metroplex. However, multiple rounds of winter precipitation during the end of the month helped alleviate some of the drought for this area towards the end of the period. Details: The majority of Dallas County started the month under D3/Extreme drought conditions. By the second week, northwestern areas of the county worsened to D4/Exceptional drought. By the end of the month, all areas were under D3/Extreme drought conditions after multiple rounds of winter precipitation affected the area. Nearly all of Rockwall County started the month in D2/Severe drought conditions. By the second week, the western areas were under D3/Extreme drought conditions. By the end of the month, all areas returned to D2/Severe drought conditions after multiple rounds of winter precipitation affected the area. By the second week of February, the western portions of Kaufman County were in D2/Severe drought conditions. Reported property and crop damage: about $49,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Frost/Freeze, from February 18, 2015 to February 18, 2015. Affected areas: Kenedy. Episode summary: A cold front pushed across Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley during the afternoon hours of February 16th. Surface high pressure centered over south central Texas, combined with clear skies, rapidly decoupling winds, and lowering dew points to provide a good setup for a radiational cooling event that resulted in a short duration freeze for Kenedy County. Temperatures across Kenedy County dropped to or below freezing for several hours during the early morning hours of February 18th. Details: Two COOP sites in Kenedy County reported temperatures below freezing. The COOP site in Armstrong reported a low of 26 degrees and the site in Sarita reported a low of 30 degrees.
