Affected areas: Brown, Coke, Concho, Crockett, Kimble, Mcculloch, Nolan, Schleicher, Sterling, Sutton, Tom Green. Episode summary: Light freezing drizzle and some freezing rain fell across a large part of West Central Texas on February 28. This lead to icy roads and numerous accidents across the area. Details: The Concho County Sheriff's office reported a quarter inch of ice on most surfaces due to freezing rain. The temperature remained below freezing through the day. A glaze of ice remains on most roads and surfaces in San Angelo, creating hazardous travel conditions. The San Angelo Regional Airport was closed until 1 PM because of icy runways. The temperature remained below freezing through the day. There were reports of ice covered roads across Kimble County due to freezing drizzle and travel was extremely difficult.

title: High Wind: California, Feb 11, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from February 11, 2015 to February 12, 2015. Affected areas: San Bernardino And Riverside County Valleys - The Inland Empire, San Diego County Coastal Areas, San Diego County Mountains, San Diego County Valleys, Santa Ana Mountains And Foothills. Episode summary: A surface high over the Great Basin brought strong winds during the morning hours on the 11th and 12 of February. Strongest winds occurred in San Diego County on the 12th. Details: CBS 8 reported a large (approximately 75-foot tall) eucalyptus tree falling on a car in Encinitas due to strong easterly winds. The report also noted a large tree down in the Rancho Santa Fe area. For a period of 1 hour winds were sustained in the upper 30s with a peak gust of 63 mph. A peak wind gust of 58 mph was reported at the Otay Mountain mesonet station between 0714 PST and 0814 PST on the 12th. Sustained winds in the 30s with gusts in the 40s and low 50s were reported between 2014 PST on the 11th and 1514 PST on the 12th. CBS 8 reported a 50 foot tree downed in El Cajon. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,000.

title: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather: California, Feb 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather, from February 22, 2015 to February 23, 2015. Affected areas: Riverside County Mountains, San Bernardino County Mountains. Episode summary: An upper-level trough developed over northern California and deepened along the West Coast with an overland trajectory, eventually moving inland through southern California. The system contained enough moisture, aided by orographic lift, to result in moderate to locally heavy rainfall over and west of the mountains, as well as significant snowfall above 5500 feet. Locally gusty west winds also occurred along the deserts slopes and thorough the mountain passes. Details: Multiple trained spotters and a CoCoRaHS observer reported 12 hour snowfall totals of 3 to 6 inches in the city of Big Bear as of 0900PST on the 23rd. Elsewhere in the San Bernardino Mountains spotters reported lighter 12 hour totals at 0900PST on the 23rd, with 1 to 4 inches reported by trained spotters in Wrightwood, 2 inches reported by a trained spotter in Running Springs, and 1 inch reported The ski resorts of Mountain High and Snow Valley reported 10 to 14 inches of snow above 7000 feet in the 12 hours preceding 0900 PST on the 23rd. As of 0900PST on the 23rd 12 hour snowfall totals of 6 inches in Green Valley Lake and Snow Summit, 8 inches at the end of Mt Baldy Road, 3 inches in Forest Falls and Arrowbear, and 2 inches at Onyx Peak and Crestline were reported.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 24, 2015 to April 24, 2015. Affected areas: Cass, Upshur. Episode summary: West southwest flow aloft with embedded disturbances in this flow allowed for vigorous thunderstorm growth across Central and North Central Texas during the afternoon hours of April 24th. A warm front that was nearly stationary across North Texas into West Central Louisiana began moving north during the late afternoon and evening hours, allowing for a warm sector airmass to move into the entire region. Moderate instability, strong deep layer shear and high lapse rates resulted in multiple modes of strong to severe thunderstorms across Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas and Northern Louisiana. Details: An EF1 tornado touched down 8 miles northwest of Linden, Texas. Damage consisted of numerous trees uprooted and snapped. Several trees took down powerlines in the area as well. Estimated peak wind speeds were between 95 and 105 mph. Patch length was 6.21 miles long with a path width of 275 yards wide. An EF1 tornado touched down 8.5 miles west southwest of Gilmer, Texas. Damage consisted of numerous trees uprooted or snapped. One tree fell on a house but damage was minor to moderate. Estimated peak wind speeds were between 95-105 mph. The path length wsa 2 miles long with a path width of 700 yards wide. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Feb 25, 2015

These storms led to multiple areas of flash flooding, and some storms produced small hail and gusty winds. Details: Reports came in of multiple streets being under at least a foot of fast-rising water in the Arlington Heights neighborhood. One house was reported to have minor flooding on property, and Pecan Creek had overflowed 1 to 1.5 feet of water over several roadways. Flooding was reported over southbound Bridlewood at W. Windsor in Flower Mound. At least a foot of water was present across this roadway. Reported property and crop damage: about $6,500.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from April 18, 2015 to April 18, 2015. Affected areas: Hood, Palo Pinto. Episode summary: Severe thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a dryline located just west of the CWA in the afternoon hours. These storms eventually merged into a line that continued marching east across most of the region. Winds up to 70-80 mph and hail up to golf ball size were reported with these storms, and a brief EF-0 tornado occurred in Hood County. Details: The Sheriff's Office reported Indian Creek Road was washed out near the Brazos River. Amateur radio operators reported a brief tornado northeast of Oak Trail Shores, on the east side of Lake Granbury / Brazos River. Reported property and crop damage: about $8,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado, from April 24, 2015 to April 25, 2015. Affected areas: Denton, Ellis, Grayson, Parker, Tarrant. Episode summary: Severe thunderstorms erupted across the region in an unstable airmass ahead of an approaching upper level trough/low. Although initially isolated to scattered early in the event, the storms eventually merged into a squall line that moved across the region. This system produced an EF0 tornado in Parker County and another EF0 tornado in Ellis County. In addition, very strong and damaging winds up to 90 mph occurred in Tarrant and Johnson County near the apex of an embedded bow echo. Flooding in Denton County left many roads closed through the day and into the morning of the 25th. Details: A National Weather Service storm survey crew found evidence of a tornado in a much wider swath of straight line wind damage. The tornado occurred in a one mile path approximately 4 miles southeast of Aledo, between River Ranch Road and Farm to Market Road 1187 in Parker County. The tornado did minimal damage to trees and power lines. A few roads were closed in Sherman; including North Harrison Ave @ East Pecan Street and West McGee St @ Newman Dr. Two and a half feet of water was reported over Trinity Blvd. Reported property and crop damage: about $173,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado, from April 26, 2015 to April 28, 2015. Affected areas: Comanche, Ellis, Erath, Hill, Johnson, Palo Pinto, Somervell. Episode summary: Several discrete supercells developed across the region producing hail up to the size of softballs, severe winds, flash flooding and tornadoes. The storms eventually merged into a squall line that moved across the region south of Interstate 20. A total of 16 tornadoes occurred on this day and most of the tornadoes were produced by one supercell. This supercell stalled in southern Johnson County for up to 3 hours and produced 8 tornadoes near the Rio Vista area also with significant flash flooding. At least one of the tornadoes rotated cyclonically. One tornado in Johnson County was rated an EF1 but the other 15 tornadoes were rated EF0s. Details: Amateur radio operators and storm chasers observed a tornado in the far northwestern corner of Comanche County. This tornado occurred over ranch land and caused little damage. Amateur radio operators and storm chasers observed a second tornado to the northwest of Sidney. This tornado also occurred over ranch land and caused minimal damage, this time much closer to the city of Sidney. Trained spotters observed a tornado to the north of the city of Proctor, on the northeast side of Proctor Lake. Several trees were damaged, but no structures suffered damage. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,590,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Mar 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from March 21, 2015 to March 21, 2015. Affected areas: Aransas, Jim Wells, Nueces, San Patricio. Episode summary: A frontal boundary stalled over the Coastal Bend on March 21st. Abundant moisture moved into the region from Deep South Texas as a strong upper level low pressure system moved into the Texas Big Bend. Widespread showers and thunderstorms formed over the Brush Country during the early morning hours. The showers and thunderstorms moved east into the Coastal Bend later in the morning. This activity then trained over the same area before noon. This led to flooding of creeks and low lying areas across the Coastal Bend during the late morning into the early afternoon hours. Details: Water was flowing across Farm to Market Road 1889 north of Robstown and on West Avenue G in Robstown. Portions of 3rd Street and surrounding roads were flooded in Agua Dulce. Several streets were flooded in Bishop.

title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2015 to March 25, 2015. Affected areas: Goliad, Victoria. Episode summary: Above normal rainfall occurred across all of South Texas except for the extreme western Brush Country during the month of March. The severe drought over portions of Goliad and Victoria Counties diminished by the end of the month after 6 to 9 inches of rainfall occurred during the month. Details: Severe drought ended over the county after much above normal rainfall occurred during the month.

title: High Wind: California, Mar 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from March 23, 2015 to March 23, 2015. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: A trough of low pressure moving through California brought strong winds to the Kern County Mountains and Desert areas on March 23. Although most of the wind gusts were 40 to 50 mph, there were a few gusts as high as 56 mph at Jawbone RAWS and Cache Creek APRS station. At the Bird Spring Pass RAWS station, winds gusted 70 to 79 mph for several hours, while Mojave AWOS gusted to 62 mph. No damage was reported from the winds. Details: The NWS owned APRS station at Mojave reported sustained winds 40-48 mph with gusts to 62 mph. High winds recorded at the Bird Springs Pass RAWS station. High winds at the AWOS at Mojave.

title: Drought: Texas, Feb 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from February 17, 2015 to February 28, 2015. Affected areas: Mills. Episode summary: Drought conditions expanded across North Texas by the middle of February due to a lack of precipitation. Details: By the middle of February, the nearly all of Mills County was under D2/Severe drought conditions. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000.

title: High Wind: California, Mar 31, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from March 31, 2015 to March 31, 2015. Affected areas: Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: A series of dry troughs of low pressure moved across California in the last few days of the March. The trough that moved through on March 31, increased the surface pressure gradients resulting in strong, gusty winds across the mountains and desert areas of Kern County, along with breezy conditions in the San Joaquin Valley. Winds were west-northwesterly 15-30 mph with gusts generally 45-55 mph across the mountains and desert areas. However, there were some gusts of 58-66 mph in a few wind-prone locations. The gusty winds continued into April 1st and 2nd. Details: Jawbone RAWS station reported sustained winds of 40-46 mph with gusts to 61 mph. These winds continued into the morning of April 1st. Bird Spring Pass RAWS reported sustained winds 35-45 mph with gusts of 58-66 mph for several hours. Indian Wells Canyon RAWS station indicated gusts of 58-67 mph for several hours.

title: High Wind: California, Apr 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 01, 2015 to April 02, 2015. Affected areas: Kern Cty Mtns. Episode summary: A series of dry troughs of low pressure moved across California in the last few days of the March with increased the surface pressure gradients resulting in strong, gusty winds across the mountains and desert areas of Kern County, along with breezy conditions in the San Joaquin Valley from March 31 through April 2. Winds were west-northwesterly 15-30 mph with gusts generally 45-55 mph across the mountains and desert areas. However, there were some gusts of 58-66 mph in a few wind-prone locations. Details: Bird Springs Pass RAWS station reported strong wind gusts. Jawbone RAWS reported sustained winds 40-46 mph with gusts to 62 mph. These winds began the night of March 31st and continued into April 1st.

title: Winter Weather: California, Feb 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from February 27, 2015 to February 28, 2015. Affected areas: West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A period of heavy snow caused travel problems in the Sierra. The heaviest snow was mainly over Interstate 80, where heavy convective snow showers occurred. Snow amounts of 4 to 10 inches were measured above 4500 feet. |Thunderstorms locally brought large amounts of small hail, covering roads in Glenn and Nevada counties. Details: Significant traffic delays occurred on Interstate 80 when a period of heavy snow caused several big rigs to slide and block Donner Pass, with long traffic backups resulting. Many cars were ill prepared for winter driving conditions and multiple car accidents were reported. CHP reported that 1000 cars needed to be turned around due to no chains or studded tires. There was 9.5 inches of new snow measured at Kingvale, 24 hour total.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 27, 2015 to April 27, 2015. Affected areas: Angelina, Cherokee, Nacogdoches. Episode summary: Low pressure aloft across the southwest United States resulted in broad southwest flow aloft across the Southern Plains into the Lower Mississippi Valley. Disturbances in this flow rounded the base of the trough and provided the lift necessary for widespread showers and thunderstorms across Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas and Northern Louisiana. A cold front was located across Northern Texas into Northern Louisiana. Moderate surface instability coupled with strong deep layer shear allowed the storms that developed to produce strong and damaging wind gusts, large hail and excessive heavy rainfall across portions of Northeast Texas. Details: Flash flooding was reported in downtown Lufkin, Texas resulting in the closure of several city streets. High water was reported near the intersection of Hwy. 21 and County Road 841 west of Nacogdoches, Texas. Excessive heavy rainfall resulted in the closure of Hwy. 69 between Rusk and Alto, Texas.

title: Heavy Snow: California, Feb 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, from February 27, 2015 to February 28, 2015. Affected areas: Greater Lake Tahoe Area. Episode summary: Low pressure over the Pacific Northwest on the 27th dropped south through California on the 28th, bringing heavy snow to the Lake Tahoe area. Details: Ski areas and an avalanche forecaster (Sierra Avalanche Center) around the Lake Tahoe area reported 14 to 28 inches of snowfall, with the highest amounts near the crest. At lake level snow amounts varied greatly, with a spotter near Meyers indicating 13 inches but many other areas around the lake and near Truckee only reporting between 5 and 9 inches.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Mar 12, 2015

Details: Thunderstorms trained across portions of Hardin County from near Sour Lake to Lumberton during the morning of the 12th. While rainfall rates were not excessive, several hours of moderate to heavy rainfall flooded some secondary roads, a section of FM 421 at a low water crossing, and one home in west side of Lumberton. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Mar 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from March 21, 2015 to March 21, 2015. Affected areas: Jefferson, Orange. As the boundary stalled heavy rain fell across sections of Jefferson and Orange Counties and Calcasieu Parish. Details: Thunderstorms trained across Jefferson County for several hours during the 21st. Jimmy Johnson Blvd, Nall street, and Highway 365 were a few of the streets that were flooded during the event. Numerous reports of cars being stalled due to high water were received as a result of the street flooding. Heavy rain from thunderstorms trained across Orange County for multiple hours. This flooded and closed several roadways around Bridge City. Reported property and crop damage: about $15,000.

Numerous photos were taken of this storm by the public, and fortunately the damage that it caused was not substantial. No injuries were reported. Details: Isolated thunderstorms developed across portions of far southeast California, including eastern Riverside county, during the afternoon hours on April 21st. For the most part the storms were not especially strong, however one thunderstorm located about 6 miles north of Desert Center produced a small, rope-like tornado which traveled nearly 10 miles over mostly open country. The tornado was first re Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 14, 2015 to May 14, 2015. Affected areas: Crosby, Lubbock. Episode summary: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across the Southern South Plains during the late afternoon and evening in conjunction with an upper level disturbance and strong moisture advection. These storms continued to expand in coverage and produce isolated severe wind and hail while moving northeast into Lubbock. At the same time, a discrete supercell thunderstorm was able to ingest unperturbed warm and moist air west of Post in Garza County. This storm also produced large hail and severe wind gusts. Widespread flooding then occurred as storms trained over Lubbock, resulting in multiple road closures and flooded vehicles. Flash flooding also impacted areas between Kalgary and White River Lake in southeast Crosby County through northeast Garza County where the above mentioned supercell remained nearly stationary through much of the evening. Details: Numerous reports of flooded roadways were received throughout the evening as three rounds of intense rainfall moved over the city, most notably over the southwestern side of town. Almost every major intersection between Milwaukee Avenue and Quaker Avenue was flowing with water, with the greatest impact being between 98th and 82nd Streets. Several cars were stranded in high water, as up to 2.5 inch A supercell thunderstorm, which initiated west of Post in Garza County, moved northeast to near Kalgary and White River Lake. This storm became nearly stationary, producing radar estimated rainfall as high as six to eight inches in a 2 hour period. A NWS Storm Survey was conducted the following day, finding water still flowing across several farm to market roads as well as numerous areas of mud. O Reported property and crop damage: about $110,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 04, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 04, 2015 to May 05, 2015. Affected areas: Garza, Hockley, Lubbock, Lynn, Terry. Episode summary: A deep fetch of Gulf moisture overspread the South Plains this afternoon in advance of a slow-moving trough. Numerous thunderstorms erupted by late afternoon across the western South Plains and spread slowly northeast through the overnight hours under weak upper level winds. The slow nature of these storms resulted in torrential rainfall rates and flooding in many areas, but the most impressive rainfall and flooding bulls-eyed in central and southern Lynn County where between 6 and 12 inches of rain was measured before midnight. Nearly all roads in Lynn County were closed by DPS officials due to standing water in excess of one foot over long stretches. The city of Tahoka became marooned by floodwaters forcing emergency officials to give stranded motorists refuge in area shelters. When these shelters either reached capacity or were threatened by floodwaters, officials transported persons to adjacent counties for safety. To add insult to injury, additional rounds of thunderstorms with heavy rain developed early in the morning on the 5th and prolonged flooding issues over much of the southern South Plains and southern Rolling Plains. Schools in Tahoka were closed on the 5th due to many roads remaining impassable. Dozens of vehicles from Lubbock to Tahoka required rescuing after motorists drove into deep floodwaters and became stranded. Most of these flooded cars were deemed complete losses after the engines became hydrolocked. One small child suffered a head injury after the car they were in hydroplaned abruptly near Southland (Garza County). Combined damage to vehicles, homes and thousands of acres of wheat crops (particularly in Lynn County) could exceed $300M. Reported property and crop damage: about $310,830,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 05, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 05, 2015 to May 05, 2015. Affected areas: Crosby. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms developed late this afternoon in the southwest South Plains and proceeded to move east and northeast into the Rolling Plains by late evening. As these storms approached the Lubbock area, they encountered greater instability and rapidly strengthened into severe storms producing some large hail from Wolfforth to the west side of Lubbock. These storms gradually weakened east of Lubbock at which time a nearly stationary supercell storms erupted in southwest Crosby County. This supercell would go on to produce baseball size hail in addition to two tornadoes southwest of Ralls; both of which remained over open land causing no damage. Details: A storm chaser documented a narrow tornado for three minutes over open land. No damage occurred. A storm chaser videoed the previous tornado rope out and eventually merge with a new tornadic circulation. This second tornado was more organized than the first and eventually crossed Highway 207 as videoed by a truck driver. No damage was observed despite crossing directly over power lines along the highway.

title: Flood: Texas, May 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from May 07, 2015 to May 07, 2015. Affected areas: Hale. Episode summary: A short wave trough moved over the West Texas region during the morning and early afternoon hours of the seventh. This trough was able to act upon strong moisture and elevated instability to create training storms and flooding across the central South Plains. The greatest impact from this activity was in Hale County along Interstate 27. Showers and thunderstorms were able to backbuild over Hale County following the passing of an outflow boundary from earlier convection.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 16, 2015 to May 16, 2015. Affected areas: Briscoe. Episode summary: A very unstable and strongly sheared air mass developed late this morning ahead of a dryline and potent upper trough. Strong and very dry southwest winds of 30 to 40 mph exited New Mexico and focused scattered thunderstorm development along the dryline before noon CST. The most significant of these storms quickly became a supercell and tracked from near Olton northeast to rural areas of northern Briscoe County accompanied by very large hail and one tornado. Additional supercells developed throughout the Rolling Plains and far southeast Texas Panhandle; one of which would later evolve into a prolific tornadic storm in southwest Oklahoma. West of the dryline, widespread blowing dust with poor visibilities occasionally as low as one quarter mile in some rural areas hampered many weekend graduation ceremonies and outdoor events. Visibility at the Lubbock Airport officially fell to three quarters of a mile during the height of the blowing dust with a peak wind measured at 50 mph. Details: An off-duty fire department volunteer observed a tornado about ten miles north-northeast of Silverton. Video from a motorist showed this tornado lasted for about one minute.

title: Flash Flood: California, Apr 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from April 07, 2015 to April 07, 2015. Affected areas: Monterey. Episode summary: A strong cold front moved through Northern and Central California during the early morning hours of Tuesday, April 7. The front generated local strong and gusty winds, brief heavy rain, and localized flooding. Details: Roadway flooding and debris caused multiple lane closures on highway 101 near the Red Barn.

title: Winter Weather: Texas, Mar 04, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Weather, from March 04, 2015 to March 05, 2015. Affected areas: Bexar, Burnet, Gillespie, Kerr, Llano, Travis, Val Verde, Williamson. Episode summary: A cold front brought below freezing temperatures and light precipitation to parts of South Central Texas. There was a mix of freezing rain, sleet, and rain over our northern counties from Kerr to Williamson. There were reports of some icy spots on roads, bridges, overpasses, and elevated surfaces. There were also reports of ice in Bexar and Val Verde Counties. No roads were closed and no accidents were reported. title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2015 to March 31, 2015. Affected areas: Bandera, Edwards, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Llano, Medina, Real. Episode summary: The north central part of South Central Texas missed out on the above normal precipitation much of the region had in March. Of the counties still in Severe Drought category (Stage D2) or worse at the end of the month, only Edwards and Medina Counties received above normal rainfall. This was only enough to move those two counties into Stage D2 from Extreme category (Stage D3). All of the other counties remained unchanged. Bandera, Gillespie, and Kerr Counties were in Stage D3 and Kendall, Llano, and Real remained in Stage D2. Fire danger was low to moderate across the area at the end of the month and of the counties in D2 or worse drought none had burn bans in effect. The Texas Crop and Weather Report issued by Texas A&M indicated supplemental feeding of livestock continued. The seven day stream flow average at the end of the month was below normal (10-24 percent) for the Guadalupe and Frio River Basins. The Medina and Nueces River Basins were much below normal (less than 10 percent). Area lakes and reservoirs continued well below normal pool elevations. Lake Amistad was up slightly to 28.8 feet below normal. Lake Travis was also up slightly at 52.8 feet below normal. Medina Lake was essentially unchanged at 89.6 feet below normal. The Edwards Aquifer rose during the month and was at 646.2 feet. This was 6.3 feet higher than at the end of March 2014 but still 21.0 feet below average. Fredericksburg remained in stage 3 water restrictions and Kerrville remained in stage 2. Details: The north central part of South Central Texas missed out on the above

title: Drought: Texas, Mar 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from March 01, 2015 to March 24, 2015. Affected areas: De Witt, Val Verde. title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 08, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 08, 2015 to May 08, 2015. Affected areas: Harrison, Red River. Episode summary: A large complex of showers and thunderstorms moved into Northeast Texas during the early morning hours of May 8th, with this complex slowing as it moved into Harrison County. Additional showers and thunderstorms containing heavy rainfall redeveloped over the same areas of western and central Harrison County, with rainfall amounts of three to in excess of six inches falling in a couple of hours, resulting in significant flash flooding near Hallsville and Marshall. ||Other scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the mid evening hours on May 8th over northern Red River County Texas, along a weak surface front and ahead of an upper level disturbance approaching from the west. These showers and thunderstorms intensified and slowly drifted northward into southern McCurtain County Oklahoma, producing damaging winds, small hail, and flash flooding in southern McCurtain County and flash flooding over Northwest Red River County. These storms weakened during the late evening due to the loss of heating and instability. Details: Harrison County Sherriff's Office reported a car was swept off the road between Marshall and Harleton. Farm to Market Road 195 closed 3 miles west of the town of Manchester due to flooding. School buses behind due to many flooded roads in the city of Marshall. Reported property and crop damage: about $106,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Mar 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from March 21, 2015 to March 21, 2015. Affected areas: Gonzales, Karnes, Wilson. Episode summary: An upper level low off the west coast and a cold front combined at to act on a moist boundary layer to produce thunderstorms some of which generated heavy rain. The heavy rain led to flash flooding in a few places. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing FM1116 and FM532 around Gonzales. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding. One foot of water over the roadway closed FM887 between Falls City and Pawelekville and FM81 was closed due to flooding between Helena and Runge. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding. Low water crossings were flooded closing County Roads 421 and 334.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 10, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 10, 2015 to May 11, 2015. Affected areas: Bowie, Cass, Cherokee, Gregg, Harrison, Marion, Rusk, Smith. Episode summary: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours over Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and portions of Southeast Oklahoma on May 10th, near a residual weak surface boundary draped along the Red River from showers and thunderstorms that had developed earlier in the day over Central and Southern Oklahoma. This boundary and an upper level disturbance moving in from the west during peak heating resulting in the development of multiple severe thunderstorms that produced damaging winds and isolated tornadoes. This severe weather outbreak persisted into the early morning hours of May 11th where some flash flooding also occurred across portions of the region from excessive heavy rainfall. Details: A bridge was washed out due to flooding on Sam Hall Road north northeast of Hallsville, Texas. Meadows Lane was closed due to flooding. Highway 80 west of Marshall, Texas was impassable due to flooding. Reported property and crop damage: about $485,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 16, 2015 to May 16, 2015. Affected areas: Collingsworth, Donley, Wheeler. Episode summary: Plentiful moisture ahead of an approaching weather system brought widespread rainfall to the area Friday night. By Saturday morning the rain and thunderstorms had mostly pushed east into Oklahoma, but the environment over the Texas Panhandle remained very moist. As temperatures warmed and instability increased, thunderstorms intensified and became more numerous. Some of the thunderstorms became severe producing large hail and damaging winds. A supercell thunderstorm moved into Donley County around 12:30 PM CST and spawned three tornadoes as it tracked northeast across Donley, Collingsworth and Wheeler counties. Damage was mostly limited to barns, trees and power poles across rural sections of these counties. However, one home sustained significant roof damage north of Hedley. Isolated EF-1 damage occurred in two tornadoes otherwise damage was consistent with an EF-0 tornado for most of its path. Details: This was the second tornado to cycle from the same parent supercell thunderstorm. Most of its track occurred in Collingsworth County. title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 13, 2015 to May 13, 2015. Affected areas: Nacogdoches. Episode summary: A band of showers and thunderstorms developed during the early and mid afternoon over Southeast Texas on May 13th, and spread into portions of Deep East Texas during the early evening hours. Locally heavy rain was common with these storms, as they moved slowly over already saturated grounds from heavy rainfall that had fallen only a couple of days prior. This resulted in areas of flash flooding across portions of Nacogdoches County that lingered through mid-evening. Details: Flooding was reported At County Road 3 and Highway 21 just west of the Douglass community.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 14, 2015 to May 14, 2015. Affected areas: Nacogdoches. Episode summary: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and early evening hours across Southeast Oklahoma and portions of Northeast Texas as a result of a very warm and unstable air mass in place. Large hail and damaging winds were reported throughout Smith County, Texas from these storms. In addition, slow moving thunderstorms containing very heavy rainfall moved over Nacogdoches County, Texas, which had seen excessively heavy rainfall for a few days prior, resulting in areas of flash flooding throughout the city of Nacogdoches. Details: A car stalled in high water in the 200 Block of South Ferdonia Street in Nacogdoches. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, May 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from May 17, 2015 to May 17, 2015. Affected areas: Shawano. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front. The storms produced damaging straight-line winds near White Lake (Langlade Co.), and a weak, EF0, tornado near Gresham (Shawano Co.). Details: A weak tornado, rated EF0, formed at 3:31 PM CDT and produced intermittent damage along a nearly five mile long path, dissipating at 3:40 PM CDT. At least a dozen trees along the path sustained damage (DI 28, DOD 1-3) and a barn lost several shingles (DI 1, DOD 1).

title: Wildfire: Wisconsin, Apr 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Wildfire, from April 13, 2015 to April 13, 2015. Affected areas: Juneau. Episode summary: An April 13th wildfire near Necedah (Juneau County) burned over 300 acres before being extinguished by the Wisconsin DNR and four local fire departments. The fire was likely started by a passing train and then spread quickly by winds that gusted close to 30 mph. Flames from the fire approached a factory, which was evacuated as a precaution. The smoke spread over a residential neighborhood prompting officials to evacuate about 44 homes. No structures were burned, but one fire fighter was treated for smoke inhalation. Details: A wildfire started by a passing train, burned 336 acres near Necedah. At one point, the flames approached a factory which was evacuated as a precaution. The smoke from the fire spread over a residential neighborhood, prompting officials to evacuate homes in the area. One fire fighter was treated for smoke inhalation. State Highway 80 south of Necedah was closed due to the fire. Reported property and crop damage: about $57,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 16, 2015 to April 16, 2015. Affected areas: Hardin, Jefferson. Episode summary: A slow moving line of thunderstorms moved in deep Southeast Texas during the evening of the 16th. Flooding occurred in portions of Jefferson and Hardin Counties after an estimated 6 to 9 inches of rain fell. Details: Six to nine inches of rain fell flooding State Highway 105 between Bevil Oaks and Sour Lake. The flooded roadway was reported by a NWS employee. Multiple roadways in Jefferson County, but mainly near Nome and Central Gardens were closed after several inches of rain fell during the evening of the 16th. Some of the roadways included in the closure were FM 365, 1406, and 366 along with Highway 347.

title: Sleet, Winter Weather: Texas, Mar 04, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Sleet, Winter Weather, from March 04, 2015 to March 05, 2015. Affected areas: Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Fisher, Haskell, Jones, Mcculloch, San Saba, Shackelford, Sutton, Taylor and 1 more areas. Episode summary: A potent upper level storm system brought a glaze of freezing rain, sleet and snow to a large part of West Central Texas. Roads became slippery and many school districts closed schools on March 5th across West Central Texas. Details: A National Weather Service Cooperative Observer measured 0.4 inches of sleet in Brownwood. Trained spotters measured about half an inch of sleet in Blanket and Bangs. Another cooperative observer located 14 miles south of Brownwood measured 0.20 inches of sleet. Trained spotters measured 0.6 inches of sleet in Coleman and 0.4 inches in Talpa. A trained spotter measured a half an inch of sleet in Lohn. Another trained spotter measured a half an inch of mostly sleet with some freezing rain in Brady.

title: High Wind: California, Apr 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 24, 2015 to April 24, 2015. Affected areas: Eastern Mojave Desert. Episode summary: A potent spring storm system brought strong winds and thunderstorms to much of the Mojave Desert. Details: A wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at Bicycle Lake ASOS.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2015 to May 25, 2015. Affected areas: Cottle. Episode summary: An exceptionally wet and cool May allowed further easing of the long-term drought across the far northern Rolling Plains, specifically eastern Cottle County where a sliver of D2 drought conditions ended after additional soaking rains in late May. Area reservoirs also saw improvement particularly at Lake Alan Henry where capacity soared to 100 percent. White River Lake and Mackenzie Lake were both lagging due to their smaller drainage basins, but had still recorded significant rises for the month.

title: Strong Wind: California, Apr 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Strong Wind, from April 13, 2015 to April 14, 2015. Affected areas: Northern Sacramento Valley. Episode summary: Wind gusts estimated around 45 mph brought down trees and branches which caused numerous power outages in Shasta County and northern Tehama County. Details: Locally strong winds caused numerous trees to fall on buildings, vehicles, and power lines in southern Redding. About 20 calls for separate wind damage events were received by emergency responders. At least 4 homes and a garage were struck by falling trees, some seriously damaged. Several cars were also damaged by falling trees and limbs. Power lines were downed in multiple locations, causing powe Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000,000.

title: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather: California, Mar 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Snow, Winter Weather, from March 01, 2015 to March 02, 2015. Affected areas: Riverside County Mountains, San Bernardino County Mountains, San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: An upper-level trough deepened along the West Coast before moving inland over Southern California and brought rain and snow showers, as well as a few thunderstorms with hail, through the morning of the March 3rd. Huntington Beach reported around one inch of hail accumulation during the morning of the 2nd. Details: A trace to 5 inches of snow was reported from 0000 PST on the 1st through 0700 PST on the 2nd across the area. The heaviest total of 5 inches was reported by a spotter 2 mi ESE of Big Bear City. Additional snowfall amounts of 4 inches in Forest Falls, 3 inches in Angelus Oaks, and 2 inches in Green Valley Lake were also reported. Multiple traffic collisions were reported in the mountain top distri Trained spotters in Idyllwild and Pine Cove both reported a 24 hour snowfall accumulation of 9.5 inches as of 0800 PST on the 2nd. A third spotter in Pine Cove reported 8 inches of snowfall in 12 hours, as of 2100 PST on the 1st. At 2100PST on the 1st a trained spotter reported a 12 hour snowfall total of 7 inches at Palomar Mountain.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 18, 2015 to May 18, 2015. Affected areas: Angelina, Cherokee, Nacogdoches, Sabine, Shelby. Episode summary: Excessive heavy rainfall was widespread across the southern half of Northeast Texas during the morning hours of May 18th. This convection developed from an upper level disturbance that moved into the region from Central Texas. Moisture was plentiful across the region as the upper level flow was from the southwest. This allowed the disturbance to tap moisture from not only the Eastern Pacific but also the Gulf of Mexico. These storms trained across the same general area resulting in some impressive rainfall totals. The end result was widespread flooding across much of the region. Details: Flash flooding was reported along FM. 706 north of the Hudson community. Flooding was reported along Rivercrest Road north northeast of Lufkin, Texas. Flash flooding was reported along FM. 2021 just off of Hwy. 69 north of the Hudson community.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 21, 2015 to May 21, 2015. Affected areas: Angelina. Episode summary: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed during the predawn hours of May 21st across the southern half of Northeast Texas. These thunderstorms produced copious amounts of rainfall which resulted in some localized flooding in and around the city of Lufkin, Texas. Details: Highway 69 south of Lufkin was flooded and closed. Highway 69 between Lufkin and Burke was closed from excessive heavy rainfall.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 23, 2015 to May 23, 2015. Affected areas: Carson, Deaf Smith, Gray, Potter, Randall, Wheeler. Episode summary: Another in a series of overnight thunderstorm complexes brought widespread heavy rain and isolated severe thunderstorm wind gusts to the Texas Panhandle. Heavy rainfall of one to two inches were common with locally higher amounts. This occurred over saturated ground resulting in excessive runoff and ponding. Details: Reports of minor flooding were received as early as 6:00 AM CDT, but as heavy rain continued across the city the flooding developed into flash flooding shortly before 7:00 AM CDT. Throughout the mid and late morning, numerous intersections become flooded and impassible. Police and fire performed water rescues from stranded vehicles. Flooding was reported outside of Amarillo as well, including abou Heavy rain on the morning of the 23rd brought flooding to much of Deaf Smith County. Flash flooding was reported on Farm to Market 1062 which was closed for a period during the morning, and on Farm to Market 1058 which was also closed. Heavy rain caused flooding in a few locations in Wheeler County. Flash flooding was reported on Highway 152 between County Road 16 and 17, where 6 to 12 inches of water covered the road. Flooding was also reported one mile west of Shamrock, where the Interstate 40 service road was impassable.

title: High Wind: California, Mar 04, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from March 04, 2015 to March 05, 2015. Affected areas: San Diego County Mountains. Episode summary: A surface high in the wake of a departing trough resulted in strong easterly winds over San Diego County. Details: High winds occurred at the Sill Hill mesonet between 2000 PST on the 5th and 0500 PST on the 6th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the east at 35-45 mph with most gusts in the high 50s to mid 60s mph. However, a peak gust of 71 mph was recorded between 2130 and 2140 PST on the 5th. title: High Wind: Texas, May 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from May 23, 2015 to May 23, 2015. Affected areas: Hale. Episode summary: A short wave trough moving overhead coupled with ample moisture produced scattered thunderstorms on the evening of the 23rd. The storms that did become severe produced severe wind gusts in Lynn and King Counties. In an area of trailing stratiform precipitation, a severe wind gust was observed at the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Abernathy (Hale County).

title: Drought: California, Mar 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from March 01, 2015 to March 31, 2015. Affected areas: Central Sacramento Valley, Clear Lake/Southern Lake County, Motherlode/Camptonville To Groveland, Mountains Southwest Shasta County To Northern Lake County, Northern Sacramento Valley, Northern San Joaquin Valley, Southern Sacramento Valley, West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. title: Heavy Rain: California, Mar 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Heavy Rain, from March 01, 2015 to March 02, 2015. Affected areas: Kern. Episode summary: A low pressure system dropping south along the California coast brought showers and thunderstorms to central California March 1st and 2nd. Although many areas received some rain, the greatest impacts from the storm were across Kern county. Parts of Kern county received 0.25 inches to 0.75 inches of rain, especially the area in the lower Kern River Canyon east of Bakersfield. This resulted in minor rock and mud slides onto Highway 178, closing the road for several hours. On the west side of Kern county, rain was a contributing factor the the development of a sink hole in the city of Taft.||Snow also fell across the mountains of Kern County during the early hours of March 2nd. Snowfall amounts ranged from 1 inch to 5.5 inches at elevations above 5000 feet. Since snow levels remained above the level of the major highways, no significant impacts were reported. Details: Rainfall of 0.49 inches fell at the APRS station in Taft. The rain contributed to the development of a sinkhole that was 200 feet long, 1 to 2 feet wide, and 1 to 4 feet deep. Five homes were evacuated as a precaution, but no damage was reported to any buildings or utilities. Rainfall on 0.74 inches at Democrat RAWS with the heaviest rain between 0225 and 0625 PST. This resulted in several small rock slides being reported at 0647 PST. The rock slides resulted in Highway 178 being closed for several hours to allow crews to clear the road. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Drought: California, Apr 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from April 01, 2015 to April 30, 2015. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continued in full force during the month of April, 2015. Temperatures continued to average above normal. While there was some precipitation in April, it was not uniformly distributed. Fresno received 1.25 inches of rain (131% of normal) while Bakersfield received only 0.08 inches (15% of normal). Overall, seasonal rainfall amounts continued to be only 50-75 percent of normal across central California. ||The U.S. Drought Monitor continued to report exceptional drought conditions across the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The 2013-2014 water year (July 1 - June 30) concluded with Fresno setting its second driest on record (4.81 inches) and Bakersfield setting its third driest (2.41 inches). For the calendar year, 2014 was the warmest year on record for Fresno and Bakersfield. The trend of below normal precipitation and above normal temperatures has continued through the first few months of 2015. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, a decrease in the snow-related tourism activity in the Southern Sierra Nevada, reduction in air quality due to persistent stagnant air, loss or reduction of ground water, wells drying up in several communities leaving them with no water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 12, 2015 to April 12, 2015. Affected areas: Ector, Midland. title: Flood: Texas, May 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from May 27, 2015 to May 28, 2015. Affected areas: Hale, Hall. Episode summary: In advance of a diffuse dryline located from near Tulia south to Brownfield, moderate instability developed this afternoon underneath weak capping and modest mid-level winds. Thunderstorms had little problem initiating during the heat of the day and several of these became supercells thanks to sufficient directional shear. Initially, the first supercell developed northwest of Silverton and went on to produce very large hail, flooding and at least one funnel. By late afternoon, another prolific supercell erupted farther southwest near Cotton Center and for the next 1.5 hours remained over southern Hale County producing giant hail to softball size, torrential rains estimated up to seven inches, and even multiple funnel clouds. From sunset through late evening, additional supercell storms developed from near Reese Center north to Olton and Memphis; many of which were proficient with large hail and flooding rainfall. Significant areal flooding enveloped a swath of southern Hale County where many roads were inundated by water; some of which remained closed through the late morning hours of the 28th. Similar flooding was reported in Memphis during the overnight hours including water of a few inches deep rushing into some buildings. Reported property and crop damage: about $350,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Winter Storm, Winter Weather, from March 04, 2015 to March 04, 2015. Affected areas: Baylor, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: A strong cold front surged through north Texas during the day of the 4th, bringing an Arctic airmass into much of the Southern Plains. As this occurred, a large scale upper level trough shifted eastward across the Southern and Central Plains region, resulting in widespread wintry precipitation. Several inches of snow and sleet fell, with significant impacts to travel. Details: Light rain transition over to a mixture of light freezing rain and sleet in the wee morning hours of the 4th. By sunrise, precipitation had transitioned over to snow. By the time precipitation had ended, Grayback received an inch of snow. Light rain transition over to a mixture of light freezing rain and sleet in the wee morning hours of the 4th. By sunrise, precipitation had transitioned over to snow. By the time precipitation had ended, areas from Seymour to Lake Kemp reported around an inch of snow. Light rain and freezing rain transitioned over to sleet and freezing rain early on the 4th. Precipitation then transitioned to snow during the morning hours. Snow was heavy at times, and by the time snow had ended during the evening, up to four inches had fallen in Chillicothe, with 3.8 inches in Quanah.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Mar 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from March 17, 2015 to March 18, 2015. Affected areas: Jim Hogg, Zapata. Episode summary: The combination of a negatively tilted shortwave trough, strong large scale ascent, a 850 mb to surface trough over the area, and abundant moisture led to the development of widespread showers and thunderstorms across the ranchlands and brush country of Deep South Texas on St. Patrick's Day 2015. Showers and thunderstorms trained over the area for several hours, dropping several inches of rain and causing flash flooding in Zapata. Details: Zapata County EM reported 2.75 inches of rainfall. Escobas Co-Op observer reported 3 inches of rainfall. Hebbronville Co-Op observer reported 3.8 inches of rainfall.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 28, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 28, 2015 to May 28, 2015. Affected areas: Hockley, Lubbock. Episode summary: Following a round of severe storms and heavy rain the night prior, strong and severe thunderstorms developed late this morning over the southwest South Plains before expanding in coverage as they spread east throughout the afternoon. Much of this activity was driven by strong moisture advection in advance of an upper impulse. A particularly intense storm in southern Lynn County redeveloped to the southeast over time and produced a vivid tornado just south of O'Donnell in nearby Dawson County (NWS Midland's forecast area). Although hail and high winds were rather common place, by far the worst byproduct of these slow-moving storms was widespread flooding throughout Lubbock county. Flash flooding was reported in Shallowater and Lubbock where dozens of cars became stranded in high water from rainfall rates measured as high as eight inches per hour. In Shallowater, just over four inches of rain fell in 30 minutes and proceeded to flood about 75 homes with up to six inches of water. Total damage to floors, walls and personal property could reach $10 million. A total of 6.93 inches of rain was measured by a NWS employee in Shallowater by early evening. One car in Shallowater was swept off the road by flowing water and carried about 100 yards in a bar ditch that transformed into a raging creek. Fortunately, the occupant was not injured. In Lubbock, five high water rescues were reported after motorists became stranded in high water. The flooding also inundated four floors at the UMC Hospital which proceeded to damage some medical records. Reported property and crop damage: about $12,000,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 05, 2015 to May 05, 2015. Affected areas: Borden, Dawson, Gaines, Howard. Episode summary: An upper level low was over Arizona and New Mexico, and an upper level disturbance associated with this low moved over West Texas. There were outflow boundaries left over from convection across the area during the morning hours that aided in thunderstorm and tornado development during the afternoon and evening hours. A couple members of the Howard County Volunteer Fire Department witnessed the tornado. The only damage seen was to a couple of power Heavy rain fell across Borden County and produced flash flooding south of Gail.
