title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 12, 2015 to April 12, 2015. Affected areas: Live Oak. Episode summary: A strong upper level low pressure system over northern Mexico moved toward the Texas Big Bend during the evening of April 12th. This disturbance interacted with deep moisture along the Rio Grande to produce a line of thunderstorms over northern Mexico. A mesoscale convective complex moved east-southeast toward South Texas and Deep South Texas. Wind damage occurred in the cities of Laredo, Kingsville, and Premont. Localized flooding occurred in the city of George West. Details: Barriers were put in place across northeast portions of the city of George West. Water was over the road along Colorado Street, including the intersections of Bowie and Austin Streets.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 14, 2015 to April 14, 2015. Affected areas: Aransas, Nueces, San Patricio. Episode summary: A frontal boundary moved out of the Hill Country as the upper level disturbance moved into northwest Texas and western Oklahoma early on the 14th. As the frontal boundary moved into an unstable air mass over South Texas, thunderstorms developed over the Rio Grande plains west of Cotulla. The area of thunderstorms organized into another mesoscale convective system that moved east across South Texas during the early morning hours. The squall line produced widespread tree damage in the Coastal Bend. This caused power outages from Kingsville to Corpus Christi with 35 thousand customers losing power at the height of the storm. Flash flooding also occurred from Corpus Christi to Rockport. Details: Several intersections were flooded in the Calallen to near Robstown area. County Road 52 was flooded all the way to the intersection with County Road 73. Many roads were flooded across the northern portions of Corpus Christi, stretching from near Tuloso along Interstate 37 into the downtown area. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 24, 2015 to May 25, 2015. Affected areas: Harrison. Episode summary: A persistent southwest flow aloft dominated the Southern Plains and Lower Mississippi Valley. Shortwave troughs embedded in this flow influenced the Four State Region during the late morning, afternoon and evening hours of May 24th. Daytime heating resulted in the instability needed to produce showers and thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced strong and damaging wind gusts and tornadoes. Details: National Weather Service Storm Survey Team determined that damage on the east side of Marshall Texas was consistent with that of a tornado. An EF1 tornado touched down on the south southeast side of Marshall and traveled almost due north. Numerous trees and powerlines were downed along the tornadoes patch and several homes had damage to them, mainly from fallen trees. National Weather Service Storm Survey Team determined that damage across Harrison County was consistent with that of a tornado. An EF1 tornado touched down south of Marshall, Texas and snapped and uprooted numerous trees. A home sustained roof damage when the wind lifted the carport portion of the roof structure. The owner also lost a 30 by 30 foot outbuilding. A warehouse also had some roof d Reported property and crop damage: about $375,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 25, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 25, 2015 to May 25, 2015. Affected areas: Bowie, Gregg, Harrison, Panola, Rusk. Episode summary: Severe thunderstorms developed across far west Texas during the early morning hours of May 25th and this cluster of severe thunderstorms evolved into a derecho, moving eastward across the entire state of Texas and eventually into Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas and Northwest Louisiana. Widespread wind damage was reported across the region during the afternoon and evening hours with flash flooding reported across portions of the region as well with a few tornadoes embedded in the line of thunderstorms. Details: Excessive heavy rainfall closed Richland Road near Pleasant Grove. National Weather Service Storm Survey Team determined that damage in Rusk County was consistent with that of a tornado. An EF2 tornado touched down approximately 9 miles west southwest of Henderson, Texas in Rusk County and traveled in a east northeast direction before lifting approximately 10 miles east northeast of Henderson, Texas. Numerous trees were snapped and or uprooted along its path. Several roads were flooded and closed in and around Kilgore, Texas. Reported property and crop damage: about $850,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 26, 2015 to May 27, 2015. Affected areas: Wood. Episode summary: Nocturnal thunderstorms that developed during the late evening hours of May 26th in association with an upper level trough across Northeast Texas were slow moving in nature. As a result, some flash flooding was reported in Wood County, Texas. Details: A car was flooded in high water southeast of Quitman, Texas along FM 3450. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 30, 2015 to May 30, 2015. Affected areas: Smith, Wood. Episode summary: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved eastward out of North Central Texas and into Northeast Texas during the morning hours of May 30th. This line of storms bowed out as they moved east and produced some wind damage across Northeast Texas and Northwest Louisiana. Some flash flooding was also produced with these storms as rainfall rates were excessive. Details: Widespread street flooding was reported in the Troup, Texas community. County Road 2088 was flooded and closed in Quitman, Texas.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado, from May 07, 2015 to May 09, 2015. Affected areas: Cooke, Denton, Grayson, Jack, Montague, Stephens, Wise. Episode summary: A cold front moved south out of the Texas panhandle on May 6th, and was draped across north Texas on the 7th and 8th. The front stalled across the northwestern sections of north Texas and combined to produce severe thunderstorms including large hail, tornadoes, and flash flooding. Flash flooding across Cooke County caused significant impacts, including a late night train derailment. Details: A 36 year old man died when his vehicle was swept away by flood waters three-quarters of a mile south of Spring Creek Road, north of Valley View, TX. A little while later, Interstate 35 north of Valley View had to be closed due to high water. Several vehicles had stalled in the high water on the interstate. Amateur radio reported that high water rescues were taking place in southwest portions of Denison, TX. Stephens County Sheriff's Department reported that FM 207 was closed due to high water approximately 4 miles southeast of Breckenridge, TX. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,330,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 09, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 09, 2015 to May 10, 2015. Affected areas: Cooke, Denton, Eastland, Erath, Grayson, Hamilton, Hill, Kaufman, Van Zandt. Episode summary: An active Spring weather pattern led to numerous severe thunderstorms, many of which produced tornadoes, across north Texas during Mother's Day Weekend. The prolonged period of strong to severe storms was made possible by a slow-moving upper level low pressure system which moved east from the Rockies through the Southern Plains. Activity began on Friday and continued through Mother's Day evening. Details: A NWS storm survey team found EF-3 damage in the city of Van. This tornado began near highway 64, near Edom before moving in a northerly direction. The storm crossed Interstate 20 on the southeast side of Van, before carving a destructive path over the eastern side of the city. The greatest damage was done in a housing development to the north of the public school administration building, where ov A National Weather Service storm survey crew found evidence of EF-3 damage to the south of the city of Cisco. The tornado began as a small funnel, just west of State Highway 206, before making a slow trek eastward. As the tornado grew, the damage occurred to several buildings along U.S. 183. One house was completely destroyed, along with a mobile home just to the south of the main house. Two cars, The Cooke County emergency manager observed a brief tornado near Lindsay. Reported property and crop damage: about $44,250,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 19, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado, from May 19, 2015 to May 20, 2015. Affected areas: Cooke, Denton, Ellis, Grayson, Jack, Montague, Palo Pinto, Wise, Young. Episode summary: Another cold front stalled across north Texas, leading to favorable conditions for thunderstorms and severe weather. The front, which stalled just south of the Red River, began to move slowly southeast during the night of the 19th and led to numerous severe weather reports across Wise, Jack, and Palo Pinto Counties. Details: A National Weather Service damage survey crew found tornado damage along a two and a half mile path across western Wise County. The tornado began on the west side of Farm to Market Road 920, west of the Balsora community. As the tornado moved eastward, several homes, mobile homes, and farm buildings were damaged or destroyed. The most significant damage was done to a mobile home, where the roof wa A National Weather Service damage survey team found tornado damage east of the city of Decatur. The tornado took a non-standard path, with the tornado taking a due south path for approximately three-quarters of a mile, before turning due east, and then slightly southeast. The tornado damaged several storage buildings, and damaged several roofs. A National Weather Service damage survey crew found evidence of a brief tornado in the city of Jacksboro. The tornado moved in a southeast to northwest direction, beginning near the intersection of 4th street and Pine. The tornado moved northwest for approximately three blocks, damaging several trees, and producing roof damage to four homes. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,830,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado: Texas, May 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado, from May 23, 2015 to May 28, 2015. Affected areas: Cooke, Coryell, Dallas, Denton, Ellis, Falls, Fannin, Freestone, Grayson, Hill, Johnson, Kaufman and 8 more areas. Episode summary: For several days, a stalled cold front, combined with abundant moisture from the Gulf of Mexico combined to produce widespread rain and thunderstorms in Texas. Several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms occurred during a four day period, producing flash flooding, and numerous reports of large hail. Tornadoes affected areas in central Texas, from near Lampasas to a deadly tornado in Milam County. Details: Emergency management reported that many roads were closed across the county due to high water. Broadcast media reported that Abrams Road and a nearby shopping center in Arlington, TX were flooded. Emergency management reported that multiple high water rescues were ongoing. Reported property and crop damage: about $37,775,500.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2015 to April 30, 2015. Affected areas: Archer, Baylor, Clay, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: With persistently warm and dry conditions, drought persisted through the month. Details: With persistent dry weather, a D4 (exceptional) through D3 (extreme) drought continued across the county. Some rainfall across the northwest portion of the county resulted in minor improvements of the drought from D4 (exceptional) to D3 (extreme). However, persisting dry conditions across the remainder of the county maintained a D4 drought. With persisting dry conditions, the northern half of the country remains under a D4 (exceptional) drought, while the southern half of the county remains under a D3 (extreme) drought.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2015 to May 31, 2015. Affected areas: Archer, Baylor, Clay, Foard, Hardeman, Knox, Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: With record rainfall throughout the month of May, drought was completely eradicated throughout western north Texas. Details: With record rainfall throughout the month of May, drought was completely eradicated throughout the county.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 16, 2015 to April 16, 2015. Affected areas: Refugio. Episode summary: A deep upper low was located over the Four Corners region on April 16th while a strong jet streak in the subtropical jet stream across northern Mexico moved into South Texas. Scattered thunderstorms formed near a weak boundary moving north through the Coastal Bend. A storm that formed over Bee County intensified into a heavy precipitation supercell. This storm produced three weak tornadoes as it moved across Refugio County. Details: A weak tornado briefly caused damage near Quintana. The tornado damaged six utility poles and broke several large tree limbs. NWS survey team estimated wind speeds were near 80 mph. A weak tornado produced damage southwest of Tivoli. The tornado damaged several utility poles. A NWS storm survey team estimated wind speeds were around 80 mph. A brief rope tornado lasted around 30 seconds. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 01, 2015 to April 01, 2015. Affected areas: Mcculloch. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance and strong surface heating resulted in the development of a few supercell thunderstorms across the Northwest Hill Country that extended north towards Brownwood and Brady. These storms produced mostly hail and a single flash flood. Details: Law enforcement reported flooding at the intersection of U.S. Highway 377 and County Road 464. Also, new fences were washed out as rainfall amounts averaged from 4.5 to 6 inches.

title: Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, Tornado, from April 26, 2015 to April 26, 2015. Affected areas: Brown, Coleman, Jones. Episode summary: As two potent upper level jet streams converged over West Central Texas on April 26, they interacted with a dryline to result in the rapid development of supercells. These supercells produced large hail, damaging winds and isolated tornadoes across the area. Later that evening, the supercells congealed into a line of storms or a quasi-linear convective system that may have generated the tornado near Lake Brownwood and the intense winds in Mason. On the 27th, isolated severe storms formed and resulted in a few reports of large hail across Brown and San Saba Counties. Details: Residents reported this tornado was on the ground for about 10 minutes 2 miles west northwest of May. The twister was also videotaped and posted on Facebook. The broadcast media reported roads flooded in Stamford. A tornado touched down near the intersection of Park Road 15 and County Road 455. The tornado continued east to Lake Brownwood. The most significant damage was to a well anchored carport in cement that was extracted by the tornado. Widespread damage was reported at Nichols Ranch to farm outbuildings, trees, homes, and boat docks.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 17, 2015 to April 17, 2015. Affected areas: Taylor, Tom Green. Episode summary: Active jet stream disturbances interacted with the dryline and an unstable airmass across West Central Texas, resulting in several episodes of severe weather across the area. Although most of the storms produced large hail, there were a few reports of flash flooding and damaging winds. Details: Heavy rainfall resulted in flash flooding in Abilene. Law enforcement reported a high water rescue in San Angelo at a low water crossing.

title: Flash Flood: California, May 19, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from May 19, 2015 to May 19, 2015. Affected areas: Modoc. Episode summary: Heavy precipitation from a thunderstorm fell on recently burned areas in southwest Modoc County, leading to localized flash flooding and a mudslide near Day California. Details: A spotter in Day California reported a mudslide up against her house. This slide was associated with a burn scarred area and affected two houses. A sheriff deputy reported that clogged culverts caused mud and water to overflow the road.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Apr 05, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from April 05, 2015 to April 06, 2015. Affected areas: Forest, Oneida, Vilas. Episode summary: A narrow band of 6 to nearly 10 inches of snow fell across far north central Wisconsin as a low pressure system moved across Illinois. The highest snowfall totals included 9.9 inches near Argonne (Forest Co.), 9.0 inches at Three Lakes (Oneida Co.), 8.5 inches at Sugar Camp (Oneida Co.), and 8.0 inches at St. Germain and Lac du Flambeau (both in Vilas Co.). Details: As much as 8.0 inches of snow fell at St. Germain and Lac du Flambeau in Vilas County. The highest snowfall totals in Oneida County included 9.0 inches at Three Lakes and 8.5 inches at Sugar Camp. Nearly ten inches (9.9 inches) of snow fell near Argonne in Forest County.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 22, 2015 to April 24, 2015. Affected areas: Coleman, Nolan, Runnels. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance interacted with an unstable airmass to produce mostly hail across West Central Texas on April 22. Then on the 24th, a much stronger upper level disturbance and an unstable airmass, resulted in a more widespread severe weather outbreak across the region. These supercell thunderstorms produced plenty of hail and damaging thunderstorm winds across the area. As a thunderstorm was developing in northwest Nolan County, it produced a landspout tornado. Details: A National Weather Survey team found damage from an EF1 tornado that tracked across rural areas of northeast Runnels County into northwest Coleman County. The tornado began about 11 miles east northeast of Winters. The storm crossed the Runnels and Coleman County Line at approximately 5 miles west southwest of Novice and ended about 2 miles north of Novice. The most significant damage was at |FM A person living near the four corners, in northwest Nolan County, videotaped a picturesque landspout tornado for a few minutes.

title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, May 28, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from May 28, 2015 to May 28, 2015. Affected areas: Marinette. Episode summary: Thunderstorms that formed in the vicinity of a stationary front across northern Wisconsin produced large hail near Niagara. Multiple storms with heavy rain tracked over Niagara and caused flash flooding that washed out part of a street. Details: Heavy rain, from multiple storms, partially washed out Brook Street and left standing water on Highway 141. The time of this event is estimated. A COOP observer in Norway, Michigan, less than 5 miles east of Niagara, reported a storm total of 2.2 inches of rain, including 1.1 inches in one hour. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Heavy Snow: Wisconsin, Apr 09, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Snow, from April 09, 2015 to April 10, 2015. Affected areas: Florence, Forest, Langlade, Vilas. Episode summary: A narrow band of heavy snow fell over northeast Wisconsin as a strengthening low pressure system moved from central Lake Michigan to northern Lake Huron. Snow totals in the band were mainly in the 6 to 8 inch range. Some of the highest totals included: 8.2 inches near Florence (Florence Co.), 7.0 inches at Crandon (Forest Co.), and 6.0 inches at Antigo (Langlade Co.) and Phelps (Vilas Co.). Details: The highest snowfall totals in Forest County were 7.0 inches at Crandon and 6.8 inches near Laona. Snowfall totals in the Florence area were in the 8.0 to 8.2 inch range. As much as 6.0 inches of snow fell at Phelps, in eastern Vilas County.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2015 to April 30, 2015. Affected areas: Bosque, Collin, Comanche, Coryell, Dallas, Denton, Ellis, Erath, Hamilton, Hill, Hood, Hunt and 13 more areas. Episode summary: Drought conditions continued across portions of North and Central Texas through the month of April, with twenty-six of the forty-six counties experiencing drought during the month. However, multiple rounds of precipitation throughout April helped lessen the severity and extent of the drought across portions of the area. Details: The northwest half of Young County spent the month in D3/Extreme drought conditions, while the southeast half spend the month in D4/Exceptional drought conditions. The northern third of Hamilton County started the month of April in D3/Extreme drought conditions while the rest of the county experienced D2/Severe drought. However, by the end of the month, most of the county had improved to D2/Severe drought conditions due to multiple rounds of precipitation. The northern half of Jack County started most of the month in D3/Extreme drought conditions, while the southern half spend most of the month in D4/Exceptional drought conditions. However, towards the end of the month, the southeastern sections of the county improved to D3/Extreme drought conditions. Reported property and crop damage: about $43,000.

title: Flood: Texas, Jun 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from June 12, 2015 to June 12, 2015. Affected areas: Lynn. Episode summary: Several slow-moving severe thunderstorms, including supercells, erupted this afternoon from Parmer County south to Yoakum County along a dryline before spreading east over the remainder of the South Plains through late evening. Many of these storms produced large hail, downburst winds and heavy rainfall. An initial supercell near Muleshoe later morphed into an intense cluster of storms that produced destructive downbursts in portions of Hale County. The worst of these winds toppled two semi-trucks traveling on Interstate 27 causing minor injuries to one of the drivers. Swaths of heavy rain also accompanied many of these storms resulting in flooded roads and fields. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,500,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 14, 2015 to June 14, 2015. Affected areas: Bailey. Episode summary: A single supercell storm developed in northwest Bailey County this afternoon (just south of West Camp) and for the next 1.5 hours proceeded to build slowly to the southwest before crossing the New Mexico state line. Although no severe weather reports were available in this remote area, Doppler radar indicated that between six and eight inches of rain fell about ten miles southwest of West Camp producing flash flooding. This storm did spawn a left-moving supercell that darted northeast into Parmer County where it later produced hail to the size of golf balls in Friona. Some damage to cars in Friona was posted on social media sites. Details: Flash flooding was observed over a portion of Northwest Bailey County, southwest of Muleshoe. Farm to Market Road 746 was covered with sand and mud after water receded following radar estimates of six to eight inches of rain.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Tornado, from April 24, 2015 to April 25, 2015. Affected areas: Atascosa, Bastrop, Bexar, Caldwell, Fayette, Guadalupe, Lee, Zavala. Episode summary: An upper level short wave trough moved through the long wave trough over the southwestern states and interacted with a dryline to produce widespread thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced large hail, damaging wind gusts, and heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. There were high water rescues in San Antonio at the following locations:|12000 block of Old O'Connor Rd.|Intersection of Mockingbird Ln. and N. Songbird Ln.|I-10W ramp at N. Brazos St.|Hwy281S at E Basse Rd.|Intersection of Stahl Rd. and Bell Dr. A thunderstorm produced a tornado that moved through an open area near the Dimmit/Zavala County line. An irrigation pivot was overturned on a ranch along with some minor outbuilding damage. No other damage was found. The path and time were determined from radar. Max winds are estimated to be 80 mph. An elderly man was working on a fence and may have hit his head and fell into a creek and drown. The creek had flowing water from recent rains. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: High Wind: California, Apr 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from April 14, 2015 to April 14, 2015. Affected areas: Se Kern Cty Desert. Episode summary: An upper level trough of low pressure moved onshore during the day on the 13th of April resulting in onshore flow across Central California. As the low pressure system began exiting the area on the 14th the pressure gradient tightened resulting in strong, gusty winds across the mountains and desert areas of Kern County. Winds were generally westerly at 25-35 MPH across the mountains and desert ares. However, there were some gust of 50-61 MPH. Details: Mojave National Test Pilot School's mesonet station reported strong wind gusts.

title: Dust Storm: California, Apr 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, from April 14, 2015 to April 14, 2015. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: An upper level trough of low pressure moved onshore on April 14th resulting in wind gusts of 45-60 MPH. An area of dust and dirt was lifted into the atmosphere, reducing visibility to near zero across Highway 180 near Fresno. The reduced visibility lead to a seven-car crash causing minor injuries and a closure of the roadway for a few hours. Details: Blowing dust reduced visibility to nearly zero along Highway 180, near Fresno, causing two multi-car accidents.

title: Heavy Rain, Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Heavy Rain, Tornado, from June 15, 2015 to June 15, 2015. Affected areas: Brown, Outagamie, Waupaca. Episode summary: Thunderstorms associated with a cold front that was moving across Wisconsin produced a brief tornado near Glenmore (Brown Co.) and a funnel cloud near Shirley (Brown Co.). The slow-moving storms also produced heavy rainfall that caused urban flooding as they moved through the area. Around 2 inches of rain fell in less than two hours in the Appleton area. Details: Heavy rain caused minor street flooding at some intersections in New London. Heavy rain caused minor street flooding at numerous locations in and around Appleton. Heavy rain caused minor street flooding north of New London where 1.73 inches of rain fell in just 30 minutes. Reported property and crop damage: about $100.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2015 to April 30, 2015. Affected areas: Brown, Callahan, Haskell, Jones, Kimble, Mason, San Saba, Shackelford, Taylor, Throckmorton. Episode summary: The drought that has plagued parts of West Central Texas since the fall of 2010 has shown signs of improvement this month across a large part of the area. Several rounds of thunderstorms alleviated the intensity and the coverage of the drought. Details: The northeast corner of Taylor County was in a severe drought. The southeast corner of Jones County was in a severe drought. Most of Shackelford County was in a severe drought.

title: Wildfire: Wisconsin, May 02, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Wildfire, from May 02, 2015 to May 02, 2015. Affected areas: Juneau. Episode summary: A small central Wisconsin wildfire destroyed six buildings southeast of Necedah (Juneau County) on May 2nd. Dry conditions across central Wisconsin helped to fuel the fire that started on a warm afternoon. The fire destroyed three houses and three outbuildings. None of the houses were occupied and were only used for storage. Details: Three unoccupied homes and three outbuildings were destroyed by a small wildfire southeast of Necedah. The fire was fueled by dry conditions and started on a warm afternoon. The fire burned about 4 acres. Reported property and crop damage: about $150,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Apr 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from April 24, 2015 to April 27, 2015. Affected areas: Jasper, Newton. Episode summary: A large upper level trough stalled over the southwest states while multiple short waves rotated around the larger trough over a few days. This produced several rounds of severe weather with tornadoes, hail, and high winds reported. The first round entered the region by late morning on the 24th as a long lived super cell tracked from Tyler County into Louisiana and then into the gulf. The second round of severe weather produced one report of wind damage while the 3rd and 4th rounds produced widespread wind damage, a tornado, and copious amounts of hail. Details: The EF1 tornado developed between FM 255 and County Road 228 snapping several trees in the area of Lowe Road and County Road 227. There was damage to at least two residences when trees fell onto homes, sheds, and vehicles. The tornado then continued to the northeast crossing Highway 96 and County Road 200 causing tree damage. When the tornado reached County Road 207 it hooked more to the north no An EF1 tornado originated near the Neches River west of Kirbyville and moved east to southeast crossing Highway 82 west of Kirbyville near the airport. The tornado continued into Newton County between FM 1013 and South Saint Aubin Road. Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped along the path damaging a few homes from debris hitting them. Some outbuildings were also damaged. The average width was 50 An EF1 tornado began Southeast of Call and moved across mostly forest. The tornado crossed the Sabine River near the east end of Magnum Road. The tornado path in Newton county was 3.94 miles long and 50 yards wide. Reported property and crop damage: about $105,000.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from June 17, 2015 to June 17, 2015. Affected areas: Dunn, Polk. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of Wednesday, June 17th from the Twin Cities, south to the Iowa border. The storms near the Twin Cities drifted eastward into west central Wisconsin. Two weak tornadoes (EF-0) developed from a storm that moved across Polk and Dunn counties. Details: A tornado knocked down about a dozen trees before entering a farm, where there was minor damage to eaves and soffits of the main building as well as to some outdoor furnishings. Winds were estimated at about 65 mph. The tornado was caught on video by a local storm chaser. A weak tornado touched down briefly, damaging several trees, a small lightweight greenhouse that was covered in plastic, and removed a few shingles from two outbuildings. The tornado moved into a field and dissipated. Winds were estimated at about 65 mph. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 17, 2015 to April 17, 2015. Affected areas: Bandera, Edwards, Wilson. Episode summary: Severe thunderstorms developed over the western Edwards Plateau in the morning hours and over the course of the afternoon and into the evening, spread eastward through South Central Texas. Details: A low water crossing on Highway 377 was flooded due to heavy rain. Multiple low water crossings were reported flooded along Highway 16 east and west of the city of Medina. A high water rescue took place in Floresville along with multiple low water crossings closed. No injuries were reported. Reported property and crop damage: about $30,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 16, 2015 to May 16, 2015. Affected areas: Pecos. Episode summary: A potent upper level storm system centered near the Four Corners region moved eastward across the Central Plains through the evening hours. Support from a dryline and weak Pacific cold front associated with the upper storm system moved southeast and caused thunderstorms in the Lower Trans Pecos where deep moisture and low level convergence was present. Details: Heavy rain moved across Pecos County and produced flash flooding in Iraan. The sheriff's department reported 1 to 1.5 feet of water that was flowing over the streets in Iraan. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Pecos County and produced flash flooding west of Iraan. The sheriff reported water flowing over US 190 two miles west of Iraan. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Pecos County and produced flash flooding south of Iraan. The sheriff's department reported water flowing over SH 349 two miles south of Iraan. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,000.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado: Texas, May 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado, from May 18, 2015 to May 18, 2015. Affected areas: Pecos, Reeves, Upton. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance moved across the region above southeast winds at the surface, which brought increasing moisture to the area. Daytime heating lead to strong instability and this combined with moderate shear brought the development of severe storms to the Upper Trans Pecos. Details: A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a tornado near Toyah Lake. The tornado was observed by a storm chaser and lasted about 2 minutes. It was located 4 miles east of Toyah Lake and no damage was reported. The path length and width were both estimated. Due to no damage being reported, it was rated as an EF-0. A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a tornado south of Pecos. The tornado was seen by a trained spotter 11 miles south of Pecos between Highway 285 and Farm to Market Road 1450. It was on the ground for approximately 5 minutes and no damage was reported. The path length and width were both estimated. Due to no damage being reported, it was rated as an EF-0. Heavy rain moved across Pecos County and produced a flash flood near Coyanosa. Several cars were reported to have swept off the road. There was a high water rescue by the Pecos County Sheriff's Department of a woman and two children in a car but no injuries were reported. The flood gauge on the road showed that the water was four feet deep. The Texas Tech Mesonet site located about two miles n Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 19, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 19, 2015 to May 19, 2015. Affected areas: Pecos, Upton. Episode summary: An upper level low was centered over the Intermountain West and upper level disturbances moved over West Texas as a result of southwest winds aloft. A dryline was present near the Texas/New Mexico border. Daytime heating combined with plentiful moisture resulted in good instability which allowed for storms to develop. Strong low level winds moved over the area after sunset allowing storms to continue into the overnight hours. There was sufficient wind speed and direction changes with height resulting in rotating severe storms which produced large hail, damaging winds, and tornadoes. Details: A thunderstorm moved across Upton County and produced several brief tornado touchdowns near McCamey according to local law enforcement and fire department personnel. No damage was reported so these tornadoes are being rated as EF-0. A thunderstorm moved across Pecos County and produced a tornado seven miles southeast of Girvin. The tornado was reported to have remained in fields and pastures. No damage was reported so the tornado was rated an EF-0. A thunderstorm moved across Pecos County and produced a brief tornado about ten miles southwest of Bakersfield. No damage was reported so the tornado was rated as an EF-0.

title: Flash Flood: Wisconsin, Jun 11, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, from June 11, 2015 to June 11, 2015. Affected areas: Green, Lafayette. Episode summary: Rounds of thunderstorms moving east along a stationary front produced several inches of rainfall and resultant flash flooding. Details: Four roads washed out south of Browntown, including portions of Fox Valley Road and Clark Road. Three of the roads were gravel and one was paved. Rainfall estimates of 4-5 inches. A few roads closed to due water flowing over them. A car got stuck in deep water when attempting to cross a low water crossing. Reported property and crop damage: about $13,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 22, 2015 to May 22, 2015. Affected areas: Brewster. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance moved northeast from Mexico over West Texas through the afternoon. Southerly winds resulted in a good supply of moisture across the area that fueled storms that formed off the Davis Mountains. The area near the Davis Mountains was characterized by a moderately unstable environment with ample shear. Details: A thunderstorm moved across Brewster County and produced a brief tornado northeast of Alpine. A storm chaser reported ground rotation for about two minutes ten miles north of Highway 90 on US 67. No damage was reported so the tornado was rated as an EF-0.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 23, 2015 to May 23, 2015. Affected areas: Brewster, Midland. Episode summary: An upper trough was slowly moving into the region from the west. Disturbances within southwest winds aloft allowed for upper level lift to move over West Texas. Southerly surface winds maintained a high moisture content. Strong surface heating with ample instability and shear lead to thunderstorms across the Trans Pecos and Permian Basin. Details: Heavy rain moved across Midland County and produced flash flooding on the south side of Midland. An NWS employee reported water to be six inches deep running over the intersection of the service road at Highway 349 and Interstate 20. No damage was reported so the cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain fell across Midland. In a time period of 10 minutes, 0.10 to 0.24 inches of rain were recorded. The rainfall rate was 1.08 inches per hour. Heavy rain fell near Alpine. A total of 0.10 to 0.24 inches was recorded over a period of ten minutes. Reported property and crop damage: about $200.

title: Winter Weather: California, Apr 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from April 07, 2015 to April 08, 2015. Affected areas: San Bernardino County Mountains. Episode summary: A weak pacific front moved through Southern California on the evening of April 7 through early morning on April 8th, producing light snowfall in the higher elevations of the San Bernardino County Mountains. Rainfall of 0.25 to 0.50 inches occurred in northern Orange County and across the slopes of the mountains in the Cajon Pass. Details: The public reported (via social media) 2 to 3 inches of snowfall in 12 hours in the Upper Moonridge area of Big Bear.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 05, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 05, 2015 to May 06, 2015. Affected areas: Coke, Haskell, Sterling, Throckmorton. Episode summary: Strong upper level disturbances, emanating from an upper low in the Rockies, interacted with a very warm, moist atmosphere and strong upper level winds over West Central Texas to produce severe weather over a three day period. There were many reports of large hail and damaging winds, and several reports of tornadoes. Although a few of these storms were large supercells, thankfully, the tornadoes remained over rural areas. Details: This was a large tornado reported by multiple storm chasers near the intersection of U.S. Highway 380 and Texas Highway 222 or about 6 to 8 miles west northwest of Throckmorton. The tornado became rain wrapped as it moved across an open field northeast of the intersection. The tornado was observed by the public about 14 miles north of Sterling City to briefly touch down on State Highway 163. It was on the ground for about one minute. This report was relayed through the Sterling County Sheriff's office. An observer had witnessed the tornado touching the ground multiple times about 4 miles southwest of Silver. This tornado path length and beginning time were estimated using radar data and eyewitness accounts. The path width was also estimated.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 25, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 25, 2015 to May 25, 2015. Affected areas: Howard, Midland, Mitchell. Episode summary: An upper level trough was over the Rocky Mountains and an upper level disturbance moving along the base of the trough was moving toward West Texas and provided additional lift. There was a lot of instability across the area as well as strong low-level winds which helped storms to develop across West Texas in the morning hours. These storms produced large hail, strong winds, flash flooding, and a tornado. Details: Heavy rain moved across Howard County and produced flash flooding in Big Spring. It was reported that the intersection of Mesa and Parkway was flooded with an estimated three feet of water. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate since no damage was reported. Heavy rain moved across Midland County and produced flash flooding in Midland. The public reported one to two feet of water over the service road at Midkiff Street and Interstate 20. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate since no damage was reported. A thunderstorm moved across Mitchell County and produced a tornado in Loraine. A damage survey was conducted the next day. The tornado touched down at approximately 9 am CDT and continued generally northeast for a distance of 0.16 miles before lifting. The tornado was on the ground for less than one minute. There was extensive damage to a barn where several walls collapsed and a pole with a ce Reported property and crop damage: about $41,500.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 12, 2015 to April 12, 2015. Affected areas: Galveston. Episode summary: An early evening and slow moving thunderstorm produced flash flooding in Texas City. Details: A nearly stationary thunderstorm produced flash flooding in and around the Texas City area.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 22, 2015 to April 22, 2015. Affected areas: Knox. Episode summary: A complex of storms raced southward across west Texas ahead of a southward moving cold front. To the east of this area of storms, scattered supercells developed during the evening hours, producing very large hail and at least one tornado near Knox City. Storms gradually moved southward through the evening. Details: A brief tornado was reported by emergency management about 6 miles northwest of Knox City. No damage is known to have occurred with this tornado.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 26, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 26, 2015 to May 30, 2015. Affected areas: Brown, Fisher, Kimble, Runnels, Tom Green. Episode summary: A very active weather pattern resulted in a high number of severe weather reports across West Central Texas from May 26 through the 28th. Upper level disturbances, rotating around a large upper level low pressure system over the western U.S., would periodically move across West Central Texas. These disturbances interacted with a dryline, outflow boundaries and a very unstable airmass, resulting in many reports of large hail, damaging winds and flash flooding. The most active days were May 26 and May 28. Scattered supercells were noted on May 26 and led to several large hail reports, while the storms on the 28th formed into a squall line, resulting in many damaging wind reports. Details: Very heavy rain flooded several water crossings including the low water crossing at Pulliam and Bell Street. Street flooding was reported in Junction. A low water crossing at FM 1221 was filled but passable. An amateur radio operator measured 3.1 inches of rain in one hour on the south side of Bangs.

title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 03, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 03, 2015 to April 03, 2015. Affected areas: Moore. Episode summary: A strong cold front moved quickly southeast across the Texas Panhandle. Strong north winds developed in its wake late on the 2nd and continued into the early morning hours of the 3rd. Sustained winds of 35 to 40 mph were common. A wind gust of 60 mph occurred at Dumas, Texas, and this was the strongest wind gust in the Texas Panhandle for this wind event. Details: A wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at the Automated Weather Observing System located at Dumas Airport.

title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 08, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 08, 2015 to April 08, 2015. Affected areas: Armstrong, Randall. Episode summary: Strengthening low pressure over Southeast Colorado resulted in a tight pressure gradient. As the dryline mixed eastward during the afternoon southwesterly winds increased. Although sustained winds were generally 20 to 35 mph, sporadic wind gusts at or above 60 mph occurred. Details: The West Texas University mesonet located near Goodnight, Texas recorded a wind gust of 71 mph. No damage was reported. The West Texas University Mesonet located 13 miles east of Canyon, Texas recorded a wind gust of 59 mph. No damage was reported.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 12, 2015 to May 12, 2015. Affected areas: Jefferson. Episode summary: A cold front drifted through the region during afternoon and evening of the 12th. Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the boundary causing flooding for portions of Beaumont. Details: Beaumont media received multiple photos from along the Eastex Freeway, Delaware Street, Lucas Drive, and other Northeast Beaumont roads that were flooded. Several cars were flooded during the event. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 11, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 11, 2015 to April 11, 2015. Affected areas: Potter. Episode summary: A weak weather system interacted with moisture flowing northward into the area resulting in isolated thunderstorm developing during the afternoon and evening. One supercell strengthened just south of Dumas and dropped hailstones up to the size of quarters. As it moved into a more favorable environment over northern Potter County, the storm produced a brief tornado. As it continued eastward it produced hail as large as tennis balls near White Deer. Details: Severe reliable storm chaser pictures and videos indicate a very weak and brief tornado touched down in far northwestern Potter County, just west of Highway 136. This section of Potter County is rural and no damage was reported.

title: Tornado: Texas, Apr 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from April 16, 2015 to April 16, 2015. Affected areas: Carson, Gray, Hemphill, Roberts, Wheeler. Episode summary: An approaching weather system interacted with a moist and unstable environment over the Texas Panhandle resulting in one of the most significant severe weather episodes of the 2015 spring season. The majority of the severe weather occurred across the eastern half of the Panhandle. Numerous hail events occurred with hail up to the size of baseballs and slightly larger occurring in the most intense supercell thunderstorms. In some cases storms were very efficient hail producers and accumulation of hail several inches deep occurred. A total of six tornadoes were identified by storm spotters, storm chasers, public officials and through official National Weather Service damage surveys. Details: An EF-0 tornado with winds estimated to have peaked at 80 mph uprooted trees with numerous branches snapped. An old outbuilding was destroyed. Much of the path is rural making it difficult to determine whether or not the path was continuous. This was a well videographed tornado which became rain-wrapped. A well photographed tornado occurred 5 miles east-southeast of Codman. No damage was reported. A damage rating of EF-0 was assigned to this tornado. A second tornado occurred northeast of Briscoe. Xcel Energy reported damage to power poles. Winds are estimated to have peaked at 80 mph. A damage rating of EF-0 was assigned to this tornado.

title: Drought: California, May 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Drought, from May 01, 2015 to May 31, 2015. Affected areas: E Central S.J. Valley, Indian Wells Vly, Kern Cty Mtns, S Sierra Foothills, S Sierra Mtns, Se Kern Cty Desert, Se S.J. Valley, Sw S.J. Valley, Tulare Cty Foothills, Tulare Cty Mtns, W Central S.J. Valley. Episode summary: The California drought continued in full force during the month of May, 2015. Temperatures continued to average above normal. While there was some precipitation in May, it was not uniformly distributed. Fresno received 0.57 inches of rain (133% of normal) while Bakersfield received 0.68 inches (377% of normal). Overall, seasonal rainfall amounts continued to be only 35-65 percent of normal across central California. ||The U.S. Drought Monitor continued to report exceptional drought conditions across the entire Central California region. This extent of exceptional drought is extremely unusual for California. The 2013-2014 water year (July 1 - June 30) concluded with Fresno setting its second driest on record (4.81 inches) and Bakersfield setting its third driest (2.41 inches). For the calendar year, 2014 was the warmest year on record for Fresno and Bakersfield. The trend of below normal precipitation and above normal temperatures has continued through the first few months of 2015. ||There continues to be significant media coverage on the on-going drought conditions. These reports include discussion of significant re-allocation of water resources from the east to west side of the San Joaquin Valley, farmers forgoing planting of some crops, a decrease in the snow-related tourism activity in the Southern Sierra Nevada, reduction in air quality due to persistent stagnant air, loss or reduction of ground water, wells drying up in several communities leaving them with no water, and an unprecedented increase in fire danger across the Southern Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 17, 2015 to June 17, 2015. Affected areas: Angelina, Nacogdoches. Episode summary: As Tropical Depression Bill continued to make progress into East Central Texas...a feeder band developed across Deep East Texas and the result was flash flooding across a few counties. Details: Heavy rainfall resulted in high water over FM 1475...FM 326 and U.S. Hwy 69 south near Buck Creek southeast of Lufkin, Texas. Heavy rainfall resulted in the closures of several roadways in and around the Lufkin community including Tom Hollins...Box Car Road...FM 1475 and FM 841. High water was reported across three different portions of FM 1818.

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2015 to April 28, 2015. Affected areas: Edwards, Kendall, Medina, Real. Episode summary: Well above normal rainfall during April moved Edwards, Kendall, Medina, and Real Counties out of Severe Drought category (Stage D2). Rainfall in these counties ranged from 150% to 300% of normal. Since the drought began in November 2010, Edwards County has been in Stage D2 or worse for all but two months (May 2012 and November 2014) until now. title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2015 to April 30, 2015. Affected areas: Bandera, Gillespie, Kerr, Llano. Episode summary: Most of Bandera County received 150% to 200% of normal rainfall in April and this was enough to move them from Extreme (Stage D3) drought category to Severe (Stage D2). Gillespie (D3), Kerr (D3), and Llano (D2) Counties remained unchanged in April despite getting above normal rainfall. The seven day stream flow average at the end of the month was below normal (10-24 percent) for the Upper Guadalupe River Basin and much below normal (less than 10 percent) for the Frio River Basin. Area lakes and reservoirs continued well below normal pool elevations. Lake Amistad was up slightly to 28.6 feet below normal. Lake Travis was also up slightly at 51.8 feet below normal. Medina Lake was up nearly two feet but was still 87.9 feet below normal. The Edwards Aquifer rose during the month and was at 647.2 feet. This was 8.5 feet higher than at the end of April 2014 but still 20.2 feet below average. Fredericksburg remained in stage 3 water restrictions and Kerrville remained in stage 2. title: Tornado: Texas, May 25, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 25, 2015 to May 25, 2015. Affected areas: Fisher. Episode summary: A strong upper level disturbance interacting with a highly unstable airmass led to the development of a squall line during the morning hours. This line of thunderstorms resulted in many damaging wind reports, an isolated tornado and large hail events across portions of West Central Texas. Details: A tornado briefly touched down near the Fisher and Nolan County Line along U.S. Highway 70.

title: Drought: Texas, May 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from May 01, 2015 to May 26, 2015. Affected areas: Bandera, Gillespie, Kerr, Llano. Episode summary: Bandera, Gillespie, Kerr, and Llano Counties received 200% to 400% of normal rainfall in May and moved out of Severe Drought category (Stage D2). These were the last four counties in South Central Texas remaining in at least Stage D2. The last time Bandera County was in less than Stage D2 drought was January 2013 and the last time for Gillespie County was October 2012. Kerr County was the hardest hit by the drought in South Central Texas. It was only better than Stage D2 for one month (May 2012) since the drought began in November 2010. title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 27, 2015 to May 27, 2015. Affected areas: Pecos. Episode summary: An upper level trough was over the western United States with West Texas under southwest winds aloft. A developing surface trough and an upper level disturbance moving over the area provided enough lift for storms to develop across West Texas. High instability and strong shear contributed to thunderstorms that produced large hail, tornadoes, and flash flooding. Details: A thunderstorm moved across Pecos County and produced a tornado about 20 miles northwest of Belding. It was described as a rain-wrapped tornado in a rural area. The time on the ground, path length, and path width were estimated. There was no damage reported so the tornado was rated as an EF-0. A thunderstorm moved across Pecos County and produced a brief tornado about 22 miles northwest of Belding. The time that the tornado was on the ground is an estimate as well as the distance traveled and the path width. There was no damage reported so the tornado was rated as an EF-0. Heavy rain moved across Pecos County and produced flash flooding in Fort Stockton. The emergency manager reported three feet of water at the flood gauge near Rooney Park. There was no damage reported so the cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $500.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 28, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 28, 2015 to May 28, 2015. Affected areas: Borden, Ector. Episode summary: An upper level trough was progressing over the Upper Midwest. Upper level disturbances were moving across the base of this trough in the West Texas region. At the surface, there was an abundance of moisture in place with strong heating that lead to very unstable conditions. High instability, strong shear, and steep lapse rates set the stage for thunderstorms to develop that produced large hail, isolated tornadoes, and flash flooding. Details: A thunderstorm moved across Borden County and produced a brief tornado about 16 miles northwest of Gail. The time the tornado was on the ground, the path width and length were estimated. There was no damage reported, so the tornado was rated as an EF-0. Heavy rain moved across Ector County and produced flash flooding in Odessa. Six inches to one foot of water was reported to be over the road at the intersection of West County Road and University Boulevard. There was no damage reported so the cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $500.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 21, 2015 to May 21, 2015. Affected areas: Jefferson. Episode summary: Heavy rain in Beaumont area flooded streets and threatened homes. Details: Slow moving thunderstorms produced heavy rain across Beaumont for a few hours. This combined with already full ditches and wet ground produced street flooding on multiple roadways. Flood waters also approached some homes along Euclid Street, and cars were stalled in under passes near Lamar University. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, Jun 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from June 12, 2015 to June 12, 2015. Affected areas: Ector, Gaines. Episode summary: Upper level troughs moving slowly over the Rocky Mountains combined with a surface trough across extreme West Texas and eastern New Mexico. Intense heating with plentiful low level moisture lead to strong instability across the area. This instability combined with strong shear allowed thunderstorms to develop and to produce large hail, flash flooding, and a tornado across the Permian Basin and the Trans Pecos. Details: Heavy rain fell across Ector County and produced flash flooding in Odessa. Streets were covered with water and there was water over the curbs and into yards from one inch of rain that fell within 30 minutes. No damage was reported. A thunderstorm moved across Gaines County and produced a tornado about one mile west of Loop. The tornado was seen by a trained spotter and reported to be brief. There was no damage reported with this tornado so it was rated as an EF-0. Both the path length and width were estimated.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 13, 2015 to June 13, 2015. Affected areas: Gaines. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance slowly progressed east across the southwest US and it provided upper level support for thunderstorm activity. Good moisture was present east of a dryline that was backed up to the mountains of West Texas. Some locations had low to mid 60 dewpoints. High instability and strong shear allowed for thunderstorms to become organized and produce large hail and damaging winds across the Trans Pecos and Permian Basin. The high moisture over the area also lead to some flash flooding. Details: Heavy rain from a line of thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall in Seminole and flooded Hwy 214 just north of Seminole leaving some patrons under a foot of water. Heavy rain fell across Gaines County and produced flash flooding on Highway 385 between Seminole and Seagraves. The flooding was reported on Highway 385 between County Roads 103 and 124. Other reports were received that indicate numerous county roads northwest of Seminole were flooded and impassable. Seminole and Seagraves fire departments were pulling cars out of ditches. The cost of damage i Reported property and crop damage: about $5,750.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 25, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 25, 2015 to May 27, 2015. Affected areas: Hardin, Jefferson, Tyler. Episode summary: An upper trough stalled over the Southwest States for multiple days while several short waves rotated around the base of the larger trough. This produced periods of severe storms and flooding in Southeast Texas. Details: Heavy rain across Lumberton flooded roads and at least one home on the southeast side of the city. The Tyler County Sheriffs Department reported several roads impassable due to high water. Flooding along wolf creek caused water to enter a camp around 3 feet deep. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 14, 2015 to June 15, 2015. Affected areas: Gaines, Reagan. Episode summary: A weak low pressure system slowly drifted east into the Great Plains with a trailing upper level disturbance rotating around the backside of the upper low. As the disturbance moved over the region, it brought thunderstorms to West Texas. Instability and shear were weak, but the high moisture content across the area caused flash flooding to develop as a line of storms moved across the Permian Basin. Details: Spotter reported water 12-18 inches deep over four lanes on Highway 385 southwest of Seagraves. Trained Spotter reported closed roads due to flooding in the City of Seagraves. A line of thunderstorms moved across Reagan County and produced significant flooding in the city of Big Lake. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $600.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 09, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 09, 2015 to May 11, 2015. Affected areas: Collin, Cooke, Denton, Ellis, Fannin, Grayson, Henderson, Hood, Lamar, Limestone, Mclennan, Navarro and 2 more areas. Episode summary: Widespread severe weather and flash flooding occurred in addition to the outbreak of tornadoes. Details: A trained spotter reported flooding across roads near Sherman Airport. Amateur radio reported that high water rescues were occurring on Poplar St in Bonham, TX. A social media report stated that flooding was occurring on Highway 75 near exit 51 in Van Alstyne, TX. Reported property and crop damage: about $7,361,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 18, 2015 to June 18, 2015. Affected areas: Angelina, Shelby. Episode summary: The remnants of Tropical Storm Bill continued to plague Northeast Texas on June 18th. A nocturnal feeder band developed across Northeast Texas and produced excessive heavy rainfall which produced flash flooding across several counties. Details: Excessive heavy rainfall resulted in the closure of Hwy. 96 with traffic being rerouted. Hwy. 87 and Hwy. 7E also had high water over them in several locations. Several highways were flooded in and around Lufkin, Texas. Those included FM 841, FM 2497 and FM 324.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 18, 2015 to May 19, 2015. Affected areas: Tom Green. Episode summary: An upper level disturbance interacted with an old frontal boundary and a tropical airmass to produce torrential rain across the Concho Valley and San Angelo. This very heavy rain caused flash flooding and resulted in many homes flooded and several swift water rescues. Rainfall amounts of 4 to 8 inches plus fell into the Concho River water shed. This water flowed into a nearly empty O.C. Fisher Reservoir, filling it to 13 percent full. Details: San Angelo police confirmed one fatality in a vehicle crash on Knickerbocker Road near Bentwood Country Club. The driver lost control in the very heavy rain as his truck hydroplaned and collided with a tree. An amateur radio operator reported 6.51 inches of rain about 12 miles south of San Angelo. A National Weather Service employee measured 4.64 inches of heavy rain. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,000,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 18, 2015 to April 18, 2015. Affected areas: Bee, San Patricio. Episode summary: Moisture remained over South Texas in advance of a weak boundary moved into the northern Brush Country. Another upper level jet streak moved across the region as the slow moving upper low moved into the central high plains. Scattered thunderstorms formed in the afternoon. The storms produced locally heavy rainfall. This led to flash flooding in the cities of Beeville, Portland, and Skidmore. Details: Rainfall amounts of around 1.75 inches in 20 minutes caused street flooding in Portland around San Saba Drive. Water reached into yards due to the heavy rainfall. Heavy rainfall produced flooding of roads in the area between Skidmore, Tynan, and Papalote. Low lying areas along Aransas River were flooded. Water reached the bottom of the bridge on Corrigan Road near Skidmore.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 22, 2015 to April 22, 2015. Affected areas: Goliad, Nueces, San Patricio. Episode summary: Several supercells developed and tracked east-southeast along a nearly stationary front stretching from the Hill Country to South Texas into the central Gulf of Mexico. These storms contained very large hail, up to tennis ball size near Austwell, and very strong winds greater than 60 mph. Wind damage and flash flooding occurred with these severe thunderstorms also. Details: Flooding occurred through several intersections around the city of Ingleside. Flooding affected the intersections of Tiner Lane and Todd Circle, 1st Street and Honeysuckle Lane, and 6th Street between Avenue A and Alana Lane. Water crossed the roadway along Lang Road near an elementary school. Many streets within Portland were flooded due to the heavy rainfall. Water flooded the roadways in several parts of Corpus Christi. Flooding was reported near Leopard and Peabody, along the South Padre Island Drive frontage road, and near the intersection of Staples and Lipe Streets. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 16, 2015 to May 17, 2015. Affected areas: Crockett. Episode summary: More supercell thunderstorms developed east of the dryline as a strong upper level disturbance moved across the region. The main impacts were large hail and damaging winds. Details: A car was washed off the road at 12th and Jones in Ozona. Local law enforcement discourage travel across Crockett County. Water covered Texas Highway 137 for 3 miles just west of Texas Highway 163.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Apr 10, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from April 10, 2015 to April 10, 2015. Affected areas: Hidalgo, Starr. Episode summary: A dissipating cold front edged south to the Rio Grande during the afternoon and evening. Hot, humid air with temperatures to around 90 combined with the surface front and upper level energy to initiate rapidly developing storms across the region. Several storms became strong to severe, with one storm dropping quarter size hail in Falfurrias. Moisture pooling along and just behind the front aided storm redevelopment over the same areas, centered on southwest to central Hidalgo County. After the rains tapered, measured and estimated totals indicated 4 to 6 inches from Penitas/La Joya northeast through north Mission, Alton, and part of Edinburg. Poor drainage areas, particularly around the colonias of Alton along and near State Road 107, were hardest hit; several homes had standing water, up to 2 feet in depth, inside them. Details: An estimated 4 to 6 inches of rain fell within a few hours. Poor drainage areas, particularly around the colonias of Alton along and near State Road 107, were hardest hit; several homes had standing water, up to 2 feet in depth, inside them. A foot of water was reported at the Penitas Shopping Plaza as well. COOP observer northwest of Alton reported 4.50 inches of rainfall. Starr County Sheriffs Office reported street flooding occurring in the town of Alto Bonito. Estimated depth of water was up to a foot in some locations. An estimated 2.5 to 3 inches of rain fell. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 24, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 24, 2015 to April 24, 2015. Affected areas: Starr. Episode summary: The combination of daytime heating, divergence aloft, plenty of moisture, and the arrival of a shortwave trough allowed for showers and thunderstorms to develop over Nuevo Leon during the evening hours and move across the Rio Grande River and over Upper Valley, brush country, and ranchlands as an MCS. Torrential rainfall of an estimated 2 to 3 inches fell within an hour over Rio Grande City, flooding dozens of roads with up to a foot of flowing water. Details: Rio Grande City Police reported that 20 to 30 streets across the Rio Grande City were flooded with at least a foot of flowing water, that the police substation parking lot had 8 to 12 inches of water and that Highway 83 had 2 to 3 inches of water on the roadway. No homes were reported flooded in the city.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jun 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from June 22, 2015 to June 22, 2015. Affected areas: Crawford, Richland. Episode summary: An early morning squall line moved across southwest Wisconsin on June 22nd. This squall line produced winds of 60 to 70 mph and two small tornadoes. The first tornado damaged trees along its path north of Wauzeka (Crawford County). The second tornado damaged a few homes and numerous trees along its path north of Westport and Port Andrews (Crawford & Richland Counties). As the squall line moved across southwest Wisconsin it produced wind damage across the southern sections of Crawford and Richland Counties and over much of Grant County. Trees, power lines and at least one barn were blown down near Casseville (Grant County), multiple power lines were snapped east of Prairie du Chien (Crawford County), barns were damaged north of Port Andrew (Richland County) and 65 to 70 mph winds with damage were reported in Hazel Green and Platteville (Grant County). Details: A tornado caused mainly tree damage in far southeast Crawford County before moving into Richland County. A small tornado damaged trees along its path in southern Crawford County between Wauzeka and Steuben. The tornado traveled across rural portions of southwest Richland County north of Westport and Port Andrews. A few homes along County Roads W and M were damaged along with numerous trees. Reported property and crop damage: about $44,000.

title: High Wind: Texas, Apr 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 01, 2015 to April 01, 2015. Affected areas: Kleberg, Nueces. Episode summary: A large area of showers and thunderstorms over the Deep South Texas moved toward Coastal Bend during the early morning hours. The precipitation rapidly diminished over the Coastal Bend and a wake low pressure area formed between Alice and Corpus Christi. Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph occurred across the Coastal Bend. The winds caused minor damage to trees and blew a boat into an recreational vehicle. Details: Corpus Christi International Airport ASOS measured a gust to 53 knots. Public reported a large tree was blown down into a home during the wake low wind event in Robstown. Public reported a boat on a trailer was blown into a recreational vehicle during the wake low wind event on North Beach. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 18, 2015 to May 18, 2015. Affected areas: Hardin. Episode summary: Slow moving thunderstorms moved across Lumberton during the late afternoon of the 18th. This occurred with already full ditches and saturated ground and produced street flooding in the Lumberton area and flooded a house. Details: Pictures and reports were received from the Lumberton area of street flooding. At least one home received some flood water during the slow moving thunderstorms. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 06, 2015 to May 06, 2015. Affected areas: Burleson, Waller. Details: Flash flooding closed roads from the Deanville area to Snook to the Somerville Lake area. Flash flooding was reported in the Hempstead area along Highway 290 from the Sorsby Road area to the Highway 6 area. Reported property and crop damage: about $14,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: High Wind, from April 24, 2015 to April 24, 2015. Affected areas: Potter, Randall. Details: The KVII Schoolnet site located at Oasis RV park measured a wind gust of 58 mph. The KVII Schoolnet site 10 miles east-southeast of Valley De Oro measured a wind gust at 60 mph.

The flooding problems were more focused in West Baraboo within construction zones that had temporary culverts in place. title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 11, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 11, 2015 to May 11, 2015. Affected areas: Grimes, San Jacinto, Trinity, Walker, Washington. Episode summary: A line of thunderstorms moved through southeast Texas during the late night through early morning hours and produced strong wind gusts and very heavy rainfall that caused some flash flooding. Details: A rainfall total of 4.80 inches in about a three hour period was measured near the intersection of Highway 190 and FM 2296. Heavy rains caused flash flooding along FM 980 North along the Trinity River area. Multiple county roads in and around the Huntsville area closed and impassable.
