title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Drought, from April 01, 2015 to April 30, 2015. Affected areas: Armstrong, Carson, Collingsworth, Dallam, Donley, Gray, Hansford, Hartley, Hemphill, Hutchinson, Lipscomb, Moore and 7 more areas. Episode summary: The dry spring pattern continued into the first half of April for the Texas Panhandle. There were a few scattered rain events early in the month, though most areas measured less than 0.25 inches of rain through April 15th. Several widespread rain events affected the Panhandle in the second half of the month, however; and most locations ended up receiving 2 to 3 inches of rain for April. This beneficial rain eased drought conditions across the entire Panhandle. A mix of Severe (D2) to Extreme (D3) Drought conditions remained along a line from near Dalhart to near Clarendon. Conditions across the rest of the Panhandle improved to a mix of mostly Moderate (D1) Drought and Abnormally Dry (D0) conditions. Amarillo recorded 2.97 inches of precipitation for the month (1.57 inches above normal), Dalhart recorded 1.30 inches of precipitation (0.22 inches above normal), and Borger recorded 4.40 inches of precipitation (2.86 inches above normal).||Soil moisture was rated from mostly adequate to short by the end of April. Prior to the onset of spring rains, dry and windy weather had left most soil moisture rated as short. The rain was too late to save winter wheat in the eastern Panhandle, though did help to ensure a good moisture profile for spring planting of summer crops across the area. Rangeland and pasture improved throughout the month, though cattle herd sizes remained limited due to prolonged drought and high cattle prices. Ranchers moved cattle to rangeland that had not been usable for several years. Upper soil zones were mostly above 40 percent full by the end of April, with

title: Drought: Texas, Apr 01, 2015
text: herd sizes remained limited due to prolonged drought and high cattle prices. Ranchers moved cattle to rangeland that had not been usable for several years. Upper soil zones were mostly above 40 percent full by the end of April, with top soil in the driest areas in the 10 to 20 percent full range (moderate agriculturally dry). Deeper soil ranged from 30 to 50 percent of normal in the northwestern Texas Panhandle to near 100 percent of normal across the southeastern Panhandle. The Palmer Drought Severity Index indicated a rating of Near Normal conditions for the Texas Panhandle. Countywide burn bans were supported in several counties.||Frequent rainfall by the end of April caused streamflows across the Texas Panhandle to be near normal. The reservoirs of Lake Meredith and Palo Duro were below 6 percent and 2 percent capacity respectively, and Greenbelt Lake was near 13 percent capacity. Water watches for several public water systems persisted throughout the month while voluntary to mandatory mild water restrictions were continued.||Economic losses due to the drought through April were predominantly the result of losses in winter wheat and supplemental feed for cattle on drought-thinned rangeland and pastures. Details: Severe Drought (D2) as depicted on the U.S. Drought Monitor. Extreme Drought (D3) as depicted on the U.S. Drought Monitor.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 27, 2015 to June 28, 2015. Affected areas: Harris, Liberty, Montgomery, Waller. Episode summary: A slow southward sagging cold front interacted with the sea breeze boundary and numerous outflow boundaries from earlier activity to produce late evening through overnight showers and thunderstorms that produced very heavy rainfall that caused some flash flooding. Also, lightning strikes damaged a couple of structures. Details: There was street flooding in and around the Jersey Village area. The flooded roadways included Highway 6 in Huffmeister and at SH 249 and Beltway 8. There was flooding that lead to road closures in and around the intersection of FM 1488 and Hegar Road. High rainfall caused flooding around the Splendora area. There was two feet of water on Kingport Road northeast of town.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain: Wisconsin, Jun 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, from June 15, 2015 to June 15, 2015. Affected areas: La Crosse, Monroe. Episode summary: Thunderstorms with very high rainfall rates and heavy rain moved across western Wisconsin during the afternoon hours of June 15th. The rainfall resulted in a mudslide south of Bangor (La Crosse County) that blocked both lanes of traffic on State Highway 162. The rain also caused Dutch Creek to come out of its banks and take out a snowmobile trail bridge and a pedestrian bridge in Bangor. The high rainfall rates overcame the drainage system on the south side of the city of La Crosse (La Crosse County) resulting in street flooding. Details: Heavy rainfall rates overcame the drainage system on the south side of the city of La Crosse causing street flooding to occur along U.S. Highways 14/61. Heavy rain caused a mudslide that blocked both lanes of traffic on State Highway 162 south of Bangor. Heavy rains caused Dutch Creek to quickly go out of its banks and take out a pedestrian bridge in Veterans Memorial Park and a snowmobile bridge. The pedestrian bridge was destroyed while the snowmobile bridge was designed to be moveable and only sustained minor damage. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Apr 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from April 14, 2015 to April 14, 2015. Affected areas: Brazoria. Episode summary: A passing shortwave disturbance initialized clusters of coastal county thunderstorms that produced severe wind gusts and street flooding. Details: Heavy rain caused residential street flooding that left some roadways impassable across northern Lake Jackson.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jul 04, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from July 04, 2015 to July 04, 2015. Affected areas: Bowie. Episode summary: Convection developed during the predawn hours of July 4th, 2015 across portions of Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas. This convection developed due in part to an area of vorticity in association with an upper level trough axis across the Southern Plains and a strong low level jet. After sunrise, this convection developed across portions of Northeast Texas as well. Intense convection at first caused damaging thunderstorm wind gusts but the storms took on a linear fashion and began to train across the same general area of Southwest Arkansas and portions of Northeast Texas. The result was very heavy rainfall where up to a foot of rain was reported across portions of Southwest Arkansas for the calender day of July 4th, 2015. Numerous road closures were reported with many roads washed out as well. Details: A car was completely submerged in a flooded intersection at Summerhills Road and Moores Lane. Hwy. 82 was flooded between DeKalb and Malta, Texas. High water was reported over Hwy. 82 and FM. 1840 in DeKalb, Texas.

title: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 27, 2015 to May 31, 2015. Affected areas: Bosque, Collin, Cooke, Coryell, Dallas, Denton, Ellis, Hill, Jack, Johnson, Montague, Palo Pinto and 3 more areas. Episode summary: The end of May brought widespread flooding to north and central Texas. By the end of the month, the region had essentially erased a four year drought in less than four weeks. Several area lakes were in surcharge capacity and releasing water downstream. The city of Dallas was impacted most of all, with one major highway closed for nearly a week due to flooding. Occasional bouts with severe weather also occurred during the final 5 days of May. Details: Flooded roadways were reported near Blum in northwestern Hill County after 2 to 3 inches or rain fell. Homes on the west side of Highway 287, across from Lake Padera, were flooded. Jack County Sheriff's Department reported flooding along Hwy 281 near the Jack/Archer County Line. Reported property and crop damage: about $15,203,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 06, 2015 to May 06, 2015. Affected areas: Archer. Episode summary: A potent Spring storm system took shape across the Southern and Central Plains. Strong surface cyclogenesis took shape during the day, allowing ample moisture to return northward with strong southerly flow. At the same time, a strong upper level shortwave trough allowed strong mid level westerlies to overspread much of the Plains region. With large instability and wind shear, the stage was set for widespread severe storm development. Storms initiated within the open warm sector ahead of the dryline. Additional storms developed during the evening hours and persisted well into the night, producing sporadic large hail and wind damage across north Texas. Details: A tornado was reported east of Lake Kickapoo at 849 pm CDT. The tornado initially moved east crossing state highway 25 about 5.5 miles northwest of Archer City. The tornado began to curve northeast as it approached state highway 79 and crossed that highway about 4 miles north of Archer City. After crossing state highway 79, the tornado then turned to the north and downed transmission lines about 6

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jul 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from July 06, 2015 to July 06, 2015. Affected areas: Oconto, Shawano, Waupaca. Episode summary: Three tornadoes formed as showers, with no lightning and with heavy rain, developed from southwest to northeast ahead of a cold front. Details: A tornado formed and heavily damaged a barn (DI 1, DOD 6) and adjacent garage. The roof of a nearby house was damaged and windows of another were broken (DI 2, DOD 3 and 4). At least two dozen trees were uprooted or snapped (DI 27 and 28, DOD 3 and 4). Average path width was 50 yards. A brief, weak tornado tore off part of a barn roof (DI 1, DOD 2) and sent wooden pallets into a nearby field. Another tornado formed and produced mainly light damage along its two mile path. The tornado uprooted or snapped at least 20 trees (DI 27 and 28, DOD 3 and 4) and caused minor damage to a house (DI 2, DOD 2). Reported property and crop damage: about $115,000.

text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 05, 2015 to May 06, 2015. Affected areas: Bastrop, Lee, Travis, Williamson. Episode summary: Heavy rain began in the Austin area and east during the evening of May 5th, persisting through the early morning of the 6th. Multiple flash flood reports were received. Details: Water was inundated at least one home in the city of Bastrop. Numerous road closures were also ongoing in the city. Numerous roads closed and water was reported in homes in extreme eastern parts of Williamson county. Numerous reports of flooding on roadways in the town of Lexington. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 11, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 11, 2015 to May 12, 2015. Affected areas: Calhoun, Duval, Live Oak, Nueces, San Patricio, Webb. Episode summary: A frontal boundary stalled north of the South Texas region during the morning hours on May 11th. Scattered thunderstorms developed in the afternoon over the Brush Country. A supercell thunderstorm was nearly stationary over southern Duval County for several hours. This caused flash flooding in the evening. A strong upper level disturbance moved out of northern Mexico during the evening hours. A mesoscale convective system developed over the higher terrain in northeast Mexico in the evening hours. The storm complex moved southeast across the Brush Country and into the Coastal Bend during the overnight hours. Flash flooding and damaging winds occurred from Duval County toward the southern Coastal Bend during the morning hours of May 12th. The severe winds caused power outages to as many as twenty five thousand customers across the southern Coastal Bend. Details: Low lying areas within the community of Bruni were flooded due to 5 inches of rainfall. Water was flowing down the streets. Several roads were flooded in central Nueces County. A spotter reported water flowing over the road on Farm to Market 43 near the intersection with Farm to Market Road 665. The road was impassable. Road was closed on Highway 44 near Clarkwood due to water over the road. Numerous roads were flooded in Port Aransas. Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

Many roads in the city of La Pryor, including Highway 83 and 57 were closed due to water over the road. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Flood: Texas, Jul 06, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from July 06, 2015 to July 07, 2015. Affected areas: Childress, Crosby, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Lubbock, Lynn. Episode summary: Multiple rounds of late-day thunderstorms developed across the South Plains and southern Texas Panhandle on the sixth followed by additional bouts through the pre-dawn hours of the seventh. These storms drifted slowly eastward, many with swaths of one to two inches of rainfall with each round. Storm total rain amounts were estimated around four inches in some parts of Crosby, Garza and Childress Counties before daybreak on the seventh. Several roads had flooded stretches across the eastern South Plains northeast to Childress County. The greatest monetary impact of these heavy rains was dealt to area crops as thousands of acres of milo, cotton and some corn suffered varying degrees of damage from flooding. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,250,000.

title: Flood: Texas, Jul 09, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from July 09, 2015 to July 09, 2015. Affected areas: Cochran. Episode summary: A slow-moving line of thunderstorms exited eastern New Mexico this evening and produced heavy rainfall and strong winds across the western South Plains and southwest Texas Panhandle. Severe winds from a microburst were measured at Lazbuddie. In Cochran County, training storms for nearly three hours produced an estimated four to six inches of rain in a swath about seven miles west of Morton and Lehman. Late this night, Texas Department of Transportation reported all roads in northern Cochran County had flooded stretches with some sections of Highway 114 closed due to two feet of standing water. A portion of Farm-to-Market Road 1169 southwest of Morton suffered some damage and was flooded for four days. Reported property and crop damage: about $600,000.

title: Flood: Texas, Jul 10, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from July 10, 2015 to July 10, 2015. Affected areas: Hockley, Lubbock. Episode summary: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms moved northeast late this afternoon and evening over much of the South Plains. An area from southeast Hockley County to the city of Lubbock saw these storms repeatedly take aim through the evening resulting in widespread flooding of streets, roads and playa lakes. Although most rainfall amounts in the flooded area were only one to two inches, rounds of heavy rains earlier in the week made for waterlogged soils. Rainfall of nearly 4.5 inches in southeast Hockley County caused portions of Farm-to-Market Road 1585 to be covered in two feet of water with currents of mud making travel nearly impossible.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 17, 2015 to May 17, 2015. Affected areas: Bastrop, Bexar, Burnet, Caldwell, Comal, Edwards, Guadalupe, Hays, Kendall, Travis, Williamson. Episode summary: A line of thunderstorms with heavy rainfall produced flash flooding across South Central Texas during the overnight hours and into the early afternoon. Details: In Round Rock TX on Sunday afternoon 4:40 PM, May 17 , a 38 year old male drowned in Brushy Creek near Chisholm Trail. His 4 year old daughter had left a gathering at a park and wondered in the creek area and tried to cross a small dam. When the father tried to go after her, they both fell into the swollen creek. The daughter was thrown to safety, the father drowned. Although the creek was not in Multiple road closures were reported across Comal County. Closures included River Road South, Hueco Springs Loop, Smithson Valley Road North, Rolling Creek, Fawn Lane, Cypress Cove Road, and Spring Branch Road. A few citizens had to be lead away from a van stranded in high water on Hoffman Lane. Several roads across the county were reported to have 3 to 4 inches of water over them. Road closures included Cole Springs Road and Goforth Road in the city of Kyle. Reported property and crop damage: about $70,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 13, 2015 to May 13, 2015. Affected areas: Denton, Erath, Hamilton, Hood, Mills, Parker. Episode summary: Thunderstorms produced flooding across a few of the central and western counties of north Texas. Details: The Mills County Sheriff's Department reported water over the intersection of FM 573 and CR 186. The Erath County Sheriff's Department reported water on southbound Hwy 377 near County Road 195. Problems were also reported on FM 847, FM 914, FM 1702, and CR 251. Granbury PD reported that streets were collecting water across the city. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 17, 2015 to May 17, 2015. Affected areas: Collin, Dallas, Johnson, Tarrant. Episode summary: Isolated thunderstorms produced localized flooding and a few reports of severe weather during the middle part of May, 2015. Details: Fort Worth Police Department reported that the creek was out of its banks and water was over Winscot Plover Road. Broadcast media reported that widespread flooding was occurring across the eastern part of the county; especially along HWY 157. Dallas Police Department reported widespread flooding from Grand Prairie North to Cockrell Hill and Irving, with numerous road closures in place.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 18, 2015 to May 18, 2015. Affected areas: Bexar, Fayette, Gonzales. Episode summary: Thunderstorms developed early in the morning producing flash flooding across the eastern areas of the county warning area. These storms exited the area by mid morning. More storms developed in the evening as well across the Edwards Plateau and Hill Country. Details: Water was reported over the roadway at Interstate 10 and the Gonzales and Fayette county line. A report of a semi-truck sliding off a roadway due to high water, and a high water rescue in the city of Gonzales were received but no additional details given. On Monday May 18th around 8:50 AM, a woman died in her Honda SUV after her vehicle was swept off a flooded road and lodged underneath a small bridge on the other side of the highway. This happened on the southwest side of San Antonio along the I-35 frontage road near Cassin Road. The vehicle drove around a barricade onto the flooded access road which was at least 2-3 feet underwater. Her body was Roads at Highway 95 and 609 were closed due to high water. Also, a number of low water crossings within the city of Flatonia had water flowing over them. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 19, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 19, 2015 to May 19, 2015. Affected areas: Lee. Episode summary: Some isolated, sub-severe storms developed in the late morning resulting in multiple reports of funnel clouds and one brief touchdown in the city of Giddings. Details: A high end EF-0 tornado touched down damaging a Ramada Hotel on Highway 290 east of the city of Giddings. Most of the damage consisted of uprooted trees rooted in wet soils while other damage included a destroyed outbuilding, whose debris were lofted into the Ramada Hotel causing window and roof damage to the hotel. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 21, 2015 to May 21, 2015. Affected areas: Burnet, Dimmit, Llano, Maverick, Uvalde, Williamson. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall resulted in flash flooding in the Hill Country and Edwards Plateau as well as the southern Rio Grande Valley during the early morning hours. Details: The intersection of Highway 83 and FM 1407 and also Loop 517 were reportedly flooded. Highway 85 was reportedly flooded at the bridge crossing the Nueces River. Highway 481 was reported closed due to flooding.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 08, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 08, 2015 to May 08, 2015. Affected areas: Haskell, Throckmorton. Episode summary: A nearly stationary upper level low over southern California was the mechanism that caused upper level disturbances to move across West Central Texas. These upper level disturbances interacted with outflow boundaries, daytime heating, and very unstable air to produce severe weather over the three day period which included large hail, damaging winds and tornadoes. Details: The sheriff's office reported a tornado about 1 mile north of Throckmorton. A trained spotter reported a tornado through the Haskell County Sheriff's office about 3.7 miles east of O'Brien. The public reported a tornado about 13 miles northwest of Throckmorton.

title: Wildfire: California, May 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Wildfire, from May 07, 2015 to May 07, 2015. Affected areas: Morongo Basin. Episode summary: Strong winds spread a vegetation fire in Yucca Valley to a house. Details: Strong winds (estimated gusts 30 knots) spread a vegetation fire to a house in Yucca Valley. Reported property and crop damage: about $30,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jun 10, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from June 10, 2015 to June 12, 2015. Affected areas: Inyo, San Bernardino. Episode summary: An unusually late-season low pressure system combined with unusually early-season deep subtropical moisture to fuel scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Some storms produced flash flooding, and isolated wind damage also occurred. Details: Water, mud, and debris flowed over Highway 190. A traffic collision in the flooded area injured two people (indirect). Rocks and debris were over Highway 190 near Father Crowley Point. Water, rocks, and debris flowed over Linn Road and Belfield Boulevard. A nearby spotter reported half an inch of rain in less than half an hour. Reported property and crop damage: about $3,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jun 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from June 30, 2015 to June 30, 2015. Affected areas: Inyo. Episode summary: An early season push of monsoon moisture fueled isolated thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Spotty high winds and flash flooding occurred. Details: Rocks and mud washed over Death Valley Road in several locations near the intersection of Highway 168. Reported property and crop damage: about $2,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 30, 2015 to May 30, 2015. Affected areas: Bexar, Caldwell, Comal, De Witt, Hays, Kinney, Travis. Episode summary: A complex of thunderstorms producing some wind damage, small hail, and eventually flash flooding moved into the western county warning area in the late morning hours. The system intensified and expanded in coverage as it progressed eastward through the afternoon hours resulting in flash flooding for much of the area. The system exited during the late evening hours. Details: Farm to market road 1863 was closed in both directions due to water over the roadway. Information provided by www.drivetexas.org. Multiple roads closed across Hays County. Hugo Road was reportedly closed due to flowing water over the roadway. The intersection of Leslie Road and Braun Road was closed due to water over the roadway. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 23, 2015 to May 23, 2015. Affected areas: Kimble. Episode summary: Isolated severe storms formed by late afternoon, resulting in isolated hail and flash flooding. Details: US Highway 377 had six feet of water over the road near South Llano State Park.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 12, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 12, 2015 to May 13, 2015. Affected areas: Brazoria, Galveston, Harris, Liberty. Episode summary: Slow moving thunderstorms produced copious amounts of rain that led to flash flooding for some locations. Communities of Webster, San Leon and Angleton were hardest hit. Details: There was widespread flooding around League City. Several roads were impassable due to high water. Widespread flooding was reported with water in homes in Angleton. Roads were flooded in and around the Dayton area, including FM 321. Reported property and crop damage: about $895,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 13, 2015 to May 13, 2015. Affected areas: Duval, Jim Wells, Nueces, Victoria, Webb. Episode summary: A stalled front along with abundant moisture and an upper level disturbance produced heavy rainfall across many areas of the Coastal Bend on May 13th, 2015. Average rain amounts of 3 to 4 inches fell with isolated amounts between 6 to 8 inches during the morning of the 13th on the south side of Corpus Christi including Flour Bluff, North Padre Island, and Mustang Island. This rainfall came on the heels of another heavy rain event, that occurred in the previous two days. ||Many streets and subdivisions in Corpus Christi were flooded. Some roads were even closed for a portion of the day. Many Corpus Christi schools delayed classes due to the widespread flooding. Similar conditions occurred in Orange Grove, Agua Dulce, and Freer. ||Several thunderstorms throughout the morning and afternoon hours exhibited signs of rotation. There were several reported funnel clouds across the area. One brief tornado touchdown was reported around 20 miles southwest of Freer in northern Webb County. Details: Tornado touched down over open country southwest of Freer. Widespread flooding occurred across the northwest portion of Nueces County affecting the communities of Agua Dulce and Banquete. Farm to Market Road 666 from just south of Bluntzer to Banquete was closed due to flooding along with FM 624 west of Bluntzer. Numerous county roads were closed from south of Agua Dulce to west of Bluntzer. Water reached several homes and businesses in Agua Dulce. Orange Water flowed over Highway 16 just south of Freer. Highway 44 east of Freer was flooded. Reported property and crop damage: about $350,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 25, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 25, 2015 to May 26, 2015. Affected areas: Austin, Brazos, Colorado, Fort Bend, Grimes, Harris, Houston, Liberty, Madison, San Jacinto, Walker, Waller and 1 more areas. Episode summary: Across already very saturated grounds, a slow moving line of thunderstorms moved into Harris County from central Texas during the evening hours of the 25th. Very heavy rainfall began in the mid evening hours across the northern portions of the county, while additional thunderstorms developed over central Fort Bend County and moved into Harris County from the southwest. A period of thunderstorm cell training occurred from around 10 PM to 1 AM from Fort Bend County into north-central Harris County where the cells merged with the line of storms moving southward from northern Harris County. Thunderstorm cell mergers continued over central and southwest Harris County for several hours resulting in widespread significant flooding. The Houston/Galveston National Weather Service Office issued their first ever Flash Flood Emergency for this event. The area's worst flooding was focused across the western portion of Harris County from the northwest side of the City of Houston to Addicks to Sharpstown to Richmond in central Fort Bend County. Hundreds of water rescues (mainly motorists stranded on area freeways and roadways) were performed by various agencies during the height of the rainfall. After daylight on the 26th, the Houston Fire Department responded to many requests for assistance of residences in flooded homes. Seven fatalities were directly related and one additional fatality was indirectly related to the flooding. Three fatalities resulted from the capsizing of a Houston Fire Department rescue boat in Brays Bayou and the other four were all flooded vehicle related. Reported property and crop damage: about $26,015,000.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 08, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 08, 2015 to May 08, 2015. Affected areas: Wichita, Wilbarger. Episode summary: Another round of storms developed across the Texas panhandle and developed into a line as it moved eastward across western north Texas. Details: A storm chaser and a law enforcement officer reported a brief tornado estimated to be 10 miles west-northwest of Vernon. No damage was reported. Law enforcement and a storm chaser reported a tornado that moved from approximately 4 miles northwest of Lockett to near Lockett. Trees were damaged and the roof was damage from a metal building (DI 21; DOD 3). A storm chaser observed a tornado approximately 3 miles north-northeast of Haynesville. The tornado produced minor damage to a metal outbuilding.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 18, 2015 to May 18, 2015. Affected areas: Austin, Colorado, Grimes, Houston, Trinity, Washington. Episode summary: Slow moving thunderstorms formed along a boundary in a very moist air mass. These produced locally heavy rainfall and areas of flooding. Details: Roads were flooded between the Navasota and Shiro areas, including the intersection of FM 302 and FM 362, FM 234, and parts of Highway 6 south of Navasota. Street flooding was reported in and around the Brenham area. Street flooding was reported in and around Columbus, including Fannin Street that was closed due to high water.

Details: A fast moving tornado briefly touched down at two points in southwest Houston. There was damage to a storage facility along and just west of Gessner Road, an apartment complex, and an office building. title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jul 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from July 18, 2015 to July 18, 2015. Affected areas: Dunn. Episode summary: A significant bow echo moved across Minnesota and then into west central Wisconsin during the early morning hours of Saturday, July 18th. These storms moved rapidly eastward, with numerous reports of downed trees and power lines. A few intense bow echo segments produced damage to sheds and outbuildings. One of the stronger storms produced an EF-1 tornado near Eau Galle. Details: A storm survey indicated an EF-1 occurred near Eau Galle, Wisconsin. The EF-1 tornado formed one mile northwest of Eau Galle, and continued generally east to four miles east of Eau Galle. Most of the damage was down trees and power lines. The greatest damage occurred just north of Eau Galle, where trees were snapped and uprooted, and a home weather station reported a maximum wind gust of 88 mph. text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 09, 2015 to May 09, 2015. Affected areas: Wichita. title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 23, 2015 to May 24, 2015. Affected areas: Cameron, Zapata. Episode summary: A QLCS rolled across all of Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley during the overnight hours of May 23rd/24th. The line tore through southern Zapata County between 9 and 10 pm on the 23rd, with wind speeds of 60 to 70 mph or more possible. The line quickly lost its punch tracking across Starr and Jim Hogg counties. However, rain added up to an inch or so for many areas, and totaled more than two inches in areas of north of Edinburg, still dealing with drainage issues from events two weeks prior. Between 2 and 3 am, the line entered Cameron County and became reinvigorated by low level convergence from east southeast winds from the Gulf of Mexico. At the same time, the line slowed dramatically, with a few stronger cells tracking over the same areas for a two to three hour period. Three to four inches of rain fell across most of Brownsville, with pockets of 5 to 6 inches over the west side, including River Bend Golf Resort, which saw widespread road, drainage, and Resaca flooding. An estimated four to five inches fell east of Brownsville. High water continued through mid to late morning in many areas of southern Cameron County as rains slowly diminished. Details: Zapata County Sheriffs Office reported knee high water over the roads in the Medina addition and between Miraflores and Highway 83 in Zapata due to swollen arroyos. Pockets of 5 to 6 inches of rain fell over the west side of Brownsville, including the River Bend Golf Resort, which saw widespread road, drainage, and Resaca flooding. title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 15, 2015 to May 15, 2015. Affected areas: Hidalgo, Willacy. Episode summary: A robust squall line marching across the Coastal Bend early in the afternoon sent surface boundaries propagating south aiding in the development of thunderstorm clusters, first near previously flooded Falfurrias, but soon would extend down U.S. 281 into portions of Brooks and Hidalgo counties that had already received more than half a foot of rain May11th and 12th. While most of the downpours held across northern Hidalgo County, enough additional rainfall would fall near Edinburg to exacerbate flood concerns in Faysville, where pumping operations would be forced to continue well into the following week (week of May 18th). An estimated four to eight inches of rain fell from northeast Hidalgo County and across Kenedy County. Two or more inches fell between 430 and 530 pm across Raymondville causing nuisance urban flooding. Details: Hidalgo County EM reported the evacuation of one home in San Manuel due to water getting into the house near Highway 281. Water rescues were also reported along FM 186 near Linn - San Manuel. Willacy County EM reported that in Raymondville, Hidalgo Street from 4th Street to 10th Street had water across from curb to curb and that the city was closing the road. Reported property and crop damage: about $20,000.

title: Flood: Texas, May 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from May 13, 2015 to May 14, 2015. Affected areas: Brooks. Episode summary: Although the weather had quieted down, a second wave of flooding washed over parts of Falfurrias, due to Palo Blanco Creek overspilling its banks. This caused road closures on Travis Street near Falfurrias High school during the late morning and early afternoon of May 13th. Some of the flooding may have been indirectly caused from upstream rainfall in northern Duval County that morning, where an estimated 5 to 8 inches of rain fell. Details: Brooks County EM reported several intersections along Travis Street being blocked off on the north side of Falfurrias due to flooding from the rising Palo Blanco Creek. Falfurrias High School reported water entering a home on North Palo Blanco due to creek rises. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 11, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 11, 2015 to May 11, 2015. Affected areas: Bastrop, Lee, Maverick, Val Verde. Episode summary: An upper level trough moved through the southern plains and a cold front pushed into South Central Texas. These features acted on a moist, unstable airmass in the warm sector developing thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced heavy rain, large hail, and damaging wind gusts. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing multiple low water crossings in the Paige area. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain totaling 3.5 inches. This led to localized flooding in Lexington. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding near Lions Park in Del Rio.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 19, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 19, 2015 to July 19, 2015. Affected areas: Riverside. Episode summary: The combination of lingering tropical moisture from former hurricane Dolores and a weather disturbance moving into southern California led to intense thunderstorms with torrential rainfall across portions of eastern Riverside county during the afternoon hours on July 19th. A cluster of slow moving thunderstorms near and just to the west of Desert Center produced more than 6 inches of rain along Interstate 10; the heavy rain caused significant flash flooding which washed out the eastbound lanes of the freeway. At this location, the interstate crossed a wash, and the flowing water raging through the wash collapsed the bridge across it. One vehicle drove into the wash; fortunately the driver was rescued and there were no fatalities. In addition, the flooding also eroded the westbound lanes of the freeway and as a result, Interstate 10 was closed indefinitely in both directions. Details: Aided by lingering tropical moisture from former hurricane Dolores, intense thunderstorms with torrential rain developed near Desert Center during the afternoon hours on July 19th. Based on radar estimates, over 6 inches of rain fell over several hours along and just to the south of Interstate 10, just to the west of Desert Center. title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, May 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 30, 2015 to May 30, 2015. Affected areas: Hidalgo, Starr. Episode summary: The combination of an approaching late season front, warm humid air, light winds that allowed an afternoon sea breeze to develop, and boundaries from storms moving south from Del Rio and Laredo set the stage for multicell thunderstorm clusters to fire, mainly from northwest Cameron and eastern Hidalgo counties westward to the Rio Grande Plains during the mid to late afternoon, which carried into the early evening. Stronger cells produced an estimated 3 to 4 inches just north of the Rio Grande in the San Juan/Alamo area, and another measured 4 inches in Rio Grande City. The torrential rain pockets left a combination of urban and more life and property threatening flash flooding, in both the San Juan/Alamo area, where the rain overwhelmed septic systems and flooded streets with known poor drainage with at least 3 feet of water, and near Rio Grande City, where U.S. 83 was flooded near Garceno, and at least one home was evacuated from floodwaters near Escobares around 7 pm. Other heavy rains, estimated up to 4 to 5 inches, fell over open ranchlands of eastern Zapata and central Brooks counties. Details: Public reported numerous roadways covered in water ranging from 7 inches to 3 feet across San Juan and Alamo, mainly south of Expressway U.S. 83. Starr County Sheriffs Office reported that a home had to be evacuated due to flooding along Lolo Flores Road in Escobares, as well standing water on roadways. La Joya COOP observer reported 1.30 inches of rainfall and minor street flooding north of La Joya. Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 13, 2015 to May 13, 2015. Affected areas: Bastrop, Edwards, Lee, Maverick, Uvalde, Val Verde, Wilson. Episode summary: An upper level trough moved out of the southwest United States and a weak warm front moved northward through South Central Texas. These combined to induce thunderstorms in a warm, moist airmass. Some of these storms produced heavy rain and damaging wind gusts. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing low water crossings on FM 1051 west of Concan, on FM 187 north of Sabinal, and on State Hwy 127 northwest of Sabinal. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing numerous roads in and around Elgin including Old Sayer Rd., FM 812 near the county line, Woody Ln. at FM 1704, and Young Prairie at FM 1704. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing FM 674 southwest of Rocksprings.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 27, 2015 to May 27, 2015. Affected areas: Blanco, Travis. Episode summary: An upper level shortwave trough moved through southwesterly flow over Texas. This disturbance provided sufficient lift to initiate isolated convection. Some of these storms produced weak tornadoes, large hail, and heavy rain. Details: A thunderstorm produced a brief, weak tornado just east of Hwy 281 near the Little Blanco River. No damage was reported. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding closing low water crossings on Joe Tanner Ln. and Old Bee Caves Rd.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 28, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 28, 2015 to May 29, 2015. Affected areas: Bexar, Burnet, Comal, Kerr. Episode summary: Convection initiated over west Texas as an upper level shortwave trough moved through the pattern. These thunderstorms eventually formed into a squall line that moved across South Central Texas. This line of storms produced damaging wind gusts and heavy rain. Details: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing multiple low water crossings on FM 1340 west of Hunt. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding making two lanes impassable on westbound Grissom Rd. from Timber Path. Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding closing numerous low water crossings in Marble Falls.

title: Tornado: Texas, May 16, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Tornado, from May 16, 2015 to May 16, 2015. Affected areas: Archer, Hardeman, Wilbarger. Episode summary: With an upper low traversing the region, a cold front stationed over the panhandles, and a developing dryline, storms developed out in the panhandles early on the 16th and made their way eastward across western north Texas through the day. Toward evening, when the severe weather occurred, the front surged eastward with a line of storms forming along it. Details: The tornado that began in northeast Hardeman County moved through the far northwest corner of Wilbarger County before crossing the Red River into Jackson County Oklahoma. No damage was known to have occurred in this rural area Wilbarger County. The tornado crossed from Jackson County Oklahoma into far northern Wilbarger County between Odell TX and Elmer OK, before crossing the Red River for the third time back into Jackson County Oklahoma. Again, no damage is known to have occurred in this portion of Wilbarger County. A video of a waterspout over Lake Diversion was relayed from a resident through KFDX TV. No damage was reported.

title: Flood: Texas, Jul 20, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from July 20, 2015 to July 20, 2015. Affected areas: Castro, Swisher. Episode summary: Scattered to numerous slow-moving thunderstorms developed this afternoon across the southern Texas Panhandle and northern South Plains. In addition to producing torrential rains and flooding over much of Castro County, winds gusted to 58 mph near Friona from a microburst. Rainfall was measured at 4.40 inches by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet near Dimmitt, 2.47 inches by an NWS COOP observer in Hart, and 3.1 inches by the public in Kress. Several roads in Castro and southern Swisher County had flooded stretches and varying degrees of crop damage were observed from heavy soil erosion and standing water. By the evening, torrential rains focused about 12 miles northeast of Silverton where radar estimated as much as eight inches of accumulated rainfall. Despite these impressive amounts, reports of flash flooding and definitive rain amounts were unavailable over this otherwise open ranch land. Reported property and crop damage: about $300,000.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 19, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 19, 2015 to May 20, 2015. Affected areas: Archer, Clay, Wichita. Episode summary: Severe storms developed near a stalled boundary across Oklahoma and the panhandles and moved eastward through the afternoon and evening of the 19th. Details: Spotters observed a tornado a about 7 miles northeast of Harrold in northwestern Wichita County. No damage was reported. A tornado was observed in far southeastern Archer County approximately 11 miles south of Windthorst. No damage was reported. Numerous spotters and law enforcement officers observed a tornado north of Buffalo Lake to the northwest of Iowa Park. No damage was reported. Reported property and crop damage: about $500,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jun 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from June 15, 2015 to June 16, 2015. Affected areas: Scurry. Episode summary: A weak low pressure system slowly drifted east into the Great Plains with a trailing upper level disturbance rotating around the backside of the upper low. As the disturbance moved over the region, it brought thunderstorms to West Texas. Instability and shear were weak, but the high moisture content across the area caused flash flooding to develop as a line of storms moved across the Permian Basin. Details: A thunderstorm produced 6-12 inches of water over portions of Highway 84 in northwestern Scurry County about 2 miles southeast of the Scurry and Garza County line. A thunderstorm that produced heavy rainfall caused FM 1269 from Fluvanna to the Garza County line and FM 612 from Fluvanna to 5 miles east of Fluvanna to be impassable due to high water. Reported property and crop damage: about $700.

title: High Wind: California, May 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: High Wind, from May 07, 2015 to May 07, 2015. Affected areas: Sw S.J. Valley. Episode summary: An upper level low moved across the northern Sierra-Nevada Range, bringing breezy winds and scattered thunderstorms. Details: The NWS owned APRS station at Sunflower Valley recorded a 63 MPH gust.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, Jun 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from June 17, 2015 to June 18, 2015. Affected areas: Hardin, Jasper, Jefferson, Newton. Episode summary: Tropical Storm Bill moved into the Central Texas coast during the 16th. Moisture continued to stream north across Southeast Texas during the 17th and 18th leading to flooding. Details: Heavy rain trained across southern and central sections of Newton County for several hours on already saturated soil. This produced roadways that were flooded out and closed for many hours. Heavy rain during the 17th produced flash flooding in south and central sections on Newton County. Multiple roads remained closed from Bon Wier to the southwest into the 18th as flood waters slowly drained. The heavy rain and flash flood event from the 17th lingered into the early morning of the 18th. Flood waters remained across southern sections of Jasper County through the morning of the 18th with many roadways remaining closed as the water slowly drained. Reported property and crop damage: about $203,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, May 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from May 14, 2015 to May 15, 2015. Affected areas: Fresno. Episode summary: An upper level low moved onto the central California coast the morning of the 14th, with the bulk of the storms energy moving through Kern County. As the system moved through the area on the 14th thunderstorms developed across the Southern and Central San Joaquin Valley, which brought heavy rainfall. This resulted in some street flooding in the Bakersfield and Fresno areas. Details: A thunderstorm moved over the Fresno area producing a few tenths of an inch a short period of time. This heavy rainfall was compounded with poor drainage which lead to areas of curb to curb flooding, one road closure at an underpass where water was multiple feet deep, and flood waters entering buildings.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 15, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 15, 2015 to May 15, 2015. Affected areas: Bee, Duval, Kleberg, La Salle, Live Oak, Mcmullen, Nueces, San Patricio, Victoria, Webb. Episode summary: Abundant moisture over the region along with a potent upper level disturbance created another severe weather and heavy rain event across South Texas on May 15th. Around daybreak, storms moved into La Salle and McMullen counties where tornadoes produced damage near Woodward. The storms continued to the east and drifted southward with widespread 2 to 3 inches of rain across La Salle, McMullen, Live Oak and Bee counties. Flooding occurred near the cities of Cotulla, Encinal, George West, and Beeville. The storms tapped into even more moisture from the Gulf of Mexico along the coast and expanded into a strong squall line. Two tornadoes occurred in the Coastal Bend at Corpus Christi and at Gregory. The damage was primarily confined to a business on the south side of Corpus Christi. Three injuries occurred near Gregory when a construction trailor flipped at a construction site. Details: Cotulla Fire Department and spotter reported high water on Farm to Market Road 468 just northwest of Cotulla. Flooding of roads occurred in Three Rivers. St. Mary's Street and Moser Avenue were barricaded. Farm to Market Road 624 was closed from Cotulla to the county line due to water over the road. Reported property and crop damage: about $495,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 20, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 20, 2015 to July 20, 2015. Affected areas: Siskiyou. Episode summary: Heavy rains associated with a severe thunderstorm caused flooding in and around Grenada California. Details: Yreka Dispatch reported at 20/1955 PST that homes were flooded in Grenada and that the Shepherd Of God Assisted Living Center was being evacuated due to water entering the building. CHP reported standing water and debris near the I-5 southbound on-ramp at 20/1919 PST along with lots of debris on the southbound side of Old Highway 99. At 20/1925 PST, they reported that the on-ramp was blocked by

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 21, 2015 to July 21, 2015. Affected areas: Siskiyou. Episode summary: Heavy rains associated with strong thunderstorms caused flooding in and around McCloud California. Details: The Siskiyou County Sheriff's Department reported Flash Flooding in the Mud Creek Basin northeast of McCloud at 21/2020 PST. They also reported Flash Flooding in the city of McCloud due to runoff from heavy rainfall.

title: Tornado: Wisconsin, Jul 13, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Wisconsin: Tornado, from July 13, 2015 to July 13, 2015. Affected areas: Richland. Episode summary: Severe thunderstorms moved across portions of western Wisconsin during the afternoon and early evening of July 13th. A small, short-lived tornado developed from one of these storms as it tracked across Lone Rock (Richland County). One house sustained roof damage and had two large trees blown down onto it. Other trees were snapped off about 20 feet above the ground. The storms also dropped large hail through the afternoon and evening, generally north of Interstate 90. The largest hail reported was tennis ball sized near Osseo (Trempealeau County) where the hail cracked the sky lights on a home. Damaging winds occurred with the storms across southwest Wisconsin with trees and power lines blown down in Richland Center (Richland County) and Lone Rock. Details: A small, short-lived tornado produced roof damage and blew down two large trees onto a house in Lone Rock. Other trees were snapped off about 20 feet above the ground. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 04, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 04, 2015 to May 04, 2015. Affected areas: Hudspeth. Episode summary: A weak upper low was located over Arizona with a surface low and trough near the Rio Grande Valley. Deep moisture was located east of the surface low with dew points well into the 50s. Heavy rain fell in the Dell City area with a report of flash flooding just south of town. Details: TXDOT out of Dell City reported 1 foot of water on highway 1437 two miles south of town.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: Texas, Jun 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from June 30, 2015 to June 30, 2015. Affected areas: Ector, Midland. Episode summary: A complex of thunderstorms known as a Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) moved through the Western Low Rolling Plains and into the Permian Basin during the early morning hours. The complex of thunderstorms was aided by an upper level trough over the Mississippi Valley which provided upper level divergence and lift over the area. A southerly low level jet was also present helping to maintain the storms. Since copious amount of moisture were available, rainfall rates were high with this system. These conditions resulted in storms that produced flash flooding and severe wind gusts. Details: A complex of storms moved across Midland County and produced flash flooding in and around the City of Midland. One foot of water was reported to be running over the service road on Business 20 just outside of Midland. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. A complex of thunderstorms moved across Midland County and produced heavy rain that resulted in flash flooding in and around the City of Midland. Several feet of water were reported at the intersection of 1788 and Business 20 which resulted in four vehicles being stranded some of which the water was up to the auto windows. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Heavy rain of 1.94 inches was measured at Midland Air and Space Port as a complex of thunderstorms moved across Midland County. Most of the rain fell between 4:30 am to 5:00 am CDT. Reported property and crop damage: about $19,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 21, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 21, 2015 to May 21, 2015. Affected areas: Nueces, San Patricio, Webb. Episode summary: A cold front moved into South Texas during the early morning hours of May 21st. Early morning thunderstorms produced flash flooding in the Laredo area. Scattered thunderstorms formed along the cold front during the afternoon over the coastal plains. The storms produced flash flooding in the Coastal Bend during the afternoon. Roads were flooded in Corpus Christi, Portland, Gregory, and Port Aransas. Details: Many streets were flooded in Portland with water reaching the sidewalks in some |areas. Frontage roads along Highway 181 were flooded from Buddy Ganem Drive in Portland to Gregory. Highway 35 service road in Gregory was flooded with several cars stalled in high water. Flooding occurred along Reynolds Street in Taft. Water was high enough to reach half way up fire hydrants. Public relayed pictures of flooding in Port Aransas. Reported property and crop damage: about $300,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 22, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 22, 2015 to May 22, 2015. Affected areas: Aransas. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms moved across the Mid-Coast region during the morning hours on May 22nd. Localized heavy rain caused flooding near the Aransas Wildlife Refuge. Details: Water flooded some of the roads leading to the Aransas National Wildlife Refuge entrance.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 23, 2015 to May 24, 2015. Affected areas: Nueces, Webb. Episode summary: A strong upper level disturbance moved out of northeast Mexico during the evening of the 23rd and into South Texas on the morning of the 24th. As the system reached northeast Mexico, a line of strong thunderstorms formed during the afternoon hours of the 23rd. The line of storms moved east across Laredo and then through the Brush Country during the evening hours. The storms produced flash flooding in Laredo. The line of thunderstorms intensified during the early morning hours of the 24th when it reached the Coastal Bend. The storms caused damage to trees and power lines across the Coastal Bend. Details: Portions of Sara Road were flooded with vehicles stalled on the north side of Laredo. A motorist was stranded in high water near the intersection of Park Drive and Taylor Street in the central portion of Laredo. The tornado touched down near Cunningham Middle School just north of Golihar Road where trees were snapped and uprooted. A residence just north of the school at the corner of Hudson and Stafford Streets sustained moderate roof damage and a had a fence blown down. The tornado continued to the northeast crossing Horne Road and parallel to Sarita Street. Dozens of trees were snapped and uprooted with Brawner Parkway from Kostoryz Road to Devon Drive was flooded. Reported property and crop damage: about $800,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 25, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 25, 2015 to May 25, 2015. Affected areas: Live Oak. Episode summary: A strong upper level disturbance moved across the central and northern portions of Texas on May 25th. A large convective complex formed over north Texas in the afternoon and surged southeast toward the middle and upper Texas coast during the evening hours. The southern end of the line moved across the northern Coastal Bend and Victoria Crossroads. Quarter sized hail occurred near George West, Beeville, and Schroeder. Details: Water flowed across the roadway on Farm to Market Road 889 west of George West.

title: Dust Storm, Tornado: Texas, May 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Dust Storm, Tornado, from May 27, 2015 to May 27, 2015. Affected areas: Carson, Hemphill. Episode summary: One of the more active severe weather days of the spring season brought large hail, bigger than baseballs in some cases, flooding, and tornadoes to the Texas Panhandle. One persistent intense supercell moved slowly across Hemphill County near Canadian and produced three tornadoes, one of which caused three injuries and was rated EF-2. Flooding from this slow moving storm closed Highway 83 north of Canadian during the evening. More flooding occurred further south in Armstrong County which caused road closures. Details: This tornado was reported by multiple storm chasers and also touched down within the damage path of the first EF-2 tornado. Eyewitness reports indicate that this tornado stayed over open fields and cause no additional damage. This was the first of two tornadoes that hit the same area within minutes. These tornadoes were documented on video within minutes of each other. It is nearly impossible to determine which tornado cause what damage but a swath of damage was noted, likely with some caused by each touchdown. Shortly after 4:30 PM CDT, outflow from thunderstorms moved north reaching Interstate 40 west of Groom. Despite recent rains, the wind was able to loft dust reducing visibility causing a multiple vehicle chain reaction accident eastbound near mile marker 102 involving one SUV and five tractor trailers. The accident resulted in one fatality.

title: Winter Weather: California, May 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Winter Weather, from May 07, 2015 to May 08, 2015. Affected areas: West Slope Northern Sierra Nevada. Episode summary: A low pressure system from the Pacific northwest dropped through the region bringing showers and thunderstorms, with up to 7 inches of new snow over the Sierra. Details: Snow caused slippery roads on mountains and passes above 6500 feet, with 7 inches of snow measured 3W of Shriner Lake Campground. This impacted mountain roads from Highway 50 southward, including Echo Summit on Highway 50, Carson Pass on Highway 88, Ebbetts Pass on Highway 4, and Sonora Pass on Highway 104.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 27, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 27, 2015 to May 27, 2015. Affected areas: Armstrong, Hemphill. Episode summary: Slow moving supercell thunderstorms brought heavy rain and flooding to two sections of the Texas Panhandle. One was near Canadian where water covered Highway 83 resulting in it's closure for a period on the evening of the 27th. The other area was in Armstrong County where some roads were closed. Details: Heavy rain from slow moving thunderstorms caused flooding on Highway 83 near Big Timber Creek. Two feet of water was reported across the highway by Law Enforcement. Highway 83 approximately 6 miles north of Canadian was closed due to the flash flooding. Slow moving thunderstorms producing very heavy rain caused flash flooding along Highway 207 approximately 6 miles east of Wayside. The heavy rain cause a mudslide along Highway 207 near the scenic overlook in Palo Duro Canyon. Other roads that were reportedly flooding include Farm to Market 285 near the curves in the road just west of Wayside.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, Jul 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from July 07, 2015 to July 07, 2015. Affected areas: Borden, Mitchell, Scurry. Episode summary: A weak cold front was bisecting the Permian Basin from northeast to southwest and a very slow moving upper level trough was over West Texas. These conditions, along with abundant moisture, resulted in storms that produced high rainfall rates and flash flooding across the northeastern Permian Basin. Details: Thunderstorms with heavy rain moved across Borden County in the morning hours and produced flash flooding. The fire department reported more than six inches of water over FM 1785 about 15 miles south southeast of Gail. Thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall moved across Scurry County in the morning hours and caused flash flooding in the city of Snyder. Emergency management reported that 28th street was flooded by Deep Creek and was barricaded off. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. A trained spotter reported two to three feet of water on FM 1982 five miles north of Lorraine. This flash flooding resulted from thunderstorms that moved across northern Mitchell County. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate. Reported property and crop damage: about $1,100.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 05, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 05, 2015 to July 06, 2015. Affected areas: Inyo, San Bernardino. Episode summary: Another push of monsoon moisture fueled more thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Significant flash flooding and isolated severe weather occurred. Details: Vehicles were stuck on Highway 190 near the Mesquite Sand Dunes with water half way up the tires. Water and mud flowed over Highway 395 4 miles S of Haiwee and also near the Coso Junction Rest Area. Water flooded the entire parking lot of the Amargosa Opera House and also entered the building. Reported property and crop damage: about $25,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 09, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 09, 2015 to July 09, 2015. Affected areas: Inyo. Episode summary: An unseasonable upper level low moving in from the Pacific helped trigger thunderstorms over eastern California and adjacent areas of western Nevada. Isolated severe weather and flash flooding occurred. Details: Debris washed over Highway 190 in Stovepipe Wells, mud and debris were over Highway 190 near the Panamint Springs Resort, severe flooding closed Panamint Valley Road, and mud and rocks were over Panamint Springs Road up to Panamint Pass. Reported property and crop damage: about $10,000.

title: Dust Storm, Flash Flood, Tornado: California, Jul 17, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Dust Storm, Flash Flood, Tornado, from July 17, 2015 to July 21, 2015. Affected areas: Death Valley National Park, Inyo, Morongo Basin, San Bernardino. Episode summary: A huge push of monsoon moisture from Hurricane Dolores fueled a major outbreak of flash flooding and severe weather in the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Details: Highway 168 was closed at Westgard Pass due to flooding and lots of debris in the road. A swift water rescue occurred on Highway 95 five miles south of the CA/NV state line. The highway was closed from I-40 to the state line. Visibility was below 1/4 mile in Joshua Tree. Reported property and crop damage: about $42,000.

title: Flash Flood: Texas, May 30, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, from May 30, 2015 to May 30, 2015. Affected areas: Bee, Webb. Episode summary: A front stalled over the Coastal Bend on the 30th. Scattered thunderstorms formed north of the boundary during the afternoon as an upper level disturbance approached from the west. Storms produced very heavy rainfall from the northern Coastal Bend to the Brush Country. Flash flooding occurred in Laredo and Beeville. Details: Many streets in Beeville were flooded. A water rescue was performed to pull a woman from a car in flood waters at Stamper Street and Alta Vista Boulevard. Major street flooding occurred in the central and southern portions of Laredo. Motorists were stranded at several intersections. Rainfall of 3 to 3 and half inches in an hour produced major flooding in the northern portions of Laredo. Flood waters were in several houses in Del Mar area of north Laredo. The North Creek shopping center at Del Mar and Interstate 35 had several cars with water to roof. Reported property and crop damage: about $425,000.

title: Flood: Texas, May 19, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flood, from May 19, 2015 to May 30, 2015. Affected areas: La Salle, Live Oak, Nueces. Episode summary: Periods of heavy rainfall occurred over the Nueces River watershed between May 11th and 16th. This led to major flooding on the Nueces River that continued downstream through the end of the month. Flooding affected the Cotulla area on May 22nd. With the amount of water moving toward Lake Corpus Christi, releases were increased to accommodate the incoming water. This led to major flooding downstream from the dam. This affected homes in the Calallen area from May 19th until the end of the month. Details: The Nueces River crested at 20.63 feet at Cotulla on the 23rd but was in major flood category from the 22nd to the 30th. The flooding caused several roads around Cotulla to be closed. The frontage road on Interstate 35 near the KOA campground was closed. Farm to Market Road 3408 and Valley Wells Road were closed. Major flooding occurred on the Nueces River from Three Rivers to downstream of George West from the 19th until the 24th. The Nueces River crested at 37.94 feet at Three Rivers on the 19th. Several county roads were closed. Homes in the River Creek Acres subdivision southeast of George West was flooded with several feet of water. Increased releases from Lake Corpus Christi led to major flooding downstream from the dam to near Calallen. The Nueces River crested at 8.7 feet at Calallen on the 24th. Homes along the Nueces River were flooded upstream from Calallen along County Road 73. Hazel Blazemore Park and Labonte Park were inundated. Reported property and crop damage: about $600,000.

title: Flash Flood, Flood: Texas, May 23, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Flood, from May 23, 2015 to May 23, 2015. Affected areas: Hardeman, Knox. Episode summary: Another round of severe storms and flooding pummeled the Southern Plains on the 23rd. Details: Texas Department of Transportation reports water over Highway 287 in Chillicothe. Several inches of water over area roads. Texas Dept of Transportation reports water over Highway 287 and on several area roads across the county.

title: Flash Flood, Tornado: Texas, May 28, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Flash Flood, Tornado, from May 28, 2015 to May 28, 2015. Affected areas: Archer, Foard, Wichita. Episode summary: Several rounds of severe storms brought flooding rains and damaging winds. Details: Highway 6 and several rural roads closed due to flooding with up to a foot of water over many roadways. Car half submerged and stranded. Report from Twitter. Highway 79 north of town covered in flood waters. Other area roads also flooded. Reported property and crop damage: about $88,000.

title: Heavy Rain: Texas, May 29, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for Texas: Heavy Rain, from May 29, 2015 to May 29, 2015. Affected areas: Zapata. Episode summary: A line of thunderstorms eased into the northern ranchlands during the pre-dawn hours producing brief downpours, plenty of lightning and heavy downpours. The downpours over Zapata resulted in the flooding of the arroyos near the Medina Addition with a foot of water reported on the roadways. As the storms neared the coast, they slowed down. The combination of the slowing momentum along with convergence from light southeasterly flow, enhanced convection across eastern Cameron County, resulting in almost 2.5 inches of rainfall in less than two hours. Details: Zapata County Sheriffs Office reported flooding of the arroyos near the Medina Addition in Zapata, along with a foot of water on roadways.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Snow: California, May 07, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Heavy Snow, from May 07, 2015 to May 08, 2015. Affected areas: San Bernardino County Mountains, San Diego. Episode summary: A very large and cold upper-level low deepened along the West Coast before moving inland directly over southern California. This late-season system brought significant rain and snow showers over and west of the mountains on the 7th and 8th. Most of these areas saw between one-quarter of an inch and one inch of precipitation over these two days. The snow level dropped to around 3500 feet with light snow falling, but not sticking at that elevation. Above 4000 feet, snow amounts ranged from 1 to 6 inches, requiring chain control on Sunrise Highway in San Diego County. Flooding due to heavy rainfall was reported at the Spring Valley Quarry Road dip and Escondido Creek on Country Club Drive, where the roads were closed. At the beginning of the event, strong westerly winds produced gusts to 60 mph at Edom Hill and 65 mph at Whitewater RAWS, both in the Banning Pass/mountain desert slope region of Riverside County. Details: CHP reported Country Club Drive closed due to water flowing over road at dip. CalTrans and San Bernardino County Public Works reported power lines down due to 2-6 inches of heavy, wet snow. CHP reported Quarry Road closed due to flooding in the low water crossing. The road had to be closed twice. Reported property and crop damage: about $4,000.

title: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain: California, May 14, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, from May 14, 2015 to May 14, 2015. Affected areas: San Diego. Episode summary: A cold, late-season upper-level low moved inland over southern California on the 14th and 15th, bringing another round of winter storm-like conditions and precipitation. The initial round of rainfall occurred the afternoon of the 14th, heaviest in Orange County and the Inland Empire. Additional intense cells developed (with thunder) between 0500-0700 PST from Oceanside to Temecula and Point Loma to El Cajon. Lindbergh Field received 1.3 inches in 1 hour and 0.71 in 9 minutes during this time, setting records. Impacts included a debris flow near Fallbrook along Highway 395, 6 high water rescues reported by Lifeguards from Midway to Mission Hills and North Park, and flooding/road closure again at Spring Valley Quarry Road dip and Escondido Creek on Country Club Drive. The Padres baseball game experienced a rare 2-hour delay as well, due to the rain. The Fashion Valley river gage on the San Diego River reached 7 feet with road closures and golf course flooding in the area. A flash flood watch was in effect for the 15th due to the widespread showers in recently burned areas and steep terrain. A flash flood warning was issued on the 14th for southwestern San Diego County due to a thunderstorm with heavy rain.|In addition to the rain, winds were very strong, gusting in the upper 50s and 60s mph below the E-W passes and along the desert mountain slopes. Details: There were reports of San Diego fire and police responding to multiple (6 incidents) swift water rescues in the Midway and Mission Hills neighborhoods. San Diego Lindbergh Field reported 1.30 inches of rain from 1900-2000 PST. The 6 hour period prior totaled 1.57 inches. The 9

text: fire and police responding to multiple (6 incidents) swift water rescues in the Midway and Mission Hills neighborhoods. San Diego Lindbergh Field reported 1.30 inches of rain from 1900-2000 PST. The 6 hour period prior totaled 1.57 inches. The 9 minute period within that main hour, totaled 0.71 inches, which is near the 1/100 return interval. San Diego Fire and San Diego city lifeguard swift rescue reported at least 3 vehicles under water and responded to high water rescues. The Midway area at the Marine Corps Recruit Depot was closed with a vehicle under 4 feet of water. A vehicle floated and damaged other vehicles. Trash cans were also reported floating. Homes on Torrance and Reynard were flooded with some resident evacuations and ga Reported property and crop damage: about $150,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 19, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 19, 2015 to July 19, 2015. Affected areas: San Bernardino. Episode summary: Very moist and unstable conditions were present across Joshua Tree National Park on July 19th, due in large part to a significant infusion of tropical moisture from former hurricane Dolores. During the afternoon hours, thunderstorms developed across much of the park, and they produced intense downpours with peak rain rates well in excess of 2 inches per hour. The very heavy rainfall led to some flash flooding in the western portion of Joshua Tree National Park which also caused debris to flow across roads near the west entrance to the park. Fortunately there were no injuries due to the flash flooding. Details: Thunderstorms developed across portions of Joshua Tree National Park during the afternoon hours on July 19th. Due to an infusion of tropical moisture from former hurricane Dolores, the storms generated torrential rainfall with peak rain rates well in excess of 2 inches per hour. The intense rainfall led to flash flooding across the western portion of the park. At about 1500PST, local law enforceme Reported property and crop damage: about $5,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 19, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 19, 2015 to July 19, 2015. Affected areas: Imperial. Episode summary: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed over the lower deserts of Imperial and eastern Riverside county during the afternoon and evening hours on July 19th. Due to an infusion of tropical moisture from former hurricane Dolores, some of the storms produced torrential rainfall with peak rainfall rates in excess of 3 inches per hour. The heavy rain led to episodes of flash flooding, one of which affected northeastern Imperial county during the evening hours. Flash flooding washed out highway 78 to the southwest of Cibola, and as a result the road was closed. Fortunately, no injuries were reported due to the flash flooding. Details: Scattered thunderstorms continued to develop across portions of eastern Imperial county during the evening hours on July 19th. Due to an infusion of tropical moisture from former hurricane Dolores, some of the storms produced torrential rainfall which led to localized flash flooding. Peak rain rates were well in excess of 3 inches per hour. At 1843PST, the California Highway Patrol reported that a Reported property and crop damage: about $50,000.

title: Flash Flood: California, Jul 18, 2015
text: NOAA Storm Events report for California: Flash Flood, from July 18, 2015 to July 18, 2015. Affected areas: Riverside. Episode summary: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Riverside county during the late morning hours on July 18th and they continued into the afternoon. Due to an infusion of tropical moisture from former hurricane Dolores, some of the storms produced torrential rainfall which led to episodes of flash flooding. One area hit hard by the flash flooding was Desert Center and nearby roads such as Kaiser Road which runs up to Eagle Mountain, and highway 177. Flash flood warnings were issued for the area around Desert Center; fortunately there were no injuries associated with the flash flooding. Details: During the late morning hours on August 18th, scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Riverside county and they affected the area around the community of Desert Center. Due to an infusion of tropical moisture from former hurricane, some of the storms produced torrential rainfall with peak rain rates well in excess of 2 inches per hour.
